result.description: Fires on scattered function words, commas and word pieces (' to', ' of', ',', 'ulate', 'ical') in abstract academic-style prose, mid-phrase. The peaks are mixed and the same tokens are often silent in the contrast, so no clear trigger or condition emerges.
result.label: Scattered function words in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on the plural ending of "cultures" or "societies" when it is the subject of a clause, as in "some Eastern societies may..." or "other cultures have...". It stays silent when the word follows "across", "among" or "analyze". It predicts a verb next.
result.label: Cultures/societies as clause subject

result.description: Fires mostly on 'ph' in "lymph" (lymph cell, lymphatic), and also on dashes, underscores in math subscripts and some function words. Silent on 'ph' in elephants or macrophages, so it needs the lymph word.
result.label: 'ph' in lymph, plus dashes/subscripts

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (in, to, with, commas) in technology/VR/AR and user-experience text, where the next word is likely a tech or domain term. Silent on many ' in' tokens elsewhere. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in VR/tech text

result.description: Fires on spatial-spread prepositions such as " across" and " over" (also " multiple", " single") after a noun in cloud/networking/tech text, as in "resources across multiple domains" or "over the internet".
result.label: across/over spread in cloud tech text

result.description: Fires on ' English' (rarely Italian/Japanese) when it ends a "X in English" phrase naming the language being studied, as in grammar-lesson titles. It stays silent when English directly modifies a noun, as in "English grammar".
result.label: "in English" language-name ending phrase

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ers' in "Supersymmetry" (the word-start "Sup" + "ers"), predicting the continuation "ymmetry". Silent on 'ers' ending words like "researchers" or "astronomers".
result.label: 'ers' inside Supersymmetry

result.description: Fires on the token 'b' when it is the piece after "micro" in "microbial" (predicting "ial"). Silent on 'b' in other words like symbiosis, Herb, or molybdenum.
result.label: 'b' in "microbial"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in technical text, such as LaTeX math delimiters (\(, \), =, {), 'es', 'are', and verbs like 'contains' in science and math passages. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Math/science LaTeX and function tokens

result.description: Fires on the subject noun or following function word (prices, demand, "to", "also", "will") in economics text about how a quantity changes with conditions, right before a verb like vary, rise, drop or decrease. Silent on prices in equilibrium or setting-price phrases.
result.label: Economic subject awaiting change verb

result.description: Fires on determiners and possessives (the, their, its, 's) in ocean, sea and seafaring writing, right before a noun. The same 'the' is silent in general text. Members include sea, ship and voyage topic detectors.
result.label: Determiners in ocean/seafaring text

result.description: Fires mostly on possessive 's after a noun like "field's" or "component's" in math/physics text about magnitude, divergence or vectors, and on some function words there. It stays silent on 's after theorem or theory names. Members are math-topic detectors.
result.label: Possessive 's in math/physics text

result.description: Fires on scattered verbs and function words (restore, maintain, includes, in, commas, ' user') where a noun object or technical term is expected next. Peaks are mixed, and the circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Diffuse mixed verbs and function words

result.description: Fires on words like "values", "of" (culture of), "to" (commitment to), and "-izes" that introduce a positive value or ideal in workplace/organizational ethics text, predicting words like integrity or respect. Silent on "values" as a plain noun.
result.label: Culture-of / values-ideal slot

result.description: Fires on ' under' directly after a noun, typically a subject noun before a verb like "underwent", "undergo" or "underpin", where "under" is the start of a split word. It stays quiet on "under" as a plain preposition in phrases like "obligations under contract".
result.label: ' under' as verb prefix after noun

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' and', also ' to', ' as', ' of') in technical or scientific expository text, such as lists of applications or properties. It stays silent on many ' and' tokens in arts/aesthetics lists. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' f' when it follows a preceding word and a continuation like fruits, fats, frying or fritters is expected. It is silent when ' f' starts the text. It pushes towards continuations such as 'rap', 'eta' and 'ernal'.
result.label: Mid-text ' f' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the token ' Indian', most strongly in text about the Indian number system. Members detect Indian/India and other nationality or language adjectives. Weak activations on unrelated fragments.
result.label: ' Indian' token detector

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, "the", "include", "as") inside technical or expository text, mid-phrase where a noun or technical term is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Diffuse target firing on assorted function words and punctuation (' the', ' first', ' and', ' of', ':') in abstract expository prose. No consistent token or context is visible; members are generic and non-discriminative.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the copula ' are' / ' is' (occasionally 'be') right after a plural or singular subject noun, especially in scientific or expository text, predicting a passive or evaluative predicate (often, typically, calculated, constructed). Silent on some 'are' cases.
result.label: Copula is/are after subject noun

result.description: Fires mostly on hyphens in compound modifiers after a prefix like multi-, high-, lower-, in urban/technical text, and sometimes on function words like "the", "with", "(". Silent on some other hyphens, such as high-income, post-war and off-site.
result.label: Hyphen in multi-/high- compounds

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "sense" (also "feeling") in "a sense of X", where an abstract quality or emotion comes next. It stays silent on " of" after nouns like complexity, interplay, nature or flow.
result.label: "sense of" / "feeling of" ' of'

result.description: Fires mostly on ' to' after "continues/continue" (e.g. "technology continues to evolve") in texts about technology and future developments. Also weakly on other verb-slot words like ' are', 'ing'. Silent on other ' to' uses.
result.label: "continues to" in tech-future text

result.description: Fires on plural or work-noun endings (works, -ies, -ets, pieces) naming artistic or creative output, such as ballets, choreographies, quartets, in arts and music text. Predicts "by"-type continuations (by, written). Silent on some "works" in generic visual-art contexts.
result.label: Plural artistic works nouns

result.description: Fires on ' not' right after a verb or subject, where a "not only / not just / not merely" contrast is expected. It boosts continuations like only, just, merely and necessarily. It is quieter after forms of "is/are".
result.label: "not" opening "not only/just"
' dich' word-start in dichotomy
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' dich' at the start of "dichotomy" (or "dichotomous"), as in "this dichotomy between motion and stillness". Members are detectors of dich and other incomplete word-starts like anth, neg, anom, Arist.

Fires on function words and verb pieces (which, of, from, down, -ating) in molecular biology text about DNA/RNA transcription and translation, where the next word is likely DNA, gene or code. Silent on generic "This is where" outside biology.
result.label: Function words in DNA transcription text

result.description: Fires on the contraction piece 'll (will) right after a closing quote mark at the start of a sentence, e.g. "...communication.'ll discuss". It predicts a bare verb next. It stays silent on "that'll" after a word.
result.label: 'll after closing quote

result.description: Fires on " into" (also commas, "means") right after "plaintext" in encryption text, where the next word is a transformed form like ciphertext or "unreadable". Silent on other uses of "into" such as "entry into" or "delves into".
result.label: "plaintext into" encryption transformation

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' tun' (tuning, tunica, tuned) when it is a partial word that needs a continuation. It predicts suffix pieces such as 'emen' or 'son'. Members detect ' tun' and other word-start fragments.
result.label: ' tun' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' fe' at the start of a split word, mostly 'feudal'/'feudalism', also 'fees', 'feather'. Members are ' fe' token detectors that boost continuations like 'ud', 'ats', 'ast'.
result.label: ' fe' word-start piece (feudal)

result.description: Fires on the last token of a noun phrase or subject-like abstract noun (analysis, time, century, ception, ism) at a clause-boundary position, where a comma or continuation is expected rather than a sentence end. Peaks are scattered across many words.
result.label: Abstract noun ending an opening phrase

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' their', 'enc', ' proceed', ' increased', pronouns and function words) in expository text, often where a possessive/pronoun or a verb is expected next. Silent on many ' their' cases, so the pattern is inconsistent.
result.label: Mixed pronoun and function-word slots

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (of, and, in, the, providing) in expository passages about ancient history, culture and religion. Peaks are inconsistent. Members detect ancient-civilization context (Egypt, Greek, Mesopotamia). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Function words in ancient-history text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, a, of, commas, and) in abstract academic prose, mid-phrase before an abstract noun. Silent on 'the' in several similar contexts, and the members are diffuse, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in abstract academic prose

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "importance", "significance", "necessity" or "benefits", where a gerund or noun phrase follows (understanding, considering). Silent on ' of' after "culture", "perspective", "nature" or "well-being".
result.label: ' of' after importance/significance

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ung' completing "unsung" (as in "unsung heroes"), predicting "hero" next. Weaker on similar words like "silent" in "silent hero" and on the 'ung' of "Hungarian".
result.label: 'ung' in "unsung heroes"

result.description: Fires on varied function words and mid-phrase tokens (the, commas, involves, in, an) inside abstract expository text about algorithms, music or science, where a noun phrase is expected next. Silent on "the" after a comma in appositive definitions. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in technical exposition

result.description: Fires on list connectors (' and', commas, 'as well as') inside lists of string instruments like violins, violas, cellos, predicting the next instrument name. Silent on 'and' in generic lists of other kinds of things.
result.label: Connectors in string instrument lists

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' the', also ' to', ' a') right after a definitional "X refers to / describes" in physics explanations like polarization and waves. It stays silent on ' the' in other physics sentences.
result.label: 'the' after "refers to" in physics

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' Bal' in Battle of Balaclava, ' the', ' as', ' famous') in passages about battles and wars, where a battle name or military term is likely to come next. Members are mostly military/history context.
result.label: Battle-history slot before battle names

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' the', 'display', 'ating', commas, 'and') in text about animal behavior, communication and social traits, where a descriptive adjective like "dynamic" or "intricate" may come next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Animal behavior text, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on verbs or connectives (aid, promote, ensure, -ing forms, 'and', 'with', 'for') in text about communication and language, where a benefit-type object like clarity or understanding comes next. Silent on -ing in other contexts.
result.label: Communication-benefit verbs in language text

result.description: Fires on ' field' as a physics term (magnetic/electric/quantum field, field lines), predicting field-related continuations like strength or lines. Silent on 'field' meaning a domain ("the field of electronics").
result.label: Physics 'field' (magnetic/electric)

result.description: Fires mostly on word pieces like " compar" (comparable) and " thr" (thrilling), plus some connective words like "of", "between", "employ", in abstract expository prose. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: compar-/thr- word starts, mixed

result.description: Fires on copulas (is/are/was/were/being) after an abstract noun subject, in abstract academic prose, where a hedge or negative predicate (often, not, problematic) is expected. Silent on some 'are' cases, e.g. after 'we' or political topics.
result.label: Copula after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the comma, " and", or "implies" right after a logical variable pair like "If P" or "P = Q", in formal conditional-logic statements (modus ponens/tollens). Silent on "and" in ordinary lists of logic terms.
result.label: Connective after "If P" in logic

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' consum' (start of "consumers"/"consumed") in economics text, predicting a suffix like "ers" or "mate". Members mostly detect ' consum' itself, with a few related to customer, supplier and stakeholder.
result.label: ' consum' word-piece in economics text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " fab" (and "Fab") when it begins "fabric(s)", mostly in textile text. It is the incomplete first fragment of a word that is about to continue. Members detect similar word-start pieces like cot-, por-, furn-.
result.label: ' fab' start of fabric(s)

result.description: Fires on "ative" in "narrative" and on " story" in "storytelling", mostly in literary-technique discussions (narrative techniques, structure, styles). It stays silent on some "narrative" tokens in other phrasings, so the condition is unclear. Predicts craft nouns such as techniques, structure and voice.
result.label: narrative / storytelling in literary craft

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, in, to, for, both, define) in abstract social, spiritual or institutional prose, where a noun or verb phrase is being continued. Silent on many ' of' tokens in other phrases. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Function words in social/spiritual prose

result.description: Fires on commas or "and" separating items in a list of company or place names (e.g. "Toyota, General Electric", "Massachusetts, New York"), where the next item is another proper name. Silent on commas after ordinary clauses.
result.label: Comma in proper-name lists

result.description: Fires on function words (are, their, its, which, commas) in technical science text on polymers, chemistry and materials, where a noun-phrase continuation follows. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit failed faithfulness, so the reading is tentative.
result.label: Function words in polymer/chemistry text

result.description: Fires on connecting words (" they", " which", " that", comma) that begin a clause about economic or financial policy, such as taxes, banks and monetary tools. Stays silent on "they" in other framings, such as a metaphor about conductors.
result.label: Clause connectors in economic policy text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (word endings like -ability, -igue, commas, ' for') in lists of material properties or abstract nouns, mostly in engineering/materials text. Mixed and low-consistency; silent on 'ion' in corrosion.
result.label: Materials-property list items, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the piece 'cient' in "Ancient" at the start of a document or heading, as in "Ancient China/India/Greece". It weakly fires on era words like "Age" and "Classical". Logits favour Greek/Greece-type continuations.
result.label: 'cient' in "Ancient" headings

result.description: Fires on words meaning "by means of / using" (using, use of, employ, through, utilize) when introducing techniques in writing about sensory description and literary devices. Silent on a bare document-initial "using".
result.label: Technique-instrument verbs in descriptive-writing text

result.description: Fires on ' who' as a relative pronoun right after a plural or person noun (individuals, employees, leaders, people), introducing a clause about what that group does. It predicts a following verb.
result.label: relative 'who' after person noun

result.description: Fires mostly on ' P' (P as a variable or the start of Pythagoras/Ptolemy-like names) and on scattered function words like ' of' and ' and' in passages about ancient Greek and Roman thought. Mixed, weakly consistent.
result.label: ' P' token and ancient-history 'of'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verbs (' to', ' the', ' towards', ' and', ' reach') where the next word is likely a language- or science-related noun. The logits favor prefixes like super/inter/inner. The evidence is mixed and the contrast is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words before technical nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'ust' in 'crust' within Earth-science text about crust, mantle and lithosphere. It also fires weakly on other tokens in geology passages, such as ' layer', 'phere' and ' the'. It stays silent on 'ust' in 'Sustainable'.
result.label: 'ust' in crust (Earth geology)

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' subt' (subtle, subtleties, subtly), mostly after verbs like convey or capture. It predicts continuations such as 'le', 'let', 'len'. Members are mostly ' subt' detectors.
result.label: ' subt' piece (subtle)

result.description: Fires on verbs of altering or modifying (change, modify, alter, manipulate, adjust) including their -ing forms and word pieces, when they take an object, as in "by modifying the...". Silent on unrelated -ing words like "lasting" or "challenging".
result.label: Change/modify/alter verbs

result.description: Fires on the word piece " impro" (start of improves/improving/improvisation), mostly after "and" or "also" in a verb slot. It was silent once, in "in terms of improving".
result.label: ' impro' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside machine-learning terminology (e.g. 'al' in convolutional, 'cement' in reinforcement, deep, neural, sequence) where the next word is likely a model type such as 'neural networks' or 'learning'. Silent on 'al' in unrelated words.
result.label: Neural network term prediction

result.description: Fires on the comma right after an introductory "for example" / "for instance" (and on "include" after "examples of"), where an illustration is about to follow. Silent on other commas, including after bare "instance" in some contexts.
result.label: Comma after "for example"

result.description: Fires on words within a phrase about Hungary losing roughly two-thirds of its territory after WWI (two, of, its, approximately, plural s). Silent on possessive 's after nations. Members mostly track war/diplomacy/treaty context.
result.label: Territory-loss fraction phrase after WWI

result.description: Fires on relative-clause openers (' which', ' that', or a comma) right after a noun naming a process or technical concept, where a verb describing it comes next. Silent on some ' which' cases, and the contrast doesn't clearly say why.
result.label: Relative 'which' after process noun

result.description: Fires mostly on " behave"/" behavior" in science and engineering text about how materials, soil or compounds act under conditions. It also fires weakly on stray tokens such as " total", " per" and " is". The evidence is mixed.
result.label: behave/behavior in materials science

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (the, commas, that, their, -ing) in expository text about computer architecture and instruction sets, where a hardware/CPU/instruction noun is expected next. Silent on 'the' in other contexts.
result.label: Function words in computer architecture text

result.description: Fires on function words (" the", possessive "s", " to", " and") inside biology text about the digestive system and cells, where a biological noun is expected next. The same " the" stays silent in ecology or general academic text.
result.label: Function words in digestive biology text

result.description: Fires on prepositions (for, to, with, in) and some commas after a noun or adjective in explanatory text about language, grammar and writing. Silent on some ' for' in other contexts; the condition is not clear.
result.label: Prepositions in language/grammar text

result.description: Fires on the piece 't' in "story|t|elling" (also "storytellers"), the split-token point where the next piece should be "elling". Members are detectors of this 't' and boost 'elling'.
result.label: 't' inside story-t-elling

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces ('ment', ' to', ' concert', ' shared') in essays about music, concerts, media and culture. Members mostly boost music/event/media words as next tokens. Peaks are inconsistent; it is silent on 'ment' in ordinary suffixes like 'entertainment'.
result.label: Music/media essay mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires mainly on a comma (also " as", " including") right after a subject noun or named topic near the start of a document, where an appositive or elaboration follows (e.g. "Yersinia pestis, also known as"). Silent on commas joining clauses.
result.label: Appositive comma after introduced topic

result.description: Fires on the word "human" / "Human" (including before -ism, -ity, rights, nature, capital), mostly in humanism and human-values text. It stays silent when "human" appears as the start of "humanism" at the beginning of a text.
result.label: "human" word detector

result.description: Fires on clause-boundary punctuation and conjunctions (;, :, ',', ' and', ' while') in text about pH, acidity and neutrality, where a clause is complete and a contrasting or continuing statement follows. Silent on ' and' joining abstract nouns.
result.label: Clause breaks in pH/acidity text

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in negative contractions (don't, doesn't, didn't, isn't), where 't' comes next. It stays silent on apostrophes in 're, 's, 'd and 'll contractions.
result.label: Apostrophe in n't contractions

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'oth' piece in "Zeroth Law" of thermodynamics, and weakly on a few other tokens like ' between'. It stays silent on 'oth' in other words (isothermal, exotherms) and in the lowercase quoted "zeroth".
result.label: 'oth' in Zeroth Law

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, semicolons, "the", "of", "reaches", "typically") in expository academic text, mid-clause where a verb or noun phrase continues. Silent on many commas in similar text; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-clause function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'idel' in "fidelity" (f-idel-ity), predicting suffix pieces like 'ity'. It stays silent on 'idel' in "guidelines" and is weak in "sidelines", so it needs the f- start.
result.label: 'idel' in fidelity

result.description: Fires on ' a' right after "X is/are/serve as" in a definitional statement where the predicate noun is expected to be an evaluative one (a vital/crucial/pivotal component or area). Silent on ' a' after "seen as", "acts as" or "need for".
result.label: ' a' in "X is a vital..." predicates

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' trans' (as in transcription), mostly in gene-regulation and molecular biology text, where it is followed by "cription"/"criptional". Weaker in other contexts such as tools for transcription.
result.label: ' trans' before transcription (biology)

result.description: Fires at scattered mid-phrase tokens (hyphens, commas, ' to', word-piece starts) where the next word is an open continuation; no single token dominates. Hyphen peaks fire only in some contexts, staying silent in well-known, one-tailed, hand-engraving.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' the', ' of') and nouns like 'bodies' in physics text about collisions, right before 'collision' or 'colliding' words. Silent on ' the' in other physics contexts. Predicts 'coll'/'col'.
result.label: 'the' before collision-related words

result.description: Fires on the copula ' is' (occasionally ' are'/' be') after a subject noun, mainly a technical term or method in statistics or econometrics text, where a predicate like "often/commonly used" or "useful/applicable" comes next. Silent on some other ' is' uses.
result.label: Copula 'is' after technical subject

result.description: Fires on varied function words and connectives (are, the, including, not, a colon) in abstract philosophy text on realism, objectivity and epistemology. Members mostly promote philosophy-related next tokens. Peaks are scattered, and the same tokens are silent in other contexts.
result.label: Philosophy-text function words

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces and function words (e.g. "hazard-ous", "indust-rial", "micro-scop", "the") in scientific or environmental text about waste, sustainability and ecology; peaks are varied and the predicted next tokens are unclear.
result.label: Environmental/science word pieces and 'the'

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and function words (adjectives, suffixes like -ative, 'of') in formal technical or academic text on probability, statistics, math and engineering. Peaks are scattered; the topic members matter most.
result.label: Academic math/stats text, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on commas (and ' or') separating items in lists of grammar terms, such as modal verbs or coordinating conjunctions, in text about English grammar. It stays silent on commas in ordinary descriptive prose about grammar.
result.label: Commas in grammar-term lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' in', ' be', ' as') and digits inside long digit strings, with only 11% consistency. It is silent on many ' the' contexts. Members are diffuse and non-discriminative; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words and digits

result.description: Fires on varied function tokens (commas, 'and', 'to', 'from') and word pieces inside lists or enumerations of types and categories in expository text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is uncertain.
result.label: List/enumeration slot punctuation, mixed

result.description: Fires on ' this' right after the preposition "at" (or "for") in time-phrases like "at this time/point/stage/period", predicting a time noun next. Silent on ' this' after "during", "that", or sentence start.
result.label: "at this" before time noun

result.description: Fires on words like "can", "prevent", "-ing" in definitions of non-excludable or non-rivalrous public goods (preventing/excluding people from using something). Silent on "can" in other topics, such as cooking. Members are diffuse and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Public-good exclusion/prevent wording

result.description: Fires on ' an' right after "played/been/became/as" when it introduces a predicate noun like "important role" or "essential component". Silent on ' an' after "include" or "point to", and on some "is an" cases.
result.label: ' an' before role/component phrase

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' met' when it starts a word that is continued, mainly in "metals" and "metallic", and weakly in "metaphor". It predicts continuations like "als" or "al". It stays silent on "metallurgist" at the start of a text.
result.label: ' met' as start of metal/metaphor

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' radi', ' the', ' in', ' as', ' on') in technical science text, where a nuclear/radio-type word (radio-, nuclear) could come next. Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit fit is weak.
result.label: Predicts radio-/nuclear science word

result.description: Fires on the noun " establishment" (occasionally " creation") when it is the head of an abstract "the establishment of X" phrase, usually after "the" in lists of reforms or initiatives, expecting "of" next.
result.label: "establishment of" as an abstract noun

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' develop', ' editing', 'ing', 'ized', function words) in abstract text about skills, music/audio tools, education or software, where a noun like skills, tools or outcomes is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' develop' is silent in some contexts.
result.label: Skills/tools-domain mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires mainly on " without", and also on " from" after "prevent(ing)", " avoid" and " prevent". These words come right after a verb phrase and before a gerund describing a negative outcome to be avoided, as in "without losing momentum". Most examples are about writing and storytelling.
result.label: 'without' / prevent-from before gerund

result.description: Fires on the adjective after "it becomes" (apparent, evident, clear), in the "it becomes apparent that…" construction, usually after an introductory "when exploring X" clause. It predicts a following "that" clause.
result.label: "it becomes apparent that" adjective

result.description: Fires on connectives like ' and', ' or', ' about', ' intended' in abstract explanatory text about grammar, verbs, actions and narrative structure. It is silent on ' and' in other abstract prose. Peaks are mixed, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Connectives in grammar/linguistics explanations

result.description: Fires on varied function words and commas (before, of, a, the) inside explanatory text about punctuation and grammar, such as periods and sentence structure. It is silent on commas in other spots. Evidence is mixed and the circuit was unfaithful.
result.label: Function words in punctuation/grammar explanations

result.description: Fires mostly on commas (also "uring", " for") after "financial reporting" in lists of duties, in business/finance text. Silent on similar commas after other finance phrases, so the condition is unclear. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Comma after financial reporting lists

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces ' hex', ' oct', ' mor' (and similar) where a longer word is being split, mainly in geometry text such as hexahedra and octahedra. Upstream members are geometry and erosion/landform topic detectors. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: hex/oct word-start pieces in geometry

result.description: Fires on ' we' right after the conjunction "as" in a subordinate clause ("as we move/enter/seek"), usually in trend or future-oriented text. It stays silent on ' we' after a comma-set-off introductory phrase.
result.label: "as we" subordinate clause

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' stim' (stimulating, stimulus, stimuli), where the next piece is likely '-ulating/-ulus'. Members mostly detect ' stim' and similar '-ulat' stems like manip, mod, reg.
result.label: ' stim' word-start piece

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (' of', ' by', ' as', word-piece endings like 'ant', 'ing') in abstract expository text. No dominant token; silent on many ' of' cases. Logits and members give no clear picture.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks, unclear

result.description: Peaks are scattered across mid-sentence function words and word pieces (' often', ' and', ' specific', ' an', 'ists') in academic or educational prose. The contrast shows ' often' staying silent, and no clear condition emerges.
result.label: Scattered mid-sentence words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on varied function words and modifiers (of, any, future, with, much) in finance/business text, where the next word is likely a finance noun. Silent on ' of' after abstract nouns like "credibility of". Mixed evidence.
result.label: Finance text modifiers before nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece "igen" in "epigenetics"/"epigenetic", predicting suffixes like "etic" or "omic". It is weak on "igen" in "antigen" and silent elsewhere.
result.label: "igen" in epigenetics

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, ' the', word pieces like 'ized', 'ines', 'ava') with no consistent token or context. Logits are weak, favoring name-like fragments. Members are diffuse and non-specific, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Diffuse mixed-token latent

result.description: Fires on skill/quality adjectives (sk-illed, successful, effective, astute, careful) in sentence-initial or modifier position before a noun, mainly in writing/craft text. It stays silent when 'illed' starts the text without 'sk'.
result.label: Skilled/effective adjective before noun

result.description: Fires on ' artists' as the plural subject right after an introductory clause ("By using the Rule of Thirds, artists can..."). It stays silent when 'artists' is the object of "by". Weaker on similar subjects like 'writers'.
result.label: ' artists' as sentence subject

result.description: Fires on ' such' right after a plural noun or category noun, where "such as" is expected to introduce examples. It stays silent when 'such' follows a preposition as a determiner ("in such explorations"). Logits favor ' as'.
result.label: 'such' introducing examples (such as)

result.description: Fires on " thorough" (also "in-depth") when it introduces an analysis or examination, typically "A thorough examination/understanding of". Pushes toward nouns like understanding, examination, analysis. Weaker on "detailed" and "comprehensive".
result.label: " thorough" before analysis nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' philosoph' when it is a person-noun stem about to take the '-ers' ending, as in 'Greek philosophers'. It predicts agent suffixes like 'ers'. Weakly fires on similar stems such as 'astronom'.
result.label: ' philosoph' before -ers

result.description: Fires on mixed word pieces, mostly 'net' in "Magnetic", ' magnetic', and hyphens in technical science text (magnetism, semiconductors, materials). Peaks are scattered and consistency is low, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Magnetic/physics word pieces

result.description: Fires on words that introduce a blending of two things (merge, merges, combine, between, "and" after technology) in art and craft text, where a pair of contrasting elements is expected next. Silent on ordinary "of".
result.label: Merging/combining two elements in art

result.description: Fires mostly on 'il' in "fossil" (also on scattered tokens like 'ing', ':', 'and') in biology/science text where a noun like species or animals is likely next. Silent on 'il' in "resilient", so it needs the fossil word.
result.label: 'il' in fossil, science text

result.description: Fires on " asset" (also " capital", " assets") as a modifier in finance text, especially before nouns like "allocation", "classes" or "structure". Silent on non-finance text.
result.label: Asset in finance noun phrases

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, 'as', 'id', 'including', verb pieces) inside lists of examples or factors in explanatory expository text on environment, ecology or history. Peak tokens are mixed and the evidence is thin; it stays silent on 'as well as'.
result.label: Example-list positions in expository text

result.description: Fires mainly on the modal " can" (also " could", "to") after a plural or collective subject, such as "we can" or "policymakers can", in academic text about economics and design. Silent on some " can" after singular abstract subjects.
result.label: Modal 'can' after agent subjects

result.description: Fires on scattered function words, hyphens, and word pieces (' for', ' of', ' between', '-', '_') in abstract technical or academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent (16%), and logits are weak, so there is no clear shared token or construction.
result.label: Scattered function-word mid-phrase positions

result.description: Fires on the comma, closing quote or conjunction (and/or) right after a quoted word in a list of quoted examples, such as 'on', or 'a' or. It expects another quoted item next, and pushes toward opening quotes.
result.label: Separator after quoted list item

result.description: Fires on ' cell' (esp. in "process of cell-ular") and scattered function words (of, to, comma, on) in biology/cell-biology text, where the next token is likely a cell-related continuation. Silent on ' cell' in other cell contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: cell and function words in biology

result.description: Fires on word pieces ending a noun about birds or clothing (jack-et, peac-ock, fe-ather, e-agle, bird) inside descriptive similes or imagery. Silent on 'ather' in 'rather than'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Bird/clothing noun word-endings in imagery

result.description: Fires on the adverb ' easily', mostly before a participle or adjective such as recognizable, accessible or understood (e.g. "both X and easily comprehensible"). It is weak on related ease words like "easy to".
result.label: Adverb 'easily' before adjective

result.description: Fires on example-introducing connectors (" as" in "such as", " like", " by", " including") after nouns for regulations, laws or standards, where a named standard or body (ISO, OSHA) is expected next. Silent on some similar "such as" cases.
result.label: Example connector before named standards

result.description: Fires on 'ations' in "fluctuations" (and 'variations') in cosmology/inflation text, where the subject slot of a sentence about quantum fluctuations is being completed. Silent on 'ations' in other words like alterations or formations.
result.label: Quantum fluctuations 'ations' in cosmology

result.description: Fires on ' fields' (also ' areas') right after a quantifier phrase like "in various" or "in a variety of", at the start of a sentence, where a list of domains follows. Silent on ' fields' after "of", "these" or "in", followed by "like".
result.label: "in various fields" domain noun

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and modifiers (of, and, its, a, increases, vast) in the middle of expository phrases, mostly in comparison or quantity contexts. Silent on many ' of' tokens, so the pattern is diffuse and unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase function words

result.description: Fires on " in" right after "measured" (or "expressed/denoted"), where a unit of measurement is expected next (watts, amperes, volts). Stays silent on other uses of " in" such as "in order to" or "change in".
result.label: "measured in" unit-introducing preposition

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ' becoming', ' where', digit '0') in expository academic text, with no consistent token. Silent on some ' and' joining nouns in lists. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on commas, semicolons and 'and' that continue a clause inside statistics or math explanations, mid-sentence after a complete phrase. Silent on commas at the start of a text fragment. Members are statistics/math topic detectors plus comma detectors.
result.label: Mid-sentence commas in statistics text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' prior' when it begins "prioritize/prioritizes" after a subject or modal (e.g. "companies prioritize", "must prioritize"). It is silent on "prior" in gerund or "to prioritized" contexts. Predicts "it" as the continuation.
result.label: ' prior' starting "prioritize"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'vol' in "ever-evolving", the word-piece after "ever-e". Members detect 'ever', 'e' and 'vol' and push the continuation "ving".
result.label: 'vol' in ever-evolving

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on scattered tokens (' the', 'F', 'Time', ' Earth', ' surface') inside technical or expository text. Peaks share no clear token or construction, and the members are mostly generic context.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after "Earth" or "planet" (Earth's, our planet's), in earth-science text. It is silent on 's in "it's", other names' possessives, plurals and verbs. It predicts a following Earth-feature noun such as surface or atmosphere.
result.label: Possessive 's after Earth/planet

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered function words (' the', ' of', ' and', commas) and other mid-sentence tokens in expository technical text, where a noun or modifier is expected next. No clear single token or construction; the circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Diffuse function-word slot in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, digits, 'the', 'and', Chinese byte pieces, dash runs) with no clear pattern. Members are mixed context features, and the circuit is unfaithful. Logits are noisy name fragments.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token unclear latent

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' in "analytical" when it modifies a following method noun, as in "analytical technique" or "analytical tool". It stays silent on 'ical' in other words (chemical, clinical, pharmaceuticals) and in some "analytical" contexts.
result.label: 'ical' in "analytical" before technique

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', possessive 's, ' of', ' describes') inside explanations of quantum mechanics, such as wave functions and the Schrödinger equation. The same words stay silent in other physics-related contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in quantum wavefunction text

result.description: Fires on 'elevate(s)' and on prepositions (to, of, into) right after nouns like depth, quality, richness, in text about enhancing writing or storytelling. Silent on 'to' in other uses like 'leading to' or 'allow writers to'.
result.label: Enhancing-writing prepositions after 'elevate'/'add depth'

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' gest' when it starts "gestures" (mid-sentence, after a word), predicting the "ures" continuation. Weaker hits on a few title-initial words like International or Network. Silent when ' gest' opens the text.
result.label: ' gest' piece in 'gestures'

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' Equ', '.', ' or', '/') inside lists of short topic or heading names, such as academic subjects and terms separated by periods. Silent on '.' after many other headings. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: List-of-topic-names item boundary

result.description: Fires on adjectives like cultural, unique, diverse, distinct that modify a following noun such as customs, identities or traditions, in text about culture and human societies. It stays silent on 'cultural' after 'of' or 'these' in some contexts.
result.label: Culture-describing adjectives before traditions

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' of', ' in', ' by', ' as') in expository science and biology-style prose, mostly where a noun phrase is about to follow. Silent on many ' the' tokens, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words before noun phrases

result.description: Fires on function words (' and', ' their', ',', ' as') in animal-trait descriptions, where a list or feature phrase about species anatomy or hunting traits continues. Silent on 'and' in other contexts, such as aquatic-species lists.
result.label: Animal trait list connectors
' f' in nutrient/science lists
result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' f' (fats, fructose, fibrous) when it comes in a list of nutrients or technical terms, such as "carbohydrates, proteins, f". It stays silent on ' f' in casual text like "their fruits".

Fires on the token ' orbit' (including in 'orbital', 'orbiters' contexts and repeated-orbit text), driven by upstream detectors of the same token. Weak activation on unrelated tokens like ' neg' and ' an'.
result.label: ' orbit' token detector

result.description: Fires on the piece "or" when it is the middle of the split word "theorems" (the-or-ems), mostly in math text. It stays silent on "or" in other words like "rigorously" or "Pythagoras", or as the plain word "or".
result.label: "or" inside "theorems"

result.description: Fires on the prefix token ' un' at the start of a negated word (unacknowledged, unpredictable, unnoticed), typically after a determiner, adverb or preposition. Members are all ' un' detectors; it predicts word continuations.
result.label: ' un' negation prefix
'res' piece before -istant/-pect
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'res' / ' Res' when it begins a word like resistant or respect (earthquake-resistant, Respect for..., disrespect). Silent on 'res' ending a word, as in 'theatres'. It pushes towards continuations like 'istant' and 'pect'.
Fires on the word piece ' li' in "can be li-kened to", predicting "ken" next. Members are mostly ' li' detectors, also covering "li-abilities". Silent on contrast text without that word piece.
result.label: ' li' in "can be likened"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' chem' (or ' Chem') that begins words like chemistry, chemical, chemists, chemometric. Strongest after "in" or a field-name context. Silent in one case after "Organometallic".
result.label: ' chem' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on prepositions (within, of, in, throughout) that follow a noun in writing-craft text about narrative, pace and plot, where a story element is expected next. Silent on 'within' in other contexts like constraints or readers.
result.label: Prepositions in narrative craft text

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' could', also 'that', 'such as', 'of') in risk and security-assessment text, where the next word is likely a risk or threat term or a negative outcome. Silent on 'could' in casual or speculative contexts.
result.label: Function words in risk-assessment text

result.description: Fires on minimizing or contrastive words like "just", "simply", "mere", "beyond" after "more than" or "goes beyond", in text about listening and communication. It predicts a listening-related activity noun (hearing). Silent on some "not just" and "more than just" cases.
result.label: "more than just" in listening text

result.description: Fires on varied function words or word pieces (" the", "one", "mos", " partial") in technical food-chemistry and science text, just before a technical term such as "spatial", "partial hydrogenation" or "histone". Members are food, fat and chemistry context detectors.
result.label: Food-chemistry word before technical term

result.description: Fires on 'ground' as the second piece of 'underground' (also 'water' in 'underwater'/'groundwater', 'face' in 'surface') in hydrology and geology text about subsurface water and utilities.
result.label: 'ground' in underground (subsurface text)

result.description: Fires most often on 'ide' in "World Wide Web", plus scattered peaks on commas, "This" and "A" at document start. Mixed evidence; the 'ide' piece is the clearest trigger, and the circuit's members are diffuse.
result.label: 'ide' in World Wide Web

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: commas (including runs of escaped commas), ' remove(s)', ' drive', and some function words in technical or process text. Peaks are inconsistent and members are diffuse; no clear shared condition.
result.label: Scattered commas and remove/drive verbs

result.description: Fires on degree adverbs like "primarily", "largely", "mainly", "predominantly" right after a copula or passive verb ("was primarily", "were largely"), usually in descriptions of how things were done historically. It predicts adjectives or participles such as "focused" or "concerned".

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' w' (as in w-ield, w-elfare, w-ages, w-ool), especially right after "such" in "such w…" lists. It predicts continuations like 'ield', 'itch', 'eta'. It stays quiet on ' w' after "the" or "social".

result.description: Fires on the word start ' quant' (also ' spec', ' simpl') when it is a verb stem right after a subject like "which" or "it", predicting "-ifies". Silent when 'quant' appears as a noun or adjective (quantifiers, quantitative, quantified).

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fat' as the start of "fatigue" (material fatigue texts), and also on ' fat' in dietary fat contexts. Members are mostly ' fat' detectors that push toward 'igue'.
result.label: ' fat' token (fatigue)

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: the suffix 'ary' after some words (revolution-ary), and ' of'/' the' after verbs like "manipulate the darkest parts of". Contexts are literary or psychological prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Mixed 'ary' suffix and 'of' in prose

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ational' (and sometimes ' social') in text about conversation, pragmatics and speech acts, e.g. "conversational maxims". It stays quiet on 'ational' in "foundational" and "organizational".

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, "the", "a", verbs like "contains/include") in expository technical text, mid-sentence where a noun phrase is expected next. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words, commas and word pieces (',', ' of', ' and', ' manage', 'ving') in abstract math, business-framework or technical prose. No single token dominates; members mostly push toward mathematical/algebraic vocabulary. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' (sometimes ' an') after "X is/as/," when defining a academic or technical field, e.g. "Hydrology is a ...". It predicts field-describing nouns like science or branch. Silent on other uses of 'a'.
result.label: 'a' introducing a field definition

result.description: Fires on function words (' a', ' the', 'person' in 'personality') that begin a noun phrase in essay-like text about design, branding, typography and menus. Silent on ' a' as a word piece or in other contexts.
result.label: Articles before noun in design text

result.description: Fires on the word piece " expl" when it starts a finite verb form like "explored" or "explores", typically after a subject such as "artists who". It stays silent when the piece begins the noun "exploration" or a gerund after "of" or "for".

result.description: Fires on sentence-boundary periods and capitalized sentence-initial "When", plus some Arabic word-initial letters, at the start of a new sentence or segment. Silent on periods after person names in name lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful.

result.description: Fires on function words (of, as, or, are, include, against) that come right before a list or object of pollutants, errors or harms, especially in "such as" in air-pollution text. Silent on many ' of' tokens elsewhere. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words before pollutant lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (in, the, that, apostrophe) in abstract academic prose, mid-sentence before a noun phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast shows the same tokens silent, so the specific need is unclear.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on ' a' right after a verb like "is", "offers", "creates" when describing a teaching method (TPR, Direct Method), where an adjective plus noun comes next. Silent on ' a' after prepositions such as "of" or after "employing".

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word endings like 'ance', 'dom', hyphens, 'to', 'both') in technical or academic text, often mid-phrase, with no consistent token. Silent on 'ance' in other words, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in technical text

result.description: Fires on example-introducing words ("such as", "like", "include", "including") that precede a list of examples, in text about nonverbal communication and body language. Silent on causal or role "as" such as "acts as".

result.description: Fires on word pieces starting "analyt"/"Anal" (as in Analytics), predicting a continuation like "ics". Silent on some "analyt" tokens in other contexts (analytical, applying analytics). Also weakly fires on scattered function words.
result.label: Analytics word-start piece
'in' piece inside "machinery"
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'in' inside "mach-in-ery", where the next piece is likely "ery". It stays silent on 'in' in other words such as "refinement" or "infrastructure". It also fires weakly on similar mid-word pieces.

Fires on the word ' resource' when it is a modifier in a compound like "resource allocation/utilization/management", typically after an adjective such as efficient, effective or strategic. It stays quiet when "resource" is a standalone noun, as in "solitary resource".
result.label: ' resource' as compound modifier

result.description: Fires on verbs and prepositions like "create/creating", "of", "up", "in" that come right before an object in materials-engineering text, where a noun like materials or products is expected next. Silent on "of" in phrases like "cusp of" or "combination of".

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after "in" (also weaker after "during") when it opens a time-period phrase such as "in the latter part of" or "in the late 1…", often at a document's start. It is silent on "in the" before topic nouns like "study" or "development".

result.description: Fires mostly on a 'g' piece inside a word after a prefix (under-g-laze, over-g-laze, con-g-estion, step-g-rowth), predicting word continuations like 'row', 'overn'. Weaker, scattered firing on ' limit', ' abund' and function words.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, 'of', 'from', 'in', 'on') in essay-style text about art, music and culture. Members are art/artist-themed. The contrast shows commas often stay silent, so the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'be' in "well-be|ing" (wellbeing), right before the "ing" suffix completes the word. Members detect 'be' and similar mid-word pieces.

result.description: Fires on instrument-introducing words like "using", "through", "of", "between" in writing-craft text about dialogue, right before a technique or noun like dialogue tags is named. Silent on "using" in pacing and timing contexts.

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "diversity" or "range/variety" (diversity of, diverse range of), mostly in biodiversity text. It stays silent on other "of" uses such as "loss of", "one of", "building block of".

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' to', also ' the', ' and', ' an') in technical explanatory text, especially 'enable processes [to] exchange' infinitive slots after a plural subject. Silent on 'to' after correspond/orthogonal/added in linear algebra. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in academic or explanatory prose: ' voice', ' one', commas after a noun phrase, hyphens in compounds like 'infinite-dimensional'. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low. The circuit is diffuse, with no discriminative members.
result.label: Diffuse mid-clause tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the verb ' respond' (occasionally ' react') as a stem before '-ing', especially in lists of listening or communication skills, such as "understanding, and respond|ing accordingly". Silent on general customer-service text.

result.description: Fires mostly on " different" (also " as", " separate", " financial", " arbitrary") in behavioral-finance text about allocating funds to different mental "accounts". It stays silent on " different" in other contexts. Weak evidence; circuit failed.

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' el' when it begins a longer word such as elasticity, elastic, elution or elusive, including after a prefix (price-elasticity, normal-elution). Predicts continuations like 'astic', 'ution', 'uc'.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word pieces like 'ing', 'al', and function words like 'the', 'from', 'human') in explanatory text, mid-phrase before a continuation. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so no clear trigger.

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Arch" (or " arch") when it begins a longer word, such as Archimedes, Archae or archives. It pushes toward continuation pieces like "ib", "ae", "ive".
result.label: Arch- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (-oring, examine, "of", "using") in ecology and conservation text where the next word is likely a species or environment term. Quiet on "exploring" in other contexts.

result.description: Fires on the word " cultural" as an adjective in discussions of cross-cultural communication, language and cultural factors, awareness and differences. Members detect "cultural/Cultural" tokens and related context words.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly commas in lists, ' minor' and mid-phrase function words, where a modifier or noun is expected next. The contrast shows commas after nouns stay silent. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.

result.description: Fires mostly on sentence-ending periods (also ' Through', ' in') in outlines about creative writing, character and conversation techniques. Silent on periods in other topics or heading-like lines. Members push writer/character/narrative words.

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " rh" (or " Rh") that begins words like rhythm, rhyme, rhetoric, predicting continuations such as "ythm"/"yme". Upstream members are mostly the same " rh" detectors. Silent in one case after "sounds and".

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cre' that starts creative/creators/creativity, mostly in art-related text, and pushes toward suffixes like 'ative', 'ators', 'ativity'. Members are mostly ' cre' detectors plus art-topic context.
result.label: ' cre' prefix before -ative/-ator

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' phys' at the start of words like physicist and physiology, where the next piece is a suffix such as 'ic' or 'icians'. Members are mostly detectors of ' phys' itself.
result.label: ' phys' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on " is" (also " becomes") in the expletive "it is possible/clear..." construction after an introductory "By doing X," clause. It stays silent on other " is" uses, such as "In the realm of physics, it is crucial" and noun-subject "X is".

result.description: Fires on 'ative' in 'connotative' (semantics/linguistics text) and on function words like ' a', ' the' in linguistic or semantic-meaning passages. Silent on 'ative' in narrative, transformative, figurative, generative. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the word " human" (or " Human") as a modifier before a noun or hyphen, as in "human-robot", "human error", "human capabilities". It is silent on the plural "humans".

result.description: Fires on the verb "take" (mostly "takes") right after a noun subject, as in "celebration takes place" or "approach takes a...". Members detect take/takes/taking forms. Output boosts plural quantity words like "various" and "multiple".
result.label: Verb "takes" after noun subject

result.description: Fires on prepositions after causal verbs like "resulted in", "led to", "leading to", "brought about", in historical or event-consequence text. It predicts a following outcome noun such as "significant" or "period". It stays quiet on "in" after other nouns or verbs.
