result.description: Fires on the apostrophe after a common noun (eye, moon, river, city) where an 's is expected next, as in a possessive. It stays silent on apostrophes in "it's" or at the start of a text.
result.label: Possessive apostrophe after inanimate noun

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied mid-sentence tokens (commas, ' to', ' a', ')', verbs) in expository text about technology, economics and arts. No dominant token; the logits are mixed. The evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered mid-sentence function tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered word pieces and function words (e.g. 'ological', 'fat'/'ty', 'of') inside biology and science text, mid-phrase. Peaks are inconsistent, and it is silent on some 'ological' cases, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in biology/science text

result.description: Fires on prepositions like "from" and "on" after verbs of deriving or basing (follows from, based on, reasoning from) in texts about deductive logic and proofs. Silent on "from" in contrasts such as "differs from" or "moves from".
result.label: Derivation prepositions in logic texts

result.description: Fires on verb endings or words like "fosters", "promotes", "encouraging" that take an abstract beneficial object (active questioning, inquiry, trust) in educational or philosophical text. Silent on noun "-ers" endings such as "philosophers" or "speakers".
result.label: Fostering/promoting verb in education text

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after a verb like push/pushing/drive, in the idiom "push the boundaries/limits". Members detect push-type verbs and promote 'boundaries'/'limits' as the next word. Silent on ' the' after other verbs.
result.label: "the" after push (boundaries/limits)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and suffixes (' its', ',', ' and', 'ing') in text about cell membranes, homeostasis and biology. Members are biology/cell/protein detectors; it stays silent on ' its' in other contexts, so the trigger is mixed.
result.label: Cell biology function-word positions

result.description: Fires on commas, "including" and "and" inside lists of chemistry applications or fields (e.g. "catalysis, material science, ..."), where another list item is expected. Silent on commas in other science sentences that aren't lists of applications.
result.label: List separators in chemistry applications

result.description: Fires on ' the' after a preposition like "in" or "within" when introducing a mathematical field, domain or space (e.g. "within the study of", "in the complex plane"). It is silent on ' the' in other slots, such as "within the set" or "are the foundation".
result.label: ' the' after in/within, math domain

result.description: Fires mainly on the word-start piece " Ch" (e.g. "Supply Ch|ain") in title-like list headings, plus some hyphens and dashes. Members detect " Ch" tokens that need a continuation such as "ain", "alleng" or "anges".
result.label: " Ch" word-start piece in headings

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' and', commas, 'esian' in Bayesian, opening quotes, ' that') in expository technical text, mostly mid-list or clause boundaries. Evidence is mixed; the contrast is silent on the same ' and' tokens, and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered function-word and 'esian' peaks

result.description: Fires on the final word of a topic-heading or subject noun phrase, mostly "technology/technologies/techniques" (also tools, editing, Apps), often at the start of a document or sentence where a verb like "is/have" comes next. Silent on "technology" mid-sentence after prepositions.
result.label: Technology noun ending a subject phrase

result.description: Fires on function words (' in', ' the', ' of', ' reduce') inside technical physics/science text, especially after "infinities that arise" in calculations. Members are physics, quantum and algebra topic detectors. Silent on ' in' in non-science contexts.
result.label: Function words in physics text

result.description: Fires on the last piece of a multi-token title or heading word (e.g. Conserv-ation, Endem-ism, intellectual property) inside lists of short topic headings, right before the heading ends. Mixed and weak evidence; silent on policy headings.
result.label: Word-ending piece in topic headings

result.description: Fires on mixed function and content words (commas, 'and', 'art', 'market', 'in', 'a') inside text about art events, galleries, markets and collectors. Silent on commas in other topics. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Art and market text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, of, a, in, parentheses) in abstract expository text about language and processes, mostly where a noun phrase is about to start. Silent on many identical 'the' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words before noun phrases

result.description: Fires on the word piece " challeng" (challenged/challenges/challenging), mostly as a verb after a subject like a movement or "that/who", as in art "challenged traditional morality". Predicts a suffix like -ed or -ing.
result.label: ' challeng' verb stem

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' catal' (start of catalyst/catalysis/catalytic), mostly in chemistry text. It predicts continuations like 'yst', 'yt', 'yz'. Upstream members are mostly ' catal' token detectors.
result.label: ' catal' word-piece (catalyst)

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (as, to, including, with, commas) shortly after "gods" or divine/religion topics in ancient-culture text, e.g. "gods such as", "gods including". Silent on the same words in non-religious contexts.
result.label: Connectors after gods in ancient religion

result.description: Fires on the adjectives " uniform" and " consistent" (sameness/consistency sense), mostly in discussions of writing or data consistency, where a noun like "usage", "output" or "-ity" is expected. Weakly on "clear" and on uniform magnetization.
result.label: uniform / consistent adjectives

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (of, the, to, all, aging) inside essays about leadership and management style, where the next word is likely a leadership or employee term. Silent on 'to' in other slots.
result.label: Leadership-essay function words

result.description: Fires on verbs of discovering or identifying ("uncover", "identify", "-ifying", "detecting") when they take an object like hidden patterns, in data analysis text. Predicts a pattern-like object next.
result.label: uncover/identify patterns in data

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in "let's" (lowercase let + '), especially in hortatory openings like "let's not", "let's be honest". Weaker on apostrophes in "don't"; silent on possessive or other contraction apostrophes.
result.label: Apostrophe in "let's"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Arab" when it is a prefix awaiting a suffix such as "-ic" or "-ian" (Arabic script, Arabian Peninsula). Members are mostly Arab detectors plus similar name-stem pieces (Pers-, Mong-ol).
result.label: ' Arab' as stem before -ic/-ian

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' cru' (start of "crucial"), mostly after "is/are/a" in phrases like "X is crucial" or "a crucial role". Members are mostly ' cru' detectors that predict "cial".
result.label: ' cru' in "crucial"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in physics and energy-generation text (electromagnetic induction, current, coils, energy) where a verb like generate/produce/yield is likely next. Silent on 'create' in music contexts; members are largely music-related and generic.
result.label: Generation/production in physics contexts

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' cultural', ' of', ' to', ' each', word pieces) in educational or academic expository text, mid-phrase before a content noun. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse, with weak members.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase tokens in academic text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' dise' (start of "diseases") in medical text, especially after adjectives like systemic or neurodegenerative, and predicts the "ases" continuation. It was silent after "plagued by" in a malaria sentence.
result.label: ' dise' piece before "ases"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " clar" (clarinet, clarity, clarification), predicting continuations like "inet" or "ity". Members mostly detect " clar" itself, plus similar prefixes like par- and pur-.
result.label: ' clar' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' mechan' when it follows a physics or science word like "quantum", "celestial" or "fluid", as in "quantum mechanics". It stays silent in "new mechanisms".
result.label: ' mechan' after quantum/physics term

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (' an', ' that', ' of', ' were', ' to') following a noun in expository text on law, military, or policy topics. Peaks are mixed and the contrast gives no clear condition, so the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Function words after nouns, formal topics

result.description: Fires on example-introducing connectors (" such as", "like", "including") after a general noun for activities, tasks or roles, right before a list of examples. Silent on "as well as" and other uses of "as".
result.label: Example-list introducer 'such as'

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' coord' (before "ination"), and weakly on other word-start fragments like ' Pol' and 'chn' in "Geotechnical". Members are mostly ' coord' detectors, so it predicts a mid-word continuation.
result.label: ' coord' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the noun ' event' (also ' moment', ' point' in 'turning point') right after an adjective like historic, pivotal, significant, or defining, which marks something as an important happening. Also fires weakly on 'event' in event-driven programming.
result.label: Significant event/moment noun

result.description: Fires on connecting words (' with', ' offering', ' offer', commas) in abstract scientific/technology prose, where a clause is about to say what a subject provides or promises (e.g. "offering an exceptional…"). Silent on 'along with'.
result.label: Offering/with before promised benefits

result.description: Fires on the modal ' can' (rarely could/may) after a plural noun or relative clause about errors, problems or inaccuracies, where a negative outcome verb like cause, arise, distort or compromise comes next. Silent on 'can' after 'we' or in neutral contexts.
result.label: 'can' after errors/problems subject

result.description: Fires on the 'igen' piece in "Eigenvalues/Eigenvectors" when it follows "E" mid-word. It stays silent when 'igen' starts the text without the preceding "E". Weak firing on other word-start fragments like ' Emb' and ' En'.
result.label: 'igen' in Eigenvalues/Eigenvectors
Discrete energy levels in physics
result.description: Fires on " energy" when it follows "discrete" in atomic/quantum physics text, as in "discrete energy levels/states". It stays quiet on " energy" in other uses, such as absorbs energy or energy released. Members predict "levels" and "states".

Fires on the word-piece ' infl' at the start of "inflation" (also inflationary, inflaton), mostly in economics text about interest rates and monetary policy. Upstream members are mostly ' infl' detectors.
result.label: ' infl' start of inflation

result.description: Fires on the word " evolution" (also "volution" in "Evolution") as a noun in "the evolution of X" style, often at the start of a title or topic phrase. It is silent in biological or "social evolution" contexts, and when "evolution" ends a phrase.
result.label: "evolution" as noun of development

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (such "as", "like", "involves", "in", "just", "your") in explanatory expository text, where a noun or example is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Diffuse expository connector words

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' in "philosophical" when it modifies a noun about a person's career, development or stance (e.g. John Dewey's philosophical career). It stays silent on 'philosophical' in generic discussion contexts.
result.label: philosophical after possessive, biographical

result.description: Fires on connective words and verbs (uses, through, of, involves, -izes) in explanations of algorithms, recursion and dynamic programming, where a method or technique is about to be described. Quiet on 'through' in other topics.
result.label: Connectives in algorithm explanations

result.description: Fires on "only" (or "to", "just", "simply") right after "not" in a "not only/just/simply X but also Y" construction, where a verb follows. Silent on "not only" followed by a prepositional phrase and on sentence-initial "Only".
result.label: "not only/just" correlative opener

result.description: Fires on 'ough' in "dough" (and sometimes ' bread') in baking and pastry text. It stays silent on 'ough' in "tough". Members are dough and baking detectors plus cooking-context latents.
result.label: 'ough' in dough (baking)

result.description: Fires mid-word on word pieces such as 'ide' in Heidegger, also 'band' in Kanband and some 'and'/'by' connectives. Strongest on the 'ide' piece of Heidegger; the rest is scattered and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Heidegger 'ide' and scattered pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (the, and, commas, organ, waves) in science/music-flavored text. Members mostly push toward music or ancient-era words, but the peaks are inconsistent. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Scattered tokens, music/ancient-leaning

result.description: Fires on the word " depending", typically after a verb or clause like "varies greatly" or "ranges from X to Y", just before "on". Upstream members detect depend-words (depending, depended, relies, based) that lead to "on/upon".
result.label: ' depending' before 'on'

result.description: Fires on function words and verb endings (with, a, to, -s, about) in forward-looking passages about future trends or developments, where the next word is likely an impact verb such as "promise", "transform" or "revolution". Silent on "with" in past-tense narratives.
result.label: Future-outlook connectives predicting impact

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'icul' in "meticulous" (also "curriculum"), a mid-word piece where the next piece is likely "-ous/-ously". It is silent in some "meticulously" contexts after a verb-like construction.
result.label: 'icul' in meticulous

result.description: Fires on words meaning protect/prevent/mitigate, mainly ' against' (also 'mitig-ate', ' prevent'), in cybersecurity text describing defending against threats or vulnerabilities. Silent on 'verification against' sources.
result.label: Defending against threats (security)

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'the', 'critical', word pieces) in academic text about assessment, evaluation, analysis and education, where a noun like assessment/testing/evaluation is likely next. Silent on some 'critical' tokens. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Assessment and evaluation context predictor

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces or numbers in anatomy and biology text (e.g. "20[6] bones", "not[och]ord"), where the next token is an anatomical or biological term. The peak tokens are varied. Members mostly carry anatomy and animal context.
result.label: Anatomy/biology term-in-progress pieces

result.description: Fires on prepositions and articles (' of', ' a', ' in', ' towards', 'through') that follow a verb or noun like "creation of", "adoption of", "stored in", often in reform or modernization text. Silent on ' of' in ordinary phrases like "concept of".
result.label: Prepositions after creation/adoption nouns

result.description: Fires on varied function tokens and punctuation (commas, 'that', 'are', periods) in text describing educational programs, courses and fields of study. Members mostly push teaching, students and education words, with the verb slot after a program subject. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in education program text

result.description: Fires on adjective endings like "connected", "dependent", "resilient", "globalized" in the slot before a noun like "world", "network" or "society", especially after "increasingly" or "more". It is silent on "interconnected" followed by a plural noun phrase ("system components").
result.label: Adjective before "world/society" slot

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' aw' when it is the start of "awareness", after words like increasing, heightened, growing, promote or raise. Silent when "aw" starts the text with no preceding context word.
result.label: ' aw' in "awareness"

result.description: Fires on the space token right before a year or century number (e.g. "early [ ]200", "the [ ]21st") after phrases like "in the early" or "during the". It predicts digits such as 1, 2, 9, 8.
result.label: Space before year digits

result.description: Fires on find/finding/identify/discover(ing) verbs, especially in math or number theory text about finding factors or solutions. Members include math, prime and algebra topic detectors plus find-token detectors.
result.label: Finding/identifying verbs in math text

result.description: Fires on "understand", "understanding", "-izing" (recognizing) and sometimes "of" or "into" in academic text about gaining understanding of a topic. It is silent on some "understand" tokens, and the cause is unclear.
result.label: understand/understanding in research prose

result.description: Fires on the mid-word pieces 'ced' in "antecedent" and 'val' in "prevalence", the point where the word is one piece from completing with an -ent/-ence ending. Weak activations elsewhere.
result.label: ante-ced / pre-val word pieces
'sh' in 'harsh' conditions
result.description: Fires on the piece 'sh' completing "harsh" (har|sh), mostly in "harsh conditions/environments" for vessels, spacecraft or organisms. Members are 'sh' detectors plus extreme-conditions context words. Silent on unrelated text.

Fires on scattered function words (in, the, and, or, can, our) mid-sentence in abstract expository prose, where a noun phrase or clause continues. Silent on ' in' before relative "which". Evidence is mixed and the peak consistency is low.
result.label: Scattered function words in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on function words (the, as, and, include, 's) right before a name of a theory or model is expected, in academic text listing theories or models. Silent on 'the' before ordinary nouns like 'role' or 'nature'.
result.label: Function word before named theory/model

result.description: Fires on varied mid-word pieces and function words (e.g. 'en' in Phoenician, 'ine' in feminine, ' while', ' the') in academic text about communication and language; it boosts ' communication'. Mixed peaks; the circuit is diffuse and weak.
result.label: Diffuse word pieces, communication-text

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a phrase about primary/secondary colors (' colors', 'shades', 'hues') in color-mixing and color-theory text. It stays silent on ' colors' in general descriptive uses, so it needs the primary-color mixing context.
result.label: Primary colors in color-mixing text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' evol' (start of evolve/evolved/evolving), usually after a plural or subject noun like "languages" or "populations". Members are mostly ' evol' detectors that predict the suffix -ve/-ved/-ving.
result.label: ' evol' word-start before -ve/-ved

result.description: Fires on the word " liberal" (or "Liberal"), mostly in political-philosophy text where it begins words like liberalism or liberal nationalism. Members detect liberal and other "-ism" ideology word pieces (libertarian, formalism, neoliberal).
result.label: ' liberal' in ideology text

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns and linking words (that, they, which, would, to) right after a plural noun in geometry/linear-algebra text about lines, angles and vectors, where a verb about their properties follows. Silent on 'that' in other topics.
result.label: Relative 'that' after geometry nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (and, to, in, makes, -less, -ous) in abstract business, design or management prose. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same ' and' is silent in plain lists of nouns. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in business prose

result.description: Fires on ' least' in "at least", mostly before a quantity (at least one/three). Upstream members detect ' least' and similar quantity qualifiers (about, approximately, exactly, only). The contrast text lacks this phrase.
result.label: "at least" quantity qualifier

result.description: Fires most on 'itation' in "[citation needed]" markers, and more weakly on scattered tokens such as list commas, ' and' and ' h' in clothing lists (hoodies, T-shirts). Mixed peaks; no single clear trigger or condition.
result.label: Citation-needed marker, mixed weak peaks

result.description: Fires on function words like "the", "this", "its" and some content words in flowery text about music and sound, where the next word is likely music-related. Silent on "the" in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Music-topic determiners before noun

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens ('AP' in CAPM, ' the', ' higher', 'ing') in science/finance explanatory text, often predicting a technical noun next. Silent on 'AP' in other CAPM mentions, so evidence is mixed and the trigger is unclear.
result.label: Mixed tokens in technical explanations

result.description: Fires on the 'colog' piece in words like "ecological" and "ecologists" (after "e"). It is silent on some 'colog' contexts in the contrast, so the condition is unclear. Members are mostly 'colog' detectors.
result.label: 'colog' piece in ecological

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (and, of, a, the, commas) inside abstract organizational, educational or communication-themed text, plus the 'oz' piece in 'Mesozoic'. Peaks are scattered, with no single dominant token or clear next-token prediction.
result.label: Function words in organizational text; Mesozoic oz

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (' to', ' that', ' they', ' which', ' should', ' also') inside formal expository text, mostly linking to a following verb or clause. Silent on many ' to' contexts, and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the token ' stage' in the theater/performance sense (stage design, stage floor, stage fear), especially as a modifier before another noun. Members are mostly ' stage' token detectors; weak firing on ' frame' and a non-theater 'stage'.
result.label: ' stage' in performance contexts

result.description: Fires on "Another"/"another"/"One"/"one" when introducing an additional item or point in an enumeration, often at the start of a sentence ("Another important factor…"). Predicts evaluative adjectives or nouns like notable, key, important.
result.label: Another/one introducing additional point

result.description: Fires on the preposition "Among"/"among" (including the "Am|ong" split and "Amongst"), most strongly at the start of a sentence or clause before "the/these/other". Pushes towards "st" and "others"-type continuations.
result.label: Among / amongst preposition

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' So' at document start, 'C' in an acronym, ' as' in 'such as', ' with' after 'along') that start or continue a term or title, often in heading or list-like text. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Scattered title and word-start tokens

result.description: Fires on ' an' right after a verb of providing/offering (provides an, providing an, offers artists an, with an), predicting a positive noun like opportunity or unparalleled. Stays quiet on ' an' after other words such as 'form an' or 'with an interest'.
result.label: ' an' after provide/offer verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' a', ',', ' or', ' the', ' of') inside lists or enumerations of components in expository text. Peaks are inconsistent and the logits are unclear, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in component lists

result.description: Fires on ' make' when it is the first piece of the word "makeup", mostly in "genetic makeup", and predicts the suffix "up". It stays silent on ' make' as an ordinary verb, as in "must make wise".
result.label: 'make' in "genetic makeup"
'the' after philosophy-verb
result.description: Fires on ' the' right after a verb or preposition describing what a philosophy field examines or is concerned with (explores the, delves into the, examines the), in ontology/metaphysics text. It predicts abstract nouns like 'nature'. Silent on 'the' after 'with' or 'into' in other uses.

Fires on " the" after "and", "to", or "in" in lists of historical or political events, where the next word is an event noun like establishment, rise or development. It stays quiet on " the" after a bare comma or in other positions.
result.label: "the" before event nouns in history

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "conservation" (conservation of energy/momentum), and weakly on conser-ves/ving word pieces. Silent on ' of' after other nouns like understanding, whirl, source, types.
result.label: "of" after conservation

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (mostly ' to', also ' report', ' also', -ing pieces) in text about employees reporting misconduct and workplace ethics. It stays silent on ' to' in data/analysis contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Employee misconduct reporting, 'to'

result.description: Fires mainly on the verb "resolve" (and -ving forms like "solving") as the verb after "should/to", where a conflict, error or problem is the expected object. Silent on "resolve" as a noun-like modifier ("conflict resolve resolution").
result.label: Verb "resolve" before conflicts/problems

result.description: Fires on the token "linear", almost always the piece after "Non" in "Nonlinear Dynamics/Systems/Regression" titles. Also fires on "linear" elsewhere, e.g. "non-linear" and "linear transformations". Members are mostly "linear" detectors.
result.label: "linear" after "Non"

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (how, determine, explaining, predict, understanding) in solid-state physics text about electronic band theory, where the next word is likely band-related (band, insulator, periodic). Silent on 'how' in general non-physics text.
result.label: Band theory explanatory words

result.description: Fires on ' an' (also ' the', ' a') introducing the next item in a list of electrochemical cell components (electrodes, an electrolyte), in electrochemistry text. Silent on ' an' in other, non-electrochemical contexts.
result.label: Article in electrochemical component lists

result.description: Fires on words that introduce a list of methods or techniques (using, including, use of, implementing, "such as", commas) in technical text about data integrity, backup and recovery, where examples of mechanisms are about to follow. Silent on plain "using" elsewhere.
result.label: Introducing technique lists in data-integrity text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' of', 'uid', 'onic', 'ic') in physics/science title or concept phrases, where the next word is likely a science-field noun like Theory, Science or Process. Silent on many ' of' in ordinary prose.
result.label: Science-topic phrase continuation, physics terms

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'icians' completing 'mathemat-icians', typically in lists of professions (mathematicians and logicians, physicists and mathematicians). Weakly fires on other agent-noun endings like '-ers'.
result.label: mathematicians 'icians' suffix

result.description: Fires mostly on the prefix ' de' (as in decolonization, degradation, depletion) in academic expository text, plus occasional other tokens like ' common' and ' Bar'. Silent on some other ' de' words, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' de' prefix in academic text

result.description: Fires mostly on the letter piece 'h' when it is the start of a word continuation like "ydr-" (dehydrogenase, carbohydrate), predicting 'yd'/'ydro'. It also fires weakly on a few function words like ' or' and ' be'.
result.label: 'h' before 'ydr' (dehydrogenase)

result.description: Fires on list or elaboration connectors (" including", commas, " as", semicolons) in art-related text, where a list of artists or art forms follows. It predicts artist names or art words. It stays silent on " including" in non-art topics.
result.label: List connectors in art text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' of', ' an', ' two', ' as', ' most') in expository science text, especially after "made up mostly/solely of" or in component lists. Silent on 'of' in "part of" or "version of". Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in composition phrases

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' d' in food and cooking text, after "the/a/your", where the next piece is likely "ish", "ining" or "ough" (dish, dining, dough). It is quieter in some other uses, such as "side d".
result.label: ' d' starting dish/dining in cooking

result.description: Fires on a hyphen inside long multi-hyphen compounds, typically after a function word like "for", "to", "of", "about" mid-phrase (state-of-the-art, what's-in-it-for-you). Stays silent on hyphens after a single word prefix or modifier (user-generated, mid-20th).
result.label: Hyphen in multi-word hyphenated phrases

result.description: Fires on the article ' a'/' an' (also ' essential') after a copula or "become/serve as" when a text describes a rhetorical or literary device, like understatement or hyperbole. It predicts a noun such as "device" or "technique" next.
result.label: Article before device noun in rhetoric

result.description: Fires on economic terms (economy, income, employment, growth, profits) in passages about business cycles and economic growth. Peaks are mixed across words, and the contrast is tech/urban-planning text, so it looks topic-bound.
result.label: Economics and growth vocabulary

result.description: Fires on the infinitive marker ' to' in "in order to" (also purpose 'to' after a clause), where an adverb or verb like achieve, ensure, effectively comes next. Silent on 'to' as a preposition or after nouns/adjectives.
result.label: purpose 'to' in "in order to"

result.description: Fires on ' surface' (and 'face') plus nearby function words in science text about particles, molecules and surface area, but is silent on some ' surface' tokens in similar text. The circuit is diffuse and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: surface in particle/molecule science text

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "to" or "for" in a list of verbs or after "tools/easier/ways", where the next word is another bare action verb or gerund (collect, integrate, analyze; manage, understand). Silent on commas before "but" or "which".
result.label: Slot before next action verb

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on varied function words and punctuation (' and', ' that', ',', ' by', ';') in expository science and humanities prose. Contrast shows silence on ' and' in other contexts, but the condition is not clear from the evidence.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires mostly on ' of' (also ' social', commas) in essays about communication and interpersonal expression, e.g. "blend of voice, language". Silent on many other ' of' tokens in similar text, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: ' of' in communication-skills text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' w' (before 'elfare', 'onders', 'age') when it follows a preceding modifier noun or adjective like 'social', 'public', 'literary', 'a'. Silent on ' w' after 'and', 'is' or 'in'.

result.label: ' an' in coordinated skill lists

result.description: Fires mostly on ' that' (also 'the', ')', 'individuals') right after a noun phrase about an innate or biological structure in the brain, introducing a relative clause. Silent on ' that' after other nouns like 'property' or 'parameters'.
result.label: 'that' after innate brain structure

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (commas in lists of abstract properties, ' of', ' influ', 'ously') in abstract academic text about properties or concepts. Evidence is scattered, with low consistency and weak, mixed members, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered abstract-text commas and 'of'

result.description: Fires on ' with' (sometimes ' to'/' by') right after compliance/comply/adhere verbs or nouns, where a regulation, law or standard is expected next. Silent on other uses of 'with' such as 'combined with' or 'begins with'.
result.label: 'with' after comply/compliance

result.description: Fires on the word piece "dri" in hyphenated "-driven" compounds (character-driven, data-driven, action-driven), just before "ven". Members are mostly "dri" detectors and "ven"-predicting pieces.
result.label: "dri" in "-driven" compounds

result.description: Fires on words describing the unbroken, unfiltered flow of thought (unfilter-ed, uninterrupted, spontaneous, the continuous) in text about stream-of-consciousness writing. Silent on 'ed' in unrelated words like conveyed or layered.
result.label: Stream-of-consciousness descriptors

result.description: Fires on the word "space" / "Space" in outer-space contexts (spacecraft, space race, Space Station), predicting compounds like craft, flight, program. Silent on "White Space" in design text.
result.label: outer-space "Space" token

result.description: Fires mostly on the word-initial piece ' l' (lenders, lending, lens, lymph, labeled) before the rest of the word, with some commas in lists. Silent on ' l' in one 'their lending' context, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Word-initial ' l' fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'unn' in "t[unn]eling" (quantum tunneling, tunnelling), and more weakly in "funnels" or "forerunners". It predicts continuations like 'eling', 'els', 'elling'.
result.label: 'unn' piece in tunneling

result.description: Fires mostly on ' ens' (start of "ensuring"/"ensures") after a comma in technical text about systems, and on scattered function words like ' and', ' an', ' will'. Silent on one ' ens' in a structures context. Mixed evidence.
result.label: ' ens' of ensuring, technical text

result.description: Fires on rephrasing or summarizing adverbs and phrases such as "to put it simply", "essentially", "in essence", "really", "basically", introducing a simplified restatement. Silent on "simply" meaning "merely" inside a comparison.
result.label: Essentially / simply restatement markers

result.description: Fires on prepositions and connectives (of, for, to, through, and) following abstract nouns in text about literary awards, publishing and recognition. Members are publishing/awards-topic detectors. Peaks are inconsistent and the same tokens often stay silent.
result.label: Prepositions in literary awards/publishing text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ad' (also ' Ad') when it begins a longer word such as adverse, adhesives, adoption, adjectives or adverbs. It pushes towards continuations like 'verse', 'option', 'her' and 'hes'.
result.label: ' ad' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on " were" after a plural subject noun about ancient artifacts, buildings or practices (tombs, ziggurats, designs), predicting a passive or descriptive predicate like "used", "intended", "constructed". Silent when " were" follows "only" or starts a text, or follows a relative clause.
result.label: "were" after ancient-topic plural subject

result.description: Fires on the word " grand" (also "elaborate") as an adjective after "the", ahead of nouns like spectacle, scheme or "-iose". Members are mostly detectors of " grand" at earlier layers. Predicts scheme/finale/io.
result.label: ' grand' adjective detector

result.description: Fires on plural person/group nouns (participants, attendees, -ers, -es endings) in subject position, right before a plural verb like "will", "should", "tend". It is silent when the noun ends a clause as an object.
result.label: Plural group noun as subject

result.description: Fires on the piece 'out' in 'Throughout', especially at the start of a document or sentence ("Throughout history/the years"). It is supported by detectors of 'out' and 'throughout' plus history-themed members.
result.label: 'Throughout' sentence opener

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in technical or scientific expository text, such as 'ation', 'linear', commas, and mid-word pieces. It is silent on 'ation' in some words like motivation and elaboration. The evidence is mixed and the logits are unclear.
result.label: Scattered technical-text word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (of, in, to, their, a, extremely) in expository text about biodiversity, species and regions, mid-phrase before a noun. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Scattered function words in biodiversity text

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after a verb like expressed, encapsulated, embodied or internalized, in art, music and style-history text. It predicts era or genre words such as period, genre, Empire. It stays silent on ' the' after prepositions like with or throughout.
result.label: 'the' after expressive verb, art history

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tur' when it starts a word like turbine or turbulent, mostly after "wind" or "water". It pushes the next token toward 'bine', 'b' and 'bul'.
result.label: ' tur' piece before -bine/-bulent

result.description: Fires on function words (to, and, that, where, a, more, involves) in diversity/inclusion and organizational-culture text, where the next word is likely "inclusive"/"inclusion". Predicts inclus-/welcome-type tokens.
result.label: Predicts "inclusive" in diversity text

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' right after the preposition 'on' (on a leaf, on a large scale, on a Saturday). It stays silent on ' a' after other words like within, like, found. Logits favour nouns like 'daily', 'Monday', 'grand'.
result.label: ' a' after 'on'

result.description: Fires on connectors (commas, "and", "also", "by", "thus", "thereby") right after a clause whose verb is "enhance", where the next word is likely "improve"-type verbs ("improve", "contribute"). It stays silent on commas in other contexts.
result.label: Connector after "enhance" clause

result.description: Fires on the word " clean" (also " cleaner"), especially as an adjective before energy, air or burning in environmental or energy text. It predicts continuations like air, energy, burning, and the suffix -er.
result.label: ' clean' word detector

result.description: Fires at the end of a title's main phrase, mostly on ' A'/' An' right after a colon in "Topic: A Guide/Introduction" style titles. Silent on ' A' beginning a name like Albert Aftalion. Predicts subtitle words like Guide or Introduction.
result.label: Title subtitle start after colon

result.description: Fires on connective words (mostly " through", also " in", " and", " includes") in advice-style text about language preservation and community projects, where the next word is likely a means or programs such as "volunteer", "local" or "projects". Silent on "through" in other contexts.
result.label: Means-connectives in language revitalization text

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "continue/continued/continues", where an infinitive verb follows. Silent on other uses of ' to' (extended to, leads to, connection to). Pushes toward verbs like evolve, push, innovate, advance.
result.label: 'to' after continue

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: commas, digits, word-start fragments like 'far', 'cl', 'cont', and function words, mostly in academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse with no discriminative members, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mixed tokens in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the end of "value" in technical or mathematical terms (p-value, key–value, eigenvalue) and on "modulo" (-ulo), plus "index". Predicts next tokens like "pairs" or "stores". It fires in math and data contexts.
result.label: value / modulo in math terms

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, with, -ors) inside text explaining English grammar, such as verbs, subjects and predicates, where a grammar term is likely to come next. It stays silent on the same words in other text.
result.label: Function words in grammar explanations

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' tr' (as in trend, trumpet, trillions, Truth), when a longer word is split after it. Members are mostly ' tr'/' Tr' detectors. Output pushes toward continuations like 'ends', 'ump', 'icks'.
result.label: ' tr' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the token ' CPU' in computer-architecture text, including 'CPUs' and mentions in metrics or component lists. It pushes toward hardware continuations like cycle, cores and registers. Members detect CPU, processor, cache and parallel processing.
result.label: CPU token in hardware text

result.description: Fires on positive quality adjectives or adjective pieces (accurate, robust, careful, proficient, effective, successful) at the start of a noun phrase, before a noun like "understanding" or "approach". Silent on 'ful' inside skillful.
result.label: Positive quality adjective before noun

result.description: Fires on modal/verb slots (' can', ' could be', ' which can') in a relative clause after a noun like "data" or "insights" that can be analyzed or used. Quiet when the subject is a person or company (e.g. "companies can").
result.label: Relative-clause "that can" after data nouns

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' of') right after "concept/principle/idea" in texts about the Teleological Argument and design. It predicts "Tele"/"tele" next. It stays silent on ' of' in other philosophy contexts.
result.label: Function word before "teleological" in philosophy

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Ind' (also ' ind') when it begins a longer word, mostly "Indigenous". Predicts continuations like 'igen', 'ividual', 'oor'. Members are detectors of Ind/ind pieces.
result.label: ' Ind' prefix, Indigenous

result.description: Fires on " the" right after a sentence-opening concessive conjunction ("While the", "Although the") at the start of a clause. It stays silent on "the" after other words like "is" or "for". Predicts a subject noun such as "rest" or "majority".
result.label: "the" after While/Although opener

result.description: Fires on the piece 'oe' inside the word "onomatopoeia" (also similar mid-word pieces like thermoelectric), right before the closing 'ia'. Members are mostly 'oe' detectors.
result.label: 'oe' in onomatopoeia

result.description: Fires on the last piece of a method or technical-process noun in statistics/science text (hypothesis testing, Significance Testing, methodologies, renormalization), where the next word is likely 'within', 'in' or 'lies'. Silent on ordinary '-ing' words.
result.label: Statistical method noun ending (testing)

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ing' of a gerund that is the title or heading at the start of a document (e.g. "Drawing", "Sculpting", "Throwing"). It stays silent on 'ing' in mid-sentence running text, such as "cross-hatching" or "mastering".
result.label: Heading-initial gerund 'ing' suffix

result.description: Fires on the word " behavior" (or "behaviour"), mostly as a noun after "the" or a modifier like "material" or "electrical", often in scientific text. It predicts suffixes like "al" and words like "patterns" or "under".
result.label: ' behavior' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word-initial prefix ' un' (as in unparalleled, unprecedented, unification, unwavering) when it begins a longer word. The members are all ' un' detectors, and the target pushes toward continuations like 'ending'.
result.label: Word-initial ' un' prefix

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, their, to, and, as, commas) mid-sentence in expository text about writing, music, or language, where a noun like "process" or "complex" is expected next. It is silent on many ' the' tokens, and the evidence doesn't say why.
result.label: Function words in expository arts/language text

result.description: Fires on verbs meaning "help/enable/allow" (help, helping, allows, enable) when a subject like "it", "which" or a process noun is followed by a benefit clause, in organizational or business text. Predicts organizations/companies next.
result.label: help/enable/allow causative verbs

result.description: Fires on importance adjectives (crucial, essential, critical, vital) after a plural subject plus "are", as in "strategies are crucial in...". It is weaker or silent after "it is/making it essential". Members detect similar adjectives like indispensable.
result.label: Crucial/essential predicate after plural subject

result.description: Fires on the document-start/boundary token (¶) that follows a sentence or short heading ending in a period, where a new document or section begins. It is silent on some boundaries after technical or business headings. The logits are mixed.
result.label: Document boundary after humanities text

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'ct' piece inside "punctual"/"punctuation" (pun-ct-), in text about punctuation rules. It also fires weakly on other mid-word 'ct' pieces and a few scattered words such as 'reduced'. It stays silent on ordinary text.
result.label: 'ct' in pun-ct-uation

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (and, the, that, -ing, -ys) in abstract philosophy/academic essay text, mid-sentence. Peak tokens are varied and consistency is low. Members mostly carry a philosophy topic; the same tokens in other contexts stay silent.
result.label: Function words in philosophy prose

result.description: Fires mostly inside word pieces like "intr-usion" and "fore-sh(adowing)" after "role/artistry of" style topic phrases, and weakly on "of/to" before a noun or gerund. It seems to predict a word continuation such as "detection" or "adows".
result.label: Intrusion/foreshadowing word-piece continuation

result.description: Fires on commas and "and"/"or" inside a list of coordinated transitive verbs (e.g. "monitor, evaluate, and improve"), where another verb comes next. Silent on "and" joining clauses or noun lists.
result.label: Separators in verb lists

result.description: Fires on the second noun (or word-ending piece) of a "between X and Y" or "X and Y" pair, completing the second item of an abstract two-way relationship. The contrast has "audiences" outside such a pair.
result.label: Second item in "between X and Y"
'ci' piece in de-ci-bel/decipher
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ci' inside a longer word, mainly 'de|ci|bel' and 'de|ci|pher', also 'bios'. It predicts continuations like 'pher', 'bel', 'phere'. Silent when 'ci' follows a period at a sentence start.
Fires on the piece 'red' inside the word "ingredients" (after "ing"), in cooking and culinary text. It is silent on 'red' in "stirred" or a word-initial "red". It pushes toward completing "ients".
result.label: 'red' inside "ingredients"

result.description: Fires on a noun (mostly ' weapons', also problem, someone, game, compiler, processor) in technical or computing-flavored text, where a compound like "-ware" or "chip" could come next. Members are generic and weak; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Weapons/technical noun, mixed

result.description: Fires on the verb "show" and its forms (show, shows, showing), including as a verb before "case" or "off". It predicts objects such as off, case, respect or affection. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: verb "show" forms

result.description: Fires on 'when' (also 'if') opening a subordinate clause, especially sentence-initial or after 'for instance' or 'particularly', where a gerund like 'considering' or a subject like 'we' or 'you' follows. Silent on 'when' in some mid-sentence uses.
result.label: Clause-opening 'when' / 'if'

result.description: Fires on word endings or adjectives like "innovative", "upscale", "vegetarian", "elegant" that describe food or dining in restaurant and menu text. It is silent on "ative" in unrelated words like "transformative" and "comparative". It predicts nouns such as offer, approaches and menu.
result.label: Culinary descriptive adjective endings

result.description: Fires on list-introducing words (" as", " including", " like", " from", "include") in energy and nuclear technology text, where a list of examples follows. Predicts names of reactor types or technologies. It stays silent on "such as" in other application contexts.
result.label: Example-list introducer in energy/nuclear text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' pun' (pun, puns, punter, punctuation, punishment) as the first token of such words. Members are mostly earlier ' pun' token detectors. Logits favour continuations like 'ctu', 'ishment', 'ting'.
result.label: ' pun' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' that' introducing a result clause after "such a way"/"ways"/"so" (e.g. "in such a way that", "so large that"), mainly in quantum entanglement text. Silent on relative-clause 'that' after plain nouns like "particles that".
result.label: Result-clause 'that' after "way"

result.description: Fires on determiners/adjectives (' a', ' the', ' deep') right after "carry/hold/bear" verbs, where a abstract load like weight, message or meaning comes next. Silent on 'the' after other verbs or prepositions.
result.label: Determiner after carry/hold verbs

result.description: Fires on varied words (together, success, work, failures, complex) in academic expository text, often after "both... and" or "their/of" phrases. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is diffuse; logits hint at a following contrast like "but" or "yet".
result.label: Scattered academic-prose word before contrast

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Cir' at the start of a line in a list of math topic headings ("Circles and ..."), predicting word-continuation suffixes. Weaker, scattered peaks on other tokens such as 'ed', ' Dur' and ' include'. Mixed evidence.
result.label: ' Cir' in curriculum topic lists

result.description: Fires on the piece 've' inside 'con-ve-' words, mainly 'conveying/conveys/conveye', and predicts the continuation 'ys'/'ying'. It stays silent on 've' in 'conducive'.
result.label: 've' in 'conveying'

result.description: Fires on the word " golden" (as in "golden rule", "golden standard", "golden dough"), peaking on all 64 examples. It fires more weakly on "Golden Age". It predicts follow-ups like age, ticket, hour, ratio, rule.
result.label: golden token detector

result.description: Fires on the word "statistical" (and the pieces "Statist"/"ical" completing "Statistical"), mostly when it modifies a following noun like methods, analysis or mechanics. It predicts words such as methods, analysis and inference.
result.label: Word "statistical" before method nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on " cannot" after an abstract subject noun (e.g. "energy cannot", "significance cannot"), where "be" is expected next. It also fires weakly on scattered mid-phrase tokens like " and", " in" and "ent".
result.label: " cannot" after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on ' the' after a verb like examining, studies, probes, or comprehend in academic descriptions of geography or spatial fields. It predicts nouns such as spatial, dynamics, relationships and distribution. It stays quiet on 'the' after 'on' or 'influence'.
result.label: 'the' after study verbs in geography

result.description: Fires mainly on the word-start piece " eleg" (elegance), and on other word-start fragments that precede an "-ance/-antly" ending (relev-, rom-, Rel-). Also fires weakly on scattered tokens like "^" in math. The peaks are mixed and the circuit is a poor fit.
result.label: " eleg" and similar word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on verbs like "require", "need", "necessitate" (also "for", "demand") after a subject such as "areas" or "issues" that calls for action. It predicts improvement-type nouns next, like attention, upgrade or modification.
result.label: require/need verbs predicting improvement

result.description: Fires on " necessary" as a modifier in "provide/equip X with the necessary [skills/tools/information]", before a noun naming resources. Silent on predicative "is necessary". Predicts resource nouns like tools, funds, infrastructure.
result.label: "the necessary" before resource nouns

result.description: Fires on plural agent/profession nouns (writers, artists, chemists, organizations) as sentence subjects, where a modal or verb like "can", "should", "must" comes next. Silent on -ers inside other words (fosters, immersive).
result.label: Plural profession nouns as subjects

result.description: Fires on " and" (also "or", ";", "whereas") right after "acids" in acid/base chemistry text, predicting " bases". Weaker on other chemistry pairs like reactants and products. Silent on "and" in other chemistry contexts.
result.label: "acids and" → bases

result.description: Fires on contrastive connectors (while, whereas, commas, semicolons, "and", "inversely,") that open the second half of a comparison between two items or approaches, predicting "whereas/while/On". Silent on "while" meaning simultaneous or "while also/maintaining".
result.label: Contrastive 'while/whereas' between two contrasted items

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' object' (also ' posit') when it is a stem likely to continue as 'ivity', 'ively', 'ives' or 'ification'. It predicts those suffixes next. Members are mostly ' object' detectors.
result.label: ' object' stem before -ive/-ivity

result.description: Fires on the word " useful" (also "ful" in related forms), often before "ness" or "for/in/tool". Upstream members are mostly " useful" detectors, with some "valuable" detectors. Predicts "ness" next.
result.label: " useful" token detector
' processes' after cognitive
result.description: Fires on the plural noun ' processes' after a modifier like "cognitive" or "biological", in academic text about mental or biological systems. It predicts continuations like "behind", "underlying", "involved". Weakly fires on similar plural nouns such as functions or connections.
Fires on the word-start piece ' intu' (as in intuitionism/intuitionist), mostly in mathematical logic text. Members are mostly ' intu' detectors across layers that favor continuations like 'ition'.
result.label: ' intu' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on conjunctions (' and', ',', ' or', ' that') right after the noun "action"/"actions" in coordinated lists, anticipating another abstract noun to follow. Stays silent on the same conjunctions after other list items (e.g., literary-element lists).
result.label: Conjunction after "action" noun

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after a scientist's surname (Ampère's, Gauss's, Snell's, Fermat's) in physics/math text, predicting a following 'Law', 'Theorem' or 'Equations'. Silent on 's after common nouns like theory or gravity.
result.label: Eponym possessive 's before Law

result.description: Fires on the word piece "uct" inside "fluctuations" (fl-uct-uations), mainly in physics or cosmology text. It predicts the continuation "u" (as in "uations"). It is silent on the contrast passage, which has no "fluctuations".
result.label: "uct" in "fluctuations"

result.description: Fires on the end of the subject noun phrase in a "when X ..." clause (e.g. "when light reflects off a surface", "when the casing"), where a verb like "fails", "hits" or "decide" is expected next. Peak tokens vary.
result.label: Subject of "when" clause, verb next

result.description: Fires on the word piece "stal" in "cry|stal" (crystal), mostly in materials science and solid-state physics text. It predicts continuations like "log" (crystallography) and words such as structures, lattice and growth.
result.label: "stal" in crystal

result.description: Fires on "secure" and "security" (also weakly "protection") in computing and cybersecurity text, typically right before a noun like measures, channel, or session. Members include detectors of secure, security and safe.
result.label: secure/security in cybersecurity text

result.description: Fires on function words and modifiers (the, in, to, much, significantly) in expository text about urban heat islands and cities. Contrast shows the same ' the' silent in other topics, so the evidence is mixed. Members include urban/city detectors.
result.label: Function words in urban-heat text

result.description: Fires on the plural agent-noun ending (-ers, -cers, -ists, customers) completing a person/group noun inside a list of stakeholders or professions (artists, producers, researchers, retailers). Silent on 'ers' in verbs or other words.
result.label: Plural stakeholder nouns in lists

result.description: Fires on the token ' night' (including 'nights', 'nightly', 'nighttime'), often after words like 'at', 'on', or 'club'. It predicts compound continuations such as 'club', 'mar' and 'fall'. Members are mostly night/time-of-day detectors.
result.label: ' night' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on the adjective " smooth" (mathematical smooth functions and smooth operation), with a few weaker hits on other modifiers like slow or various. Predicts adverb or superlative suffixes such as "ly" and "est".
result.label: "smooth" adjective detector

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in academic or technical text, mostly the 'ation' suffix (e.g. market pen-etr-ation), also ' of', commas and 'between'. Silent on 'ation' in other words like manifestation. Predicts analytic/critical-type words weakly. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered academic-text suffix and function tokens

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece "de"/" De" (case variants) at the start of a word split into pieces, such as deified, Deuterium, Deception, depletion, Depression. It predicts word-continuation pieces like "comm", "grad", "vis".
result.label: word-initial "de" piece

result.description: Fires on the word " number", mostly in "the number of ..." in mathematical or technical text. It is silent on "composite number" followed by "into", where "number" is a noun being described.
result.label: "number" in "the number of"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' the', ' a', 'és', ' painting', ' sounds') mid-phrase in academic expository text on linguistics, education, or social science, where a noun phrase is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and it is silent on many ' the' tokens.
result.label: Academic prose mid-phrase function words
' abs' word-piece before 'urd'/'orb'
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' abs' at the start of a split word, mostly in 'absurd/absurdity', and pushes towards continuations like 'urd' and 'orb'. Members are mainly ' abs' detectors plus other word-start fragments.

Fires on the word-piece ' Th' in "Law of Th(ermodynamics)", where it is the start of a split word after "of". It is silent on ' Th' at the start of a document or after other word pieces. It pushes towards 'erm'.
result.label: ' Th' before 'ermodynamics' after "Law of"

result.description: Fires on a comma right after a short noun phrase naming a topic or subject of study (e.g. "The study of polymers,"), where an elaboration follows such as "including", "such as" or "which". It is quiet on commas after longer clauses.
result.label: Comma after topic noun phrase

result.description: Fires on "seen" (also "witnessed", "saw") when a period, era or field is the subject of "has seen / saw / witnessed" and a significant change or improvement is expected next. Silent on "has been made" constructions.
result.label: Era "has seen" significant change

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Ro' right after "The" in a title like "The Role of X in History", where the next piece is expected to be "le". Silent when ' Ro' starts the text without "The" before it.
result.label: ' Ro' in "The Role of" titles

result.description: Fires on the word piece "sur" inside "subsurface" (mostly in geology and exploration text), predicting "face" next. Members detect "sur" and similar prefixes before "face", "vey" or "prise".
result.label: "sur" in subsurface, before "face"

result.description: Fires on "committee" (and the "itte" piece of "committee") in corporate governance text about boards and board committees such as Audit. Upstream members detect Board, directors and committee words. It predicts committee-related continuations. Silent on general board text without committee.
result.label: board committee word in governance text

result.description: Fires on possessive markers ('s, S, his) after a person's name, especially a historical figure like Henry, in biography text. It predicts a kinship or life-event noun next (death, mother, wife, brother). It stays silent after 's on inanimate nouns (war's, country's).
result.label: Possessive 's/his after a person

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ation' completing "pronunciation" in language-learning and phonetics text. It stays silent on 'ation' in other words like incorporation, hyphenation, preparation and punctuation. Predicts nouns like patterns, variations, problems.
result.label: 'ation' in pronunciation

result.description: Fires on the end of a physical or scientific noun (medium, molecule, particles, materials, units) that is the subject of a following predicate. Logits favor words like "involved", "itself", "relative". Silent on bare "ions" as a standalone noun.
result.label: Science noun awaiting participle

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' from', also ' as', ',', ' or', ' a') in list or range constructions, where a source, scope or category is about to be named ("from small farms to...", "in industry, medicine, and..."). Silent on some 'from' in transition contexts.
result.label: Range/scope function words, 'from'

result.description: Fires mainly on the piece "ven" in "uneven" (uneven distribution, unevenly, uneven settlement). It also fires weakly on a few function words like "like" and "of". Members are mostly "ven" detectors.
result.label: "ven" in "uneven"

result.description: Fires on verbs of reducing or lessening (reduce, reducing, mitigating, minimize, decrease), mostly in environmental or green-chemistry text. It predicts a harm-type object next, such as waste, environmental effects or exposure.
result.label: Reduce/mitigate verbs in environmental text

result.description: Fires on prepositions like " of", " from", " using" in linguistics/semantics text about word meaning and scales (e.g. semantic differential), where a technical term is expected next. Silent on " of" in general history or other prose.
result.label: Prepositions in linguistics/semantics writing

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' equ' (start of equitable, equity, equipped, equities), predicting continuations like 'itable', 'ipped', 'ity'. Members are mostly earlier-layer ' equ' detectors.
result.label: ' equ' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ep' (or ' Ep') when it begins a longer word such as epidemic, epistemic or epic, and predicts continuations like 'ist', 'ide' and 'igen'. It stayed silent on one 'Social ep|istemology' example.
result.label: ' ep' word-start piece (epidemic, epic)

result.description: Fires on the end of a noun that is the object of "affect/impact/influence" in travel and tourism text, such as "preferences", "destination selection", "choice" and "decision". It is silent on plain "-es" endings elsewhere. Predicts "regarding/about/on".
result.label: Tourist preference/choice noun after impact

result.description: Fires on the auxiliary ' had' after a subject noun or relative pronoun, where a past-perfect verb is expected. It pushes towards adverbs like previously, already and originally. Members are mostly ' had'/' have' detectors.
result.label: ' had' past-perfect auxiliary

result.description: Fires on the object noun (process, processes, workflow, operations) right after a verb like streamline/simplify/automate, i.e. the thing being made more efficient. Silent on 'process' as a plain noun elsewhere.
result.label: Object of streamlining: process/workflow

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' by', ' come', ' was') and word pieces in expository text about history, politics and social topics. Peaks are inconsistent. Members include military and diplomatic detectors. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Scattered function words in historical/political prose

result.description: Fires on function words (as, much, and, the, only) in text about the English language, silent letters and linguistics, where the next word is likely a language-related noun like "English". Fires inconsistently, and the circuit shows mostly linguistic topic context.
result.label: Function words in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on " of" after abstract nouns like "implications", "understanding", "investigation", "quantification" in academic or scientific prose. It is silent on some identical phrases, so the contrast doesn't show what separates them.
result.label: "of" after abstract academic nouns

result.description: Fires on the noun completing the object of "transcends/goes beyond mere X" (pleasure, perception, enjoyment, experience), in essays about art, music or aesthetics. Members detect "more than just / beyond mere" frames.
result.label: Noun after "beyond mere"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " ens" when it begins "ensures/ensuring" after a subject noun phrase or clause, predicting the completion "ures/uring". The contrast text has no such verb position.
result.label: " ens" start of "ensures"

result.description: Fires on plural-variety words like "various", "different", "diverse", "other" right after "from" (or "across") when borrowing or origins are described, e.g. words from various tongues. It predicts source or background nouns. Silent after "development of".
result.label: "from various/different" sources

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs in software-engineering text (code review, maintainability) where the next word is likely a software quality term like bugs, readable, debugging or refactor. Peaks on ' maintain', ' overall', ' ensure', ' that', 'of'.
result.label: Software quality prediction slot
Word-piece 'gen' mid-word
result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'gen' inside longer words (emergencies, sub-genres, hydrogen, transgenic), and occasionally on ' analog' before a suffix. Members are mostly 'gen' detectors; it predicts word-continuation suffixes like 'ces', 'res', 'heim'.

Fires on auxiliary " have"/" has" after a plural or abstract subject noun (art forms, music genres, technology), in present-perfect statements about cultural or historical topics. It predicts continuations like "been", "become", "always", "continu-".
result.label: Present-perfect have/has after subject noun

result.description: Fires mostly on ' black' before 'hole' in physics/cosmology text (black hole thermodynamics, entropy, radiation), with occasional other tokens. It stays silent on ' black' at the start of a text or in a plain list of objects.
result.label: 'black' in black hole physics

result.description: Fires on single digits (2, 3, 4, 5) inside long runs of numbers, lists, times, fractions or decimals, where more digits or separators follow. Silent on digits inside years like 1905 or 1995 in prose.
result.label: Digits inside numeric strings

result.description: Fires on ' testing' right after "hypothesis" (statistical hypothesis testing) and on ' are' after plural subjects like "opinions" in epistemology/statistics text. Silent on "testing" in generic rigorous-testing contexts.
result.label: hypothesis testing / opinions are

result.description: Fires on the piece 'h' in "res|h|aped/reshaping", after the "res" prefix, predicting continuations like "aping" or "aped". It stays silent on 'h' in other words such as "prosthetic".
result.label: 'h' in "reshaped"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cul' at the start of "culinary", after an article, adjective or preposition, and predicts the continuation "inary". Members are mostly ' cul' detectors, so it is a token-level feature.
result.label: ' cul' start of "culinary"

result.description: Fires on the head noun of a subject noun phrase after an adjective at the start of a document, like "Effective persuasive writing" or "Good storytelling". The noun is a skill or activity, and the next word is likely a verb such as "requires" or "involves".
result.label: Skill-noun subject awaiting verb

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces ('scop', 'rom', 'om', 'sc') inside scientific instrument or technique words like microscope, spectrometer, spectroscopy, where the next piece is a suffix such as -es, -ies, -etry, -eters.
result.label: Microscope/spectrometer word-piece

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' then', ' are', ' include', ' ways', ' by') in expository text, mostly where a verb or connective follows a plural or abstract subject. Evidence is mixed, with weak consistency and no clear logits.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on " even" starting a concessive clause after a comma, as in "even when / even though / even if". It stays silent on " even" inside a phrase, such as after "or" or "before". Predicts " if", " when" and "though".
result.label: Concessive ' even' after comma

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "continue/continued" (and weakly after "proved" or "begin"), where an infinitive verb follows. It stays silent on ' to' as a preposition (testament to, home to) or purpose 'to'.
result.label: ' to' after continue

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' disput' (disputes, disputed), mostly in territorial, legal or geopolitical text. It predicts a suffix continuation. Members are mainly other detectors of ' disput' and similar stems such as challeng, tax and diplom.
result.label: ' disput' stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on ' or', ',' or ' and' right after a person/group noun (individuals, children, parents, families) in a list of social actors, predicting another group noun like families, groups, entities or households.
result.label: Conjunction after people/group noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece "sculpt" / "pt" in "Sculpture" (and weakly on related art words) when the word is about to be completed with "-ure", in art-related text. It is silent on " sculpt" in the contrast mid-sentence examples.
result.label: Sculpt(ure) word piece in art text

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (the 'am' of cross-contamination, 'into' after 'categorized', 'main', 'such') in expository text about categories, food safety or cooking. Mixed peaks, low consistency; 'am' is silent in other words like 'food contamination'.
result.label: Mid-phrase tokens in categorization/food text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' deb' as the start of "debate/debated/debating" (also "debt"), mostly after words like "been", "historically", "philosophical". Predicts continuations such as 'ated', 'atable', 'unk'.
result.label: ' deb' word-start (debate/debt)

result.description: Fires mostly on " Simple"/" simple" in "Future Simple" tense in grammar/language-learning text, with scattered weaker hits on function words like "with" and "sever". Silent on "Simple" in "Past Continuous and Simple Present". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Future Simple tense in grammar text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' decent' when it starts "decentralization/decentralized", the first piece of a split word. It predicts the continuation 'ral'. Similar word-start pieces (ancest-, aber-, lub-) feed it.
result.label: ' decent' in decentralized

result.description: Fires on the token " rest" (also "Rest"), including as a word-start piece in "restoration", "resting" or "perrest". Predicts continuations like "raint", "oration" and "rained". Its circuit is made of detectors for " rest".
result.label: rest token / rest- word start

result.description: Fires on prepositions like ' in', ' across', ' within' that follow a statement about a method's role or use in tech/ML text, introducing a field (e.g. "in computer science", "across various fields"). Predicts field names like Computer, image.
result.label: Preposition before a field of application

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns and modals (' that', ' which', ' can', ' they') right after a pollutant or contaminant noun, where a verb about harmful effects follows (disrupt, accumulate, pose). Silent on complementizer 'that'.
result.label: Relative 'that/can' after pollutants

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cu' when it begins "cuisine" after a word like global, international, regional or fusion. It predicts the continuation "isine" (logits 'is', 'ps'). Silent on text without this split word.
result.label: ' cu' start of cuisine
' R' predicting 'ouss' (Rousseau)
result.description: Fires on the standalone token ' R' when it begins a name or word, mainly in the Rousseau context (after Voltaire, Jean-Jacques). Pushes toward 'ous', 'ouss' continuations. Silent on ' R' in lists of first names like Richard or Robert.

Fires on the word " visual" used as a modifier after a preposition or verb (providing, through, using, blend) and before a noun such as stimuli, elements or representation. Silent when it starts the text as a bare subject.
result.label: ' visual' as modifier after preposition

result.description: Fires on participle-like or adjective word endings and stems (grounded, conducive, drawn, made, linked, specific) where a complement like "by", "in", "to" or "enough" is expected next. Mixed tokens, low consistency.
result.label: Participle/adjective awaiting complement
' end' as word-start piece
result.description: Fires on the token ' end', especially when it begins a longer word (enduring, endangered, endorsement, endless) and the next piece is expected. Weaker on ' end' as a standalone noun ("the end of").

Fires on the word "random" (and "randomly", "Random") in statistics and methodology text, such as random sampling, random variables, and randomization. It pushes towards continuations like sampling, assignment, generator and -ization.
result.label: "random" word detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' clim' as the start of "climax", "climactic" or "climate", predicting continuations like 'ax', 'actic', 'ates'. Members are mostly ' clim' detectors, plus similar split-word pieces such as 'stra' and 'atmos'.
result.label: ' clim' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the linking word (like, to, of, as) right after a comparison or equivalence expression ("equivalent of", "similar to", "feels like", "likened to"), where a gerund or analogy is expected next. Silent on plain "just like" or "quite like".
result.label: Analogy connector after comparison phrase

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'en' piece inside "millennium" (mill|en|nium), predicting a following suffix like 'ni'. It stays silent on 'en' in other words such as Enlightenment or sentence. A few weak hits on function words like " for" and " typically".
result.label: 'en' in "millennium"

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'o' in the middle of a longer word (sm-o-othing, aerof-o-il, Bar-o-que, mem-o-ization), predicting a continuation such as 'other', 'othing' or 'quent'. Some weaker firing on scattered function words.
result.label: Mid-word 'o' piece (smoothing)

result.description: Fires on the piece 'animate' in 'inanimate', as in personification text about giving human qualities to inanimate objects. Predicts nouns like objects, entities, animals. Members detect animate, mundane, ordinary, object and human-quality cues.
result.label: 'animate' in 'inanimate'

result.description: Fires on a first word-piece of a split multi-token word (phys-, fl-, tur-, D-, intr-) following an academic adjective or topic word, where a suffix like -iology, -uctuations or -moil comes next. Predicts word-completing suffixes.
result.label: Split-word opening piece in academic phrases

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'astr' in "gastronomy/gastronomic" (after 'g'), predicting 'onomy'/'onom' next. Weak on similar pieces like 'gourmet' and on 'astr' in astronomy.
result.label: 'astr' in gastronomy

result.description: Fires on the verb ending of "differ"/"vary" (diff-ers, var-ies, differed) where the verb is about to be followed by "greatly/widely/significantly from/depending". Silent on 'ers' in plural nouns like centers, philosophers, polymers.
result.label: differ/vary verb ending

result.description: Fires on verbs of reducing or eliminating (reduced, reducing, reduces, eliminating) where a technology or process lowers a cost, barrier or burden. It predicts objects like costs, barriers, constraints, traditional limits.
result.label: Reduce/eliminate verbs lowering costs or barriers

result.description: Fires on plural product nouns (structures, materials, fragments, proteins, pieces) that are the object of a creating/producing verb, often followed by "with specific properties". Silent on 'structures' in math or data-structure contexts.
result.label: Created plural nouns (structures, materials)

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' to', also 'the', 'an', 'of') in text about the Catholic Church, the Inquisition and church doctrine. It stays silent on ' to' in other historical or legal contexts.
result.label: Function words in Church/religion text
Temperature/humidity in measured-parameter lists
result.description: Fires on 'temperature' and the 'ity' of 'humidity' (also density, intensity) when listed as a physical or environmental parameter being measured. It predicts words like level, content, rate. Silent on 'ity' in rigidity, fluidity, plasticity.

Fires on " to" (sometimes " in") right after causal verbs like "leads", "leading", "lead", "result" in "result in", where an outcome comes next. It stays silent on infinitive "to" and on "to" after nouns or adjectives.
result.label: "to/in" after lead/result verbs

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' the', ' and', 'ical', ' more', ' that') mid-phrase in academic or technical prose, where the next word is a modifier or noun in a specialist topic. The evidence is mixed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Mid-phrase tokens in academic prose
