result.description: Fires most on the 'vers' piece in "inversely/inverses" (not in "uncovers", "lovers", "oversaw"), and weakly on function words like "the", "in" after "proportional to" and on " Anti" in "Antiquity". Mixed evidence.
result.label: 'vers' in inversely, plus scattered function words

result.description: Fires on ' the' after a causal or driving phrase (as a result of, due to, driven by, such as) in essays about societal or technological change, predicting a trend noun like "rise", "development", "exponential". Silent on many other ' the'.
result.label: ' the' after causal phrase, change

result.description: Fires weakly on varied nouns (food, service, data, EM, access) that end a compound or noun phrase, mostly in service/IT/food contexts. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is unfaithful; evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed noun-ending tokens (food, service)

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (of, or, and, the, on) and word pieces inside abstract expository sentences, mid-phrase. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same ' of' is often silent. The logits are unclear, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on "among" / "Among" (also "Amongst"), especially as a preposition introducing a group after "are/were/being" ("are among those who..."). Predicts group-referring continuations like "those", "them", "the".
result.label: "among" preposition before a group

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ital' inside "revitalization/revitalize", predicting a suffix like -ization or -izing. Members are mostly 'ital' detectors plus other -ize suffix-predicting pieces.
result.label: 'ital' in revitalization

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, '0' subscripts, 'of', 'or', list-joining words) with no consistent token or context. Members mostly detect list/coordination positions in technical text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Scattered list-position tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, on, that) right before an expected "aesthetic(s)" in art/beauty/philosophy text. Members push toward beauty and art words. It stays silent on "the" in other contexts.
result.label: Function word before "aesthetic"

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, is) inside business, finance and risk-management text, where the next word is likely a risk or finance term. It stays silent on 'the' in general academic or historical text. Members are mostly risk, finance and organization topic detectors.
result.label: Function words in risk/finance text

result.description: Fires on sensory-quality nouns like " taste", " texture", and flavo(u)r "or" in food and sensory-science text, especially as a noun in a list or after "both/including/between". Silent when "taste" is a verb (make food taste good).
result.label: Taste/texture as sensory noun

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' pro' when it begins a longer word, mostly 'proactive' but also prototype, probe, prose, proletariat. It stays silent on ' pro' at the very start of a document. Logits favour continuations like 'active' and 'tot'.
result.label: ' pro' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (' and', ' the', ' of', ':', ',') in expository text about knowledge systems and abstract topics, where the next word is likely a noun like 'system' or 'data'. Silent on many ' and' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words before knowledge-system nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and commas (',', ' the', ' any', ' a') in technical expository text about systems, entropy and computing. Peaks are inconsistent and the same comma often stays silent, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ut' inside "pollutants" (poll-ut), predicting the suffix 'ants'. It stays silent on 'ut' in other words such as "scrutinized" or "-utal".
result.label: 'ut' in "pollutants"

result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "Fermi-Dirac" (after a physics surname like Fermi, before the second name). Stays silent on hyphens in ordinary compounds such as non-conscious, decision-making, cost-effectiveness and cutting-edge.
result.label: Hyphen in Fermi-Dirac

result.description: Fires on ' fluid' as a standalone noun in physics text (e.g. "the fluid", "a fluid"). It stays silent when 'fluid' is a modifier in "fluid dynamics/mechanics". Occasionally fires on ' Mach' and ' object'.
result.label: 'fluid' as head noun

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, most often ' more' (as in "tend to be more reactive"), plus ' Equ', ' are' and commas. It stays silent on many other ' more' contexts, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered ' more' and misc tokens

result.description: Fires on ' must', ' to' and ' also' right after a subject like "leaders", "companies" or "it is essential", where a bare action verb comes next. It appears in business-strategy text about agility. It is silent on other uses of ' to'.
result.label: Modal/infinitive slot before action verb

result.description: Fires on quantifier/plural determiners such as ' various', ' these', ' several', and 'of' in 'range/array of', where a plural noun for kinds of things (techniques, technologies, methods) is expected next. Silent on some 'various' uses, so context matters.
result.label: Various/these before plural kinds

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'indu' in "Hindu" (Hinduism, Hindu philosophy), when it follows the 'H' piece. Members are mostly 'indu' detectors plus other religion-name pieces (Buddh, Islam-ic, Calvin-ism).
result.label: 'indu' in Hindu

result.description: Fires mainly on " of" (also " in") right after stage/phase/process/step nouns, as in "final stage of" or "process of", where a named activity or project comes next. It stays silent on "process of" in music-related text.
result.label: "of" after stage/process nouns

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' (' after "garbage collection", 'ER' in CERN, 'ing' in reclaiming, 'handle') mostly in garbage collection / memory management text. Members push GC-related tokens. Silent on ' (' in other topics.
result.label: Garbage collection context tokens

result.description: Fires on connector words (as, like, including, from, beyond, commas) that introduce a list or elaboration of operating-system services and kernel functions. It stays silent on causal ", as it provides" clauses, so it seems to need the example-list slot.
result.label: OS services list-introducing connectors

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly arrows ('=>', '->'), a lone 'n', and ' fast', plus odd mid-word pieces. Peaks are inconsistent (17%), and the members are diffuse and mostly non-specific. The pattern is unclear.
result.label: Arrow tokens and scattered misc

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' the', ' and', ' of', ' their', ' for') mid-phrase in expository academic text, where a noun or modifier is expected next. Evidence is mixed: it is silent on many ' the' tokens, and the members are diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, the, from, same, how, any) mid-sentence in abstract academic or technical prose, often before a noun phrase. Silent on many ' of' tokens after nouns like "theory of". Evidence is mixed and logits are unclear.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (' that', ' of', ' how', ' describes') right after a clause about Newton's laws or motion, such as "first law states that". Silent on 'that' in other physics contexts. Members detect Newton's-law and motion context.
result.label: Connector words in Newton's laws text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' emb' (embark, embroidery, embellish, embody), predicting continuations like 'ark', 'roid', 'rac'. Members are mostly ' emb' detectors.
result.label: ' emb' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the token ' counter' as a verb or prefix (counter American influence, counteract, counterpart, counterpoint, counterbalance). Members are mostly ' counter' detectors that predict continuations like 'act', 'bal', 'part'.
result.label: ' counter' verb/prefix

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (periods, commas, "workers", "labor", "significant") in labor, workforce and travel-related text, where the next word is likely a labor term. Members predict worker, job, labor and skill. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Labor/workers context, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on function words (and, represent, of, as, the) in passages about contour lines, maps and terrain, where a map or landform feature is being described or represented. Silent on 'and' in other lists or subjects.
result.label: Function words in map/terrain descriptions

result.description: Fires on the object noun (people, life, subjects, world) after verbs like depict, portray or represent in descriptions of Realism art. It is silent on 'life' in phrases like 'everyday life' or 'human life'.
result.label: Realism depiction object nouns

result.description: Fires on ' with' (rarely ' have'/' possess') right after a plural noun, introducing a property of that noun ("elements with unique characteristics", "atoms with similar..."). Silent on verb-governed 'with' (confronted with, reacts with, association with).
result.label: noun-modifying 'with' (having property)

result.description: Fires on the last token of a field, topic or technology noun phrase (machine learning, computer science, CRM), which is the subject of a historical sentence ("In the 1980s, X ..."). Members predict a past-tense verb like "experienced" or "became" next.
result.label: Subject noun of historical sentence

result.description: Fires on the token " Renaissance" when it is used as a bare modifier or subject (e.g. "Italian Renaissance", "Renaissance art", sentence-initial). It stays silent after "the" ("during the Renaissance"). Weakly fires on Enlightenment and Baroque.
result.label: Renaissance without preceding "the"

result.description: Fires on scattered function-word and affix tokens ('-' after "anti", ' as' in "known as", ' can', ' dis') in abstract academic prose. Peaks are mixed and inconsistent; '-' stays silent after self/non/two/cold. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Mixed function tokens, anti- hyphen

result.description: Fires on the token ' decision' as the first word of a compound such as "decision trees", "decision-making" or "decision models". Predicts continuations like trees, making, process. Members are mostly detectors of ' decision' itself.
result.label: ' decision' in compounds

result.description: Fires on a comma right after a plural technical noun phrase (e.g. "techniques," "devices," "systems,"), where a trailing modifier like "often utilizing" or "typically incorporated" comes next. Silent on some commas after similar nouns.
result.label: Comma after technical noun phrase

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, a, their, studying) in explanatory text about motion, kinematics and dynamics, where the next word is likely a physics or math term like motion or velocity. Silent on 'of' in other contexts like robotics or classical mechanics.
result.label: Function words before motion-physics terms
' world' in world-building writing
result.description: Fires on ' world' when it is the first piece of a compound or phrase like worldbuilding, worldscapes or worldview, in text about crafting fiction ("create compelling world…"). It predicts building/view/wide continuations. Silent on the contrast passage about storytelling, which has no ' world'.

Fires on ' be', ' it', ' become' and similar slots after modals (may/can) in technical text, where a negative or difficulty-type predicate is expected next (costly, difficult, disrupted, fragile). Silent when 'be' is followed by neutral uses such as 'be used' or 'be applied'.
result.label: Modal 'be' before negative predicate

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and prefixes (' the', ' by', ' on', ' un', 'with', 'account') in academic explanatory prose, where the next word is likely a variation/difference-type term. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast shows the same ' the' staying silent.
result.label: Scattered function words before variation terms

result.description: Fires on the possessive ' his' when it begins a noun phrase about a person's life or work in biographical text, often after a clause-opening word or preposition. Predicts nouns like career, plans, models.
result.label: Biographical possessive ' his'

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on ' gig' (in "gig economy") plus assorted word pieces and function words (whereby, such as, due to). Mixed evidence; seems to anticipate a noun-like continuation such as 'economy', but the circuit is weak and unspecific.
result.label: Gig economy and mixed word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' fant' (start of "fantasy", "fantastical") when it is followed by a continuation like "asy". It predicts the suffix pieces "asy"/"as". Members are mostly ' fant' detectors, with some similar prefix detectors (fuz, amb, chrom).
result.label: ' fant' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' right after a preposition (across, for, after, on, at, of), introducing a new noun phrase. It stays quiet on ' a' after copulas or adverbs like 'be', 'also', 'always', or after 'create'.
result.label: ' a' after a preposition

result.description: Fires on ' and' (also ' but', ',', ' more') right after an adjective in a coordinated adjective pair, like "powerful and independent". Silent when 'and' joins nouns or verbs.
result.label: 'and' joining adjectives

result.description: Fires on ' the' after "half/part/quarter/end of" in temporal phrases, where a century or decade number (20th, 19th) comes next. Silent on 'the' after "of" in non-temporal-portion phrases like "explorations of the" or "phase of the".
result.label: 'the' after "half of" before century

result.description: Fires on commas in lists of field or topic names (e.g. "photography, videography, sound design") and occasionally on function words like "the", "of", "to" in academic text. Silent on commas after introductory clauses. Mixed evidence.
result.label: Commas in topic/discipline lists

result.description: Fires on ' be' directly after "cannot" (e.g. "cannot be overstated", "cannot be fully understood"). It stays quiet on ' be' after "may not", "might", "will" or "to".
result.label: ' be' after "cannot"

result.description: Fires on connectives and function words (commas, "of", "and", "as", "including") in academic prose about philosophy and fields of study, where a list or a field name (e.g. "philosophy", "the development of") is likely to come next. It stays silent on some commas in similar text.
result.label: Connectives in academic philosophy prose

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (and, of, commas, in, including) inside technical passages about speech recognition and language processing, where the next word is a speech or language technical term. Silent on 'and' in other list contexts.
result.label: Connectives in speech/language technology text

result.description: Fires on function words (' to', ' people', ' also', ' as') in text about social conformity and the Spiral of Silence, especially 'likely/inclined/tendency to' before 'conform' or 'remain silent'. Silent on ' to' in statistics and programming text.
result.label: Conformity/silence theory function words

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (commas, "of", "as", "and", "the") in the middle of abstract academic or expository phrases, where a noun or word-piece continuation follows. Evidence is mixed; the logits are weak and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Mid-phrase function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a word or surname that is incomplete and needs a continuation, mostly ' Lind' after "Dr." in lists of names, also ' sug' (sugars) and other mid-word fragments. Predicts suffixes like 'ams'.
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments, esp. Dr. Lind-

result.description: Fires on ' most' in "even the most [experienced/dedicated]" and on 'and'/'to'/'the' in "from X to Y" or "both X and Y" spans about kinds of people (novice to expert). Silent on plain "most" meaning "the majority".
result.label: "even the most" skill-level spans

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' its', ' the', ' to', ' are') and word pieces like ' hem' in technical or scientific prose. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' its' is silent in several contexts. The evidence does not show what separates the firing cases.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Ch' in "Supply Chain" (predicting "ain") and on ' val' in "valued/valence". These are incomplete word beginnings where the next piece completes the word. Weak elsewhere.
result.label: Ch of Supply Chain, val- word starts

result.description: Fires on ' dis' (in "disorder"), ' band'/' Band' in physics-style text, and a few function words, in scientific contexts about entropy or band theory. It stays silent on 'dis' in "disperse". Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: dis(order) and band in physics

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments ' heav' (before "ier" in heavier elements) and ' sug' (before "ars"), plus a few other word pieces like 'ic' in deficit. Predicts a word-completing suffix. Mostly science text; weak evidence.
result.label: heav- / sug- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start fragments of Latinate verbs/nouns (' decre', ' constru', ' gover', ' introdu', ' estab') where the word continues with a suffix such as -ases, -ctions or -ns. Mixed evidence, low faithfulness.
result.label: Latinate word-stem fragments before suffix

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (without, less, who, has, such as, full) in expository academic text, mid-clause before a predicate or complement. Peaks are inconsistent and the same token 'without' is silent elsewhere, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Mixed function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces 'h' in "carbohydrate" (carbo|h|ydrate) and 'ist' in "redistribute/redistribution", where the word continues. Also fires on a long run of zero-width characters. Predicts word continuations like "ribution".

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix 'ic' in "therapeutic" in music-therapy text, sometimes on words like ' its' after "utilize". It is silent on some other 'ic' endings and on "therapeutic" in other spots. Members are music/therapy topic detectors.

result.description: Fires mostly on ' or' after the abstract noun "ownership" (ownership or relationship/control) in linguistics-style text, with scattered other peaks (' land', '(', ' and'). Silent on ' or' after other nouns. Evidence is mixed and weak.

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'm' in the split word "paradigm" (also in "paradigmatic", "pragmatic"-like splits), predicting "shift" or "-atic". Silent on 'm' in other words like "realm" or "Programmatic".

result.description: Fires on 'also', 'still', 'simultaneously', or 'while' right after a 'while' clause, as in "X while also/still doing Y". It stays silent on 'also' in 'not only... but also'.
result.label: Adverb after 'while' (while also/still)

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of punctuation marks (e.g. "periods, question marks, colons, semicolons"). Stays silent on commas in other grammar or punctuation sentences, so it needs the list-of-marks construction.

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ut' in the middle of "micronutrients" (micron|ut|rients), after "micron" or "macron". Silent on 'ut' at word start or in "coconut", so it needs the preceding nutrient-prefix piece.

result.description: Fires on varied function words or word pieces (' (', 'it', ' that', ' to', verb endings) in abstract academic prose, mostly where a subject or noun phrase is followed by a verb or clause. Silent on some ' (' tokens, so the trigger is mixed.

result.description: Fires on function words (the, that, for, and, 's) inside project-management text about scope, where the next word is likely "project" or "scope". Silent on the same words in other business or analysis contexts.
result.label: Function words in project scope text

result.description: Fires on the word "soil" (and the "il" piece of "Soil") in texts on soil science and geotechnics, such as soil properties, structure, and mechanics. Members are mostly "il"/" soil" detectors plus context words that precede "soil".
result.label: Soil token in soil science

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (the, only, of, as, commas, 'io') in expository text, mid-phrase where a noun or technical term comes next. Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is diffuse and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase function-word firing

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (commas, 'that', 'above', 'is', 'for', '-ly') mid-clause in expository essay-style text about communication and skills. Peaks are scattered and the contrast comma stays silent, so the pattern is diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the comma or 'and' right after 'efficiency' in a list of benefits or goals (efficiency, service quality, cost...). Silent on 'and' or commas in other lists. Predicts a next list item like effectiveness, accuracy or waste.

result.description: Fires on ' an' after a negation or "merely/just/so much" framing ("is no longer an", "not merely an", "not just an"), where a contrasting noun phrase is expected. Silent on ' an' in plain "is an" or "becomes an" contexts.

result.description: Fires on the 'in' piece inside the word "Multinomial" (Mult-in-omial), also weakly in "multinational". Silent on 'in' in other words such as "fascinating" or "trinomitics".

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' Id', ' the', possessive 's, 'their', 'an', identity-matrix 'I', 'U') with no single shared trigger; the peaks are mixed and the circuit failed to reproduce them well. Members are broad hubs.

result.description: Fires mainly on " of" right after a heading-like word such as "Adverbs of" (manner/time) in grammar-lesson lists. Silent on ordinary "of" in narrative or descriptive prose. Weak activity elsewhere on commas and "the".

result.description: Fires on plural nouns like "examples", "applications", "studies" or "instances" when an intro sentence announces that a section will explore or illustrate them (e.g. "delves into practical applications"). Silent on "this example illustrates".

result.description: Fires on verb stems like ampl-, simpl-, intens-, fort-, clar-, ident- where the word continues with the suffix "-ify" (ifies, ifying, ification). Its output pushes those suffix tokens next.
result.label: Stem before -ify suffix

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ogn' (as in "cognition", "cognitive"), plus other word-start fragments like 'ca', 'ag', ' capac', ' pract', ' virt' that need a completion such as "-ition" or "-itive". Peaks on 'ogn' appearing at the start of a sentence or after a break.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (possessive 's, for, the, of, and, a, an) in expository prose, mid-phrase where a noun or content word is expected next. No single token dominates; the members are mostly generic function-word detectors. Evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words before content

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'ole' inside "intermolecular" (predicting "cular"), with weaker hits on other word pieces and digits. It stays silent on 'ole' in "Molecular" at the start of a sentence.
result.label: 'ole' in intermolecular

result.description: Fires on the piece ' as' when it begins the word "asserts"/"asserting" (split as 'as'+'ser'), predicting 'ser' continuation. It stays quiet on ' as' used as a standalone conjunction or preposition ("as it states", "such as").

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'FE' piece in the acronym "Finite Element Analysis (FEA)", just after the opening parenthesis. A few weaker peaks fall on function words and punctuation. Members detect capital-letter acronym pieces.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' to', ' can', 'ity', commas, ' these', ' and') in technical expository text, mid-phrase. Peaks are mixed and the contrast shows the same ' to' staying silent, so the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' II' in "Type II error", 'su' in "well-suited", an apostrophe, ' are') in technical or scientific explanatory text, especially statistics. No single token dominates; the circuit is diffuse and weakly faithful.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and modifiers (' inner', ' and', ' that', ' the', ' internal') in the middle of a noun phrase, where an adjective like "inner/large/living" could come next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse.

result.description: Fires on prepositions or connectives (among, between, of, from, by) after nouns of concern, conflict or power in historical/geopolitical text about nations and powers. It predicts country or military-diplomatic terms next. Peak tokens are mixed.

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns ' that'/' which' introducing a relative clause after a noun like "earlier approaches", "static models", "early methods", where the clause describes older or contrasting ideas. Silent on many other relative 'that' cases.

result.description: Fires on the word-piece "co" (mostly " co") when it begins a longer word such as cooperative, coating, cocktail or coaching. It pushes toward continuations like "operation", "aching", "ck", "pper".

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' comp' when it begins a longer word, peaking where the continuation is "licate/licating" (complicate). It also fires weakly on other comp- words like compelling and composting. Silent on the whole word "complex".

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (periods ending short list-like headings, ' the', ' directly', ' a', word fragments) with no clear pattern. Logits push toward words like quarter, wave, lake, micro, macro. Peak consistency is low and the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'comp' piece after the prefix 'un-' (uncomplicated), and also on list commas and connectives (',', ' and', ' between', ' various') in enumerations of academic topics. Mixed; the 'un-' word-piece part is the clearest.
result.label: un-'comp' pieces and list commas

result.description: Fires on the verb "change" and its forms (changes, changing, adjust, alter) when used as a transitive or active verb, often with a following object like color, direction, or perspective. Mostly in language, grammar, or descriptive text.
result.label: Change verb forms

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' expl' when it begins the verb "explored" (passive "will be explored", "are explored"). It is quieter before "-oring" or "-oration" in noun or participle uses.
result.label: ' expl' starting "explored"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (and, of, from, such, both, -abling) mid-phrase in academic text, where a continuation is expected. Peaks are inconsistent, with no dominant token. The logits are weak and mixed, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sust' when it begins "sustainable", especially after adverbs like "ecologically" or "environmentally" or after "more". It is silent on "sustainability" and "sustains" in some contexts.
result.label: ' sust' in "sustainable"

result.description: Fires on a linking verb (' was', 's' in it's, ' is', ' were') right after a subject like "it", "files", "lunch", where an adverb or predicate comes next. Silent when 'was' follows a bare noun in a different construction.
result.label: Copula after subject (was/is/'s)

result.description: Fires on ' to' (also ' can', ' quickly') right after a technical subject like a system or vehicle, where a verb of function or purpose comes next ("designed to", "allows them to", "vehicles can"). Silent on ' to' as a preposition ("similar to", "from X to Y").
result.label: Infinitive 'to'/'can' before function verb

result.description: Fires on function or verb words like "using", "the", "of", "use" in writing-advice text about sentence structure, active/passive voice and sentence variety, where the next word starts a technique or device. Silent on "using" in other contexts.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' (', ' Music', 'ed', '0') in text about sound, music and acoustics; members mostly push music-related next words. Peaks are inconsistent and it stays silent on some ' (' tokens, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Music/sound context, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: 'ent' in "lentil", "of" after "advent", "different", "def". Peaks are inconsistent and the members are generic context. The contrast shows 'ent' silent at the end of words like "permanent" and "inherent".
result.label: Mixed 'ent' in lentil, advent of

result.description: Fires on the word " deep" (also "deeper", "Deep") in many contexts: deep learning, deep-dive, deepest, deeper insights. Members are mostly detectors of "deep" itself, and the logits favour continuations like -ening, -ened and -est.
result.label: Token "deep"

result.description: Fires on mixed function-word positions (' the', ' a', commas in lists, ' specific') in abstract expository text, where a noun is expected next. Silent on many ' the' tokens, and the circuit is diffuse, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse function words before noun

result.description: Fires on the piece "row" inside "Microwave" (mainly "Cosmic Microwave Background"), where the next piece should be "ave". Weaker in lowercase "microwave" and other mic-row- words.
result.label: "row" in Microwave

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after a time-period opener, such as a year or decade phrase followed by a comma ("By 1979, the") or "a period of ... the", in historical-era text. It stays silent on "the" after "beginning of" or "years of".
result.label: "the" after era/date phrase

result.description: Fires on commas and function words (when, of, with) right after an introductory time-period phrase such as "During this period," or "to 2000, when", in academic history-style text. Silent on many similar commas, so the condition is weakly specified.
result.label: Comma after historical period phrase

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ',', ' to', ' and') and word pieces in abstract expository text, where a verb or noun phrase is about to continue. Contrast shows ' the' after 'in' is silent. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after an object of adapt/tailor/adjust/modify verbs (e.g. "adapt our methods to", "tailoring messages to"), where "to" introduces the target or purpose (suit, fit, meet). Silent on other ' to' uses such as "approach to" or "crucial to".
result.label: ' to' after adapt/tailor object

result.description: Fires on verbs of supplying a benefit, mainly " offer(s)", also "providing/provide", when a subject (often "which" or a noun like arrays) is about to be described as giving something valuable. Predicts an upcoming adjective or noun object.
result.label: offer/provide verbs before benefit

result.description: Fires on ' under' as a prefix at the start of a word (underestimate, understating, undergo), where a suffix is expected next. Silent when 'under' is a standalone preposition in a list of prepositions.
result.label: ' under' as word-prefix

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' fundamental', ' of', ' the', ' essential') in expository academic text on philosophy, history, or biochemistry, where a noun like a core concept or category is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Academic exposition connective tokens

result.description: Fires on the word-piece "emp" (Emp/emp), as the start of words like unemployment, employment, empowering, empiricism. It predicts continuations such as "loyment", "loy", "ower". It stays silent on "empathy".
result.label: emp- word piece (employment/empower)

result.description: Fires on function words after a plural subject noun (' they', ' also', ' that', ' who', ' which') where a plural verb is expected next, like 'are' or 'have'. Silent on some ' they' in other clause positions.
result.label: Plural subject pronoun before verb

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' is', ' or', ' than', ' as', ' these') in explanatory text about nonverbal communication, listening and body language. Silent on ' is' in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: Function words in nonverbal communication text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' qual' (start of "qualitative") in methodology text, mostly after "quantitative and/or" or in lists of research approaches. It predicts the continuation "itative". Members detect qual/quant pieces.
result.label: ' qual' before "itative"
'iden' in 'evidenced'
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'iden' in "evidenced" (as evidenced by), predicting the suffix 'ced'. Members include other mid-word pieces that precede 'ced'/'cing' endings (reinforced, unprecedented).

Fires on commas and "and" inside a list of abstract skill or quality nouns (precision, patience, timing, creativity) after "requires/involves", where another quality is expected next. Silent on commas after ordinary clauses or noun phrases.
result.label: List separators among skill qualities

result.description: Fires on capitalized ' Within' opening a sentence right after a full stop or document start. Lowercase mid-sentence 'within' only weakly activates it, and it stays silent there.
result.label: Sentence-initial 'Within'

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' the', ' of', 'is', commas, word fragments like 'inter', 'mach') in explanatory or academic text, where the next token is a word continuation or fragment. No single token or clear context dominates; the circuit evidence is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-word and function-word firing

result.description: Fires on the end of plural or category head nouns in biology and science text (pathways, interactions, System, responses, -ulation), where a subject noun phrase is complete. Silent on 'ulation' in other contexts such as 'Simulation' or 'accumulation'.
result.label: Biological system/process noun endings

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (by, of, to, colon, comma) in texts about history of philosophy and ancient Greece, where a philosophy or Greek-related word is likely to come next. Silent on colons in other academic text.
result.label: Function words in philosophy history text

result.description: Fires on list-introducing or continuing function tokens (commas, "such as", "including", "-ing") inside enumerations of event or festival organization tasks (ticketing, security, sound, venue). Predicts next item such as stages or phases. Silent on commas in business text.
result.label: Event-logistics list connectors

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " ac" (or " Ac") when it begins a longer word, mostly "acoustic(s)", and predicts continuations like "oust", "ous". It also fires weakly on "acute" and "acids".
result.label: " ac" start of "acoustic"

result.description: Fires on mixed function words, mostly ' are' and "'re", often where a predicate like "not just/only" or a comparison ("unlike", "higher", "lower") follows. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' are' is silent in many contexts.
result.label: Are/'re before "not just" contrasts

result.description: Peaks scatter across unrelated tokens (partial word pieces like 'atr' and 'ad', plus ' a', ' producing', ' by', ' these') in explanatory academic text. No dominant token or clear condition. The circuit's members are mostly generic context.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, academic text

result.description: Fires mainly on the word-piece ' ra' in "cooling rack" (wire rack), where the token starts a split word. Weaker activity on other word-start fragments like pre-, ep-, stro-. Circuit is mostly ' ra' detectors; the rest is mixed.
result.label: ' ra' piece in "cooling rack"

result.description: Fires on linking words (mostly "against", also "of", "by") after hedging/protection or volatility phrases in finance text, e.g. "hedge against", "winds of". Silent on "against" meaning competition or opposition.
result.label: Finance risk-hedging "against" connector

result.description: Fires on varied adjectives and nouns in lists of categories or attributes (physical, spoken, visual, measures), in text about accessibility, security or protected characteristics, where a comma or "and/or" is likely to follow. Silent on some 'physical' contexts.
result.label: Category word before list continuation

result.description: Fires on ' of' after collective nouns like "web", "network", "array", "system" in the "intricate/complex web of X" construction, predicting abstract relational nouns. Silent on some similar ' of' cases, so the condition is not fully clear.
result.label: 'of' after "intricate web/network"

result.description: Fires on 'the' (also 'a', 'an') right after a copula or 'serves as' that begins a defining claim, like "dialogue is the fundamental element". Silent on 'the' in other slots, e.g. "is the use of" or "consider the".
result.label: Article after 'is' in definitional claims

result.description: Fires on "the" (also 's, "specific") after "depends on / align with / understand / including", where a requirement-like noun comes next (requirements, type, scope, needs). Silent on other "the" uses.
result.label: "the" before requirements/needs

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' c' (a lowercase c starting a new word, often split from a following piece like 'athedral', 'ats', 'afes'). It predicts continuations such as 'athed', 'afé', 'rop', 'ues'.
result.label: word-initial ' c' fragment

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (discarded, these, of, -able) in waste, recycling and reprocessing text, just before a word for waste material. Members are mostly waste/refuse-themed context latents. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Waste recycling material-noun anticipation

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Rob' (also ' diam', ' pale') when it is the first piece of a longer word, mainly "Robotics" in lists of subject headings; predicts continuations like 'ot'. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Rob- start of Robotics

result.description: Fires on customer/consumer/user/client as the object of "current", "present", "responding to" etc., where the next word is likely needs, preferences or sentiment. Silent on "customer" in other slots like "customer engagement" or "customer base".
result.label: customer/user before needs/preferences

result.description: Fires mostly on ' right' in lists of Buddhist Eightfold Path elements ("right understanding, right intention"), and on separators in such lists. Also weakly on scattered tokens like zeros in binary strings. Mixed evidence; the circuit is poorly faithful.
result.label: Eightfold Path 'right' list items

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (the, their, to, using, stable) in technical science/math/chemistry text, where the next word is likely a technical noun such as components, energy, or radiation. Peaks are mixed, and the same words are silent in other contexts.
result.label: Function words before technical science nouns

result.description: Fires on ' for' when it is the start of a word split into pieces (fore-, forge, forage), typically right after 'to' in an infinitive slot. It stays silent on ' for' as a preposition meaning 'for purpose'.
result.label: 'for' as word-start piece (foresee, forge)
' const' as word-start fragment
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' const' when it starts a longer word split into tokens, such as constancy, constitute, constrained. It pushes toward continuations like 'ra', 'itut', 'ancy'. Silent on unrelated text.

Fires on scattered function words (' as', ' the', ' of', 's') mid-phrase in expository text, where a noun is expected next (e.g., 'chain', 'columns'). No dominant token; the peaks are inconsistent and the members are diffuse.
result.label: Function words before expected noun

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ath' piece in "cathode"-like words (c-ath-odes) in electrochemistry text, with weaker firing on scattered function words (of, a, comma) in technical science passages. Mixed and low faithfulness.
result.label: 'ath' in cathode words

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (aging, of, including, parentheses) in corporate finance text about working capital, liabilities and expenses, where a financial term like debt, liquidity or rent is expected next. Silent on "managing" in other contexts.
result.label: Finance list/management slot predicting liabilities

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Pic' at the start of "Picasso", especially in lists of artists or after "Pablo". Upstream members are mostly ' Pic' detectors, plus other word-start fragment detectors.
result.label: ' Pic' start of Picasso

result.description: Fires on ' make' when it is the first piece of the compound "makeup", especially in "genetic makeup", predicting a suffix like "up". Stays silent on ' make' as an ordinary verb, as in "must make wise".
result.label: "make" in "makeup"

result.description: Fires on determiners and quantity words like " a", " single", " one", " entire" that introduce a singular unit (e.g. "a single word"), mostly in linguistics text. It stays quiet on " a" in other constructions such as "such a tradition".
result.label: Singular-unit determiners in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on " our" right after verbs of challenging or questioning (challenge, question, reconsider, revolutionize) where the next word would be an abstract noun like assumptions, understanding, or intuition. Silent on " our" after "of" or "is".
result.label: "our" after challenge-type verbs

result.description: Fires on the word " instead", mostly in "X instead of Y" substitution phrasing, and weakly when it opens a clause after a semicolon or comma. Members are detectors of " instead" and " rather" (as in "rather than"). Silent on text without it.
result.label: " instead" substitution word

result.description: Fires mostly on ' half' as a compound modifier before a hyphen (half-life, half-step), and occasionally on ' Sp' in "Oil Spill". Silent on "half–life" with an en dash, so it seems to need the hyphenated compound context.
result.label: ' half' in half-life / half-step

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ang' piece in Hangul (H-ang) and on scattered word fragments or function words in linguistics and writing-system text (phonetics, syllables, alphabets). Evidence is mixed; the circuit is weak.
result.label: Hangul 'ang' in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on sentence-ending periods (occasionally colons) in culinary and food-preparation text about flavor, tenderness and cooking technique. It stays quiet on periods in other topics such as finance or security.
result.label: Period in cooking/food text

result.description: Fires on the word piece "orient" in hyphenated compounds like object-oriented or task-oriented, just before the suffix "-ed" or "-ated". It weakly fires on similar pieces such as "center" in "patient-centered".
result.label: "-orient" before -ed suffix

result.description: Fires on the suffix "ually" in "visually", mostly in "both visually ..." phrases about appealing design, food or art. It predicts appealing-adjective continuations such as "striking", "appealing" and "arresting".
result.label: "visually" before appealing adjective

result.description: Fires on objects and words in cleaning and hygiene instructions (hands, water, tools, surfaces, commas in lists, "thoroughly") in food-safety or sanitation text. Silent on "hands" in a non-hygiene context.

result.description: Fires on the 'y' piece inside the word "recycling" (rec|y|cling, recyclable), predicting the continuation 'cl'/'cling'. Silent on other text, such as "zero-waste" passages without this split word.

result.description: Fires on function words and adjectives (of, the, rich, musical) in text about historical or traditional music and culture, such as Byzantine liturgical music. It seems to anticipate heritage or cultural words next. Evidence is mixed and the consistency is low.
result.label: Function words in historical music text

result.description: Fires on function words (' any', ' their', ' the', commas, 'as') that begin a noun phrase or list item in expository text, e.g. "free from any kind of", "such as their". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Function words opening noun phrases

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "the", "about" and similar function words inside lists or coordinated noun phrases in abstract expository text (management, data systems). It is silent on many commas in similar text, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: List separators in expository text

result.description: Fires on possessive markers (apostrophe-s, "their", "his") that refer back to an artist, author or chef in discussions of art and creative work. It predicts nouns like work, vision or influences. It stays quiet on "their" that refers to other groups.
result.label: Possessives referring to an artist

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' Her' in Heraclitus/Heroplastus, ' Theory', ' are', commas) in philosophy and academic lists of thinkers and topics. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful, so the pattern is loose.

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' in "geotechnical" in engineering text (e.g. geotechnical engineering/risk). Silent on 'ical' in other words like analytical or dynamical, and on some geotechnical contexts.
result.label: geotechn-ical suffix in engineering

result.description: Fires on " in" right after a noun like "moment", "event", "chapter" or "turning point" that is described as pivotal or significant, where "in the history of…" comes next. It stays quiet on " in" after "increase" or "disparities", and on " in" before a date.
result.label: " in" after pivotal moment/event

result.description: Fires on the letter token 'r' when it appears as a mid-word piece (neut-r-ino, ir-r-ational, nut-r-itional, det-r-imental) or as a standalone letter. Predicts word continuations like 'ational', 'iment', 'uly'.

result.description: Fires on the 'LED' piece (also 'CD') in display-technology acronyms such as OLED, QLED and LCD, mostly right after a prefix letter. It stays silent on other tech acronyms like CPU and GPU.

result.description: Fires on the word piece "co" in "eco" (e|co), mostly before "-friendly" or "-conscious" in environmental text. Members detect "eco"/"ecolog"/"environmentally" pieces and push toward hyphen and "friendly/conscious".

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' Sh', ' R', 'leb' (also ' sh', ' d') where the word is unfinished and continues in the next token, e.g. Space-Sh-uttle, R-isk, whist-leb-lower. Pushes toward suffix pieces.

result.description: Fires on connector words (from, both, as, including, of) that introduce a list or range of organisms in marine ecology text, where a set of species or animals is expected next. Silent on "from" in non-enumerating uses.
result.label: List-introducing connectors in marine ecology

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (hyphens, parentheses, word-piece fragments, spaces in Arabic or Cyrillic or garbled text) with no consistent token. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is low-faithfulness, so it looks like a diffuse mid-word or noisy-text feature.

result.description: Fires on function words and commas (',', ' a', ' in', ' of') in academic game-theory/economics text, where the next word is likely a game-theory term like Nash, player or games. Silent on commas in other technical topics.

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces mid-word, mainly 'inst' in "brainstorming" and ' Tre' in "Search Trees", plus a few other fragments. Logits favor continuing into a longer word (topological, etic). Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' vis' when it begins a word like viscous, viscosity or viscosity-related terms, especially in fluid physics text. Members are mostly ' vis' detectors that push toward continuations such as 'cos'.

result.description: Fires on the verb "help"/"helps" after a subject (often "can help", "also helps") when a verb like identify, understand or manage is expected next. Silent when "helps" starts the text with no subject before it.
result.label: verb "help/helps" after subject

result.description: Fires mostly on 'öd' in "Schrödinger", and weakly on word-start fragments like ' ju' in "juxtapose" or ' sp'. These are mid-word pieces where a word continues. Predicts suffix-like continuations.

result.description: Fires on adjectives (intricate, complex, vast, rich, coherent, harmonious, continuous) right after "a/an" in abstract, flowery descriptions, where a noun like "tapestry" or "framework" is expected next. It stays silent on some "intricate" cases without that slot.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' and', ' of', ' the', '**', commas) inside abstract academic or essay-style prose about skills, language and systems. The peaks are inconsistent, and the same ' and' is often silent elsewhere. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on function words (of, our, the, later, on) in science text about cosmology/astronomy, where the next word is likely a physics or astronomy term. Silent on 'of' in other abstract contexts; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words before cosmology terms

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, "an", "the", word pieces) inside lists or phrases about musical elements, such as rhythm, scales, chords. Upstream members push "musical/music" next. Silent on commas in other topics.
result.label: Music-theory list tokens

result.description: Fires on function words or adjectives (the, a, important, essential, significant, relevant) right before an object noun in data-science text about selecting, retaining, or capturing key features. Silent on 'the' after traversing or within.
result.label: Key-feature determiner in data science

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after "During" (often sentence-initial), where a historical period or event is expected next (war, revolution, early days). Silent on ' the' in other constructions.
result.label: "During the" before historical period

result.description: Fires on ' a', ' the' or ' its' right after verbs like "marked" or "experienced" in historical-change phrases, where a noun like "significant shift", "new era" or "revolution" comes next. It stays quiet on 'a' after "emerged as" or "through".
result.label: Article after "marked/experienced" before significant change

result.description: Fires on words naming social, domestic or occupational spheres (household, domestic, managerial, professional, social) in texts about gender roles and division of labor, after phrases like "limited to" or "assigned to".
result.label: Gender-role sphere words (household, domestic)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'og' inside "hierog-lyphic/lyphs", predicting the 'lyph' continuation. It stays silent on 'og' in "orthogonal/orthogonality", so it needs the "hier" prefix.
result.label: 'og' in hieroglyph

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (of, the, within, mainly, parentheses) in text about animal taxonomy, especially the cat family Felidae/Carnivora, where a taxon or species term is expected next. Silent on the same tokens in other topics.
result.label: Function words in animal taxonomy text

result.description: Fires on the token ' present' (the word piece before suffixes like -ations, -ers), mostly as the start of "presentations" in communication contexts. Members are detectors of ' present' in various senses; contrast stays silent without it.
result.label: ' present' token, presentations

result.description: Fires on ' to' after "began/started/begin" (inception verbs) before a bare verb, especially in academic or historical prose. Silent on some other "began to" cases, so the condition is not fully clear. Predicts verbs like recognize, notice, take, see.

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied function words (' the', ' that', ' in', ')') in academic prose, where the next token is a modifier or continuation. Contrast shows the same ' the' often silent, and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the final token of a noun used metaphorically as a channel or means ("serves as a condu-it", "medium", "vehicle", "gateway"), after "serves/acts as a...". Predicts "for/through/into". Silent on "it" inside words like "prioritizing" or "facilitates".
result.label: conduit/medium metaphor noun after "serves as"

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece " lig" (as in ligands) in coordination chemistry text, with occasional weaker firing on " cycl" (cyclotron) and some function words. Upstream members detect " lig" and chemistry context.
result.label: lig- of ligands in chemistry

result.description: Fires on function words (the, to, and, 's) in mathematical or economic explanatory text, where the next word is likely a math term like "mathematical" or "algebraic". Silent on the same words in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words before math terms

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' di' when it is a split-off start of a longer word, especially "diagnostics" after a technical noun (plasma, X-ray, medical device). Pushes toward "agnostics"/"agnostic" continuations.
result.label: ' di' piece before "agnostics"

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, used, as, from) in history-of-civilization or ancient-mathematics text, where the next word is likely "ancient", "Egypt", "Greek" or "connection". Silent on many "of" tokens, such as "development of". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words before ancient-history terms

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase tokens (commas, "ongoing", "resilient", "in", "the") in abstract academic or organizational prose about education, leadership and policy. Peaks are mixed, and it is silent on commas in other contexts.

result.description: Fires on the word " Old" in "Old English" (and similar historical language-stage names like Old French/Norse), in texts about the history of English. Members mostly detect " Old" or period words like Middle/Norman.

result.description: Fires mostly on commas inside long lists of single abstract nouns (values, fields, skills) where the list continues, e.g. "integrity, honesty, loyalty". Silent on commas after adjectives or in non-list clauses. Occasionally fires on ' each' or ' of'.
result.label: Comma in noun lists

result.description: Fires weakly on assorted function words (and, comma, or, is, a) mid-sentence in expository technical text, often in geodesy, mapping and navigation passages. Peaks are inconsistent and it is silent on many 'and' tokens. Logits are mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' of', ' are', ' is', 'sub', 'ological') in expository academic text, with no dominant token. It is silent on many ' of' contexts, and the evidence doesn't show what separates them. The circuit is diffuse and weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires mainly on " of" in the title-like phrase "The Age of" (Discovery/Exploration/Enlightenment) at document start, and on "gam" in gametes/gametophyte. Silent on " of" in ordinary phrases like "era of" or "period of".

result.description: Fires on the capitalized logical operators AND / OR (e.g. "NOT (A AND B)", "AND (∧), OR") in text about logic, Boolean operations and connectives. Members are mostly logic-topic detectors.
result.label: Capitalized logical AND/OR operators

result.description: Fires on " the" right after a causal verb or connector (led to, resulted in, responsible for, contributed to, and) where a nominalized process noun follows (the formation/creation/degradation of). Silent on " the" after locative prepositions like "in the".
result.label: "the" before causal outcome nouns

result.description: Fires on nouns for logical claims, such as "argument(s)", "statements" and "assertions", in texts about logic, proofs and mathematical reasoning. Members detect logic and reasoning context and the word "argument".
result.label: Logical argument/statement nouns in logic texts

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (of, the, that, their, a) and word pieces in abstract academic prose, mid-phrase before a noun. Silent on many ' of' tokens, and the evidence doesn't show what separates them. Weak, diffuse circuit.
result.label: Scattered function words in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on " the" directly after a verb like highlighted, demonstrated, illustrates, revealed, or a phrase like "reminder of" or "testament to", where an abstract noun (consequences, challenges, importance) is expected next. Silent on " the" after plain "of".
result.label: "the" after highlighting/demonstrating verbs

result.description: Fires on the plural nouns or labels naming the bodies in the zeroth law of thermodynamics (' systems', ' objects', ' B' in "system A and B") when two or more systems are in thermal contact. Silent on 'systems' in generic property statements.
result.label: Thermal-equilibrium systems being paired

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Sp"/" sp" (Spelling, spices, spending, spin), a split-off beginning of a longer word. Predicts continuations like "elling", "anning", "atial", "ices". Silent on other S-words such as Series.

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' perce' in perceive/perceived/perception, mostly after "is/was/be/people", and predicts the suffix 'ived'/'iving'. Members are mostly ' perce' detectors plus similar prefixes like surv, rev, pract.
result.label: ' perce' prefix of perceive

result.description: Fires on 'opol' in "geopolitical" and on " that" after "culinary technique/cooking method" (relative clause introducing a description). Mixed peaks across two unrelated contexts; weaker hits on other science word pieces.
result.label: geopol- piece and 'technique that'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas in lists, ' of', ' the', ' a', ' with') in expository academic or technical prose. The peaks share no single token and the contrast evidence is mixed, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the 'uz' piece in "fuzzy" (f|uz|zy), mainly in fuzzy logic/sets/relations text. Members are mostly 'uz' detectors from earlier layers; it predicts the following 'zy'.
result.label: 'uz' in "fuzzy"

result.description: Fires on varied function words (are, in, is, and, -ively) in text about computer memory hierarchy and caches, where the next word would be a memory/cache term. Silent on "are" in chemistry/physics text. Members are cache and memory topic detectors.
result.label: Function words in memory-hierarchy text

result.description: Fires on the 'D' in "3D" (also "dimensional" in "three-dimensional"), in contexts about 3D modeling, printing and graphics. Members are mostly 'D' detectors. The contrast text lacks the token.
result.label: 3D 'D' token

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (a, the, and, to, 's, include, by) in technical or engineering-style text, mainly where a noun like a process or quantity is expected next. Logits favor words like high, rapid, break. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces of long adjectives like "multif-ac-eted" (mostly 'ac', also 'et') and 'pre' in "unprecedented", where the word is still incomplete. Mostly one word, multifaceted, in essay-style text.
result.label: multifaceted / unprecedented word-piece

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (of, by, with, using, later) in texts about writing systems, scripts, numerals and languages. The members point to scripts, alphabets and numerals, but the peaks are mixed and the same ' of' often stays silent.
result.label: Function words in writing-system text
Initial G of acronym in parentheses
result.description: Fires on the capital 'G' that begins an acronym after an opening parenthesis, as in "Geographic Information Systems (GIS)". It predicts the acronym's remaining letters. It stays silent on 'G' inside a word like ArcGIS.

Fires on the word-start piece " sav" in "savings", mostly after "cost" (cost savings), predicting the "ings" continuation. Weakly fires on other split word starts like "ir" in irradiance and "territ".
result.label: " sav" in "cost savings"

result.description: Fires mainly on " trade"/" Trade" (especially in "trade-offs") and on a few other scattered tokens like " So" in "Soil" at heading starts. Predicts "-offs" continuations. Mixed, polysemantic peaks.
result.label: trade of trade-offs, mixed

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' myth' (mostly as the start of myth-ology, myth-ological, myth-ical, myths). Members are mainly ' myth' detectors across layers. It is silent on a text about tales that doesn't use the word.
result.label: ' myth' token detector

result.description: Fires on the start of a chemistry term, such as 'P' in a polymer abbreviation like (PET) or (PLA), ' py' in pyruvate, 'Co' in CoA, or 'h' in dihydroxy. It stays quiet on 'P' at the end of ATP or RuBP.
result.label: Chemical term-initial fragment (P, py, Co)

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments of long technical or academic words, mostly the 'polit' piece in socio-political/geopolitical, also 'cio', 'mon', 'orth', 'ag' in crystal-system names. It fires where the word is incomplete and a continuation piece is expected.
result.label: Word-start fragments in academic terms

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' liv' when it begins a longer word such as livestock or livelihoods, where a continuation like 'est' or 'elihood' comes next. Weak on similar pieces like ' alg'.
result.label: ' liv' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on verbs or prepositions right after an abstract subject that introduce what it covers or how (involves, comprises, includes, by, "also called"), in definitional passages about policy, finance or social topics. Peaks are mixed and weakly consistent.
result.label: Definitional verbs introducing scope or means

result.description: Fires on ' especially' (or ' particularly') right after a copula like "is/are/becomes", as in "is especially true/important". Silent when it follows a comma introducing a noun-phrase qualifier ("..., especially for readers").
result.label: "is especially" after copula

result.description: Fires on function words (' by', ' a', ' include', commas) in explanatory text about how something functions or contributes, e.g. "it acts as [a]" or "providing [added]". Silent on passive agent "by". Evidence is mixed; the logits are weak.
result.label: Function-role slot in explanatory text

result.description: Fires mid-word on word pieces such as 'l' in "cutlery" and 'ens' in "utensil", plus occasional other mid-word pieces. It stays silent on 'l' in other words like "bowl" or "proliferation", so it needs the specific word.
result.label: Mid-word piece in cutlery/utensil

result.description: Fires on 'ification' in the "[clarification needed]" editorial tag, and on ' needed' or placeholder slots like "Case Study 2 Description..." inside bracketed annotations. Silent on 'ification' in other words (stratification, gamification).
result.label: clarification-needed bracket tag

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Mag" at the start of a word that continues as "net-" (Magnetic, Magnets), including at the start of a heading. It pushes towards continuations like "net". It stays silent on the full word "magnetic".
result.label: ' Mag' before 'net' word piece

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' of', ' for', '/', ' to', ' through') in the middle of a phrase, mostly where a noun phrase follows. Peaks are inconsistent and the target is silent on many ' the' cases, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words before noun phrase

result.description: Fires on varied function words (for, while, in, commas) in technical text about measurement, statistics and data, where the next word is likely a measure or metric term. Peaks are scattered and the contrast is inconsistent, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Function words before measure terms

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and periods in academic or technical expository text (e.g. ' its', ' and', ' the', '.'), mid-sentence where a technical noun or verb is likely next. It is silent on periods that end a sentence before a paragraph break. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Diffuse function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on a comma after an item in a list of abstract plural nouns (interests, behaviors, strategies, beliefs), where the list continues with more items and "and/or". Silent on clause-level or after-phrase commas.
result.label: Comma inside abstract-noun lists

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a clause describing a cause-and-effect change in science text (e.g. "the barrier lowers,"), where a participle like "allowing", "enhancing" or "reducing" comes next. Silent on commas before "which" or in definitions.
result.label: Comma before consequence participle

result.description: Fires on function words or modifiers (the, of, on, specific, new, essential) that follow a verb or preposition in abstract mathematical or technical prose, where a mathematical noun is expected next. Silent on many identical ' the' contexts, so the cue is unclear.
result.label: Function words before math nouns

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', possessive 's, ' its') right before a noun in computing-history text, such as operating systems, GUIs and Unix. It stays quiet on ' the' before dates or periods like "the 20…" or "the 19…".
result.label: the/'s before computing noun

result.description: Fires on ' we' as the subject right after "the way" (or "how"), as in "transformed the way we interpret...". Silent on ' we' in other clauses such as "As we move" or "we can expect". Weaker on "the way people".
result.label: 'we' after "the way"

result.description: Fires on the verb "facilitate" (facilitates/facilitating/facilitate) and similar enabling words like "allows for", where a verb is about to be followed by an object such as communication or access. Silent on other -ating words like communicating.
result.label: facilitate / enable verbs

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (contribute, the, and, 0) inside text about data normalization, scaling and standardization of features. Members are statistics and scaling topic detectors; the peak token itself is not consistent.
result.label: Data scaling/normalization text slots

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments that begin a longer word, mostly ' cap' (cap-and-trade, capillary, capability) and ' x' in 'xylem', where the next piece is a continuation. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Word-initial fragment 'cap' / 'x'

result.description: Fires on connectives (" and", " of", " including", " or") inside lists or noun phrases in war and resource-loss history text, such as "resources, including manpower and materiel". Silent on "and" after comma-separated lists in other contexts.
result.label: Connectives in wartime resource lists

result.description: Fires on the word-initial fragment ' dev' (before 'astate', 'oting', 'otional'), where the next piece completes a split word. Weaker on other incomplete word starts like ' St' in 'Stellar', 'un-im-provised'.
result.label: ' dev' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' more', ' break', ' them', ' next', 'in', 'Complete') at points where a short completion follows, mostly in customer-service or advice text. The peaks are mixed and the contrast shows ' more' silent in comparatives, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in service-advice text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and modifiers (native, for, his, complex, robust, berg) mid-phrase in technical or academic prose, where a noun or abstract concept is expected next. Silent on 'berg' in Gutenberg. Evidence is mixed and low-consistency.
result.label: Mid-phrase modifiers before abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a full clause about culture, religion or society and is followed by a trailing elaboration (e.g. "with…", "often…", "their…"). It stays quiet on commas after introductory phrases and in simple lists.
result.label: Comma after clause, before elaboration

result.description: Fires on 're, are, be, being, just after a subject (often "they/we") in verb-slot positions where a participle or adjective like aware/willing/-ing is expected next. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Copula/auxiliary before predicate complement

result.description: Fires on the capital ' N' token when it starts a new line or document, as the first letter of a word like Nuclear or Nouns. It is quiet on 'Martin' in a list of names. Next-token logits favour continuations such as 'ern', 'ray' and 'ock'.
result.label: Line-initial ' N' token

result.description: Fires on subject-position pronouns or relative words (' it', ' which', ' that') that follow a noun phrase or colon and start a clause describing what a biological system or organ does. It predicts a present-tense verb such as 'is', 'houses' or 'works'.
result.label: Relative/pronoun before verb in biology

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, and, comma, with-the) in advice-style text where a manner or quality noun is expected next, like "with the same ease/precision" or "a touch of humor". Predicts quality nouns such as wit, skill, ease.
result.label: Function words before manner/quality nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (of, the, in, and, these) in academic science text about physics, decay and vibrations. Peaks are inconsistent and it stays silent on 'of' in linguistics passages. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in physics-science prose

result.description: Fires on the word " active" when it modifies a following noun like listening, participation or engagement, in communication or teamwork text. It stays silent on some " active" tokens in similar contexts, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: ' active' before listening/participation

result.description: Fires on relative/pronoun words (" which", " it", " that") and commas that follow a described subject and begin a clause about it, where a verb like "is/has/provides" is expected. Silent on some ", which" cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Clause-linking which/it/that after subject

result.description: Fires on function words (a, the, its, this, several) and some suffix pieces in science-style text, especially physics/cosmology, where a technical noun is expected next. Logits are mixed and weak. Consistency is low.
result.label: Determiners before technical science nouns

result.description: Fires on function words (the, a, an, in, that, each) in technical statistics/math/science prose, where the next word is likely an abstract technical noun (distributions, boundaries, limits). Silent on many 'the' in other contexts. Mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in technical math/stats text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'im' inside "ferrimagnetism/ferrimagnetic", predicting a continuation like 'agnet'. It stays silent on 'im' in other words such as "mimics". Weak activation on other word pieces.
result.label: 'im' in ferrimagnetic

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' the', 'ian', ' this', ' as') in art-history and arts text, such as "against the", "Egyptian", "French". Logits favor suffix pieces like 'ite'. Silent on 'the' in corporate-governance text. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Art-context function words and suffixes

result.description: Fires on ' is' (also ' was', ' being') right after a distributive subject like "every/each X", as in "each slide is a frame". Silent on ' is' after other subjects such as "this" or abstract nouns.
result.label: 'is' after each/every subject

result.description: Fires on function words (can, or, and, to, as) in text about music and emotional or mental effects, where a mood or emotion word is likely to come next. Silent on ' can' in other topics.
result.label: Function words in music-emotion text

result.description: Fires on the verb "are"/"is" (or "rather") right after an abstract subject like "mathematical truths" in philosophy-of-mathematics text about formalism vs. Platonism, where a claim about the nature of truth follows. Silent on "are" in ordinary or logic contexts.
result.label: Copula after "mathematical truths" in formalism

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and word pieces (' an', ' of', ' for', ' the', ' and', 'ometric') in abstract academic prose, mid-phrase. Consistency is low and the contrast does not show a clear condition. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in academic prose
' execut' word-start before -ives
result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece ' execut' (as in "executives") when a noun-forming suffix like "-ives" is expected. It also fires weakly on other word starts like ' parent' and on some function words. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
Fires on the word piece ' fant' (start of "fantasy", "fantastical") when the word is mid-sentence, predicting the continuation "asy"/"astic". Silent when "fantasy" opens the text at document start.
result.label: ' fant' piece before "asy"

result.description: Fires on varied function tokens (commas, 'and', 'with', 'has', 'to') mostly inside lists or elaborations of a noun phrase in expository text; the peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse, with no clear discriminating members.
result.label: Diffuse list/connector punctuation latent

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also 'through', 'ly', 'and') in abstract academic prose, right before an abstract noun like "interplay", "emergence", "study". Silent on 'the' before dates or fixed phrases such as "on the other hand".
result.label: 'the' before abstract noun, academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ecc' (as in "ecclesiastical"), predicting a following "les…" continuation. Members include detectors of other word-start fragments (Rem, app, mon, oph) that also lead to "les"-type completions.
result.label: ' ecc' start of ecclesiastical

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like "Rec" (Enhanced Oil Recovery), "ent" in "nutrient", and "bu" in "buoyancy", in earth, soil and water science text. It is a word-piece latent that predicts continuations of those words.
result.label: Word pieces in soil/water science terms

result.description: Fires on a copula or auxiliary (was/were/is) or an adverb right after it (often, largely, heavily) in passive or descriptive statements by an abstract subject, where a participle like "conducted" or "influenced" is expected. Silent on some "was" tokens in historical narration.
result.label: Copula/adverb before passive participle

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments of a word split across tokens (' dow' in downturn, ' pu', ' cro' in crochet), plus a few LaTeX openers. Seems to mark an incomplete word start awaiting a continuation. Mixed evidence, weak faithfulness.
result.label: Word-start fragment tokens (dow, cro, pu)

result.description: Fires on the quantifier " Many" (and weakly " many"), mostly as the first word of a document or sentence, starting a subject like "Many of these…". Members include detectors of Many, Some, All, Several.
result.label: Sentence-initial "Many" quantifier

result.description: Fires on the word " informed" in "make informed (decisions)", mostly business-analysis text. Members are detectors of " informed" that push toward "decision", "choices", "consent". Weaker on other adjectives after "make", like "appropriate" or "better".
result.label: "informed" in "make informed decisions"

result.description: Fires on ' setting' (also ' set'/'sets') as a verb after a comma or relative clause, in idioms like "setting the stage", "setting new records", "setting it apart". Members are detectors of set/setting and similar verbs like laid.
result.label: verb 'setting' in idioms

result.description: Fires on ' marks' (also represents, signifies, marking) when a historical period or event is said to mark the beginning or a transition of something. Context is historical-era descriptions; the verb comes after a period or event subject.
result.label: Period 'marks' the beginning

result.description: Fires mostly on ' on' (also ' the', ' of', commas), strongest after "walking on" in the idiom-like "walking on a tight(rope)". Silent on other uses of ' on' (on the other hand, influence on). Peaks are scattered, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: 'on' after walking (tightrope)

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' right after a cooking technique name (e.g. "Steaming, a" or "Steaming is a"), where a descriptive noun phrase defining the technique comes next. Silent on ' a' in other kitchen or food sentences.
result.label: 'a' after cooking technique name

result.description: Fires on the word piece " challeng" (and the following " pos" in "challenges posed"), mainly right after "the" in "Despite the challenges..." or "address the challenges posed by". It stays silent on "challenges" after "these" or "several", or after "poses".
result.label: "the challenges posed" phrase

result.description: Fires mostly on commas separating items in a list of abstract nouns or parallel verbs (e.g. "passion, authenticity", "designing, developing"), plus some " of" tokens. Silent on commas after clauses or introductory phrases. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Commas inside lists of abstract nouns
