result.description: Fires on ' well' as the first piece of "wellbeing"/"wellness" (e.g. "mental well-being", "physical wellness"), predicting "being", "-" or "ness". Silent on "as well as" and on some "wellness programs" cases.
result.label: ' well' in wellbeing/wellness

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (' a', ',', 'with', '(') in culinary text where a list of flavors, textures or tools is being offered or described; predicts culinary terms like 'sous', 'mise'. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Culinary description function words

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ph' (also ' Ph') when it begins a word like phonetic or phonemic, mostly in linguistics text. It is silent when ' ph' starts the document. It predicts 'on' as the next piece.
result.label: ' ph' before phonetic/phonemic

result.description: Fires on ' and' that follows the object of "goes beyond / transcends / rejected traditional X", where the sentence continues with a further verb or contrast (instead, into). Silent on ordinary coordinating 'and' in lists or pairs.
result.label: 'and' after "goes beyond X"

result.description: Fires on scattered word pieces that begin a word or phrase and need a continuation, such as ' rad' (radar), ' exhib' (exhibitions), ' up', and sometimes ' the'. The peak tokens are mixed and the evidence is weak; the logits favour word-start continuations like 'rag' and ' situ'.
result.label: Mixed incomplete word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and fragments (the, with, used, _, of) in passages about origins or early history of science and ideas. It predicts source-like nouns (base, root, source). Peaks are inconsistent, and the same token is often silent elsewhere.
result.label: Function words in origins-of-science text

result.description: Fires on "between" and nearby function words (the, to, and) in phrases like "relationship/connection between the nervous system and...", mostly in biology or science text. Silent on "between" after some nouns like interplay or interactions, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Relationship-between in science text

result.description: Fires on the prefix " non" and the hyphen right after "non" (non-linear, non-homogeneous, non-normal), predicting the word piece that follows. It stays silent on hyphens in other compounds like second-order or large-scale.
result.label: "non" prefix and its hyphen

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, 'of', 'to', 'the', 'stone', 'back') in academic or expository text, mid-phrase where a noun or compound continuation is expected. No single token dominates; the same comma often stays silent.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function tokens

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (commas in lists, ' loss' in "lossless", ' is' in "isomerism") where a word or list item is followed by a continuation. Silent on many commas in similar lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Mixed commas and word-piece splits

result.description: Fires on abstract head nouns like "introduction", "use", "integration", "analysis", "models", "approach", often as subject of a sentence. Predicts technical modifier-like next tokens (machine, model, cell, language). Members are weak and mixed.
result.label: Abstract process nouns (introduction, use)

result.description: Fires on " brought" (occasionally " bringing") when a historical or abstract cause, like the Industrial Revolution, an era or an invention, is the subject, as in "brought about". Members are detectors of bring-forms that predict "about" or "forth".
result.label: "brought" (about) after a causal subject

result.description: Fires on the word piece " expl" when it begins a word like exploration, explorer or explored. Members are mostly " expl" detectors. It stays silent on some " expl" tokens, such as at text start, and the contrast doesn't clearly show why.
result.label: ' expl' start of exploration

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: 'tr' word pieces (Altruism, filtrate) plus function or modifier words like 'and', 'shared', 'including', 'necessary' that precede a noun in a list or phrase. Evidence is mixed and low-consistency.
result.label: Mixed 'tr' piece and connector words

result.description: Fires mostly on ' government' (also party, company, annual, school) when it is a modifier noun right before a record-type noun like reports, publications, statistics. Predicts such nouns next. Silent on 'government' used as a standalone subject.
result.label: Government as modifier before reports

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'dep', mostly in 'interdependence', and sometimes on 'lim' or 'cipl' (interdisciplinary), when a longer word is partly spelled out. It predicts the suffix 'inary' or 'end'.
result.label: 'dep' piece in interdependence

result.description: Fires on the word piece "res" after a hyphen in compounds like "earthquake-res|istant" and "heat-res|istant", predicting "istant". It stays silent on "res" inside other words, such as "theatres".
result.label: hyphenated "-res" before "istant"

result.description: Fires on 'ights' in "insights" and on " insight", mainly in "gain/provide valuable insight(s) into ..." phrasing. It predicts " into". It is silent when "insights" is a subject or sits sentence-finally.
result.label: insight(s) before 'into'

result.description: Fires on the "t" of negative contractions (wouldn't, won't, don't, can't) and on " not" after a modal or auxiliary, before a verb like mind, want or notice. Silent on stray apostrophe-t fragments and word-internal t.
result.label: Negation n't before a verb

result.description: Fires on 'ing' ending of adapt/adjust (also ' adapt', ' adjust' themselves) in communication-skill text, where an object like "one's approach" or "to" follows. Silent on 'ing' in other verbs such as developing, maintaining, respecting.
result.label: adapt/adjust verb, especially -ing

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' bro' when it is likely to continue as "broader", mostly after "provides/offering/providing" in academic text. It pushes the next token towards 'ader'. Weakly active on other word-start pieces.
result.label: ' bro' predicting 'broader'

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a clause about developments or advancements in a field, e.g. "advancements in linear algebra,". It predicts an elaborating continuation such as "particularly", "including", "such as" or "leading to". It stays quiet on commas after time phrases or in other constructions.
result.label: Comma after developments-in-field clause

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' d' when it begins "dough" in baking or pastry text (rolling, folding, layering dough). It predicts 'ough' as the next piece. Members are mostly ' d' detectors plus baking-context members.
result.label: ' d' starting "dough" in baking

result.description: Fires on ' not' right after a copula like "is" or "are" (e.g. "Wine is not just..."). It predicts hedging continuations such as only, just, merely, solely, necessarily. It stays silent on "do not" and "let's not".
result.label: "is not" before just/only/solely

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' to', ' of', ' the', 'net', 'gold', 'dollars') in expository passages, with no single dominant token. Members are mostly generic function-word hubs, so the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks in expository text

result.description: Fires on function words (how, to, of, that, more) mid-sentence in explanatory text defining properties like permeability, resistance or toughness. It seems to anticipate a property-related continuation. Silent on 'how' in philosophy contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in physical-property definitions

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "the state" in descriptions of entangled particles, where the next word is "another/the other/its partner". It stays silent on other 'of' uses like "heart of" or "flow of".
result.label: "state of" before another particle

result.description: Fires on " the" right after "at" when it begins a scale phrase like "at the individual/national/macro level". Silent on "the" after other prepositions. Members detect "at" plus level-words and push toward "level".
result.label: "the" after "at" (level phrases)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (' of', '.', ' the', 'ing') in abstract academic or essay prose about art, science and math. Silent on many other ' of' tokens, and the evidence does not show what separates them.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a historical-period phrase, mainly ' era' and ' period' after a period name (the Classical era, late medieval period). Silent on some 'era' tokens, e.g. after 'This' or 'pre-recorded', so the cause is unclear.
result.label: Historical era/period noun

result.description: Fires on the mid-name word piece of philosopher names ('ot' in Aristotle, 'ir' in Peirce), predicting the name's continuation such as 'le', 'elian', 'eles'. It stays silent when 'ot' is a separate word start or in other words like dichotomy.
result.label: Aristotle/Peirce name-piece mid-token

result.description: Fires mostly on "BI" in the acronym "(BI)" right after "Business Intelligence". Weaker on a few other tokens like " unique". Members detect "B" pieces, "intelligence", and acronym-forming technical title phrases.
result.label: BI acronym after Business Intelligence

result.description: Fires on ' both' right after a preposition (in/for/to both), where a paired "both X and Y" is expected. It is silent on ' both' after a verb or "are", as in "are both effective".
result.label: 'both' after a preposition

result.description: Fires on ' in' right after "ways" when a relative clause follows ("the ways in which..."). It predicts "which" or "whom" next. It stays silent on ordinary ' in' after nouns such as "aids in" or "found in".
result.label: "ways in which" preposition

result.description: Fires on the word " rapid" (and weakly on similar speed words like swift, fast, or "unprecedented") before nouns such as pace, growth, industrialization or technological change. It pushes the next token toward those nouns.
result.label: "rapid" before change/growth nouns

result.description: Fires on ' integer' (also ' number'/' numbers') as a noun in math text about primes, modular arithmetic and number theory, e.g. "for any integer a". Predicts variable names like p, n, m.
result.label: integer in number theory statements

result.description: Fires on the word " nuclear" (and "lear" in "Nuclear") when it is followed by something like reactor, power, facilities or weapons. It pushes the next token toward reactor and facility words.
result.label: ' nuclear' predicting reactor/facility

result.description: Fires on ' the' in abstract expository text, where it starts an abstract noun phrase after a preposition, comma or conjunction (e.g. "through the meticulous…"). Predicts nouns like use, inclusion, incorporation. Silent on 'the' before story or author subjects.
result.label: 'the' before abstract process nouns

result.description: Fires on the token ' interval' in statistics text (confidence interval, interval estimation, interval-level), and predicts continuations like 'estimation', 'estimates' or 'width'. Members are mostly ' interval' detectors plus statistics context.
result.label: ' interval' in statistics

result.description: Fires on function words (a, the, any, in, for, various) in abstract expository text about discourse, argument, communication and philosophy, where the next word is likely "debate/discussion/exchange". Silent on the same words in other contexts. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words before debate/discussion nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cos' (also ' atmos') when it begins a word like cosmic, cosmos or cosine, and pushes the next token towards 'mic', 'mos' and similar continuations. Mostly seen in cosmology text.
result.label: ' cos' word-start before -mic/-mos

result.description: Fires mostly on ' d' in "moral/ethical dilemmas" (predicting "ilemma"), with weaker firing on some 'and'/'the' tokens. Silent on "the dilemma" singular after "the". Mixed, low-consistency circuit.
result.label: ' d' of moral dilemmas

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns ("that", "which") and modals ("can", "may") following a noun naming a problem, risk or cause, where a causal or effect verb is expected next (indicate, trigger, cause). Silent on some "that" uses, such as complementizers.
result.label: Relative 'that'/modal before effect verb

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and determiners (' all', ' these', ',', ' stored', ' respective') in abstract expository text on economics, finance and physics, mid-clause before a noun. Pushes toward economic nouns weakly. Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (mostly ' and', also ' on', ' in', word pieces) in academic or abstract text, often after a topic term in a title-like pair such as "Uses and Gratifications". Silent on many other ' and' uses. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Academic term-pair 'and' connector
Unprecedented ending 'ented', predicts levels
result.description: Fires on the final piece 'ented' of "unprecedented" (weaker on 'led' in "unparalleled"), pushing the next token toward 'levels', 'amounts', 'scale'. Silent on unrelated text.

Fires on linking prepositions (to, by, with, saw) after a verb or participle that attributes a development to a cause, such as "thanks to", "driven by", "transformed by", "saw ... with", in tech-history prose. It predicts "the advent/development of" style nouns.
result.label: Causal prepositions before "advent of"

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' in', also ' the', ' of') right after phrases about Columbus, voyages and exploration of the Americas, where a year or place is expected next. Silent on ' in' in other contexts, such as 'changes in'.
result.label: Function words in Columbus exploration text

result.description: Fires on the 'l' piece in "pro-l" as in proliferation, prolific, proliferative, and predicts the continuations 'ifer' or 'ific'. It needs the preceding 'pro' piece.
result.label: 'l' in pro-liferation / prolific

result.description: Fires on the token ' public' as a noun or adjective in the sense of the public sector, public at large or public goods, typically after "the". It stays silent in "public order" and "public-private", and predicts words like good, interest, eye and sector.
result.label: ' public' as in public sector

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (of, type, such, retain, closing paren) in geology text about volcanoes, where the next word is likely a volcano term like ash, lava or volcano. Silent on ' of' in other earth-science contexts.
result.label: Volcano-text slot before volcanic terms

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation ('.', ' of', ' and', ' for', ' or') in expository text about water quality, monitoring and science, often where a subject seems dropped. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in technical expository text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' En' when it follows 'the' or 'Age of' and starts 'Enlightenment' (or similar En- words). It stays silent when ' En' starts the text. It pushes the next token toward 'light'.
result.label: En- in "the Enlightenment"

result.description: Fires on the article " an" (and the "an" piece in words like "anaerobic"), where the next word starts with a vowel. Members detect " An"/" an" and push vowel-initial continuations. Silent on "an" in "the anaerobic" contrast.
result.label: Article "an" before vowel word

result.description: Fires on emotion nouns (love, hope, happiness, joy) listed as items in a series of emotions, e.g. "basic emotions such as happiness, sadness". Silent when "love" is a verb ("I just love to"). Predicts further emotion words.
result.label: Emotion nouns in lists

result.description: Fires on function words (the, an, a, from, hyphen) in technical or explanatory text, mostly where a noun phrase is about to start. Silent on many ' the' tokens, and the evidence doesn't show what separates them.
result.label: Function words before technical noun phrase

result.description: Fires on the 'dis' piece in "inter|dis|ciplinary" (also 'if' in "mult|if|aceted"), predicting 'cipl'. It stays silent when 'dis' follows a hyphen with no 'inter' before it.
result.label: 'dis' in interdisciplinary

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Ro" when it begins "Role" in repeated "The Role of X in History" essay-title lists. It predicts continuations of the word such as "le", "ots" and "oted".
result.label: " Ro" in "The Role of"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'vol' in "ever-evolving" (e-vol-ving), right before 'ving' is predicted. Weak activation on other mid-word pieces like 'lus' and 'frontier'.
result.label: 'vol' in "ever-evolving"

result.description: Fires on the 'r' token in "wide-r|anging", where a split-up word is being completed, and pushes the next token towards "anging". It is silent on 'r' in other words such as "neutrino". Members detect 'r', ' arr' and ' R' word-starts.
result.label: 'r' in wide-ranging

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (create, communicate, validate, "creation of") in text about prototyping and product development, where the next word is likely "prototype", "mock", or "feedback". It stays silent on "creating" in general engineering text.
result.label: Prototyping verbs predicting prototype/mock

result.description: Fires on "to" in "due to" (also "because of", "faced", "encountered") where a cause or problem is introduced, predicting negative nouns like "poor", "limitations", "lack". Silent on some "due to" cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Causal "due to" before problems

result.description: Fires on 'ound' in "prof-ound" when it follows "have/had a" and predicts an impact/effect noun ("had a profound impact"). Silent when "profound" is followed by "-ly" or used attributively elsewhere (e.g., "profound symmetry").
result.label: profound before impact noun

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and modifiers (' relatively', ' the', ' of', ' and') in expository text, mid-phrase where an adjective or noun is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse function-word slot before modifier

result.description: Fires on nouns for surrounding setting or circumstances (landscape, environment, conditions, threats, genre) in business/analysis text, often ending a noun phrase before a clause like "within which". Silent on "landscape" in a literary sense.
result.label: Surrounding environment/conditions nouns in analysis

result.description: Fires on the verb ' mirror' (mirror/mirrors/mirrored) meaning "reflect or resemble", with an abstract subject such as music, poetry or trends. Weaker on similar verbs like matches or rivals. Predicts an object like "those", "life" or "society".
result.label: verb 'mirror' meaning reflect

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' vis' at the start of a split word, mainly in viscous/viscosity/viscoelasticity in fluid-mechanics text. It predicts continuations like 'cos', 'c', 'cid'. Silent on other fluid text without this token.
result.label: ' vis' piece before 'cosity'
'al' piece in "anomalies"
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'al' inside "anom-al-ies" (anomalies), predicting a suffix like 'ies'. It stays silent on 'al' in other words such as detrimental, organismal, reveal. Also weakly fires on 'aly' in "anomaly".

Fires on the word piece ' sh' when it begins a verb like shaping, shaped or shifting, mostly after "role in" or "been" in abstract academic text. It predicts continuations such as 'aping' and 'ifting'.
result.label: ' sh' start of shaping/shifting

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' l' when it begins the word "lens/lenses" (e.g. after "converging", "convex", "the"). Pushes the next token toward "enses"/"ens". Silent on other text without this split word.
result.label: ' l' starting "lenses"
' difficult' as predicate adjective
result.description: Fires on the word " difficult", mostly as a predicate adjective after "it/be/make it" (e.g. "find it difficult to"). Weaker on related words like "impossible" and "unknown". Members are detectors of difficult/easy/impossible-type adjectives.
Fires on the period ending a person's name (e.g. "Sergey Brin.", "Tim Cook.") in a list of names, one per line. Silent on periods after topic or subject headings in similar line-by-line lists.
result.label: Period after person name in list

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces ' facil', ' necess', ' precip' (also ' neces', ' prior', ' digit') where the next piece is likely "itate/itated". It predicts the "-itate" suffix continuation.
result.label: Stems before "-itate" suffix

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, to, involves, not) inside academic explanations of media influence and public opinion, where the next word is likely a media-effect noun or verb. Silent on 'the' in physics/materials text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Function words in media-theory text
"According to" sentence-opening 'to'
result.description: Fires mostly on ' to' in "According to" at the start of a sentence or document, where a source or person is expected next. It also fires weakly on other prepositions, such as "complicated by". It stays silent on ' to' in other uses.

Fires on varied function words and nouns (" of", " type", " function", " loops") in technical math/science text, often right after a noun like "numbers of the second/first kind". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Math terms: "numbers of the first kind"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' clar' (start of clarity, clarification, clarinet), predicting continuations like 'ity', 'ification', 'inet'. Silent in one case ("provides clarity"), so the condition is not clear.
result.label: ' clar' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on function words (into, involves, is, on) right after "dataset" or "cross-validation" in explanations of k-fold splitting, where the next word is likely partition/subsets/k. Silent on "into" in other contexts like "data into manageable parts".
result.label: k-fold dataset splitting connectors

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectives (and, or, as, than, commas) and some words like "improved" in technical expository text. Peaks are inconsistent and the target is silent on many 'and' tokens in lists. The pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered connectives in technical prose

result.description: Fires on word-initial pieces ' Mes', ' Pale', ' Ne' that begin era or region names (Paleolithic, Mesozoic, Neolithic, Mesopotamia), predicting a continuation like 'ol', 'oz', 'o'. Mostly in prehistory or geology text.
result.label: Mes-/Pale-/Ne- era-name prefixes

result.description: Fires on " due" in causal "due to" after a predicate (is largely due, effective due, doubt due). Members are mostly " due" detectors plus words like related/attributed. Silent on the contrast text, which lacks " due".
result.label: causal ' due' (due to)

result.description: Fires on the word " reaction" when used as a modifier before another noun in chemistry text (reaction mechanisms, rates, conditions, intermediates). It predicts kinetics-type continuations such as rates, mechanisms, k, dynamics.
result.label: " reaction" as noun modifier

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'voir' in "reservoir" in petroleum/reservoir engineering text, with weaker firing on subsurface/groundwater word-ends ('face', 'water'). Predicts physical-property nouns such as depth, pressure, flow.
result.label: reservoir 'voir' in petroleum text
Social protection/welfare scheme noun
result.description: Fires on the last word of a social-policy compound such as "social protection" or "social welfare" (also safety, security). It predicts policy-program nouns next, like schemes, measures, programs and policies.

Fires on varied tokens (' to', 'RT', 'ci', ' sound') inside definitions of reverberation/decay time ("time for sound to decay by 60 decibels"). Silent on ' to' in unrelated history/humanities text. Circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: Reverberation decay-time definition tokens

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (additional, often, adding, describe, its) inside explanations of English grammar, especially participles and modifiers. Members are grammar/sentence-topic latents; it is silent on spelling-rule text.
result.label: Grammar explanation of participles/modifiers

result.description: Fires on the word piece " fol" when it begins "folding"/"fold", mostly after "protein" or in other folding contexts. It pushes the next token toward "ding", "ds" or "ded". Silent on unrelated dough-layering text.
result.label: " fol" start of folding

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' subt' (start of subtle, subtlety, subtly), with weaker activation on ' bal'/'Bal' pieces. Upstream members are mostly ' subt' detectors. It is silent when ' subt' starts the document, so it needs preceding context.
result.label: ' subt' word-piece (subtle/subtlety)

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " intr" (intrinsic, intricate, intriguing), mostly in academic or descriptive text. Predicts continuations such as "insic", "usion", "ude". Upstream members are mostly " intr" detectors.
result.label: " intr" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word pieces ' flash' (as in flashbacks) and ' layer' (as in layered, layering) that begin a compound word, mostly in storytelling or literary-technique text. It predicts word continuations like -back, -ed and cards.
result.label: flash- / layer- word starts

result.description: Fires on word pieces completing sense words like "sc-ent", "sm-ell", "arom-a", especially in smell/taste/flavor text; predicts suffixes such as "-ally" or "profiles". Silent on "ent" in unrelated words like "accentuating".
result.label: Scent/smell word-piece endings

result.description: Fires on function words (of, how, with, on, by) in geography-themed academic text, especially in definitions of the field of geography. It pushes toward spatial, regional and mapping words. The same words are silent in other humanities texts.
result.label: Function words in geography text

result.description: Fires on ' community' used as a modifier of a following noun (community-based, community-building, community engagement), predicting words like building, life, planning. Silent on 'global community' as a standalone noun.
result.label: community as modifier

result.description: Fires on chemistry/food-science noun pieces such as ' carbon', ' ice', ' acid', 'gen', and word-ending 'ter' (butter), and promotes continuations like ' cub', 'cre', ' dio'. Mixed tokens; the strongest members are carbon detectors.
result.label: Carbon/ice chemistry and food nouns

result.description: Fires on the token ' advent', mostly in "the advent of ..." phrases about a new technology or development. Upstream members are mainly ' advent' detectors that also promote "-ure" continuations, as in "adventure".
result.label: ' advent' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece "cular" completing "molecular" (also "molescular"), in chemistry text. It predicts structure-like nouns such as stability, structure, geometry and interactions.
result.label: "cular" in molecular

result.description: Fires on the piece 'oe' inside "onomatopoeia" (also in words like thermoelectric), where the token is a mid-word fragment. Members are mostly 'oe' detectors. Logits are not informative.
result.label: 'oe' in onomatopoeia

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' published', ' between', ' are', quote marks) in academic text about logic, mathematics and philosophy, such as Frege and Sinn. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Logic/math academic prose, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the numeric prefixes " multi" / "Multi" and " tri" at the start of a compound word, before the rest of the word (multi-player, multiples, triangles, trials). It predicts continuations like "plex", "ples", "part".
result.label: multi- / tri- word-start prefix

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'omet' (also 'met', 'imet', 'geomet') inside words like econometrics, biometrics, symmetry, organometallic, where the next piece is likely 'rics', 'rical' or 'ries'.
result.label: 'omet' piece before -rics/-rical

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' Pro' (Prophase), ' De', ' N', ' F' that begin a longer word, apparently predicting a continuation such as 'ponents'. Silent on ' N' in other names (Art Nouveau). Members are generic, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Word-initial fragments like Pro-, N, F

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after "during" (also "in the", "of the") when a time period or era is expected next, like "during the dot-com…" or "during the early…". Predicts period words such as early, late, mid, new.
result.label: 'the' before a time period

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'dis' in "interdisciplinary" or "transdisciplinary", predicting 'cipl'. It also fires on 'le' in the title "Role of...". Members are mostly 'dis' detectors. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: 'dis' in interdisciplinary (plus 'Role')

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' r' (also ' R') as a separate token that begins a word like "ratios" or "rho", often right after a space-split or preceding word. It pushes the next token toward continuations such as "ati", "ho" and "anging".
result.label: Split word-initial ' r' token

result.description: Fires on the verb " involves" (also " involve") after an abstract process noun subject like "analysis", "assessment" or "approach" in business or analytic text. It predicts a following action verb such as collect, comparing or measuring.
result.label: " involves" after process-noun subject

result.description: Fires on odd, fragmentary tokens: broken byte pieces, 'ampa', ' Germania', 'overline', ' où', Cyrillic fragments, 'std'. No shared meaning; the pattern looks like rare or mid-word pieces, and the logits are mixed.
result.label: Rare fragment tokens, mixed

result.description: Fires on example-introducing words (like, as, include, including) that follow "services" in ecosystem-services text, right before a list of examples such as provisioning or regulating services (food, water, climate regulation). Silent on "as" in other uses.
result.label: Ecosystem services example-list introducers

result.description: Fires on the word " dark" (occasionally " bright", " white") as a modifier, especially before suffixes like -er/-est/-ened or nouns like matter and energy. Predicts continuations such as 'ened', ' sides', ' matter'. Nearly all members are dark detectors.
result.label: ' dark' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' rather' in the contrastive "X, rather than Y" construction, where ' than' is expected next. It stays silent on "but rather" (no "than" follows).
result.label: "rather than" contrast

result.description: Fires on ' to' in a date range "from YEAR to ..." right after a year, where an end year or "the present/recent" is expected. Silent on ' to' as a preposition or infinitive marker.
result.label: "to" in year ranges

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece " ped" and "agog" in "pedagogy/pedagogical" in education text, with weaker firing on scattered function words like "virtue" (of), "for", and "as". Predicts word continuations such as "agog".
result.label: pedagogy word pieces (ped/agog)

result.description: Fires on the verb stem " discuss" right after a document-part subject like "section" or "part" (e.g. "section discusses"), where the next token is a verb suffix such as "es". Silent when a different verb follows "section".
result.label: "section discuss(es)" verb stem

result.description: Fires on word endings of negative-leaning evaluative adjectives (confrontational, offensive, deceptive, antagonistic, disingenuous) describing how behaviors are perceived in cross-cultural communication. Silent on positive 'constructive/productive/attentive' -ive endings.
result.label: Negative perception adjective suffixes

result.description: Fires at the end of a decade or period noun phrase (e.g. "1930s", a period name followed by a comma or parenthesis), where a verb like "witnessed", "saw" or "marked" is predicted next. It is silent on "1970s" inside mid-sentence prepositional phrases.
result.label: Period subject awaiting "witnessed/saw"
' role' after "play a ... "
result.description: Fires on " role" (or " roles") in the idiom "play(s) a significant/crucial/important role", after the verb "play" and an adjective. It stays silent on "The role of..." where there is no "play".

Fires on the word " real" (or " Real") as a word or word start, in "real numbers", "real analysis", "realism", "realms". Predicts continuations like "ms", "ism", " analysis", " numbers". Mostly strong in mathematical text.
result.label: ' real' token (real numbers/realm)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and commas (',', ' the', ' as', ' are', ' to', ' how') mid-sentence in expository text, often after statistics or process verbs. Logits favour adjectives like 'past', 'current', 'available', 'enough'. Evidence is diffuse and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Diffuse mid-sentence function words

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (" of", " the", "classify", "distinguish") in knot-theory text where the next word is likely "knot"/knot invariant names (Jones, Alexander). Silent on " of" after "understanding" in general math text.
result.label: Predicts knot terms in knot text

result.description: Fires on the prefix ' un' as a standalone token that starts a negated or reversed word (unlock, uncover, unravel, unmet). It predicts word-stem continuations such as 'cover', 'lock', 'read', 've'.
result.label: ' un' prefix before verb/adjective stem

result.description: Fires on connector tokens (such as, including, colon, of, and) right after a mention of "benefits", where a list of benefits comes next. Predicts words like reduced, increased, improved.
result.label: Connector introducing list of benefits

result.description: Fires on ' intellectual' as an adjective in historical or cultural-era text (Renaissance, periods of intellectual and cultural activity), predicting curiosity, awakening, energy. Silent when it opens a text with no preceding context.
result.label: ' intellectual' in cultural-history context

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, and, their, by, for) after abstract nouns or verbs in expository text, where a noun phrase continues. Silent on 'of' after "understanding/use/processing". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Function words after abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verbs (the, of, to, that, retain, keep) mid-clause in expository text, where a noun or content word is expected next. Silent on "the" after "to" or "similar to". Evidence is mixed and the circuit unfaithful.
result.label: Mid-clause function words before noun

result.description: Fires on the word " distribution" (spatial, economic, or sales-channel sense), mostly after "the" or an adjective. It pushes toward continuations like "al", "patterns", "channels" and "networks". Members are mostly " distribution" detectors.
result.label: ' distribution' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' for' (sometimes ' of'/' to') right after a benefit noun like "happiness" or "benefit", where a beneficiary comes next (everyone, society, all, both). Silent on ' for' after verbs or phrases like "allows for" and "aim for".
result.label: ' for' after benefit noun, beneficiary next

result.description: Fires on connecting words (mostly ' of', also commas and '-ing' pieces) in abstract, environmental or technical expository text, where the next word is a resource, substance or process noun. It stays silent on ' of' after some nouns like influx, surge or distribution.
result.label: ' of' before substance or process nouns

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, and, to, from) in academic explanatory text about biology and language study, where the next word is likely a field-specific noun. Silent on the same words in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is poor.
result.label: Function words in science/linguistics exposition

result.description: Fires on the 'R' of the abbreviations VR and AR (virtual/augmented reality), mostly when the abbreviation is spelled out in parentheses or used as a technology term. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: R in VR/AR abbreviations

result.description: Fires mostly on " stem" in "pluripotent stem cell" and similar biology text, plus scattered tokens in cell/biology passages where a cell-related noun is likely next. Silent on "neural stem" in the contrast. Predicts cell-type continuations.
result.label: Stem cell biology token before "cell"

result.description: Fires on the last word of a technical noun-phrase term, such as "signal processing", "transportation management" or "information processing", where the phrase names a field or system. It is silent on some "management" cases, such as database or risk management. It weakly predicts nouns like "landscape" or "framework".
result.label: Technical compound-term final noun

result.description: Fires on ' has'/' have' right after an abstract subject noun like "Music" or "symbolism" in essay-style text about culture and art, predicting perfect-tense continuations ("has always", "has long", "been"). Silent on 'has' after "individuals".
result.label: has/have after abstract cultural subject

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ('ible' in irreversible, 'isions' in collisions, 'that', 'their', 'processes') in physics text about entropy and irreversibility, where a plural noun like processes or steps is expected next. Silent on 'ible' in 'audible'.
result.label: Entropy/irreversibility physics text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verb pieces (' the', ' has', ' requires', 'ing', ' all') in technical expository text, mostly where a verb or object is about to follow. Peaks are inconsistent. Logits weakly favor 'ret'/'reading'/'returning'.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on ' the' after origin phrases such as "derived from", "originating from", "dating back to", "roots in", where a nationality, era or source is expected next. Stays silent on ' the' after other prepositions or verbs.
result.label: 'the' after origin-from phrases
Bab- in Babylonian
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Bab' at the start of "Babylon/Babylonian", mostly in math and history text, and pushes the next token towards 'yl'. Members are mostly ' Bab' detectors.

Fires on connectives (and, or, comma, as, whereas) right after "Type I" or "Type II error" in hypothesis-testing text, where the next word is likely "Type" or "false". Silent on "and" in other statistics lists.
result.label: Connectives after Type I/II error

result.description: Fires on the token ' research' as a noun, usually after an adjective or possessive (earlier, pioneering, original research). Pushes the next token toward 'ers', institutions, facilities and 'conducted'. Members are mostly ' research' detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: ' research' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' it' (also 'model', 'concept') as the subject pronoun of a main clause that follows a concessive or contrastive clause ("Although it...", "While X was developed, it..."), predicting a verb like "still", "fallen", "wouldn't".
result.label: Subject 'it' after concessive clause

result.description: Fires on the word "board" (or "Board") when it means a corporate governing board, as in "Board of Directors", "board members", "board independence". Only weakly fires on "cutting board". Predicts room, members, composition, independence.
result.label: Corporate board token

result.description: Fires on ' that' (occasionally ' which') as a relative pronoun after a plural event noun in historical or military text, like wars, battles or tensions. It is silent on 'that' after other nouns such as tapestry, kingdoms or anxiety.
result.label: Relative 'that' after historical events

result.description: Fires on plural noun endings (funds, expenditures, challenges, impacts, benefits, earnings) in finance/economics-style abstract text, mostly on nouns for gains, costs or losses. Predicts words like 'versus', 'against', 'losses', 'faced'. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Plural cost/benefit nouns in economics text

result.description: Fires on forms of the verb "draw" (draws, drawing, draw), especially in the figurative sense "draws on/upon", "drawing from", "draw attention/connections". Predicts continuations like upon, from, parallel, connections.
result.label: verb "draw" (draws on/from)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Cal' when it begins a longer word, mostly in 'Calvin'/'Calvinist', predicting 'vin'. Weaker on other word-initial fragments such as ' Monte' and ' da'.
result.label: ' Cal' as start of Calvin

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' em' when it starts a longer word, most strongly in "fosters em|pathy" and also em|otion, em|issions, em|blem. It pushes the next token toward path, otion, anci.
result.label: ' em' word-start piece (empathy)

result.description: Fires on adjective-ending suffixes like -ized/-ined/-ated inside a noun phrase after "a/an", where a noun such as system, approach, or form is expected next. Silent on -ized verbs (emphasized, prioritized).
result.label: Adjective suffix before system/approach noun

result.description: Fires on function words like ' by', ' involves', ' one' right after "proof" or a description of proof by contradiction, where the next word is the method (assuming, contradiction). Silent on ' by' in other logic/math contexts.
result.label: proof by contradiction method words

result.description: Fires on the word piece " intr" at the start of words like intricate, intriguing, intrinsic, mostly after "the", "an" or "and". It pushes toward continuations such as "igue", "igu" and "icate". Upstream members are mostly " intr" detectors.
result.label: ' intr' word-start piece (intricate/intriguing)

result.description: Fires on "of", "the", or possessive "s" right after "measure/indicator of" or "a country's" in GDP and macroeconomics definitions, where the next word is likely an economic aggregate (total, gross, value, national). Silent on "of" in other economic phrases like "use of".
result.label: Economic measure-of / country's slot

result.description: Fires on the word " without" in mid-sentence, after a verb or clause, where it introduces a missing accompaniment (e.g. "without any", "without regard"). Predicts continuations like warning, consent, permission, modification.
result.label: ' without' after a clause

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' enc' when it starts a verb like "encapsulates" right after a subject such as "it" or "that" in abstract science or explanation text. It predicts continuations like 'aps', 'odes' and 'lose'.
result.label: ' enc' starting encapsulates-type verbs

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' inter' (prefix of interference, interrogative, interjection, interconnection) and pushes toward continuations like 'ference', 'vent', 'medi', 'dependencies'. Members are mostly ' inter' detectors across layers.
result.label: ' inter' prefix token

result.description: Fires mostly on the first word piece of a document or heading, especially ' Begin' (before 'ning') and 'Cir' (before 'cles'), plus scattered mid-word pieces and punctuation. Logits favor suffix pieces like 'ning'. Mixed evidence otherwise.
result.label: Word-start piece expecting 'ning' suffix

result.description: Fires on modal or auxiliary verbs (will, can, turn) right after a relative-clause subject like "relationships that" or "connections", where a verb such as help, allow, or enable is expected next. Common in self-help or communication advice text.
result.label: Modal verb after relative-clause subject

result.description: Fires on particles like ' away', ' off', ' back' right after a transitive verb such as peel, cut, or slice, where an object noun (layers, skin, excess) is expected next. Silent in contexts without a verb-particle construction.
result.label: Verb particle away/off after peel-cut verbs

result.description: Fires on the token " result" in the phrase "as a result (of)", also "is a result of". Members are mostly " result" detectors in earlier layers. Output pushes toward "of" and "-ant" continuations.
result.label: " result" in "a result of"

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' d' (a space-prefixed "d" that starts a longer word such as dough, dining, dishes, damping). Predicts continuations like "ough", "ining", "ishes". Silent on some ' d' before "ish" in other contexts.
result.label: Word-initial ' d' fragment

result.description: Fires on the capital word-start token ' L' when a following word piece is expected (e.g. "Dough L|ayering", "L1", "Lucas number L"). Predicts continuations like 'ayer', 'anguages', 'ingu'. Peaks all in one document type.
result.label: Capital ' L' word-start token

result.description: Fires on ' own' following a possessive (their, its, your, narrators') as in "their own words" or "its own right". Predicts words like unique, right, distinct, kind.
result.label: Possessive + 'own'

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns (that/which) or adverb pieces (elegantly) right after a mathematical or physics equation/law noun, where a verb like "describe/express/relate" is expected next. Silent on "that" in other constructions.
result.label: Relative clause after equation nouns

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'ht' in hashtag/fraught and 'qu' in earthquake, where the next piece is a suffix such as -ags or -ake(s). Logits boost 'ags', 'ake', 'akes', 'aking'.
result.label: Word-piece before -ags/-ake suffix

result.description: Fires on the article "a/an" or an evaluative adjective or word piece (essential, vital, crucial, integral) after "is/as a(n)", where a noun like factor, element, or attribute comes next. Quiet on "a" after "like" or "such as".
result.label: Adjective before role noun (is an essential...)

result.description: Fires on ' to' (also 'its' in 'traits') in natural selection text, after "tend to" or "helping them to", where survival or trait spread is described. Silent on ' to' after "contribute to" or "point to", or in "ability to".
result.label: 'to' in natural selection "tend to"

result.description: Fires on scattered modifier or comparative tokens (flexible, -er, -ier, existing, the) inside expository text about technology or language. It's diffuse and inconsistent, and silent on 'flexible' in a payment-methods context.
result.label: Scattered comparative/adjective modifiers in expository text

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' Lar' (in "Law of Large Numbers") and ' sur', where the next piece completes the word (ge, plus, pass). Mostly peaks on ' Lar' in that phrase; weaker on ' sur', ' lon'.
result.label: Word-start fragments Lar/sur

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (' to', ' which', commas, 'maintenance') inside text about software/system maintenance, where the next word is likely maintenance-related (repair, defects, maintenance). Silent on ' to' in unrelated contexts.
result.label: Maintenance-topic function words

result.description: Fires on the restrictive adverb " only" (occasionally " just") when it modifies a following verb, phrase or quantity, as in "exists only in", "touch a circle only once". It is silent in "not only". Predicts limiters like once, partially, occasionally.
result.label: restrictive "only" adverb

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' scient' (as in "scientists") when it is a split-off start of a word, and predicts the continuation 'ists' or similar suffix. Upstream members are mostly detectors of Scient/scient tokens.
result.label: ' scient' word-start token

result.description: Fires on varied function words and connectives (also, it, to, by, forms, simultaneously) in essays about how arts or activities benefit cognition and creativity, where a verb like "enhances", "fosters" or "cultivates" is expected next. Silent on "also" after "while" or "but".
result.label: Connectives before benefit verbs in arts essays

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often ' jour' (before "ney"), plus ' be', ' to', ' must' in scientific-proposition phrasing. Logits favor word-piece continuations like 'ne'/'ney'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: jour(ney) and mixed word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' and', ' a', ' given') and 'essential' in expository technical text, often after verbs like identify, establish, or are essential. Contrast shows ' the' silent in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Function words in expository definitions

result.description: Fires on plural subject nouns (mostly ' characters', also experiences, phenomena, dialects) in abstract essay-like text, where a verb is expected next. It is silent on many other ' characters' occurrences, and the contrast doesn't show why.
result.label: Plural subject noun before verb

result.description: Fires on ' both' right after a linking verb (can be both, are both, is both), where it opens a predicate like "both X and Y". Silent on 'both' after a preposition before a noun, as in "importance of both sides".
result.label: 'both' after linking verb

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after the preposition "on" (also "onto"), as in "on the surface", "on the other hand", "on the circle". Silent on ' the' after other words or prepositions. Predicts nouns like fly, part, outside.
result.label: ' the' right after "on"

result.description: Fires on the word "proof" (also "Proof", "proofs") as a noun in mathematical or logical text, e.g. "proof by contradiction" or "proof assistants". Weaker on non-math uses such as "proof public sites". Silent on general logical-argument text that lacks the word.
result.label: the word "proof"

result.description: Fires on the word "method"/"methods" (including before "-ology"), in technical or academic text about procedures or techniques. Pushes the next token toward "ologies"/"ology". Members include method-token detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: "method(s)" token, predicts -ology

result.description: Fires on function words (to, of, which, describe, denotes) right after the subject "perfect aspect" in English grammar explanations, where a description of what it expresses comes next. Quiet on the same words elsewhere in such texts.
result.label: Function words in perfect-aspect grammar text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' called', ' and', ' with', 'ian', ' political') in academic or explanatory text, where the next word is a noun-like concept (' or', ' economic'). Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' met' when it is the start of "metaphor(s)" in writing and literary-technique text, predicting the continuation 'aph'/'ap'. It stays quiet on ' met' as a whole word, such as "was met with", and on the already-complete "metaphoric".
result.label: ' met' beginning "metaphor"

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a split proper name, mainly ' Th' in "Law of Thermodynamics" and ' Lock' in "John Locke", and predicts the continuation piece (erm, e, hart). Silent on ordinary text.
result.label: Split name start: Th(ermodynamics), Lock(e)

result.description: Fires mainly on the "aving" piece in compound modifiers like "life-saving" or "energy-saving", just before a noun such as technology, equipment or practices. Weak activity on a few other tokens. The contrast text does not show what it needs.
result.label: -saving compound modifier suffix

result.description: Fires on linking words (" of", " with", " like", " as", commas) in history-of-linguistics/scholarship text where a scholar's name is expected next, e.g. "the work of", "century with". Silent on " of" in other topics.
result.label: Linking word before scholar name

result.description: Fires on the word " men" (occasionally " males") when it is used in discussions of gender roles, contrasting men and women in social or historical contexts. Upstream members detect men/women/masculine tokens.
result.label: "men" in gender-roles text

result.description: Fires on the piece "ake" in "stakeholder" (st|ake), predicting "holder"/"hold"/"owner" next. Upstream members are mostly "ake" detectors in the same word.
result.label: "ake" in stakeholder

result.description: Fires on "literature" (also poetry, "Liter-ature") when it appears as an item in a list of arts and humanities fields (art, music, drama, film). Predicts nouns like reviews, festival, schools.
result.label: literature in arts lists
'onym' piece in synonym
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'onym' after 'syn' (synonym, synonyms, synonymy, synonymology). Members are mostly 'onym' detectors across layers, plus other -onym/-ym word pieces. Weak activation on a few other word pieces.

Fires on scattered function and modifier words (' and', 'both', ' including', ' increasing', ' food') in expository text, mostly where a conjunction or modifier precedes a further item. Logits favor prefixes like multi-, inter-. Evidence is mixed and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered connectives before prefixes

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: 'ous' in "Continuous" (grammar tense headings), and scope/preposition words like 'across', 'throughout', 'including', 'of'. Evidence is mixed, with low consistency and a weak circuit fit.
result.label: Continuous 'ous' and scope prepositions

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (use, of, enables, through, where) in economics text, in slots where an economics-related word is likely to come next. Predicts economic/econom tokens. Silent on "of" in other fields like logic or philosophy.
result.label: Function words in economics text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' dis' as a prefix starting words like disruption, disaster, disorder, dislocation, discharge. It predicts continuations such as 'rupt', 'ru', 'aster'. Members are mostly ' dis' detectors.
result.label: ' dis' prefix token

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' elev' (as in elevate), and more weakly ' cultiv' (cultivate), where the next piece is likely a verb suffix like -ate/-ating. Logits favor completions such as 'fill', 'atable'.
result.label: ' elev' / ' cultiv' verb stem

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, for, their, a, by, becomes) in essay-style text about writing, literature and storytelling techniques, where a noun like text, narrative or story is expected next. Silent on some 'their' cases in linguistics text.
result.label: Function words in literary-craft prose

result.description: Fires on ' a' right after "become/remains/is" (or a noun subject) when it introduces a predicate noun like "a crucial component" or "a challenge" in abstract expository text. Stays quiet on ' a' after other verbs such as "achieving", "led to" or "necessitate".
result.label: ' a' before evaluative predicate noun

result.description: Fires on the token 'K' inside the acronym QKD (Quantum Key Distribution), after 'Q', and predicts 'D' next. Other 'K' uses, like Runge-Kutta, are handled by upstream members.
result.label: K in QKD acronym

result.description: Fires on ' and' (rarely a comma or ' or') joining plural nouns in a list of technical or academic terms, such as "keys and foreign references". It stays silent on some common pairs like "shapes and sizes". Output pushes towards ' other' and ' their'.
result.label: Conjunction joining plural technical nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (how, of, the, when, 's, periods) in expository text about the Tragedy of the Commons and public goods economics. Silent on 'how' after 'on/learn' in how-to text. Peaks are varied.
result.label: Commons/public-goods economics function words

result.description: Fires on the word " due" in causal "due to" phrases, after a noun or verb describing an effect (e.g. "occurs due to", "largely due to"). Most members are detectors of " due" itself.
result.label: causal "due" in "due to"

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', 'or', ' which', ' prevent', ' either') in abstract explanatory prose defining concepts, such as probability, physics or economics, where a noun phrase or verb is expected next. Contrast shows ' the' often silent, so it is weak and mixed.
result.label: Function words in definitional academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word ' no' right after a copula or verb ("is no", "are no", "was no"), as in "is no longer", and pushes towards ' longer', ' exception', ' stranger'.
result.label: "is no" before longer

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (periods, ' f', ' seed', ' and', ' require') in academic-style text, often where a word beginning is expected next, e.g. 'f' continuing into 'fuzzy' or 'fairness'. Peaks are inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens predicting f-words

result.description: Fires on the word " high" (also High/highest) as a modifier before a noun, such as "high levels", "high-quality" or "high-speed". It pushes the next token towards "-", "standards", "levels" and "degree". Silent on the contrast text.
result.label: "high" as modifier before noun

result.description: Fires on the token ' method' when it starts a sentence as the subject, right after a full stop, in explanatory text about techniques. It is silent on 'this method' or 'elimination method'. It pushes towards suffixes like -ically and -ology.
result.label: Sentence-initial ' method' as subject

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ch' in "ever-ch(anging)", right after "ever-" or a similar hyphen prefix, and predicts "anging" or "alleng". It stays silent on 'ch' inside words like "eschewing" or "tech".
result.label: 'ch' in ever-changing

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after a scientist's name (often pairs like "Rutherford and Curie's") when a noun like work, discovery or contribution is expected. Silent on some possessives, including after Bohr, de Broglie and non-scientist or title nouns.
result.label: Possessive 's after scientist names
'eds' in 'seeds'
result.description: Fires on the 'eds' piece completing 'seeds' (occasionally ' seed'), in garden and plant contexts. It pushes toward plant-related continuations such as plant, germ and root. Silent on 'eds' in other words like 'mechanicses'.

Fires on the "ance" piece at the end of "governance", especially in corporate governance text. It stays silent on "ance" in enhance, accordance and acceptance. It predicts words like structures, frameworks, codes and models.
result.label: "ance" in governance

result.description: Fires on the token ' popular', most strongly in "rise in popularity" and "popular culture", and predicts suffixes like -ity, -ized and -izing. Upstream members are mostly ' popular' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' popular' token detector

result.description: Fires on a place or scene noun right after "the" (streets, air, town, room, edge, side), in descriptive scene-setting prose. It seems to predict compound or location continuations such as yard, side, room, hall.
result.label: Setting noun after "the"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " impress" as the start of a word like impressive or impressions, predicting suffixes such as -ive, -ively, -ions. It is quieter when "impress" is a standalone verb.
result.label: " impress" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on verbs or verb pieces (shape, create, discover, reveal, -ing) in writing about characters and narrative, right before an expected object like "their inner/personal ...". The word ' with' peak is not reliable, since it stays silent in other topics.
result.label: Character-writing verb before 'their' object

result.description: Fires on ' company' (weakly ' organization') after "the/a", in corporate-governance or workplace text about the organization itself. It pushes towards possessive 's, culture, executive. Silent in the contrast, which has no 'company' token.
result.label: ' company' as organization noun
'iffer' in "Differential"
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'iffer' in "D-iffer-ential", mainly in "Differential Equations" headings. It predicts continuations like 'ential'. Early-layer 'iffer' detectors drive it.

Fires on adjectives or modifiers (complex, intricate, wider, diverse, distinct, shared) placed before an abstract noun in historical or political analysis prose, predicting nouns like politics, causes, circumstances. Silent on 'more complex' in an argument context.
result.label: Descriptive adjective before historical abstraction

result.description: Fires on ' Q' and ' statement' as logical or mathematical placeholder variables in modus ponens / conditional statement text ("if P implies Q", "conditional statement (if P"). Also weakly on a few word pieces. Circuit evidence is mixed.
result.label: Logic variable Q / conditional statement

result.description: Fires on "shape/shaping/shapes" and similar influence verbs (affect, influence, guide) where a subject like shared values or beliefs acts on people's behavior; predicts nouns like employees, behavior, members. Mostly in social/organizational text.
result.label: Shape/influence verb before behavior

result.description: Fires on ' also' right after a subject noun or auxiliary (e.g. "have also", "technology also") in expository text, before a main verb. It stays silent when 'also' follows "but" or "while" in a subordinate or contrastive clause.
result.label: ' also' before main verb

result.description: Fires on function words (to, the, involves, -ing) right after a verb like "refers/denotes/involves" in definitions of presupposition or implicit meaning in linguistics. It predicts the next word as assumption, presupposition or background belief.
result.label: Presupposition definition slot, predicts assumptions

result.description: Fires on ' since' right after a perfect auxiliary (has/have since) meaning "from then until now", as in "has since become". It stays silent on ' since' after "especially", which isn't that construction. It pushes towards ' then'.
result.label: "has since" after perfect auxiliary

result.description: Fires on the final noun of a plural or abstract subject noun phrase (science, systems, properties, resources, -ologies), where a plural verb like "are/have/include" is expected. Fires inconsistently; silent on "computer science" in some contexts.
result.label: Subject-noun-phrase head awaiting verb

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' advoc' (advocate, advocating, advocacy), mostly in descriptions of ideologies or movements. Members are mainly ' advoc' detectors plus verb-stem pieces that precede "-ate".
result.label: ' advoc' word-stem detector

result.description: Fires mainly on the ' U' token that starts "U.S." (United States), especially in historical or military text such as alliances and conflicts. Weaker peaks on a few other tokens (' offer', ' or', ' Sign') are mixed.
result.label: ' U' of U.S. in history

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ourse" in "discourse", as in "discourse analysis". It predicts "analysis" and similar words next. Many upstream members are also "ourse" detectors.
result.label: "ourse" in discourse

result.description: Fires on varied positions in scientific text where a word is likely to continue into "coll-" words (collapse, collide, colloid), e.g. ' col', ' L' in LTD, ' (' and '-'. Predicts 'lapsed', 'lide', 'der'. Mixed, low-faithfulness circuit.
result.label: Predicts coll- word continuations

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'com' (or ' Com') when it begins a longer word such as complement, comfortable, compress or comprehension. It pushes towards continuations like fort, bin, par, position. Silent on the word 'commas'.
result.label: 'com' word-initial piece

result.description: Fires on the ' ent' piece that starts "entanglement" (also 'Ent', and some other quantum-physics pieces like 'istic') in quantum text, predicting 'ang'/'rop' continuations. Silent on ' ent' when entanglement follows other words without quantum context.
result.label: quantum ' ent' (entanglement) piece

result.description: Fires on "like" / "such as" introducing examples in music-genre text, mostly before band or artist names (heavy metal, punk). Silent on "like" in art or other non-music lists. Predicts names like Iron, Dark, Met.
result.label: Example-introducing 'like/as' in music

result.description: Fires on the word piece " pro" when it begins a longer word split into pieces (probe, proton, progression, projections), mostly after "triode"/"planar"/"central" in probe text. Predicts continuations like "be", "ton", "gression".
result.label: " pro" word-start piece
'see' in 'overseeing'
result.description: Fires on the 'see' piece (and 'es' in 'oversees') inside 'oversee/overseeing', mostly in corporate-governance text about committees overseeing company matters. It needs the 'over' prefix, not standalone 'see'.

Fires on mixed positions, often ' poll' (before 'ution') and function words like ' the'/' in' in economics or policy text, where a word-start piece is being predicted. Peaks are inconsistent, and the circuit is weak (low faithfulness).
result.label: Poll- word start, mixed function words

result.description: Fires on the word "validation" (and related pieces like verification/calibration/acceptance endings) in testing, verification and quality-assurance text. It predicts words like "against", "checks", "testing" next.
result.label: "validation" in testing/verification text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' lon' when it starts 'longevity' (also weakly 'zeit' in 'zeitgeist'), predicting a continuation like 'ge'. Mostly in engineering and durability contexts, after words like safety and.
result.label: ' lon' in 'longevity'

result.description: Fires on the period right after a section number (e.g. "### 4.", "2.1.") at the start of a numbered heading. It stays silent on sentence-ending periods after titles or prose.
result.label: Period after section number

result.description: Fires mid-word on a piece inside a long prefixed adjective, mostly 'rict' in "unrestricted", also pieces like "alle" in "unparalleled". It fires where a suffix such as -ed is expected to complete the word.
result.label: Mid-word piece in un- adjectives

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' autom' (automation/automating) and 'estr' in 'orchestration', where the word is unfinished and the next piece is likely 'ation' or 'ated'. Mostly tech/DevOps text.
result.label: autom- / orchestr- word stem

result.description: Fires on the word " social" (also " Social") as an adjective before a noun such as justice, issues, responsibility or structures. It pushes the next token toward words like justice, movements, inclusion and causes. Most members are earlier-layer detectors of " social".
result.label: ' social' adjective token

result.description: Fires on an abstract head noun (principle, factor, aspect, objective, challenge, advantage) right after an adjective like "key", "important", "main", "core" at the start of a statement. It predicts a following "is" or "lies" clause.
result.label: Abstract noun after "key/important"

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ic' (occasionally 'ical') completing the word "rhetoric" / "rhetorical". Stays silent on 'ic' in other words like empiricism or anarchic.
result.label: 'ic' ending of rhetoric

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, to, as) right after "work" is being defined or described in physics text, where the next word would likely be work-related (done, performed, Work). Silent on the same words in other physics definitions not about work.
result.label: Function words after physics "work"

result.description: Fires on ' a' after "was/stand as/has been" when a historical period or decade is the subject (e.g. "The 1930s was a pivotal..."), anticipating a period-characterizing noun like "pivotal time". Silent on ' a' in other subjects.
result.label: ' a' describing historical periods

result.description: Fires on infinitive ' to' (also 'can', 'help') introducing a purpose clause in cooking and flavour text, such as "can be used to enhance". It stays quiet on 'to' after other verbs or in non-culinary contexts like "tuned to detect".
result.label: Purpose 'to' in culinary text

result.description: Fires on minimizing adverbs like "merely", "just", "simply", "purely", mostly after "not"/"more than"/"is" in "not just X" style contrasts. It pushes toward a following article or noun phrase such as "a", "an", "another", "about".
result.label: Minimizing adverb 'merely/just/simply'

result.description: Fires on the token " depth" across contexts (tree depth, image depth estimation, water depth, depth and breadth). Members are mostly detectors of " depth" itself. Weakly also on "height" or "length" nouns.
result.label: ' depth' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on mid-word pieces 'do' (in "redox") and 'ich' (in "Carmichael"), where a rare word is still being spelled out. Weak firing on some function words. Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Mid-word 'do'/'ich' in rare words

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' sp' (also ' Sp') at the start of a word split into pieces, such as span/spanning, spelling, spices, sp3. It pushes towards continuations like 'ans', 'anning' and 'anned'.
result.label: ' sp' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the comma right after "instance" or "example" (as in "for instance," / "for example,"), where an illustration is introduced. Silent on ordinary clause-boundary commas.
result.label: Comma after "for instance/example"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (function words, word-start fragments like ' prom', ' ev', ' cred', ' inaug') where the next token is likely a word continuation such as 'inence', 'ibility', 'idenced'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Predicts word-continuation fragments

result.description: Fires on relative/linking pronouns (which, that, they) after a plural noun naming biological or chemical substances (metabolites, flavonoids, proteins), where a verb like act, serve, or confer comes next. Silent on some "which" clauses in other contexts.
result.label: Relative pronoun after plural science nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' voc' (mostly before "abulary"), after adjectives or determiners like "new", "strong", "your". Predicts the continuation "ab". Rare weak firing on 'li' in "appliances".
result.label: ' voc' start of vocabulary

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a bare list of technology or field names (e.g. "artificial intelligence, machine learning, analytics,"). It stays quiet on commas that end a clause or lead into a participle phrase such as ", leading to".
result.label: Comma in lists of tech fields

result.description: Fires on the document-start/boundary token (shown as ¶) when it comes after a short topic-title line in a list of headings, such as "Mathematics." or "Ecological Succession." It is silent on the first position and after long sentences. Next-token logits favor topic-like words.
result.label: Boundary token after topic-list titles

result.description: Fires on the noun " choice" or " selection" (also "choosing") when it is the subject of a sentence or clause, typically "the choice of X" or "selection process". It mainly appears in technical or culinary contexts. It predicts "between", "of" or "criteria".
result.label: choice/selection as head noun

result.description: Fires on "found"/"finds" (also "find", "finding") when a non-human subject such as a concept, technique, or instrument "has found" its way, use, or place. Predicts words like "expression", "its", "new", "use", "resonance".
result.label: 'found' as 'found its way/use'

result.description: Fires on the verb or preposition after "a branch of physics/science that..." (studies, deals with, focuses on, involves), where the next word is the subject matter, especially fluids and flow. Silent on ordinary "with" in other uses.
result.label: Field-definition verb before subject matter

result.description: Fires on the auxiliary ' has'/' have' after a noun subject in essay-style text about influence or impact, where a present-perfect verb like "not only inspired" follows. Silent on "geology has become" in a historical sentence.
result.label: has/have before "not only" perfect

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cru' when it begins "crucial", mostly after "is" in phrases like "X is crucial for/to". Many upstream members are themselves ' cru' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' cru' in "crucial"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ar' completing "Laminar" in fluid-dynamics text (laminar flow). Weak activations on a few function words elsewhere. Members include 'ar' detectors and fluid/flow-word detectors.
result.label: 'ar' in "laminar" (flow)

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a list or phrase of rules (standards, requirements, regulations, laws) in compliance and regulatory text, where a following word like "set" or "specified" is expected. Silent on some "standards" in other phrasings.
result.label: Regulatory rule nouns in compliance text
'become' predicting evolving significance
result.description: Fires on ' become/becoming/became' (occasionally 'as', 'into') when a subject such as festivals is described as turning into something increasingly significant. Silent on 'become' in a plain comparative ("areas become more closely linked"). Predicts adjectives like cultural, significant, global.

Fires on possessive markers (apostrophe, 's) after individual/user/person nouns, and on "individual"/"own", in ethics and rights text, where the next word is likely a right or trait like autonomy, rights, liberty or privacy. Silent on "Today's" and "it's".
result.label: Possessive of individual, then rights

result.description: Fires on word pieces like ' int' (before "ake", as in water/energy intake), 'ites' in "satellites", and ' payload'. Mostly the ' int' piece in intake-type contexts, with a few other scattered tokens. Predicts "ake".
result.label: ' int' of intake, satellites

result.description: Fires on plural subject nouns like ' groups' (also -isms, -s) that are about to take a plural verb, e.g. "various ethnic groups coexist/live". Silent when the noun is followed by a period or ends a phrase after "between/among".
result.label: Plural subject noun awaiting verb

result.description: Fires on the piece 'all' inside "cryst-all-" words (crystalline, crystallization), predicting suffixes like -ine, -ization. It stays silent on 'all' in "metallic", so it needs the crystal- prefix.
result.label: 'all' in crystall- words

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ut' inside "scrutiny" (and "scrutinizing"), predicting "iny". It is weak or silent on 'ut' in other words like "statutory", though members also respond to 'ut' in pollutants and commutation.
result.label: 'ut' in "scrutiny"

result.description: Fires on nouns meaning a case or circumstance (scenarios, situations, situation, scenario), mostly after adjectives like hypothetical, possible or worst-case. It pushes toward "where" or "involving" as the next word.
result.label: scenario/situation nouns before "where"

result.description: Fires on list separators (commas, "and", "or", "),") inside lists of causes or problems like errors, failures and data corruption, where a further negative item (lack of, poor, incorrect) is expected next. Silent on "and" in neutral lists.
result.label: List separators in cause-of-error lists

result.description: Fires on "light" (and sunlight, light rays, radiation) in physics or optics-style text about light, scattering and rays. Silent on sound wave text. Predicts continuations like cast, filtered, ray, dim.
result.label: light as physical phenomenon

result.description: Fires on adjectives like cultural, unique, distinct, diverse, and "genetic" that modify a following noun in texts about diversity of societies or species. It predicts nouns like identities, characteristics, traditions, attributes.
result.label: Diversity adjectives before attribute nouns

result.description: Fires on nationality or regional adjectives (Indian, Chinese, European, Arab) used as modifiers before a noun like mathematics, science, or civilization, mostly in history-of-science text. It predicts nouns such as society, history, intellectual.
result.label: Nationality adjective before culture noun

result.description: Fires on the noun "relationships" (also "connections", "-hips" in "partnerships", "relations") when it is the head noun of a phrase about people or entities. It pushes the next token toward "between", "with" or "among".
result.label: relationships / connections noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'am' (and 'ism') after "se" in "seamless" and "seismic", predicting a suffix like "less", "lessly" or "ic". It stays silent on 'am' in other words such as "ice-cream".
result.label: "am" in "seamless"/"seismic"

result.description: Fires on "crucial", "essential" or "critical" when used as a predicate adjective after "is/are" (e.g. "precision is crucial for…"), anticipating a following "for/to". Silent on attributive uses like "an essential role" or "essential depth cues".
result.label: Predicative "crucial/essential" adjective

result.description: Fires on the token ' convergence' in mathematical text (series, sequences, Fourier analysis). It pushes the next token toward convergence-related nouns such as rates, tests, criteria and speed.
result.label: ' convergence' in math text

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ious' completing "harmonious" (weaker on "synergistic", "symbiotic"). It predicts nouns of balance or blending such as "blend", "balance", "proportion" and "combinations".
result.label: harmon-ious suffix

result.description: Fires on ' intellectual' (also ' cultural') as an adjective in Renaissance-style descriptions of a period of intellectual, artistic and cultural flourishing, e.g. "a period of intellectual revival". Silent on some other uses, such as "literary and intellectual traditions".
result.label: intellectual in period-of-flourishing phrases
