result.description: Fires on word-start fragments (e.g. ' dec' before 'isions', 'p' in Responsibility) and some function words where a word continuation suffix such as 'isions' or 'ons' is expected. Mixed peaks; weak consistency.
result.label: Incomplete word-piece awaiting suffix

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a split verb stem (unders-, ill-, enh-, im-, enc-, fost-) in academic-style prose, right where a verb like "underscores" or "illuminates" is about to be completed. It predicts the suffix, such as -ributes, -poses or -uminate.
result.label: Verb-stem fragment before suffix

result.description: Fires on function words like " involves", " to", " of" in explanatory text defining paraphrasing (or similar skills like listening), where the next word is likely a verb describing the process, such as restating in original words. Silent on " involves" in other topics.
result.label: Paraphrasing definition connectors

result.description: Fires on the final piece "ory" of "inventory" (also "ventory"), in business stock-management text. It pushes toward words like management, control, turnover and levels.
result.label: "inventory" word ending, before management

result.description: Fires mostly on the mid-word piece 'ere' in "cerebrum/cerebellum/cerebral", with weaker firing on other mid-word fragments such as 'ide' and 'cer'. Members are detectors of 'ere' fragments.
result.label: 'ere' inside cerebrum

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs like "of", "understanding", "understand" in art-criticism text about analyzing or interpreting artworks and artistic intent, where the next word is likely art-related (works, art, texts). Silent on "of" in generic social-science text.
result.label: Art criticism interpretation connectives

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ref' when it starts a word like refining, refinery, refinement, refraction or reflexive, and pushes the next token toward continuations such as 'in', 'ining' and 'ract'. Most windows are about metal or petroleum processing.
result.label: ' ref' word-start piece (refining)

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'ynast' piece in "Dynasty" after a Chinese dynasty name (Shang, Zhou, Tang, Song, Yuan), with weaker firing on scattered word pieces and commas. Circuit is low-faithfulness and mixed.
result.label: Dynasty 'ynast' word piece

result.description: Fires on word pieces 'arith', 'Cos'/'cos', 'yth' that are the start of a word continuing with "-mic"/"-m(s)" (logarithmic, cosmic, rhythm). Predicts the "mic/ms/m" continuation.
result.label: Word piece before -mic/-ms ending

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ater' piece in "catering"/"caterers" and "extraterrestrial", plus scattered words like "organ", "to", "include" and "purchase". Mixed evidence; the 'ater' fragment is the main trigger, and the 'catering to' phrase is the clearest context.
result.label: 'ater' in catering / extraterrestrial

result.description: Fires on the hyphen after "end" (end-user, end-to-end), predicting "user/users" next. It stays quiet on hyphens in other compounds like decision-makers, user-centered, resource-intensive.
result.label: Hyphen after "end" (end-user)

result.description: Fires on the 'o' in "Indo" (as in Indo-European), right before the hyphen and "European". It stays silent on 'o' in other words like Mesoamerica, Proto-, or Iroquoian.
result.label: 'o' in Indo-European

result.description: Fires mostly on ' rock' and other words in geology/erosion/sediment passages (transport, depositional, the), where the next word is likely a geological process or surface term. Members are erosion, glacier and sediment detectors.
result.label: Rock in erosion/sediment geology text

result.description: Fires on intensifying adverbs (-ly, significantly, greatly, directly) placed before a verb like affect, impact, influence, determine, predicting such verbs next. Silent on -ly adverbs in other positions (chiefly, markedly evolved).
result.label: Adverb before affect/influence verb

result.description: Fires on 'and' or commas in lists right after 'science' or scientific/academic field words (science, physics, biology), where the next item is likely another field such as engineering, technology, mathematics or philosophy. Silent on 'and' in other contexts.
result.label: List separator after science fields

result.description: Fires on the verb " break" (also "breaking") right after "can/to/help", as in "break down barriers" or "break the cycle". It pushes toward particles like free, into, through and down.
result.label: verb "break" before particle/object

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ologies'/'ology' completing the word "methodologies"/"methodology". It stays silent on the same suffix in "technologies", so it needs the preceding "method" piece. It predicts words like "employed" and "applied".
result.label: -ologies in "methodologies"

result.description: Fires on plural nouns for physical entities (objects, atoms, electrons, particles) in physics/science explanations, often as the subject or object of a motion or arrangement description. Silent on abstract physics terms like phonon mode.
result.label: Plural physical-entity nouns in physics

result.description: Fires on function words (of, that, the, commas) in software development/engineering text, where the next word is likely a software term like bug, refactor or deployment. Silent on the same words in non-software contexts such as finance or history.
result.label: Function words in software-engineering text

result.description: Fires on "lay"/"laid" (and "paving") in the idiom of laying the groundwork or foundation, as in "laying the foundation for". Members detect lay/laid tokens. Weak activation appears on a few unrelated tokens.
result.label: lay the groundwork/foundation

result.description: Fires on the token ' norm' (as in "cultural norms", "normative"), mostly in social-science or cultural contexts. It predicts continuations like -ative, -ativity and -s. Members are mostly earlier ' norm' detectors.
result.label: ' norm' word-start (norms/normative)
'red' in ingredient
result.description: Fires on the piece 'red' inside the word "ingredient(s)" (split as ing+red), predicting the continuation 'ient'/'ients'. Members are mostly 'red' and ' ing' detectors from earlier layers.

Fires mostly on the word-start piece ' vers' (as in versatile/versatility) and similar incomplete word beginnings like ' vol', ' u' (ubiquitous), 'Aut'. It predicts continuations such as 'atile' and 'at'. Weaker, mixed cases exist.
result.label: ' vers' fragment predicting 'atile'

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (to, that, this, these, analysis, patterns) in analytical essay prose, often where an abstract noun like "story" or "context" is expected next. Members mostly relate to writing, narrative and plot. Mixed evidence.
result.label: Analytical prose slot before abstract noun

result.description: Fires on the piece 'icon' when it is the middle of the split word "semiconductor(s)" (sem|icon|ductor), following 'sem'. It stays silent when 'icon' starts the text or follows other pieces such as 'sil'.
result.label: 'icon' inside semiconductor

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cook' when it is the start of a compound or derived word (cooking, cookbook, cookware, cooktop), and predicts suffixes like ing/book/ware/ery. Members are mostly ' cook' detectors.
result.label: ' cook' as word stem

result.description: Fires on function words (of, in, with, celebrated, only) in text about knights, nobles, chivalry and medieval courts, where the next word is likely to be an honor/grandeur-type noun. Silent on 'of' in unrelated phrases like 'coat of arms' or 'of course'.
result.label: Function words in chivalry/nobility text

result.description: Fires on commas and "and"/"or" separating items in a list of abstract positive qualities or skills (honesty, passion, authenticity, confidence), predicting another such quality noun next (dedication, commitment, precision).
result.label: Separators in lists of virtues

result.description: Fires on an opening parenthesis (or dash/bracket) after a term in linguistics or language-study text, where a gloss, example or abbreviation follows. It stays silent on parentheses in other topics, such as names or PDE. Logits favour linguistic words.
result.label: Parenthesis in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on the word " fair" (fairness, fair trade, fair treatment), mostly in ethics or economics text. It predicts suffixes like "ness" or "y". Members are mostly earlier " fair" and "equitable" detectors.
result.label: ' fair' token detector

result.description: Fires on commas and conjunctions (and, or, as well as) in lists of nouns about food, ingredients and production processes, where another noun like processes, components or finished items is expected next. Silent on some commas in other clause types.
result.label: List separators in food/process lists

result.description: Fires on ' as' (also 'became', 'a', 'an') after a subject when the word introduces the role or status it takes on, as in "emerged as", "serving as", "radio became an". Silent on "seen as", "as well as", and temporal "as".
result.label: Role-predicate 'as/became' after subject
'm' in dis-m-antle
result.description: Fires on the piece 'm' in the split word "dismantle/dismantling/dismantlement", predicting the continuation 'ant'. It stays silent on 'm' ending other words such as paradigm, enthusiasm, realm. Weakly fires on 'm' in other split words (Pragmatic).

Fires on the final noun or word piece of academic-activity phrases after a scholarly modifier, e.g. "scientific inquiry", "scientific exploration", "philosophical discourse", "scientific discovery", "evolutionary research". Predicts continuations like "conducted".
result.label: Scholarly inquiry/research noun after field adjective

result.description: Fires on the noun " topic" (also " theme", " topics") when it is the object of a phrase like "choose the right topic" or "main topics". Upstream members are mostly topic/theme/subject detectors. Predicts words like "discussed" and "sentence".
result.label: topic / theme noun detector

result.description: Fires on ' it' right after "when" (also "unless"), as the subject of a subordinate clause, especially in "when it comes to". Predicts ' comes'/' come'. Silent on ' it' in other positions, such as after "as" or as an object.
result.label: "when it" → comes to

result.description: Fires on the ending piece ('ve', 'ves', 'ive') of the verb "delve" (also dive/venture-like verbs), predicting "deeper"/"into". Silent on contractions like "we've" and on "convection".
result.label: "delve" verb ending piece

result.description: Fires on the document-boundary token (shown as ¶ / <s>) that separates short, title-like or topical academic lines, right after a sentence or heading ends and a new document starts. Silent on ordinary mid-text tokens.
result.label: Document-start boundary token

result.description: Fires on the comma (or colon/semicolon) right after an introductory phrase such as "for example," or "for instance,", where an illustration or elaboration follows. It stays quiet on ordinary clause-joining commas.
result.label: Comma after "for example"

result.description: Fires on " Global" as the first word of a line or heading in a list of course or topic titles (e.g. "Global Supply Chains"). Weak on lowercase "global" mid-sentence. Pushes toward "Position", "supply", "Navigation".
result.label: Global as heading-initial word

result.description: Fires on "cial" completing "Financial" (and on " financial") in finance contexts, predicting finance nouns like instruments, institutions, products, reporting. Silent on "cial" in "crucial".
result.label: Financial word piece, finance nouns next

result.description: Fires on the token ' advantage' when it is the stem of "advantageous" (e.g. "can be advantage|ous"), pushing the next token toward the suffix "ous". It is weak on plain "advantage"/"disadvantage".
result.label: advantage- stem before -ous

result.description: Fires on the prefix " meta" (and "Meta") as a word-start piece, as in meta-analysis, meta-narrative, metafiction. It predicts continuations like "analysis" and "comment". Upstream members mostly detect " meta" itself.
result.label: meta- prefix token

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, with, both, -level) in workplace motivation and organizational psychology text, especially where a noun like attachment, commitment or satisfaction is likely next. It is silent on 'of' in generic non-psychology contexts.
result.label: Function words in organizational psychology text
Artificial Intelligence 'elligence' piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'elligence' completing "Artificial Intelligence", often in titles and headings. Weakly on ' intelligence' after "artificial". Silent on generic technology text without that phrase.
Fires on the word piece ' abstra' (start of "abstraction/abstractions"), predicting the "-ction" continuation. Members detect ' abstra' and similar "-ction" word pieces (constru, extra, attra, au).
result.label: ' abstra' before -ction

result.description: Fires on the newline/document-boundary token (shown as ¶) that follows a short topic-title line in a list of terse headings (e.g. "Immunology.¶"), where a new heading or section begins. Silent on a document-initial ¶.
result.label: Newline after list-of-topics heading

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " fost" (start of foster/fosters/fostering), strongest after a relative "that" following a noun like "environment" or "culture", where a verb "fost-ers" is expected. Weaker after other nouns; silent when "fost" follows "in" or "of" or starts a sentence.
result.label: ' fost' after "environment that"

result.description: Fires on prepositions or verbs like "for", "of", "towards", "developing" that come before a goal or object in quantum computing and technology text (e.g. "paving the way for"). It is silent on "for" in many similar contexts, and the logits favour "fault", "stabil", "practical".
result.label: Quantum-computing prepositions before technical goals

result.description: Fires on the pronoun " we" (also "We") as the subject starting a new clause or sentence in expository text, often after a period or comma. It stays quiet when "we" follows "where" or "in which" in a relative clause.
result.label: Clause-initial "we" in exposition

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tail' as the start of "tailor" (e.g. "can tailor their approach"), predicting the "or" continuation. Weaker on "tailored". Members are mostly other ' tail' detectors.
result.label: ' tail' before 'or' (tailor)

result.description: Fires on the verb ' add' (also adds/adding) in the sense of contributing a quality, as in "can add depth/color/excitement". Members are mostly detectors of 'add' forms. Predicts nouns like depth or character.
result.label: 'add' as contributing a quality

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces 'under' (e.g. thunderstorm split as th|under, 'under the weather') and ' infrastr' (before 'ucture'), where a longer word continues. Logits favour word-completing suffixes.
result.label: 'under' and 'infrastr' word-pieces

result.description: Fires on verbs and prepositions that introduce an object of analysis or understanding, such as "insight into", "understanding", "examine", "analyze" and "explain", in abstract mathematical text. It predicts nouns like "relationships", "how" and "properties".
result.label: Insight-into / understanding in math text

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a second object after "combine/blend/merge X with [domain] NOUN" (skill, principles, commentary, motifs), where a blended-domains phrase is being completed. Pushes toward verbs like "to/creates". Peaks are mixed.
result.label: Noun completing "blend X with Y" phrase

result.description: Fires on words inside title-like topic phrases (e.g. "Understanding Digital Palette", "Producing a Weather Map"), in academic or course-style headings. It predicts a following subject noun such as book, record or Audio. Peaks are mixed.
result.label: Title-phrase words predicting subject nouns
' rh' word-start piece (rhythm, rhyme)
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' rh' at the start of words like rhythm, rhyme and rhetoric, and pushes the next token towards continuations like 'ythm' and 'yme'. Upstream members are mostly ' rh' detectors across earlier layers.

Fires on scattered word-start or mid-word pieces ('1' in a year, 'co' of cooperation, ' between') in text about treaties and diplomacy, such as the Helsinki Accords. Peaks are mixed, and the same '1' stays silent in other year contexts.
result.label: Diplomacy-text mixed pieces (1, co, between)

result.description: Fires on the word " contributions" (also " contribution" and "contributors"), mostly where someone's or something's contributions are discussed. It predicts " to" or "towards" next. Members are mostly detectors of the same word.
result.label: ' contributions' token detector

result.description: Fires on the final piece "ate" in "corporate" (split as corpor-ate), as in corporate governance or corporate social responsibility. It stays silent on "ate" in other words such as incorporate, permeate, mitigate and innovate.
result.label: "ate" ending "corporate"

result.description: Fires on the pronoun " we" as a clause subject, usually after a comma or sentence break in expository text. It predicts a following verb such as want, shall, aim or ensure. It stays silent on "we" in a relative clause or at the very start of a text.
result.label: Subject pronoun " we" before verb

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of cultural elements (customs, languages, architecture, crafts, religion), where another cultural-domain item is expected next. Silent on commas in ordinary clauses or non-list uses.
result.label: Commas in cultural-element lists

result.description: Fires on determiners (' the', ' its', ' a') that begin a second or coordinated noun phrase in descriptive praise of a style or work, e.g. "and the allure of", "characterized by its elegance". Predicts abstract qualities like clarity, sense, desire.
result.label: Determiner before abstract quality noun

result.description: Fires on 'in' that opens a new clause or parenthetical phrase after a comma or dash (", in which", ", in general", "— in fact"), predicting fixed phrases like 'other', 'particular', 'short', 'which'. Silent on 'in' after a noun like 'role in'.
result.label: Clause-initial 'in' after comma

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' em' when it is the start of "emissions", mostly after "greenhouse gas" or "carbon", and predicts "issions". Weakly fires on other em- words such as embody and empathy.
result.label: ' em' before -issions

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ense' completing the word "suspense" (mostly "suspenseful"), in writing about storytelling and plot. It predicts the suffix 'ful'/'fully' next. Weakly fires on related words like surprise and mystery.
result.label: 'ense' in suspense(ful)

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (commas, ' the', ' of') in abstract expository text about epistemology, belief systems and expert systems, where an analysis-type noun may come next. Peaks are scattered; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in abstract theory text

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, about, include, considers) in explanatory text about survival analysis and time-to-event statistics, where the next word would be a term like survival, censoring, lifetime or death. Silent on 'of' in other statistical phrases.
result.label: Function words before survival-analysis terms

result.description: Fires on plural-variety determiners (" different", " multiple", " various") placed before a plural noun, especially in technical text about combining or distributing data, views or sources. Predicts nouns like views, sources, modal.
result.label: different/multiple/various before plural noun

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ed' completing "subject" in "subjected (to)", as in materials subjected to stress. It stays silent on 'ed' in other verbs such as overlooked, feathered or borrowed.
result.label: 'ed' in "subjected to"

result.description: Fires on " in" introducing a setting or context in communication/tone-in-situations text, especially "such as in-person meetings" or "in Western cultures". Predicts communication nouns like emails, written, customer. Silent on " in" in other topics.
result.label: " in" for communication settings

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after the generic pronoun "one" (one's own ...), predicting " own" or "self". It stays silent on 's after "it", nouns like "world" or "speaker", and other non-"one" contexts.
result.label: possessive 's after "one"

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ative' in "collabor-ative" (also cooper-ative), predicting nouns like efforts, problem, spirit. Silent on 'ative' in innovative, narrative, participative.
result.label: collaborative suffix 'ative'

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix "al" in "disposal" (also "ing", " prior", " increasing"), where the next word is likely a noun like "methods" or "site". Silent on "al" in other words like "portrayal" or "institutional".
result.label: "disposal" suffix 'al'

result.description: Fires on function words and adjectives (' the', ' to', ' essential', 'cial') in sentences saying something is crucial or contributes to organizational functioning, especially in organizational behavior text. It stays silent on many ' the' tokens elsewhere. Predicts words like 'formal', 'organiz', 'operation'.
result.label: Organizational-contribution phrasing, 'the' slot

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ural' completing "architectural" (after "architect"). It stays silent on 'ural' in "structural". Predicts nouns like styles, designs, wonders, projects.
result.label: 'ural' in "architectural"

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, their, an) right after verbs like measure/evaluate/assess in text about measuring innovation, predicting "innov(ation)" next. Silent on 'of' in other business contexts.
result.label: Function word before predicted 'innovation'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' une' (start of "unequal", "uneven") and pushes the next token toward 'qual', 'ven', 'quality'. Upstream members are mostly ' une' detectors; weak activation elsewhere.
result.label: ' une' prefix before qual/ven

result.description: Fires on an apostrophe that comes right after sentence-ending punctuation (a period) and starts a new sentence or clause, as in ".'s important" or ".'t". It stays silent on possessive or contraction apostrophes attached to a word, such as "one's" or "someone's".
result.label: Apostrophe after sentence-final period

result.description: Fires mostly on ' that' in a cleft-like construction after a time phrase ("it wasn't until the 20th century that", "during this time that"), where the clause continues with a subject. Silent on relative or complement 'that'.
result.label: Temporal cleft 'that'
Computing noun modifier before technical noun
result.description: Fires on a noun used as a modifier in computing/networking text (process, system, device, frame, network, command), where another technical noun is expected next (timeout, ports, tables, interrupt). Silent on 'process' in general business or engineering text.

Fires on the piece "inal" in "marginal" (marginal utility/cost/analysis), in economics text. It stays silent on "inal" in "seminal", so it needs the "marg" prefix. Predicts "-ized"/"utility"-type continuations.
result.label: "inal" in "marginal" (economics)

result.description: Fires on abstract head nouns (area, aspect, topic, element) right after an evaluative adjective like crucial, critical, important, significant, in a "has become a crucial area of..." predicate. Predicts " of". Silent after "this area".
result.label: Head noun after "crucial/important" adjective

result.description: Fires on the word "digital"/"Digital" (any case), as in digital printmaking, digital art, digital media. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same word. Silent on unrelated text such as music streaming.
result.label: Digital token detector

result.description: Fires on the word "set"/"Set"/"sets" in mathematical text, mostly in "set theory" contexts. It predicts continuations like theory, membership, operations and builder.
result.label: "set" in set theory

result.description: Fires on the piece 'uct' inside "fluctuations" (fl|uct|uations), predicting continuation like 'uate'. It stays silent on 'uct' in other words such as "infrastructures".
result.label: 'uct' in fluctuations

result.description: Fires on the piece 'our' inside the word "sourcing"/"sourced" (s-our-cing), predicting the suffix 'cing'/'ced'. Members are 'our' detectors in word-internal positions; it is quiet on whole-word ingredient text without this split.
result.label: 'our' inside "sourcing"

result.description: Fires on function words (the, comma, and, of) in technical text about chemical, biological or engineering processes, where the next word is likely a chemistry or engineering term. Silent on the same words in other contexts.
result.label: Function words in chemical engineering text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " cos" (before "mic"/"mos"), mainly in cosmology text. It predicts continuations like "mic" and "mos". Also weakly fires on "ynt" in "syntactic".
result.label: ' cos' word-start piece (cosmic)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' comp' when it starts a word, most strongly where "compliance" is the expected continuation (e.g. "ensure comp", "IT comp"). It pushes the next token toward "liance". It fires weakly on other comp- words such as "compelling" and "competitive".
result.label: ' comp' predicting 'compliance'

result.description: Fires on the 'ent' piece of 'underwent' (also weakly 'undergone'), after a subject like a field or thing that changed. It predicts words like 'significant', 'rigorous', 'revision'. It stays silent on 'ent' in words like 'prevalent' or 'stringent'.
result.label: 'ent' in 'underwent'

result.description: Fires on " only" in the "not only" construction, right after "not" with a verb expected next (enabled, enriches, illustrated). Predicts verbs like "advanced", "improved", "enhance". Silent in other contexts.
result.label: "not only" correlative 'only'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fost' as the start of "foster/fosters/fostering", mostly in abstract essay text about communication or collaboration. It predicts the suffix (er, ers, ered). It is silent on some ' fost' tokens, notably "fostering" after "also" or "in".
result.label: ' fost' start of foster

result.description: Fires on scattered connective tokens (' and', commas, ' including', 'och') in academic or technical prose, often linguistics or music. Peaks are mixed and inconsistent. The contrast shows ' and' in plain lists stays silent.
result.label: Connectives in academic linguistics prose

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "trying" or "attempting" (infinitive marker of an effort verb, often in "like trying to solve..." comparisons). It stays silent on ' to' after adjectives or nouns like "helpful to" or "given to".
result.label: ' to' after trying/attempting

result.description: Fires on ' that' as a relative pronoun right after an abstract noun describing a skill, tool, technique or art form ("a powerful tool that can..."). Silent on demonstrative or complementizer 'that' (emphasize that, with that person).
result.label: Relative 'that' after skill/tool noun

result.description: Fires on the noun " shift" meaning a change or transition, as in "a fundamental shift" or "paradigm shift", usually the subject of a clause. It predicts "from", "towards" or "occurred". It stays silent when "shift" is used as a verb.
result.label: noun "shift" (paradigm shift)

result.description: Fires on math/computing nouns like " algorithm", " algebra", " mathematics", " method", often where a suffix such as -ic/-ical could follow. It is silent on some " algorithm" tokens (e.g. after "Euclidean" or "RSA"), so the condition is unclear.
result.label: algorithm / algebra math terms

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly " of", also possessive "s", "possess") in abstract essays on nature, art, spirituality and the sublime, where the next word is likely a lofty noun (inspiration, spiritual, sacred). Silent on " of" in other, more mundane constructions.
result.label: "of" before lofty abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on commas, "as well as", "and" and "),". These separators fall inside lists of infrastructure types (transit, water, sewage, electricity), where the next item is likely communication, telecom or utilities. Silent on commas after "networks" in other contexts.
result.label: Infrastructure list separators

result.description: Fires on the 'AL' piece in the acronym SALT (Strategic Arms Limitation Talks), after "(S", in Cold War arms-control text. It pushes the next token toward 'T'.
result.label: AL in SALT acronym

result.description: Fires mostly on a hyphen in compound words, strongest in "step-growth" after "step" or "chain" in polymer text, predicting a word-piece continuation. Also fires weakly on function words like "of", "the", "and". Silent on other hyphens like "higher-", "non-".
result.label: Hyphen in step-growth compounds

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' fir' when it begins "firms" (economics text), predicting 'ms'. Also weakly fires on 'iz' in "Organizational" and on ' the' after "understanding". The circuit is mostly 'fir' detectors.
result.label: "fir" before "ms" (firms)

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ang' in "Michelangelo", predicting 'elo' next. Members also detect 'ang' in other words such as "entanglement", but the target peaks on the name. It is silent on the Leonardo da Vinci contrast text.
result.label: 'ang' in Michelangelo

result.description: Fires mid-word on incomplete word pieces in topic or heading lists, mainly 'chni' in "Techniques", plus ' Indust' (Industrial) and ' relief'/' appro'. It seems to predict a suffix completing the word (ries, ry, ction).
result.label: Word-fragment in heading lists

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (and, in, to, may, can, providing) in technical or scientific expository prose, after a clause where a continuation follows. It is silent on many ' and' tokens in lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on a passive past participle (established, created, formed, initiated, attained, reached) right after "is/are/be", completing a passive verb. Silent when "established" is an adjective after "with/to".
result.label: Passive participle after auxiliary

result.description: Fires on the word piece "agement" completing "engagement", mostly in marketing or business metrics contexts (customer, audience, community engagement). It predicts nouns like metrics, strategies, levels and tactics.
result.label: "engagement" suffix 'agement'

result.description: Fires on 'from', 'with', ':' or 'the' introducing the start of a process or lifecycle description (e.g. "journey from", "begins with", "stages:"), predicting initial-phase words like conception, idea, planning. Silent on 'from' meaning source.
result.label: Lifecycle start: 'from'/'begins with'

result.description: Fires on function words (for, and, offer, of, to) in technology/materials text, right before a predicted benefit or improved-performance word like "faster", "longer", "higher", "dens(ity)". Silent on many other uses of " for".
result.label: Function words before performance-benefit terms

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' of', ' should') and word pieces mid-phrase, where the next word is open. The peaks share no clear token or construction, and the same ' the' stays silent in the contrast. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'enger' piece in "messenger" (messenger RNA) in molecular biology text. It also fires weakly on ' mathematical' in Egyptian papyrus text and on a few other tokens. Members include 'enger' detectors and biology/gene-expression context.
result.label: 'enger' in messenger (RNA)

result.description: Fires on a comma that follows a full stop, where a sentence-ending period is immediately followed by a comma and a new fragment or list item starts. It stays silent on ordinary mid-sentence commas after a clause or phrase.
result.label: Comma right after a period

result.description: Fires on ' is'/' are' right after a plural or abstract subject noun phrase in academic/scientific text (e.g. "research on X is", "studies are"), where a progressive or ongoing predicate comes next (continuing, focused, evolving). Silent on other 'is' uses.
result.label: Copula after scientific subject noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ur' when it begins a longer word, mainly "urgency" in "urgency and importance" task-prioritization text. Predicts continuations like "gency". Members are mostly ' ur' detectors plus other word-start fragment detectors.
result.label: ' ur' start of 'urgency'

result.description: Fires on abstract nouns such as "entities", "entity", "nature" and "ideas" in philosophical or conceptual discussion of separate things and wholes. It predicts part/unit-like nouns next. It is silent on "entities" in database-style text.
result.label: Abstract 'entities' in philosophical text

result.description: Fires on the suffix pieces 'ent' and 'ic' that finish "covalent" and "ionic" in chemical-bonding text. It is silent on 'ent' in unrelated words like "inherent" and "substituent". Its logits push towards "bond".
result.label: covalent/ionic suffix before "bond"

result.description: Fires on ' the' after "X is" or "refers to" in a definitional sentence about an abstract concept (cohesion, rhythm, motivation), anticipating an abstract noun like "process", "basis", "foundation". Silent on some similar "is the" cases.
result.label: 'the' in concept definitions

result.description: Fires on the em dash token that follows a completed clause or noun phrase in abstract expository prose, introducing an elaboration or appositive. Members are mostly em-dash detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: Em dash after clause

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ure'/'uring' completing "vent-ure/venturing" (corporate venturing, venture capital). It stays silent on 'uring' in nurturing, ensuring and enduring. It pushes toward ' capital'.
result.label: vent-ure suffix piece

result.description: Fires on a hyphen or en dash joining a noun or compound's first part to a following word, as in "problem-", "data-" or "concept-to-operation-". It is silent on hyphens after "cross", "20th" or "fiberglass", and on a hyphen at text start. Boosts next-token words like making, building and testing.
result.label: Hyphen in noun compounds

result.description: Fires on commas and function words (and, in, of, how) in abstract expository text about probability, statistics and math, mid-sentence where a technical term should follow. Mixed peaks; members mostly push probability-related continuations. Weak, inconsistent.
result.label: Function words in probability/math exposition

result.description: Fires on function words (and, on, with, -ized) in passages about the Protestant work ethic, where "emphasis/emphasized hard work, frugality" is being listed. It stays silent on 'and' in other lists, so it appears tied to this passage's theme.
result.label: Emphasis on hard work, frugality

result.description: Fires on the space or dash token right before a year's digits in ancient Greek philosophy dates (e.g. "Socrates (470-399", "circa 470"), where the next token is a digit. It stays quiet on similar year spaces in other history contexts.
result.label: Year-start separator in ancient Greek dates

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' simultane' (simultaneity, simultaneous), mostly in physics/relativity text. It predicts suffix continuations like -ity/-ous, as shown by members that detect similar stems (continu, proxim, autonom).
result.label: ' simultane' word-stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (' multiple', ' that', ' on', ' with', 'uting') in descriptions of memory interleaving, spreading addresses across memory banks. Silent on ' multiple' in other computing contexts. Logits favor '-ade/-ading' endings, which look unrelated.
result.label: Memory interleaving spread connectors

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' trans' (start of a split word), strongest in 'phase trans-' before 'itions'. Weaker on other trans- words like transcends, transpiration, Fourier Transform. Predicts continuations such as 'itions', 'fers', 'itional'.
result.label: ' trans' prefix, phase transitions

result.description: Fires on "purposes" or "functions" (also roles, uses) when they follow adjectives like distinct, diverse, unique or multiple, in phrases about things serving different purposes or roles.
result.label: Purposes/functions after "serve distinct"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fost' in "foster/fostering/fosters" as a verb in workplace or communication text. It predicts the completion 'er', 'ering' or 'ers'. It stays silent when ' fost' starts a sentence or document.
result.label: ' fost' of verb foster

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ptic' in "haptic" (also 'ic' in "Haptic"), in text about haptic feedback and technology. It predicts continuations like glove, feedback and correction. The contrast text on interactive environments stays silent.
result.label: haptic word piece 'ptic'

result.description: Fires on ' into' right after a verb of change or development (evolved into, expanded into, turn into), where the next word names the resulting form. Silent on ' into' after nouns like "research into" or "insight into", or after "integrating into".
result.label: ' into' after evolve/transform verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (mostly ' the', also ' for', ' like') and word pieces in mathematical/technical text, e.g. Riemann hypothesis, induction, algebra. Silent on ' the' in writing/literary text. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: ' the' in mathematical text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ded' at the start of "deductive", and on ' Cont' before "inuous" in tense names. Predicts continuation pieces like 'uct' and 'inu'. Mostly a detector of these split word beginnings.
result.label: ' ded' / ' Cont' word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' harm' when it begins "harmony" or "harmonious" (e.g. "visual harmony", "culinary harmony"), and predicts continuations like 'ony'. It stays silent on ' harm' in "harmonizing" after a verb.
result.label: ' harm' start of harmony

result.description: Fires on the final piece of "photosynthesis" (' thesis' after 'photosyn'), and less on 'iration' in "respiration", in biology text on plant metabolism. Silent on other biology topic lists.
result.label: photosynthesis / respiration word ending

result.description: Fires on the token ' class' (and 'class') in technical contexts such as machine-learning classifiers, inheritance, and taxonomy. It predicts suffixes like -ification, -ified and -ifier. It stays quiet on 'class' as a verb stem or in social-class dynamics.
result.label: ' class' before -ifier/-ification

result.description: Fires on a comma right after a coordinated pair of concepts ("X and Y,") in academic-style text, where a clause like "which are fundamental/essential" or "respectively" follows. Predicts words like both, two, respectively.
result.label: Comma after paired concepts "X and Y,"

result.description: Fires on function words (to, of, being, involves) right after animals/species/survival subjects in biology text about physiological states like hibernation, where a description of the state or its outcome comes next. Silent on 'of' in other phrases like 'birds of paradise'.
result.label: Function words in animal survival biology

result.description: Fires on 'stone' in 'cornerstone' when used figuratively as a foundational concept ("a cornerstone of theory"). Weakly on similar words like 'staple'. Predicts 'of', 'in', 'upon' next.
result.label: cornerstone as foundational concept

result.description: Fires on the word " strength" (e.g. tensile strength, shear strength, strength-ening). The contrast text contains no "strength" token. Output pushes towards suffixes like -ening, -ened, -ens, and plural s.
result.label: Token ' strength'

result.description: Fires on the noun " use" in "the use of" after "involves/requires/necessitates the", in expository text about methods. Silent when "use" is a verb ("we use", "to use"). Predicts " of".
result.label: Noun "use" in "the use of"

result.description: Fires on "such as" / "like" / "including" introducing examples after "civilizations" or ancient societies, predicting a named ancient culture next (Greece, Mesopotamia, Egypt). Silent on "such as" after other nouns (systems, services, workers).
result.label: "such as" before ancient civilizations

result.description: Fires on "itation" in the Wikipedia-style "[citation needed]" tag (also "clarification" in "[clarification needed]"), and predicts " needed". Silent on "itation" inside ordinary words like "hesitation".
result.label: citation needed tag

result.description: Fires on list-introducing words ("including", "such as", "include", commas) right after "environmental factors" in biology text about plant or microbial growth. It predicts the factors that follow, such as temperature, light exposure, availability and nutrients.
result.label: Introducing environmental factor lists

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ance' (also 'ances', 'ening') completing the verb "enhance" (or heighten) in writing/literature text, predicting an object like "the richness". Silent on 'ance' in nouns such as resonance or substance.
result.label: enh-ance verb suffix

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments that begin a known multi-piece name or term, mainly ' A' in "Middle Ages" and ' Haw' in "Hawking", also ' Bol' and ' Dar'. It predicts the continuation piece (ges, king, tons).
result.label: Name-start fragments (Middle A|ges, Haw|king)

result.description: Fires mainly on 'une' inside "cuneiform" (c-une-iform) and on the hyphen in "COVID-19", mid-word or mid-compound pieces where a specific completion follows. Silent on 'une' in "lune-isform", a different word.
result.label: cuneiform 'une' and COVID- hyphen

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "the beginning/start/genesis" when describing an event marking the start of an era or development. Silent on ' of' after other nouns like "introduction", "understanding", "advantage", "Age". Predicts a, an, significant.
result.label: "beginning of" in era-marking phrases

result.description: Fires on function words (" of", " the", " how") right after measurement or quantifying words (measurement of, measures the, quantifies how), predicting magnitude nouns like distance, intensity, dispersion. Silent on other " of" phrases such as "in terms of" or "course of".
result.label: Function word after measuring verbs

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ref' when it begins a word like refinement, refining, reflexive or refraction, mostly after "the" or "and". It predicts continuations such as 'in', 'lections' and 'ined'. It is silent on 'reflecting'.
result.label: ' ref' word-start (refinement)

result.description: Fires on names of software tools, languages and libraries (Jenkins, Python, Perl, GitHub, MySQL, PyTorch pieces) inside lists of developer tools. Silent on generic continuous-integration prose. Boosts next tokens like library/libraries.
result.label: Software tool and language names

result.description: Fires on the word ' fuel' as a noun, mostly in nuclear reactor text (fuel cycle, fuel fabrication, fuel processing). It predicts continuations such as pellet, rod, cells and assemblies. Engine-fuel contexts also appear in the members.
result.label: ' fuel' noun token

result.description: Fires on the word "key" (key/Key), mostly in cryptography text such as "symmetric key", "asymmetric key", "key distribution". It also fires more weakly on "key factor". Members detect "key" and encryption context.
result.label: "key" in cryptography

result.description: Fires on ' is' after a long abstract noun-phrase subject (e.g. "monitoring of pH levels", "effective scheduling"), in formal expository text, where an evaluative predicate like "essential" is expected. Silent on short subjects or "goal is".
result.label: ' is' after abstract nominal subject

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (to, with, of, for, or, near, clear) in expository text, where a noun phrase is expected next. No dominant token; the contrast shows it silent on many ' to' uses.
result.label: Scattered connectors before noun phrase

result.description: Fires on creative-production verbs (wrote, composed, performed, created) right after a subject like composers, troubadours or artists, in historical text about music, poetry and art. Predicts works, songs, or poetry as the object.
result.label: Artists' creation verbs (wrote/composed)

result.description: Fires on the head noun (behavior, relationships, trade, plural endings) that is the object of "impact/influence/affect", where an adverb or outcome word like "significantly" or "outcome" would come next. It is silent on "behavior" in other constructions.
result.label: Object noun after impact/influence verbs

result.description: Fires on the pronoun " it" (or "It") starting a new clause after a semicolon, comma or period, where it refers back to a abstract subject like a strategy or process and the next word is a verb such as "also includes" or "provides".
result.label: Clause-initial " it" before verb

result.description: Fires on mixed function words and fragments (mostly ' of', also 'not', ' new', ' network') in technical or academic prose, often where a technical term such as a language or science word comes next. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' of' is often silent.
result.label: Scattered ' of' in technical prose

result.description: Fires on verbs of bringing about or promoting (create, creating, promote, achieve, foster) in urban planning text, where the next word is likely a desirable urban quality like mixed-use, compact or walkable. Silent on 'create' in a non-urban employment context.
result.label: Urban-planning 'create/promote' verbs

result.description: Fires on connectors (and, in, including, commas) in lists of application domains for AI/technology, where the next item is a sector like health, security, retail, or autonomous systems. Silent on 'and' in generic lists of abstract nouns.
result.label: Connectors before application-domain lists

result.description: Fires on "not" (or n't) after a copula or auxiliary like is/are/should, in a "X is not just/only/merely…" frame. It predicts "just", "only" or "merely" next. It stays quiet on "not" after does, choose or "were", or in "not just through".
result.label: "is not" predicting "just/only"

result.description: Fires on linking words (that, through, by) after verbs or nouns in economics text about supply-side growth, where a mechanism or causal claim follows (e.g. "is that", "achieved through"). Silent on some 'that' in similar claim phrasing, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Supply-side economics linking words

result.description: Fires on the word piece "our" in "contour", mostly in topographic map and contour line text. Members also detect "our" in other words (outsourcing, Gourmet), and the target predicts "line", "lines" and similar next.
result.label: "our" in "contour"

result.description: Fires on verbs and linking words (-ing, 'ensuring', 'for', 'keeping', 'empowers') that come before an object of benefit or outcome in business and IT-strategy writing, for example 'critical for ensuring the sustained...'. It is silent on many other -ing endings.
result.label: Business purpose verbs: ensuring, for

result.description: Fires on the word piece " met" when it is the start of a longer word such as metaphor, metals, metabolic or meticulous, and pushes the next token toward continuations like "aph", "icul" and "ap". It stays quiet when "met" is the whole word at document start.
result.label: ' met' as start of longer word

result.description: Fires on ' is' right after an abstract noun-phrase subject (e.g. "Its beauty is", "the diversity of styles and loops is"), where the next word is likely an evaluative or predicate word. Silent after pronouns, "that", or "there".
result.label: ' is' after abstract noun subject

result.description: Fires most on ' relativ' (relativity/relativistic) in physics-style text, but also weakly on scattered function words like ' of' and ' the'. It stays silent on ' relativ' in moral/cultural relativism. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: ' relativ' in physics, plus scattered ' of'

result.description: Fires on the 'ier' piece completing "Le Chatelier", right before "'s Principle". It is silent on a lowercase "chatelier" in a different context. It pushes the next token towards " Princi".
result.label: 'ier' in Le Chatelier

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verb pieces (it in "exhibit", of, between, like, convey, capture) in explanatory text on photography, physics and science, where a noun phrase is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed function words in science/photography text

result.description: Fires on 'ic' completing "Strategic", strongest in title-like headings at document start (e.g. "Strategic Resource Allocation"). Weaker mid-sentence, and silent on 'ic' in other words or some mid-sentence "strategic" uses.
result.label: 'ic' in "Strategic" headings

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' disc' after an adjective like scholarly, philosophical or Hindu, where it starts 'discourse' (or discriminate). Silent when ' disc' begins a document or follows a semicolon. Predicts 'ourse'.
result.label: ' disc' before 'ourse'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' forec' (start of forecast/forecasters/forecasting), mostly in business or economic text. It pushes the next token towards 'ast', 'asted', 'aster' and 'asts'. Upstream members are mostly ' forec' detectors.
result.label: ' forec' word-piece predicting 'ast'

result.description: Fires on the token ' followed', mostly in sequence statements like "X, followed by Y" that describe one event or stage coming after another. It pushes the next token toward ' closely', ' by' and time spans.
result.label: ' followed' in sequence phrases

result.description: Fires mainly on the word-piece " Ent" at the start of "Entropy" or "Entanglement", especially in headings or at the start of a sentence. Members are mostly Ent/ent detectors. Weak activity elsewhere on function words.
result.label: Ent- piece (Entropy/Entanglement)

result.description: Fires on the word " virtual" (occasionally " digital") as a modifier before a noun like space, environment or reality, mostly in texts about art and technology. Members are detectors of virtual/digital.
result.label: " virtual" modifier before nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' prompt' (prompts, prompting, promptly), mainly when a suffix is expected next. Logits favor suffixes like -ly, -s, -ness, -ing. Members are mostly ' prompt' detectors, plus ' trigger'.
result.label: ' prompt' token before suffix

result.description: Fires on a comma (or dash) right after "all" or a sentence-initial adverb like "after all," or "sometimes,". Members detect "all" plus quantifier-like continuations. Silent on commas elsewhere, e.g. after clauses.
result.label: Comma after "all" / "after all"

result.description: Fires on connectors (and, comma, 's, their) right after "credibility"/"trustworthiness" in explanations of ethos in rhetoric, where the next word is likely authority, trust, character or credentials. Silent on 'and' in other persuasion text.
result.label: Ethos credibility list connectors

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (plural endings, commas, 'and', 'for', 'years', 'monument') in abstract academic or expository prose about environment, science and society. Peaks are inconsistent, with no single token or construction. The logits are unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the 'ene' piece in "entrepreneur/entrepreneurs/entrepreneurial/entrepreneurship", after "entrepr", and pushes toward the continuation 'ur'/'urs'. Upstream members are mostly 'ene' detectors in the same word.
result.label: 'ene' inside entrepreneur

result.description: Fires on scattered function and verb tokens (the, exposed, improve, when, to) in technical chemistry, materials and surface-science text, often where a chemistry-related noun is expected next. Peaks are mixed and weak; the circuit is low-faithfulness.
result.label: Chemistry/materials text, mixed function words

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' of', ',', 'ic', 'ing', ' and', ' into') in academic or health/science prose, where the next word is open. It stays silent on ' of' in computer-science text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is low.
result.label: Function words in academic health prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' whe' (mostly the start of "wheat", e.g. in lists of crops), predicting the continuation "at". A few weak firings occur on commas and 'of'.
result.label: ' whe' piece before "at" (wheat)

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' des' (also ' ent') when it begins a longer word such as desperately, desires, desirable, and predicts continuations like -ire, -irable, -perate. Mostly silent elsewhere.
result.label: ' des' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (and, to, the, be, current, match) in technical or expository prose, where the next word is a technical noun or verb. Peaks are inconsistent; the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the final piece "or" in "Semiconduct|or" (semiconductor), predicting physics/devices/materials continuations. It stays silent on "conduct|or" (conductor) and on "tailor", so it needs the word semiconductor.
result.label: "or" ending semiconductor

result.description: Fires on the word "dynamic"/"Dynamic" as an adjective, most strongly in technical phrases like "dynamic typing", "dynamic routing", "dynamic memory allocation". It weakly fires in general "dynamic competitors". It promotes next tokens like typing, dispatch, adjust.
result.label: "dynamic" adjective, technical

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' expl' (or 'pl' after 'Ex') when it begins the word "exploration"/"explorers", predicting continuations like 'oration', 'orer', 'oring'. Mostly in history/Age of Exploration text.
result.label: expl- start of exploration

result.description: Fires on the word ' utility', most strongly in economics or utilitarian-theory text (utility of consumption, marginal utility). It is weaker in the plain 'usefulness' sense. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' utility' token (economics sense)

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (with, from, as, involves, include, addresses) that follow a technical subject in definitional academic text and introduce what it involves or deals with. Peaks are scattered and weakly consistent. Silent on "benefits from".
result.label: Connector after technical topic noun

result.description: Fires on "demonstrate" (and "demonstrating") as a verb whose subject is people or groups, in leadership or workplace text. It predicts a following quality noun such as commitment, dedication, respect or integrity.
result.label: verb "demonstrate" before virtue nouns

result.description: Fires on the word " failure" (rarely " fail"), mostly in engineering and fatigue-analysis text, where it is followed by "modes" or similar. Upstream members are failure-token detectors plus fatigue, loading and stress context.
result.label: ' failure' token, engineering fatigue context

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments of rare technical or scientific terms, especially 'oz' in Paleozoic/Mesozoic, plus pieces like Han, Pale, ith, and garbled byte tokens. It is silent on 'oz' in Cenozoic and Proterozoic, so it is inconsistent.

result.description: Fires on tokens a few positions into a document that opens with "While" or "Although", landing on varied following tokens (apostrophes, word pieces, hyphens). Members detect the opening "While" and document-start newlines.

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ops' completing the word "workshops" (worksh|ops). It relies on the preceding 'worksh' fragment, and members detect 'ops' and other word-ending pieces.

result.description: Fires on the 'ries' ending of "symmet|ries" (plural of symmetry), especially in physics text on gauge or global symmetries. Silent when "ries" follows a bare 'met' fragment without the 'symmet' context.

result.description: Fires on database-related nouns (stores, schema, design, databases, data) in discussions of NoSQL/SQL database types and schema flexibility. Silent in relational normalization text. Members are mostly database/data token detectors.

result.description: Fires weakly on the 'y' of "mastery" (and "of" after "master") in text about mastering correlative conjunctions. It is inconsistent, since it is silent on the same 'y' in similar contexts. The evidence is thin and the members are generic.

result.description: Fires on the piece 'eries' completing the word "galleries" (after "gall"), mostly in art and museum contexts. Members include 'eries' detectors and art/museum topic features.

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, often word endings or pieces ('cer', 'ats', 'ation', 'ries') and words after 'across'/'types'/'formats' in technical text about varying systems. Evidence is mixed and weak; the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Weak, scattered circuit. Peaks on ' mask' and the words right after it (' off', ' confusion') in one repeated sentence about "might mask...", plus stray apostrophes. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin and mixed.

result.description: Fires mostly on " for" right after "essential"/"crucial" (importance adjectives), as in "is essential for X". Silent on some "for" cases, e.g. after "allow" or "planning", so it depends on that construction.

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ous' (and 'ard') completing the word "hazardous" after "hazard"/"Haz". It stays silent on 'ous' in other words like "meticulous" or "continuous". Members detect hazard pieces and 'ous' endings.

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'icus' ending of "Copernicus" (also weakly on related tokens after Copernicus). Members detect the Cop/ern/icus pieces of the name.

result.description: Fires on pieces of the word "finance" (mainly "ance" after "fin", also " fin", " psych") in academic text about finance and technology or economics. It stays silent on "ance" in "nuance" or "enhance".

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (and, of, Information, Linear, word continuations) in text near the start of documents about computer science and related academic fields. Silent on 'and' in mid-document technical sentences. Weak, mixed evidence.

result.description: Fires on ' like' right after "'s" (it's like...) when introducing an analogy or comparison, often followed by a gerund ("like being on", "like playing"). Silent on "look like" or "appear like", and in some "it's like" contexts.

result.description: Fires on word pieces completing "lyre"/"lyric" (re, ric) and "aulos" (ulos) in text about ancient music or poetry, after the piece "ly". Members detect "ly", "lyr" and music words.

result.description: Fires on tokens in the slot right after the phrase "The foundation of" at document start (e.g. "of", "structure", "systems", "construction"). Members detect "foundation" and ' of'. It stays silent on ' of' in other phrases.

result.description: Fires on ' industrial' (and following nouns like policies, processes, industry) when it is used as a modern adjective for industry/manufacturing, often at document start. Silent when it is part of 'industrial revolution' or historical-era phrasing.
result.label: modern 'industrial' adjective, not revolution

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces (clever, displays, manip-, soph-, strateg-) inside abstract expository text about skills, techniques and writing, often after an adjective like "effective". Peaks are scattered, and the circuit failed, so the evidence is weak.

result.description: Fires on single digit tokens (0, 8, 3, 7, 5) inside hyphen-separated numeric sequences, such as angle lists, scores or measurement series. It stays quiet on digits within years or decades like "20th" or "1960s".
result.label: Digits in hyphenated number sequences

result.description: Fires on body-part/sense-organ nouns, mainly ' ears' (also eye, skin, windows), when listed alongside other sense organs such as "eyes, ears, nose". Members detect eye, gaze, sensory and ears tokens.
result.label: Sense organ nouns in lists (ears)
Suffix pieces of "restrict" words
result.description: Fires on the word piece completing or being "restrict" (restrict-s, restrict-ive, non-restrict-ive, restricting), in text about restrictive clauses and limiting. It stays quiet on 's' in other words like "truths".

Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on mixed tokens (' Prize', ' este', 'ie', ' Women', ' who' after a name). Members are mostly generic token detectors; only a Prize/award member is discriminative. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered mixed tokens, Prize/award hint

result.description: Fires on ' being' (also ' considered', ' widely') right after a sentence-opening concessive "Despite" or "Rather than/While", where a participle phrase begins. Silent on 'being' as a noun or mid-sentence gerund.
result.label: 'being' after sentence-initial Despite

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'al' completing the word "disposal" (dispos+al), mostly in waste-management text. It stays silent on 'al' in other words such as "accidental" or "detrimental".
result.label: 'al' in "disposal"

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ization" when it completes a word after a stem (mechan-, industrial-, urban-, global-), strongest in industrialization/mechanization contexts. Silent when "ization" starts a text with no stem before it.
result.label: -ization suffix after word stem

result.description: Fires on the continuation piece 'iment' (also 'iments', 'ary') after the word-start 'sed', completing "sediment" in geology/sedimentology text. Members are 'sed' and 'iment' detectors plus glacier and rock context.
result.label: sed|iment word completion

result.description: Fires on " progress" (occasionally " change") when it directly follows an adjective like "Technological" or "Morphological" in a title-like or list-like phrase. It stays silent when "progress" follows other words such as "significant", "continued" or "led to".
result.label: Progress after "-ological" adjective

result.description: Fires on word-ending pieces like 'ation' (innovation), 'ric', 'ision', and ' UI', mostly in tech-history prose. It is inconsistent: it stays silent on 'ation' in other similar contexts. The circuit is weak and mostly generic members.
result.label: Suffix 'ation' in tech-era text

result.description: Fires on " system"/" systems" after "circulatory" (circulation-related text). Silent on "system" after respiratory, cardiovascular, or "This". Members detect "circul" and "blood" tokens.
result.label: system after circulatory

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens (word pieces like 'ance', 'iv', ' a', quotes) in generated text about data encryption and security. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mixed tokens in encryption text

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ency' completing "contingency", mainly in "contingency planning/plans" in risk-mitigation text. It stays silent on 'ency' in other words (transparency, consistency) and when "contingency" ends a phrase.
result.label: 'ency' in contingency planning

result.description: Fires on forms of "raise" (raised, raising, raise) and the "row" piece of "eyebrow", often in eyebrow-raising contexts. Weaker on the words following "raise" (e.g. "a child"). Silent in unrelated technical text.
result.label: raise / eyebrow word forms

result.description: Fires on sentence-initial " Over" and on "course" in "Over the course of", the opening of a time-span phrase; also weakly on "over time" and "Over-" prefix words. Members detect " Over" tokens and word-initial pieces.
result.label: Sentence-initial "Over the course"

result.description: Fires on pieces of "emblem" (emblem, emblematic) and on " of" right after emblem/emblematic, i.e. "emblem of X". Stays silent on " of" after ordinary nouns like "examples of" or "sound of".
result.label: emblem(atic) and "emblem of"

result.description: Fires on pieces of the name "Huygens" (Huyg-ens, -Fresnel, Principle) and weakly on optics/wave words like light, wave, lenses. Mostly a Huygens-name detector in physics text, with a mixed set of peaks.
result.label: Huygens name and wave optics

result.description: Fires on punctuation and connectives (period, comma, "which", "in", "while") after finance text about currency, exchange rates, swaps, and derivatives. Silent on periods after "etc." or in non-finance lists. Members detect finance terms like currency, futures, and rates.
result.label: Punctuation in currency/finance text

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside "epidemiology" and its derivatives (epidemi-ological, -ology, -ologist, epide-mi). Silent on "-ological" in other words such as "biological", so it needs the epidemiology word context.
result.label: epidemiology word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ic' inside "ridicule/ridiculed" (rid|ic|ule), typically in humor or satire text. It stays silent on 'ic' in other words such as caricature, heroic, hyperbolic.
result.label: 'ic' inside "ridicule"

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on mixed tokens (' or', ' number', ' BE', 'ON', function words) in technical or academic text. Members are generic token detectors with no discriminative structure; the evidence is mixed and unclear.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token low-confidence latent

result.description: Fires on preservation/protection verbs (preserve, restore, protected, safeguarding) in art and cultural-heritage conservation text. Silent on "to preserve" in environmental/ecosystem contexts. Members detect museum, art, and conservation words.
result.label: Preserve/restore in art conservation

result.description: Fires on the noun after "intercultural"/"cross-cultural" (communication, interactions, context) and on the "ural" piece of "intercultural". Silent on "communication" in other phrases, such as "nonverbal communication" or "communication styles".
result.label: Intercultural communication head word

result.description: Fires on the word right after "soil" in soil-science and geotechnical text (soil properties, health, strength, sampling, quality). Silent on "properties" after other nouns or fragments like "il". Members detect "soil" and material words.
result.label: Word following "soil" in soil text

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside or just after words beginning with "h" (hatching, hedging, hormone, honeybees, hues), mostly mid-word fragments like 'atch', 'ed', 'orm', and ' h'. Predicts continuations of h-words.
result.label: h-word fragments (hormone, hedging)

result.description: Fires on ' with' that follows a comma after a full clause, opening an absolute/elaborating phrase ("..., with each genre..."). It stays silent on instrumental or accompaniment 'with' directly after a noun or verb, as in "plowing fields with a smile".
result.label: Clause-final comma ', with' construction

result.description: Fires on the word "function"/"functions" in mathematical or programming text (derivatives, composite functions, higher-order functions). Members are mostly detectors of "function(s)" plus math-topic words. Silent on unrelated math-flavored text without the word.
result.label: word "function(s)" in math context

result.description: Fires mostly on the "aps" piece of "swaps" in financial derivatives text (interest rate or currency swaps), and weakly on pieces like "changed" in "exchanged" and "ational". Silent on "aps" at the start of a sentence or in other contexts.

result.description: Fires on mid-word or word-ending fragments (e.g. 'ic', 'ank', 'ising', 'les') inside longer compound or split words. Peaks are scattered and contrast shows silence on the same pieces in other words, so the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ations'/'ation' completing the word "fluctuations" (fluctuation). Silent on 'ations' in other words like concentrations, innovations, installations. Members detect the "fluct"/"fl-uct-u" pieces before it.

result.description: Fires on the token ' structure' as a head noun, especially after a modifier like secondary, tertiary, quaternary, or basic. It is silent on "Phrase Structure Rules", where the word is capitalized and part of a title. Members are mostly detectors of 'structure' and similar words.
result.label: ' structure' after modifier

result.description: Fires on word-piece suffixes (-ative, -ation, -ated, -oti) inside the word "Negotiation/Negation/Negative" right after the "Neg" piece. It stays silent on "-ative" in other words like "innovative".

result.description: Fires in text about Alessandro Volta and his battery: on 'ile' (pile), ' battery' after Volta's, and the digits of the date 1800s. Silent on 'ile' in unrelated words like anopile. Members detect 'Vol' (Volta) plus electricity/chemistry words.

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ol' inside multi-piece words, such as Ne-ol-ithic, phosph-ol-ipid, Cop-ol-ymers, cholester-ol and soil orders like Gelis-ol. Needs a preceding word fragment.

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase nouns and word pieces (auditory, shock, rain, Hamiltonian, reaction), often in technical or science text. It is inconsistent, and the members are generic token detectors, so the pattern is weak.

MAP in WMAP spacecraft name

Plural ending of event nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' brid' (start of bridge/bridging/bridged) when it is split from its suffix, and weakly on 'const' and 'fost'. Predicts suffix pieces like 'ges', 'ged', 'ging'.

result.description: Fires on the piece 'os' completing "logos" in the rhetoric triad "ethos, pathos, and logos". Silent on 'os' at document start or ending a name like "Atropopoulos". Weaker on ' ag' in agility/agile.

result.description: Fires on the piece 'NG' at the end of capitalized acronyms such as QRNG, RNG and PNG, where the letters before it spell out the acronym. Weak activation on a few other word pieces.

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'iss' inside longer words such as Meissner, fortississimo and permissibility. It weakly fires on a few other mid-word pieces. Members are mostly 'iss' detectors in early layers.

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'pe' inside words split into tokens, like ins-pe-ctions, tra-pe-zoids, chick-pe-as, tightro-pe, single-pe-aked. Weaker on 'cope' and 'grape'. Members are mostly 'pe' detectors.

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ics' (or 'ic') completing "mechanics", especially "Quantum Mechanics". It stays quiet on 'ics' in other words such as thermodynamics, electrostatics and basics.

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' construct' (as in constructivism, constructive, constructs, theoretical construct), mostly when it starts a word that continues with a suffix. Members are mostly ' construct' token detectors.

result.label: ' vari' word-start piece (varieties)

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ed' in "craft+ed" / "handcraft+ed" (crafted with care, handcrafted features). Silent on 'ed' after other stems like root-ed, convey-ed, adorn-ed, so it needs the craft stem.
result.label: 'ed' after craft stem

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ur' at the start of a split word such as urgent, urgency, urinary or urine. Members are mostly detectors of ' ur' and of other word-start fragments.
result.label: ' ur' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'ib' in "Fibonacci" (also 'im', ' Rem', 'Math'), early in a multi-piece word after a capitalized first piece. Silent when 'ib' starts the text with no preceding piece.
result.label: 'ib' inside Fibonacci-like words

result.description: Fires on the verb "represent" (and representing/represented) when a plural or subject noun, like nodes, edges, or a variable symbol, is said to stand for something. Common in technical explanations of graphs, statistics, and math notation.
result.label: verb "represent" in technical mappings

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'und' (in H-und's, ger-und), 'le', 'atic', ' Ing' (in Ingredients), where a word is split into pieces. Peaks are mixed, with no single clear context; the circuit is weak.
result.label: Mid-word fragments 'und', 'le', 'Ing'

result.description: Fires mainly on the piece 'ier' inside the name "Navier" (Navier-Stokes), with weak activity on 'inclus'/'clus' pieces. Members detect ' Nav', 'kes', and 'ier' pieces from earlier layers.
result.label: 'ier' in Navier-Stokes

result.description: Fires on the token ' electric' (as in electric propulsion, vehicles, charge, fields), mostly as a modifier before a noun. Members detect 'electric' and related electromagnetic words like magnetic, current and field.
result.label: ' electric' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " expected" (occasionally " returns"), in both "expected value/returns" finance phrasing and "it is expected that" uses. Built from early-layer detectors of "expected"/"expect" tokens plus finance-related context members.
result.label: " expected" token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' fost' (as in fostering), and also on ' innov', ' team', ' orch' and similar partial word pieces in business or tech prose, where a word is unfinished and about to be completed.
result.label: ' fost' and similar word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on word-ending pieces like 'els' in "Markov Models", 'folio' (portfolio), and ' crisis' in "financial crisis". It is a mix of tokens in technical or finance text, with some completion of split words (Mod-els, Mod-us).
result.label: Word-ending pieces: Models, portfolio, crisis

result.description: Fires on word endings (-ating, -ations, -ates) and ' translate' when they continue the word family of "translate/translation/translator". Silent on other -ating words like "incorporating" or "elevating".
result.label: translate/translation word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cry' when it begins "crystal"-type words (crystallization, crystal lattice) in physics and chemistry text. It stays silent when ' cry' is at the very start of the document, as in "crystallograph…".
result.label: ' cry' in crystal words

result.description: Fires on the token right after "public" (-ly, -ity, hyphen, " and"), such as "publicly", "publicity", "public-private". Silent on "-ly" after other words like "increasingly" or "solely". Members detect "public" and its common continuations.
result.label: Word-piece continuing "public"
' like' introducing example names
result.description: Fires on ' like' (also 'such' of 'such as') after a plural group noun such as artists, writers or theologians, where a list of example people is about to follow. Silent when ' like' lacks that preceding noun.

Fires on the piece 'cept' inside "Concept" (e.g. "Conceptual Framework"), also in "receptors". It stays silent when 'cept' starts the document with no "Con" before it. It predicts suffixes like 'ual'.
result.label: 'cept' in Concept/receptor

result.description: Fires on mid-word suffix pieces completing a rare word, mostly 'ifies' in "signifies", also 'pler' in Kepler and 'ieve' in Sieve. Members detect the "sign" + ified/ifier/age family. Fairly mixed peaks.
result.label: Word-ending pieces: signifies, Kepler, Sieve

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ance' (also 'ence') completing a noun like surveillance, reluctance or dominance. It stays quiet on 'ance' in 'finance' and 'enhance', so it needs the noun-suffix use after a word stem.
result.label: -ance noun suffix in surveillance

result.description: Fires on a noun (tool, option, advantages) right after an evaluative adjective such as essential, crucial, advanced, significant, in expository technical text. It is weaker on other nouns in similar slots.
result.label: Noun after evaluative adjective

result.description: Fires on words like "combined", "equally", "equal" and "lying" in probability and math explanations (e.g. "equally likely", "combined probability"). Peaks are mixed and the logits are unclear. Members are mostly math and statistics context.
result.label: Equal/combined in probability text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sem' when it begins "semiconductor" in materials/electronics text, after words like n-type, doped, pure, extrinsic. Silent when ' sem' starts the text with no preceding context.
result.label: ' sem' in semiconductor

result.description: Fires on the token " Roman" (also Byzantine pieces) in history text about Rome and the Eastern Roman Empire, usually after "the". Silent when " Roman" starts the text. Members are Roman, ancient-history and Greek/Latin detectors.
result.label: ' Roman' in ancient history text

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ation' completing the word "incorporation" (after 'incorpor'). It stays silent on 'ation' in other words such as experimentation, narration and reevaluation. It weakly fires on 'vulner' in "vulnerability".
result.label: 'ation' in "incorporation"

result.description: Fires on participle/adjective words like " desired", " opposed", " measured" that precede a noun or "to" after verbs such as achieve, maintain, compare (e.g. "achieve desired effects", "as opposed to"). Mostly the token " desired".
result.label: "desired"/"opposed" past-participle modifiers

result.description: Fires on the period ending a person's name in lists of names with titles (Dr., Prof., Professor), one name per line. Silent on periods in abbreviations like etc., i.e., e.g. Weaker on ordinary sentence-final periods.
result.label: Period after names in title lists

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece ' Bron' (Bronze Age, Brønsted-Lowry) when it starts a word after 'the' or similar. It also fires weakly on 'this' and on pieces like ' sa' and ' Bro'. It stays silent on 'Bronze-aged' at document start.
