result.description: Fires on " security" or " encryption" when it follows an adjective or modifier (strong, effective, robust, regular, multi-layered) in cybersecurity text. It stays silent on "data security", where a noun precedes it.
result.label: security after adjective modifier

result.description: Fires on ' to' in the phrase "due to", typically in a parenthetical giving a cause in technical text. It stays silent on ' to' after verbs or nouns such as "lead to", "contribute to" and "sensitivity to", and in infinitive "to".
result.label: "to" in "due to"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' of', ' vector', ' field', ' integr', ' curve') inside advanced math text about curl, vector fields and integrals, such as Stokes' theorem. It stays silent on ' of' in non-math or generic contexts.
result.label: Vector calculus context tokens

result.description: Fires on determiner-like words such as " these", " various", " their" before a plural noun in academic or explanatory text. It is inconsistent, since it is silent on many " these" tokens. Members are generic and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Plural determiners these/various/their

result.description: Fires on the object word or adjective right after a verb of seeking or wanting (seeks, sought, wanted, hoping), such as "innovative", "new", "authentic", "warm". It is silent on the same word pieces in other contexts.
result.label: Object after seek/want verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' them', ' and', ' before', ' who', ' that', 'wide') in abstract academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent and members are generic token detectors, so no clear pattern emerges.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word or word piece right after the degree adverb "too" (too hard, too soft, too talkative, too intricately, too much, too excessive), i.e. the adjective/adverb being modified. Silent on "over" in unrelated uses like "overboard" or "excitement over".
result.label: Word following "too"

result.description: Fires on the suffix of "advancements"/"advances" (ements, ances, ancement), typically as a subject noun before "in <field>" in scientific or technological history. Silent in one case after "intellectual advancements," so context matters.
result.label: advancements/advances suffix token

result.description: Fires on the determiner (' the', ' this', or a space before a year) right after "during", where a time period or era is expected (e.g. "during the 19..."). Silent after "in", "since", "as".
result.label: Determiner after "during"
' altern' word-piece (alternating)
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' altern', almost always in 'alternating' (also 'alternatively'). Members are detectors of word-start pieces that precede suffixes like -ating/-ation, plus ' altern' token detectors in early layers.

Fires on the token right after "slip" in ceramics terms such as "slip-casting", "slip casting", "slip preparation" and "slip molding". It also fires weakly after similar word pieces like "dip" and "flip". The members are mostly material, art and process detectors.
result.label: Token after "slip" in ceramics

result.description: Fires on word pieces and tokens right after the word "quadratic" in math or computing text (Nyquist 'qu', 'ues' in residues, 'tion' in probation, programming (). Weak, mixed evidence; the members are mostly generic math and word-piece detectors.
result.label: Pieces following 'quadratic' in math text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (processing, or, in, compression pieces, degradation) that directly follow the word "image" in image-processing text. Silent on " or" after other nouns like sensor or telescope.
result.label: Token after "image" in imaging text

result.description: Fires on the last piece of an adjective inside a negated comparison "not as ADJ as" (e.g. "While not as well-known as", "not as prevalent as"), just before the second "as". Quiet outside this construction.
result.label: Adjective ending in "not as ADJ as"

result.description: Attention-layer latent peaking on scattered tokens (' that', ' and', ' the', ' life', word pieces) in academic/essay prose, with no consistent token or context. Silent on many ' that' cases. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks, unclear

result.description: Fires on ' in' (also ' from', ' results') right after "results"/"resulting"/"result" in a causal "X results in Y" construction. It stays silent on ' in' in other uses, such as "in compliance" or "in baking".
result.label: "results in" causal preposition

result.description: Fires on "person" (or "third"/"-") in "close third-person" narration, driven by members detecting the word "close". It stays silent on "second-person", "first-person" and plain "third-person" without a preceding "close".
result.label: "close third-person" narration

result.description: Fires on the 'ab' piece in "Athabaskan" right after "Ath", and more weakly on 'ens' in "Athens". It stays silent on 'ab' in "vocabulary". Members mostly detect " Ath" and Greek/Athens-related pieces.
result.label: 'ab' after Ath (Athabaskan)

result.description: Fires on the word "for" when it opens a parenthetical or gloss giving purpose or intended use, as in "he (for a male person)" or "logging (for well characterization)". It is quiet on "for" directly after a noun in a list.
result.label: "for" in parenthetical purpose glosses

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Land" (as in Landscape, Landscaping, Land-on), mostly at the start of a document. Members detect " land" and similar word-start pieces. Predicts continuations like "sc".
result.label: ' Land' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on ' Paul' right after "Federal Reserve Chairman" (before Volcker), and weakly on neighbouring tokens in that phrase. Silent on Paul in other contexts such as Paul Samuelson or Ron Paul, so it needs the central-bank chairman context.
result.label: Paul in "Chairman Paul Volcker"

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention-layer target firing on scattered tokens (commas, 'for', 'approach', math notation like braces and exponents) in technical or academic prose. Members are mostly math and technical-term detectors. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit fails faithfulness.
result.label: Diffuse technical/math prose tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and digits (' the', ' an', year digits like 9 or 7 in 1969/1979) mostly after 'to' or in dates. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered 'the' and year digits

result.description: Fires on nouns or modifiers inside a noun phrase that follows a possessive or "such as" style slot (' members', ' existing', ' characteristics'), expecting the phrase to continue. The evidence is thin and mixed, and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Noun-phrase modifiers like members, existing

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after 'back' in "tracing/dating/going back to" (origins in time). Silent on other ' to' uses such as 'turn to' or '14th to the'. Members detect the preceding 'back' token.
result.label: ' to' after 'back' (dating back to)

result.description: Fires mostly on commas that end an item in a list of abstract nouns or phrases (diverse perspectives, cultures, communication styles) in social/cultural prose, where another list item or clause continues. Silent on commas that end a clause.
result.label: Commas in lists of abstract nouns

result.description: Layer-4 attention target firing on scattered tokens (' leaves', ' water', ' that', ' particle', 'ent', ' and') mostly mid-phrase in technical or scientific text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse scientific mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on " has" in "there has been" after an opening time-span phrase ("Over the past decade, there has been…"). It stays silent on " has" after a plain noun subject such as "Significant progress has".
result.label: "there has" after time-span opener

result.description: Fires on the token right after an "-ism" philosophy/movement name used as a subject (e.g. "Realism and", "ism emphas", "ism os"), where a verb or conjunction follows. Silent on "and" in economics and cost text.
result.label: Word after -ism movement subject

result.description: Peaks scatter over unrelated tokens (word pieces like 'mi', ' conduct', ' to', ' which', ' with') mid-phrase in technical or expository text. The logits and members show no coherent pattern; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear
Final M of SIEM acronym
result.description: Fires on the final 'M' of the acronym SIEM (also ' Systems' after SIEM), when the acronym is being completed after 'SIE'. Members detect acronym-ending letters and the IE piece. Silent when the acronym is absent.

Fires on varied tokens ending items in lists of business, technology or academic terms (commas, plural endings, ' an', ' with'). It's weak and inconsistent, and the circuit failed. Members are mostly generic token detectors.
result.label: List items in professional topic lists

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "closer" (also close/near-type words), i.e. the proximity "closer to" construction. It stays silent on ' to' after verbs like "refer to" or after "important to".
result.label: "closer to" proximity ' to'

result.description: Fires on list items, commas, 'and'/'or', and word pieces inside a list of nouns that follows 'conveying'/'essential for conveying' in abstract explanatory prose. It is silent on commas in other lists about symbolism and themes.
result.label: List items after 'conveying'

result.description: Fires on the word right after "in terms" (mostly " of", sometimes " their" or " [" after "in terms of"), i.e. the slot introducing the respect in which something is compared. Silent on " of" in other noun-of phrases.
result.label: "in terms of" continuation

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "analogous" (analogous to). Silent on ' to' in other constructions such as "in addition to", "likened to", or infinitive "to". Members mostly detect the "analog-ous" word pieces.
result.label: ' to' after "analogous"

result.description: Fires on the 'abling' piece of "enabling", typically in a participial clause after a comma ("..., enabling X"). Members detect 'abling' and related allow/enable words (allow, enabled, enables, facilitated, allowing).
result.label: 'abling' in "enabling"

result.description: Fires on scattered word-piece or mid-word tokens (dried, dissolve, merocrine, growth, canvas) in cooking, materials and art text. Peaks are diverse and the circuit failed, so the evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered word pieces, cooking/materials text

result.description: Fires on tokens just after the word "classic" (or "famous"), such as " and", "reci|pes", " ing|redients", where the word after it continues the phrase. It is silent on " and" in other contexts.
result.label: Token following "classic" modifier

result.description: Fires on ' priority' (and the following token such as 'in', 'ues', 'inheritance') in computing/scheduling text like priority queues, inversion and inheritance. Members detect priority, prioritize, task, scheduling and importance words.
result.label: priority in scheduling contexts
Word after "governments" as subject
result.description: Fires on the token right after or at the end of "governments" (e.g. "around", "across", "have", "must", "ments"), where governments is the subject of the clause. Silent on unrelated text without governments.

Fires on the piece 'ar' right after 'plan' (planar, planarity), and more weakly on ' plan' itself. It needs the preceding 'plan' token; standalone 'ar' stays silent. Members detect ' plan' and 'plan-es' tokens.
result.label: 'ar' completing 'planar'

result.description: Fires on the token right after "less than" / "lower than" / "higher than" (often the space before a number like 90 or 180), where a comparative expects a value. Silent after "is", "exactly" or "below".
result.label: Token after comparative "than"
Open paren before abbreviation or name
result.description: Fires mostly on ' (' after a multi-word term or person's name, where an abbreviation or parenthetical follows (e.g. "X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)", "Side-Angle-Side (SAS)"). Stays silent on some similar parentheses, so the condition is unclear.
Fires on the piece 'd' at the end of "Absur" in "Absurd"/"Absurdism" (philosophy text). It stays silent on 'd' in "surdity" without "Ab" before it. Members are generic 'd' detectors.
result.label: 'd' in Absurd/Absurdism

result.description: Fires on the possessive "'" or "s" right after the name Pascal (Pascal's Triangle/Theorem), weakly after other famous names like Smith. Silent on possessives after common nouns like triangle's or theorem's.
result.label: Possessive after Pascal

result.description: Fires on the piece after "Br" inside rare names and words, mainly the 'n' in "Brønsted" (also 'ou' in Brouwer). Silent on ordinary text. Members detect "Br" plus following pieces like 'us' and 'id'.
result.label: Br-prefixed name middle piece (Brønsted)

result.description: Fires on the word " key" as a noun or adjective, e.g. "the key to", "public key", "key steps". It stays silent when "key" is a word fragment (keyboards) or starts a sentence without a preceding "the" or noun-like context.
result.label: word 'key' as noun/adjective

result.description: Fires on mixed function tokens (' on', ',', ' (', ' from') in expository text, often after a noun phrase, such as before an acronym in parentheses. Silent on ' on' after 'impact/emphasis'. Evidence is scattered and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered function-token after noun phrase

result.description: Fires on verbs or modals (had, should, must, becoming) right after a subject noun like "curricula" in education/teaching text, e.g. "it became clear that curricula had to be revised". Members are mostly education/teaching context detectors.
result.label: Modal verb after curricula subject

result.description: Fires on the 'ps' piece inside "ellipsoid"/"ellipsis" (also 'pt' in "elliptical"), after the "elli" prefix. It stays silent on 'ps' in other words such as GPS.
result.label: 'ps' in ellipsoid/ellipsis
Theorem token after named result
result.description: Fires on ' theorem' / ' Theorem' (including 'Theorem' in names like Stokes' Theorem, Chinese Remainder Theorem, and 'automated theorem proving'). Members are mostly detectors of the same token in earlier layers.

Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (word-start pieces like ' pre', ' histor', 'ment', and ' of' in titles) where the next piece likely completes a word or name. Circuit is weak and diffuse; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-word fragment tokens, diffuse

result.description: Fires mainly on the token ' orbit' (and orbit-related pieces) in astronomy or physics text about orbiting bodies and orbitals. Members are mostly orbit/orbital token detectors plus space-related words such as astronaut and celestial body.
result.label: ' orbit' token in astronomy text

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (k, of, and, Street, or, document start). Members are mostly finance/economics and legal word detectors. The evidence shows no coherent trigger; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered finance/legal context, unclear

result.description: Fires on a stray 's' token that follows a sentence-ending period with no space, as in "development.s like Facebook". It looks like a glitchy fragment that starts a new word. It stays silent on plural 's' attached to a noun.
result.label: Stray 's' after period

result.description: Fires on the verb or word-start right after "to" in "using X to [verb]" purpose clauses (facilitate, reveal, create, control), often the first piece of a longer verb. Peak tokens are varied, so this reads as a slot rather than a single word.
result.label: Verb after purpose "to"

result.description: Fires on word pieces following a prefix like "anti-", "Counter-", or "avant-" (e.g. "ac" in anti-academic, "Re" in Counter-Reformation, the hyphen itself). It needs a prefixed or hyphenated compound with an anti/counter-style prefix; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Pieces after anti-/Counter- prefixes

result.description: Fires on programming language names (Python, JavaScript, Ruby) and the 'and' or slash right after them, in lists of languages and tools in programming text. Silent on non-programming text.
result.label: Programming language names in lists

result.description: Fires on the word right after "a key/important/crucial factor in" (mostly " the" or " in", sometimes a word start like "agricult"), where the next word names what is influenced. Silent on " the" in other constructions.
result.label: Token after "factor in"

result.description: Fires on the token ' T' when it is a standalone letter or abbreviation, such as T cell subtypes (T_H), TP/TQ variables, or a T symbol in math and science text. It stays quiet on 'T' in 'TUI technology'.
result.label: Standalone ' T' letter/abbreviation

result.description: Diffuse attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens: digits inside numeric or formula strings, ' of', commas, and odd tokens. Silent on '2' in years like 2009 or 2000. Circuit is mostly generic token detectors; evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mixed digits in formulas, not years

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, nouns like perspective, pattern, borders, planet) in academic text about language, linguistics and philosophy. Members detect linguistic/philosophical word pieces. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered academic linguistics/philosophy tokens

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'mic', 'm', 'el', 'um' inside technical science words (mesoplasm, mesopelagic, reticulum), in biology and atmosphere or ocean text. It stays quiet on 'mic' in 'cosmic'.
result.label: Mid-word pieces in science terms

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ative' (also 'ation') completing the word "regenerative"/"regeneration", mostly in regenerative medicine text. It stays silent on 'ative' in other words such as innovative, preventative, collaborative.
result.label: regener-ative suffix piece
'ual' in bilingual/multilingual
result.description: Fires on the piece 'ual' completing "biling-ual" (also multilingual), in text about bilingualism and education. It stays silent on 'ual' in other words such as "mutual" or "lingual" after "ling".

Fires on word pieces (' t', 'icul', 'phon', ' intr') that begin or continue a fancy word in the flowery opening of a document, like "In the intricate tapestry of". Silent on ' t' in mid-text words like tension or tune.
result.label: Word pieces in flowery essay openings

result.description: Fires on the pieces of "advocate" words (advoc-, -acy, -ates, -ating) when the word is being built up or repeated, as in "advocacy" or "advocates for". Silent on "Customer Advocacy", so it seems to depend on the context.
result.label: advocate/advocacy word pieces

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' that', ' in', word endings like -ening, -ations, -ising) in abstract academic prose on history, economics and social change, often where a noun phrase is about to be modified. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Abstract social-history prose, varied tokens

result.description: Fires on the plural suffix 's' after a noun stem, most strongly "truth" + s ("truths") in logic and math text. It stays silent on 's' inside words (impossibility), verb -s and possessive 's.
result.label: Plural 's' in "truths"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (Spain, Italy, Britain, hyphens, 'undert') within text about European nations and powers in history or international relations. Peaks are inconsistent. Members mostly detect countries, nations, Europe and military/diplomatic themes.
result.label: European nations/powers context, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on tokens shortly after "scalable/scalability/scaling" in tech text (e.g. "scalable and", "scalable infrastructure", "scaling being"). Members detect scal-/ability pieces. It stays silent on ordinary "and" without a preceding scal- word.
result.label: Words following "scalable/scaling" in tech text

result.description: Fires on tokens right after a document-initial "Two" (e.g. "Two dominant", "Two-", "Two paradigms"), where the text is introducing a pair of things; also on "categories"/"distinct". Silent on hyphens in other words like "step-growth".
result.label: Words following opening "Two"

result.description: Fires on the completion of "decision making/makers" (tokens "making", "ers", " decision") after the word "decision", and weakly on nearby slots. Members detect "decision" and the hyphen in "decision-making".
result.label: decision-making / decision makers

result.description: Fires on the subscript or symbol token right after a capital "L" used as a math variable (e.g. the underscore in L_n, Lucas numbers). Members detect "L" followed by l/z/_/( characters. Weak firing on L at the start of words.
result.label: Subscript after math variable L

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ont' inside "deontology/deontic/deontological", and weakly in "spontaneous". It needs the preceding "de" or "sp" piece, and it predicts word-continuation pieces like "ological".
result.label: 'ont' in deontology

result.description: Fires on the ending piece (-ates, -ating) of "facilitate" forms, e.g. "facilitates cross-cultural...". Stays silent on other -ates verbs like correlates, dedicates, translates. Members detect the "facil" piece and facilitate-related tokens.
result.label: facilitate verb ending (-ates/-ating)

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, ' their', ' for', ' model', word fragments like 'min', 'ous') in technical or academic expository text. Peaks are scattered and silent on many commas. Circuit is weak and mixed, with no clear pattern.
result.label: Scattered tokens in technical prose

result.description: Fires on function words (the, to, their, being) that follow a verb or noun and precede an object noun phrase, in abstract academic text. Peaks are scattered and the contrast is unclear, so the pattern is weak and mixed.
result.label: Function words before object noun phrase

result.description: Fires on ' and' right after a name like "Martha Graham" in lists of people (dancers, artists), and on ' Graham' after "Martha". Silent on ' and' after other list items such as dates or parentheses.
result.label: 'and' after Graham in name lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Par' (also 'm' in Parmigiano), as in Parthenon, Parmenides, paradox. It needs the piece to begin a word that is still unfinished, with the ending predicted next; the contrast text has no such piece.
result.label: Par- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the "od" piece in split "flo|od" (also "oding", "plain" in floodplain), mainly in hydrology/flood-risk text. The same "od" in "Geodetic" is silent in contrast, so it needs the preceding "flo".
result.label: flood 'od' word piece

result.description: Fires on connectors (' and', ' for', comma) right after "mining" or "mineral(s)" in mining/mineral-resource text, as in "minerals and ores". Members detect min/mineral word pieces. Predicts mineral nouns like ' cer', ' foss'.
result.label: 'and' after mining/minerals

result.description: Fires on the 'FO' piece in the acronyms FIFO and LIFO (queue/stack ordering), mostly after 'FI' or 'LI'. Weakly fires on other acronym-initial pieces like 'LI' or 'LO' in acronyms.
result.label: FO in FIFO/LIFO acronyms

result.description: Fires on the piece 'om' when it follows 'bi' inside bio- words (biomaterials, biomass, biomimetic, biomolecule). It stays silent when 'om' starts a word.
result.label: 'om' after 'bi' in bio- words

result.description: Fires on 'power' as the piece after the prefix 'over' in 'overpowering' / 'overpowered'. Members detect 'over' plus word pieces (est, b, shadow) and 'power' itself. Weaker on 'overshadowed'.
result.label: 'power' in 'overpowering'

result.description: Fires on the token completing a word that follows "dry" (dry br-ush, dry punch-line, dry humor, dry-point). It stays silent on "brush" without a preceding "dry" (brushstroke, brushes).
result.label: Word completions after "dry"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, often mid-word pieces or function words like ' and', ' to', ' FROM', in varied contexts. No coherent pattern; contrast also contains ' and' where it is silent. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Scattered mixed function-word and subword peaks

result.description: Fires weakly and diffusely on varied mid-sentence tokens (word pieces, function words, symbols) in lists and expository text. Peaks share no token or meaning, and members are generic token detectors. Evidence is too thin to say more.
result.label: Diffuse mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Fires on mid-word or word-final pieces of technical or linguistic terms (e.g. 'lex', ' model' in "threat modeling", 'etic', '-ment'), where a suffix is expected next. Circuit fails and is diffuse; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-word pieces in technical terms

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces ('astic', 'ol', 'op', 'o') inside words like scholastic, schizophrenia, after the 'sch' start. Silent when 'ol' starts the word or follows a capitalized 'Sch' in some contexts.
result.label: Mid-word piece after 'sch'

result.description: Fires on the 'ation' ending of "appreciation", and weakly on the word after it (" and", " also", " the"). It stays silent on 'ation' in other words such as communication, innovation and reconciliation.
result.label: appreciation word-piece 'ation'

result.description: Fires on the token right after a form of "add" (e.g. "added to", "added in"), mostly ' to' following "added". Silent on ' to' after other words like "need", "used", "suited". Members detect "add/added/adding/additive".
result.label: Preposition after "added"

result.description: Fires on word pieces (-ing, -ive, 'the', 'a') inside the gerund or noun phrase right after the opening "When it comes to" at a document start. It stays silent on 'ing' elsewhere in mid-text.
result.label: Phrase after "When it comes to"

result.description: Fires on the first token or word piece of the object after "approach to" (e.g. "a" in "a|esthetics", "curr|icul|um", "sour|cing", "narr|ative"). Silent on ' a' as a standalone article after other words.
result.label: Word start after "approach to"
'prov' in thought-provoking
result.description: Fires on the piece 'prov' in "thought-provoking" (and similar "-provoking" compounds), with weaker activity on the following 'oking' or ' and'. Predicts continuations like choices or scenarios. Members are mostly generic.

Fires on function words (mostly " to", also " with", " the", " can make") right after "users" as the object of allow/enable/ensure verbs, in user-experience and interface text. Silent on " to" after other nouns such as researchers or customers.
result.label: function word after "users" in UX text

result.description: Fires on ' as' right after a verb or noun of viewing or regarding (view X as, describe as, seen as), introducing how something is characterised. Silent on comparative 'as...as' and on 'not as' or 'sometimes as'.
result.label: 'as' after view/regard verbs

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention latent firing on varied connective tokens (' and', ',', ' which') and noun-phrase endings in abstract essay-style text about culture and politics. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is poorly faithful.
result.label: Diffuse connectives in essay text

result.description: Fires on 'navigate' and its variants (navig-, navigating) and on the following words in the figurative phrase, such as 'through', 'the' or 'complex', as in "navigate the complex waters". Members are mostly navigate-token detectors.
result.label: navigate / navigating complex terrain

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied tokens (word endings like -ibility, -itive, verbs like contains/were, 'together', 'signed'). No clear shared token or context; members are generic token-level detectors. The circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mid-word and verb tokens

result.description: Fires on the word or piece right after "challenge/challenged/challenging" plus conventional/traditional, e.g. " traditional", " narr", " conception", in text about literary or artistic movements breaking norms. It stays silent on "traditional" in other constructions.
result.label: Challenging traditional norms, next word

result.description: Fires on the 'isions' piece of "collisions" when the preceding context is about elasticity (e.g. "elastic collisions"). It stays silent on "collisions" without an elastic context. Elastic-detecting members (the 'astic' pieces) drive it.
result.label: 'isions' in elastic collisions

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target firing on varied tokens: commas, word-start fragments (' st', ' tit', 'ing'), and abstract nouns like ' fundamental'. Evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness; members are generic token detectors.
result.label: Mixed commas and word fragments

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ending abstract academic nouns or following them (expansion, -ment, -ism, 'of', 'in') in dense scholarly lists about social, economic or philosophical topics. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is poor.
result.label: Abstract academic noun endings

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word pieces like 'asure', 'th', ' unique', ' are', ' Selection') in technical or list-like educational text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit fails faithfulness, so no clear trigger is visible.
result.label: Scattered mid-word pieces, technical text

result.description: Fires on the comma or "more" right after "furthermore" (also "further"/"more" in "further"/"moreover"-type additive transitions), where the text adds another point. Silent on ordinary commas in lists or after other connectives.
result.label: Comma after "furthermore"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, often word endings or mid-word pieces, plus ' ahead', ')', ' in' and ' by'. No clear shared meaning or construction. The circuit fails faithfulness and its members are mostly generic.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Attention latent firing on varied word-ending or noun tokens (-ients, -es, writers, commas) in abstract expository prose, often a noun or verb ending a subject phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse noun endings in expository prose

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied tokens (' not' after "but", ' qual', commas, digits, ' the') within list-like or coordinated sequences. Circuit failed faithfulness; members are generic token detectors, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered list-position tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly verbs or word pieces in instructional or list-like text (' care' after 'they', ' apply' after 'then', 'ives', 'm'). No single token or construction dominates. Silent on 'great care'.
result.label: Scattered verbs in instructional text

result.description: Attention latent firing on varied tokens (suffix pieces like 'ism', 'ious', list commas, 'and', 'on') inside abstract academic prose, often in lists of nouns. Peaks are scattered with low consistency; the evidence for a specific trigger is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in abstract academic lists

result.description: Attention latent firing weakly on varied mid-word and noun tokens (sites, societies, regions, adhering, concise) in academic text about language and culture. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is unfaithful, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered academic word-piece tokens

result.description: Fires on "Just" in the term "Just-In-Time" (inventory control) and on the hyphen right after it; weaker on other hyphens or "First". Silent on ordinary hyphens in compounds like "in-depth" or "decision-making".
result.label: Just-In-Time hyphen/Just

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "aspect" (also "component") in "X is a fundamental/crucial aspect of...". Silent on " of" after "web", "dozens", "preservation", or "much".
result.label: "of" after "aspect"

result.description: Fires on the auxiliary or modal verb (should, will, is, are, was) right after the subject of a clause introduced by "whether". It is quiet on the same verbs in ordinary clauses without "whether".
result.label: Verb after subject in whether-clause

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments inside longer words or names (Meg-ad-eth, Sh-ang-hai, mix-ing-redients, construct-ively), but stays quiet on 'ad' ending 'salad'. Weak, scattered circuit that fails faithfulness; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-word fragments in split words

result.description: Fires on the word right after or inside the verb phrase following a plural subject plus "have" (e.g. "movements have progress-ively", "epics have capt-ivated", "have historically"). It marks the main-verb or adverb slot after "have" in abstract academic prose.
result.label: Verb or adverb slot after plural "have"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' in', ' and', 'ency', ' systems', 'ics') inside abstract business, governance and risk-management prose. Peaks are mixed and the target is often silent on the same tokens, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Business/governance prose, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the word piece "quisition" at the end of "Inquisition" (the Spanish Inquisition). Members include detectors of "quisition" in "Acquisition" (language acquisition), so the piece is detected across words, but the target peaks on the Inquisition sense.
result.label: "quisition" in Inquisition

result.description: Fires on the comma right after a sentence-initial "...sequently" (a "Consequently,"-style opener at the start of a sentence). It stays silent on commas after "therefore" or "hence" mid-sentence and on list commas.
result.label: Comma after sentence-initial "sequently"
'ivity' in productivity/conductivity
result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ivity' completing "productivity" (and weakly "conductivity"). It stays silent on 'ivity' in "connectivity" and "inclusivity", so it needs the specific preceding word piece, mostly "product".

Fires on varied tokens ending a technical noun phrase in science text, such as 'pressure' after 'temperature and', 'memory', 'phases', and 'chord-al'. It is inconsistent, silent on 'pressure' in some similar physics contexts, and the circuit is mostly generic.
result.label: Scientific noun-phrase completion, inconsistent

result.description: Fires on the verb or verb-start piece (' en' of enriched, 'ided' of aided, 'ed', 'enh') right after "greatly" in passive constructions like "greatly enriched/aided by". Silent on ' en' not following "greatly".
result.label: Verb piece after "greatly"

result.description: Fires on the word piece right after "very" (e.g. very s-ophisticated, very st-iff, very bl-urry), usually the first fragment of a split adjective. Silent on the same pieces after "more", "and" or "using", so it needs "very" directly before.
result.label: Word piece after "very"

result.description: Fires on the suffix pieces ('ion', 'es', 'ive') inside the word "cohesion" and its relatives (cohesive, coherence, cohomology), after a split "coh"/"oh" start. Members detect the coh-/oh- fragment and its continuations.
result.label: Suffix piece inside "cohesion" words

result.description: Fires on items in a list of "knowledge ..." terms (knowledge acquisition, knowledge representation), on the word piece or noun after "knowledge". Silent on "data acquisition", so it needs the knowledge-engineering list context. Members are mostly weak token detectors.
result.label: Knowledge acquisition/representation list items

result.description: Fires on the word right after "health and" (well-being, safeguard, nutrition), i.e. the second item of a "health and X" pair. Silent on "as well as" and "societal well-being". Circuit members are diffuse and weak.
result.label: Second item after "health and"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly mid-phrase word pieces or nouns in academic or technical text (' language', ' to', 'ual', ' Ada', ' class'). The peaks share no single token or construction, and the circuit failed to reproduce the target well.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase technical tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' to', 'ing', ' often', ' the', ' each') in expository text, mostly mid-phrase before a verb stem or suffix. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is unfaithful, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words, weak pattern

result.description: Fires on the first word after "interaction(s)/interplay between", as the first element of the pair (Earth, a, organ-, gla-, elect-). It stays silent on ' Earth' in other constructions, such as "the Earth's atmosphere".
result.label: Word after "interaction between"

result.description: Fires on the word ' cell' (also ' cells', ' Cell') in biology text about cell membranes, walls and immune cells. It stays silent on 'cell' in an electrochemistry sense ('cell potential'). Members are mostly 'cell' token detectors.
result.label: biological 'cell' token

result.description: Fires on the last token of a noun or noun phrase (plural nouns like motifs, cues, technologies) in a list of abstract items, often where a conjunction or "such as" follows. Evidence is scattered and the circuit is weak.
result.label: End of plural noun in list

result.description: Fires on the word "physics"/"Physics", often after a modifier such as Particle, Nuclear, Atomic or Modern, or in lists of science fields. It stays silent on "Physical Chemistry" and other fields. Members detect physics and science-field words.
result.label: Physics word detector

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'to', 'universe', word pieces like 'ad' in Faraday) inside science and philosophy text. Peaks are scattered, consistency is low, and the same commas stay silent elsewhere, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in science/philosophy text

result.description: Fires on word pieces in magnification/optics text: "magnifying", "magnification" suffixes, "glass" in "magnifying glass", and "micro". It is silent on "ifying" in unrelated words such as "identifying". Members are optics, lens and imaging detectors.
result.label: Magnifying/magnification optics words

result.description: Attention latent firing on scattered tokens (' and', commas, ' vol', math factorial digits, mid-list words) with no dominant token or clear context. Members are diffuse token detectors; the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Attention-layer latent firing on the token after or within "generalization/generalizing" (e.g. "from", "(", "ge", "different"), carrying the word-generalize context forward. Members detect "general"/"-izations" pieces; silent on ordinary " to".
result.label: Tokens following "generalization" word

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ement' in "aforementioned", where it follows 'afor' and predicts 'ioned'. Members are mostly 'ement' detectors from early layers. Weak activation on other word pieces like 'apex' and 'henceforth'.
result.label: 'ement' in aforementioned

result.description: Fires on varied tokens inside technical or business title-like phrases (e.g. "Relationship Management", "Memory Allocation Techniques", "Planned Maintenance Optimization ("), often the word after a topic noun. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Technical/business term phrase continuation

result.description: Fires on "communication" (or the "ation" ending of Communic-ation) right after "intercultural", in text about intercultural communication competence. Stays silent on "ation" in other words or in plain "Communication" without that cultural context.
result.label: communication after "intercultural"

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied tokens (periods, commas, ' and', word fragments) in garbled or fragmentary academic text. Members are generic token and word-piece detectors, and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered punctuation in garbled text

result.description: Fires on the word after or within "groundbreaking" (aking, work, studies, discovery, foundation) in academic text about research. It stays silent on "groundwork" in some contexts, so the evidence is mixed. Members detect the "bre"/"aking" pieces.
result.label: Groundbreaking research work continuation

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on mixed tokens (' of', 'ation', '{', ' feature', LaTeX symbols) in science/math text. Circuit fails faithfulness; members are generic word-piece and topic detectors, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered science/LaTeX tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on the 'cular' piece of "Molecular" when it is split as Mole+cular, strongest at the start of a document or title, e.g. "Molecular Dynamics". It stays silent on mid-sentence lowercase 'mole'+'cular'.
result.label: Mole-cular at title start

result.description: Fires on the token right after "gut" (' health', ' h' of "hormones"), in digestive/gut-health text. Silent on ' h' in "hormonal" after other words like "involves" or "through". Weak activity on hyphens and other tokens.
result.label: Token after "gut" (health/hormones)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' to', ' which', ' losses', 'oral', word fragments, ' of') in abstract academic prose, with no clear shared pattern. Members are generic context features; the circuit failed faithfulness and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function-word and fragment peaks

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece "util" (and "iz"/"IT" pieces within it) in utilitarian, utilization, utilize, utilities, where more word pieces follow. Members are mostly detectors of the " util" token.
result.label: "util" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the first letter or piece after the prefix "inter" (m in intermolecular, c in intercultural, also dis, le, rog, qu), where a word continues. It stays silent on 'm' in other words such as paradigm or enigmatic.
result.label: Word piece after "inter" prefix

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (word pieces like 'ulate', ' mel', ' my', and function words like ' and') in science/climate-style text, where a word continuation follows. Peaks are scattered and inconsistent; the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered mid-word and connective tokens

result.description: Diffuse attention target peaking on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ' for', ' through', ' how', 'izing') in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is a failed fit with weak, generic members.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks, unclear

result.description: Fires on 'ideology' and its continuations (ologies, ology, following words like 'is', 'emerged') and related -ism/-ical tokens in political or philosophical text. Silent on some 'ide|ologies' cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Ideology word pieces, political philosophy

result.description: Fires on ' half' (occasionally ' part') right after "the second" as in "the second half of...". It stays silent after "latter" (latter half), so it needs the ordinal "second" before it.
result.label: "second half" after ordinal

result.description: Fires on adverbs and words (mostly, -ly, -ally, in, partially) that follow "composed" in "is composed entirely/mostly/partially of/in...". It needs the "composed of" construction; members detect "composed"/"consisting".
result.label: Modifier after "composed" construction

result.description: Fires on 'on' or 'to' in "based on" / "according to" / "depending on" when introducing the criterion for classifying or categorizing things. Silent on "based on" in non-classification contexts and on spatial 'on'.
result.label: Classification criterion: based on / according to

result.description: Fires on the 'on' piece inside "Spintronics" (Spintr-on-ics), in spintronics/quasiparticle physics text. It stays silent on 'on' in photon or phenomenon. Members detect 'on' after quasi-particle stems like phon-, plus spin- tokens.
result.label: 'on' in Spintronics

result.description: Fires on plural country words (" nations", " countries") right after "developed"/"developing" in economics text about development. Silent on "nations" without that preceding modifier or in other positions.
result.label: nations/countries after developed/developing

result.description: Fires on function words (' their', ' they', ' with', ' to') that follow a subordinating word like "since/as/so that" and start a clause whose verb is coming up. It stays silent on ' their' after "and" or as an object possessive. Predicts modal or verb continuations.
result.label: Clause-initial they/their after conjunction

result.description: Fires on ' from' that opens a range or spectrum ("from X to Y") after a list-introducing clause about variety, e.g. "come in all shapes and sizes, from simple...". Silent on 'from' meaning origin or source.
result.label: 'from' opening a range

result.description: Fires on the token right after "brain" (apostrophe of "brain's", hyphen in "brain-computer", " and", "imaging"). It is silent on apostrophes after other nouns. The circuit mixes punctuation detectors with brain/neuro context members.
result.label: Token following "brain"

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after "Min" in "Min-Max" (scaling), predicting the second half of the compound. Silent on hyphens in other compounds like trade-offs, large-dimensional, state-of-the-art.
result.label: Hyphen in Min-Max

result.description: Fires on verbs like "includes", "involves", "considers" that follow a relative "that/which" clause describing an approach or strategy (e.g. "a multifaceted approach that includes"). Predicts a list of components next.
result.label: Relative-clause "includes/involves" verb

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ism' (also 'ist', 'istic') when it completes the word "humanism"/"humanist". It stays silent on 'ism' in other words such as scholasticism or neoclassicism.
result.label: -ism suffix in humanism

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (' that', ' the', ',', ' to', ' as') in dense technical or academic prose, but not consistently on the same token. Members are generic topic and token detectors, so the evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose
"yr" in labyrinth
result.description: Fires on the piece "yr" inside "labyrinth" (and "labyrinthine"), predicting the "inth" continuation. Weak activation on a few other word fragments like "b" in turbines.

Fires on the word " musical" (also Music/Musical), mostly as an adjective before a noun like "instruments" or "activities". It is silent in some cases, such as at the start of a text or after "folk", so it seems to need a preceding context word.
result.label: Adjective " musical" before nouns

result.description: Fires on ' and' joining two nouns in a short title-like pair right after a document or line start, such as "Art and Technology" or "Food and Religion". It is quieter on ' and' in longer running prose.
result.label: ' and' in title-style noun pairs
Word-start ' mult' (multi- prefix)
result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' mult' (multi-, as in multifacet, multilingual, multinomial), predicting a continuation of the word. Members are mostly detectors of the same ' mult'/' Mult' token.

result.label: Standalone verb 'listen' / 'listening'
result.description: Fires on ' listen' and ' listening' as a whole word, especially the verb in imperatives or advice about attentive listening, and predicts adverbs like 'closely'. Silent when 'listen' is a word piece in 'listeners'. Members detect listen/listening and related tokens.
Fires on the word piece 'ult' inside "cultural" (socioc-ult-ural, interc-ult-ural, C-ult-ural). Members are mostly detectors of 'ult' after a 'c' prefix. Weakly fires on 'lect' in "eclectic".
result.label: 'ult' in "cultural" word piece

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after an agent-noun in the plural or singular, such as conductor, rulers, orchestrators, transporter, in the "the X of Y" metaphor. Stays silent on ' of' after abstract or process nouns like tradition, part, design, execution.
result.label: ' of' after agent nouns
' eth' piece before 'ical'
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' eth' when it starts a word like "ethical" or "ethics" in mid-sentence, after words such as "of", "the", "and". It is quieter after "virtue" and at document start. Members are mostly ' eth' token detectors.

Fires on ' scientific' and a few other words (' clear', ' of', ' confidence') in abstract text about research, statistics, and trust in science. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is mostly statistics/research topic members.
result.label: Scientific/research-context word slot

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments inside longer words, mainly 'age' in "wage" and ' fer' in "fermentation". Upstream members detect the 'w'+'age' piece and ' fer' piece. Logits are not clearly meaningful.
result.label: wage / fermentation word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' hier' at the start of words like hieroglyphs, hierarchy, hieratic, where the next piece completes the word. Members are detectors of ' hier' and similar word-start fragments.
result.label: ' hier' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' prov' at the start of a split word, mostly 'providers' or 'provisions' after 'healthcare', 'care' or 'insurance'. It is silent on nearby text without that piece. Members are detectors of other word-initial fragments.
result.label: ' prov' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'ce' completing "sauce" (sau|ce), in cooking text. Weakly fires on similar word-final pieces like 'ze' in glaze. Members detect the 'ce' piece and cooking-related word fragments.
result.label: 'ce' in "sauce"

result.description: Fires on ' the' that begins a new item after a comma in a list of institutions, states, or historical entities (e.g. "Plato and Aristotle, the tragedies"), or after an introductory clause. Silent on ' the' after prepositions or in "one of the".
result.label: ' the' after comma in lists
"in" inside "fascinating"
result.description: Fires on the piece "in" inside "fasc-in-ating/ated" (also similar mid-word pieces like "intr-igu-ing"). Stays silent on "in" in other words such as "reminiscent" or "Michelin". Predicts suffix pieces like "ating".

Fires on the split-word piece ' aw' (before "areness"), mainly after a modifier like phonemic/phonetic/environmental, and on "-B[ased]". Silent on ' aw' after a conjunction or verb in intercultural-communication text.
result.label: ' aw' in "…awareness" after modifier

result.description: Fires on ' for' (sometimes ' to') right after "the time it takes", introducing the infinitive-like clause ("takes for half of atoms to..."). Silent on ' for' after nouns or adjectives like "support for" or "advantageous for".
result.label: "it takes for" construction

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces like " personal", " bi" (biases, biological), "obi", "auto-bi" that are likely followed by a suffix continuing the word. Silent when "personal" starts a word directly (personalisation at document start).
result.label: Word-start pieces: personal, bi-

result.description: Fires on the articles " a" / " an" right after a copula "is" in a definitional predicate ("X is a crucial aspect/form of..."). Silent on "a" after prepositions like by, towards, as.
result.label: Article 'a' after "is"

result.description: Fires on the 'r' token in "neut|r|ino(s)", after "neut" mid-sentence. It stays silent on 'r' in "high-rise" and on "Neutrino" at document start.
result.label: 'r' inside neutrino

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'ac' (cacophony, polysaccharides, adjacency) and 'ian' (variances) inside a longer multi-piece word, after a word-start piece such as c, var, polys. Silent on ordinary whole words.
result.label: Mid-word fragments 'ac'/'ian'

result.description: Fires on the verb ' act' (also ' acting') as a standalone word, typically after a subject or modal ("they act as", "must act"). Silent when 'act' is the start of a word like "actively".
result.label: Verb 'act' as standalone word

result.description: Fires on the preposition (' on', ' through', ' into') right after "walking" or similar motion verbs, especially in "like walking on/through ..." figurative comparisons. Silent on 'on' after verbs like "think back" or "keeping you".
result.label: Preposition after walking/moving verbs

result.description: Fires on ' mean' as the statistical average (the mean, sample mean, near the mean), in statistics text. It is silent on sentence-initial "mean" with no statistical context before it, and only weakly active on "meanings".
result.label: statistical 'mean' (average)

result.description: Fires on the word " employee" used as a modifier before a noun (employee engagement, turnover, productivity) in workplace/HR text. Members detect "employee" and "staff" tokens and workplace context.
result.label: ' employee' as noun modifier

result.description: Fires on the en dash '–' joining numbers in ranges, such as years (1874–1943) or numeric spans (13–14–15). It stays silent on dashes between letters or words, as in acid–base or P–n junction.
result.label: En dash in numeric ranges

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces 'iast' (in ecclesiastical) and 'atr' (in theatrical), word fragments that are followed by an '-ical' suffix. Members detect other word-start fragments that precede suffixes like -ical.
result.label: Word fragments before -ical (iast, atr)
' util' word-start piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' util' at the start of words like utilization, utilize, utilitarian, and occasionally ' incorpor'. Members are mostly ' util' and ' use' token detectors. The contrast text has no such word piece.
Fires on the token ' best', mostly in "best practice(s)" after a preposition or verb. It predicts continuations like practice, case, action. Weak firing on adverbial "best engage".
result.label: ' best' before practice(s)
Noun right after "equal"
result.description: Fires on the noun completing "equal ___" (treatment, work, rights, employment, representation), and more weakly on similar rights/labor nouns. Members detect "equal", equity, and rights/inclusion vocabulary. Silent on general labor-policy text without "equal".

result.label: Word "model" in named models
result.description: Fires on the token " model"/" Model" (also the stem of "modeling"), especially after a modifier in named models or techniques such as Waterfall Model, fluid mosaic model, predictive modeling. Silent on contrast text without the word.
Fires on word-piece endings 'oms' in the heading "Idioms" (also 'aste' in "Waste") in list-like topic headings. Weaker on other mid-word pieces. Peaks inside specific words, not on a general meaning.
result.label: Idioms 'oms' / Waste 'aste' pieces

result.description: Fires on the 's' of a decade plural (1980s, 1990s) that is the second item in a range or list of decades, e.g. "1970s and 1980s", "1920s to early 1950s". Silent on a lone decade like "the late 1980s".
result.label: Decade 's' ending a range

result.description: Fires on the word ' even' itself, mostly as an adjective (even number, even layer, evenly spread) and more weakly as the adverb 'even the most...'. Upstream members are mostly ' even' token detectors.
result.label: ' even' token detector

result.description: Fires on the noun " transformation" (occasionally " shift" or " transition") as a change-of-state noun, typically after "underwent a significant/revolutionary". Members are detectors of transformation/transform tokens across many contexts.
result.label: ' transformation' noun after "underwent a"

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments inside longer words, mostly 'opol' in geopolitics and monopoly, also 'nt' in sovereignty and 'ig' in sovereignty. It is silent when 'opol' starts the text with no 'ge' or 'mon' before it.
result.label: Mid-word 'opol' piece (geopolitics, monopoly)

result.description: Fires on the word piece " dead" when it begins a longer word such as deadlock or deadline, where the next piece is expected to complete the compound. Mostly in technical text about concurrency and scheduling.
result.label: ' dead' in deadlock/deadline

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "used"/"is often used" (also "a way to", "intended to"), where it introduces an infinitive of purpose. It stays quiet on prepositional 'to' such as "refers to" or "ratio to".
result.label: purpose infinitive 'to' after used
' fis' word-start piece (fiscal)
result.description: Fires mainly on the word-start piece ' fis' in 'fiscal' (policy, federalism, multipliers). It is supported by members detecting other incomplete word starts such as ' au', ' rev' and ' pur'. It predicts a continuation of the word.
Fires on ' of' right after "Law" (e.g. "Law of Sines", "First Law of Thermodynamics"), weakly after "laws". Stays silent on ' of' after other nouns like range, field, realm, conservation.
result.label: ' of' after "Law"

result.description: Fires on the copula ' is'/' are' right after an abstract or technical noun subject (e.g. "knowledge is", "algorithms are"), predicting a predicate like "essential" or "typically". Silent after pronouns or "there/these/that are".
result.label: Copula after noun subject

result.description: Fires on 'ance' in "surveillance" and on ' monitoring' (and similar), in technical text about monitoring, sensing and testing. It stays silent on 'ance' in other words such as finance, governance, enhance and reliance.
result.label: surveillance / monitoring terms

result.description: Fires on the word " central" when it follows "the" or a similar determiner mid-sentence, mostly in "the central bank" and "central charge". It stays silent when " central" is the first token of the document.
result.label: " central" after determiner

result.description: Fires on ' complex' as an adjective right after "a"/"is a" (e.g. "is a complex process/field"). Silent when it starts a text or follows "more" or "and". Weaker on 'intricate'.
result.label: "a complex" adjective after article

result.description: Fires mainly on the mid-word piece 'ot' in "dichotomy/dichotomies", plus a few other mid-word pieces and separators. It needs the token to sit inside a longer word being built, and it predicts word-continuation pieces.
result.label: 'ot' inside "dichotomy"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' mem' (memoir, memories, memo) as it begins a longer word. Members are detectors of ' mem' and of other word-start fragments. It pushes the next token towards 'ories'.
result.label: ' mem' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on ' and' (occasionally a comma) joining two abstract or plural nouns in a coordinated pair or list, like "artists and public performances" or "Education and democracy". It is silent on some fixed or closely bound pairs such as "supply and demand" and "words and phrases".
result.label: ' and' joining coordinated nouns

result.description: Fires on word-ending suffix pieces like 'ing' (lighting) and 'ness' (stillness), plus a few other tokens, mostly in art/media/tech text. Silent on many 'ing' endings of verbs, so it likes noun-like suffixes; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Noun suffixes -ing / -ness

result.description: Fires on word-ending pieces that complete plural nouns (circ-uits, dev-ices, sens-ors, services) in technical text, plus a stray '0'. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low, so the pattern is weak and mixed.
result.label: Plural noun suffix pieces in technical text
'id' piece in "humidity"
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'id' in the middle of "hum-id-ity" (humidity in climate/forest text), expecting 'ity' next. Silent on 'id' at the start of a document or word, so it needs a preceding word piece such as 'hum'.

Fires on mid-word fragments inside longer split words, mainly 'sten' in "sustenance", also 'c' in Mercator, ' Catal', 'ary'. Members detect specific word pieces (sten, pers, ited, ens, po) and predict suffix-like continuations such as 'ance'.
result.label: Mid-word fragments, esp. su-sten-ance

result.description: Fires on abstract intellectual nouns like "ideas", "principles" and "concepts", mostly after an adjective or modifier, in history-of-thought or science text (e.g. "basic ideas", "early concepts"). Silent on the Enlightenment-literature contrast passage.
result.label: Ideas/principles/concepts nouns after modifier
Hyphen after "free"
result.description: Fires on the hyphen token right after "free" (free-rider, free-range, free-market, free-morpher). It stays silent on hyphens after other prefixes such as non-, under-, and shape-. Members detect "free" and its variants (freezes, freezing) plus generic hyphens.

Fires on mid-word pieces in regional/colonial-history text, such as ' Af' (African/Afro), 'ies' in Dutch East Indies, and 'w' in "underwent". Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit is weak.
result.label: Af-/Indies word pieces in colonial contexts

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ocracy" completing "democracy" (after "dem"). Members detect "dem-ocracy", "democr-atic", "liberal" and political-governance words.
result.label: 'ocracy' in "democracy"
' aw' piece in 'awareness'
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' aw' when it begins the word "awareness" (e.g. "environmental aw|areness"). It predicts the continuation 'aren'. Members are mostly detectors of the same ' aw' token.
Fires on the final piece 'ous' of "Continuous" when it completes the grammar tense name (Perfect Continuous, Present Continuous). It stays silent on 'ous' in other words like nebulous or synchronous.
result.label: 'ous' ending Continuous tense

result.description: Fires on the piece "find" inside "wayfinding", "wayfinders" and "pathfinding", right after "way" or "path". Members mostly detect "find" and other word-start pieces that get completed into longer words.
result.label: "find" in wayfinding

result.description: Fires on the token ' object' as a modifier in computer-vision phrases like "object recognition/detection/tracking", predicting words such as detection or recognition. Weaker on "objectives" and "direct objects".
result.label: ' object' in object recognition

result.description: Fires on the piece 'pt' inside "pe-pt-" in peptide/peptidyl/peptidoglycan. It stays silent on 'pt' in "apoptosis", so it needs the preceding "pe" prefix.
result.label: 'pt' in peptide words

result.description: Fires on 'ing' word endings and similar gerund-like nouns (addressing, borrowing, rolling, feeding) right after "different/various/physical"-type modifiers, in a noun slot. Silent on many other 'ing' tokens, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Gerund noun after 'different' modifier

result.description: Fires on the token ' ones' used as a pronoun-like noun replacing a previously mentioned noun, usually after an adjective ("vibrant ones", "best-looking ones"), and in "oneself" forms. Members are mostly ' ones' detectors.
result.label: ' ones' after adjective

result.description: Fires mainly on " sous" in the cooking term "sous vide", predicting a continuation piece. It also fires weakly on word-start pieces in cooking and food text, such as "pas|try". Members are cooking and culinary detectors.
result.label: " sous" in sous vide cooking

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments of a longer word that is still incomplete, such as 'pron' in pronouns, 'tra' in traits, and 'in' in Multinomial. Silent on 'in' inside other words like molinellary or distinctions.
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments (pron, tra, in)

result.description: Fires on the word " character"/" Character" in lists or contrasts of categories (e.g. "Character vs. ..."), where it is a standalone item. It stays silent on "character development" in fiction-analysis text.
result.label: character as listed category item

result.description: Fires on the plural noun ' thoughts', usually after a possessive or determiner ("their thoughts", "the thoughts of"). It stays silent on the singular 'thought' in "between thought and feeling". Members detect thought, idea and mind-related words.
result.label: ' thoughts' plural noun

result.description: Fires mainly on '0' in long runs of zeros (binary-like or decimal strings such as 0.000010100), and also on 'ent' in 'nutrient' and 'al'/'an' word pieces. It stays silent on '0' in ordinary numbers like 20 or 80%.
result.label: Zeros in long digit strings

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' im' when it is a mid-text word start, mostly in 'imputation' (also 'imputed', 'imbuing'), following a preceding word. It is silent when ' im' is the first token of the document.
result.label: ' im' piece in imputation

result.description: Fires on " the" right after "some of" (also weaker after "one of", "half of"), typically leading into a superlative like "most". Stays silent on " the" after other words or prepositions.
result.label: "the" after "some of"

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after a verb of perceiving or grasping (memorize, hearing, capturing, grasp the...), where an abstract object noun follows. Quiet on ' the' after prepositions like 'for' or 'to' before possessive nouns.
result.label: 'the' after perception/grasp verbs

result.description: Fires on the word "humor" (also "humour", "sarcasm" pieces, "jokes", "wit") in texts about humor and sarcasm. Members are mostly humor/laugh detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: humor and sarcasm words

result.description: Fires on the piece 'cular' when it completes the word "molecular" (mole+cular). It stays silent on 'cular' in prefixed words such as "macromolecular" and "intramolecular".
result.label: 'cular' in "molecular"

result.description: Fires on the verb or noun ' impact' (also ' affect', ' influence') right after a comma or clause, often as a participle-like continuation (", impacts on", ", impacting"). Silent on 'impact' after 'the', 'direct' or 'to'.
result.label: ' impact' after comma clause
Word-start piece 'hum' (humidity, humorous)
result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' hum' when it begins a longer word such as humidity, humidifiers, humid or humorous. Silent when ' hum' starts the document with no preceding context. Members are mostly ' hum' detectors in earlier layers.

Fires on ' which' as a non-restrictive relative pronoun after a comma following a named theory, concept or technical term in academic or explanatory text, introducing a clause about it. Silent in some physics/chemistry contexts.
result.label: Relative 'which' after named concept

result.description: Fires on 'hold' in share/stakeholder words and on ' fashion', plus occasional other tokens like ' intelligence' or ' wind'. Mixed peaks; members mostly detect 'hold' in shareholder/stakeholder. Weak, partial circuit.
result.label: hold in shareholder; fashion

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ber' when it ends a word started by an earlier piece, strongest in "fi|ber" (fiber materials, fiber optics), weaker in "cy|ber" and "straw|berries". It stays silent when 'ber' starts a text.
result.label: 'ber' after fi- / cy- prefix

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: ' of' after nouns like 'degrees' or 'fabric', word pieces such as 'olds' in 'Manifolds', and words like 'network' or 'overhead'. Peaks are inconsistent. It is silent on many other ' of' uses, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered ' of' and word pieces

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' fu' in "fossil fuels" (predicting "els"), and also on the digit '3' at the start of numbers like dates (3400, 3500) or list items. Weaker on other word-start pieces like 'icon' and 'Trad'.
result.label: ' fu' in fossil fuels, and '3'

result.description: Fires on the first fragment of a word split into pieces (sens-, aud-, forec-, determ-, imag-) after an adjective like "personalized", "precise", "more", where the next piece completes the word. Silent on "sens" in "sensory feedback" after "and".
result.label: Word-initial fragment after adjective

result.description: Fires on 'phase', 'stage' or 'step' when it names a numbered or ordinal step in a multi-step process, such as 'second phase' or 'final stage'. It stays quiet on 'phase' in a descriptive use like 'transformative phase'.
result.label: Process phase/stage after ordinal

result.description: Fires on the word "media"/"Media", most strongly as a capitalized heading-initial word like "Media Buying" or "Media Planning" at line start. Weaker for lowercase "digital media". Silent in "social media".
result.label: Media as heading word

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces like ' chem', ' sculpt', ' art' right after "digital" or "computational" (digital art, digital sculpture, computational chemistry). Silent on "chem" in plain chemistry contexts without that modifier.
result.label: digital/computational + art/chem/sculpt

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' absol' in "absolutes/absolutism", especially after "moral" or "ethical", and sometimes on ' worth' in philosophical text. It predicts word-completion pieces. Members detect word-start fragments.
result.label: ' absol' in philosophical absolutes

result.description: Fires on word pieces that start a positive-quality word after "a"/"an" or similar, mainly " delight" (as in "a delightful"), also "igu" (intriguing) and "eleg" (elegance). It predicts suffix continuations like "iful".
result.label: delight/intrigue/elegance word starts

result.description: Fires on word pieces in molecular/atomic chemistry and physics text, such as "orbit" in molecular orbitals, "cular", "geometry", "struct" and "trans" in spectroscopy. Members detect chemistry terms like molecule, orbital and electron.
result.label: Molecular chemistry term fragments

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ract' inside longer words such as detract, distract, refract and retractable, after a prefix piece (det-, dist-, ref-). Members mostly detect 'ract' and similar mid-word pieces.
result.label: 'ract' word piece (detract/distract/refract)

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces and a few heading words like 'ving' in "evolving", ' surg', ' Bond', and 'oid' in "steroids". Peaks are scattered and weak, and the logits are mixed, so no single trigger or condition is clear.
result.label: Scattered word pieces: evolving, Bond, steroid

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after a short word stem, most strongly in "cap-and-trade". It stays silent on hyphens in common compounds like market-based, cost-effective, long-term and re-balance.
result.label: Hyphen in cap-and-trade

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: 'ary' in repeated "Literary ..." list headings, digits in number strings, and '=' slot before 0 in equations. Silent on 'ary' in other words. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low.
result.label: Mixed: Literary list 'ary', digits

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after the prepositions "by" or "using" (also "through", "with") in technical math/science text, as in "using the formula" or "by the ideal". It stays quiet on ' the' after verbs like "reverse", "holds" or "identifies".
result.label: ' the' after by/using prepositions

result.description: Fires on ' and' (sometimes ' or') joining two abstract nouns in a coordinated pair, often at the start of a document or title (e.g. "Debt and equity", "Education and democracy"). Silent on some ' and' in similar pairs, so the extra requirement is unclear.
result.label: ' and' between paired abstract nouns
"ors" in "directors" (board)
result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ors" completing "directors", mostly in corporate board governance text (executive/non-executive directors). Stays silent on "ors" in other words like "investors".

Fires on the word piece ' emer' (start of emerged/emerges/emerging) when it follows a noun subject such as a movement, genre or technology that "came into being". It is quieter when the word starts a sentence or follows "to".
result.label: ' emer' as verb "emerged" after subject

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' bi' / ' Bi' that starts bio- words (biomedical, biological, biogeographic, biology). Members are detectors of this same piece. The contrast shows it stays silent on unrelated text.
result.label: Word-initial 'bi' of bio- words

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', quote marks, ' as', commas) inside lists of grammar terms or quoted words in English-grammar/linguistics text, e.g. lists of conjunctions. Silent on ordinary 'and' in regular prose about writing.
result.label: List connectives in grammar text

result.description: Fires on the 'ces' (or 'cing') piece completing "introduces"/"introducing", where the verb brings in a new concept or idea. Silent on 'ces' in other words such as "audiences".
result.label: introdu-ces / introdu-cing suffix

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ced' at the end of "sourced", especially in "locally sourced". It stays silent on 'ced' in "evidenced". Upstream members detect 'ced'/'cing' pieces and local-sourcing context.
result.label: 'ced' in "locally sourced"

result.description: Fires on "ining" in "examining" (and on " examine"), i.e. the scholarly verb of analysing or investigating something. It stays silent on "ining" in other words like "redefining" or "imagining".
result.label: examining / examine verb

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a word or compound that is likely to continue into a technical term (exc|avating, well|bore, acid–base, meas|uring), but not on 'well' in 'as well as'. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Technical word-start fragments, not 'as well'
-ity suffix in elasticity
result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ity' completing technical nouns, strongest in "elasticity" (economics/physics). It stays silent on 'ity' in words like electricity, scarcity, equity, vigority.

Fires on ' in' right after a proper noun (place, country, organization) where a year is expected next, as in "Conference in London in 19…". Silent on ' in' after common nouns or verbs like "found in" or "shifts in".
result.label: ' in' after name, before year

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' (sometimes 'ic') completing "geotechnical", in engineering text. It stays silent on 'ical' in other words like empirical, mechanical, ecological, biogeochemical.
result.label: geotechn-ical suffix

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after a classifying noun like "type", "kind", "forms", "sort" (e.g. "some type of", "other forms of"). It stays silent on ' of' after "aspect", "terms", "strengths" or "basics".
result.label: ' of' after type/kind nouns

result.description: Fires on the 'll' piece inside the word "syllable(s)" (sy|ll|able), in linguistics text about syllable structure. Silent on 'll' in other words such as "you'll" or "llalabries".
result.label: 'll' in syllable

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces, mostly 'ag' in Pythagorean and similar words, plus 'conjug' and 'ate' in technical or mathematical terms. It is silent on 'ag' in Epicthagoratic, so it needs specific word contexts.
result.label: Pythagorean 'ag' word-piece

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ization' when it completes "Decolon-ization", helped by upstream colonial/colon detectors. It stays silent on 'ization' in other words such as Globalization, nationalization, Optimization and reorganization.
result.label: Decolonization 'ization' suffix

result.description: Fires on ' the' (also ' that') right after the quantifier "all" (all the plants, all the people). Silent on ' the' after other words such as "of the" or "in the" without a preceding "all".
result.label: ' the' after 'all'

result.description: Fires on the verb " tend" (also "tends") right after a plural or generic subject, in statements like "X tend to be/increase". It fires weakly on a few related words such as "corresponds" and "aff".
result.label: ' tend' verb after generic subject

result.description: Fires on ' game'/' Game' (game theory, video game contexts) and also on 'le' in "Role" at the start of titles like "The Role of…". Two separate triggers, with no shared condition visible.
result.label: 'game' token and 'Role' 'le'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' intr' when it begins "intricate/intricacies", typically after "the" or "an" in academic-style text. It is silent on 'intr' in "intrinsic". It pushes towards 'icate'-style continuations.
result.label: ' intr' starting "intricate"

result.description: Fires mostly on the word-start piece " combin" before "atorial" in math text about combinatorics. It also fires weakly on other word-start fragments such as "igen" and " St". Its inputs are detectors for combin- and related word pieces.
result.label: " combin" before -atorial

result.description: Fires on the token ' data' when it is the object of a verb like analyzing, collecting, capturing or interpreting. It stays silent when ' data' is a modifier before another noun (data management, data processing). Members are mostly ' data' detectors.
result.label: ' data' as object noun

result.description: Fires mainly on "In" in the acronym expansions "First-In, First-Out" / "Last-In, First-Out" (FIFO/LIFO), and secondarily on " after". Silent on unrelated text. Evidence is mixed beyond these two tokens.
result.label: "In" in First-In/Last-In; " after"

result.description: Fires on the article ' an' (sometimes ' a') right after a verb that requires an object, such as necessitate, signifies or require. It is silent on ' an' after prepositions like 'from' or 'between'.
result.label: Article 'an' after demanding verbs

result.description: Fires on a plural noun (often plural 's' or words like symbols, vehicles, instruments) right after "serve/act/function as", naming what something serves as. Predicts a following "for/into" phrase. Silent on ordinary plurals elsewhere.
result.label: Plural noun after "serve as"

result.description: Fires on ' Chinese' and on the ' Ch' piece of 'Chain' in repeated "Supply Chain" headings, plus China/Asian-type words. Members are detectors for Chinese/China/Ch tokens. Weak elsewhere.
result.label: Chinese / Ch token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on long runs of dash characters (separator lines, often at document start or after a paragraph), and weakly on word pieces like 'omet' in 'organometallic'. Evidence is mixed beyond the dash runs.
result.label: Long dash separator runs
