result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'in' inside the name "Bose-Einstein" (E-in-stein), plus scattered other tokens (' Lucas', ' Sea', ' half'). Silent on 'in' in words like fascinating, vein, refinement.
result.label: 'in' inside Einstein

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' St' at the start of a word or heading, mostly the ' St' of "Stellar" at a document or section start, and more weakly on pieces like 'ural'. Members are mostly ' St' detectors. Predicts word continuations.
result.label: ' St' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on 'rock' in 'bedrock' used metaphorically as a foundation, and more weakly on 'stone' in 'cornerstone' and 'ar' in 'pillar'. Needs the foundation-metaphor word piece, not generic text.
result.label: bedrock / cornerstone foundation metaphor
' focus' and abandon/Ex word starts
result.description: Fires mostly on ' focus' (also 'abandon', 'Ex', 'ly' in glycogen, 'foc-al') as noun or word start, often early in a passage. Silent on one 'traditional focus is on' example, so the condition is unclear.
Fires on the piece 'ot' in "homotopy" (hom|ot|opy), in algebraic topology text. It is silent on unrelated contexts, and weakly fires on ' binary' and 'vit' in other words.
result.label: 'ot' in homotopy

result.description: Fires on the word ' civil' (as in civil rights, civil disobedience, civilization), mostly as a standalone word before 'rights' or as the start of 'civilization'. Members are mostly ' civil' token detectors.
result.label: ' civil' token detector

result.description: Fires on "development" or "evolution" (also "growth") as the head noun right after "The" at the start of a document/title, as in "The evolution of…". It stays silent when the word follows a modifier like "plot", "urban" or "conceptual".
result.label: Sentence-initial "The development/evolution"

result.description: Fires on determiners or quantifiers (an, a, some, any, either, both) right after the preposition "for", as in "for an infinite set". The same determiners after other verbs or prepositions leave it silent.
result.label: Determiner after "for"
' media' in "mixed media"
result.description: Fires on the token ' media' (also ' Media'), most strongly in "mixed media" in art contexts. It fires only weakly on "social media" or "enrich media". Members are mostly detectors of media/Media.

Fires on the digit '9' within multi-digit numbers, such as years like 1789 or long strings of nines and digits. It stays silent on '9' as the second digit of a 19xx century pattern (e.g., 1[9]th, 1[9]35).
result.label: Digit 9 in later number positions

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' em' as a prefix at the start of a word like embrace, empathize, emissions, emotion, mostly after a verb or preposition. Silent on some ' em' contexts such as after a noun or at the start of a sentence.
result.label: ' em' word-start prefix
Plural 's' after acronyms
result.description: Fires on the plural suffix 's' attached directly to an all-caps acronym (MGFs, LSTMs, DAGs, RBMs) in technical text. Stays silent on verb 's' endings and on possessive apostrophe-s.

Fires on the suffix piece 'atic' completing "chromatic" (chromatic aberration, Achromatic/Apochromatic lenses). Members detect chrom- word pieces like chromosome and chromatography. Silent on 'atic' in other words such as "noechaumatic".
result.label: 'atic' in chromatic

result.description: Fires mainly on " instant" (as in "instant messaging", "instantaneous"), and weaker on "three-" hyphen and "best". Members detect instant, simultane-, spont- pieces, predicting word continuations like "-aneous". Silent on "instant" at document start.
result.label: "instant" before messaging/-aneous

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cor' when it begins "corrosion" (also weakly "corrupt"), in materials and corrosion-types text. Members are mostly ' cor' token detectors across early layers.
result.label: ' cor' start of corrosion

result.description: Fires on ' order' as a noun after "the" (the order of reaction, order of arrangement, group order, taxonomic order). Silent on "second order" and on "in order to".
result.label: noun 'order' after "the"

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments, especially 'as' inside words like Plasmon or endoparasites, and on ' Error' in "Type I and Type II Errors". Silent on 'as' in quasi or seas. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is a weak fit.
result.label: Word-fragment 'as' and Error

result.description: Fires on the word " speech" (occasionally " voice") in speech-technology text such as speech recognition, synthesis and analysis. Members are detectors of speech, spoken, audio and pitch tokens. Silent on unrelated AI text.
result.label: speech (recognition/synthesis) token

result.description: Fires on ' for' right after a need/demand-type noun ("the need for", "demand for", "respect for"), where a noun phrase follows. Silent on ' for' in other uses like "for instance" or "used for".
result.label: 'for' after need/demand nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " en" that begins a longer word (enzyme, envelope, enabling, enrichment, encompasses). Members mostly detect " en" itself. The contrast has no " en" token, so it stays silent.
result.label: ' en' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on a closing parenthesis ')' that ends a short parenthetical, often a variable, index, label or single word like "(n)", "(1)", "(þæt)". Silent on ')' closing a longer phrase.
result.label: Closing parenthesis after short item

result.description: Fires on ' against' (also across/among) right after "performance" or similar nouns in comparison/benchmarking contexts, as in comparing performance against standards. Quiet in unrelated marketing text.
result.label: Performance compared 'against' benchmarks

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments or word pieces in multi-token words and names (mer-gers, Bron-te, Ant-it-rust, prepar-ation), plus some noun-phrase tokens. Peaks are scattered and inconsistent; evidence is weak and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Mid-word fragments of split words

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ive' in "Descriptive", especially the heading "Descriptive Statistics". It stays silent on 'ive' in other words such as objective, intuitive, collective and predictive.
result.label: 'ive' in "Descriptive"

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' compar', ' Compar', ' hy' (hyphenation, hybridization) and similar, when the word is split into pieces and continues (comparative, comparisons). Silent on 'comparable' in one contrast.
result.label: compar- / hy- word-start fragments

result.description: Opening quote mark (' "') that starts the next item in a quoted list of words, e.g. "to," "from," or "my", "your". Silent on quotes that open a single phrase, not a list.
result.label: Opening quote in quoted word lists

result.description: Fires mostly on " Latin" as a standalone word (Latin squares/rectangles, Classical Latin), with minor peaks on word pieces like "iction" and "ent". Silent on "Latin" in the hyphenated "Latin-speaking" at the text start.
result.label: Latin word token

result.description: Fires on the word " physical" itself, mostly in philosophy of mind passages (mental vs. physical, physicalism, dualism). Weaker in other uses like physical experiences or the digital world. Supported by members detecting " physical" and philosophy-of-mind context.
result.label: ' physical' in mind-body philosophy

result.description: Fires on closing braces like '}}' and '!}' at the end of LaTeX fractions or square roots in math formulas, plus a few scattered tokens. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: LaTeX closing braces in formulas

result.description: Fires on the verb ' express' (also 'ing' in conveying/expressing) after "to/can" when artists or art forms are the subject, as in "allows artists to express themselves". It stays silent on the adjective "expressive".
result.label: Artists to 'express' (verb)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "engine" (or " engine") as the start of words like engineer/engineering, and in compounds like steam-engine. Members are mostly detectors of "engine" and similar word-start pieces that continue into -ers/-ering.
result.label: engine token (engineer/engineering)

result.description: Fires on the infinitive marker ' to' right after verbs of striving or intent such as "sought to", "seeking to", "attempt to", "aim to". It stays silent on ' to' after "response", "helped", "began" or "means".
result.label: ' to' after seek/attempt verbs

result.description: Fires on ' the' after passive or causal verb phrases like "founded on", "supported by", "dictated by", "influenced by", "born from", in abstract or scientific explanation. It stays quiet on ' the' after verbs like "emphasizes" or "highlighting".
result.label: ' the' after "by/from/on" explanatory phrases

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments early in a document or phrase, mainly 'fficient' in "Efficiently", also 'isson' in Poisson and ' Prof'. Appears to be mid-word pieces of efficiency-related or technical words; silent on repeated "Dr. Name" lists.
result.label: Word fragments: 'fficient', 'isson', Prof

result.description: Fires on the copula ' are' or ' is' right after a subject noun that is a technical or generic topic term (QC, JPEGs, standards, functions), in a definitional or general-statement slot. Quiet after 'there', after 'and', or when the verb is a progressive.
result.label: Copula after generic technical subject

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' surv' (survive, survival, survivor), mainly after "for", "to" or "of". Members are mostly detectors of ' surv' and similar word-start pieces like arch, rev and ach.
result.label: ' surv' word-start piece
' perce' word-piece before -ive/-ived
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' perce' at the start of "perceive/perceived", predicting the suffix 'ived'/'ives'. Weakly fires on similar incomplete word starts like ' benef'. Members are detectors of ' perce' and similar prefixes.

Fires on plural abstract content nouns like points, ideas, details, as objects of study or note-taking verbs (highlighting key points, summarizing ideas, filtering details). Appears in learning, communication and presentation text. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Key points/ideas/details as objects

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'cient' in "Ancient" (headings like "Ancient Maya/Egypt"), and more weakly on ' primitive', ' ancient', and 'sc' in "microscopy". Members are detectors of 'cient' and ancient-civilization names (Sumer, Babylon, cuneiform).
result.label: Ancient / 'cient' in ancient civilizations

result.description: Fires on word stems or pieces in mid-word position (launch, contract, Perform, Decomm-ission, Vol-unte) where a suffix like -ing, -ual, or -er is expected next. Silent on whole-word list items in headings.
result.label: Stem before suffix completion

result.description: Fires on the piece 'c' inside the name "Mycenae/Mycenaean" (My|c|enae). It stays silent on 'c' in other words like "showcased" or "cuneiform", so it needs that specific word.
result.label: 'c' in Mycenae
' compreh' word-start piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' compreh' at the start of "comprehension", "comprehending" and "comprehensive". Members are mostly detectors of this same piece, and the target pushes toward continuations like "ension" and "ensive".

Fires on the piece 'atic' completing "dramatic" (mostly in arts/theatre text), with a few other word-piece completions like Man-if-esto. Silent on 'atic' in "operatic" and in an odd "ram-atic" fragment.
result.label: 'atic' in "dramatic"

result.description: Fires on the plural noun " signs" (also " signals") in a variety of contexts, such as street signs, smart signs and disease signs. Members are mostly detectors of signs/signal/marker tokens.
result.label: ' signs' / ' signals' token

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' develop' when it follows a modifier like "recent", "new", or "technological" and is the start of "developments". It is silent when ' develop' starts the text. It predicts the suffix 'ments'.
result.label: ' develop' in "developments"

result.description: Fires on the word " price" (also Price) in economics text, often as a modifier before another noun, as in "price controls", "price changes" or "low price sensibility". Members are price/pricing detectors. It is silent on "price war" at the start of a text.
result.label: ' price' as economic modifier

result.description: Fires on ' in' (or sentence-initial ' In') when it starts a new clause or list item after a semicolon, comma or period, introducing a field or context ("; in economics", "In essence"). It stays silent on ' in' mid-phrase after a noun or verb.
result.label: Clause-initial " in" after punctuation

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ome' in "genome" (also weaker on 'et' in "genetics" and 'IS' in CRISPR), in genetics and biotech text. Silent on the full word "genetic" in the contrast text.
result.label: 'ome' piece of genome

result.description: Fires on ' silent' and on the word piece 'ore' inside words like chemoreceptors, thermoreceptors and offshore, plus some other mid-word pieces. It is silent on 'ore' in other words such as 'plore'.
result.label: ' silent' and 'ore' word pieces

result.description: Fires on the first word right after "involves/involve/involved", the start of the activity described (e.g. manipulating, engaging, dividing). It predicts a verb-stem continuation, often -ing forms. It stays silent on "act" in "active listening" where no "involves" precedes.
result.label: Word right after "involves"

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like 'U' (UX, UAT, matrix U), ' rom' in romantic, and ' Sc', where the token starts a word or abbreviation that continues with a further piece. Mostly 'U' tokens across UX and math contexts.
result.label: Initial 'U' / 'rom' word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the word " performance" (also "Performance" and the piece "formance"), mostly in technical text about systems, databases and computing efficiency. Built from upstream detectors of the same word. Predicts continuations like "tun(ing)".
result.label: ' performance' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' avail' (start of "availability") before the "-ability" suffix is completed. Members detect avail, -ability, and similar stems like cap-, toler-, scarc-. Predicts suffix completions such as "ability".
result.label: ' avail' stem before -ability

result.description: Fires on word-suffix pieces ('ical', 'ing', 'ed') directly after the stem 'graph' (graphical, graphing, graphed). Stays silent on 'ical' after other stems such as analyt-, ecolog-, Mathemat-.
result.label: Suffix after 'graph' stem

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'er'/'ers' ending "Polym(er)" as a complete word in title-like lists of science or engineering fields, or in plural "polymers". It stays silent when 'er' is mid-word, as in "polymerization" or "polymeric".
result.label: Polymer word-final 'er' suffix

result.description: Fires on " the" right after "without" (also weakly "avoid the", "without any"), where a noun like "need" or "subtle hint" is expected. Silent on "the" after other prepositions or verbs.
result.label: "the" after "without"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' emer' (emergence, emergent, emergency, emerged), where the next piece is likely 'gent', 'ging' or 'ges'. Members are mostly detectors of the same ' emer' token.
result.label: ' emer' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word or token right after the modal "may" or "might" (suggest, be, use, require, choose to, have), where a hedged verb is expected. Silent on "pect" inside "perspectives". Fires in hedged descriptions of cultural and behavioural generalizations.
result.label: Verb slot after "may/might"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' can', ' to', ' arithmetic', commas) in text about CPUs, processors and computing operations. Peaks are inconsistent. It stays silent on ' can' in other technical contexts, so it seems tied to the CPU/computer-operations passage.
result.label: CPU operations passage, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the 'ern' piece in 'modern' when split, as in postmodernism, and on ' modern' or 'Contemporary' used as a period or style word in arts and literature text. Predicts continuations like 'post' or 'conscious'.
result.label: 'modern' word piece (postmodernism)

result.description: Fires on the word " internet" (also " Comput" in "Cloud Computing") when it modifies a following noun, as in "enable internet services" or "high-speed internet". It stays silent when "internet" starts a text before "'s".
result.label: ' internet' as modifier word

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in the contraction "don't" (also doesn't, didn't, isn't), after a "don"/"n" stem. Silent on apostrophes in "it's", "there's", "'ll" or possessives.
result.label: Apostrophe in don't-type negations

result.description: Fires on the token ' experience' (or 'experiences') as a noun after a modifier such as dining, guest, culinary, or immersive. Members are mostly ' experience' token detectors. The contrast text has no such word.
result.label: ' experience' noun after modifier
'hard' in Leonhard (name piece)
result.description: Fires on the token 'hard', mostly as the ending of the name Leonhard (Euler). Weaker on other 'hard' pieces such as Hardware, and on ' Middle' in 'High Middle'. Members detect 'hard' and Leon-/Bern- name pieces.

Fires on the 'odes' piece inside "geodes-" words (geodesy, geodesists) after "ge", with members tracking geodesy word pieces (Geodetic, longitude, geoc-). Silent on a word-initial 'odes'. Also weakly on other word fragments.
result.label: 'odes' in geodesy words

result.description: Fires on ' and' (rarely ' or') joining two short parallel nouns or names, like "double and single", "HR and senior", "Spanish and Portuguese". It is quieter on 'and' after longer noun phrases or in lists.
result.label: ' and' between paired nouns

result.description: Fires on the word " same", mostly in "the same X" phrases that state identity or equality of things (same pressure, same memory, same atomic number). Members are mostly " same" and "identical" detectors.
result.label: " same" after "the"

result.description: Fires on degree adverbs like " mostly", " largely", " relatively", and the suffix "ly" in "Eco-friendly", typically after "made up", "due", or "consisting". Members detect mostly/mainly/partly and -fully/-ically adverb endings.
result.label: Degree adverbs: mostly, largely, -ly

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments, mostly 'lo' in "overexploitation" and 'aren' in "awareness", where a word is split into pieces. Seems to need those specific words; silent on other text about resources.
result.label: Mid-word 'lo' in overexploitation

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ong' completing "Str|ong" (Strong Force, Strong Typing, Strong Authentication), also 'lish'. Silent on 'ong' without a preceding "Str" at the start. Members detect 'ong' and 'ateg'.
result.label: 'ong' after Str (Strong)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "lacement" completing "displacement", mostly in physics/kinematics text. Members detect the "lacement" token and related suffix pieces like "ment" and "ersion" after "disp".
result.label: "lacement" in displacement

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ra' in "infra" as the word "infrared" is being spelled out (inf|ra|red). Silent when 'ra' starts a fragment without the preceding "inf". Weakly fires on other "inf-" word pieces.
result.label: 'ra' inside "infrared"

result.description: Fires on tokens that precede or begin a date or era: ' Kingdom' after Old/New/Middle/Roman, and the start of year numbers like '1' in 1050 or 1800. It predicts a following date or 'around'. Mixed peaks, with the weaker contexts unrelated.
result.label: Kingdom and year-start tokens before dates
' potential' before risk/threat nouns
result.description: Fires on the word ' potential' as an adjective, mostly in risk and security text (identify potential threats, potential harm). It pushes the next token towards risk, threat, loss and harm words. Members are mostly ' potential' detectors.
Fires on the word piece 'vin' in "Calvin" (Calvinism, Calvinist, Calvin's). Weak activations on ' can' and ' may' are minor. Members are mostly 'vin' token detectors.
result.label: 'vin' in Calvin

result.description: Fires on ' as' used as a conjunction meaning "while/because" after an adjective like "increasingly important/common/relevant" (e.g. "becoming important as technology advances"). Silent on "such as" and "serve as".
result.label: ' as' conjunction after "increasingly important"

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'y' (also 'ancy', 'ing') completing the verb "occupy"/"occupancy", mostly in physics text about electrons occupying states. Silent on 'y' ending other words like flinky, shadowy, tragedy.
result.label: 'occupy' word-ending y

result.description: Fires on the token right after the word "early" (e.g. "early on", "early as", "early form", "early explorations"), with "early" as the preceding context. It is silent on " on" after other words like "research on". It predicts stage/period continuations.
result.label: Token following "early"

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments that begin a longer word, mainly ' resid' (in "residues"), also ' diag', ' indic', ' quot'. Predicts suffix pieces like 'ue', 'uals', 'ding'. Evidence is mixed across several prefixes.
result.label: Word-prefix fragments: resid, diag, indic

result.description: Fires on the 'ving' piece in "evol-ving" (also "ch-anging", "evol-ve"), especially in "constantly/ever evolving". It stays silent on 'ving' in "improving", so it needs the evolve word.
result.label: 'ving' in "evolving"

result.description: Fires on " non" as a prefix, mostly in "every/all/each non-key (prime) attribute" in database normalization (2NF), and in technical math/CS text with "non-" terms. It predicts mathematical nouns like element or subgroup.
result.label: "non" prefix in technical text

result.description: Fires on the word "magnet" and its variants (magnetic, magnet-, magnets), including word pieces like "magnet" in magnetosphere. Members are detectors of magnet/magnetic/electric tokens in physics text. It stayed silent on one text-initial " magnetic".
result.label: magnet / magnetic token detector
Jac in Jean-Jacques Rousseau
result.description: Fires on the piece 'Jac' in "Jean-Jacques", as in Jean-Jacques Rousseau, in lists of Enlightenment philosophers. Members include a ' Jean' detector, 'Jac' detectors, and philosophy-context members.
Fires on mid-word fragments, mostly 'osp' in "Geospatial", also ' conf' in "confined/confinement" and 'dom'. Predicts word continuations like 'atial' and 'aces'.
result.label: Word-piece 'osp' in Geospatial

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments that begin a longer word, mainly ' vol' (volcano, volatility) and ' pot' (potatoes), also ' pill' and ' pal'. It predicts the continuation piece of the word.
result.label: Word-start fragments vol/pot

result.description: Fires on the token right after an adjective ending in -able/-ible (countable n-ouns, actionable out-comes, sustainable energy), where a noun or word continuation is expected. Silent after "used" in a similar slot.
result.label: Token after -able adjective

result.description: Fires on the isolated piece 'e' in numbered/hyphenated sequences (2e-3e-5e) and after prefixes like macro-, micro-, socio-, in-, where 'economic', 'efficiency' or 'evolution' would continue. Predicts 'conom', 'vol', 'ffic'.
result.label: 'e' piece before conom/vol continuation

result.description: Fires on the 'p' piece inside a split word, mainly 'trans' + p + 'iration' (also 'cas-p-ase'), where a following completion like 'iration' or 'ase' is expected. It stays silent on 'p' in 'Precipitation'.
result.label: 'p' inside trans-p-iration

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "start" or "beginning" (e.g. "marking the start of"), in the sense of the onset of something. It stays silent on " of" after other nouns like "end", "adoption" or "wave".
result.label: " of" after start/beginning

result.description: Fires on the token ' us' (pronoun or word start as in 'usable/usability') and on ' chron' in 'chronology'. It fires on these word pieces that typically continue into a suffix, mostly ' us' after verbs like allows, help, challenge.
result.label: ' us' and ' chron' word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ron' inside words like electron, microelectronics, acronym, mostly after 'elect'/'ac' pieces. Occasionally fires on ' Friedrich' in 'Carl Friedrich'. Members are detectors of 'ron'/'ric' pieces in electronics words.
result.label: 'ron' in electronics words

result.description: Fires on the words " left" and " right" (direction or side, including "left out", "left over"), across rotation, position and abstract uses. Members are mostly detectors of left or right. Silent on the contrast, which has no such word.
result.label: left / right direction words
Supply chain topic word continuations
result.description: Fires on word pieces following "Supply Chain" in lists of supply chain subtopics (W-arehousing, Returns, Pro-curement, Forecast-ing). Members detect "chain" pieces. Silent on "management" in other resource/asset contexts.
Fires on the suffix 'ing' when it completes the word "questioning" (question + ing). It stays silent on 'ing' in other verbs like challenging or highlighting.
result.label: 'ing' in "questioning"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ton' at the end of the name Dalton (and similar names like Bray-ton, Proton), mainly in science text. It stays silent on a misspelled name like "Datson".
result.label: 'ton' ending of Dalton

result.description: Fires mainly on the token " input" (as in input/output devices, input data), with a few hits on "vex"/" convex". Members are mostly detectors of " input" and related tokens such as feedback and output. Next-token logits favour " out" and "-".
result.label: ' input' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' mark' when it is the start of a split word, especially "markets" after a modifier (financial, money, bond, commodity). It is silent when "mark" opens the text or follows a verb like "stabilize".
result.label: ' mark' piece in compound "markets"

result.description: Fires on commas separating items within a list of examples or terms (e.g. "who, what, which", "my, your, his, her"), mostly in text about grammar or enumerated concepts. Silent on commas after sentence-initial adverbs or conjunctions.
result.label: Comma inside enumerated lists

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments ' dr' (drilling) and ' surve' (surveying/surveillance) in technical text, predicting suffix pieces like 'ational', 'ill', 'iling'. Weakly on similar stems such as 'situ' and 'gravit'.
result.label: dr-/surve- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece ' imp' when it starts "implications"/"implication", and also on 'LP' in "NLP". Predicts a continuation like 'lications'. Members are mostly ' imp' detectors.
result.label: ' imp' before 'lications'

result.description: Fires on the word " work" (and " works"), most strongly as the physics quantity "work done by a force" in work-energy contexts. Weaker on workplace or verb uses. Members are mostly detectors of " work" itself.
result.label: ' work' token, physics sense

result.description: Fires on function words (with, on, to, when, a, for, of) right after a verb or adjective in the opening of generic essay-style documents about writing or brands, where a complement comes next. It is silent on many 'with' tokens, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words after verbs in essays

result.description: Fires on ' on' (and ' upon') right after reliance/dependence words such as "reliant", "dependent", "relying", "depend upon". It stays quiet on ' on' after other words like impact, focus or constraints.
result.label: on/upon after depend/rely words

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'x' in "nexus" (also 'pect' in "Aspect"), a word fragment within a longer word. Members are mostly 'x' detectors, including the variable x in math. Silent in ordinary text.
result.label: 'x' inside "nexus" word piece

result.description: Fires on ' as' right after a verb of labeling or viewing (labeled as, viewed as, regarded as, known as, deemed as), introducing how something is characterized. Silent on 'such as' examples.
result.label: 'as' after labeling/viewing verbs

result.description: Fires on the token ' smart' used as a modifier in compounds like smartphone, smart home, smart appliances, and predicts product-like continuations (watch, phone). Members are mostly ' smart' token detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' smart' as tech modifier

result.description: Fires on capitalized function or word-start tokens (The, To, Under, What, About) inside Title Case headings or titles, where each word is capitalized. Silent on ' The' starting an ordinary sentence in normal-case prose.
result.label: Function words in Title Case headings

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ual' inside longer words, such as concept-ual, fact-ual, mut-ual, habit-ual and grad-ual. It is followed by suffixes like -ized, -ism or -ity. Members mostly detect 'ual' itself.
result.label: 'ual' suffix piece in words

result.description: Fires on 'silent' and the piece 'ent' when it completes "Silent" (Silent Way/Method), plus 'ently'. It stays quiet on 'ent' in other words such as "inherent".
result.label: Silent / Sil-ent word

result.description: Fires on verbs of translating or interpreting input (interpre-ting, translated, interpret, understood), especially about source code or data being converted or read. Predicts data/input-like objects. Silent on "typesetting".
result.label: Interpret/translate verbs on code or data

result.description: Fires on the word piece " stream" when it begins a compound like "streamline" in fluid-dynamics text. It predicts continuations such as "lined" or "lines". Weak activation on "hand" in "on the other hand".
result.label: ' stream' before -line compounds

result.description: Fires on the word " possible" (also "possibility", weaker "potential"), mostly as a modifier in modal-logic or probability text such as "possible worlds" or "all possible outcomes". Silent on the surrounding modal-logic text without the word itself.
result.label: "possible" word detector

result.description: Fires on the word " size" as a noun in technical or scientific text (particle size, sample size, set size, effect size). Members are mostly detectors of " size" plus similar measurable-property nouns like name and rank.
result.label: Noun ' size' detector

result.description: Fires on the first word piece of a split surname or rare name, mainly ' Bol' (Boltzmann), also ' Lap' (Laplace), ' Rad', ' Fre'. It sits where a continuation piece like 'tz' or 'lace' is expected next.
result.label: Name-initial fragments: Bol, Lap

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'it' in "vitational" (gravitational, garbled), and some 'ul', 'ag', 'ist' pieces. Silent on 'it' in ordinary words like exhibit, merit, necessitates. Appears tied to rare or split word pieces.
result.label: Word-piece 'it' in split "vitational"

result.description: Fires on a mid-word fragment inside a longer capitalized proper name or academic term (Princi-ple, Hell-enistic, Am-pere, Pos-itivism, existenz-ialism). It needs the word to be unfinished, not a common word like "ample".
result.label: Mid-word piece of academic proper names

result.description: Fires on the word "print" and its variants (printing, Print, printed), mostly in printmaking and printing-press contexts. Members are mostly print-word detectors. Weak firing on "ec" is a minor edge case.
result.label: print / printing token

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' sp' (spelling), ' ph' (phonetic), ' hom' (homophones) in text about language, linguistics and grammar. Predicts continuations such as 'elling' or 'ambigu'. Quiet on non-linguistic topics.
result.label: Linguistic word-start fragments (sp, ph, hom)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ins' when it is the start of a longer word such as insurance, insights or inscribed, mid-sentence. It is silent when ' ins' begins the document or text.
result.label: ' ins' word-start piece (insurance/insights)

result.description: Fires on the piece 'sp' in "unspoken" after the prefix "un", predicting the continuation "oken". Silent on other un- words like "unscripted". Weakly fires on other word-start fragments.
result.label: 'sp' in "unspoken"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' phenomen' (start of "phenomenology"/"phenomenological") in philosophy-style titles and phrases. Members are mostly detectors of phenomen/phen/omen pieces. Silent on the contrast text, which lacks that token.
result.label: ' phenomen' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on the word "proof"/"proofs" in mathematical or logical text, especially in lists of proof techniques (direct proof, proof by contradiction). Members include proof-token detectors plus math-context members such as metric spaces and algebra.
result.label: "proof" in mathematical contexts

result.description: Fires on the word piece after "coh" (er, es, om) when completing "coherent/coherence/cohesion/cohesive". Silent on "er" in other words like "richer".
result.label: Suffix piece after "coh-"

result.description: Fires on incomplete word stems of long Latinate words (anticip-, optim-, recogn-, accur-) that are followed by a suffix like -ate, -izing, -ately. Seems to mark a mid-word stem awaiting its ending.
result.label: Latinate word stems (anticip-, optim-, accur-)

result.description: Fires on " early" (and " earliest") after "the" when it means an early period or stage, e.g. "the early 19th century" or "the early Neolithic". It stays silent on "as early as", "and early", and "to early" before dates.
result.label: "the early" period/stage modifier

result.description: Fires on the middle pieces 'ney' or 'ne' in the split word "kidney(s)", after the ' kid' token, in biology and medical text. The contrast (a "filter" metaphor without the word kidney) stays silent.
result.label: kid-ney word piece

result.description: Fires on " how" introducing an embedded clause after verbs of examining or explaining (exploring, examining, showing how...) in academic, analytical prose. Members are mostly detectors of how/why/where/whether.
result.label: "how" after examine/explore verbs

result.description: Fires on forms of "lead" (leading, led, lead), most strongly on "leading/led to" expressing causal consequence, as in "temperatures rise, leading to...". Members are detectors of lead/led/leading tokens.
result.label: Causal "leading/led to"

result.description: Fires on ' Dr' at the start of a line in a list of names, where each line is a "Dr. Surname." entry following earlier "Dr. Surname." lines. Silent on lists of plain names without a title.
result.label: Repeated ' Dr' in name lists

result.description: Fires on the adverb ' carefully' (weakly on other manner-adverb endings like -ically/-fully), usually before a verb such as choose, select or observe. Pushes toward verbs and participles like selected or task.
result.label: ' carefully' adverb detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece "os" inside science words split into pieces, most often "nucle|os|ynthesis" and also "chrom|os|omes". It needs the "nucle-" or "chrom-" prefix context in technical science text.
result.label: "os" in nucleosynthesis-type words

result.description: Fires on the word-start pieces " infl" / "fl" in "inflation", "inflaton", "inflammation", strongest in cosmic inflation contexts, and predicts "ation" next. Also weaker for economic inflation. Silent on unrelated cosmology text lacking this piece.
result.label: infl- word start (inflation)

result.description: Fires on the time-span noun ' years' (also decades, centuries, months) in durations like "for hundreds of years" or "for many years". Upstream members detect time-unit words in lists of durations.
result.label: Duration unit 'years'

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside biology/microbiology terms, mainly 'og' in "pathogens" and 'ial' in "bacterial", in scientific text about infection and immunity. Silent on casual conversational text.
result.label: pathogen/bacterial word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' def' (mostly in "deficit"), where the word continues with further pieces. It predicts suffix pieces like 'ies', not a whole word. Members are mostly ' def' detectors plus other word-start fragment detectors.
result.label: ' def' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the token ' printing' (3D printing, offset printing, printing press), mostly after a modifier noun. Members are detectors of print/printing/press tokens. Silent on 'print age' in the contrast text.
result.label: ' printing' token detector

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ed' completing the word "targeted" (e.g. targeted gene editing, targeted therapy). It stays silent on 'ed' in other verbs like highlighted or broadened.
result.label: 'ed' in "targeted"

result.description: Fires on function words (of, that, and, B, are) right after the word "events"/"Event" in probability text about mutually exclusive events. Predicts event-related continuations like happening/occur. Silent on "of" after other nouns.
result.label: Function word after "events"

result.description: Fires on the token " Bell" as a surname or name piece, most strongly in "Bell Numbers" in math text. Members are mostly detectors of " Bell" itself. It weakly fires on word pieces like "ce" in "oceans".
result.label: Bell name token (Bell numbers)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ced' inside words like "antecedent" (also "unprecedented", "Procedures"). It stays silent on 'ced' at the end of "reinforced". Members detect 'ced' and 'ante' pieces.
result.label: 'ced' in antecedent

result.description: Fires on " Model" (occasionally " Standard") in the phrase "Standard Model" of particle physics, including Supersymmetric Standard Model. Supported by cosmology and particle-physics context members and "Standard" detectors.
result.label: Standard Model (physics) token

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'ag' (also 'agn', 'abil') in the middle of multi-piece words like reim-ag-ining, st-agn-ant, pl-ag-iarism, where a suffix is expected to follow. Silent on whole-word uses.
result.label: 'ag' mid-word piece

result.description: Fires on the word " academic" (adjective before a noun such as programs, standards, disciplines, life). Upstream members detect academic/educational/scholarly word pieces. Silent on the contrast text, which has no " academic" token.
result.label: ' academic' token detector

result.description: Fires on the suffix pieces 'ic' and 'ics' at the end of "Econom-" in economics headings or topic lists (e.g. "Public Econom|ics"). It stays quiet on 'ic' in other words such as Ethnomusic, Deficits and Electromagnetic.
result.label: Econom-ic/ics suffix in economics

result.description: Fires on the word " environments" (also "rooms", "environment") when it ends a noun phrase naming a setting, such as "virtual environments" or "multi-user environments", mostly in education and technology text. Silent on unrelated contexts.
result.label: "environments" after setting modifier

result.description: Fires on a period that follows a single initial or short fragment inside a name, abbreviation, or number (H.P., S.V., 2.1, U.S.S.R.), not on sentence-ending periods. Next-token logits favor single letters.
result.label: Period after initials or abbreviations

result.description: Fires on manner or frequency adverbs (easily, quickly, often, always) placed between a modal or auxiliary and its main verb, as in "can easily", "can quickly". It predicts a base verb next. It is silent on "carefully" after a verb.
result.label: Adverb after modal, before verb

result.description: Fires on mid-word suffix pieces like 'ious' (harmon-ious), 'ward' (awk-ward), 'ene', 'icate' (del-icate), completing an adjective. Mostly after a word stem, strongest on 'harmonious'.
result.label: Adjective suffix pieces (-ious, -ward)

result.description: Fires on a few unrelated word pieces: ' tone' (writing/voice tone), 'cent' inside 'incentive', and 'ps' in 'ellipses'. Mostly detectors of these specific tokens; the contrast shows ' tone' can stay silent at document start.
result.label: tone / incentive 'cent' pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' co' (as in coating, copper, cooperation) when it begins a longer word that is continued in the next token. Members are mostly ' co' detectors.
result.label: ' co' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragments ' cal' (calories, calibration, calorimeter) and ' sh' / ' Sh' (shaves, shaped, shifting) when they begin a longer word. Next-token logits favor continuations like 'aping', 'ifts', 'adows'.
result.label: Word-initial cal/sh fragments

result.description: Fires on the token 'stone' in the word 'cornerstone', used figuratively as a foundation of something. Other uses of 'stone' and similar foundation words (heart, foundation) contribute only as inputs.
result.label: 'stone' in cornerstone

result.description: Fires on the word " one" used as a pronoun or numeral (generic "one", "one's", "one of"), often at the start of a sentence after "As". Members are mostly detectors of "one"/"One" itself.
result.label: Token " one" detector

result.description: Fires on ' activities'/' activity' (also 'actions') right after the word "human", mostly in environmental or Anthropocene text about human impact. Silent on general history text without this phrase.
result.label: Human activities (environmental impact)

result.description: Fires on word-fragment tokens 'g' and 'com' in the middle of a word, where the word continues in the next piece (con-g-estion, under-g-laze, subject-com-plement). Also the 'g' of "e.g.". Silent on the whole word "compliments".
result.label: word-initial fragments 'g' and 'com'

result.description: Fires on the "I" of the abbreviation "AI" (artificial intelligence) after "A", also weakly on "elligence" in "Intelligence". Silent when "I" starts a word or is in other acronyms like IoT.
result.label: "I" in the acronym AI
"ural" in "plural"
result.description: Fires on the piece "ural" completing "plural" (pl-ural), mostly in grammar text about singular/plural subjects. Weakly on similar endings like "reflexive". Supported by members detecting "pl" + "ur/ural" and grammar context.
Fires on word-start pieces like ' organiz', ' oper', ' sched' that are followed by the suffix "-ational"/"-uling", in organizational-management text. It predicts the 'ational' continuation.
result.label: Organiz-/oper- before -ational

result.description: Fires on the word "plants" (also "Plant"/"plant") in botanical contexts, such as vascular plants, seed plants, or plant hormones. Weak on "plant" in other senses (rooted, planted). Silent in a list of biotech headings.
result.label: Botanical 'plants' token

result.description: Fires on the noun ending social-movement phrases such as "social justice", "Civil Rights", "civil rights", and "inequality", in text about activism and equality. Silent on "justice" at the start of a document.
result.label: Social justice / civil rights noun

result.description: Fires on the split-word piece " Elect" at the start of "Electroweak" (e.g. "the Electroweak Theory"), weakly on "elect" in electromagnetism. Predicts name-like suffix tokens. Members are "Elect" detectors in physics text.
result.label: Elect- in Electroweak

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'qu' (and sometimes a hyphen after a prefix like anti-) inside a longer word, as in Antiqu-ity or earthqu-ake, where the word continues. It is silent on 'qu' in Liquid. Predicts suffix pieces such as 'ity'.
result.label: 'qu' mid-word piece (Antiquity, earthquake)

result.description: Fires on past-participle verbs like "directed", "driven", "motivated", "inspired" in "X-directed / driven by / motivated by" constructions, often in discussions of motivation or conflict types. Members detect participles that usually precede "by".
result.label: Participles before "by": directed/driven/motivated

result.description: Fires on 'als' in "deals (with)" and on " dealing", where the word means "is about / treats the topic of". It stays silent on 'als' in "reveals". Predicts "with", "how", "whether" type continuations.
result.label: "deals/dealing with" topic verb

result.description: Fires on "determine"/"determining" and similar verbs like identify, discern, pinpoint, estimate, mostly in technical or mathematical text. It expects an object of measurement or decision, such as whether, the amount, or the optimal value.
result.label: determine / identify verbs in technical text

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "use" (also "application"/"utilization") in technical text, as in "involves the use of X". It stays silent on " of" after other nouns such as "order of" or "product of".
result.label: "of" after "the use"

result.description: Fires on structural-noun tokens like " stack", " ring", " shell" used as technical terms (electron shell, algebraic ring, stack in computing). Predicts nothing clear; members are per-token detectors for stack, ring, shell, table.
result.label: Technical structure nouns: stack, ring, shell

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ing' right after the stems "lay" and "mark" (laying, marking), and more weakly after a few other verb stems. It stays silent on 'ing' after stems like threaten, maintain, dissect and correct.
result.label: 'ing' after lay/mark stems

result.description: Fires on the 'bs' piece of "Adverbs" when it starts a document or heading in English grammar text (e.g. "Adverbs of manner"). Members are grammar-topic detectors (clause, past, plural) plus 'bs' detectors.
result.label: 'bs' in "Adverbs" grammar heading
Hyphen in Sapir-Whorf style compounds
result.description: Fires mainly on the hyphen in the name compound "Sapir-Whorf" (also Scytho-Sarmatian), plus some word-ending pieces like -atic/-ates. Silent on hyphens in Indo-European, pre-Socratic or human-environment. Seems to need a hyphen joining two surnames or ethnonyms.

Fires on the word piece ' catal' (start of catalyst/catalysis/catalytic), in chemistry text, and pushes toward the continuation 'yst'/'yt'. Members are mostly detectors of ' catal'/' Catal', plus some chemistry reaction context.
result.label: ' catal' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the final piece of a scholar's surname split into tokens, mainly 'eman' in Kahneman and 'sky' in Tversky. It also fires weakly on other name endings like Grover and Carnap. It needs a preceding name fragment in a list of thinkers.
result.label: Kahneman/Tversky surname ending

result.description: Fires on the word "angular" (or "Angular") in physics contexts such as angular momentum, velocity, displacement and acceleration. Members are mostly detectors of the same token. It weakly fires on a few word-start pieces like "altern" and "dio".
result.label: angular (physics) token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece "imate" in "Climate" at the start of a heading, and also on suffix pieces like "ity" in "hospitality" and "al". Mainly environmental or topical list headings; peaks are mixed.
result.label: Climate 'imate' and suffix pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' Saf' at the start of "Safety" (e.g. "Health and Safety", "Food Safety"), just before the "ety" completion. Members detect safety-related words and word starts.
result.label: ' Saf' piece before "ety"

result.description: Fires on the ending piece (-ve, -ves) of "revolve/revolves" in "revolve around", predicting " around". It stays silent on "crave". Weaker on "encircle". Members detect word-piece endings like cent-ers, -ves.
result.label: revolve(s) around word ending

result.description: Fires on single-letter word pieces (c, i, v, n, r, w) that appear as stray fragments appended after a complete word, often at the start of a glued or bracketed insertion. Silent when the letter is mid-word, as in 'transcends' or 'placements'.
result.label: Stray letter fragment after word

result.description: Fires on the word " or" when it joins two alternatives or introduces an alternate name or synonym, such as "Reformation or ...". Members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of " or". Silent on the contrast text.
result.label: " or" joining alternatives

result.description: Fires on the ' poll' piece in "air pollution" and other pollutant words (pollutants, acoustic pollution), where it is the start of a split word. It stays silent on ' poll' in "more polluted environments".
result.label: ' poll' in air pollution

result.description: Fires on the word " factors" (occasionally " factor") when it follows a modifier or quantifier such as "multiple", "several", "major" or "external". It stays silent when " factors" begins the text with no preceding context.
result.label: word " factors" after modifier

result.description: Fires on present-tense or base-form verbs (stayed, travel, perceive, pursue, choose, visit, delve) that follow a plural or "those who/we" subject and expect an object or complement next. Silent on 'age' inside nouns like vintage or homage.
result.label: Verbs after plural/relative subjects

result.description: Fires on ' and' joining abstract measurable quantities in a list or pair (magnitude, frequency, duration and ...), predicting words like frequency, scope, extent. Silent on 'and' in lists of engineering or process items.
result.label: 'and' after measurable-property nouns

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments in the middle of longer words, mostly 'cel' in porcelain, also 'lex' in reflexively and 'las' in cytoplasmic. Predicts word-completing suffixes like -ium, -ion, -atori.
result.label: Mid-word 'cel'/'lex' fragments

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after "single" (single-use, single-step, single-atom), where a compound modifier follows. Stays silent on hyphens after other words like equation-, back-, cost-, eco-. Weak secondary hits on other word pieces.
result.label: Hyphen after "single"

result.description: Fires on the token right after the word "flow" (e.g. "flow|ing", "flow| of", "flow rate"), predicting water-like continuations. Silent on "ing" in other words like analyzing or mastering, so it needs "flow" just before.
result.label: Suffix or "of" right after "flow"

result.description: Fires on ' and' (occasionally ' or') joining two short academic field or topic names, like "Music and Dance" or "Art and Education" in course or subject listings. Silent on 'and' in technical lists of properties or adjectives.
result.label: 'and' between subject-area names

result.description: Fires on the word " production" as a noun in economic or manufacturing text, such as "food production" or "factors of production". It stays quiet when "production" is used as a modifier before another noun, as in "rapid production times" or "production methods".
result.label: ' production' as head noun

result.description: Fires on the token " vision" in technical computer/machine vision contexts, especially after "stereo", "binocular" or "computer". Members are mostly " vision" detectors. The contrast text has no " vision" token, so the evidence for a condition is thin.
result.label: ' vision' after stereo/computer

result.description: Fires mostly on " order", especially in the sentence-opening "In order to" purpose phrase. It also fires weakly on modal-like words such as " can" and " would". Many members are " order" detectors.
result.label: " order" in "In order to"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ac' mid-word, mostly in "fast-paced" (fast-p|ac|ed), also in polysaccharides-type words. It stays silent on 'ac' in "Heraclitus". Weaker on other mid-word pieces like 'ies' in "mysteries".
result.label: 'ac' piece in fast-paced

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ent' right after 'acc' in words like accent, accentuate and accention. It stays silent on 'ent' starting a word or in 'attentive'. Members detect 'acc' and 'ent' pieces, and the logits favour 'uate'.
result.label: 'ent' inside 'accent' words

result.description: Fires on a few unrelated word pieces: ' wet' in "wet-on-wet" painting, 'Europe' in Indo-European, and 'ake' in "stakeholder". Mixed, polysemantic target; members are mostly language/word-piece detectors.
result.label: wet / Indo-Europe / stakeholder pieces

result.description: Fires on the verb " provides" (also " provide"), mostly when it follows an abstract or formal subject and leads into an object like "a powerful tool" or "the foundation for". It is silent on some uses after subjects such as "it" or "theory".
result.label: ' provides' verb detector

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' Ba', ' pag' (pagan), ' Bac', ' PM', ' Lö' that begin a longer word or name and need continuation. Silent on 'Ba' inside 'Bacon' after 'Francis'. Members are mostly generic subword/foreign-token detectors.
result.label: Word-initial fragments ' Ba', ' pag'

result.description: Fires on suffix pieces like 'atic' (mostly in "systematic"), also 'ized' and 'orous', in descriptions of formal, rigorous, structured approaches. Predicts words like formal, definit, cod.
result.label: Systematic/formalized suffix pieces
'pher' in atmospheric
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'pher' in "atmospheric" (Atmos-pher-ic), also in similar pieces like "peripherals". Members mostly detect 'pher' itself and predict the suffix 'ic'.

Fires on the word piece ' expect' when it is the start of "expectations" (split into expect + ations). The contrast text without that word piece stays silent. Predicts suffixes like -ations and -ancy.
result.label: expect- stem before -ations

result.description: Fires on the em dash (and similar dashes) in academic or expository prose, typically after a noun phrase where a clause or elaboration follows. Members are mostly dash detectors across variants.
result.label: Em dash in expository prose

result.description: Fires on ' communication' right after "non-verbal/nonverbal", in text about body language (eye contact, facial expressions, gestures). Silent on 'communication' after other adjectives like effective, professional or compassionate.
result.label: Non-verbal communication

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments completing a word, mostly 'itative' in "qualitative", also 'ze' in "breeze" and 'p' in "Streep". Silent on "quantitative", so it seems to need the "qual-" prefix. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Word-ending fragments, esp. qual-itative

result.description: Fires on "of" inside hyphenated compounds like stream-of-consciousness, state-of-the-art, time-of-flight, out-of-order. Needs a hyphen before "of" in a hyphenated compound; plain "of" elsewhere stays quiet.
result.label: "of" in hyphenated compounds

result.description: Fires on the token ' ground' in all its uses (electrical ground, ground-based, groundwork, dry ground). Members are mostly ' ground' token detectors; the contrast text lacks the word.
result.label: ' ground' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' and' (sometimes a comma) right after a person's name in a pair of thinkers or writers, like "Plato and", "Thales and", predicting another name (Aristotle, Pythagoras). Silent on 'and' joining common nouns or concepts.
result.label: 'and' after a person's name

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments mid-word or ordinal suffixes, mainly 'st' (1st century, cry-st-al), 'i' in Fermi, and 'old'. Members detect 'st', 'th' and digits. It seems to need a word-internal or ordinal-suffix position.
result.label: Ordinal and mid-word fragments (st, i)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'par' inside "transparency" (also 'par' in "separable", and 'ific' in "Trans-Pacific"), i.e. a mid-word fragment after "trans"/"se". Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: 'par' in transparency

result.description: Fires on a determiner (mostly ' these', also 'the', 'this', 'their') right after the fragment "standing" at the start of a clause, as in "standing these processes is crucial". Silent on ' these' after prepositions or verbs.
result.label: determiner after "standing" fragment

result.description: Fires on "as" (in "such as") and "like" (and German "wie") when they introduce a list of examples after a plural noun, especially innovations, technologies or advancements. It stays silent on comparative or other uses of "as".
result.label: Example-introducing "such as" / "like"

result.description: Fires on ' growth', mostly as a noun after "personal", "professional" or "emotional" in self-improvement or business text. It also fires weakly on "improvement". Earlier members detect growth, development and success tokens.
result.label: ' growth' after personal/professional

result.description: Fires on a word piece right after a standalone "c" token, e.g. the "n" in c1, c2, ..., cn (linear combination coefficients), and on continuations like c-ement, c-ushion, c-ater, c-ations. It needs the preceding "c" and is silent on "n" elsewhere, as in "yearn".
result.label: Piece after token "c" (cn, cement)

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'e' in "Appeal", 'ts' in "experts", and 'ient' in "experiential". It peaks on the 'e' of "Appeal" in headings. It looks like a word-piece completion latent, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-word fragments (App-e-al, expert-s)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'emes' (also 'eme', 'aph') completing linguistic terms like morphemes, phonemes, and metaphors. It appears in linguistics text, and members track language and sound vocabulary.
result.label: -emes ending in linguistics terms

result.description: Fires on commas, mostly after a word or phrase within a list or clause, such as list items (color, shape, form) or numbers. Silent on some commas after introductory phrases or before "which". Condition is unclear.
result.label: Comma in lists and clauses

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragments ' ag' and ' ep' (agenda, agency, aggression, agile; epic, epidemiology, epistemic) when they begin a longer word split into pieces. Next-token logits are mixed.
result.label: Word-initial ' ag' / ' ep' fragments

result.description: Fires on the modal verb ' can' after an abstract or inanimate subject noun (information, policies, feedback, trust) in expository text, predicting a verb like 'be' or 'lead'. Silent on 'can' after fiction/narrative-setting subjects or at text start.
result.label: Modal ' can' after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " Fund"/" fund" when it is the start of a longer word, especially "Fundamental(s)" at titles or document starts. It predicts continuations like "ament" and "amental".
result.label: Fund- start of "fundamental"

result.description: Fires on the final 'ment' piece of "Enlightenment" (the Age of Enlightenment, Enlightenment thought). It stays silent on 'ment' in other words such as "abandonment".
result.label: Enlightenment 'ment' suffix

result.description: Fires on the en dash '–' used as a separator in chains of ranges or lists (years, numbers, country pairs like Austria-Hungary–Russia–). Needs a dash that continues a sequence of items; quiet elsewhere.
result.label: En dash in range/list chains

result.description: Fires on the word " applications" (or " application") as a noun, mostly software or practical uses, e.g. "create applications", "for applications where". It is quiet in some scientific or industrial "applications" at the end of a phrase.
result.label: ' applications' token detector

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces ' inst', 'enti', ' differenti' that are followed by "-ability" (instability, differentiability), predicting 'abil'/'ability' next. Silent on plain "different".
result.label: inst/differenti before -ability

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ologies' (also 'ology') in the word "methodologies". It stays silent on the same suffix in "technologies". Predicts words like selection, procedure, employed.
result.label: methodologies suffix

result.description: Fires on word pieces in agriculture and farming text (agricultural, domestication, cultivation, crop rotation), predicting farming words like crops, tillage, agriculture. Silent when 'ural' appears outside farming context.
result.label: Agriculture and farming word pieces

result.description: Fires on the adverb "often" (mostly the piece "ften" in "Often" at document start, and " often" after "is/are"). Members detect often, sometimes, usually and frequently. The target is silent on unrelated text.
result.label: Frequency adverb 'often'

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ingu" in "lingu-" words (linguistics, ethnolinguism, sociolinguistic), at the start of a document or inside compounds. Predicts "istic"/"istics" as the continuation.
result.label: "ingu" piece of linguistics words

result.description: Fires on a noun or word-piece right after "a/an/the" in flowery, abstract prose, such as "a series of", "a paragon", "a towering figure". It expects a noun-of phrase to follow. Peak tokens vary.
result.label: Noun after article in ornate prose

result.description: Fires on the 'ying' piece in 'conveying' (communicating information, messages, ideas). Weaker on 'convey' itself. Members detect 'ying' and convey-type words; the contrast is silent on 'transmission'.
result.label: 'ying' in 'conveying'

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ab" in the middle of "vocabulary" (also weakly on similar mid-word pieces like " et", " pron", " ill"), predicting a continuation of the word such as "ul". Mostly in language and education text.
result.label: "ab" inside "vocabulary"

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ive' completing "express-ive" (expressive performances, expressive interpretation). Much weaker on other -ive adjectives like attentive or persuasive, and silent on productive, passive and collective.
result.label: 'ive' in "expressive"

result.description: Fires on the token ' shapes', most strongly after geometric adjectives (triangular, round, irregular shapes). It also fires more weakly on the verb use ("shapes our experience"). Members are detectors of shape/shapes and geometry words.
result.label: ' shapes' token detector

result.description: Fires on the verb "buy" and "purchase" (and pieces like buy-ers, purch-asing, bu-ying) in market or finance text about buyers and sellers, trading and contracts. It is silent on general derivatives text that doesn't use buying words.
result.label: buy / purchase in market text

result.description: Fires on the piece 'vent' inside words like "intervention(s)", also "unconventional" and "solvent". It needs the word-internal position after a prefix such as inter-, uncon- or sol-, not a standalone word.
result.label: 'vent' piece in intervention

result.description: Fires on coordinators (' and', ' or', '-', '/') joining two adjectives or modifiers, e.g. "semi-structured and unstructured", "serifs or sans-serif". Silent on 'and' ending a list of three or more items.
result.label: Coordinator between paired adjectives

result.description: Fires on " movement" as a head noun after "the" (or an adjective) in scientific explanations, e.g. "the movement of atoms/heat/current". Silent when "movement" starts the text with no preceding determiner.
result.label: "the movement of" noun in science

result.description: Fires on a middle given name (Joseph, Wilhelm, Gö) inside a multi-part name of a philosopher or scientist, when a surname is expected next, as in Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling. Silent on plain name lists.
result.label: Middle name in philosopher names
' maxim' word-start token
result.description: Fires on the token ' maxim' (maxim, maximization, maximizing, maxims), whether as the noun 'maxim' or the start of 'maximize' words. Predicts suffix pieces like 'izers' and 'agi'. Members are mostly ' maxim' detectors plus optim/minim.

Fires on commas separating items in a list of nouns (e.g. "planning, design, installation"), especially abstract process or attribute lists. Silent on commas after introductory adverbs or phrases such as "thus," or "ultimately,".
result.label: Comma inside noun lists

result.description: Fires on the word " medical" as a modifier in healthcare-themed text (medical equipment, staff, devices). Members detect healthcare, medicine and patient words. It stays silent on a health-data ethics passage that has no " medical" token.
result.label: ' medical' in healthcare text

result.description: Fires on the token ' L' (space-L), often as a symbol or start of an acronym/name, such as the Lucas number L(n), L1 regularization, or the start of a capitalized word. It is silent on ordinary text without the token.
result.label: Token ' L' detector

result.description: Fires on the word " mobile" (mobile phones, devices, commerce, apps), almost always as a modifier before a noun. Many upstream members are also detectors of " mobile". It slightly promotes next tokens like " phone".
result.label: ' mobile' token detector

result.description: Fires on word pieces in phonetics/linguistics text about vowels and consonants (vowel, vowels, "sounds" after vowel, consonants), predicting sound/phon-type continuations. Silent in general language text without phonetics.
result.label: Vowel/consonant phonetics terms

result.description: Fires on the word or word piece right after "for" (an adjective or noun start like medium, joint, precise, symmetrical) in a "X for ADJ/NOUN ..." phrase. Predicts "purposes/sake/reasons"-style continuations. Peak tokens are varied.
result.label: Word after "for" in purpose phrases

result.description: Fires on the word "rate"/"rates" as a head noun after a modifier (sampling rate, growth rate, instantaneous rate, rate law). Pushes next-token predictions toward "rates"/"rate". Members are mostly detectors of "rate"/"rates" and similar words like speed.
result.label: rate / rates noun

result.description: Fires on the middle piece of a split, rare surname after "Br" (Br-ou-wer, Br-us-ilov, Brø-n-sted), where the name continues with more pieces. Silent on "ou" in other names like "J.ouer".
result.label: Mid-piece of Br- surnames

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Dynam' as the start of "Dynamics" (Fluid Dynamics, Microsoft Dynamics), with weak activation on a few other tokens like ' slow', ' role', ' gro'. Members are detectors of 'ynam'/'Dynam' pieces.
result.label: ' Dynam' in Dynamics

result.description: Fires on the word piece "iger" inside "refrigerant", "refrigeration" and "refrigerated". It is weakly active on "er" in "minerals". Members are detectors of "iger" and of "ation" in refrigeration.
result.label: iger in refrigerant/refrigeration
' collabor' word-start piece
result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' collabor' (as in collaborate/collaborative), almost always before a suffix like -ate or -ative. Members detect collabor-, cooper-, and related word pieces. Peak tokens are almost all ' collabor'.
Fires on the word-piece 'ots' at the end of a split word, as in kn-ots, d-ots, Sp-ots, Rob-ots. Silent on the plain word 'knot', so it needs the 'ots' piece after a preceding fragment.
result.label: 'ots' suffix piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' polar' at the start of words like "polarization" or "polarizers", mostly after "of". Members are mainly ' polar' token detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' polar' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'ms' of "rhythms" (also 'mic'/'ythm' in rhythmic/rhythm) in music text. Members detect the rhyth- prefix plus music context. It predicts musical continuations like melody, pattern and flow.
result.label: rhythms word-ending 'ms' after rhyth-

result.description: Fires on the word " character" (and "character") in writing about fictional characters and character development, often before a possessive or "development". Members are mostly character-token detectors that push toward -ization/-ised style continuations.
result.label: ' character' in fiction writing

result.description: Fires on the comma right after the phrase "after all" (often following a dash), introducing a justifying clause. Other commas, such as in lists or after other phrases, stay silent or weak.
result.label: Comma after "after all"

result.description: Fires on precision-related modifiers such as " precise", " exact", and " precision", mainly before nouns like measurements, quantities, or timing in writing about accuracy and communication. Predicts nouns like specification and details.
result.label: precise / exact / precision words

result.description: Fires on ' ever' (as in "ever-evolving") right after "an", typically in opening phrases like "In an ever-evolving...". Silent on ' ever' after "the". Weaker on other nouns/words after "a/an" such as era, age, region.
result.label: "an ever-" after indefinite article

result.description: Fires on the verb right after a relative "that" (e.g. "ideas that resonate", "phrases that reflect", "conditions that impact"), mostly the start of "reson-" and "reflect". It needs the verb slot of a relative clause.
result.label: Relative-clause verb: resonate/reflect/impact

result.description: Fires on an incomplete word-start fragment (Tre, Pl, Se, imp) in a title-case heading or title, where the next piece completes the word (Trees, Planning, Seas, implications). Logits favor suffix pieces.
result.label: Word-start fragment in titles

result.description: Fires on commas and conjunctions ("and", "or") that continue a list of abstract nouns or items (e.g. "strength, power, safety, comfort,"), plus "and" inside hyphenated compounds. Silent on clause-level commas.
result.label: List-continuation commas and "and"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' phot' (photography, photon, photogrammetry) and occasionally ' aer' (aerobic), where the word is split and continues with a suffix. Silent on unrelated text. Members are mostly ' phot' detectors.
result.label: phot- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on ' musical' (also -ic/-omic endings) when it modifies a following noun like "notation", as in "musical notation systems". It stays silent on ' musical' after "their", "wider" or "sharing". Evidence for the exact condition is thin.
result.label: ' musical' before technical noun

result.description: Fires on " in" (or " within") right after a change/variation noun such as changes, fluctuations, shifts, trends, introducing the changed quantity. It stays silent on " in" after "role" or "participate".
result.label: ' in' after change/fluctuation nouns

result.description: Fires on the passive participle 'ized'/'ified' in "characterized by" (also 'defined', 'influenced', 'shaped' by), where the next word is expected to be "by". Silent on 'ized' in verbs like "revolutionized" or "harmonized" that take direct objects.
result.label: "characterized by" participle ending
'order' after hyphen prefix
result.description: Fires on the token 'order' as the second part of a hyphenated or prefixed compound, such as first-order, in-order or disorder. It is weaker on 'periodic'. It stays silent on 'orderly'.

Fires on the end of an adjective or head noun inside a "the most ..." superlative phrase (creative, abundant, catastrophic, metallic element), where a comparative continuation like "than ever" or "recorded" may follow. Silent on 'ating' in unrelated words.
result.label: Superlative phrase adjective endings
' ste' word-start before 'ering'
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ste' when it starts a split word, mostly 'steering' (adaptive/electric/power steering). Members are mostly ' ste' detectors. It weakly fires on similar word-start fragments.

Fires on noun-forming suffix tokens (-ulation, -ption, -ing, reduction) ending technical words in acoustics/soundproofing text, such as absorption, soundproofing, noise reduction. Silent on "manipulation" and "modulation" in audio-software contexts.
result.label: Acoustic/soundproofing term suffixes

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' oscill' (as in oscillator, oscillation), peaking in physics text. Upstream members are mostly detectors of this same token. It predicts word continuations like 'ations'.
result.label: ' oscill' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on ' years' (also ' centuries', 'decades') right after a large number or quantity of time, as in "11,700 years ago". It predicts ' ago'. Members detect time-unit words and digit strings.
result.label: Time unit after large number

result.description: Fires on mid-name word pieces in a person's name, especially first-name or surname fragments (Hay, von, Ort, Sab, Emil, Bren) in lists of famous scientists, and on odd Arabic or garbled-byte pieces. Predicts surname continuations such as ' von'.
result.label: Partial surnames in scientist name lists

result.description: Fires on word pieces following a lowercase or capital "d" that continue a word, mostly "ile" in "dilemma", also "end" in "dendritic", "amp" in "damping", "ating" and "ining". It needs the preceding "d" fragment.
result.label: Word piece after split "d" (dilemma)

result.description: Fires on ' then' as a sequencing adverb mid-sentence, after a preceding clause or "and" (e.g. "and then", "; then", "is then validated"). Silent when ' then' starts the text with no prior step.
result.label: Sequential ' then' after prior step
Mixed: ' common', 'en' in Phen-, prime mark
result.description: Fires on a mix of tokens: ' common' (and ' proper' in grammar contexts), the 'en'/'on' piece inside words like Phenomenology and Phonetics, and the prime mark in coordinates. No single clear shared role.
Fires on motion verbs, mainly " moving" and " move" (also " travel"), especially in physics text about moving objects, particles, fluids or observers. Members detect move/moving/movement tokens.
result.label: moving / move motion words

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ence' completing the word "essence", mostly in philosophy text about essence and existence. It stays silent on 'ence' in other words such as impermanence, interdependence and permanence.
result.label: 'ence' in "essence"

result.description: Fires on a word piece (mostly 'ous', also '&') directly after a capital 'R' at the start of a name or acronym, as in R-ous-seau, R-ous-burgh, R&D. It stays silent on 'ous' as an adjective suffix, as in 'ambiguous'.
result.label: Piece after initial R (Rousseau, R&D)

result.description: Fires on the token " stress", most strongly in mechanics/engineering contexts (tensile, compressive stress, stress-strain) and also in other uses. Members are mostly detectors of "stress" and "stresses" at earlier layers.
result.label: ' stress' token detector

result.description: Fires on commas and other connectors (' by', ' or', ' in', apostrophes) that follow a noun in expository lists or enumerations, but is silent on many commas before participial clauses. The pattern is mixed and the evidence is thin.
result.label: Commas and connectors in enumerations

result.description: Fires on scope-wide adjectives such as " overall", " general", " larger" and " full" right after "the", before a noun like structure, performance or picture. Mostly appears in economics and analysis text. It predicts nouns like impact, context and scope.
result.label: "the overall" scope adjective

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Mathemat" (start of Mathematical/Mathematics), mostly at the start of a line or heading such as a title list. Weaker on " mathematics" mid-sentence. Members are mostly detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' Mathemat' word piece
Word piece 'pt' in skeptic
result.description: Fires on the middle word pieces 'pt'/'ptic' in "skeptic/skeptical/skepticism", after the 'ske' piece. Weak activation on similar mid-word fragments in philosophy/academic words (Descartes, scholars).
Fires on the word-start piece ' ep' (as in epic, epidemic, epistemic, epistolary), where the next piece is usually a suffix like 'ic', 'ide' or 'ist'. Members are mostly ' ep' detectors.
result.label: ' ep' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' evol' (evolve/evolved/evolving), usually after a subject noun, predicting a suffix like 've' or 'ved'. Weaker on similar pieces such as ' del' and ' dram'. Members are mostly ' evol' detectors.
result.label: ' evol' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on verbs and nouns of obtaining, extracting or assessing (obtain, extract, assess, resource, sensor) in technical earth-science, geology and engineering text, often after "for/to/of". Predicts geoscience word pieces like meteor, ge, rock.
result.label: Extraction/obtaining terms in geoscience engineering

result.description: Fires on ' median' and on 'omed' in repeated "Biomedical" course-title lists, with weaker firing on a few other words (' worst', ' north'). Members are statistics/math word detectors (mean, variance, median). Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: median / 'omed' in Biomedical

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after "second" (also "first"), as in second-order logic or second-person. It stays silent on hyphens after other words like non-, decision-, conception-. Predicts continuations like "order" or "person".
result.label: Hyphen after "second"

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'ad' (Akkad, Leadership), 'on' in "Decolonization", and ' Mass' in "Mass Spectrometry". Mixed word fragments inside longer words or terms; silent on 'ad' in other words like Stradella.
result.label: Mid-word fragments ad/on/Mass

result.description: Fires on the magnitude word ' million' (sometimes ' thousand') right after a number or quantity word, as in "250 million years" or "several thousand stars". Members are detectors of million/billion after numbers.
result.label: million/thousand after a number

result.description: Fires on the word " during" when it follows a noun phrase and introduces a historical period or era (e.g. "during the Middle Ages"). Members are mostly detectors of " during" itself.
result.label: ' during' introducing a time period

result.description: Fires on the word " visual" (or "Visual") as a modifier before a noun, such as visual elements, visual experiences or visualization. Members are mostly detectors of the same token. The contrast text has no "visual" token.
result.label: ' visual' token detector

result.description: Fires on the opening parenthesis ' (' that follows a noun or noun phrase in a list or description, where a parenthetical such as an abbreviation, example, or number is about to start. It stays silent on a line-initial ' (' and after some analysis phrases.
result.label: Parenthesis after noun phrase

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ive' when it completes the word "supportive" (after "support"). It stays silent on 'ive' in other words such as constructive, attentive, cohesive.
