result.description: Fires on the verb ' allow' / ' allows' (also weakly ' also' or ' and' before it) when it follows a subject noun phrase, usually before 'for'. It is silent when 'allows' starts the text with no subject. It predicts ' for' or an object.

Fires on " of" right after a historical period noun such as "Age" or "Era" (e.g. "The Age of Reason", "Era of Studio Recording"). It stays silent on "of" after ordinary nouns like "scenes of" or "qualities of".
result.label: "of" after Age/Era period nouns

result.description: Fires on the final pieces of the acronym "SVM" / "SVMs" (the 'M' or plural 's') after "Support Vector Machines", in machine-learning text. Predicts ML-related continuations. Silent on 'M' in other words like "Mind".
result.label: SVM acronym end in ML text

result.description: Fires on the preposition (' with', ' between', ' among') right after the noun "interactions"/"interaction", where the next word names the interacting parties. Silent on 'between' after other nouns such as interplay, negotiation or interdependence.
result.label: preposition after "interactions"

result.description: Fires on ' idea' when it is the head noun right after an opening "A central/key/crucial" at the start of a document (e.g. "A central idea in..."). Silent on ' idea' mid-sentence, such as "This idea" or "the idea of".
result.label: "A central idea" at document start

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens, often ' L', ' powerful', ' into', or words after "creating/bisects" in geometry or art text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness, so no clear pattern emerges.
result.label: Scattered mixed tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on mixed connectives and word pieces (" and", ",", " or", " to") inside lists in environmental, nuclear and chemical waste text. Silent on "and" in design/product lists. Evidence is weak and the circuit failed.
result.label: Connectives in environmental/chemical lists

result.description: Fires on adverb suffix pieces (-entially, -ically, -itionally, -ably) that start a sentence right after a full stop, forming a sentence-opening adverb like "Essentially," or "Additionally,". Members detect -ly/-ically suffixes.
result.label: Sentence-initial adverb suffix pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (spaces before numbers, commas, "),", word endings) in lists and academic or historical prose. It is silent on some spaces before digits. Peaks are mixed, so the pattern is weak and unclear.
result.label: Scattered punctuation in list-like prose

result.description: Fires on the word or piece right after "X over" in a comparison, such as "contract negotiation" in "collaboration over contract negotiation" or "over time". It is silent with "instead of". Evidence is mixed across peak tokens.
result.label: Noun after "over" comparison

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' and', ' or', ' the', ' as', ' proven') mid-sentence, often in abstract or legal/academic text. Contrast shows ' and' often silent, and the members are weak and generic, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on the word right after "stepping" (back, on, out, stones, into the), the continuation of a "stepping ..." phrase. It stays silent on "the" after other "into" verbs like diving, delving or digging into.
result.label: Word after "stepping"

result.description: Fires mainly on ' just' (also ' than', ' a') in "X is more than just Y" constructions, where a "more than" frame sets up a contrast. Silent on ' just' after "not" in "not just ... but".
result.label: "more than just" construction

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' expl' (start of explore/exploration), mostly early in a document after a short opener like "Our", "While", "Upon". Silent on some mid-text ' expl' tokens, so it seems to depend on position or context.
result.label: ' expl' token near document start

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on mixed tokens (' and', ' their', word pieces like ' W', ' SY', 'ies'), often mid-phrase in lists or technical text. Silent on many ' and' cases. Evidence is thin; circuit failed to reproduce well.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function/word-piece firing

result.description: Diffuse, low-consistency target firing on varied tokens (' and', commas, ' they', word-endings) mid-list or mid-phrase in expository academic text. Members are generic token detectors; no clear single trigger or condition is visible.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase function tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in a text about the termination stage of protein synthesis: "ination" in "Termination" at document start, "final stage", "outlines". Silent on "termination" after "the term". Evidence is mixed and the members are diffuse.
result.label: Termination stage of translation (mixed)

result.description: Fires on function tokens (' is', ',', ' as') right after a philosophy-concept subject, such as "the Transcendental Ego" in Husserl text. It stays silent on "phenomenology is" and similar. Members are philosophy-topic detectors.
result.label: Verb after philosophical concept subject

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention-layer latent peaking on varied tokens (' and', ' of', ',', ' channels', ' is') in abstract academic prose. Members are generic token detectors; the contrast shows silence on ' and' in similar contexts, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse function-word latent, abstract prose

result.description: Fires on the token right after "challenging" (or similar difficulty words), such as situations, terrain, or, economic. It is a slot after a difficulty adjective, and the members mostly detect challenge/difficulty words.
result.label: Token after "challenging"

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on 'aging' in 'managing' and on function words (that/can/are/the) after a subject noun. It is silent on 'aging' in other 'managing' contexts, and the members are generic token detectors, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered 'aging' and function words

result.description: Fires on a word or word piece that follows a hyphenated "X-based" compound (Region-Based Convolutional Neural Network, PCR-based o-, graph-based Semi-Supervised Learning), mid-term or mid-word in the noun phrase. Peak tokens vary; the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Word after "-based" compound modifier

result.description: Fires diffusely on varied tokens (commas, ' and', Arabic word pieces, 'new') mostly at points where a continuation follows. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and noisy, so no clear meaning emerges.
result.label: Diffuse mixed-token connective firing

result.description: Fires mostly on ' of' (also 's', 'ed') in the phrase "take heed of", right after "heed"/"he-" word pieces. It stays silent on ' of' in other constructions such as "era of", "One of", "ahead of".
result.label: ' of' after "take heed"

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "version(s)" or "copy/prototype" nouns (versions of, version of), where a copy or variant of something follows. Silent on " of" after "number", "development", "design" or "atoms".
result.label: "of" after version/copy nouns

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (' became', ' definition', ' in', 'ative', document start) in abstract academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent, it is silent on many ' became' contexts, and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered abstract-prose tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a multi-token word (' phen', ' imag', ' organ', ' ha', ' inst') in scientific or academic text, where the word is incomplete and a continuation is expected. Silent on ' phen' in 'phenomena' after 'these'. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Word-start fragments in science text
'to' after continue(s)
result.description: Fires on ' to' right after "continues/continue/continued" (e.g. "technology continues to evolve"), sometimes on ' continues' itself. Silent on other uses of ' to' such as "due to" or "from X to Y".

Fires on " of" or " the" right after "dawning" (e.g. "the dawning of civilization / the 20th century"), a phrase about the beginning of an era. Silent on "of" after other nouns like advent, emergence, superiority. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: "of/the" after "dawning"

result.description: Attention-layer target firing on varied positions (function words like "of", "and", adjectives, mid-word pieces) in abstract academic prose. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is diffuse, so the trigger and condition are unclear.
result.label: Diffuse academic-prose positions

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' where', ' in', ' stark', word pieces) at positions where a noun or context word could be followed by a setting or manner phrase. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low. Silent on some ' where' examples.
result.label: Scattered tokens before setting/context phrases

result.description: Fires on ' of' (and a few following words) right after the noun "frequency", in scientific text about measured quantities. It stays silent on ' of' after other nouns like speed, history, progression or dance.
result.label: ' of' after "frequency"

result.description: Attention-layer target firing on scattered function words and word pieces (one, of, as, and, be, when) in academic or technical text. No dominant token and no clear shared construction. Members are mixed token detectors, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic text

result.description: Fires on ' history' in the phrase "throughout history" (also "throughout human history"). It stays silent on ' history' after "the" or in "cultural history", where the word is a plain noun.
result.label: 'history' after 'throughout'

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (pre, K, In, p, to, or, work) mid-word or mid-phrase where a continuation is expected. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is weak. Members are generic token detectors.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in cooking and temperature text, such as the 0 in "350°F", the space before a number, and "ment" in "investment". Peaks are mixed and consistency is low. Members include cooking and heat detectors. The circuit failed its faithfulness check.
result.label: Cooking temperature text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, 'the', 'allows', word endings) in expository science and academic text, often after a noun or topic term. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful; no clear single trigger or condition.
result.label: Scattered punctuation in expository text

result.description: Fires on the comma right after a sentence-initial "Nowadays" at the start of a new sentence. It stays silent on commas in lists or after other clauses. Members are mostly generic comma detectors.
result.label: Comma after sentence-initial Nowadays

result.description: Fires on the verb " exist" (plural subject, as in "free groups exist because"), and sometimes the following " in". Members are mostly detectors of " exist" and its "existential" pieces. The contrast is a text without it.
result.label: verb "exist" detector

result.description: Fires on the verb or word right after the subject "segment" in a description of what a text segment covers (delves into, highlights, discusses, explores). Silent after "chapter" or "section", so it needs the word "segment" as subject.
result.label: Verb after "segment" summarizing content

result.description: Fires on scattered function-word and word-piece tokens (' and', ' the', 's', ' for') in expository geography, history and culture prose, often mid-phrase before a second item or noun. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed to reproduce the target well.
result.label: Mixed function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the token after "unique"/"distinctive" plus a noun-ish word (propositions of, linguistic, traits, product or service,), where the next word would elaborate the distinguishing properties. Peak tokens are varied; evidence is mixed and low-consistency.
result.label: After unique/distinctive: property slot

result.description: Fires on 'the' or 'of' inside the opening phrase "At the turn of the (century/20th)" at the start of a document. Silent on 'the' after other prepositions like "of the" or "during the". Members are mostly generic 'the' detectors.
result.label: "At the turn of the" opener
Subject pronoun after where/how clause
result.description: Fires on subject pronouns (' they', ' you', ' we') and 'as' inside an embedded clause after "where", "how" or "as much about", as in "stay where they are". It stays silent on 'they' after a colon, semicolon or main-clause verb.

Fires on the open parenthesis after a technical term or multi-word name, where an abbreviation or symbol like (PMF), (CAD), (P) is likely to follow. Silent on parentheses that start ordinary asides like "(or ...)".
result.label: Parenthesis introducing abbreviation

result.description: Fires on transitive verbs like promote, cause, allows, assess, help, right after a modal or "to" with a subject noun phrase, where an object noun comes next. Silent on "promote" after "also" or a comma. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Verb after modal predicting object

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit: target peaks on varied function words (' where', ' of', ' with', ' since', ' secure') and document start, in abstract expository text. It is silent on some ' where' cases, and members are diffuse token detectors, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed function-word peaks, diffuse circuit

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' en' in "automatic enrollment" (after "automatic"), where it begins a word like enrollment. Silent on ' en' in other words such as enrich, enhanced, enforce, encompasses.
result.label: ' en' in "automatic enrollment"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' we', ' expl', ' this', 'of') inside "as we move forward / progress further" style sentences about exploring or understanding a field. Silent on ' we' in other clauses such as "perhaps we should" or "as we look".
result.label: "We move forward" exploration phrasing

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly commas but also ' when', ' as', ' the' and word pieces, in scientific or technical text. The contrast shows commas in similar text staying silent, so the condition isn't clear. The circuit fails and its members are generic.
result.label: Scattered commas in technical text

result.description: Fires on function words (and, is, of, it, to) and word pieces shortly after "repetition" or "repetitive" in text about repetition. Members detect repet-/-ition tokens. It stays silent on "and" in other contexts without repetition nearby.
result.label: Function words after "repetition"

result.description: Fires weakly on assorted function words and mid-phrase tokens (' and', ' their', ' these', ' essential', ' been') in expository academic text, where a following noun or continuation is expected. No clear single token or construction; the circuit is a weak, low-faithfulness fit.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires mostly on " in" right after "changes" (changes in Earth's / the market / consumer behavior), plus a few other tokens. The contrast shows the same "changes in" also staying silent, so the extra condition is unclear. The circuit failed its faithfulness check.
result.label: "in" after "changes"

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside multi-word topic or course-name list items (e.g. "Biomedical Ethics", "Financial Technology", "IoT") in list-like headings separated by paragraph breaks. Silent on some "ics" endings like "Mathematics". Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Topic-title word pieces in lists

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied mid-phrase tokens (adverbs, conjunctions, word pieces) in abstract academic prose, often where a continuation is expected. Peaks are scattered and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on scattered punctuation and function words (commas, "),", "and", "of", "to") in abstract expository lists and business or academic prose. No dominant token, and it is silent on many commas. The circuit failed and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered punctuation in expository lists

result.description: Fires on function words (that, the, as, such as) right after metrics/measurement language (KPIs, measure, indicators), where a measured quantity is about to be named. Predicts metric/benchmark-type words. Silent on 'that' after generic business insights.
result.label: Function words after metrics/measurement talk

result.description: Fires on the final '4' of "BB84" (also the '9' in a year like 1984), in quantum cryptography text. It is silent on '4' in IP v4 or a section number "4.", so it needs the BB84 name context.
result.label: BB84 protocol name final digit

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and word pieces (' and', '-', ' the', ',', ' of') in technical or academic prose, mid-list or mid-phrase. Peaks are scattered with low consistency, and the members are generic token detectors. No clear single role.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic text

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (' different', ' to', ' (', ',', 'by', word pieces) in expository technical text. No consistent token or context; the circuit failed and members are generic. Logits favor science/technical words weakly.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires mostly on ' tort' in legal text ("modern English tort law"), with a few weaker hits on word pieces like 'ation' in "Quadratic Equation". Supported by legal and legislation-related upstream members. The circuit failed faithfulness, so the picture is partial.
result.label: ' tort' in legal text

result.description: Fires mostly on "rop" in "crop" and on "," or " and" following crop-related terms in agricultural/biotech text (crop efficiency, crop diversification and). Mixed peaks and low consistency; evidence is weak.
result.label: crop word piece and following connectives

result.description: Fires on function tokens (comma, "and", "to", "into", "the") that directly follow the word "flat" or a list item in a flat/curved/tonal context, in art or linguistics text. Silent on commas elsewhere.
result.label: Connector token after "flat"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' assess' (assessment/assessing), mostly in environmental, educational or technical assessment tool contexts. It stays quiet on 'assess' in business risk-assessment text. Members are 'assess' detectors that push 'ment'.
result.label: ' assess' word piece, non-business

result.description: Fires on ' adapt' when it begins "adaptive" right after "such as" or "like" in a list of technologies. It stays silent on the verb "adapt to", as in "models that adapt to changing conditions".
result.label: ' adapt' in "such as adaptive"

result.description: Fires on the subject slot right after a sentence-initial "using X," clause: ' it', ' one', or agent nouns like policymakers/investors/readers (-ers). It stays silent on "researchers" in object position.
result.label: Subject after "using X," clause

result.description: Fires on function words (and, of, on, with) or a repeated "Computer" right after "computer science/engineering" context, where the next word is likely a field term like science or engineering. Silent on 'and' in other lists.
result.label: Function words after computer-science phrases

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on ' analysis' (notably after "error"), plus ' shape', ' to', ' can', ' aid'. It stays silent on "analysis" after thorough/critical/comprehensive. Members are generic and non-discriminative; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered 'analysis' after 'error'

result.description: Fires on " the" (also "like", " today") right after a sentence-ending period followed by "like", as in ".like the idealized shape". Silent on ordinary " the" mid-sentence after verbs or prepositions. Members are mostly generic token detectors.
result.label: "like the" after a period

result.description: Fires on function words that introduce an example or list item, like "such as", "like", "including", "being the", often before a named example. It is inconsistent, and the same "as" is silent in other contexts. The circuit is weak and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Example-introducing connectives (such as)

result.description: Fires on commas, "of", "that", "who" right after a noun naming an ancient civilization (Indus Valley Civilization, Sumerians, Hittites), where a descriptive clause or appositive follows. Silent on commas after similar nouns in other settings.
result.label: Punctuation after ancient civilization names

result.description: Fires on commas and ' and' inside lists of abstract nouns (security, transaction management, and logging; risk assessment, business continuity, and...), at the join before the next list item. Evidence is mixed: it is silent on similar list 'and's, so the circuit is weak.
result.label: Abstract-noun list separators

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, 'is', 'found', digits, word pieces) in expository science and food text, mid-phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so no clear trigger or condition emerges.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase expository tokens

result.description: Fires on the word right after "riding" (on, a, the) inside simile-style "it's like riding..." phrases comparing an abstract process to an activity. Silent on similar "like walking on a" contexts, so the condition is narrow and unclear.
result.label: Function word after "like riding"

result.description: Fires on function words (' are', ' and', ' as', ' that') right after the subject "principles" (or similar), e.g. "principles and concepts", "principles serve as". Predicts law/apply-type continuations. Silent on ' are' after other subjects.
result.label: Function words after "principles"

result.description: Fires on connective function words (' and', ',', ' to', ' who', ' as') in abstract expository prose about organizations, processes or ideas, where a list or continuation follows. It stays silent on the same ' and' in many similar contexts, so the condition is unclear. The circuit failed.
result.label: Connectives in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the end of the first noun phrase after "balance" (e.g. "risks and benefits", "new products", "responsibilities"), where a "with/between" contrast is expected next. Silent on the same tokens elsewhere, such as "dialogue".
result.label: Noun ending balance-X phrase

result.description: Fires on connectives or continuation tokens (" and", ",", " in", "innovation") right after "creativity" or "foster creativity" lists. Silent on " and" in other contexts, so it needs the creativity context. Members detect "cre-ativity".
result.label: Token after "creativity" in lists

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function tokens, mostly commas in lists of items or steps (e.g. "approval, closure, inspection"), plus "and", "that", "two". Evidence is mixed. The circuit failed and members are diffuse.
result.label: Commas in lists, mixed function words

result.description: Fires on tokens shortly after the verb "fill" (e.g. "fill the", "fill an atom", "fill in", dough after "filling an empty"), at varied positions in the phrase. Fill-detector members feed it. It stays silent on ordinary " and" without "fill" earlier.
result.label: Tokens following the verb "fill"

result.description: Fires on tokens in the predicate after the modal "must" (e.g. "must be", "must convey ... and", "must have ...,"), where a requirement is being listed. Silent on "can be" or "may be", so it needs "must".
result.label: Continuation after "must" requirements

result.description: Weak, mixed layer-6 attention latent peaking on varied tokens (' pain' in paints, 'ors' in transistors, ' increased', '0' in a year) where a word is part of a combination or mixing context. Circuit failed, so evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed tokens in combining contexts

result.description: Fires on ' of' after an abstract action or process noun (detection, identification, creation of ...), in technical or academic text. It stays silent on some 'of' after similar nouns like development, study, exploration, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' of' after process nouns

result.description: Fires on an opening quote mark (or comma) that follows a quoted word in a list of quoted example words or markers, such as "well," "so," in linguistics text. It stays quiet on a quote that opens a single example after "such as".
result.label: Quote mark in quoted-example lists

result.description: Fires on " mark" and the following hyphen in the "mark-and-sweep" garbage collection algorithm name. It stays silent on hyphens in other compounds. Weak activation on "mark" in market/marketing words.
result.label: mark-and-sweep garbage collection
' with' after a noun or comma
result.description: Fires on the word ' with' when it follows a noun or a comma and introduces an added element, as in "X, with a career…" or "in the 1960s with the emergence…". It stays silent on some ' with' tokens after clauses, and the contrast doesn't show why.

Fires on scattered function words (' your', ' be', ' like', ' are', ' while') in second-person, advice-style text, often after a subject or modal. It stays silent on some ' your' tokens after prepositions or verbs. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered 'your'/'be' in second-person text

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on commas, "and", and "to" after a noun or verb like "seeking", often where a list or continuation follows. Contrast commas in other lists stay silent. Members are mostly generic token detectors; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered commas, 'and', 'to' connectors

result.description: Diffuse attention-based target peaking on assorted tokens (' implicitly', ' and', ' the', ' of', word-start pieces) in abstract academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent and members are generic list/word-piece detectors; the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mixed function-word peaks

result.description: Fires on 'also', 'commonly', 'known' or 'often' right after a comma following a subject noun at the start of a text, introducing an alias ("X, also known as..."). Silent on 'also' used as a plain adverb mid-clause.
result.label: Alias introducer: ", also known as"

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on scattered tokens such as ' sometimes', ' Computer', ' in' and ' for' in computing or technical prose. Members are generic and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in technical prose

result.description: Fires on the word right after "understand" (or "know"), e.g. "understand the", "understand not", "understand their". It is an attention-based latent that marks the object slot of the verb. The peak token itself varies.
result.label: Word after "understand"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ending a noun phrase in a list or coordination (comma, "or", plural endings, "claims", "efforts"), mostly in expository text about weather, risk and abstract topics. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Noun-phrase end in lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly the article ' a'/' an' (also 'B', 'even'), where a noun phrase is expected next. It is silent on many other ' a' tokens. Members are mostly generic early-layer 'a' detectors, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered article 'a' before noun

result.description: Fires mostly on sentence-ending periods in abstract expository prose, sometimes at the start of the next sentence or on words like "as" or "to". It stays silent on many other periods, and the evidence doesn't show what separates them.
result.label: Sentence-final period in expository prose

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' and', ' en', 'ization', ' modification') in formal scientific or expository prose, especially ' and' inside noun-phrase coordination. It stays silent on ' and' after commas in casual, metaphorical text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: 'and' in formal expository coordination

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (' in', ' the', digits, ' it') in abstract expository prose about culture, history or art. Peaks are inconsistent and the same ' in' is silent elsewhere. Members are generic and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on ' and' (also ' as', ' or') in lists of social-science factors, e.g. "socio-cultural developments, and" before the final item. Silent on similar list-final 'and' in other contexts; the circuit is weak and the condition is unclear.
result.label: List-final 'and' in socio-cultural lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function tokens (commas, "and", "is", "of", "are", "can") inside expository lists and noun-phrase sequences in formal or technical prose. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak. Silent on some commas in similar lists.
result.label: Commas and function words in lists

result.description: Fires on the prepositions ' in' and ' into' (also weakly ' to', ' with') after a noun, notably in title-like phrases such as "The Role of Technology in History" and "Idioms in Education". Silent on some ' into' cases such as "insight into".
result.label: Preposition 'in'/'into' after noun

result.description: Fires on the token inside or right after a list item following "include/includes" (e.g. "include more", "include pian-os", "include real-time"), where an enumerated item is being introduced. Peak tokens vary; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Items within "include" lists

result.description: Fires at varied positions right after a "X has been an essential/integral component/element/part of ..." framing, on words continuing the phrase (life, for, the, inter-, element). Peak tokens are mixed, and it stays silent on some 'inter' tokens in similar sentences.
result.label: Essential-component-of phrase continuation

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on varied noun or suffix tokens (' structure', 'ing', ' instrument', ' delete') that end a phrase, often after a noun modifier. It stays silent on ' structure' in other contexts. Evidence is thin and the members are generic.
result.label: Mixed phrase-final tokens, structure/-ing

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (many, product, projects, 'ing', ' of') in economics and finance text. Members are mostly economy and finance detectors. The peak tokens are inconsistent, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Finance/economics text, varied tokens

result.description: Peaks scatter across unrelated tokens (word pieces like 'ide' in fluoride, ' gas', ' of', ' the', ' as'), mostly mid-word or within noun phrases in technical text. Consistency is low and the circuit fails faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on "ival" in "differential survival" and on ")," closing a parenthetical in a list, just before "reproduction". It stays silent on "ival" in plain "survival" without the "differential" before it. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: differential survival / list-closing paren
Connector words after abstract nouns
result.description: Fires on connective function words and dashes (through, from, to, —) that link a clause to a following elaboration, in abstract academic or art prose. Silent on 'through' after motion verbs. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.

Fires on varied tokens (periods, "to", "on", "providing", "-oring") in expository text about tailoring or structuring a process or approach, where a verb or noun phrase describing a method or step is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent. The same period token is often silent.
result.label: Process/method description, varied tokens

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens ('ph' in allophones, ' from', ' software', ' data', ' and'). It is silent on 'ph' in polyphonic. Members are mostly generic token detectors and list-start markers; evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed tokens, 'ph' in allophones

result.description: Fires on connective or function tokens (' and', ' as', ' with', ',', '-') inside abstract lists or coordinated phrases in data, research and business text. Stays silent on many ' and' tokens, and the cause is unclear. Weak circuit.
result.label: Connectives in abstract data-topic lists

result.description: Fires on the particle after "opens/opened" (mainly " up", also " for" in "opening doors for") when a subject like new tools or techniques creates new possibilities, in creative or technical prose. Predicts a following "new"-type object.
result.label: opens up (new possibilities)

result.description: Fires on words and punctuation inside a list of requirements right after "the need/necessity/demand for" (e.g. "need to create robust, efficient, and"). It is silent on ordinary "and" elsewhere. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Tokens after "need for" phrases

result.description: Fires on conjunctions and commas (' and', ',', ' or') that join items in a list of named things, such as types of solids or people's names, where another name follows. It stays quiet on 'and' after common-noun lists like faces, edges.
result.label: Conjunction before next named item

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "sense" in "sense of X" (our sense of self-worth, sense of harmony). Silent on ' of' after other nouns like components, context, density, personality.
result.label: ' of' after "sense"

result.description: Fires on a comma or "and" right after the word "peace" (peace, stability, and… / peace and security), in a list of goals. Silent on commas after other nouns. Members detect "peace"/"peaceful" plus generic comma/and list positions.
result.label: Comma/and after "peace" in lists

result.description: Fires on the pieces of "avant-garde" (mainly "gar", also "de" and the hyphen) when the word is spelled out. It stays quiet on "gar" in other words such as "Edgar". Early members detect " avant" and the hyphen.
result.label: avant-garde word pieces

result.description: Fires weakly on varied connective or mid-phrase tokens (' and', ' with', 'ization', ' quality', ' uses') in abstract expository text about music, soil, or sodium. Mixed peaks and a failed circuit; the contrast does not clearly show what separates it from silent ' and'.
result.label: Mixed connectives in expository text

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit firing on scattered function and adjective tokens (' be', ' are', ' political', ' financial', "'"). Silent on ' be' after 'can' in other contexts; members are mostly generic rare-token detectors. Evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered be/are/political tokens

result.description: Fires on "of" (and word pieces like -ical, -ological) right after quality/reliability/accuracy/authenticity-type nouns, where a scientific or analytic object comes next. It stays quiet on "of" after "use", "field", "application".
result.label: "of" after quality/reliability nouns

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking mostly on ' of' after abstract nouns (collection of, breakdown of), plus scattered tokens like ' water', 'ing', ' both'. Silent on many other ' of' contexts; the circuit failed and members are diffuse, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered ' of' after nouns (weak)

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (' the', ' for', ' and', ' of') and word pieces in abstract expository prose, often after 'of' or a verb. The same ' the' often stays silent, and the evidence doesn't show why. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "importance" or "significance" (e.g. "the importance of X"). It is silent on some other "importance of" cases, so the rule is not fully clear. Upstream members detect importance/significance words and "of".
result.label: "of" after importance/significance

result.description: Fires on the comma that ends a sentence-opening "Despite its X" concessive phrase, just before the main clause. It stays quiet on commas after other openers like "For those unfamiliar..." or "From ear to toe".
result.label: Comma after "Despite its…" opener

result.description: Fires on virus- and bacteria-related word pieces (' vir', 'b'/'acter', 'and') in microbiology and genetics text, e.g. "viruses", "bacteria", "viral vector". Silent on general genetics text without these microbe words.
result.label: Virus and bacteria word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ' of', ' in', 'us') in academic or expository text, often mid-list or after a noun in a coordinated phrase. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness; the contrast shows no clear condition.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on tokens in and right after the name Mendeleev (the "le" piece, "'s", " in") in chemistry/atomic-science text. It stays silent on "'s" after other scientists' names, so it seems tied to Mendeleev.
result.label: Mendeleev name continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on the 'ing' piece in 'plementing' (implementing), after the 'plement' fragment. It stays silent on 'ing' in other words like maintaining, proofing, employing. Members include a 'plement' detector and implementation-related members.
result.label: 'ing' in 'plementing'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' as', ' in', ' of', ' for', 'Q') in technical or academic text. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' as' is silent in "such as" in the contrast. The evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires on "The" when it begins a title of a work (show, play, epic, publication) inside quotes or a list of titles, e.g. 'The Shadow', "The Importance of…". It stays silent on ordinary running text.
result.label: "The" starting a work title

result.description: Fires on the word " Media" (also " media"), mostly as a heading at the start of a line or document, like "Media Strategy" or "Media Evaluation" in marketing-plan outlines. It stays silent on other headings such as "Public" in the contrast.
result.label: Media as a heading word

result.description: Fires on the pieces of "co-stimulatory signals/molecules" in immunology text: "atory" within co-stimul-atory, then " signals" or "molecules" right after it. It stays silent on " signals" in other immune contexts without "co-stimulatory".
result.label: co-stimulatory signals/molecules

result.description: Fires mostly on commas (also "ate", "and") separating items in a list of verb phrases or abstract nouns about promoting collaboration, innovation, or discourse. Silent on commas in some similar lists of virtues, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Commas in abstract promotion lists

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens in technical or math text (' in', ' within', 'uro', 'auss', ' attached'), often a word right after a noun, before a relative "which". Members are generic and non-discriminative; the evidence is unclear.
result.label: Mixed technical-text tokens, unclear
' such' after "applications/fields"
result.description: Fires on ' such' (as in "such as") right after a noun like "fields" or "applications" in phrases like "important in fields such as". It is quieter after other nouns such as concepts, methods or mechanisms.

Fires mostly on " is" (also " of") after a quoted nickname like "The God Particle," before a predicate such as "an essential element". Silent on " is" after plain subjects like "The bottom quark". Members are diffuse and low-specificity, and the circuit failed.
result.label: " is" after quoted nickname appositive

result.description: Fires mostly on ' health' (also ' gold', 'lic', 'ably', ' for') after a preposition like 'in' in policy/economics text, but stays silent on some ' health' cases such as 'financial health'. Circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: ' health' after 'in' in policy text

result.description: Fires on the word right after "Dendritic" at the start of a document (" cells", " polym", " structure"). It stays silent on " cells" after other words like "T cells" or "antigen-presenting cells". Members are mostly generic word-piece detectors.
result.label: Noun after "Dendritic" at start

result.description: Fires weakly on varied tokens inside lists or coordinated noun phrases (commas, "and", "in", nouns like management/practices) in expository text. The pattern is diffuse and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the trigger is not clear.
result.label: Diffuse list and coordination positions

result.description: Fires on function words like " to", " for", " be" after "essential/crucial/important (for X)" in writing-advice and grammar text, but the same " to" often stays silent in similar contexts. The circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Infinitive 'to' after importance phrases

result.description: Fires on 'of', 'from' or '(' right after "life cycle" / "lifecycle" (assessment) phrases, in sustainability and engineering text. Silent on 'of' after other nouns like "analysis of" or "impact of".
result.label: 'of' after life cycle

result.description: Fires on varied early-document tokens, mostly ' Song' (songwriting) at the start of a text, and on words like ' requires', ' typically', ' not'. Peaks are scattered and inconsistent; members are generic token detectors.
result.label: Scattered early-document tokens, 'Song'

result.description: Fires on connective or function words (and, in, or, while, commas) that follow a clause about small sizes or statistics and introduce a continuation. The same ' and' is silent in plain lists, so the evidence for what it needs is thin.
result.label: Connectives after small/statistics clauses

result.description: Fires on conjunctions (' and', ' or', commas) and some word pieces in technical science/ML text (biology, neural networks, data). It is silent on many ' and' tokens in general text, so the pattern is mixed and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Conjunctions in technical science text

result.description: Fires on varied function and filler words (and, of, an, is, economic) in text about law, regulation and economics, apparently preparing a legal or economic term next. Members detect legal and financial word pieces. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Legal/economic text, varied function words

result.description: Fires on " Capital" in the title "The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism", just before "ism". Members include Luther and Church detectors, suggesting Protestant/religion context supports it.
result.label: Capital in Spirit of Capitalism

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of fields, disciplines or topics (e.g. "mathematics, chemistry, ..."), mid-list after a noun. It stays quiet on commas after a single term like "science," that is not part of an enumeration.
result.label: Comma in list of fields

result.description: Fires on the function word or verb right after the subject "incentives" (are, and, be, play, like), in essays about incentives. It stays quiet on 'are' after other subjects such as ethics or frameworks. Logits favour reward/pay words.
result.label: Word after "incentives" subject

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention-layer target firing on mixed tokens (' the', ' of', ' complex', ' like') mostly after verbs like "simplifying" or "understanding" in technical text. Members are mostly word-piece detectors; the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Diffuse function words after technical verbs

result.description: Fires on ' have' right after the acronym-like "TAs" (plural "As" ending), as in "TAs have become more...". Also fires on "As" pieces. Silent on ' have' after ordinary nouns or relative "that".
result.label: ' have' after acronym plural "TAs"

result.description: Fires on the word or word piece right after "standardized", "unified" or "structured" (catalog-ing, financial, comma, -ess, -ations). It marks the noun slot in a standardization phrase. Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Word after standardized/unified

result.description: Fires on the document-start token (shown as ¶) when it follows a preceding passage, often at a boundary between concatenated documents or topic lists. It stays silent at many other such boundaries, and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Document-start token after prior text

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention-layer target firing on scattered tokens (' the', ' of', ' becomes', ' to', word pieces), often inside title-like or named phrases such as "Land of the Free". The circuit failed faithfulness; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Diffuse function-word and piece firing

result.description: Fires on math notation tokens like parentheses, '=' and the start of the right-hand side in text describing "the general form" of a function or equation. Peaks are scattered and weak; the same '=' stays silent in other equation contexts.
result.label: Math notation after "general form"
Hyphen in "cutting-edge"
result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "cutting-edge" (after "cutting"). It stays silent on hyphens in other compounds such as "eco-friendly", "ill-suited" or "-based". Weak activation appears on "ge" pieces in geology words.

Fires on ' logical' (also 'ic' in 'epistemic') in a specific abstract philosophy/logic passage, e.g. after "categorical" in text on deductive reasoning. Silent on ' logical' in other contexts. Circuit is weak and diffuse, with philosophy-themed members.
result.label: ' logical' after 'categorical' in philosophy

result.description: Fires on the final piece of an acronym such as TCR or BCR, the 'R' or 'TC' after "T cell receptor (" in immunology text. Silent on 'R' in a different context (virus-infected (TCR) infr...). Members are mixed acronym and generic detectors.
result.label: Receptor acronym TCR/BCR piece

result.description: Fires on the verb " rely" right after a plural subject, as in "Artists rely heavily on...". Weaker on related forms like "relied" and "depend". Members detect rely/depend/reliance words that predict "on" or "heavily".
result.label: ' rely' verb before 'on'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' imag' (imaging, imagery, imaginary), where the next piece completes the word. Upstream members are mostly ' imag' token detectors across layers, plus a few detectors of other word-start pieces such as fa, l, Spect.
result.label: ' imag' word-start piece

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target firing on scattered function words (' is', ' more', ' as', ' them') in culinary or knife-related text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit fails faithfulness; members are generic and non-specific.
result.label: Scattered function words, culinary text

result.description: Fires on adjectives of care and rigor (meticul-ous, careful, proper, thorough) right before a noun like attention, planning, or adherence. Members detect careful/thorough/rigorous words. Likely predicts nouns of process.
result.label: Careful/meticulous adjective before process noun

result.description: Fires on " of" right after a quality-type noun (quality, depth, nuance, complexity, clarity) following "elevate/enhance/enrich" in abstract, essay-like text. Silent on " of" after other nouns, such as "power of" or "utilization of".
result.label: " of" after elevate-the-quality nouns

result.description: Fires on conjunctions and function words (' and', ' or', ' but', ' in') after a clause or list item, plus ' Mov' in ARIMA. Silent on many ' and' tokens in other contexts. Weak, low-faithfulness circuit; condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered conjunctions after list items

result.description: Fires on commas (also 'and', 'or') separating items in a list of examples, e.g. foods, sauces, materials, after "such as" or "including". Silent on commas in ordinary clauses or non-list uses.
result.label: List-item separators in example lists
Mid-term word-piece continuation in technical terms
result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in the middle of multi-piece technical terms or names (Kaplan-Meier, VR, nonparametric, ray tracing), where a continuation is expected. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit failed and is weak evidence.

Fires on varied tokens inside business/legal-style expository lists and noun phrases (' and', ' or', ' legal', 'atives' in 'initiatives'), but stays silent on 'atives' in 'narratives'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Business/legal list connectives and word pieces
" of" after "success" at document start
result.description: Fires on " of" right after "The success" at the very start of a document. It stays quiet on " of" after other nouns such as importance, quality, aspect or interaction. Members mostly detect "success" and its variants.

Fires on varied tokens (verbs, word pieces, commas, 'the') mid-sentence in technical or scientific text about genetics, clustering and maps, where a technical noun is expected next. The peak token is not consistent, and the same 'the' stays silent in other places.
result.label: Technical text mid-phrase, varied tokens

result.description: Fires on the last piece of a word or compound right after "entrenched", mostly "service" in "fee-for-service" and suffixes like "-ist" in "mercantilist". Evidence is thin and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Word end after "entrenched" (fee-for-service)

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (' in', ' and', ' to', ' need', ' new') in abstract academic/scientific prose, mid-phrase after a noun or verb. Fires inconsistently and stays silent on some ' in' cases; evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires weakly on varied tokens in one passage about weather and humanity's "thirst for"/"quest to understand", mostly on ' for', ' patterns', ' understand'. Silent on other ' for' uses. Members are diffuse and the circuit fails, so evidence is thin.
result.label: Thirst/quest for understanding phrasing

result.description: Fires weakly on varied tokens ending a noun phrase, often plural abstract nouns like 'points', 'approaches', 'techniques', 'qualities', or 'FS'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed, so the pattern is not clear.
result.label: Plural method/viewpoint nouns, mixed

result.description: Fires mostly on ' with' after a comma that opens a trailing absolute clause ("culture, with its..."), in descriptive essay-like text; also occasionally on '.' or ' the'. Silent on some ' with' in similar contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Comma-led ' with' clause opener

result.description: Fires on word pieces or nouns inside long comma-separated lists of abstract process nouns (dissemination, utilization, maintenance, facilitation), mostly mid-word or on list items. Members are list-comma and "etc"-style list detectors.
result.label: Items in abstract noun lists

result.description: Diffuse attention-layer target firing on scattered tokens (word endings, prepositions like for/in/or/to, 'on', 'its') mid-sentence in formal prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and unfaithful, so no clear meaning emerges.
result.label: Diffuse mid-sentence function-word latent

result.description: Fires on the token " breaks" (plural noun) in text about narrative or writing pauses, such as "narrative breaks serve as...". Members detect break/breaks/breaking tokens. Weak on other break- pieces. Silent on contrast text without it.
result.label: "breaks" as narrative pauses

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (function words, word pieces, nouns) in abstract academic prose, mid-phrase where a noun or technical term is expected next. Peak tokens are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase academic prose

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit firing on scattered function words (' and', ' the', ' its', ' makes', ' study') in academic or expository text. Members are generic token detectors and the contrast shows no clear separating condition; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on function words (' a', ' the', ' to', ' in') right after a sentence subject like "combination of X and Y" or "amalgamation", i.e. the verb-then-object slot after a combining/integration noun. Silent on ' a' in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function word after 'combination' subject

result.description: Fires on tokens (' the', word pieces like -ives, -istic, -ions) that complete the object of "setting"/"set" (goals, objectives, the tone, the stage). It stays silent on 'the' after other verbs like "incorporate" or "into".
result.label: Object slot after "setting"

result.description: Fires on the suffix "ness" completing "consciousness" (and weakly on " conscious" before it) in philosophy-of-mind text. It stays silent on "ness" in other words like "directedness" or "richness".
result.label: "ness" in "consciousness"

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (word pieces like 'ion', 'ary', 'ful', and ' resource', ' to') in definitional passages about access control and abstract concepts. Peaks are scattered and the members are mostly generic token detectors, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in definitions

result.description: Fires diffusely on varied function words and mid-phrase tokens (and, that, their, -ling) in technical or academic text on math and science. Peaks are inconsistent, and the circuit is low-faithfulness with no discriminative members.
result.label: Diffuse technical-text function words

result.description: Fires on tokens within text about prime numbers and number-theory conjectures (Twin Primes, "Prime Conjecture", "prime numbers", "are"), but stays silent on "conjecture" in other contexts like the Poincaré Conjecture. Needs the prime-number topic.
result.label: Prime number theory text

result.description: Fires on " the" (occasionally " of" or " that") right after "second half of" or "latter half of", where a century or decade comes next. It stays silent on "of the" after other nouns such as "dawn of" or "movements of".
result.label: "the" after "second half of"

result.description: Fires on the verbs of giving or taking in acid-base and redox chemistry, mainly 'ate' in "donate" and ' accept' after "bases", plus related words like 'gains' and 'pairs'. It stays silent on 'ate' in "conjugate" or "consolidate".
result.label: Donate/accept in acid-base chemistry

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (word pieces, "of", "as", "both") inside abstract academic sentences of the form "how X can contribute to / function as / affect Y". Peaks are scattered; the circuit seems to track that "how ... verb" frame.
result.label: Abstract "how X can affect Y" frame

result.description: Fires on tokens right after the word "thematic" (narrative, map, elements, and, development), i.e. the word or piece following "thematic". It stays silent on " elements" after "these" or "narrative", so it needs the preceding "thematic".
result.label: Token following "thematic"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'our' inside "flour"/"flourish" (fl+our), mostly in "flourished/flourishing". Members are detectors of this 'our' after 'fl'. Predicts continuations like -ishing/-ished.
result.label: 'our' in flour/flourish

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'ived', ' with', word endings) inside lists of abstract nouns in academic or social-science prose, such as legal or social frameworks. Mixed peaks and a failed circuit; the condition is unclear.
result.label: List-like academic prose, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on " and" (also " or") joining two nouns in a pair of parallel items, strongest in "tokamaks and stellarators" in fusion text. Silent on "and" ending longer lists or joining clauses.
result.label: "and" joining two paired nouns

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ending a noun phrase in technical text (enterprises, browsers, language, conductors, 'a', 'in'), often after "within/between/inside". Members suggest predicting a context or setting noun. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Technical phrase-end before context noun

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (suffix 'ing', 'and', 'or', 'the', 'that') mostly inside paired or coordinated phrases like "opportunities and challenges" or "young and old". Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Coordination slots in paired phrases

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (has, have, that, a, a verb after a subject) right after a long abstract subject noun phrase about the influence of crafts, math or science, where a predicate about impact is expected. Silent on relative 'that' after a noun.
result.label: Predicate slot after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on " but" or " also" in the "not only X but also Y" correlative construction, at the second half after the first clause. It stays silent on "but" in other uses, such as plain contrastive "but" after a comma.
result.label: "not only... but also" second half

result.description: Fires on function words (and, of, an, a, is) right after the word "basis" in linear algebra text, e.g. "A basis is an...", "basis and the concept". Silent on "and" in other math contexts without "basis" just before.
result.label: Function words after "basis" (linear algebra)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (of, to, between, it, 's) in abstract expository text about science, economics and society. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on punctuation or function words (comma, "and", "among", "on", "the") right after the word "debates" or similar debate/discourse nouns in academic text. Silent on commas after other nouns. Members include debate-preposition detectors ("around", "over", "on").
result.label: Function word after "debates"

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens, such as 'and', commas, 'our' and word pieces, usually where a new word or word continuation is expected. Peaks are mixed and the circuit failed. The contrast shows 'and' ending lists is silent.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after the verb "overlook" (or overlooking/overlooked), as in "often overlook the dining experience". Stays silent on ' the' after other words or prepositions like "with the" or "at the".
result.label: ' the' after 'overlook'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' and', commas, ' the', ' to') and word pieces in expository lists and technical prose, but stays silent on ' and' ending a comma-separated list. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mixed connectives in expository prose
'ception' in "deception"
result.description: Fires on the piece 'ception' when it completes the word "deception" (de|ception). It stays silent on 'ception' in other words like "preconceptions", where members detecting 'de' plus the piece matter.

Fires on the first token (often ' the', ' sust', ' a', ' N') right after "prioritizes" or "emphasizes" near the start of a document, where the next word is the thing being prioritized. Silent on ' the' after other verbs or words.
result.label: Object after prioritizes/emphasizes

result.description: Fires on ' fixed' (also arbitrary, limited, absolute) when it follows a negation like "is not", as in "meaning is not fixed". Members detect negation words and static/limited adjectives, in abstract philosophical or conceptual text.
result.label: "not fixed" after negation

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (function words like ' to', ' of', ' the', plus word pieces) in academic-style text, with no consistent token or context. The contrast shows ' to' silent in many places. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function-word positions, unclear

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target peaking on plural-person or quantifier words like "individuals", "all", "them", "users", and occasionally mid-word pieces. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin and the circuit failed.
result.label: Plural people/quantifier words (weak)

result.description: Fires on ' Fre' as the first piece of the surname "Freire" after "Paulo", in education-theorist lists. Silent on ' Fre' starting "Freeman" in a list of famous people. Members are mostly education/teaching topic and word-piece detectors.
result.label: Fre in Paulo Freire

result.description: Fires on connectors like " even", " (", " and", " sometimes" right after "dozens (or/and)", where a larger quantity ("thousands", "millions") is about to be given. Silent on " even" in other uses.
result.label: Escalation after "dozens" toward thousands

result.description: Fires on ' into', ' among', ' are' and similar words right after a "if n items are distributed/placed" clause in pigeonhole-principle-style combinatorics statements. Silent on ' into' in other uses (divide into, insight into).
result.label: Pigeonhole distribution: items placed into/among

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' in', ' by', ' rather', ' to', ' another') that follow a verb or participle and introduce a prepositional or contrastive phrase, in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast offers no clear rule.
result.label: Scattered prepositions after verbs

result.description: Fires after "create/foster an environment" (or "conditions"), on the noun or the following relative-clause word (in, which, where, around), where a clause describing the setting is about to be introduced. Silent on "business/workplace environment" as a plain noun.
result.label: Created environment, relative clause linker

result.description: Fires on " revolution"/" Revolution", most strongly in the math phrase "solids of revolution" (also "axis of revolution"). It stays silent on "revolutions" after "circles and" and "volume revolution".
result.label: revolution in "solids of revolution"

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', ' are', ' while', comma) right after the word "facts" or in fact-versus-opinion contrasts. It stays quiet on 'and' in ordinary lists of emotions or items.
result.label: Connectives in facts-vs-opinions text

result.description: Fires on varied function or continuation tokens (" two", " which", " as", plural "es") in documents about overfitting/underfitting in machine learning, at early positions in the text. Silent on " two" without that topic context.
result.label: Overfitting-text function words

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "phase"/"stage" in process-description text (e.g. "final phase of the...", "last stage of developmental..."). It stays silent on "of" after other nouns like "every stage of" or "part of", so it is selective.
result.label: "of" after final phase/stage

result.description: Fires on " I" in the quoted Descartes phrase "I think, therefore I am", the " I" right after "therefore". Weak activation on words after "think" in casual speech. Silent on a bare "Cogito" mention.
result.label: "therefore I am" — I

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (mid-word pieces, 'and', commas, nouns after adjectives) in abstract academic-style prose, mostly where a noun phrase or word is incomplete or continues. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in abstract prose

result.description: Fires mainly on " engaged" (especially "keep readers engaged"), and occasionally on "th" in Carthage or similar word pieces. Members detect engage/engaged/engagement forms. It stays silent on "emotionally connected" phrasing.
result.label: "engaged" after keep readers

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yn' inside "nucleosynthesis" (also photosynthesis, Keynes, polynomial), where the next piece is likely 'thesis'. It is silent on the surrounding topic words without this piece.
result.label: 'yn' in nucleosynthesis

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments of multi-piece words, such as 'Hus' in Husserl, 'amb' in gambling, and 'cor' in underscoring or incorporating. It predicts a continuation piece and is silent when 'Hus' starts the document.
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments (Hus, cor, amb)

result.description: Fires on the word "engineering" as a noun ending a field phrase or after "in" (e.g. "structural engineering", "In engineering,"). It stays quiet when "engineering" is an adjective-like modifier before another noun (e.g. "engineering disciplines", "engineering material").
result.label: "engineering" as a field noun

result.description: Fires on the end of a noun or word piece naming a kind of language or literature, such as styles, genres, written, or spoken English. It follows "various" or "literary" style modifiers. It stays silent on "regular expressions" in computing.
result.label: Literary/language category nouns (styles, genres)

result.description: Fires on the token ' sun', most strongly when it is a word stem before a suffix like -light, -spots, -beams, -hat (e.g. "converting sunlight"). Weaker on standalone "the sun". Predicts compound continuations such as 'light'.
result.label: ' sun' as compound stem

result.description: Fires on " where" introducing a relative clause that defines or explains a process, concept, or technical term (e.g. "decay, where unstable..."). It is silent on "areas where they need...". Predicts "in" or "by" next (whereby, wherein).
result.label: "where" defining a process clause

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' intr' (start of intricate/intricacies) right after "the" or "an", as in "insight into the intr...". Silent on ' intr' directly after verbs like "unlocking", "amplify", "through".
result.label: ' intr' after the/an (intricacies)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' mechan' (start of mechanics/mechanisms), strongest after a physics modifier like classical, celestial, statistical or quantum. Weaker at sentence start or with other preceding words; silent on contrast text lacking it.
result.label: ' mechan' after physics modifier

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'enz' (as in Lorenz, senzati) and sometimes 'nt' in 'sovereignty'. It needs the token to be inside a longer split word; members detect other mid-word fragments like 'ester', 'ptic', 'ust'.
result.label: Mid-word 'enz' fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yt' in cell-biology words like phagocytosis, endocytosis, exocytosis and cytotoxic, where it follows 'c' or 'oc'. Upstream members are mostly 'yt' detectors.
result.label: 'yt' piece in -cytosis words
Letter 'n' token
result.description: Fires on the bare single-letter token 'n', whether as a variable, an escaped "\n" fragment, or a mid-word piece (super-n-ova, eth-n-ography). Upstream members are detectors of the same 'n' token.
Fires mostly on '&' inside abbreviations like M&A or M&E, also on ' Environment' at the start of a document title. It is silent on '&' at the very start of the text, where no letter comes before it.
result.label: Ampersand in abbreviations like M&A

result.description: Fires on ' those' (also 'individuals', 'people') as a pronoun-like noun for a group of people, especially after "to/for" in support or aid contexts, anticipating a relative clause ("those who..."). Silent on 'those' after "particularly" or "be".
result.label: Group 'those' after support preposition

result.description: Fires mostly on " the" (also "of", "ional") after "the rhythm/pace/tempo of" in writing-pacing text, before "narrative/story". Members detect pace/tempo/narrative words. Silent on " the" after "aspects of" in other contexts.
result.label: "the" after pace/rhythm of (narrative)

result.description: Fires on ' including' introducing a list of examples or subgroups after a general noun phrase (e.g. "everyone, including individuals with..."). Members detect include/including/such as. Silent in at least one financial-analysis "including" case.
result.label: ' including' introducing example subgroups

result.description: Fires mostly on ' AV' in "AVL Trees", plus scattered word pieces like 'ass', 'se(ek)', 'ival' inside longer words. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is only partly clear.
result.label: AV in AVL Trees, word pieces

result.description: Fires mostly on " quest" in "the quest for X" (search/seeking-for nouns), with scattered weaker hits on other tokens. Members detect search/query/necessity words that precede "for". Circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: "quest" in "quest for"

result.description: Fires on the word piece "break" in "outbreak" (disease outbreaks) and on " Ge" at the start of a document in geodesy terms (Geodetic, Geoid). Mostly two token-specific pieces inside particular words.
result.label: outbreak 'break' and Geo- start

result.description: Fires on an opening parenthesis ' (' placed right after a noun or noun phrase in academic-style prose, where a parenthetical with examples, abbreviations or clarification follows. Silent on ' (' after adjectives or at text start.
result.label: Parenthesis after noun phrase

result.description: Fires on prepositions (" of", " from", " in") after a noun in abstract descriptive prose, where a noun complement follows. Silent on many other " of" uses (e.g. "layers of", "capable of", "face of"). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Prepositions after nouns (of/from/in)

result.description: Peaks scatter across unrelated tokens (' for', ' traces', ' starting', ' through', word pieces) in expository history/academic text. No consistent token or context; the circuit failed and members are generic.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token target, unclear

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " Pro" at the start of a longer word (Probability, Protagonist, Prospect), where it is a fragment that needs a continuation. Silent on other tokens in the contrast.
result.label: Pro- word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on "aring" in "wearing" (split as we|aring) and on " wear" as a verb, mostly with clothing context. Members detect the wear/aring pieces. Weak activation on a few stray tokens.
result.label: "wearing" / "wear" word pieces

result.description: Fires on the start of a new topic-title line in lists of academic subject headings (e.g. " Cultural" after a line break, "International", "lingu-istic"), often the first word of a term in a list of course or topic names. Mixed and weak evidence.
result.label: List-item topic title words (Cultural, International)

result.description: Fires on ' a'/' an' (also 'mere', 'supp') right after a "not only/just/merely/more than just" negated-restriction phrase, where a contrasting "but" clause is expected. Silent on ordinary ' a' after verbs or prepositions.
result.label: article after "more than just/merely"

result.description: Fires on the word piece "inter" when it follows the prefix "re" (as in "reinterpreted"). Members detect prefix pieces like inter, im, def and product after "re". The target is silent on "intersect" in the contrast.
result.label: "inter" after re- prefix

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'on' in "harm-on-ious/harmonize" and on 'oust' in "ac-oust-ic", mid-word pieces in sound/music/design text. Weakly on 'compos' in "compositions". Predicts suffixes like -ious or -ic.
result.label: Mid-word 'on' in harmonious, 'oust' in acoustic

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' mel' (start of "melody"), mostly when it follows "harmony and" or a comma in a list of music elements. It is quiet on "mel" in plural "melodies" after adjectives or "these".
result.label: ' mel' in music list (melody)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "mo" in "turmoil" (after "tur"), mostly in discussions of emotional or internal turmoil. Members are detectors of "mo" and of other mid-word fragments.
result.label: "mo" inside "turmoil"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " diplom" (and "plom" in "e-diplomacy") before endings like -atic, -acy, -at. Members are mostly detectors of the same fragment, plus other incomplete word stems.
result.label: diplom- word fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece "vit" (starting "vitamin") in nutrition and food text, and on "it" inside words like "gravitational". Members detect vit/Vit, nut-, and food-source words.
result.label: vit- piece in vitamin

result.description: Fires on ' to' completing a "from X to Y" transition or shift (agrarian to industrialized, feudalism to capitalism). Silent on ' to' after "due", "led", "began" or "contributed".
result.label: 'to' ending from-X-to-Y transitions

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' absor' (start of absorb/absorption/absorber), mostly in sound-absorption and physics text, and predicts completions like 'ption' and 'bing'. Members are mostly ' absor' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' absor' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'am' inside longer words like seamlessly, ceramic, creaminess, among, and on ' Ch' in "Supply Chain" at document start. Silent on 'am' in "Examining". Mostly a mid-word fragment detector, with a weak logit push toward suffixes like -lessly.
result.label: 'am' mid-word fragment (se-am-lessly)

result.description: Fires on the piece "urban" inside the word "disturbances" (dist|urban|ces), where it is a mid-word fragment. Members detect word-piece fragments that precede a "-ces" ending.
result.label: "urban" in "disturbances"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'in' inside "ref-in-ement/ery" (and ' cam' in camera words), a mid-word fragment where a suffix like -ement or -ery follows. Silent on 'in' in prominence, Ruin, Einstein.
result.label: Mid-word 'in' in refinement

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece "raction" in refraction/diffraction, in optics and physics text. It is silent when "raction" starts a document with no "ref" or "diff" before it. Weak activation on a few other word pieces and "of".
result.label: "raction" in refraction/diffraction

result.description: Fires on the word piece "lex" inside "reflexive/reflexivity/reflexion" (also "Flexibility"). It stays silent when "lex" starts the text with no "ref" before it, so it needs the preceding "ref" piece.
result.label: "lex" in "reflexive"

result.description: Fires on ' with' after a verb or noun when it introduces a manner phrase, as in "approach it with composure" or "serve with dignity". It predicts abstract manner nouns like care, regard or respect. It stays quiet on accompaniment or association uses of 'with'.
result.label: ' with' introducing manner phrase

result.description: Fires on verbs of signification such as "indicates", "represents", "signifies", mostly after a technical subject like a coefficient or value, where the verb introduces what it means. Weakly on "describes" and "representing".
result.label: Indicates/represents meaning verbs

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Go' when it is the start of a split "Goal" (e.g. "Specific Goal", "Goal 4"). It stays silent on the complete word "goal" in lowercase. Logits favour completions like 'al'/'setting'.
result.label: ' Go' as start of 'Goal'
Mid-word pieces in medical therapy terms
result.description: Fires on word-internal pieces (onal, ap, ine, ics, ant) inside multi-token medical/biomedical words, such as monocl-onal, Ther-ap-ies, radi-other-apy, in therapy and treatment text. Members are medical-context detectors predicting a continuation of the word.

Fires on ' well' as the start of a word or compound (well-being, well-defined, wells) and on word pieces like 'law' in flawless, 'exception'. Silent on 'as well as'. Predicts word-continuation suffixes.
result.label: 'well' prefix in compounds, not 'as well as'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Ne' at the start of a split name, mostly "von Neumann" (also Neuronal, Neo-). Members detect ' Ne' and similar first pieces of split surnames; the next token is a continuation piece like "umann".
result.label: ' Ne' in von Neumann

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ipped" in "equipped" (equ|ipped), as in "is equipped with". Members detect the "equ" prefix plus "ipped"/"ips" pieces. Silent on text without the word.
result.label: "ipped" in "equipped"

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ament' piece in "testament" (as in "a testament to"), with weak scattered activation on other word pieces, Arabic endings and zero-width characters. Members detect the "test" prefix and the "ament" piece.
result.label: 'ament' in "testament"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sh' when it begins a word like "shaping" right after a comma (participial clause, e.g. "centuries, shaping"). It stays quiet on ' sh' after "in" or in "shifts".
result.label: ' sh' starting "shaping" after comma

result.description: Fires on ' work' (also book, paper) as a noun naming a scholar's authored output, especially after "seminal", "pioneering" or a possessive in academic biographical text. Silent on 'work' in other senses or slots.
result.label: Seminal work noun after praise adjective

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment ' spons' (sponsorship) and on 'och' in 'mitochondrial', i.e. incomplete word pieces that need a continuation. Silent on the contrast text, which has no such fragment.
result.label: spons / och word-piece fragments

result.description: Fires on the piece 't' inside "story|t|elling" / "storytellers", after the split "story" token, and pushes towards "elling/eller" continuations. It stays silent on 't' in "don't".
result.label: 't' in story-t-elling

result.description: Fires on the word " such" when it directly follows a plural noun, as in "benefits such as" or "challenges such as", where it introduces examples. It stays quiet when " such" follows a comma or "of", or starts a clause.
result.label: "such" after a noun (such as)

result.description: Fires on the token ' X' (or ' x') as a standalone letter, mostly the 'X' of "X-ray" and "XRF" in technical text, and also as a variable name in math. Silent on unrelated physics text without the letter.
result.label: Letter X token (X-ray, variable)
