result.description: Fires mainly on the token " simulation" (also at the start of " Liter" in "Literary") in technical or scientific text. Members are mostly detectors of "simulation" and related words such as MD, simulations and models. The contrast text is silent where the word is absent.
result.label: ' simulation' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " common"/" Common" in phrases like "Least Common Multiple", "common practice", "common assets", and "common themes". Upstream members are mostly detectors of "common" at earlier layers.
result.label: word "common" token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on " inner" (as in "inner membrane" or "inner function"), with scattered weaker hits on "1", "Real", and word pieces. Members detect "inner"/"internal". The circuit is a poor fit, and the peaks are mixed.
result.label: " inner" token with scattered pieces

result.description: Fires on the piece 'are' inside the name "Pareto" (P-are-to), after the 'P'. It stays silent on 'are' in "welfare" or when 'are' starts a word. Members include detectors for 'are' after P and similar name fragments.
result.label: 'are' inside Pareto

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in a possessive 's after a noun (cuisine's, chef's, glacier's), where a possessed noun follows. Silent on contraction apostrophes such as it's, what's and don't.
result.label: Possessive apostrophe after noun

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments of longer split words, mainly 'alg' in "amalgamation" and 'mit' in "mitochondrial"/"mitigation", also 'Alg' in "Algorithms". It sits at an incomplete word piece where a continuation is expected.
result.label: Split-word fragments alg/mit

result.description: Fires mostly on " defect" in materials-science text (point defect, line defect, lattice defect), with weaker activity on function words like "the" and "of" in technical math or science instructions. Members are mainly defect/fault detectors.
result.label: defect in technical science text

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens in historical or origin-themed text, mainly ' back' in "traced back", plus ' Middle' (Ages), ' Iron' (Age) and word pieces. It is silent on "falling back" (non-historical). Members detect ancient-history and origin words.
result.label: Historical origin "traced back" words

result.description: Fires on the adjectives " simple" and " straightforward", strongest in "not as simple as" and "a simple task" constructions. It stays silent on "from simple mechanisms", where "simple" follows "from".
result.label: "simple"/"straightforward" after "as"

result.description: Fires on the token " active" / " Active", mostly in the grammar sense (active vs passive voice) or in terms like active listening and active systems. Silent on some " active" contexts, e.g. at the start of "active voice" or after "an".
result.label: ' active' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' organ' when it begins "organize/organise" in the sense of arranging or structuring (data, concepts, music). It stays silent in "organism", and the logits favor non-biological continuations.
result.label: ' organ' in organize (arranging)

result.description: Fires mainly on the piece 'ac' inside words like "fast-paced" (also in polysaccharides), and more weakly on ' period' and ' era'. Members are mostly 'ac' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: 'ac' in "fast-paced"

result.description: Fires on plural or suffix word endings (-ets, -s, -ements, -ics) completing a topic heading in outline-style lists of short titles, e.g. "Labor Markets", "Pronouns". Silent on the same suffix in running prose or other headings.
result.label: Plural endings in outline headings

result.description: Fires on a word-initial fragment (mostly ' d', also 'p' in 'fast-paced', 'rac', ' condu') that starts a longer word split across tokens, such as 'ethical d|ilemma'. Mostly in academic or abstract text; the next piece is predicted to complete the word.
result.label: Word-start fragment ' d' before continuation

result.description: Fires on ' if' (also ' though') right after 'as' in the "as if / as though" comparison construction, introducing a hypothetical scenario. It stays silent on conditional 'if' such as "for example, if" or "sure if".
result.label: "as if" comparison clause

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' aer' when it begins a word like aerodynamic or aerodrome, mid-sentence. It is silent when 'aer' is the first token of the document. Weak activity appears on other word-initial fragments.
result.label: ' aer' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on " needed" in inline wiki-style editorial tags like "[citation needed]", "[clarification needed]", "[note needed]". It also weakly fires on similar words such as "necessary" or "required" after a noun.
result.label: " needed" in citation-needed tags

result.description: Fires on ' is' when it has no real subject before it: sentence-initial, after a colon or comma, or in a question ("Why is", "Or is"). The subject appears to have been dropped. It stays quiet on ' is' after an ordinary explicit subject.
result.label: ' is' lacking a subject

result.description: Fires on the 'ff' piece inside the split word "graffiti" (gra|ff|iti). It needs that word-internal position; members detect 'ff' and similar mid-word fragments.
result.label: 'ff' inside "graffiti"

result.description: Fires on 'and' (or comma) right after the noun "health" in a list of concerns, e.g. "human health and the environment". Silent on 'and' in other lists such as pollutants or practices.
result.label: 'and' after "health" in lists

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces (' plot', ' character', ' lab', ' met', ' inn') in essays about fiction, storytelling and narrative craft, often at word starts. Members are mostly narrative/reader/character topic detectors, so the peaks are mixed.
result.label: Narrative-craft essay word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word " relative", most strongly in grammar text about relative pronouns and clauses, and more weakly in "relative to" comparisons. Members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' relative' token (relative pronoun/clause)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' emot' (start of emotion/emotional) in essay-like text, usually after a verb or preposition such as "convey", "expression of", "insight into". It stays quiet in some contexts, such as at the start of a text or after "and".
result.label: ' emot' word piece

result.description: Fires on superlative or ordinal words like " earliest" and " oldest" right after "the" or "one of the", before a noun such as "recorded" or "known". It stays silent when "earliest" starts the text with no preceding "the".
result.label: "the earliest/oldest" superlatives

result.description: Fires on focusing adverbs such as "particularly", "specifically", "especially" and "particular(ly)", mostly after a comma or semicolon introducing a narrowing qualification in academic text. Silent when "particularly" is a plain intensifier in "being particularly crucial".
result.label: Focusing adverbs: particularly, specifically

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces completing durability/lifetime-type nouns: "lifes-pan", "longe-vity", also "tre-asure". Appears in engineering/product-durability text about extending lifespan or longevity of components.
result.label: lifespan/longevity word endings

result.description: Fires on the past-tense suffix 'ed' (also 'ased') of reporting verbs like "highlighted", "showcased", "underscored", where a clause about a finding or need follows. It stays silent on 'ed' in other verbs such as "challenged" or "ushered".
result.label: Past-tense 'highlighted'-type verb ending

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'and', 'vs', 'versus', word pieces) inside lists or contrasts of items, such as "such as crisp versus creamy" or "creamy, crunchy". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: List and contrast separators

result.description: Fires on ' magic' used figuratively, mostly after "like a", "a form of", "a kind of", as a metaphor (magic trick). Silent when 'magic' starts a document with no preceding context.
result.label: Figurative ' magic' mid-sentence

result.description: Fires on the word piece " discover" when it is a stem expecting a suffix like -ing, -ies, -ed (e.g. "like discovering"). Silent when " discover" begins "discoveries". Members detect discover/cover/discovery word-family pieces.
result.label: ' discover' stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on ' not' in "whether or not", and on "neither/either" in correlative pairs (neither...nor, either...or). Silent on ' not' in "not just", "or not" at clause end, or "but not".
result.label: Correlative 'whether or not' / neither

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' der' when it starts a split word, mainly 'deregulation' (also 'derailing'). It is silent when ' der' begins 'deregulatory' at the start of the text. Members detect ' der' and similar word-start fragments.
result.label: ' der' piece in 'deregulation'
'ot' in homotopy
result.description: Fires on the piece 'ot' inside 'hom-ot-opy' (homotopy), in topology text. It stays silent on 'ot' in other words such as 'knot'. Members detect 'ot' after a word-start fragment like 'hom', 'gen' or 'totip'.

Fires on verbs of causing or igniting, mainly ' spark' (sparked ideological...), also ' fuel', 'spurred', ' entertain', ' prompt', when a subject sets off a development. Members detect spark/trigger/ignite words and their suffixes.
result.label: spark / fuel / spur causation verbs

result.description: Fires on the end of technology or field words (' technology', 'ologies', 'ology', 'ure', 'science') when they end a noun phrase, e.g. "water treatment technologies", "renewable energy technology". It stays silent on 'technology' after "of" or "or".
result.label: Technology/-ology noun phrase endings

result.description: Fires on ' shift', ' Success' (at the start of "Successful/Successive"), ' transition' and similar change words. It stays silent on ' shift' after "paradigm", "important" or "technological", and fires when the word starts a sentence or clause.
result.label: shift / Success / transition word starts

result.description: Fires on ' without' when it follows a completed clause or action and introduces a "without doing X" modifier (e.g. "express feelings without defending"). It stays silent when 'without' follows 'because', 'but' or 'not'.
result.label: ' without' after a completed clause

result.description: Fires on ' foundation' (also 'rock' in bedrock, ' basis') when used figuratively as the base something rests on, as in "form the foundation of". Members are detectors of foundation/basis words.
result.label: Figurative 'foundation' as basis

result.description: Fires on the digits '0' or '1' inside ISO standard numbers (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001, 25010), i.e. the later digits of the code. It stays silent on '0' in years and decades such as 1970s or 20th.
result.label: Digits inside ISO standard numbers

result.description: Fires on ' on' used as a locative/location preposition after a noun or passive verb (displayed on a screen, tasks on their own, devices on the network). Silent on ' on' after verbs like rely/depend/work or meaning "about".
result.label: ' on' as locative preposition

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ty" completing the word "loyalty", mainly in customer-loyalty and marketing text. Members detect "ty" after "loyal" and related customer-relationship words.
result.label: "ty" ending "loyalty"

result.description: Fires on the word ' vast' itself, mostly as a quantity adjective before nouns like amounts, volumes or datasets (e.g. "analyze vast amounts of data"). Members are mostly detectors of ' vast' and similar words such as large or enormous.
result.label: ' vast' quantity adjective

result.description: Fires on the second piece of labor/work compounds: "market" after labor/labour, "place" or "force" after work. Silent on "market" in other contexts such as "fair market" or "the market's". Needs a labor/work-themed preceding word.
result.label: labor market / workforce compound

result.description: Fires on the "ence" ending of "essence" (also "essentially") in the sentence-opening phrase "In essence," meaning "basically". It stays silent on "essence" as a noun, as in "the essence of culinary...", and on "opulence".
result.label: "In essence" summarizing phrase

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' rig' when it starts "rigor" after an academic-field adjective (mathematical, linguistic, theoretical rigor), often in "X rigor and Y" phrases. It stays quiet on "rigorously" after a verb.
result.label: ' rig' in "academic rigor"

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces in heading-like multiword terms, mainly 'ain' in "Supply Chain" at the start of a document, and ' isol' in "isolation". Weaker on other word fragments. Peaks are scattered and fairly inconsistent.
result.label: Word fragments in title headings

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments in long, multi-piece words (uncon-vent-ional, double-bl-ind, Ass-ess-ment), where the word is incomplete and a suffix is expected. Logits are weak; the peaks are diverse word pieces.
result.label: Mid-word fragments in long words

result.description: Fires on ' the' and nouns like ' notes' or ' identity' after verbs like "enhances" or "adds to" in text about music, rhythm and melody. It is silent on ' the' after prepositions such as "to" or "from". Members are mostly music-word detectors.
result.label: Object noun slot in music text

result.description: Fires on the word pieces 'odes' and 'o' inside "geodesy" and "geoid" (after "ge"), in geodesy/surveying text. Members detect geodesy fragments like 'od', 'etic', 'odes'. Silent on general sea-level text.
result.label: Geodesy / geoid word-piece

result.description: Fires on verbs of adapting to or satisfying needs: the "ate" of "accommodate", and "meet"/"suit"/"to" in "tailored to meet/suit needs". Silent on other "-ate" verbs like collaborate, incorporate, automate.
result.label: accommodate / meet needs verbs

result.description: Fires on ' approach' (also 'ach', '-ology', ' perspective') when it follows a modifier naming a method or school, like "constructivist approach" or "Agile approach". It stays silent when 'approach' starts a sentence or follows a generic adjective like 'strategic' or 'holistic'.
result.label: Named-method 'approach' after modifier
' techn' before 'ologies' after noun
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' techn' / ' Techn' (start of "technologies") right after a noun modifier like "display", "sensing" or "voice recognition". It predicts "ologies". It is silent after "advanced" and at the start of a text.
Fires on the word piece "per" at the start of a word, mostly in "high-performance" (also periph-, permeable, angiosperm), predicting continuations like "formance". Weaker on " Energy" in headings.
result.label: "per" word piece, high-performance

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' impl' (as in "implants") when it begins a longer word, mostly in biomedical or engineering text. Members are detectors of other word-initial fragments (restaur, er, struct), which suggests it responds to an incomplete word-start.
result.label: ' impl' word-start fragment (implants)

result.description: Fires on "Tree"/"trees" when it ends a named data-structure or algorithm term, especially AVL trees, Red-Black trees, binary trees and decision trees. It is quiet on general computing text that doesn't name a tree type.
result.label: Tree in data-structure names

result.description: Fires on the word " physical" itself, mostly when it contrasts with virtual or digital things (physical hardware, presence, infrastructure, addresses). Members are mostly detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' physical' token detector

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside "Mesopotamia" and "Sumerians" ('am' in Mesopot-am-ia, 'umer' in S-umer-ians), in ancient Mesopotamia history text. Silent on garbled or misspelled variants of the word.
result.label: Mesopotamia/Sumerian word pieces

result.description: Fires on ' being' right after a plural or noun subject (e.g. "structures being developed", "methods being used"), where it works as a passive or participial verb. Silent on "Despite being" after a preposition.
result.label: ' being' after noun subject

result.description: Fires on the "aging" piece of "managing" (also weakly on " manage"), when it follows "man". Stays silent on "aging" in "leveraging" and "disengaging". It predicts objects such as resources or risk.
result.label: "aging" in "managing"

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ologies' completing 'technologies' (also ' tools', ' technology'), mostly after modifiers like "assistive" or "semantic". It stays silent on some 'technologies' and 'methodologies' contexts, and the contrast doesn't show why.
result.label: 'technologies' plural suffix 'ologies'

result.description: Fires on articles (' a', ' the', ' an', ' their') directly after a form of "play/played/playing", as in "play a role" or "playing the cards". Silent on ' a' in other constructions like "just a" or "has a".
result.label: Article after "play"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' del' in mid-sentence, mostly as the start of "delicate" after a determiner or verb. It is silent when "delicate" opens the text. Weaker on other ' del' words like "delved" and "delays".
result.label: ' del' start of "delicate"

result.description: Fires on 'j' inside "disjunction/conjunction"-type words and on ' World' in "World War"/"World of", i.e. word pieces where a specific continuation follows. Mixed, low-faithfulness circuit with two main token families.
result.label: 'j' in disjunct- and ' World' (War)

result.description: Fires on the word piece " lic" at the start of "licenses/licensing/licensed", in legal and music-rights text. Members include lic detectors plus rights, legal and copyright context features.
result.label: " lic" piece of license words

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' prefer' (as in "preferences") when it starts a word, plus ' termin' and ' Professor' at the start of a name line in a list of academics. Silent in one "user preferences" context, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' prefer' word-piece (preferences)

result.description: Fires on the first word piece of a longer word near the start of a document or sentence, often after "The" (aesthetic, seamless, captivating, long-term). It is silent on the same pieces mid-sentence, such as "seamlessly" or "ceramicists".
result.label: Word-initial piece after sentence-initial "The"

result.description: Fires on the hyphen directly after the prefix "non" (non-abelian, non-homogeneous, non-linear), in technical text. It stays silent on hyphens after other prefixes or words such as far-, over-, high-. Members detect "non" and the following hyphen.
result.label: Hyphen after "non" prefix

result.description: Fires on the verb or particle after "As we/you…" in essay-style openings, as in "As we move into", "As we embark on", "As we enter". It marks a transition verb after a "we" subject. It stays quiet on "and move beyond".
result.label: "As we move/embark on" transition verb

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Arab' when it begins a word like Arabic or Arabian, where a suffix such as 'ic' or 'ian' comes next. It is silent in one case where ' Arab' comes before 'ic and Heb…'.
result.label: ' Arab' word-start (Arabic/Arabian)
Copula after mathematical subject
result.description: Fires on ' is' / ' be' (also 'can be', 'are') right after a subject noun phrase in math-theorem style text, e.g. "every integer greater than one is", where a predicate comes next. Silent on many other 'is' tokens.

Fires on the token ' situ' in the Latin phrases "in situ" and "ex situ" (conservation, soil methods). Members are mostly ' situ' detectors plus word-piece detectors for incomplete words such as gravit-, organiz-, divers-.
result.label: ' situ' in in situ / ex situ
' isol' word-piece in isolation
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' isol' at the start of "isolation" or "isolate", mostly in biogeography and science text. It also fires weakly on a few other word-start fragments such as 'emp' and 'pre'.

Fires on the word piece " entrepr" (start of entrepreneur/entrepreneurship/entrepreneurial) when the rest of the word is still to come. It predicts continuation pieces like "ene". Weak firing on a few other split word starts.
result.label: ' entrepr' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the end of "fossil fuels" (mostly the "els" piece of "fu|els", also " fuel"), in environmental and energy text about fossil fuel dependence and renewables. Weak elsewhere.
result.label: fossil fuels "els" ending

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " recogn" (recognizes), especially when an abstract noun like theory, perspective or approach is the subject of "recognizes". It predicts suffix pieces like -izes/-izing.
result.label: " recogn" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the prefix " post" (post-colonial, post-structural, post-launch) when it is a hyphenated prefix meaning "after". It stays silent when " post" begins words like "postulate", where it is a word piece.
result.label: post- prefix meaning "after"

result.description: Fires on the final token of historical event names, mostly "formation" in "Reformation" and " Revolution", in history outlines about Protestant Reformation-era topics. Silent on art-criticism headings.
result.label: Reformation / Revolution historical event ends

result.description: Fires on ' them' as the pronoun object right after a verb like allow, enable, teach or provide (e.g. "allows them to"). It stays silent on ' them' as the start of "themes"/"thematic" and in other uses like "drawing them in".
result.label: ' them' after allow/enable verbs

result.description: Fires on consequence adverbs like "thus", "effectively", "thereby" that open a participle clause after a comma, describing a result of the preceding clause. Predicts a verb like "resulting", "leading", "creating".
result.label: Consequence adverb before participle

result.description: Fires mostly on commas (also 'more', 'eg') inside lists of abstract fields or topics, such as "philosophy, mathematics, astronomy" or "navigation, architecture, engineering". It stays silent on commas after "properties" that introduce a clause. The circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Commas in topic/field lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' fla' (flaws, flaunting, flaky, flawed) when it begins a longer word. It predicts continuations like 'ws' or 'iration'. The contrast shows it stays silent on the whole word 'weaknesses'.
result.label: ' fla' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments, mostly 'ene' inside longer words (bottlenecks, entrepreneurs, ethene, Hermeneutic), also 'alls' in firewalls. It is silent on 'ene' in the name René, so it needs the word-internal context.
result.label: Mid-word 'ene' piece (bottlenecks)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cult' when it begins 'cultures', typically after 'across', 'diverse', 'various' or 'other'. It predicts the 'ures' completion. Members are mostly detectors of ' cult' and 'Cultural'.
result.label: ' cult' in 'cultures'

result.description: Fires on the word " credit" in finance and banking text, especially before "risk", "rating" or "assessment" (e.g. "robust credit risk management"). It stays silent on interest-rate text without the word credit.
result.label: ' credit' in banking text

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of abstract nouns (techniques, methods, materials, practices), mid-list where more items follow. Silent on commas ending a list or clause, e.g. before "which" or "emphasizing".
result.label: Comma inside noun lists

result.description: Fires on the plural noun (methods, challenges, techniques, ologies) completing a coordinated list of abstract nouns like "strategies and methods" in generic educational or professional text, where more such nouns are expected. Silent on math "methods".
result.label: Plural noun ending "X and methods" lists

result.description: Fires on abstract plural nouns (practices, values, beliefs, interests, methods, skills) that are items in a comma-separated list of abstract concepts, usually in cultural or educational text. Silent when 'practices' follows a modifier or 'and'.
result.label: Plural abstract noun in list

result.description: Fires on ' with' that opens an absolute/elaborating clause after a comma (", with its molten…", ", with Spain and Portugal…"). Stays silent on ' with' as a verb or preposition complement (filled with, interacting with, along with).
result.label: Comma-introduced ' with' clause

result.description: Fires mainly on " tell"/" tells" (verb of telling a story) and on "Per" in "Future Perfect"/"Present Perfect" grammar headings. Members detect tell/telling and similar verbs (perform, play, sing). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: tell/tells and "Per" in Perfect

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' de' when it begins a longer English word, especially "degradation" in polymer text. It predicts continuations like 'grad' or 'compose'. It stays silent on 'Thermodynamics deals' (where ' de' starts "deals").
result.label: ' de' prefix before 'grad' words

result.description: Fires on the word " such" right after a plural noun, where "such as" or "such that" would follow. It stays quiet on " such" used as a determiner before a noun, as in "causes such compounds" and "by such men".
result.label: ' such' after a noun

result.description: Fires on 'ar' (also 'ur', 'yc', 'itar') as a mid-word fragment inside rare names and transliterated titles, such as Jawaharlal, Kiparsky, Mukhtasar. Silent on 'ar' in Nagarjuna, so it needs particular word contexts.
result.label: 'ar' fragment inside rare names

result.description: Fires on ' for' right after the noun "need" (also "necessity"), as in "the need for X". Stays silent on ' for' after other nouns like "framework for", "used for", or "measures for".
result.label: ' for' after "need"

result.description: Fires mostly on the word-start piece ' ling' (as in "lingua franca"), and weakly on ' a' or ' mental'. Members detect incomplete word fragments (ling, rib, Ide, pie, ple) where a longer word continues.
result.label: ling- word-fragment (lingua franca)
' po' in "poised"
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' po' after "is/are" when it begins "poised to" (e.g. "AI is poised to"). Members detect ' po' pieces generally, and the target is weakly active on "paramount".
Fires on the piece 'm' in the middle of a longer word where more letters follow, such as Prag|m|atic, Dile|m|ma, Car|m|ichael, enig|m|atic. It stays quiet on 'm' ending words like realm and palm.
result.label: Mid-word 'm' piece (Pragmatic, Dilemma)

result.description: Fires on verbs and nouns of calculating (calculate, calculating, compute, "calculation of") in math or science text, where a quantity is about to be named as the object. Predicts quantity-like nouns.
result.label: calculate/compute verbs before quantities

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' assess' (as in assessment), strongest after 'risk' or other risk/analysis terms. It is a first piece that is usually followed by '-ment'. Earlier members detect 'assess', 'risk' and '-ment' words.
result.label: ' assess' in risk assessment
' convergence' token detector
result.description: Fires on the word ' convergence' (rarely 'gence'), mostly in mathematical text about sequences, series and limits. Members are mainly upstream detectors of convergence/convergent, plus some math-context latents.

Fires on mid-word fragments, mostly 'alla' in "fallacies", also 'ur' in "heuristics" and 'Econom'. It needs the piece inside a longer word that is still being spelled out; the standalone 'alla' in "allachievements" stays silent.
result.label: 'alla' in fallacies word-piece

result.description: Fires on the noun ' point' or ' moment(s)' right after an adjective like turning, pivotal or defining, meaning a significant historical juncture. Silent on other uses of 'point', such as 'at the point' or 'comparison point'.
result.label: Turning point / pivotal moment

result.description: Fires mainly on the mid-word piece 'u' in "Altruism" (also 'in' pieces like webinars, ponin). Silent on 'u' in "linguistic". Members are mostly 'u' and 'in' token detectors. Weak, mixed circuit.
result.label: 'u' in Altruism word piece

result.description: Fires on the word " entropy" (and pieces like "vern", "ropy") in physics and information-theory text. Members are mostly entropy detectors plus related physics terms such as velocity, momentum and eigenvalues. Silent in a thermodynamics sentence that lacks the word.
result.label: entropy word detector

result.description: Fires on the word "application" (also "Application"), mostly as a noun meaning putting something into use, as in "implementation and application of...". Members are mostly detectors of this token.
result.label: Token "application"

result.description: Fires on the verb ending of "exposes", "reveals" and similar (poses, als, shows) when a subject like a study or examination is the agent and an object that is revealed comes next. Weaker on "showing" and "see".
result.label: Reveals/exposes verb endings

result.description: Fires on the comparative suffix "er" in "cooler" (also "der", "mer") in climate/temperature text, where a "than" or comparison may follow. It stays silent on "er" in other words such as "riser" or "nearer", and weakly on "darker".
result.label: Comparative "cooler" suffix in climate text

result.description: Fires on the word " red" (also "Red"), as in red-black trees, red flag, redshift. It seems to fire when "red" is a word or a prefix piece that may continue into a compound. It fires on every shown example of the token.
result.label: " red" token detector

result.description: Fires on the 'break' piece in 'outbreak' (e.g. disease outbreaks), after 'out'. Silent on related health text without the word. Upstream members detect 'break' after 'out' and disease context.
result.label: 'break' in 'outbreak'

result.description: Fires on the 'ut' piece in "pharmaceutical" (and biopharmaceutical), with weaker firing on ' phr' in "noun phrases". Silent on 'ut' in "pollutant" and "therapeutic".
result.label: 'ut' in pharmaceutical

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Saf" (as in Safety) in capitalized title-like phrases such as "Food Safety Training" or "Safety Engineering". It needs the piece to begin a word that continues; weakly fires on other word-start fragments.
result.label: Saf- word-start in Safety

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Gott' at the start of "Gottfried" (Leibniz's first name), in lists of mathematicians and scientists. Members detect first-name or surname-start pieces of historical figures such as Bern-, Bol-, Pic-, Isaac.
result.label: ' Gott' in Gottfried Leibniz

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after "of" in phrases about a project or process lifecycle or phases (e.g. "all phases of the project", "beginning of the planning process"). Silent on ' the' after other "of" or verb contexts.
result.label: 'the' after 'of' in lifecycle phases

result.description: Fires on ' such' right after a comma that follows a plural noun phrase, introducing examples ("X, such as ..."). It stays quiet when ' such' follows the noun with no comma.
result.label: ", such as" after comma

result.description: Fires on ' Roman' (also ' Rom', ' Gree(k)', 'ol' in Mongol) as an ancient civilization or empire adjective in history text, e.g. "the Roman Empire". Members are mostly Roman detectors.
result.label: Roman/Greek ancient civilization adjective

result.description: Fires on " and" joining two nouns in a short title-like pair right after a capitalized heading word at document or line start (e.g. "Education and democracy", "Food and Religion"). Weaker on list-final "and"; silent on mid-sentence "and".
result.label: "and" in "X and Y" title pairs

result.description: Fires on creation/enrichment verbs (' create', 'enrich', 'enhance') right after "can" with a professional subject like teachers, educators or chefs, in education/practice-advice text. It stays quiet on 'create' after "to" or in other constructions.
result.label: "can create" after educators/professionals

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' check' when it begins a compound and is followed by a suffix, such as check-ins, checkpoint, checksum. Upstream members are mostly ' check' detectors that push towards point, points, ers and list.
result.label: ' check' as compound-word start

result.description: Fires on contrastive conjunctions, mainly ' while' and ' whereas', often after a semicolon or at the start of a sentence, introducing a contrasting clause. It stays silent on some ' while' cases, such as after commas or where 'while' means 'during'.
result.label: Contrastive 'while' / 'whereas' conjunction

result.description: Fires on the final word piece of a food or ingredient word (gar-lic, bar-ley, on-ions) inside comma-separated lists of foods and cooking ingredients. It stays quiet on non-food text.
result.label: Ingredient word endings in food lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, often word-start or mid-word pieces (product, port, u, its, etic) where a word is being continued or completed. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same token ' its' is silent in other contexts. Evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered word-piece continuation, unclear

result.description: Fires on the caret '^' in LaTeX exponents and on long runs of dashes (markdown horizontal rules after a paragraph). Members detect LaTeX backslash/comma symbols and math notation. Mixed, low-faithfulness circuit.
result.label: Caret and dash-rule symbols

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ized' in "characterized" (as in "characterized by"), mostly in historical or art-period descriptions. It stays silent on 'ized' in other words such as "organized" or "harmonized".
result.label: 'ized' in "characterized by"

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "or" and "/" that join items in a list of abstract nouns (ideas, concepts, and entities; words, phrases, sentences, and texts). It is silent on commas in other roles, such as after introductory phrases.
result.label: List separators between abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece (' ref', ' adv', ' expl', ' comp') right after "further", where a suffix like -inement or -ancement is expected. Silent on ' ref' after "the" or "and".
result.label: Word piece after "further"

result.description: Fires on the word ' against' as a preposition after a noun or verb of opposition, defense or comparison (defense against, wars against, protect against, performance against). Predicts threat or target words like enemy, potential, certain.
result.label: ' against' after opposition/defense words

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'lex' in "reflexive/reflexively" and similar words (e.g. "flexibility"), a mid-word fragment. Many members are detectors of 'lex' itself, plus grammar-terminology context. The next-token push is toward suffixes like 'aneous'.
result.label: 'lex' piece in reflexive

result.description: Fires on "meat" (also "chicken" pieces like "icken", "ats") in cooking and food-preparation text, such as poaching, grilling, sautéing or cured meats. Members detect meat, food and cooking terms.
result.label: meat in cooking contexts

result.description: Fires on the word piece "onic", most strongly in "Harm|onic" (harmonic analysis/motion), and also in similar pieces like homoph|onic. Weak activation on "kin|etic". Upstream members are mostly "onic" detectors plus music/instrument topic.
result.label: "onic" in "Harmonic"

result.description: Fires on ' Eastern' and ' Western' (weaker on East/directions) used as geopolitical or regional modifiers, such as Eastern Europe, Western bloc, Eastern Front. Predicts Europe/European/Roman next. Silent on Cold War text lacking these words.
result.label: Eastern/Western regional modifier

result.description: Fires on ' variables' (mostly after "independent/dependent") and on word endings like "ality" in "causality", in statistics/econometrics text. Members detect variable(s) tokens and statistical terms.
result.label: Statistical 'variables' in econometrics text

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments (reg, g, co, ant, rot, hyphen) in scientific, mostly molecular biology text, where a longer technical word is being continued. Predicts biology-style word continuations like -ibberellin or -operative. Silent on one 'reg' in 'regulation' contrast.
result.label: Biology word-fragment prefixes

result.description: Fires on separators (comma, hyphen, "to", "and") right after a number inside numeric lists or ranges, such as "0, 1," or "1.6-2.0-1.7", predicting another number next. Silent on ordinary prose commas.
result.label: Separator after number in lists/ranges

result.description: Fires on "menu" / "Menu" and "restaurant" tokens, strongest on "Menu" as a heading at the start of a document or section in restaurant/culinary text. It was silent on one "menu" in a non-food context.
result.label: Menu / restaurant word in food context

result.description: Fires on ' on' in "depending on" (also "depended on"), where it introduces the factor something varies with. Stays silent on ' on' as a locative or other preposition, like "on stage" or "based on".
result.label: "depending on" – on

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces of technical or academic terms like ' Nav' (Navier-Stokes), ' Orth' (Orthographic), 'ier', 'rod'. Mostly early fragments of a multi-piece word where a technical continuation is expected, in math/physics/linguistics text.
result.label: Technical term opening fragments (Nav, Orth)

result.description: Fires on ' beyond' as a verb-complement after "go/goes/extends" (X goes beyond mere/just...). It is silent on "and beyond" as a noun-phrase tail. It predicts "simple/mere/just/simply".
result.label: "goes beyond" before mere/just

result.description: Fires on function or linking words (and, their, supports, food) in environmental and conservation text about species, habitats and ecosystems. It predicts a next noun like habitat, fish, species or conservation.
result.label: Ecology text, predicts habitat/species noun

result.description: Fires on the word "entropy" (and its piece "ropy" in "Entropy") in physics and information-theory text. It is silent on a Second Law of Thermodynamics sentence where the word does not appear. A few weak firings on unrelated word pieces.
result.label: Entropy word detector

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' res' when it begins a longer word such as reservoir, reserves, resilience or resin. Members are mostly ' res' detectors. Predicts continuations like 'erves', 'ili', 'embl'.
result.label: ' res' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ound' piece in "profound", and less on word pieces like 'elev' (elevates) and 'cultiv' (cultivating), in formal academic prose. The next word is likely an abstract noun such as role, depth or implications.
result.label: profound / elevate / cultivate word pieces
'um' ending "vacuum"
result.description: Fires on the piece 'um' completing the word "vacuum" (physics text). It stays silent on 'um' in "quantum" and "aluminum", and is only weakly active on "gravitational".

Fires on the word " role" (or " roles"), mostly in phrases like "play a crucial role" or "their role in". Many upstream members are themselves detectors of the same token. The one contrast example doesn't contain the token.
result.label: Token ' role' / ' roles'

result.description: Fires on uppercase word fragments like EN, O, DO, SO in the middle of all-caps strings, including gibberish or chemical-like caps text. Quiet on normal lowercase prose.
result.label: Uppercase mid-word fragments (EN, O)

result.description: Fires on the word piece " concentr" (start of concentration/concentrated), mostly in science text about substances or gases, predicting the suffix "ations". Weak on a few other nouns like resolution or capacity.
result.label: ' concentr' word piece before -ations

result.description: Fires on words following stretching/holding instructions (repeatedly, upwards, and, -ed, tightly) in how-to text about stretching dough, hands or material; predicts body parts like legs, feet, fingers. Silent on ' in' in other contexts.
result.label: Stretching-instruction continuation words

result.description: Fires on the 'g' in "e.g." when it introduces examples in a list of types or categories, often followed by a comma. Also fires weakly on ' caus' and some word-piece 'g' tokens.
result.label: 'g' in "e.g." examples

result.description: Fires on 's, a following quote, 'and', or suffix pieces right after a philosopher's name (Plato's, Platon'S "The Republic", Chomskyian) in philosophy text. It stays silent on 's in "it's" or after Aristotle in other contexts.
result.label: Possessive after philosopher names

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments (' du', ' hall', ' orn', ' cup') that begin a longer word split across tokens, e.g. du|ality, hall|mark, orn|amentation, in technical or academic prose. Logits favor completion pieces like 'ality'.
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments (du, hall)

result.description: Fires on ' that' as a complementizer introducing a clause after a verb of saying, showing or indicating (clarifies that, indicates that, suggesting that). Silent on relative-pronoun ' that' after nouns.
result.label: Complementizer 'that' after reporting verbs

result.description: Fires on ' when' right after a noun or verb like "occur", "arise", or "takes place" that introduces a condition clause (e.g. "errors occur when", "hazards arise when"). It stays silent on "even when" and on "when presented with".
result.label: 'when' after occur/arise

result.description: Fires on a word stem that is incomplete and about to take the suffix "-ation" (carbon fix|ation, relax|ation, valu|ation, appreci|ation). Predicts suffix continuations like "ence", "ative".
result.label: Stem awaiting -ation suffix

result.description: Fires mainly on the suffix 'ological' after linguistic stems like phon- or morph- in linguistics text, with weaker hits on other tokens. It stays silent on 'ological' in biological text.
result.label: linguistics 'ological' suffix (phonological)

result.description: Fires on the word " partial", mostly in "partial differential equations / partial derivatives" in math text. It also fires weakly on a few odd tokens such as "ogeneous". Members are mostly detectors of "partial" and similar modifiers.
result.label: ' partial' in math terms

result.description: Fires on the word " mass" / " Mass", most strongly in "critical mass" and other physics-style noun uses. It stays silent in one example, "how mass distribution", so context matters. Many members are mass-token detectors.
result.label: Physics "mass" after critical

result.description: Fires on the word " purpose" (also weakly on near-synonyms like "intention"), predicting suffixes such as -ful, -fully, -ally. Members are mostly detectors of purpose, intent, meaning and reason words.
result.label: ' purpose' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ulative" completing "cum-ulative", mostly in CDF/probability text. It needs the "cum" prefix; the contrast "accumulation" doesn't trigger it. Rare weak hits on other word pieces.
result.label: "ulative" in "cumulative"

result.description: Fires on the token ' sources' (plural noun), across contexts like primary sources, various sources, types of sources. Members are mostly detectors of ' sources' or ' source' at earlier layers.
result.label: ' sources' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word-start pieces " hom" and " heter" (homogeneous, homologues, homonyms, heterogeneous), with some weaker firing on "ity" in words like relativity. Members are mostly " hom" detectors.
result.label: hom- / heter- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the modal ' can' (occasionally ' may') when it follows an abstract or sentence-initial subject, often right after a full stop with the subject missing, and is followed by 'be'. It stays quiet on 'they can' and 'words can'.
result.label: Modal ' can' after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative pronoun " those" (also " ones") used as a stand-in for people or things, typically before a relative clause ("for those who", "including those that"). Predicts "who"/"interested"-style continuations.
result.label: "those" before relative clause

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece ' lif' (as in lifespan, lifecycle, lifeworld) when it begins a compound after "the"; also weakly on other word-initial fragments like ' moder' and ' Mac'. Members are mostly ' lif' detectors.
result.label: ' lif' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the verb ' help' (or 'helps') right after a subject such as 'can', a noun or 'that', where a bare verb comes next (reduce, maintain, understand). Logits favour verbs like reduce, remove, maintain.
result.label: verb 'help' before an infinitive

result.description: Fires on the prefix token " un" (or " Un") when it starts a word after a preceding noun or word, mainly in academic text, as in "unravels", "unlocks", "Unified". It is silent when " un" begins the text.
result.label: Prefix " un" mid-sentence

result.description: Fires on the verbs "begins" and "starts" (also began, begin) when a subject noun such as a process, journey or stage is said to start, typically before "with" or "at". Weaker on "began" and "Beginning".
result.label: Process "begins/starts" verb

result.description: Fires on the '0' in the second year of a year range like 2000-2001 or 2007-2009, where the '0' follows '2' after a hyphen. It stays silent on '0' in decade forms like 1980s or 1990s.
result.label: Zero in second year of range

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' phot' (start of "photography") after food or culinary words, as in "food photography". It stays silent on "dealing with photography" in a non-food context. Predicts "ography" continuations.
result.label: phot- in food photography

result.description: Fires on the word " layer" / " layers", most strongly in technical lists such as network or neural-network layers (input layer, transport layer). Also fires more weakly on figurative or physical layers. Members are mostly layer-token detectors.
result.label: Word "layer(s)"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ue' (or 'ues') right after a 'c' in a split-up word like "cue", as in "c|ue". It stays silent on 'ue' at the end of "dialogue".
result.label: 'ue' after c (cue)

result.description: Fires on the "ights" piece of "insights" after "valuable/offer/provide", as in "provide valuable insights into". It stays silent on some academic or linguistics "insights" contexts, so it seems to need that offering-insight phrasing.
result.label: "insights" after valuable/provide

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ing' completing the word "breathing" (breath + ing). It stays silent on 'ing' in other words like maintaining or moving. It pushes toward words like room, life, new, exercise.
result.label: 'ing' ending "breathing"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' meteor' (start of meteorology/meteorological/meteorologist), predicting an "-ological/-ology" continuation. Supported by weather, climate, rain and precipitation detectors in the circuit.
result.label: ' meteor' before -ology

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' gl' when it begins a word like gluten, glutenin or gluon, mid-sentence. It is silent when 'gl' starts the text or a hyphenated 'gluten-free'. Logits favour continuations like 'uten'.
result.label: ' gl' start of gluten/gluon

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'ist' in "pr-ist-ine" (and similar word fragments like 'tt', 'cut'), where the word is still incomplete. It stays silent on 'ist' as a suffix meaning a person or movement (Cubist, Expressionist).
result.label: 'ist' inside 'pristine'

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a phrase after "across" (mostly "borders", also sectors, channels, cultures, genres, boundaries), as in "across borders and regions". It needs the "across X" construction, and is silent on other text.
result.label: Noun after "across" (borders)

result.description: Fires right after "word"/term in etymology statements ("comes from the Greek word for", "word 'x'", "means"), where a gloss or quoted translation comes next. Silent on ordinary "for" uses.
result.label: Etymology gloss slot after "word"

result.description: Fires on ' also' right after a subject, especially "it also" following a "more than just X;" clause, where a verb like involves, serves or means comes next. Silent on "but also" and "is also" after a noun subject.
result.label: "it also" after "more than just" clause

result.description: Fires on the word " background" (cultural/diverse backgrounds, personal background, also background noise or radiation). Members are mostly detectors of " background" itself; the contrast is a passage on diversity without the word.
result.label: word ' background'

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'omed' in "Biomedical" when the word is split into Bi + omed, mostly in repeated title lists like "Biomedical Sensors / Data Analysis". It mostly matches the sub-token 'omed' itself.
result.label: 'omed' in Bi-omed-ical

result.description: Fires on the token " compression" in data/image/audio compression text (lossless, lossy, wavelet compression). Upstream members are mostly compression detectors plus signal-processing words like filtering, noise and formats.
result.label: ' compression' in signal processing

result.description: Fires on a hyphen or en dash joining a compound modifier, mostly after adjectives like "large", "small", "larger" where a scale/type/class word is expected. Silent on hyphens after "one", "self", "problem", "cost".
result.label: Hyphen in size-adjective compounds

result.description: Fires on "Urban"/"urban" (and "rural"), especially as a capitalized heading word at the start of a document or section, and in urban planning or development text. It pushes toward suffixes like "-ization", "sprawl" and "development".
result.label: Urban / rural word detector

result.description: Fires on the word " transfer" (also "Transfer", "transferred"), mostly as a noun after a modifier such as electron, genetic, or momentum. Predicts suffixes like "ring". Members are mostly detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' transfer' token detector

result.description: Fires on the verb-ending 's' in "aligns" (third-person singular), right where "with" is expected next. It stays silent on possessive 's and plural 's.
result.label: "aligns" verb ending predicting "with"

result.description: Fires on ' different' (also ' various', ' all') right after "across", "among", "between" when describing variation over a set of settings, areas or types. It stays silent after "due to", "using" or "offer".
result.label: 'different' after across/among

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece " Ge" (as in Geoid, Geodesy, Geomorphic) at the start of a heading or topic-list item in earth-science text. It stays silent on other topic headings, such as biology fields.
result.label: Ge- at start of geoscience term

result.description: Fires on plural suffix pieces (-ys, -ges, -els, -ches, -es) ending split nouns in lists of landforms, terrain and structures (tunnels, ridges, lanes, cliffs, islets). Needs a geography or landscape listing context; silent on 'analyses'.
result.label: Plural endings in landform lists

result.description: Fires on an incomplete word-stem piece, mostly ' preced' (preceded/precedes) and ' wis' (wisely), where a suffix like -ed, -es or -ely is expected next. Members detect similar mid-word stems such as poll-, Tim-, lic-.
result.label: Word stem awaiting suffix (preced-)

result.description: Fires on the verb-ending "s" in "affects" (also weakly "highlights"), after a subject like "water" or "clutter", where a direct object comes next. Silent on plural or possessive "s".
result.label: verb "affects" third-person s

result.description: Fires on prefix word pieces like ' anti', ' self', ' counter', 'auto' that are expected to be followed by a hyphen or word completion (anti-establishment, self-awareness, counterparts). Predicts '-' next.
result.label: Anti/self/counter prefix before hyphen

result.description: Fires on a noun (cell, energy, repair, storage, transport) right after "essential for / regulating / support" in nutrition and biology text about lipids and vitamins. It predicts health-related nouns like membranes. Silent on "cell" in "cellular" or technical cell-biology text.
result.label: Biological function noun after "essential for"

result.description: Fires on the token " person" (mostly as a word stem, e.g. "personification", "person versus society", "first person"). Predicts suffix continuations like -ality, -ification, -hood. Members are mostly " person" detectors.
result.label: ' person' token stem detector

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ili' in "resilience" (after "res"), predicting 'ence'. Weakly fires on 'h' in "reshaped". Members detect the "res" + middle-piece pattern (ili, il, er) in resilient/reservoir words.
result.label: 'ili' in res-ili-ence

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' challeng' (challenges) and ' obst' (obstacles), when a noun about difficulties is being formed. It predicts the ending pieces 'acles', 'es' and similar.
result.label: challenge / obstacle word start

result.description: Fires on the word " stress" in every example, both mechanical (tensile, squeeze stress) and psychological/linguistic uses. Members are stress detectors plus related words like fatigue, load, anxiety, fear.
result.label: Word ' stress'

result.description: Fires on ' fields' (or ' field') right after "magnetic" or "electric" in physics text about electromagnetism. Silent on ' fields' meaning areas of study, as in "various fields" or "other fields".
result.label: Physical field after magnetic/electric

result.description: Fires on the word "instruction" (and the piece "ruction" in "Instruction"), mostly as a noun modifier in computer-architecture text such as instruction pipelining, fetch and execution. Stays silent on unrelated systems text.
result.label: "instruction" token detector
water token in hydrology text
result.description: Fires on the word "water" (including "water" as a suffix in rainwater/groundwater, and "Water"), mainly in environmental or hydrology passages about the water cycle, resources and management. Silent on unrelated environmental text without the word.

Fires on mid-word uppercase fragments (SE, CH, GE, AD, ES, AST) inside words written in all-caps text, such as ITSELF, PROMISE, ROASTER'S. Weakly on acronyms like FMEA and SAS. Predicts further capital letters continuing the word.
result.label: All-caps mid-word fragments

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' harm' / 'Harm' when it begins "harmony/harmonic" and the next piece is expected to be 'ony' or 'onic'. Silent when ' harm' appears at the very start of the text, as in "harmonic vocab…". Members are detectors of the same token.
result.label: harm- start of harmony/harmonic

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces inside long technical words, mostly biology/immunology terms like re-ceptor, TC(R), phosphol-ip-ase, hormones, though also 'sk' in skill. Predicts word-completion pieces. Mixed, moderate evidence.
result.label: Mid-word pieces in biology terms

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments 'iv' and 'uls' inside words like pulsar, pulses, pivotal, herbivores, after an initial 'p' or similar prefix. Predicts continuations like 'otal'. Also weakly on odd bytes.
result.label: 'iv'/'uls' word-piece in pulsar/pivotal

result.description: Fires on the word "functional" (and "al" in "Functional") in mathematical or programming contexts like functional analysis or functional programming. Weakly fires on "ome" in "biomechanics". Silent on the word "function(s)".
result.label: "functional" in technical fields

result.description: Fires on words right after a copula or auxiliary (is/are/was/has been) in descriptive statements about a concept's role, e.g. "is often cited", "are still used", "is integral", "is a cornerstone". Predicts a predicate adjective or adverb continuation.
result.label: Predicate position after copula

result.description: Fires on past-tense verbs "was"/"were" (also "underwent") right after an abstract historical or academic subject, like a movement, era, or field, where a description such as "marked by" or "influenced by" follows. Silent on "was" in some other constructions.
result.label: Was/were after historical subject

result.description: Fires on function words and adjectives like " in", " into", " powerful" inside advanced mathematics text (analysis, algebra, differential equations). It boosts next-token predictions of "mathematical/algebraic". Silent on " in" in chemistry text.
result.label: Math-context words predicting "mathematical"

result.description: Fires on adjective suffixes like -ical, -ological, -ist, -istic ending a philosophy-related word (philosophical, epistemological, materialist), anticipating a noun like inquiry, framework, or theories. Silent on -ical in non-philosophical words like critical or apolitical.
result.label: Philosophical adjective suffixes (-ical, -ist)

result.description: Fires on the verb " allow"/" allows" after a subject noun (technique, method, tool), as in "X allows for…" or "allows artists to…". It predicts " for" or a person object next. Members are mostly detectors of allow-words.
result.label: verb "allow(s)" after subject

result.description: Fires on policy-type nouns (Policy, policy, laws, statements) right after "Environmental" or similar environment/governance modifiers. Silent on "Environmental Engineering" in a list of fields, so it needs the policy/regulation noun in an environmental context.
result.label: Environmental policy noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece "uct" inside "fluctuations"/"fluctuating" (after "fl"), mostly in economic or currency text. Members are mostly detectors of this same piece.
result.label: "uct" in "fluctuations"

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ographic' mainly in "Biogeographic" headings at document start, with weaker firing on 'istic' and 'ography'. It stays silent on 'ographic' in "logographic", so it needs the bio-geo word context.
result.label: Biogeographic 'ographic' suffix

result.description: Fires on the particle (mostly ' up', also in/with/on) right after the verb "end" ("end up with/as/in"). Stays silent on ' up' after make, call, get or tidy. Members detect "end" pieces and ' up' tokens.
result.label: particle after "end" (end up)

result.description: Fires on the preposition ' for' (sometimes ' to') right after verbs of preparing or adapting, such as "prepare for", "prepared for", "adapting to". It stays silent on other uses of ' for', such as "for years" or "for instance".
result.label: preposition after prepare/adapt

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'oph' in the middle of words, mostly "hom-oph-" (homophone, homophony) and similar Greek-derived terms (Aerophones, esophagitis, eosinophilic). Predicts continuations like 'istic' or 'ones'.
result.label: 'oph' word piece in homophone

result.description: Fires on ' has' (and ' have') as a perfect-tense auxiliary after a subject noun, predicting a participle like "been", "continued" or "enabled". Silent on text without this auxiliary.
result.label: Perfect auxiliary 'has'/'have'

result.description: Fires on the relative pronoun ' that' right after a plural noun, strongest after "models" (new models that...). Predicts model-related continuations. Quieter after other nouns like changes or processes.
result.label: Relative 'that' after "models"

result.description: Fires on the word "commas" (comm|as, ' comma') when it appears in lists of punctuation marks or grammar and writing-style rules, such as "symbols such as commas, periods". Silent on lists of rhetorical devices.
result.label: comma in punctuation lists

result.description: Fires on the verb slot after "while also" (or "while"), on words like "also", "acknowled(ging)", "emphas(izing)", "serving", "maintain(ing)", where a second participle clause is being added. Silent on "also" in other positions.
result.label: Participle after "while also"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " scatter" as a stem, mostly in physics text on Rayleigh or Thomson scattering, including before suffixes like -ing and -er. Predicts continuations such as "ing" and "off".
result.label: ' scatter' word stem

result.description: Fires on ' language' right after "English" (e.g. "the English language"). It stays silent on ' language' in generic phrases like "study of language" or "our own language".
result.label: ' language' after English

result.description: Fires on the "actions"/"reaction" piece in "reactions", especially in redox or reduction/oxidation reaction text. It stays silent on some "reactions" in general chemistry contexts, so it seems to need the redox-style setting.
result.label: Redox "reactions" token

result.description: Fires on ' the' (also 'of', 'understand') after verbs like "map out", "insight into", "about" in linguistics/language-origins text, before an object noun such as network or migrations. Silent on many other ' the' in similar contexts.
result.label: 'the' after uncover/trace verbs, linguistics

result.description: Fires on plural domain nouns like " areas" or " fields" right after "in" (e.g. "applications in areas/fields"), where a "like/such as/where" list or clause typically follows. Silent in other contexts.
result.label: Domain nouns 'areas/fields' after 'in'

result.description: Fires on "acid" / "acids" (often the "ids" piece of "acids") in chemistry text, especially after names like carboxylic, hydrochloric or citric. Silent on unrelated text, so it seems to need a chemistry context.
result.label: acid(s) in chemistry text

result.description: Fires on the adverb " partly" (also " partially") when it modifies a following cause or attribution, as in "due partly to", "was partly caused by", "attributed partly or entirely". Members detect degree adverbs like mostly, largely and fully.
result.label: ' partly' degree adverb before attribution

result.description: Fires mostly on 'ega' in "omega" (e.g. omega-3), plus mid-word pieces like 'u' in "fluctuations", hyphens after prefixes such as anti-, and ' Dark' in "Dark Matter". It looks like a word-piece completion detector, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: 'ega' in omega, mid-word pieces

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a phrase like "the latest frontier", "a new area/era/field" (frontier, area, era, field), where something is described as a new or emerging domain, usually followed by "of" or "in".
result.label: New frontier/area/era noun

result.description: Fires on the period ending a short topic-title line in a list of headings or topics (e.g. "Education and the arts.", "Flutes."), before a newline and the next item. It is silent on some similar title periods, and the contrast doesn't show why.
result.label: Period after list-item topic titles

result.description: Fires on the word "integration" / "integral" (also "integr-" and "integrals"), mostly in calculus contexts such as limits of integration, integration by parts, line integrals. Weaker on non-math "integration of X".
result.label: integration / integral word

result.description: Fires on the article ' a'/' an' right after "possess" (leaders possess a unique set of...), predicting trait nouns like attributes, qualities, characteristics. Silent on ' a' after "is" or "offers". Members include possess detectors.
result.label: Article after "possess"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' vac' (as in vacuum, vacancies), predicting a continuation like 'u' or 'aneous'. Members detect similar word-start fragments such as hel, whe, pest, casting.
result.label: ' vac' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the token ' character' as a word stem, most strongly when it begins a verb or noun like characterize/characterization in scientific text. It pushes the next token towards suffixes such as -ization, -ized, -izing.
result.label: ' character' before -ize suffixes

result.description: Fires on the word piece " contradict" (contradictory, contradictions, contradicting) as a word-start before a suffix, predicting suffixes like 'ory', 'ant', 'ial'. Members mostly detect similar word stems such as contradict, conflic, exceed, complement.
result.label: " contradict" word stem

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ility' (also 'ibility') completing "versatility", strongest there; weaker on agility and flexibility. Silent on 'ility' in "desirability", so it needs the word versatility/flexibility-like stem.
result.label: 'versatility' suffix 'ility'

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' se' when it begins a longer word (seismic, seamless, seeds, sewage, sectors). It predicts continuations like 'ctors', 'am', 'cur'. It stays silent on other tokens such as 'scene'.
result.label: ' se' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word " derivative" (calculus or finance sense), occasionally on " fraction" or " transaction" in math/finance text. Members mostly detect " derivative(s)" at earlier layers.
result.label: " derivative" token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece "igue" completing "fatigue", mainly in engineering text about material or hull fatigue, crack growth and stress loading. Members include other "igue" detectors and stress/loading/foundation engineering features.
result.label: "igue" in "fatigue"

result.description: Fires on the first fragment of a word split into pieces (' pro', ' st', ' em', ' consult', ' cogn') right after a quantity-increase word like "greater" or "increased", predicting a suffix continuation such as -ation or -isation.
result.label: Word-start fragment after "greater/increased"

result.description: Fires on ' first' (also ' important', 'crucial', 'most') in a "The first/most important [step/thing]" ranking phrase, after "the" or "most". It stays silent on 'first' as an adverb ("by first discretizing") or sentence-initial.
result.label: "The first/most important" step phrase

result.description: Fires on a hyphen joining a noun-like first element to a following modifier, as in side-side-side, diameter-related, technology-driven. It stays quiet after right, two, in (right-angled, two-dimensional, in-depth). Predicts suffixes like level/based/related.
result.label: Hyphen in compound modifiers

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ographic' in words like Biogeographic, Orthographic and Demographic. It peaks most strongly on 'Bioge|ographic' in title-like headings. It is weaker on 'chromatographic' and 'cryptograph'.
result.label: 'ographic' suffix piece

result.description: Fires on ' with' as an instrumental or manner preposition after a noun or verb (wipe with gentle water, executed with great precision). It stays silent when 'with' follows 'start' or 'begins'. Logits favor words like care and precision.
result.label: ' with' as manner/instrument preposition

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces like ' May' (in Mayan/Mayans), ' Bo' (Boer), 'RE', ' AD' that are incomplete and need a suffix to finish the word. Predicts word continuations such as 'an', 'er'.
result.label: Incomplete word-start pieces (May-, Bo-)

result.description: Fires on the ordinal suffix 'th' after a century number (e.g. 16th, 18th), especially in century ranges like "16th-18th"; predicts "century". Silent in at least one plain "19th century" case, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Century ordinal suffix 'th'

result.description: Fires on the "ission" piece of "fission", mainly in nuclear physics text ("Nuclear fission"). It weakly fires on "lear" in "nuclear" and on "emission". Members detect nuclear-themed tokens and the "ission" piece.
result.label: Nuclear fission 'ission' piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sign' (signifier, signified, signage, sign language) when it is a stem that continues into a longer word or compound. It predicts suffixes such as -ified, -age and -ifier.
result.label: ' sign' as word stem

result.description: Fires on the word " story" as a noun, such as "a compelling story" or "superhero story". It is silent on "story" in "and story" or "and storytelling". Members are mostly story/tale detectors. Logits favor "line", "post" and "link".
result.label: noun ' story' after modifier

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' consum' (start of consumers/consumed), mostly after "how" or "that" in economics text. It pushes the next token towards 'ers'. Members are mostly ' consum' token detectors.
result.label: ' consum' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word " modern" (also "Modern"), most strongly after "for"/"of"/"in the" in history-of-ideas phrasing like "laid the groundwork for modern…". Members are mostly detectors of "modern".
result.label: Word "modern" after foundations phrasing

result.description: Fires on word pieces in the middle of a multi-token term, mainly ' agricult' after "precision" (precision agriculture/farming), also ' far', ' Vector', 'Opt'. Silent on ' agricult' after sustainable/urban or sentence-initially.
result.label: precision agriculture word-piece

result.description: Fires on the final piece of "standpoint"/"viewpoint" and on "perspective" in "from an X standpoint/perspective" phrases. It marks the point-of-view noun and weakly fires on similar phrases like "at first glance" and "in simplest terms".
result.label: standpoint / viewpoint / perspective noun

result.description: Fires on the token ' Google', especially in lists of tech companies or cloud services (e.g. "Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform"). Members include Google and Oracle detectors. Mostly a token detector; weak firing on a few unrelated tokens.
result.label: ' Google' token in tech lists

result.description: Fires on word-ending suffix pieces (-ining in dining, -ity in hospitality, -ment in entertainment) in hospitality, restaurant and food contexts. It predicts industry or experience-type continuations.
result.label: Hospitality/dining word suffixes

result.description: Fires on the word piece "pect" inside "perspectives" (pers|pect|ives), and also on "pect" in "Respect". Members are mostly "pect" detectors. It predicts a continuation like "ives".
result.label: "pect" piece in perspectives

result.description: Fires on " traffic" (rarely other flow-like nouns such as water) after simulate/analyze/predict-type verbs, where a flow or behavior word comes next. It stays quiet on computer "network traffic".
result.label: Road traffic before flow/behavior
'uro' in neuro- words
result.description: Fires on the 'uro' piece in "neuro-" compounds (neuroscience, neurological, neuroimmune), and weakly on ' neu' before 'roscience'. Members detect 'uro' after 'Ne'. Fires on that word piece, not on other uses.

Fires on ' with' after a noun or verb phrase when it introduces a manner or accompaniment phrase (e.g. "with modern materials", "with precision"). It stays silent on ' with' in fixed expressions like "familiarity with", "in accordance with" and "challenges with".
result.label: ' with' introducing manner/accompaniment

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' gu' (also ' div') when it begins a longer word, mostly "guidelines", and predicts continuations like 'idel' or 'ides'. Members are mostly ' gu' detectors, including ones for "guild" and "guided".
result.label: ' gu' word-start piece (guidelines)

result.description: Fires on the token ' life' in prehistoric or biological text, such as 'marine life' and 'complex life', where 'forms' often comes next. It is quiet in other contexts.
result.label: ' life' in evolutionary biology contexts

result.description: Fires on " for" after advocate/advocating (and similar verbs like call, aim) where it introduces the cause being supported. It stays silent on " for" after nouns like foundation, desire, or in duration phrases.
result.label: ' for' after advocate-type verbs

result.description: Fires on the word " result" (and "results") as a noun in "as a result of" or as a verb in "results in / result from", marking a causal link. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: "result" in causal phrases

result.description: Fires on the word " early" (rarely " ancient") when it means an early stage of a field or technology, as in "early cave paintings" or "early research". It stays silent in "early 20th century" date phrases.
result.label: ' early' as early-stage modifier
' dict' in dictate/dictator
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' dict' at the start of "dictate/dictated/dictatorship", where the next piece is likely 'ate' or 'ator'. Members mostly detect similar stems (domin-, motiv-, acceler-, fost-) that precede -ate.

Fires on word stems that are usually followed by a suffix, mainly ' colon' (colonization, colonies), also ' pool', ' branch' and ' bank'. It predicts suffix pieces like 'ing', 'ies', 'izers'. Mostly colon-detector members.
result.label: Word stems before suffix: colon, pool

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a noun or word (Rub, conduct, high, ch) right after "like a / akin to a / as ... as an" in a metaphor or simile. It is weak outside that comparison slot.
result.label: Word after simile "like a"

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'rac' (extracellular, embracing), 'ak' (sneaky, awakening, Tokamak) and 'ist'/'ism' when they sit inside a longer word. Members are token detectors for 'ak' and 'rac'. It predicts a word continuation.
result.label: Mid-word fragments 'rac', 'ak', 'ist'

result.description: Fires on the word " health" as a standalone word, strongest in "financial health" of a company. It stays silent when "health" is a word-start piece in "healthcare". Predicts continuations like "and", "of", "indicators".
result.label: financial " health" standalone word

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'od' when it is a mid-word fragment, mostly in "emb-od-iment/embodied", also par-od-ies, Ge-od-etic, K-od-ak. Silent on 'od' in "eonoderm". Predicts suffixes like 'ied', 'iment', 'ies'.
result.label: 'od' fragment in embodiment

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' prior' before 'itize/itizing' and on 'look' in 'overlooked', where the next piece is a suffix (-it, -ed). Silent on ' prior' after "that" in some contexts, so a construction effect may exist.
result.label: prior(itize) and overlook word pieces

result.description: Fires on the token ' industry' (e.g. "culinary industry", "music industry", "industry-standard"). It mildly pushes toward words like standards and benchmark. Members are mostly earlier-layer ' industry' detectors.
result.label: ' industry' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'uro' in "neuro-" compounds (neurological, neurodevelopmental, neuroeconomic), where it follows "ne". It is silent when 'uro' starts the text with no "ne" before it.
result.label: 'uro' inside neuro- words

result.description: Fires mostly on digits inside long runs of repeated digits (0s, 9s) in numeric strings, plus scattered mid-word pieces and nouns. Silent on a '0' in an ordinary number like "100 years". Evidence is mixed and the consistency is low.
result.label: Digits in long digit runs

result.description: Fires on the word " philosophy" itself, as a noun in phrases like "analytical philosophy", "philosophy of science" or "in philosophy". Members mostly detect philosophy-related word pieces such as Philosoph, philosoph and the "y" of Philosophy.
result.label: ' philosophy' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' the' or ' of' right after words like epitomize, epitome, zenith, quintessence, pinnacle, i.e. a slot where something is described as the embodiment or peak of a quality. Predicts words like excellence, elegance, triumph.
result.label: Epitome/pinnacle 'of' slot
Hull piece in engineering headings
result.description: Fires mainly on the 'ull' piece in "Hull" at the start of engineering/naval section headings (Hull Materials, Hull Coatings). Weaker on word-final pieces like 'craft', 'ical', 'ement' in technical text. It predicts construction and engineering words.

Fires on the final pieces of the word "paradox" and its derivatives ("parado-x", "paradox-ical", "paradox-es"), after "parado" has been seen. Weakly fires on similar suffixes like "ironic". Predicts continuations such as "ical" and "contradict".
result.label: paradox word ending

result.description: Fires on ' and' joining two nouns in a short title or heading-like phrase at the start of a document (e.g. "Food and Ethnicity", "Education and society"). It is quiet on 'and' in some longer headings with verbs or abstract phrases.
result.label: 'and' in "X and Y" headings
'tr' mid-word fragment (filtration)
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'tr' in the middle of a longer word, mainly 'fil|tr|ation', also 'Al|tr|uism', 'ul|tr|asonics' and 'synchro|tr|on'. Predicts a word-completing continuation such as 'ation'. Silent on ordinary whole words.

Fires on the token ' demand' (economic or on-demand sense) in supply-chain, forecasting and economics text. Members are mostly earlier-layer ' demand' detectors. It predicts continuations like forecasting, prediction and -ing.
result.label: ' demand' token detector

result.description: Fires on a predicate adjective after a copula ("are common(place)", "were prevalent", "are preferred", "is necessary"), where the next words are likely a complement or reason. It stays silent on attributive "common" as in "our common humanity".
result.label: Predicate adjective after "are/were"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (output, hardware, user, air, electrical) inside technical/engineering and computing descriptions, often a modifier or noun in a technical noun phrase. Peaks are scattered; logits point to institutional or engineering nouns. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Technical systems-engineering noun phrases

result.description: Fires on ' as' directly after "act/acts/serve/function" meaning "act as a X" (role sense). Silent on 'as well as', 'also as', and comparative 'as'. Predicts role nouns like agent, catalyst.
result.label: 'as' after act/serve (role as)

result.description: Fires on mixed mid-word pieces (lo in Apollo, ull in hull, wide) and on ' and' joining coordinated items, often after "peace". Peaks are scattered and low-consistency; no clear shared condition.
result.label: Scattered word pieces and 'and'
Mid-word pieces: bin, itude, hing
result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'bin' in Combinatorics/recombination and 'itude' in multitude, where the word is still unfinished. It is silent on the start of 'Mult…' in the contrast.
