result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ous' inside "Wareh-ous-ing" (also Aque-ous, R-ous-burg) and on ' she' in "she-ar/she-aring". It stays silent on adjective-suffix 'ous' (prosperous, meticulous), so it needs a mid-word position.
result.label: Mid-word 'ous' in Warehousing, 'she' in shear

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe token itself when it comes right after a word or name and is followed by a suffix like 's, 'll, 've, 'd or 're (possessive or contraction). Predicts those suffix letters.
result.label: Apostrophe before suffix (possessive/contraction)

result.description: Fires on the single letter 'n' used as a math variable (index, subscript, factorial or combinatorial argument) in mathematical text. Silent on 'n' inside quotes at the start of a document, where it is not a math variable.
result.label: Variable 'n' in math expressions
' top' as start of topology words
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' top' when it begins a longer word, mainly 'topologies' and 'topographical', and also 'top quark'. It stays silent on the complete word 'topology'.
Fires on the token ' framework' (and more weakly ' frameworks'), mostly in lists or overviews of software and conceptual frameworks. Members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' framework' token detector

result.description: Fires on a mix of function words (' if', ' an', ' a') and ' remark', mostly where the word starts a conditional or modifier phrase. It stays silent on ' if' after verbs like "check if" or "know if". Members are noisy and non-discriminative; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Conditional 'if' / 'an' mixed function words

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-sentence tokens (word pieces, 'their', 'to', 'as') in text about the ITIL IT service framework. Peaks are mixed and the contrast silences it on 'comprehensive' in other contexts like PLM. The circuit failed and looks weak.
result.label: ITIL framework text, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on words right after the verb "hold/held" (a crucial position, held deep-seated, hold 75%, hold power), in the object phrase's modifier or first word. Silent after "is/was a". Predicts role/stock-like nouns.
result.label: Object phrase after "hold"

result.description: Fires on scattered function tokens (' of', ' in', commas, document start) in physics/science-style text after nouns like "formation" or "arrangement". Contrast shows it silent on the same ' of' in similar contexts, so the condition is unclear. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered 'of'/'in' after abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on the word or word piece right after "a"/"an" in a noun phrase describing a period or era (e.g. "an un-", "a significant", "an era"). It is where an adjective or noun is about to start. Evidence is mixed and the circuit was unfaithful.
result.label: Word after "a/an" in era descriptions

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'oph', 'igu', ' capt', ' ne' and on ' not'/'s' right after "'s" in descriptive text, where an adjective or word is being built. It is silent on 'oph' in some "sophisticated" contexts, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Word fragments after 's

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens: digit '4' inside years, commas, ' and', and document start, in abstract philosophical text. Members include '4' detectors and philosophy/comma features, but the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered digit 4 and comma peaks

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied tokens (word endings like 'ity', commas, ' try', ' situations', ' attached') in academic or expository prose. No clear shared token or construction; the circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Diffuse mixed-token expository latent

result.description: Fires on connectors (' and', commas, ' than', ' just') right after the word "numbers" or number/math-related nouns in "not just numbers and…" or "beyond numbers and…" phrasing. It stays quiet on 'and' in other lists and descriptions.
result.label: Connector after "numbers" in not-just phrases

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a verb stem (man-, evalu-, interpre-, document-) in a comma-separated list of gerunds/process verbs, predicting an -ing suffix. Silent on 'man' after a plain verb like "includes".
result.label: Verb stem in gerund list, predicts -ing

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (generate, share, story, the) in writing and idea-sharing text. Members are mostly generic token detectors; the circuit failed faithfulness, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed creative/ideas words, unclear

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' brid' (start of "bridge/bridging", e.g. "Network brid|ges"), predicting completions like -ges/-ged/-ging. Members detect ' brid' and similar split-word starts such as ' mer' (mergers).
result.label: ' brid' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the verb or word right after an abstract subject noun like "choice" or "selection" (is, not, goes, transcends, emerges as), where the text is about to say the choice matters or goes beyond something. Silent on "is" after other subjects.
result.label: Verb after "choice/selection" subject

result.description: Fires on function words (the, is, are, there) and subject nouns right after an introductory "Along with ..." phrase, where the main clause's subject or verb begins. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is weak.
result.label: Main clause after introductory phrase

result.description: Fires on function words (to, in, of, the) right after verbs like "allows"/"enabling" in simulation and modeling text, where a simulation-related verb or noun is expected next. Silent on many other "to" cases, so the condition is only loosely identified.
result.label: Function words before simulation verbs

result.description: Fires on varied function tokens (commas, ' are', ' also', ' be', 'include') in expository lists of factors or considerations, where a list or further item is expected. Peaks are scattered and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: List-of-factors connectives, weak

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on ' sector' in "each industry sector" (business chess text), plus scattered tokens like ' land', 'ematic', ' b'. Members are generic token detectors; circuit failed faithfulness, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Industry sector, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on varied function words (and, or, of, in, which, indicate) in abstract expository prose, often after a completed noun phrase or list item. Silent on many 'and' tokens in lists. Weak, mixed evidence; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the possessive ending ('s or ') after "viewer(s)" in art and visual-composition text, such as "the viewer's eye". It also fires weakly on a few other words. It stays silent on other possessives, such as "artist's" and "it's".
result.label: Viewer's possessive in art text

result.description: Fires mostly on the final '0' of a year like "2010" after "occurred on April 20, 201", and weakly on scattered tokens such as "inside" or "people". Peaks are mixed and consistency is low. Members feed on "in/on [a]" prepositional contexts.
result.label: Final digit of year after date

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' in', ' and', ' computer', ' pipeline') in technical computer-architecture text, e.g. "improvements in instruction processing". Silent on ' in' in other contexts. Weak circuit, mixed evidence.
result.label: Computer architecture text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on connectives (and, as, to, or) or "processes" following "natural ..." in contrasts of natural versus human-made causes, e.g. "natural processes such as", "volcanic eruptions, and anthropogenic". Silent on "natural and human" and on other lists. Weak circuit.
result.label: Natural vs human-made contrast connectives

result.description: Fires mostly on commas in lists of business concepts right after "customer satisfaction/loyalty" (customer-centric business text), plus a few words like "increased". Silent on commas after similar terms like efficiency, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Commas after customer satisfaction lists

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' particles', ' and', 'atter', ' to') in particle-physics text about matter/antimatter asymmetry and CP violation. Members are physics-topic detectors (Higgs, forces, dark matter). Silent on 'particles' in other physics contexts.
result.label: Matter-antimatter asymmetry physics text

result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "human-computer interaction", appearing in a list of application areas after "surveillance". Also fires on "care" in "healthcare". Silent on the same hyphen in other contexts, such as lists of fields or "real-time". The circuit is weak and the members are generic.
result.label: Hyphen in human-computer after surveillance

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (and, comma, printing, reducing) inside lists of art and craft techniques, like 3D printing and glaze effects. Members are art, printmaking and ceramics topic detectors. Silent on 'and' in general technology or arts text.
result.label: Art technique list continuation

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function tokens (commas, "the", "is", "that", "which") and word endings like "ived" in academic expository prose, after a noun phrase or clause. It is silent on some commas in the contrast. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered commas and function words

result.description: Fires mostly on 'ographic' in "cryptographic keys", plus document-start tokens and ' synchron'. Silent on "cryptographic systems", so it needs the following-context slot (keys). Weak, failed circuit with mixed evidence.
result.label: cryptographic keys / document start

result.description: Fires on words right after a "not just X, but (also)" contrast, such as "as", "rather", "functions", or "their", where a second, added role or claim is introduced. It is weak and inconsistent, and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: After "not only... but also" clause

result.description: Fires on prepositions and function words (to, on, with, for) in text about CPU cache and memory hierarchy, e.g. "closest to the processor". Silent on "to" in other memory-related text, so the cache-description context matters. Weak, unfaithful circuit.
result.label: Prepositions in CPU cache descriptions

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on connectives (and, with, commas, more, different, various) in expository text about music and arts exchange. Silent on many 'and' tokens in other contexts; evidence is thin and the circuit failed.
result.label: Connectives in music/arts expository text

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (of, and, the, commas, verbs) inside text about blending or merging fields like engineering, biology, and the arts. It stays silent on many 'of' tokens in similar text, and the evidence doesn't show why.
result.label: Function words in interdisciplinary-fusion text

result.description: Fires on varied head nouns or modifiers (supplies, techniques, developed, efficiency) ending a technical noun phrase in scientific or technical prose. Peaks are mixed and the circuit failed, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Technical noun-phrase endings (weak)

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (veget'ables', ' fluid', ' meat', ' and', ' of'), often mid-noun-phrase in food or technical prose. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase noun tokens

result.description: Fires mostly on coordinating ' and' (also ' or', '-wise') joining two items, notably after the acronym "(WRB)" in a soil-classification list. It stays silent on many other ' and' uses, and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Coordinating 'and' after acronym

result.description: Fires weakly on the subject noun of a clause (particle, scientist, processor, robot) just before a modal or verb like "must perform" or "can perform". Peaks are mixed and the circuit is low-faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Subject noun before modal verb

result.description: Fires on the digit '7' as the decade digit in a year ("19[7]5", "19[7]0") right after the title of a US education law (Education for All Handicapped Children Act). It stays silent on '7' in other year forms such as "1970s", "194[7]" or "18[7]0".
result.label: '7' in 1970s year of education act

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and content words (' to', ' the', ' in', ' many') in abstract academic or expository prose. Members mostly detect list-final nouns and word endings before punctuation. The pattern is mixed, and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose
'lass' piece in Neoclassicism
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'lass' inside "Neoclassicism" / "Neoclassic" / "neoclassical", mostly after "Neoc". It is a within-word piece detector; members mostly detect 'lass' and similar mid-word fragments.
Fires on words in lists of punctuation marks (e.g. "commas and periods", "question marks and exclamation") in text about punctuation and grammar. It is silent on ' and' in ordinary prose.
result.label: Punctuation-mark lists in grammar text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and connectors (essentially, in, to, of, as, creates) in economics text about information asymmetry, mid-sentence before a predicate or noun phrase. Silent on ' where' after a comma. Mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in asymmetry economics text

result.description: Fires on varied connective or suffix tokens (' where', 'izing', 'uting', ' of', ' how') in texts about inanimate narratives and creative writing, where a clause or verb object is about to follow. Consistency is low; the contrast shows ' where' staying silent in a self-help-books passage.
result.label: Connectives in inanimate-narrative writing

result.description: Fires on the field-name word completing "Philosophy of X" list entries (science, religion, perception, knowledge) and on discipline suffixes like -ics. It is silent on -ics in running prose about ethics or metaphysics.
result.label: Philosophy-of-X field name

result.description: Fires on function words (the, a, as, it) shortly after "World War I" at the start of a document, in text about the First World War. Silent on the same words in other contexts. Evidence is mixed; circuit faithfulness is weak.
result.label: Function words after World War I

result.description: Fires on function words and connectives (like, such as, across, the, commas) that introduce examples or elaboration after a statement, as in "scriptures such as". Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Example-introducing connectives, weak

result.description: Peaks on scattered tokens (' these', ' affect', ' radi', ' hard', 'acoustic') in physics/science prose, mostly mid-sentence before a verb or word continuation. Evidence is mixed; members are noisy token detectors and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered science-text tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (commas, "that", "form", "by", "with") in climate and atmospheric-science text about air masses and ocean currents; predicts climate/meteorology terms such as latitude. Commas fire only in some contexts.
result.label: Climate-text function words and commas

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens: 'ally' in "universally", 'including', ' data', and document start. It is silent on 'ally' in "socially", so it looks word-specific, but the evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mixed 'ally'/'including' tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires at mid-word or mid-phrase positions on varied tokens (' to', ' e', ' cry', ' and', commas) where a word or phrase continues. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed, so the evidence is weak. Logits favor science-like word starts (carbon, organ).
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (of, in, on, comma) in short passages about rationalism and philosophy, right after the topic phrase. It stays silent on 'of' in other philosophy contexts such as empiricism. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in rationalism text

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (commas, 'to', 'the', 'in', word-ending pieces like 'ity', 'ing') in expository text, mid-phrase. No single token or construction dominates; the logits are mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function tokens

result.description: Fires on connectives like ' and', ' or', ' cannot' in cosmology/physics text after "matter"-type terms (dark matter, matter and antimatter). Silent on many ' and' in the same topic, so the exact condition is unclear. Circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: 'and' in cosmology matter lists

result.description: Fires mostly on " children" as the subject of a clause in educational/developmental text (e.g. "children sing", "children who"), and weakly on "to" or "with" before a verb or object. Silent on " children" in some other slots, such as after "engage" or "and".
result.label: Children as clause subject

result.description: Fires mainly on the comma right after the word "phenomenon", where a relative clause ("which is/occurs/emerged") follows. Weaker on words after "phenomenon" like "occurs". Silent on commas after other nouns, such as "magnetic field,".
result.label: Comma after "phenomenon"

result.description: Fires on function words (' is', ' must', ' be', ',') right after a subject noun phrase, especially quantified subjects like "all left descendants must". Silent on many ' is' tokens in other contexts. Weak, mixed evidence; circuit failed.
result.label: Verb slot after quantified subject

result.description: Fires on function words ' that' and ' a' that begin a clause or noun phrase after a preceding noun or verb phrase. It is silent on many other ' that' cases. Members are diffuse and the circuit failed, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Function words 'that' / 'a' (weak)

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and function words (e.g. "chorus", "versatile", "its" after "such as the Pantheon with") in descriptive passages about music or architecture. Silent on "chorus" in some contexts. Weak circuit with mixed evidence.
result.label: Mixed word pieces: chorus, its, -ished

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on possessive 's after "Frederick Sanger" plus scattered tokens (' a', '2', ' such', ' personal'). Contrast shows 's silent after other names and contractions. Members are generic; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered tokens, Sanger's possessive

result.description: Fires on the last token of a noun phrase after "questions/debates/concerns about/regarding" (e.g. "the moral", "ethical", "sacredness", "attainability"), where an abstract issue is being discussed. It is silent on ordinary "the" elsewhere.
result.label: Abstract issue noun after "questions about"

result.description: Fires on words like "overall", "experience", "culinary", "memorable" in flowery dining/culinary-experience prose, often just before a noun like "experience" or "mood". It stays silent on "overall" in some other contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Dining-experience descriptive modifiers

result.description: Fires on the piece 'arg' when it follows 'b' inside 'bargain', 'bargaining', 'bargainer'. Members are mostly 'arg' token detectors in early layers. Also fires weakly on 'arg' in 'jargon'.
result.label: 'arg' in bargain words
