result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'log' in crystallography, phylogenetic, syllogism, and on ' orth' / ' trig' in technical science words. It fires within scientific words being spelled out, with weaker hits on 'and' in lists of crystal systems.
result.label: Technical word fragment 'log' (crystallography)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ni" inside "omnipresent" (om|ni|present), where the next piece is likely "present". Members detect mid-word fragments such as "ni" in Millennium and "chni" in Techniques.
result.label: 'ni' in omnipresent

result.description: Fires on the capital letter ' M' as a word-initial fragment that begins an acronym or name (MOS, MRAM, MRI, MGF, MIDI), where further letters follow. Members are mostly detectors of ' M' itself.
result.label: Acronym-initial ' M' token

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (' and', ' that', ' a', ' an') in abstract expository prose, mid-phrase where a noun phrase continues. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the exact condition is unclear. It is silent on some ' and' tokens in philosophy/math text.
result.label: Function words in abstract expository prose

result.description: Fires on varied verb-like or function tokens (making, improve, -ine in undermine, than, and, to) in essay-style text about communication and feedback, where a verb or object is expected next. Silent on 'ance' in 'enhance'. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Verb slots in communication essays

result.description: Fires on the token " Quant" (start of "Quantum", also "Quantifiers"), mostly at the start of a line or heading in lists of topic titles. Members are detectors of " Quant" itself.
result.label: ' Quant' token at heading start

result.description: Fires on "practices" (also "practice", "Pract|ices") when it completes the phrase "best practices". It stays quiet on "practices" after other words such as design, documentation or these.
result.label: "best practices" completion

result.description: Fires on ' order' in "in order to" (and other 'order' uses) and on 'iast' in "ecclesiastical". Two unrelated tokens; silent on similar purpose-clause text without 'order'.
result.label: 'order' and 'iast' (ecclesiastical)

result.description: Fires on the leading digit '1' of a four-digit year (e.g. 1000, 1800, 1900) right after "from", "between" or "(" in date-range contexts. It stays silent on '1' in ordinal centuries like "19th century".
result.label: Leading '1' of a year

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (word pieces like 'ol', 'the', 'of', 'an') in abstract, expository text about engineering, technology and science, where a noun or verb is expected next. Evidence is mixed and the token pattern is weak.
result.label: Expository engineering text mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on varied connecting tokens ('-', ' where', ' without', ' from', ' to') in text about online or digital communication contrasted with traditional face-to-face interaction. It anticipates a next word like 'physical' or 'previous'. Silent on other hyphens.
result.label: Connectives in digital-vs-traditional communication

result.description: Fires on math-related modifier words, mainly " number" (number sense, number theory), also " mathematical", " numerical", " pattern", in math-education or math text. Seems to predict a following noun such as theory or compound pieces.
result.label: Number / mathematical modifier words

result.description: Fires on the word piece " altern" at the start of "alternating", where the word continues with "-ating". Members detect similar word-start fragments (coord, bin, compar, ordin) that need a suffix to complete.
result.label: ' altern' start of "alternating"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (the, or, to, intent, how, use) in abstract explanatory prose about linguistics or concepts. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same ' the' is often silent, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in abstract expository prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'chan' in "mechan-" words, mainly biomechanics/mechanics (biomechanical, mechanics, mechanisms), and on capitalized ' Mechan' pieces. Members are detectors of chan/Mechan pieces that predict suffixes like -ical/-ics.
result.label: 'chan' piece in mechanics words

result.description: Fires on the variable 'x' when it is the argument inside a function call in calculus text, such as f(x), u(x) or v(x), in discussions of derivatives and products or quotients of functions.
result.label: x as function argument

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' hy' when it begins a word like hyphen, hyphenation or hybrid, mid-sentence. It stays silent when the word starts the document, so it needs a preceding context token.
result.label: ' hy' word-start (hyphen/hybrid)

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' settled', ' in', ' on', ' of', ' through') in passages about the origins and early history of a field or civilization (agriculture, early computing, machine learning). Mixed peaks, low consistency; predicts nothing clearly.
result.label: Origins/early-history narrative tokens

result.description: Fires on the word "Theory"/"theory" (and weakly "theories") ending a named theory, such as "Uncertainty Reduction Theory" or "Arrhenius theory". Weaker on "this theory"/"this idea". Silent on unrelated statistics text.
result.label: Named "Theory" word

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yth' in "Pythagorean" (after 'P'), also in similar pieces like 'rhythms'. Silent when 'yth' starts a word, as in "ythagorasia". Output logits are not clearly interpretable.
result.label: 'yth' piece in Pythagorean

result.description: Fires on scattered word pieces in academic or science text (Dal- of Dalton, sci-fi, carbohydrate, social contract), often a first piece of a longer term. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the evidence is unclear.
result.label: Scattered word-start pieces in academic text

result.description: Fires on the word "flow"/"flows" (and "flowing") as a verb, most strongly when an abstract or fluid subject like ideas, emotions, music or capital moves smoothly. Weakly on similar movement verbs.
result.label: "flow" as a verb of movement

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (digits, word fragments, ' or', ' for', ' medical') in explanatory, encyclopedic-style text. No consistent trigger or condition is visible; the circuit failed and members are generic.
result.label: Scattered tokens in explanatory text

result.description: Fires on function words (by, the, of, with) mid-sentence in abstract essay-style prose about writing, communication and storytelling. Peaks are scattered and the logits are not clear. The contrast shows no clear rule for when it stays silent.
result.label: Function words in writing-advice prose

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (intricate, complex, mastery, a, s) in descriptions of a composer's or artist's style, such as Bach's intricate polyphony. Members are mostly music and art topic detectors. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Praise of composer's intricate style

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' pod' when it begins 'podcast', 'podcasting' or 'podcasters', and predicts 'cast' next. Members detect ' pod' and 'cast' pieces plus other word-initial fragments that need a continuation.
result.label: ' pod' before 'cast'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' deliver' (as in deliverables, delivering), mostly in project-management text. It is weaker on the verb 'to deliver' and stays silent on nearby text without the word. Members are detectors of deliver/-ing.
result.label: ' deliver' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on mixed function tokens, mostly ' (' after a temperature or numeric value (e.g. "375°C (175"), also ' and', ' capac' and a few word pieces. Silent on ' (' introducing prose asides. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Parenthesis after numeric units

result.description: Fires on possessive ' their'/' its' right after "for" (or similar prepositions) in praise constructions like "prized/known/renowned for their X", predicting a quality noun next. Quieter after "of", "through", "in".
result.label: their/its after "known for"

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'rig' in "irrigation" (also 'tr' in "infiltration"), a word fragment before "-ation" in environmental or agricultural text. Weakly fires on similar pieces before "-ation" or "-ing", such as "veget" and "she".
result.label: 'rig' inside irrigation

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, to) and some nouns like 'hydro' in technical/scientific expository text, often after nouns like "flow characteristics of" or "into". Stays silent on 'the' in "one of the" or "nature of the". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in technical prose
'od' in Thermodynamics
result.description: Fires on the token 'od' as the middle piece of "Thermodynamics" (e.g. "Law of Therm|od|ynamics"), predicting "ynamic" continuations. It is silent on 'od' in "thermodynamic quantities", and weakly active on similar pieces like 'ad' in "Faraday".

Fires on the token " capital" (also " Capital") in finance and economics text, such as working capital, capital structure and capital market, and in capitalism or capitalization. It predicts word continuations like -ize, -ization and -ism.
result.label: ' capital' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' is' (sometimes ' are') right after an abstract noun subject such as "journey", "experience" or "road", before a predicate. It stays quiet after pronouns like "it" and in some other subjects.
result.label: ' is' after abstract noun subject

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often ' MongoDB' after "such as/like" in database text, plus function words (' a', ' offer', ' for') in technical software/database passages. Members are mostly generic technical-context attention heads. Peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: MongoDB and tech-text function words

result.description: Fires on " with" after communication verbs like connect, engage, communicate, where a person or audience object follows (connect with fans, engage with consumers). Silent on " with" meaning accompaniment, synonymous with, or integrating with.
result.label: "with" after connect/communicate verbs

result.description: Fires on pieces of the word "electro..." (' electro', 'imet' in electrogravimetry, 'ro' in Electrode) in electrochemistry text, especially when electrogravimetry/electroplating are listed. Silent on ' electro' before electrode/static in other contexts. Weak and mixed evidence.
result.label: electro- word pieces in electrochemistry

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' re' mid-word, mostly after nuclear, chemical or redox words, where it starts "reactions" or "reactor". Silent on some ' re' tokens in other contexts, such as at document start or after "spontaneous".
result.label: ' re' in nuclear/chemical reactions

result.description: Fires on the punctuation of "e.g.," / "i.e.," (the period or comma after "e.g") and sometimes a colon, when introducing a list of examples in linguistic or technical explanatory text. Silent on plain prose without such example markers.
result.label: e.g., example-introducing punctuation

result.description: Fires on the ending of a plural noun (-hips, -ues, -onds, relationships, conflicts) that is the subject at the start of a sentence, where a plural verb like "are" or "can be" comes next. Silent when the plural noun is an object.
result.label: Plural subject noun before verb

result.description: Fires weakly on varied connective and list-position tokens (' and', ',', ' their', ' mixture', ' or') in academic, list-like text, but stays silent on many ' and' tokens in similar lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse list connectives in academic text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly relative-clause ' which' and ' was' after it, plus ')', word pieces like 'ial', and hyphens. Silent on some ' which' after a comma in technical text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered ' which' and function tokens

result.description: Fires on prepositions (' in', ' for', ' to') right after an adjective of importance such as essential, crucial, fundamental or critical. It stays silent on 'in' in other slots, such as after nouns or verbs like 'proficiency in'.
result.label: Preposition after 'essential/crucial'

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix 'ic' in words like Germanic or Strategic, with scattered peaks on ' to', 'l' and other tokens. It stays silent on 'ic' in acid-related words (acidic, phosphoric, electromagnetic). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Suffix 'ic' (Germanic-type), mixed

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ant' when it starts a word like antibodies, antibiotics, antiviral, antiparticles, or antigenic, where the next piece is completed as 'anti-'. It is silent on other text.
result.label: ' ant' as start of 'anti-' words

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'acy' completing "privacy" (priv|acy), in text about data protection and consent. It stays silent when 'acy' starts a document with no preceding 'priv'.
result.label: 'acy' in "privacy"

result.description: Fires on ' perspective' (also 'point' in viewpoint) when it is a noun for a viewpoint, typically after adjectives like "unique" or "crucial" and before "on". Silent on technical "linear perspective" and sentence-initial use.
result.label: ' perspective' as viewpoint noun

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' leadership', 'ment', ' style', 'ation', ' which') in abstract academic/social-science prose about collaboration, empowerment and leadership. Mixed evidence; silent on some ' leadership' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Abstract leadership/collaboration prose tokens
Word-initial fragments before continuation (py-)
result.description: Fires mostly on the word-start piece ' py' (as in pyruvate, pyramids) after glycolysis-type text. It also fires on a few other word-start fragments like 'cir', ' D' and a year's '1'. Members detect other prefix pieces expecting a suffix.

Fires on the token " home" / " Home", both as a modifier (home cooks, home producers, homeowners, home recording) and in "at home"; also in "homeo-" word starts. Members are mostly detectors of "home".
result.label: " home" token detector

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'esian' completing "Bayesian" (also Keynesian-type words), after the word start "Bay". Members detect 'esian' and similar adjective suffixes like -ctic, -antic.
result.label: Bayesian 'esian' suffix

result.description: Fires on the word " number" (also "Number"), mostly as a head noun in "the number of…" or "a number of", and in math contexts like "natural number" or "quantum number". Members are mostly " number" detectors.
result.label: the word "number"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (" the", " of", ",", " unique", " several") and the piece " G", mid-sentence in expository prose. Members are generic token detectors from list-like text; no clear shared trigger or condition.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' syn' at the start of words like synaptic, synonym, synergy, synchrotron. Members are mostly ' syn' token detectors. The logits are mixed and do not give a clear next-token prediction.
result.label: ' syn' word-start token

result.description: Fires on the "ance" piece of the verb "enhance" (also "enhances", "improve"), mainly in food and flavor text, predicting an object like taste or flavor. Silent on "ance" in nouns like "fragrance".
result.label: enhance verb, "-ance" piece

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' las' / ' Las' (before 'er') and on 'polym'/'ym' in 'polymer', i.e. word fragments that need a suffix like '-er' to complete. Mostly in technical science text; predicts the completing suffix.
result.label: las- / polym- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the word " bare" (as in "bare bones", "bare minimum", "bare ground"), often in metaphorical or analogy phrasing. Members detect bare and similar adjectives like plain, raw, empty, open. Next-token logits are mixed.
result.label: ' bare' adjective token

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ic' completing "macroscopic" in statistical-mechanics/thermodynamics text. It stays silent on 'ic' in "microscopic", "spectroscopic", "semiclassical" and similar words.
result.label: 'ic' ending "macroscopic"

result.description: Fires on a sentence-ending period after an instructional or technical statement (e.g. audio, editing, formatting advice), where a new sentence is about to start. Silent on periods after abbreviations like "etc." or "b." or before paragraph breaks in other contexts.
result.label: Sentence-final period in instructional text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' By' when it begins "Byzantine" after "the" (mid-sentence), predicting a continuation like 'zan'. Silent when Byzantine is the first token of the document. Weak activity on other word-start fragments.
result.label: By- start of Byzantine

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens in physics-flavored text, mostly 'ons' (phonons), ' force', and 'ification'. The logits favor motion verbs like pushing, moving and driving. The 'ons' peak is silent in 'silencerons', so it needs a physics context.
result.label: Physics force/phonon terms

result.description: Fires on words meaning subtle or slight, mostly the 'le' in "subtle", also " slight", "slightest" and "quiet", in descriptions of small, understated gestures or changes. Predicts "ty" or "yet" continuations weakly.
result.label: subtle / slight understatement words

result.description: Fires on the word pieces 'ital' and 'ization' inside "revitalization"/"revitalize", mostly in language-endangerment and preservation text. Weakly fires on other -ization words like "homogenization". Quiet on unrelated contexts.
result.label: revitalization word pieces

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (' mark', apostrophe, digits, 'ations', mid-word pieces) with low consistency. No clear shared trigger or condition. It appears to fire mid-word or mid-phrase in expository text, where a continuation is expected.
result.label: Scattered mid-word pieces, unclear

result.description: Fires on the 'ist' piece of 'twist' (also twists, twisty) in writing-advice text about plot twists. It stays silent on 'ist' in 'protagonist', so it needs the word-piece after 'tw'.
result.label: 'ist' in 'twist'

result.description: Fires mostly on " Franz" in "Archduke Franz Ferdinand" (WWI assassination context), with a few weak hits on unrelated tokens like " out", " stability" and garbled text. Members detect Ferdinand, Sarajevo, Austria-Hungary.
result.label: Franz in Archduke Franz Ferdinand

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments and some function words (im, ason, bol, ' in', 'ever') where a word is incomplete or being continued; peaks are scattered with no single token. Contrast shows silence on 'im' inside other words like polymers.
result.label: Scattered word-piece fragments, low consistency

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ation' when it completes the word "transportation". It stays silent on 'ation' in other words like legislation, degradation, innovation. Upstream members detect the "transport" stem and related infrastructure context.
result.label: 'ation' in transportation
Digits inside long decimal numbers
result.description: Fires on mid-number digit tokens, especially '0' and '1' in long decimals or figures like 1.6180339 or 6,000, plus occasional 've' word pieces. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak and mixed.

Fires on varied tokens (weather, visual, ver-, statistical, 2, and) that start a modifier or noun in the middle of an abstract academic phrase; peaks are scattered and low-consistency. The evidence does not show a clear shared trigger.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase academic modifiers

result.description: Fires on ' used' (also employed/applied) as a reduced relative participle right after a plural noun like "methodologies used" or "techniques used", in expository text. It is silent on ' used' in passive or active verb uses.
result.label: Post-noun participle 'used' (techniques used)

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ym' piece in "Polymer" in a list of academic field or journal titles (Polymer Science/Engineering), with weaker hits on ' loss', ' data', ' step'. Members are diffuse and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: 'ym' in Polymer titles

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Festival' (especially in "Music Festival" headings), plus scattered nouns like ' evolution', ' valley', ' arc'. Festival-detecting members are discriminative; the rest is mixed, so the target looks polysemantic.
result.label: Festival plus scattered nouns

result.description: Fires on a standalone 'v' token (or ' V'/' v') that begins a word split into pieces, e.g. 'v' in sous-vide, vague, curviness, v4. Also fires on ' Rob' in 'in Robotics'. Predicts continuations like 'ague', 'antage', 'ular'.
result.label: Word-initial 'v' fragment

result.description: Fires on function words (' to', ',', ' the') in explanations of experimental design and statistics, especially "assigning sample units/participants to ... groups". Silent on ' to' in other topics. Logits are unclear; the circuit fails.
result.label: Function words in randomization/experiment text

result.description: Fires mostly on ' L' in "L1, L2" style lists and on adjectives before technical nouns (raw, executable, finished, machine) in compiler/computing text. Mixed peaks; the circuit is diffuse and its members are mostly generic attention latents.
result.label: ' L' and modifiers in compiler text

result.description: Fires on the piece "o" in "stereo" (Stere|o) when the word is split into tokens, e.g. "stereo vision" or "stereo image". It stays quiet on a standalone "o". Predicts word-continuation pieces such as "ots", "ters", "estig".
result.label: "o" inside split word "stereo"

result.description: Fires on the word "conversation" and its pieces ("convers" + "ations", also "dialogue"), mostly as an object of verbs like engage in or facilitate. Members are mostly conversation/discussion detectors. Predicts little clearly.
result.label: conversation word

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' re' when it starts a word like redox or reactions, in chemistry and electrochemistry text. It is silent on some ' re' tokens, such as at the start of a document, after "the", or in "rechargeable".
result.label: ' re' prefix in redox/reactions

result.description: Fires on the subword piece 'ios' inside scientific words, mainly 'meiosis' and 'bio-' compounds (biosensors, biosemiotics). Members detect 'ios', 'mos', 'otos' and 'os' pieces in technical biology terms. Weaker on 'osa' and 'orm'.
result.label: 'ios' piece in biology terms

result.description: Fires on " control" as a noun completing a compound after a modifier (voltage control, attitude control, quality control, access control). Silent on "a control system" and on the verb "to control".
result.label: Noun 'control' after modifier

result.description: Fires on the plural noun ' factors' (also areas, concepts, considerations) right after adjectives like "key", "primary", "crucial" in a "X and Y are the key factors" predicate. Silent on "combination of factors" or "environmental factors".
result.label: Key/important 'factors' predicate noun

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: word fragments, gibberish Cyrillic pieces, " brand", " former", "as", mostly in linguistics/grammar text. No dominant token or clear condition; the peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered word-piece fragments, grammar text

result.description: Fires on the first word piece (often a single letter or short fragment like 'e', 'c', 'ar', 'vi') right after an opening parenthesis, where a parenthetical is starting. Logits favor closing parentheses, so it tracks being inside a parenthetical.
result.label: First token inside opening parenthesis

result.description: Fires on ' by' introducing a method or means clause after a noun, as in "counting by using", "enumeration by alternately adding". Silent on passive agent 'by' ("influenced by", "played by") and "proof by contradiction".
result.label: ' by' introducing a method

result.description: Fires on causal verbs like "brought" (about) and "usher-ed" (in) after a historical or technological change as subject (Industrial Revolution, internet), predicting "about/in" and a result such as a new era or changes.
result.label: Change-bringing verbs: brought about, ushered in

result.description: Fires on the token ' sources' when it follows a quantifier or modifier like "various", "different" or "primary" (e.g. "information from various sources"). It stays silent when ' sources' begins the text with no preceding modifier.
result.label: ' sources' after various/different
Sentence-ending period in philosophy text
result.description: Fires on the period ending a sentence in abstract philosophy passages (idealism, realism, mathematical truth), occasionally on ' and'. It stays silent on periods in other contexts, such as logic or narrative text and abbreviations like "i.e.".

Fires on the word-start piece ' batt' (also ' brut') when it begins a longer word like battles, battled or battlements. It expects a continuation such as '-les'. Weakly fires on similar word-start pieces like 'un-orth'.
result.label: ' batt' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word " code" / " Code" (also "codes"), mostly when it modifies a following noun, as in "code coverage", "code review", "code-switching". Covers both software and linguistic senses. Predicts compound continuations.
result.label: "code" as compound modifier

result.description: Fires on ' which' (sometimes ' that') introducing a relative clause after a comma or noun, mostly in technical or process descriptions (techniques, methods). Contrast shows it is silent on some ' which' after scientific nouns like colloids, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Relative 'which' after technique nouns

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (Victorian's 'ian', year digits, 'of', 'and') in essay-like text about literary or historical periods and story structure. It predicts academic field words such as 'sciences' and 'fields'. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Literary and historical period essays

result.description: Fires on varied words in science text about pairing, bonding, or working together (pairs, together, bond, between, complementary, atom). It stays silent on the "-ate" verb ending in words like "resonate" or "curate", so it tracks the interaction sense, not the token.
result.label: Pairing/bonding and cooperation words

result.description: Fires on the word piece "astic" in "plasticity" (neuroplasticity, synaptic plasticity) and also in "elastic". Members detect "astic" and predict suffixes like "ity".
result.label: "astic" in plasticity/elastic

result.description: Fires on the word piece "rupt" in "disrupt" (disrupts, disrupting, disruptive), mostly when it is a verb taking an object such as a process or environment. Silent on other word pieces in the contrast.
result.label: "rupt" in "disrupt"

result.description: Fires on incomplete word pieces in the middle of a longer word, mainly 'RI' in MRI, ' indust' (industries) and 'opol' (geopolitics, monopolistic). Members are word-start fragment detectors that expect a suffix continuation.
result.label: Mid-word fragments: RI, indust, opol

result.description: Fires on the ' B' in immunology text about B cells (B cell, BCR, B lymphocyte), in adaptive-immune-response contexts. Silent on at least one 'B cell' example, so the condition is not fully clear.
result.label: B in B-cell immunology

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in academic or explanatory text (word endings like "comes", "al", " them", " A", " where"), with no dominant token. It is silent on "comes" in one similar context. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in academic text

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'eg' inside longer words (vinegar, electronegativity, Hegel, Kierkegaard), and sometimes the hyphen in "Agenda-Setting". It needs the piece to sit within a word that is still being completed.
result.label: 'eg' word-piece inside words

result.description: Fires on ' in' right after an abstract academic noun or adjective, such as "a concept in" or "prevalent in", where "the field of" or an area of study comes next. Silent on ' in' after "occurred" or "strides".
result.label: ' in' before "the field of"

result.description: Fires on varied adjective-like or modifier tokens (conceptual's "ual", abstract, physical, hypothetical) in an explanatory passage about abstract models. Silent on "conceptualizing". Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Abstract/conceptual modifier tokens in explanations

result.description: Fires on problem-type nouns (issues, challenges, difficulties, problems) that are the object of "address/addressing/facing" verbs. Silent on "scalability issues" in a plain list, so it seems to need the addressing/handling construction.
result.label: Challenges/issues as object of addressing
PI in PPI acronym
result.description: Fires on the 'PI' token completing the acronym PPI (protein-protein interactions), and sometimes on '0' in long runs of zeros. Members detect final pieces of capitalized acronyms and biology terms.

Fires on the token " product" in math and science text, such as "the product of determinants", "inner product" and "product rule". It is silent on general linear-algebra text that doesn't contain the word.
result.label: ' product' in math contexts

result.description: Fires on ' as' used in the role/function sense ("adopted as", "role as", "used as", "served as") introducing what something is used or treated as. Silent on the "such as" example-list construction.
result.label: ' as' meaning "in the role of"

result.description: Fires on the suffix "-ize/-izes/-izing" at the end of "maximize" (also "optimize"), especially in economics or optimization text about maximizing utility, output or efficiency. Silent on "emphasize" and "prioritize".
result.label: -ize suffix in maximize/optimize

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' curr' when it starts a longer word such as currents or curriculum, after a preceding word. It is silent when ' curr' begins the text. Weak activation on a few other word pieces.
result.label: ' curr' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on "complexity" and the "-ities" of "complexities", especially in "capture the complexities of human thought/nature" phrasing. It is silent on other text. It predicts verbs and abstract continuations only weakly.
result.label: complexity / complexities noun

result.description: Fires on the end of a role or agent noun (leader, baker, dabbler, teacher, designer) in "transform/turn from an ordinary X into a skilled Y" framing. Silent on 'ist' in non-agent words like twist or protagonist.
result.label: Agent noun in transformation phrase

result.description: Fires on the verb "predict" or the "-ing" (also -ate/-ast) ending of predicting/forecasting/anticipating, when the word is about predicting outcomes. It stays silent on "-ing" in unrelated words such as bonding or adapting.
result.label: predict / forecasting word pieces

result.description: Fires mostly on the ' fa' piece of "fauna" (e.g. "Biogeographic fauna") in biogeography/ecology text, with weaker firing on assorted list items and function words. Peaks are mixed, so the pattern is partial.
result.label: ' fa' in fauna (biogeography)

result.description: Fires on the domain noun ending a phrase like "heroes of the physiological world" or "sculptors of our planet's surface" in flowery "unsung heroes of X" praise text. It stays quiet on "world" in fiction or narrative contexts.
result.label: Domain noun after "heroes of the"

result.description: Fires on the word ' concept' when it follows an adjective like "fundamental", "essential" or "important" in a predicate-noun phrase ("X is a fundamental concept in..."). It stays silent when ' concept' starts a sentence or clause with no such modifier.
result.label: ' concept' after fundamental/essential adjective

result.description: Fires on prepositions or verbs (to, in, for, fosters) right after "understanding is essential/crucial/aids", where the next word is likely a comprehension verb like grasp or appreciate. Silent on "in" after other adjectives or nouns.
result.label: Preposition after 'understanding is essential'

result.description: Fires mostly on the token " For" (also "for", "To", " that"), especially "For" at sentence start or as the piece in "Random Forests" before "instance/example". Members detect "for" variants and "for example" continuations.
result.label: "For" token, "for instance" style

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' negoti' (negotiation, negotiate, negotiators) when it follows preceding context, predicting suffixes like 'iation'. Silent when ' negoti' starts the document, so it needs preceding text.
result.label: ' negoti' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on ' thousands' in "hundreds to thousands of" quantity phrases and on the 'struct' piece of "unstructured/structured". The two peaks are different tokens, and the weaker contexts are scattered.
result.label: ' thousands' and 'struct' (unstructured)

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments (' mon', ' unf', ' im', ' pro', 'lig') in legal and economic text, where the next piece completes a word like monetary, unfair, imbalance, prosecution or negligence. Members are mostly legal and regulatory topic detectors.
result.label: Legal word-start fragments (mon-, unf-, im-)

result.description: Fires on the word ' average' (noun/adjective, as in average-case, the average value, on average), mostly in statistics and algorithm-complexity text. Upstream members are mainly ' average' token detectors across layers 2-6.
result.label: ' average' token detector

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (' and', ',', 'gradually', 'with', 'within', '+') mid-phrase in abstract expository prose. No single token dominates; ' and' is often silent in lists, so the evidence is mixed and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered connectors in expository prose

result.description: Fires on noun stems like institution, instrument, exception, monument, element when they are likely to be followed by an '-al' or '-ation' suffix (institutional, instrumental, exceptional). Predicts 'al', 'ality', 'ally'.
result.label: Stem before -al suffix

result.description: Fires on ' When' as a sentence-opening subordinating word at the start of a document or paragraph (e.g. "When it comes to…"). It stays silent on ' When' in at least one paragraph-start case, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Sentence-initial " When"

result.description: Fires on the noun "transition" and close synonyms (transformation, shift) when used as a change-of-state noun, predicting "from/into/between/towards". Members are mostly detectors of "transition" and "transform" at earlier layers.
result.label: Transition / transformation noun

result.description: Fires on words meaning "foundation" in the metaphorical sense (foundation, basis, bedrock, cornerstone) after "forms/is the", where something is described as the underpinning of other concepts. Predicts "for" or "of".
result.label: Foundation/basis metaphor nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment ' ob' (mostly in "objection(s)"), plus a few other word-initial pieces like ' meta', ' dest', ' TH'. Contrast shows it is silent when the whole word is used instead of the split piece.
result.label: ' ob' fragment in 'objection'

result.description: Fires on function words (beyond, the, with, across, of) after verbs or nouns in globalization or cross-border text, where the next word is likely "international", "global" or "abroad". Silent on "of" after nouns like "decline of" in historical text.
result.label: Function words predicting international/global

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' et' when it starts a longer word, such as "etched" or "eternal", splitting into pieces. It predicts continuations like 'ernal' and 'ched'. Members detect ' et' and similar word-start fragments (' rh', ' cla').
result.label: ' et' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' of', ' in', ' for', 'ernel', 'term', 'CM') in technical or expository text, often mid-term or in a noun phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and ' of' is often silent. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires on words for harm or damage (' damage', 'uries', ' injury', accidents), especially in safety or prevention contexts such as PPE and equipment checks. Weaker on 'wear and tear'. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: Damage and injury words

result.description: Fires mainly on 'light' inside "Enlightenment" (and 'en' pieces), plus slashes within numeric or fraction-like strings such as "2/3/4" or "15/18". Silent on slashes between words or in "9/11". Mixed, with two distinct triggers.
result.label: Enlightenment 'light' and numeric slashes

result.description: Fires on the word stems " induct" and " predict" (also "predict" in "unpredictable") when they are unfinished word pieces, just before a suffix like -ive, -able or -or. It predicts these suffixes next.
result.label: induct/predict stem before -ive

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' sm' / ' Sm' (the start of words like smarts, smiling, smoking) and pushes toward continuations such as 'arts', 'arter', 'ash', 'iley'. Members are mostly ' sm' token detectors.
result.label: ' sm' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the ending of a culture/people/civilization adjective or demonym (Islamic, Arab, Mesopotamian, Ottoman, Armenian) in historical-cultural text, predicting nouns like Empire, region or period. Silent on 'ic' in prehistoric or monolithic.
result.label: Ethnic/cultural adjective endings in history

result.description: Fires on plural endings ('s', 'ors', 'es') attached to a noun stem, mostly in 'strengths' (strengths/weaknesses) and 'flavors'. It stays silent on apostrophe-'s' and on other plurals like 'resolutions'.
result.label: Plural suffix after noun stem

result.description: Fires on determiners (' a', ' its', ' an', ' more') right after "into" in transformation/conversion phrases ("turned into a", "consolidated into a"). Silent on ' a' in other constructions. Predicts a resulting-form noun.
result.label: Determiner after "into" (transformation)

result.description: Fires on the 's' after an apostrophe when it begins a text or sentence (contraction of "it is" / "that is", e.g. "'s not exactly", "'s the engineer"). Silent when 's' follows a word, as in "it's", "there's", "let's".
result.label: Sentence-initial apostrophe-s contraction

result.description: Fires on frequency adverbs ' often' / ' frequently' placed right after a plural or abstract subject noun (e.g. "Literature frequently employs", "Western societies often interpret"), before the main verb. Quiet when 'often' follows a comma or "there is".
result.label: often/frequently after subject noun

result.description: Fires on the closing piece 'sky' of a surname, mainly Chomsky, also other word-final pieces (het, op, edia). Members detect surname endings (Kahneman, Thaler, Einstein, Tversky) in academic text.
result.label: Surname ending 'sky' (Chomsky)

result.description: Fires on the word "Revolution"/"revolution" (including the start of "revolutionary"), in named revolutions and the general noun. It pushes toward suffixes like "ary". It stays silent in one "Industrial Revolution" example.
result.label: Revolution token, predicts -ary

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yl', mostly the end of "vinyl" (records, streaming, CDs), and also in words like syllogisms and acetylation. Silent when 'yl' starts a text with no preceding piece.
result.label: 'yl' piece, esp. vinyl

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' emot' (start of emotion/emotional) in psychology-style text about emotions. It stays silent on some ' emot' tokens after "and", "their", "for", or "understanding" in music-therapy and coping contexts.
result.label: ' emot' token in emotion text

result.description: Fires on the verb 'work' (work/worked/working) when people or groups are the subject doing work, e.g. "work together", "engineers work with". Silent on 'work' as a noun meaning a piece of writing or research.
result.label: verb 'work' with agent subject

result.description: Fires on the ending of a tech-feature noun (analyt-ics, experiences, systems, algorithms) in lists of AI-powered or smart features, where the next words describe what the feature does. It stays quiet on 'ics' in other uses, such as electronics or robotics.
result.label: AI feature noun in tech lists

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after "beyond" (beyond the realm/scope/confines of). It predicts boundary words like borders, limits, scope. It stays silent on ' the' after other words such as for, where, offers.
result.label: ' the' after "beyond"

result.description: Fires on ' syntax' as a noun (language syntax) and on the 'D' ending the acronym QKD. Silent on related words like 'syntactic constituents'. Members include syntax detectors and capital-letter fragments; the circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: ' syntax' and acronym 'D' (QKD)

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' cl' (clay, clues, clutter, cloning) and ' hum' (humidity), where a word is split into pieces and the next piece continues it. Predicts continuations like 'ues', 'aturing', 'otted'.
result.label: Split-word ' cl' / ' hum' fragments

result.description: Fires on the first word or piece of a noun phrase right after "the rise/advent/emergence/proliferation of" (e.g. digital, nation, professional, civil-). It likely predicts modern-era innovations like "Online" or "mod". Silent on "digital" elsewhere.
result.label: Modifier after "the rise of"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' empir' (before -ical/-icism), occasionally ' aggregate'. Members are detectors of ' empir' and similar incomplete stems (induct-, inqu-, Class-, graph-) that precede an -ical/-ive suffix.
result.label: ' empir' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly "the", also "of", "by", "from") in text about the Middle Ages, medieval periods and humanism, especially after "from", "influenced by" or "flourishing". It stays silent on "the" in some similar period phrases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in medieval-history text

result.description: Fires on list separators (' and', ' or', commas) inside lists of nouns naming environmental or causal factors (climate, geological, ocean variables), where the next item is another factor. Logits favor 'factors'/'internal'.
result.label: List separators in factor lists

result.description: Fires on ' moral' and on 'etic' in 'Aesthetic' (also weakly ' economic', 'aesthetic'), in philosophy/ethics-style text where a value-type adjective precedes a noun like judgment, values, or obligation. Members are mostly ' moral' detectors.
result.label: moral / aesthetic value adjective

result.description: Fires on the ordinal suffix 'TH' (or 'th') after a number, mostly in century ranges like "11-13TH" or "6th-10TH century", predicting 'century/centuries' next.
result.label: Ordinal 'TH' before century

result.description: Fires on past participles like "improved", "refined", "enhanced" used predicatively after "is/were/are" (passive verb slot), often before a "by/through/thanks" phrase. Silent when "improved" is an attributive adjective before a noun ("and improved productivity").
result.label: Passive improved/enhanced participle

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece " Me" when it begins a longer word split into pieces (Meissner, Measurement, Meiosis, Measure). It pushes the next token toward "asure". Silent on the full word "measure".
result.label: Word-initial " Me" fragment

result.description: Fires on the word " dynamic" (also " Dynamic") when used as a modifier before a noun, as in "dynamic systems", "dynamic programming", "dynamic range". It is silent when the word starts a text with no preceding context.
result.label: " dynamic" as adjective modifier

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces like "ance", "ence" or "ray" in names of spectroscopy and resonance techniques (nuclear magnetic resonance, X-ray fluorescence). It stays silent on "ance" in unrelated words such as "abundance". Predicts "Spect" continuations.
result.label: Resonance/spectroscopy technique name endings

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ations" when it completes "expectations" (expect|ations). It stays silent on "ations" in other words such as foundations, collaborations and negotiations. Output pushes towards "expect", "expectation", "about", "regarding".
result.label: "ations" ending "expectations"

result.description: Fires on the ending piece of abstract technical process nouns such as bifurcation, breakdown, collapse, curvature, decline, often in scientific or academic text. It seems to predict a following "of" or "in" phrase.
result.label: Technical process-noun endings (breakdown, collapse)

result.description: Fires on the piece "act" completing the word "counteract" (counter + act). It is silent on repeated or garbled "act" strings. It pushes toward words meaning opposing or against.
result.label: "act" in "counteract"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Sat' when it begins "Satellite" (split into Sat+ellite), especially in satellite/GPS communication text. Weaker on other word-initial fragments like Rel-, Cont-, fug-. Predicts a continuation like "ellite".
result.label: ' Sat' start of "Satellite"

result.description: Fires on the adverb ' carefully' (also -ously/-fully endings like meticulously) right before a participle or verb such as chosen, crafted, designed. It predicts words like chosen, selected, planned.
result.label: Manner adverb 'carefully' before participle

result.description: Fires on the noun " work" (also " works") meaning someone's creative output or piece, especially after a possessive like "their work" in writing and art discussions. Silent on other uses in the contrast passage.
result.label: "work" as creative output

result.description: Fires on the ending noun or word piece of a "rebirth/revival/surge/awakening/explosion/transformation" noun, in descriptions of a cultural movement, mainly the Renaissance. It is silent in other text about the same period.
result.label: Renaissance revival/surge noun endings

result.description: Fires on the word "festival" (and Festival, festiv-, festivals), and weakly on similar event words like "event" or "events". It is often a modifier or head noun in music-festival text, and it pushes towards words like grounds, circuit and planning.
result.label: Festival word detector

result.description: Fires on ' with' opening an absolute/elaborating clause after a comma following a full clause (", with the introduction of…"). Silent on ' with' as a verb complement (coincided with, filled with).
result.label: Comma-introduced ', with' clause

result.description: Fires on the "IT" piece of the acronym JIT (Just-In-Time), right after "J" in parentheses or compound use such as "JIT compilation". Predicts continuations like compilation or acronym-ending pieces.
result.label: JIT acronym "IT" token

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments inside longer words, mainly 'ific' (Sign-ific-ance, Art-ific-ial) and 'mean' (mean-ings), plus similar pieces like 'vere', 'est', 'ask'. Predicts suffix continuations such as 'ant', 'ance', 'ings'.
result.label: Mid-word fragments ific/mean

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ber' in "reverberation" (rever|ber|ation), in acoustics text. Members mostly detect 'ber' after 'rever' or similar word-internal pieces.
result.label: 'ber' inside reverberation

result.description: Fires on ' energy' right after 'renewable' (also clean/alternative energy), predicting words like sources, integration, solutions. Stays silent on 'energy' in other contexts such as energy savings, efficiency, or usage.
result.label: 'energy' after 'renewable'

result.description: Fires on the piece 'geon' in "burgeoning" (bur|geon), right after 'bur', and predicts a suffix like 'ing' or 'ed'. Appears in growth-of-an-era text. Silent in contrast text without this word.
result.label: 'geon' in burgeoning
Memory token (computing)
result.description: Fires on the word "Memory"/"memory", most strongly as a heading or topic word in computer-architecture text (Memory Hierarchy, Memory Management). It fires more weakly on "memory" in other uses, such as memory loss. Members are mostly detectors of this token.

Fires on the word " depending", mostly after verbs like "vary" or "differ" (often with "greatly"), where "on" is expected next. Members include detectors of depend/depending/relies and "greatly" after vary.
result.label: "depending" after vary
' analy' word fragment before suffix
result.description: Fires on the split word piece ' analy' (analyte, analyzer), mostly in chromatography and chemistry text. It predicts suffix pieces like 'zes', 'zer', 'se'. Weakly fires on similar truncated stems such as 'allo' and 'expres'.

Fires on the word piece " multip" at the start of "multiplicity", mostly in linear algebra text about algebraic and geometric multiplicity. It predicts the continuation "licity". Members detect " multip" and similar word-start fragments.
result.label: " multip" before "licity"

result.description: Fires on the verb " allows" (also " allow") after a subject noun such as a technique or abstraction, predicting " for" or a beneficiary next. It is silent when " allows" starts the text with no subject before it.
result.label: ' allows' after a subject

result.description: Fires on the final token of workplace-outcome nouns in lists of organizational results (morale, productivity, turnover rates, customer satisfaction), usually after "lower/higher/improved". The contrast shows silence outside such outcome lists.
result.label: Workplace outcome metric nouns
Hyphen in problem-solving compounds
result.description: Fires on the hyphen token, most strongly in "problem-solving" and similar compounds (task-, side-side, priority-). It stays quiet on hyphens in other compounds like cost-efficiency or cross-disciplinary. Members mostly detect hyphens and "problem" before it.

Fires on the word " chef" (weaker on the "fs" of "chefs") in cooking and kitchen text. Members detect chef/chefs and related occupation or role words like composer, director, artist, and culinary terms.
result.label: chef token in culinary text

result.description: Fires on mixed positions in generic expository prose, mostly sentence-end periods, " reson" (before ate/ance), "also" and "establish". Silent on many periods in similar text. Predicts verb-like continuations such as "themselves", "support", "unfold". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed periods and 'reson' in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the word " common" (or "Common"), most strongly in "greatest/least common divisor/multiple" in math text. It is weaker in other uses such as "more common" or "commonplace". It pushes towards continuations like divisor, pool, wealth and place.
result.label: "common" in greatest common divisor

result.description: Fires on the '0' token right after a leading '2' in year-like numbers (2008, 2013, 20th century, 2020). It stays silent on '0' in other positions such as 2004, 1970, or 210.
result.label: Second digit '0' in 20xx years

result.description: Fires on the token ' develop' when it begins the noun 'developments' (e.g. 'plot develop-', 'political develop-'), predicting the suffix 'ments'. Members are mostly detectors of 'develop' and its variants.
result.label: ' develop' before -ments

result.description: Fires on ' just' right after "beyond" or "more than", in the "not limited to just X" sense. It stays silent on ' just' after "not" or "are" (e.g. "are just like"). Members detect just/mere/simply/only plus "beyond".
result.label: 'just' after 'beyond'/'more than'

result.description: Fires on function words (of, and, to, that) right after abstract ethics/rights nouns like dignity, responsibility, treatment, rights, where a duty or obligation-type noun is expected next. Silent on 'of' after diversity, superiority, context.
result.label: Function words after rights/duty nouns

result.description: Fires on the verb ' hold'/' holds' when a subject (often an abstract noun) is followed by something like "hold significant importance/promise". Predicts words like particular, promise, central, great. Silent in other contexts.
result.label: verb "hold(s)" before importance

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces or word continuations (emble, fect, factor, iving, ged, um) inside multi-token words or names, often in lists of short headings. Peaks are scattered and the logits are mixed, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mid-word piece continuation, scattered

result.description: Fires on the word " data" (also "information", "datasets") as the object of processing or analysis, e.g. "analyze numerical and unstructured data". Silent in "big data" and "data-driven" compounds.
result.label: ' data' as analyzed object

result.description: Fires on ' audio' and on pieces of 'auditory' (aud-itory, auditor-ial), plus 'acoustic', mostly where the word modifies a following noun (audio-visual, auditory engagement). Predicts words like stimuli, experiences, inputs, elements.
result.label: audio / auditory modifier word

result.description: Fires on the 'ent' piece completing "underwent" (also 'un-pre' of "unprecedented"), typically in "X underwent a significant transformation". Silent on 'ent' in other words like "prevalent".
result.label: 'ent' in "underwent"

result.description: Fires on separators (comma, "and", "or", slash) after a named item in an example list of proper names (methods, tools, auction houses, artists), as in "such as Otsu and ...". Predicts another name next. Silent on commas after common phrases.
result.label: Separator after listed example names

result.description: Fires on the word after "professional" (boundaries, settings, and, in, roles) in text about professional conduct and communication. It predicts "professional"-type continuations. It stays quiet on "and" in general communication text without "professional" before it.
result.label: Word after "professional" in conduct text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'id' inside longer words, mainly 'mer-id-ian' (prime meridian), also Dravidian, Procyonidae, subsidies. Mostly a mid-word 'id' piece; a few weak hits on other word fragments.
result.label: 'id' piece in meridian-type words

result.description: Fires on the token " ensemble" in both music (orchestra, chamber groups) and statistical-mechanics senses. Members are mostly ensemble/orchestra detectors. Its logits favor " cast" and similar group words.
result.label: ' ensemble' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ical' in "Biomedical" at the start of a document or title (also 'ot' in "Robotics"). It stays silent on 'ical' in Mechanical, Spherical, Lexical and Statistical, so it seems tied to this particular word.
result.label: Biomedical 'ical' / Robotics 'ot' pieces

result.description: Fires on ' Great' as part of a proper name or historical term, such as "the Great Depression", "the Great War", "Great Lakes" or "Sejong the Great". Predicts continuations like War, Britain or Fire. Members mostly detect ' Great' and similar name-leading words.
result.label: ' Great' in proper names

result.description: Fires on the 'est' piece in "celestial" (also weakly on ' plan'/' planet' in astronomy text), predicting the continuation 'ial'. Silent on 'est' in "aesthetic", so it needs the cel- prefix context.
result.label: 'est' in "celestial"

result.description: Fires on ' in' (sometimes ' on') right after a verb and its object in cooking or process instructions, introducing the medium or container, such as cooking food in boiling water or cooling in ice water. It stays silent on 'in' after nouns or inside words.
result.label: 'in' after verb+object, cooking medium

result.description: Fires on word pieces in physics text that precede Einstein-related or relativity/kinetic terms, such as ' Albert' before Einstein, ' kin' in kinetic, ' relativ', and ' Lor' in Lorentz. It predicts ' Ein' next.
result.label: Albert/kin- in relativity physics

result.description: Fires mostly on fragments of multi-byte or corrupted characters (replacement-character tokens in CJK or Arabic text) and on scattered tokens like ' solutions' and 'ives'. The peaks are mixed and the circuit's own evidence is weak.
result.label: Broken multibyte character fragments

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ro' in the middle of a longer word, such as brushst-ro-kes, spect-ro-scopy, ward-ro-bes, tight-ro-pe. It predicts a continuation piece like 'kes' or 'scop'.
result.label: 'ro' mid-word piece

result.description: Fires on ' with' directly after a noun (theater with, zones with, Latin with) where it introduces a descriptive attribute phrase. Silent when 'with' follows a verb or adjective as in 'affiliated with', 'interact with', 'replacing ... with'.
result.label: noun-modifying 'with'

result.description: Fires on the token ' distribution' as a noun for how things are spread (species, electrons, products), mostly after "the". It is silent when the word starts a text with no preceding context. It pushes toward ' pattern(s)'.
result.label: ' distribution' noun after determiner

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied noun-ending word pieces and nouns in expository or academic text (e.g. 'ulation', 'recovery', 'environmental', 'ures'). The peaks share no single token or construction, and the circuit looks diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse academic noun-ending pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' conclus' (start of "conclusions"/"conclusive"), mostly after words like "conclusive", "unbiased", "validity of" in scientific or reasoning text. Predicts suffixes like -ions and -ive.
result.label: ' conclus' word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'avel' in 'wavelength(s)', after the 'w' start of the word. It predicts 'ength' next. It stays silent when 'avel' begins the text with no preceding 'w'.
result.label: 'avel' in wavelength

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ings'/'ation' completing error words like misunderstandings or misinterpretation, and occasionally 'and' after confusion, in text about cross-cultural communication problems. Silent on 'ings' in 'meanings'.
result.label: Misunderstand-ings suffix in communication errors

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' st' when it begins a split word, mostly 'stakeholders' after words like "various", "all", "among". Silent when ' st' starts the document or is part of other words like 'striving'.
result.label: ' st' starting 'stakeholder'

result.description: Fires on the dash (en dash, hyphen, or space/"to") separating the start year from the end year in a year range, typically birth–death dates in parentheses, right before the second year's digits (e.g. "1902–191").
result.label: Dash inside year ranges

result.description: Fires on a comma ending a clause or list item in descriptions of processes or methods (risk assessment, project planning). It is silent on commas inside plain noun lists. Predicts continuations like "which", "then", "followed".
result.label: Comma after process-step clause

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ous' completing "hazardous", mostly before nouns like chemicals, waste, materials. Silent on 'ous' in other words such as poisonous and mountainous. Predicts material/waste/zone nouns next.
result.label: hazard-ous suffix

result.description: Fires on the possessive/object pronoun " her" (and "Her"), especially in biographical text about a woman, before a noun like her creations, dishes or contributions. Members are mostly "her" detectors.
result.label: Pronoun " her" in biographies

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' soci' at the start of words like societies, societal, sociolinguistics, sociology. Members are mostly ' soci' detectors. The next-token logits favour completions such as 'etal' and 'eties'.
result.label: ' soci' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word stems ' maxim' and ' minim' (as in maximize/minimize) when a verb is expected, pushing toward the '-ize' suffix. Weakly fires on similar verb stems like 'fort' (fortify) and 'stabil'.
result.label: maxim-/minim- verb stem before -ize

result.description: Fires in text about tree data structures (binary trees, BST) on words like "data", "efficient", "-based", "-like" that precede a structure noun. Predicts tree/node/leaf/indexing. Silent on "data" in generic data-quality contexts.
result.label: Tree data-structure modifier words

result.description: Fires on the token ' design' (also the start of 'designing'/'designers') as a noun or verb, often after "the" or a field word, as in "the design of experiments". It predicts suffix pieces like 'ate'/'ations'. It was silent on one "packaging design" example.
result.label: ' design' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'anc' in "advancements" (also "enhancements"), predicting the suffix "ements". Mostly in technology/society passages; one contrast case of "advancements" in a history context was silent.
result.label: 'anc' in advancements

result.description: Fires on the word ' context', mainly after "the" in phrases like "in the context of". It is silent when 'context' follows "between" or "linguistic". Upstream members are mostly ' context' detectors.
result.label: ' context' after "the"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' govern' (stem of governance, governments, govern), mostly when the next piece completes it as 'ance' or 'ments'. Predicts those suffixes. The silent contrast text lacks the token.
result.label: ' govern' stem before -ance/-ments

result.description: Fires on the word " original" used as an adjective after a determiner or possessive (the original language, your original content), meaning the first or source version. It predicts nouns like source, author, text.
result.label: " original" as adjective

result.description: Fires on the last token of a science or philosophy topic noun (atom, magnetism, gases, perception) inside a "X's Law/Model of [topic]" phrase naming a scientist's work. It predicts verbs like laid, established, introduced. Silent on the same suffixes in other contexts.
result.label: Topic noun ending a named-theory phrase

result.description: Fires on the word piece " chem" when it begins "chemistry", especially after "analytical", "computational" or "atmospheric". It stays silent when the piece leads into "chemist(s)", as in "enabled chemists" or "Russian-Italian chemist".
result.label: chem- in "chemistry" after field adjective

result.description: Fires on the word-final piece 'us' in 'Celsius' (also weakly on endings like -at, -as, -ds, -ation, -ium), in science/heat-and-temperature text. Upstream members include heat/cooking/temperature detectors and 'us' detectors.
result.label: Celsius word-ending 'us' piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece " out" when it begins a compound word split across tokens, such as "out|comes", "out|break" or "out|look". It is strongest in "healthcare outcomes". It predicts continuations like "comes", "look" and "break".
result.label: " out" as start of outcomes/outbreak

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Tem" (capitalized, as in Temperature or Temporal) in titles and sentence starts of technical text. It is silent on lowercase "temporal" mid-sentence. Predicts continuations like "por" and "per".
result.label: Capitalized ' Tem' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word ' tasks' (occasionally ' operations' or ' duties') when it is the object of performing, assigning or organizing work, often after an adjective like routine or complex. Predicts continuations like 'performed' or 'efficiently'.
result.label: ' tasks' as work items

result.description: Fires on the word " designed", mostly in passive "X are designed to..." after a plural or instrument noun, and predicts "to" or "specifically". Members are mainly earlier " designed" detectors plus similar passive participles.
result.label: ' designed' in "are designed to"

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' govern' / ' Govern' as the start of words like governance or governments, predicting suffixes such as 'ance', 'ments', 'ed'. Members are mostly detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' govern' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on digit tokens (9, 8, 6, 7) in approximate numeric quantities such as "around 70%", "approximately 299,7…", "75°F", mostly in science text. Silent on a digit inside a year like 1905.
result.label: Digits in approximate measurements

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verb pieces (to, of, -ining, -ving, tips, guidance) in expository or technical text where a verb or noun is about to take an object or complement. Weak, mixed evidence; silent on purpose-clause "to".
result.label: Function words before objects, technical prose

result.description: Fires on the piece 'p' right after a hyphen in "fast-paced" (and weakly "high-priority", "high-pitched"), where the word continues with "aced". It predicts continuations like 'ac', 'read'.
result.label: 'p' in fast-paced

result.description: Fires on quality adjectives or adjective pieces (proper, effective, -ive, -ful, efficient) that precede a noun in writing about communication, predicting nouns like use, usage, consideration. Silent when "proper" starts the document.
result.label: Quality adjectives before a noun

result.description: Fires on connectors (' and', ' to', ' or', ' through', '-') right after a decade expression like "the 1990s", where a range continues ("and into the early…", "to the early…"). Silent on 'and' joining ordinary nouns or clauses.
result.label: Connector after decade in time range

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ent' in the word "patent" (pat|ent), including "patentable", in intellectual property text. It stays silent on 'ent' in other words such as "intelligent". Weak activation on a few other word pieces.
result.label: 'ent' in pat-ent

result.description: Fires on the word piece " challeng" when it is a noun stem expecting "-es", after a quantity or adjective like "significant", "unique" or "several". It stays silent when the next piece is "-ing" (it is challenging) or when "challenges" starts a sentence.
result.label: noun "challeng(es)" after adjective

result.description: Fires on the word ' particular' (including in 'in particular' and before suffixes like -ity or -s) in mid-sentence, especially in abstract or philosophical text. It stays silent when the word starts the text. Members are detectors of particular, specific, certain and unique.
result.label: ' particular' word detector

result.description: Fires on word stems that are incomplete and need a suffix such as -y, -iness or -ing (' breath', 'itt', ' color', ' dress'), in essay-style prose. It predicts suffix pieces like 'y', 'iness' and 'ty'. The peaks are mixed and activation is weak.
result.label: Word stems awaiting suffix (breath, itt)

result.description: Fires on commas, slashes, or "or" after a demographic category like race, age or gender in a list of social categories. It predicts the next category, such as religion, race or sexual. Other lists of abstract nouns stay silent.
result.label: Demographic category list separators

result.description: Fires on plural place nouns like towns, cities, streets, homes, mostly in urbanization or industrialization text. It predicts words like "folk", "filled" or "built". The contrast is abstract digital/personal text, where it stays silent.
result.label: Plural settlement nouns in urban text

result.description: Fires on the verb ' find' (also finding/finds), most strongly in math or procedural instructions like "first find the mean". It fires more weakly on noun uses like "findings". It predicts continuations such as "out" and "ings".
result.label: ' find' verb in procedures

result.description: Fires on the token ' bread' in every example, including compounds like bread-making, bread knife and bread makers. It weakly fires on food words like dough and pizza. It predicts word continuations such as 'th' or ' mak'.
result.label: ' bread' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token ' sight' in "sight-reading" in music-learning text, predicting a continuation of the compound word. Members are mostly detectors of ' sight' and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: ' sight' in sight-reading

result.description: Fires on ' more' used as a comparative determiner/modifier directly before a noun or adjective (after "for", "to", "of", "by", "in"), as in "need for more straightforward". It stays silent on ' more' after linking verbs like "became/be/are".
result.label: ' more' as noun-phrase comparative

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'enc' in "stencil" and 'ir' in "aspirations", "chirp" and "Stirling", plus occasional divider dashes. The next token is a word continuation. Mostly word-piece detectors.
result.label: Mid-word pieces 'enc'/'ir' (stencil, aspirations)

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ic' completing "Magnetic" (e.g. "Magnetic Fields" headings), after the pieces Magnet/Mag. It stays silent on 'ic' in other words like physicists, athletic, economic. Predicts magnetism-related nouns.
result.label: 'ic' completing "Magnetic"

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' Me', 'mm', ' tre' that begin a word whose continuation is likely 'asures'/'asure' (Measures, treasures), also Meissner, dilemmas. Predicts 'as...' continuations.
result.label: Me- fragment predicting 'asures'

result.description: Fires on "pect" in "Respect" (and " respect") meaning esteem, as in "Respect for human dignity"; stays silent on "pect" inside "perspectives". Predicts suffixes like -ful/-fully.
result.label: Respect (pect) as esteem

result.description: Fires on the word " combined" used as a participle, usually after a noun phrase and a comma ("factors, combined with…"). It predicts "with" or "together" next. Members are mostly detectors of combine/combined/blended.
result.label: ' combined' participle before 'with'

result.description: Fires on a mid-acronym or mid-word capital letter piece (G in MGFs, T, AT, ER) right after an initial capital like M, in technical acronyms; predicts further uppercase/name-like continuations. Silent in plain name lists.
result.label: Mid-acronym capital letter piece

result.description: Fires on a comma right after a short name or list item, such as a surname in "Surname, Given name" catalog entries or an item in a list of nouns. It is silent on commas that follow a clause and introduce a participial phrase.
result.label: Comma after name or list item

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' comprom' (compromise/compromising) before a suffix like -ise/-ising. Members are mostly detectors of ' comprom' and similar word-start fragments (diplom, resol, stabil, synchron) that predict suffixes.
result.label: ' comprom' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word " why" introducing a subordinate clause after verbs like understand, explain, explore, or "reasons"/"is why". It predicts the clause subject (certain, some, we, they).
result.label: " why" after explain/understand

result.description: Fires on the word "zones" (or "zone"), most strongly in climate-zone text such as polar or climatic zones. Earlier-layer members detect "zone(s)" and similar words like regions and areas.
result.label: "zones" token in climate text

result.description: Fires on the decade digit (mostly 9, also 8) in "late/mid 19X0s" phrases, such as "late 1990s". It stays silent on the 9 in years like 1920s, 1970s or 2009, so it needs the late/mid-decade construction.
result.label: Decade digit after "late/mid 19"

result.description: Fires on word-initial or mid-word fragments that need a continuation, mostly ' prospect' (prospect theory, prospects), also 'uct' in infrastructure, ' divis', ' conject'. Predicts suffix pieces like 'inals' or 'ican'.
result.label: Incomplete word fragments, mainly 'prospect'

result.description: Fires on function words (" the", " from", " of", " occurred") in descriptions of geological eras and periods (Cenozoic, Paleogene, Eocene), especially before dates or the next era name. Silent on " the" in other historical or general contexts.
result.label: Function words in geological era text

result.description: Fires on a standalone space token right before a century or year number, mainly after "15th and", "16th and", "17th and" in century ranges, where the next token is a number starting with 1. Silent on the space after "The" or "early".
result.label: Space before second century in range

result.description: Fires on the contrast pivot after a "not just/not simply X" clause: " but", " rather", "it's", or ";" it, where the second half says what something really is. Silent on ordinary "but" clauses.
result.label: Not just X, but rather Y pivot

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' st' when it starts a split word, mostly the 'st' of "stakeholder" after "strategic" or "stake", and also in "Stellar" and "strive". It predicts continuations like 'ake', 'riv' and 'ems'.
result.label: ' st' word-start piece (stakeholder)

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' r' when it begins a longer word, mostly "rhetoric/rhetorical", also "ratios" and "rasa". Predicts continuation pieces like 'het'. Silent when the word is not split after ' r'.
result.label: ' r' start of "rhetoric"

result.description: Fires on the 's' of "let's" (contraction of "let us"), predicting a verb like examine, say, take or consider. Stays silent on 's' in "it's" or other possessive/contracted forms. Also fires on long dash divider lines.
result.label: let's contraction 's'

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative " these" as a determiner before a plural noun, mostly after a verb or preposition (monitor these, in light of these). Members are mostly detectors of "these" and "this". It predicts a following plural noun.
result.label: demonstrative " these" before plural noun

result.description: Fires on the token piece "oga" completing the word "Yoga" (Karma Yoga, Jnana Yoga, Purpose of Yoga), in text about Indian philosophy. Members are mostly "oga" detectors plus Buddhism/Hindu-term members.
result.label: "oga" in Yoga

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' th' when it is the first fragment of a split word like thrive, therapeutic, thesis, theme, thistle. It pushes toward continuations such as 'rive', 'era', 'riv'.
result.label: ' th' split-word start (thrive, therapy)

result.description: Fires on ' from' that opens a range or transition ("vary from X to Y", "change from", "ranges from", "spans from"), expecting a following "to". Silent on source/origin uses like "comes from" or "radiation from the atmosphere".
result.label: 'from' starting a range

result.description: Fires on the 's' piece inside a split scientific word, mostly "electroly|s|is", where it predicts the suffix "is". It stays silent on plural 's' after acronyms like LEDs or OLEDs.
result.label: 's' inside electrolysis-type words

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ert' inside longer words, mainly "Inertia"/"inertial", also "exerted", "entertained", "Hertwig". Members are mostly 'ert' token detectors.
result.label: 'ert' piece in inertia

result.description: Fires on plural policy-type nouns (initiatives, strategies, measures, practices, policies) that end a noun phrase in sustainability or management text, often as a subject before a verb like "must" or "can". Silent on some "strategies" in other phrasing.
result.label: Plural strategy/measure nouns as subject

result.description: Fires on ' Otto' (Otto Cycle) and the 'antine' piece of 'Byzantine', plus occasional name fragments. Two specific word pieces, supported by members detecting 'antine' and medieval/historical context.
result.label: Otto and Byzantine word pieces

result.description: Fires on the token piece 'AP' inside capitalized acronyms such as CAPM, CAPT, SAP and APO, mostly in finance or business text. Upstream members are mainly 'AP' token detectors.
result.label: 'AP' in acronyms (CAPM, SAP)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' li' when it begins a longer word such as lipoproteins, lipid, likened or liabilities. Members are mostly ' li' detectors, with a few for other word-start pieces.
result.label: ' li' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece " post" when it begins a longer word or compound (posture, postulate, post-processing), predicting a continuation like "ure" or "mod". It stays silent on unrelated text.
result.label: ' post' as word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' pot' when it starts a longer word such as potatoes, pottery or potency, and pushes towards continuations like 'atoes', 'tery' and 'ato'. It stays silent on ordinary cooking text without this piece.
result.label: ' pot' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ins' when it is a word-initial fragment after a preceding word, mostly starting "insurance" (also insights, insufficient, inscribed). It is silent when ' ins' begins the text, with no preceding word.
result.label: ' ins' fragment mid-text (insurance)

result.description: Fires on determiners, possessives or modifier pieces right after "align(ed/ing) with" (e.g. "with the", "with their", "company's"), where the next word would be goals, objectives or interests. Silent on "the" elsewhere.
result.label: Object slot after "align with"

result.description: Fires on a comma that follows a completed sentence, right after a period, where a new clause starts in lowercase. Stays silent on ordinary mid-sentence commas after clauses or phrases.
result.label: Comma right after sentence-ending period

result.description: Fires on plural nouns for people or things (words, people, stories, individuals) right after "the" or "and the" in a coordinated noun phrase. Predicts "themselves/involved". Silent on "words" after adjectives or prepositions like "in other words".
result.label: Plural noun after "the" (people/things)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' met' when it begins a longer word like metallic, metaphor, metabolic or metamorphosis. It predicts continuations such as 'aph', 'abol' and 'icul'.
result.label: ' met' as word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word " two", most strongly in "X and Y are two distinct/fundamental…" statements introducing a pair of things. Weaker on "There are two main types" and on "three".
result.label: ' two' in "X and Y are two"
