challenges (verb) + traditional norms
result.description: Fires on the suffix 'es' (sometimes 'ing') of the verb "challenges" when a subject challenges conventions or traditional forms. Stays silent on the noun "challenges" (difficulties) and on other -es verbs. Predicts 'conventional/traditional'.

Fires on commas, "and", or "like" after a method or analysis type inside a list of research or analysis methods (e.g. "methods include qualitative content analysis, ..."). It predicts further method nouns such as analysis, reviews, regression. Silent on commas in general prose.
result.label: List separators in analysis-method lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment " ro" (also " rob", " reci", " migr") in the middle of a split word, mainly before "ast"/"cket" (roast, rocket). Needs a preceding word, not word-initial "roasting". Predicts word continuations like "pes", "ots", "cket".
result.label: " ro" word-start fragment before continuation

result.description: Fires on the word " research" (also "Research"), mostly as a subject noun or before "ers"/"efforts" in technology or science prose. It pushes toward "ers" as the next piece. It stays silent when "research" is the first token of the text.
result.label: ' research' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token " ever", mainly in the "ever-" prefix construction ("an ever-changing", "ever-expanding"), and more weakly in "than ever" or "Will X ever". Members are mostly " ever" detectors.
result.label: "ever" in ever-changing

result.description: Fires on a domain noun ending a compound topic phrase (pottery-making, music production, naval architecture, industry) after "a turning point/breakthrough in the history of X", just before a verb like "occurred" or "marked". Silent in "smaller-scale production processes".
result.label: Field noun after "turning point in"

result.description: Fires on abstract nouns ending a noun phrase about availability or latitude (flexibility, support, freedom, resources, investment), often after "little", "more", or "lack of". Logits favor "than", "available", "due", "compared".
result.label: Abstract nouns of flexibility/support/resources

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' kn' (as in knot) and ' erg' (as in ergonomic), plus a few other word-starting pieces. Predicts continuations completing the word (e.g. 'ot', 'onomic'-like suffixes). Mostly seen in technical, abstract text.
result.label: kn- / erg- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on word endings (-es, -ements, -acy, -ement) completing achievement/success nouns like "successes", "achievements", "supremacy". Silent on -es in unrelated words like "poses" or "businesses". Members detect success/achievement stems.
result.label: Suffix of success/achievement nouns

result.description: Fires on the word "language"/"Language", strongest when it starts a new line in a list of linguistics topic headings (e.g. "Language Testing", "Language Policy"). Silent on mid-sentence uses like "second language" or "diverse language types".
result.label: Language as topic-heading start

result.description: Fires on ' using' and ' installing' (also ' applying') when they introduce a method or means, as in "using precise language". Silent when ' using' follows "by" or "application". Predicts method-like nouns such as frameworks, methods and approaches.
result.label: ' using' / ' installing' method gerund

result.description: Fires on ' all' right after the article "an" when it starts a hyphenated compound like "all-out", "all-hands", "all-encompassing". It stays silent on ' all' as a quantifier or inside words like "allure".
result.label: "an all-" compound opener

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (that, a, of, match, postulates, linking) that introduce a described relation or object in explanatory, technical prose. Peaks are scattered and the contrast is not clearly separable, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Function words in explanatory technical prose

result.description: Fires on the word pieces inside geological epoch names, mainly "ene" and "ist" in Pleistocene, in earth-history and geology text. It also fires weakly on other mid-word pieces such as "ol" in Decolonization.
result.label: Pleistocene word pieces

result.description: Fires on a bare 'v' token that begins a word split into pieces (vapses, vagab, vaude, vader), and weakly on other word-start fragments like ' o', ' pe', ' inst'. Predicts continuations such as 'ague', 'antage'.
result.label: Word-initial 'v' fragment

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "absence" or "lack" (absence of, lack of), anticipating a negated thing. Silent on ' of' after other nouns like "problem of" or "nature of".
result.label: ' of' after absence/lack

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'aph' inside split words, mostly "met|aph|ors" and also "An|aph|ase" and "met|aph|ysics". Upstream members are mostly 'aph' detectors. Logits favor suffix pieces like 'ent' and 'rable'.
result.label: 'aph' piece in metaphor

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' w' (a space-prefixed 'w' that starts a split word), mostly in economics text before 'ages'/'age' (wage), and also before welfare, wavelength, wool. It pushes towards continuations like 'ages', 'elf', 'oven'.
result.label: word-initial ' w' fragment (wage)

result.description: Fires on word pieces in transportation-related text ("ation" in transportation, "ways" in roadways, " transport", " roads"), predicting infrastructure/route continuations. Silent on "ation" in unrelated words like legislation or automation.
result.label: Transportation infrastructure word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece "rom" inside "aromatic"/"aroma" (after "a"), also in "achromatic". Members mostly detect "rom" in these words. Weak activation on other mid-word pieces.
result.label: "rom" in aroma/aromatic

result.description: Fires on ' tax' (and sometimes ' and') in "government spending and tax(ation)" within fiscal-policy text, where a tax term is expected to follow spending. Silent on ' tax' as a modifier or in other constructions.
result.label: Spending-and-tax in fiscal policy

result.description: Fires on ' hair' and ' radiation' as a modifier noun in safety/protection contexts (hair restraint, radiation shielding), predicting protection-related words. Members include safety, hygiene and radiation detectors.
result.label: hair/radiation as safety modifier

result.description: Fires on adjectival suffix pieces like 'istic' (mostly in "linguistic"), also 'ological', 'ative', after academic/social-science stems, predicting nouns like identity/expression. Silent on some 'linguistic' cases, so the extra condition is unclear.
result.label: Adjective suffix 'istic' in linguistic

result.description: Fires on the nouns " titles" and " status" (also " title", " value") in discussion of social rank, honorifics, capitalization of job titles, and prestige. Members include detectors of " titles" and " status" (as in "status quo") and prestige-related tokens.
result.label: titles / status nouns

result.description: Fires on the opening parenthesis ' (' after a technical or scientific term (e.g. nitrogen, plant hormones, particulate matter), where an abbreviation, symbol or clarification follows. It stays silent when the term is in a plain list without a parenthesis.
result.label: Parenthesis after technical term

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' prof' (as in proficiency, profits, profound) when it is a split-off beginning of a longer word. Windows mostly show 'language prof|iciency'. It predicts word continuations such as 'essions' and 'ic'.
result.label: ' prof' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the final piece of abstract nouns, mostly plural or suffix endings (-ities, -ation, halls, periods, landscape, intervals) in academic prose. Silent on the contraction 's (it's, muse's). Peaks are mixed and weakly consistent.
result.label: Abstract noun endings in academic prose

result.description: Fires on plural computer-science nouns, mostly " algorithms" and also "structures", "problems", "procedures", after a modifier like "genetic", "recursive", "efficient". Members detect algorithm tokens. Logits push toward optimization and efficiency words.
result.label: Algorithms and CS plural nouns

result.description: Fires on the token " Berlin", mostly in Cold War history contexts (Berlin Wall, Berlin Blockade, holdings in Berlin). Many members detect Berlin itself. Weak activation on " air" and " Napoleon".
result.label: Berlin token (Cold War contexts)

result.description: Fires on the token ' do' (also ' did') when it is a word-start fragment of a longer word, such as 'dopamine', 'doping', 'dozens' or 'didactic', not the auxiliary verb. Predicts continuations like 'z', 'ctr', 'actic'.
result.label: ' do' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the 'R' in the abbreviation "VR" (virtual reality), mostly right after "V". It also fires weakly on related virtual-reality words like "graphics" and "simulations". Upstream members detect AR/VR/reality/immersive terms.
result.label: VR abbreviation 'R' token

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ular' when it completes "cellular" (also intracellular), as in "cellular functions/responses". It is silent on 'ular' at the start of a document with no "cell" before it.
result.label: 'ular' in "cellular"

result.description: Fires on ' into' after verbs of digging, delving, diving, falling or wandering (delving into, diving into, digging into), where into means entering a topic or space. Silent on ' into' meaning transformation or conversion (turning X into Y, break down into categories).
result.label: ' into' after delving/diving verbs

result.description: Fires on the abstract noun (' aspect', ' part', ' component') right after an adjective like fundamental, integral, vital or key, in the phrase "a fundamental aspect of X". It expects "of" next.
result.label: aspect/part after "fundamental/integral"

result.description: Fires in lists or pairs of contrasting aspects (advantages and dis-, strengths and weak-, benefits and costs) at the point where a negative counterpart such as disadvantages, weaknesses, limitations or challenges is expected next.
result.label: Predicts disadvantages/weaknesses after positives

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " ins" that begins longer words like inscribed, insights, insurance and insulators. Predicts continuations such as "ights", "pection" and "u". Silent on text without this piece.
result.label: " ins" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on ' must' (also ' to' after "essential/important") in advice-style sentences like "To do X well, one must...", right before a verb of skill or requirement. Silent on 'must' after a specific subject in plain statements.
result.label: Generic 'one must' in how-to advice

result.description: Fires on a capital letter (mostly D, also B, N, MA) inside an uppercase acronym being spelled out, such as GDPR, DAC, MAC, SSD or R&D. It mostly predicts the acronym's next letters, such as 'PR'.
result.label: Acronym letters, especially D

result.description: Fires on the word " deep"/" Deep" (as in deep learning, deep connections, deepening), with weaker firing on "ep" in "steeped". Predicts continuations like -ening/-ened. Members are mostly earlier "deep" detectors.
result.label: deep token detector

result.description: Fires on technical process nouns (reduction, identification, extraction, purification, conservation) ending a compound in technical/engineering text, where a noun like "strategies/techniques/methods" often follows. Silent on verb forms like "reduce/reducing".
result.label: Technical process nouns like reduction

result.description: Fires on 'point' completing the word "counterpoint" in music-theory text. Upstream members are music-related (scales, instruments, composers) plus a 'point' token detector. Weak activation on other word-final pieces.
result.label: counter|point in music text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens about origin or derivation (' derived', ' translated', 'etched', 'deriving', ' Mit' pieces) in historical or cultural prose. Logits favor ' as' and quote marks. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Derived/translated origin words, mixed

result.description: Fires on ' a' (occasionally ' an') right after a document-opening "In", as in "In a schoolyard setting…". Silent on ' a' elsewhere, such as after verbs or inside words like "akin".
result.label: "In a" at document start

result.description: Fires on the plural noun ending of a person or group noun (songwriters, designers, businesses, teams) that is the object of "help/helping", right before a verb like understand or achieve. Silent on the same plural as subject or after other words.
result.label: Plural agent noun after "help"

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ored' (also 'ined') in passive "X is explored/examined in detail/this section" sentences, where a topic is being covered. It pushes toward words like topics, fields, areas, separately.
result.label: passive 'explored/examined' in scope statements

result.description: Fires on ' drum' (and ' hip' in hip hop) in music text, often as a word-start before a suffix like -mer, -ming, -head. Silent on general music prose without these words. Members are music-genre and instrument detectors.
result.label: drum / hip in music contexts

result.description: Fires on the word " advanced" / " Advanced" used as an adjective before a noun (advanced level, advanced topics, advanced technology). Pushes towards nouns like topics, levels, versions, stages. Members are mostly "advanced" token detectors.
result.label: Adjective "advanced" before noun

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments inside particular words: 'id' in humidity, 'fert'/'il' in fertile/fertilizer/fertilization, weakly 'explos' in explosion. It predicts suffixes like -ification, -ity.
result.label: hum-id-ity / fert-ilizer word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word " associated", most strongly in noun phrases like "their associated X" or "the associated Y" in technical or scientific text. It is weaker in "risks associated with". The circuit is built from upstream " associated" detectors.
result.label: ' associated' before a noun

result.description: Fires on the piece 'i' inside the word "idioms" (Id|i|oms), right after "Id", in headings like "Idioms in Media". Silent on 'i' in other words such as "hyperblemi".
result.label: 'i' inside "Idioms"

result.description: Fires on word-ending suffix pieces like -ization, -ologies, -ies, -cies completing abstract plural or noun forms, mostly in energy/engineering text ("energy utilization strategies", "conversion technologies"). Silent on "ionization" in a chemistry-like context.
result.label: Abstract noun suffixes in energy text

result.description: Fires on articles (' a', ' the', ' an') right after a verb like "provide", "forms", "embodying" in expository science or technical text, where an evaluative noun such as "cornerstone" or "fundamental" is expected. Silent on articles after prepositions or "but".
result.label: Article after descriptive verb, expository

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ont" inside "sp-ont-aneous" (and "spontaneity"), predicting "aneous". It is silent when "ont" starts the text without the "sp" before it.
result.label: "ont" in "spontaneous"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'est' when it sits inside a longer word, such as A-est-hetic, Under-est-imation, cel-est-ial or liv-est-ock. It is silent on ordinary text without that piece. It pushes toward continuations like 'het', 'imation' and 'ock'.
result.label: 'est' mid-word fragment

result.description: Fires on the articles ' a' / ' an' right after "marked by", "characterized by", "galvanized by" or similar verbs, where an abstract noun like shift, growth or focus comes next. Silent on "as an" and "within an".
result.label: Article after "marked by" (abstract change)

result.description: Fires on the adverb " essentially", most strongly right after "plays" (plays essentially a role). Weaker after "forming" or "becoming". Members are mostly detectors of "essentially" and similar hedges (merely, exactly, literally, almost).
result.label: ' essentially' after "plays"

result.description: Fires on the token ' switch', mostly in networking text such as "network switches", and also as a verb ("networks that switch"). Members are mostly ' switch' detectors; the contrast text is silent on networking passages without the word.
result.label: ' switch' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' Rock'/' rock' (also ' classical') when it names a music genre, in passages about music styles. Quiet on general music text without the genre word. Members detect other genre words like metal, punk, jazz, folk.
result.label: Rock music genre word

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after "throughout" (also weakly "around/across"), where a span noun like entire, day, year, lifetime is expected next. Silent on ' the' after ordinary verbs like reduce or overseeing.
result.label: 'the' after throughout/across

result.description: Fires on the verb or adverb (are, is, be, were, remains, still) right after a subject like "differences", "disparities" or "gap". It predicts a predicate such as "apparent", "stark" or "between". Silent on "are" after other kinds of subjects.
result.label: Copula after differences/gaps subject

result.description: Fires on ' arguments' / ' argument' as a noun in discussions of persuasion, logic and reasoning, after modifiers like compelling, persuasive or logical. Silent when the word starts the text with no preceding context.
result.label: argument(s) in reasoning text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cru' as the start of "crucial", mostly after "play a" or "is/be", and predicts the continuation "cial". The contrast shows no ' cru' example.
result.label: ' cru' start of "crucial"

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after foundational nouns like foundation, basis, bedrock, cornerstone, building blocks, as in "the foundation of X". Silent on ' of' after other nouns such as art, act, purpose. Predicts positive modifiers like "any", "successful", "effective".
result.label: ' of' after foundation/basis nouns

result.description: Fires on the piece "al" completing the word "peripheral" (peripher|al), after the "peripher" fragment. It stays silent on "al" in other words such as instrumental, ribosomal or isochronal.
result.label: "al" in "peripheral"

result.description: Fires on " of" right after nouns meaning a constituent or part (components, elements, constituents, building blocks, part) of something. It stays silent on " of" after other nouns such as operation, characteristics, limitations or realm.
result.label: "of" after component/element nouns

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (commas, 'ization', 'AD', 'ate', '(') in abstract academic or philosophical prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast also contains commas, so the evidence for a specific trigger is thin.
result.label: Scattered tokens in abstract academic prose

result.description: Fires on the first or middle piece of a rare proper name split into word pieces (Z, Zaris-ki, Rob-bins, Arc-angelo), mostly in lists of names. It pushes toward continuation pieces like 'O', 'har', 'jo'. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Rare name fragment, Z-initial

result.description: Fires on the word piece "predict" in the middle of words like unpredictable, unpredictability and predictor, with weaker firing on "comp" in "encompass". Mostly the piece before a suffix such as -able or -ability.
result.label: "predict" word piece mid-word

result.description: Fires mainly on the suffix "ography" in "photography", and more weakly on " photograph", " camera" and "photographic". It fires in photography-themed text. It is silent on other 3D-imaging text in the contrast.
result.label: photography word endings and camera terms

result.description: Fires on a few unrelated tokens, mostly " since" and " rest" (also " Kind", " as") in academic or encyclopedic text. Members detect "since" and "rest" tokens. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so this looks like a loose token set.
result.label: Since / rest token mix

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' cer' (as in ceramic/ceramics) when it begins a longer word, mostly in materials and art text. Members are mainly detectors of ' cer' and similar word-start fragments like poly, mus, Gla.
result.label: ' cer' start of ceramic

result.description: Fires on the word right after "until" (the, a, they, it, at, much), i.e. the start of the clause or noun phrase giving the endpoint. It pushes toward words like arrived, reached, moment, conditions.
result.label: Word following "until"

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments inside long, rare academic words (De-ception, anis-otrop-ic, Ali-en-ation, per-ception-al), mostly 'err', 'ception', 'cept', 'ement', where the word is still incomplete. Weak on other pieces.
result.label: Mid-word pieces of rare academic words

result.description: Fires on the word "food"/"Food", strongest on repeated "Food and X" headings and on food in regulatory or sustainability phrases. Predicts follow-ons like security, service, handling. Members are mostly food-token detectors.
result.label: food token detector

result.description: Fires on plural nouns (e.g. industries, countries, authors) that directly follow "various" or "different", ending a category-plural noun phrase. Silent in text without that quantifier-plural construction.
result.label: Plural noun after "various/different"

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'avel' in "wavelength" (and 'cart' in "Descartes"), a word fragment before the rest of the word; predicts continuation like 'ength'. Silent when 'avel' starts the text.
result.label: 'avel' in wavelength / 'cart' in Descartes

result.description: Fires on a period that ends a short title-like heading or name line (e.g. "Resource Allocation Session.", "Engineering.") followed by a paragraph break. It stays silent on periods inside abbreviations or mid-sentence.
result.label: Period ending short heading line

result.description: Fires on hyphen, double-hyphen and em-dash tokens used as standalone dashes, especially in runs of dashes or number lists (-2 -3 -4) and dash separators. Silent on hyphens inside words or quoted word pieces.
result.label: Standalone dash and hyphen runs

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' divers' mid-sentence, before it is completed as "diversity" or "diversification". It is silent when ' divers' starts the text. It pushes the next token toward -ity, -ification, -ify.
result.label: ' divers' word-piece before -ity

result.description: Fires on the last digit of a year (often the third or fourth digit, e.g. 1987, 1918, 703) in historical or scientific dates. It stays silent on earlier digits such as the 8 in 1860s or 1980.
result.label: Final digit of a year

result.description: Fires mainly on "akes" in "high-stakes" (also "stakes" in other uses), with weaker firing on "place", "maintained", "made" after passive/verb constructions. Mostly a "stakes" piece detector with a mixed tail.
result.label: "stakes" word piece 'akes'

result.description: Fires on the noun slot after "depending on the ..." (nature, type, context, application, degree), where a following "of" or a choice-determining noun is expected. It needs a "varies/depends on" construction; the contrast sentence has no such dependence.
result.label: Slot after "depending on the"

result.description: Fires on ' light' in the idiom "shed/shedding light on", after a form of "shed". It predicts " on" next. It stays silent on ' light' at the start of a text or in other uses, like the lighting sense.
result.label: "shed light on" idiom

result.description: Fires on the word " cycle" (also " cycles") in many contexts: life cycle, water cycle, Carnot cycle, economic cycles. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token. It predicts cycle-related continuations like " cycles" and " phases".
result.label: ' cycle' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on ' energy' in "Gibbs free energy" (members detect Gibbs, 'bs', G, thermodynamic). Silent on 'energy' in other contexts like "between energy, pressure". Also weakly on 'ou' in Sturm-Liouville.
result.label: Gibbs free energy 'energy'

result.description: Fires on word pieces that start a longer word and are likely to be continued by a suffix, mainly ' Victor' (before -ian) and 'ad' in 'Leadership'. Predicts continuations such as 'ership', 'io' and 'olph'.
result.label: Victor / Lead- word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on " of" directly after the noun "process" (e.g. "The process of ..."), predicting a gerund or change-type word next. It stays silent on " of" after other nouns such as start, history, front or integration.
result.label: " of" after "process"

result.description: Fires on " due" in the causal phrase "due to" after a clause or noun phrase, as in "widely used in industries due to their...". It predicts qualifiers and causal continuations such as "sole", "largely" and "partly". It is silent on text without this phrase.
result.label: causal "due" before "to"

result.description: Fires on a past participle (characterized, defined, structured) in a passive "is often X-ed" slot, where "by" is expected next. It stays silent on "centralized" or "capitalized" as ordinary word pieces.
result.label: Passive participle before "by"

result.description: Fires on the word right after "mitigate" or "reduce" (e.g. "the", "these risks", "vulnerability"), where the next word is a negative outcome such as effects, risks or damage. It stays silent on "the" after other verbs.
result.label: Object slot after mitigate/reduce

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ium' at the end of chemical element names (sodium, lithium, titanium, magnesium), especially in lists of elements or minerals. Weaker on similar endings like 'Citium' or 'silicon'.
result.label: 'ium' ending of element names

result.description: Fires on precision-related and technical modifier words (precision, advanced, specialized, meticulous, smart) in engineering or science text, often before a technical noun like machining, measurement or control. Silent on general design text.
result.label: Precision and advanced technical modifiers

result.description: Fires mostly on " native" before "speaker(s)" in language-learning text, with weaker firing on other modifier nouns like "local", "treatment", "growth". Members are detectors of native/local/target modifiers; predicts a following noun like speaker.
result.label: "native" before speakers, language learning

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' phen' (also ' phenomen') that begins "phenomena", typically after adjectives like physical, optical or quantum. Members are mostly ' phen' detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: ' phen' start of phenomena

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'ro' in "grassroots", 'to' in "farm-to-table", 'neum' in "pneumatic", where a word is still incomplete. Silent on 'ro' in other words (assroots, terroirs), so it needs the specific word context.
result.label: Word-piece 'ro' in grassroots

result.description: Fires on ' second' or ' latter' (also ' late', ' half') right after "during the", in phrases like "during the second/latter half of the…". Predicts ' half' or ' part' next, i.e. a period-of-time subdivision.
result.label: "the second/latter" before half

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, a, first) in explanations of step-by-step procedures or proofs, especially just before "initial/first" step or base case. Weak, mixed evidence; the same tokens elsewhere stay silent.
result.label: Function words before initial step

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments like 'ru' (Const-ru-ctions, Inter-ru-ptions, dis-ru-ptions) and ' constru' that are mid-word and predict a continuation such as 'ctions' or 'ptions'.
result.label: 'ru' fragment before -ctions/-ptions

result.description: Fires on the 'ut' piece inside "pharmaceutical" (pharmace|ut|ical), including biopharmaceutical. It stays silent on 'ut' in other words such as pollutants and hermeneutic.
result.label: 'ut' in pharmaceutical

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Id"/" id" when it begins a word like "Idioms" or "Idiomatic", predicting continuations such as "iom". Silent on " id" inside "idiomatic construct" mid-sentence; peaks at heading-like starts.
result.label: Id- start of Idioms

result.description: Fires on commas or "and" right after "urbanization" (or similar human-activity items) in lists of drivers of environmental or societal change, predicting the next item such as agriculture or industrialization. Silent on commas after other clause-ending nouns.
result.label: List separator after urbanization

result.description: Peaks mostly on 'umann' in "von Neumann", plus scattered function words like ' between', ' by', ' in' in academic text. Consistency is low and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: von Neumann 'umann' plus scattered function words

result.description: Fires on the comma that closes an introductory purpose clause ("To compute variance, one must first…"), in statistics/math procedure text. It predicts the main clause to follow (then, apply, sum). It stays quiet on commas before "including" or "such as" in general prose.
result.label: Comma after procedural math clause

result.description: Fires on the 'actions' piece of 'reactions' (split as re|actions), mostly in chemistry text such as redox or nuclear reactions. Members are mostly 'actions' detectors at earlier layers.
result.label: 'actions' in re|actions

result.description: Fires on the digit '4' as the second digit of a four-digit year starting with 1 (e.g. 1443, 1475, 14th century). It stays silent on '4' in later positions, as in 1764 or 1874, and on '4th' without a leading 1.
result.label: Digit 4 in 14xx years

result.description: Fires on the word " win" (and " winning") as verb or noun, including "win-win" and "both win". Members are mostly win detectors plus related words like award, fair and games. Predicts "wins", "over".
result.label: ' win' token detector

result.description: Fires on the suffix of "groundbreaking" (-aking) and "pioneering" (-ering), weaker on "seminal", as a praise adjective before a noun like "work" or "research". The next token is predicted to be "work", "idea" or "concept".
result.label: groundbreaking/pioneering suffix before "work"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'anced' in 'nuanced', usually before nouns like understanding, interpretation or expression. It is fed by detectors of 'anced' and related word pieces (subtle, holistic, meticulously).
result.label: 'nuanced' suffix 'anced'

result.description: Fires on forms of "capture" (capture, capt-uring, capt-ures) and on "into" after "draws readers", in writing about art, stories and audience engagement. Predicts objects like attention or nature.
result.label: capture (audience/attention) in creative writing

result.description: Fires on the word " such" after a noun phrase or comma, where it introduces examples ("such as"). Members are mostly " such" detectors at earlier layers.
result.label: "such" introducing examples

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' anom' (start of "anomalies") when it is split off as a prefix, mostly in lowercase text about data or computer science. Silent in the all-caps "alIES" variant. Predicts continuations like "aly".
result.label: ' anom' prefix of anomalies

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ension' completing the word "tension", mostly in writing about storytelling and pacing, where tension builds and is released. Members include detectors of 'ension' and of related words like excitement, suspense and conflict.
result.label: 'ension' in "tension" (narrative)

result.description: Fires on " of" right after a noun that follows "this" (this type of, this field of, this form of, this era of). Silent on " of" after other nouns like "virtue of" or "understanding of".
result.label: "of" after "this + noun"

result.description: Fires on the verb ending (-ing, -s) of "reflect" (also "mirror-ed") when the verb is the word being completed, as in "art reflects/reflecting the changing society". Silent on -ing after other verbs like highlight or cook.
result.label: Inflection ending of "reflect"

result.description: Fires on the last token of a plural agent noun or subject noun (-ists, -ans, -ers, users, 'the') that begins a relative clause, where a verb like could/must/has comes next. Silent on -ists inside other constructions.
result.label: Subject noun before reduced relative verb

result.description: Fires on ' to' introducing a purpose clause ("in order to" sense) after a complete clause or requirement, e.g. "must be implemented to distinguish", predicting ensure/avoid/prevent. Silent on infinitival 'to' after verbs, "adherence to", or "compared to".
result.label: purpose-clause 'to' after requirement

result.description: Fires on "supply" (or the "ly" ending of "Supply" at the start of a document) in supply-chain text, where the next word is likely "chain". Members are detectors of "supply", "procure-" and related logistics words.
result.label: Supply in supply chain context

result.description: Fires on the word " labor" / " labour" (also "Labor"), mostly as a noun modifier in economics and policy text such as labor markets, costs, demand. Weakly fires on the "labor" start of "laboratory" and "collaboration".
result.label: labor / labour word

result.description: Fires on the word " business" (mostly as the stem before "-es" in "businesses") in analytics and corporate text, strongest after verbs like "helping" or "allows". Predicts continuations such as "intelligence" or "-es".
result.label: ' business' token in analytics text

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ant" inside "mercantilism"/"mercantile" (after "merc"). It is silent on "ant" in other words such as "abundant", so it needs that word context.
result.label: "ant" in mercantilism

result.description: Fires on the adjective "mathematical", including the "ical" piece of "Mathematical" split into Mathemat+ical. It predicts abstract nouns such as concepts, models, entities and principles. It stays silent on the noun "mathematics".
result.label: Adjective "mathematical" / Mathemat-ical

result.description: Fires on the word "engineering" as a field of study, mostly in lists of disciplines (physics, chemistry, engineering) or "from engineering to economics". Silent in "genetic engineering".
result.label: engineering as academic field

result.description: Fires on the token 'b' as a word piece in "Pro-b-ability" (also "probabilistic", "probable"), at a title start. It stays silent on the full word "probability" in running text. Weakly fires on 'b' in other words like turbines.
result.label: 'b' piece in Pro-b-ability

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (by, of, it, and) in definitional text about geographic or ecological regions, e.g. "regions are defined by / characterized by". It predicts geography words like regional, mountain and spatial. The same "by" is silent in other science topics.
result.label: Geographic regions definitional function words

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ength" completing "wavelength" (including "wavelengths"), in physics and optics text about waves. Members are "ength" detectors plus frequency and length related latents.
result.label: "ength" in wavelength

result.description: Fires on the piece 'om' inside "chromosomes" (chromos|om|es), after the "chromos" piece. It stays silent on 'om' in other words, such as "bi|om|olecule" or a word-initial "om".
result.label: 'om' in chromosomes

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ug' in the middle of a word, mostly 'fra|ug|ht' in "fraught with", and also in words like Conjugation or adjugate. Members are mostly 'ug' detectors.
result.label: 'ug' in fraught

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' break' (also breaking/breaks), mostly where it begins a compound like breakdown or breakthrough, and pushes the next token toward 'down', 'through', 'up'. Silent when ' break' is the first token of the text.
result.label: ' break' before down/through

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' coord' when it begins "coordination" (e.g. coordination chemistry, coordination number or complex). Members are mostly detectors of ' coord' and similar prefixes.
result.label: ' coord' start of coordination

result.description: Fires on the piece 'cal' completing the word "Fiscal" (as in "Fiscal Policy"), weakly on other 'cal' word-endings. Upstream members detect 'cal' after "Fis" and partial word pieces.
result.label: 'cal' in "Fiscal"

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces like -ony, -ist, -onic, and plural -s in irony, twist, pun words, in texts about literary devices and humor. Silent in pragmatics text on word use.
result.label: Irony/twist suffix in literary-device text

result.description: Fires on commas (and some word pieces like "for" in rain-forest) right after "solar" in lists of renewable energy sources such as "solar, wind, and…". Silent on commas after other nouns in energy text.
result.label: Comma after "solar" in energy lists

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (modal, allowing, for, by, of) in text about extensions of formal logic, such as modal or second-order logic, where the next word is likely "modal" or "operators". Members are logic, proof and philosophy topic detectors.
result.label: Logic-extension text, predicting modal

result.description: Fires on the word piece " strateg" (start of strategic/strategies), mostly in game-theory and strategic-interaction text. It is silent on many other occurrences in business-planning contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' strateg' word piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' morph' when it is mid-word and continues into "-emes" or "-ological", mostly in linguistics text about free and bound morphemes. It is silent when ' morph' starts the text.
result.label: ' morph' piece in morpheme

result.description: Fires on the 'y' piece right after "ph" at the start of a word like phylogenetics, phytohormone, phylum. It predicts 'log'-style continuations. It stays silent on 'y' in other words like empathy or ethylene.
result.label: 'y' in ph-y word start

result.description: Fires on ' motor' (motor neurons, motor control, motor skills) and on ' well' in "as well as", mostly in neuroscience/anatomy text. Silent on unrelated "movers" contrast text.
result.label: motor / "as well" in neuroscience

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ur' right after 'bl' in "blur", "blurry", "blurred", including "blurring". It is a mid-word fragment, and it weakly fires on other 'ur' pieces such as "mercury".
result.label: 'ur' in "blur" word piece

result.description: Fires on "while" introducing a participial clause that adds a simultaneous action after a main clause (e.g. "X while also doing Y"). Predicts continuations like also, still, maintain, using, remaining.
result.label: "while" before simultaneous participle

result.description: Fires on a hyphen inside a long multi-hyphen compound (e.g. what's-in-it-for-us, man-in-the-middle, out-of-order), typically the second or later hyphen. It stays silent on the single hyphen in simple two-part compounds like world-wide or non-destructive.
result.label: Hyphen within multi-part compounds

result.description: Fires on word pieces 'ater' (in c-ater-ing, c-ater to) and 'tain' (per-tain-s) where the word is a verb that continues with "to" (cater to, pertain to). Weak on similar pieces like 'ere' in cereals.
result.label: cater/pertain word pieces before "to"

result.description: Fires on ' as' right after a sentence-opening time or place phrase and comma (e.g. "In the 1980s, as", "During the 18th century, as"), where 'as' begins a clause or "as early as" phrase. Silent on "as well as" and causal 'as' after other clauses.
result.label: ' as' after introductory time phrase

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', commas, 'the', 'an') inside English grammar explanations, especially in lists of pronoun or preposition types. Silent on many ' and' tokens in similar text, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Connectives in grammar-explanation lists

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in contractions after pronouns like that, they, you, it (that's, they're, you're, it's), before 's/re. It is silent on other apostrophes, such as n't after "Don" or "wouldn", and on 've and 'll.
result.label: Apostrophe in pronoun contractions

result.description: Fires on the noun " reach" in marketing and advertising contexts about audience reach (expanding, maximizing, increasing reach). It is quieter on other senses, such as network routes to reach something.
result.label: Audience 'reach' in marketing

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces completing an item in a comma-separated list of nouns (alumin-um, bar-ley, rye, plum), predicting a word-ending piece. Peak tokens are scattered, and it is silent on 'um' in non-list text such as 'optimum'.
result.label: Word endings inside lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' obst' (as in "obstacle(s)") mid-sentence, after a determiner like "many" or "an". Silent when it starts a document. Members detect obst/hurdle-like fragments and boost the "acles" continuation.
result.label: ' obst' start of "obstacles"

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'od' in "aerodynamics"/"aerodynamic" (also 'geodetic'), and weakly on other word-internal pieces like 'ps' in "psyche" or 'atom'. Silent on 'od' in "cathodic".
result.label: 'od' inside aerodynamics

result.description: Fires on ' complex' (and 'icate' in 'intricate') as a predicate adjective after "more"/"became more", typically in "more complex and intricate". Silent when 'complex' is an attributive modifier before a noun, e.g. "managing complex systems".
result.label: "more complex" predicate comparative

result.description: Fires on the word "product"/"products" in several senses: commercial goods, chemical products, and mathematical product (product rule, inner product). It is silent on unrelated text. Predicts suffixes like "-ivity".
result.label: ' product' / ' products' token

result.description: Fires on the quantifier " every" (occasionally " each") when it starts a subject or object noun phrase after a clause opener such as "so that", "where" or "includes". It predicts a singular part noun next, such as component or piece.
result.label: "every" / "each" quantifier

result.description: Fires on the word right after a form of "set/setting" (e.g. "setting the stage/tone", "set new benchmarks"), anticipating objects like stage, tone, standards, benchmark or "apart". Silent on "the" after other verbs like "with" or "convey".
result.label: Object slot after "set/setting"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " mer" as a split-off start of a word like "mergers" or "merchandise", predicting continuations such as "gers", "ges", "itute". Weaker on " subst" (substance). Silent on "emer" inside a word.
result.label: word-initial ' mer' piece (mergers)

result.description: Fires on the token ' Dr' at the start of a line in a list of names (e.g. "Dr. Johnson.¶ Dr. Williams"). Members are mostly ' Dr' detectors from earlier layers. Silent on lists of names without Dr.
result.label: ' Dr' starting list-of-names entry

result.description: Fires on a comma ending a full clause or noun phrase in history, arts or culture prose, where a participial, relative or additional clause follows (encouraging, which, with, followed). Silent on commas in simple lists of names.
result.label: Clause-ending comma in history/arts prose

result.description: Fires on adverb suffixes (-ally, -ically, -ly) that complete a sentence-initial adverb, as in "Generally speaking," "Specifically," "Historically,". Silent on mid-sentence "-ally" such as "culturally and economically". Predicts "speaking"/"though".
result.label: Sentence-initial adverb suffix -ally

result.description: Fires on the token ' growth', mostly after an adjective or noun modifier (sustainable, rapid, exponential, economic). Members are mostly ' growth' detectors; its output favours next words like rates, trajectory, curve.
result.label: ' growth' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token " Middle" as the first word of "Middle Ages" (also "Middle East"), often after Early/Late/High. Predicts continuations like East, Ages-type words. Members are mostly " Middle" detectors.
result.label: Middle in Middle Ages

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' et' when it begins a split word such as "etcher" or "etching" (plasma etching, wet chemical etch). Members detect ' et' and similar word-start fragments (rh-, cla-, cos-, ox-) that predict a continuation.
result.label: ' et' start of etch- words

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Cons" (capitalized, e.g. Sequential Cons-istency) when it begins a longer word such as "Consistency". It pushes toward continuations like "istent"/"cious".
result.label: " Cons" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment " aud" (as in auditory, audience, audit) before the rest of the word is seen. It predicts continuations like "itory", "itor", "ible". Members are mostly " aud" detectors.
result.label: ' aud' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word " stability" (occasionally " convergence") in technical math, engineering and numerical-analysis text, often as the noun after "the" or "ensuring". Predicts property-like next words such as coefficients, properties or rate.
result.label: stability / convergence noun

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' activ' (activated, activation, activator, activist) in biology/immunology text, and occasionally ' lig' (ligand). Predicts suffix continuations like 'ated', 'ic', 'ios'. Members are mostly ' activ' detectors.
result.label: ' activ' word-piece before suffix

result.description: Fires on the piece " is" when it is the start of a split word like "isomerism", "isomers" or "isotope" (iso- words in chemistry). It predicts continuations such as "omer" and "ot". It stays silent on " is" used as the verb.
result.label: ' is' as start of iso- words

result.description: Fires on a verb, auxiliary or "of" right after a subject noun or pronoun inside a "why/how/that" clause (e.g. "why we", "why it's", "tools we use... are"). It is silent on some "are" after long subject noun phrases.
result.label: Auxiliary after subject in why-clauses

result.description: Fires mainly on the word " voltage" (also " temperature", " entropy") as a physical-quantity noun before words like levels, regulators or control. Members detect voltage, electric, DC and frequency tokens. Predicts quantity-change words such as control, change and scales.
result.label: voltage / physical quantity noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'wh' in "overwhelming" (e.g., "without overwhelming readers"), predicting the continuation 'elm'. It needs the 'over' prefix; it stays quiet on other wh- words and on overpower.
result.label: 'wh' in overwhelming

result.description: Fires on the word "competition" and on pieces of "compete"/"Competition" (ete, ition), mainly in economics or market-policy text and in ecology. Likely predicts continuations like "law", "policy" and "against".
result.label: competition / compete word pieces

result.description: Fires on ' played' (also 'plays'/'playing') right after a subject, mostly in the idiom "have played a significant/crucial role" in expository text. Members are detectors of play-verb forms.
result.label: "played" in "played a role"

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after "one" (one's identity, one's own), and more weakly after other person-like nouns. It stays silent on "it's", plural "contexts", and some possessives like "world's" or "speaker's". Predicts " own".
result.label: Possessive 's after "one"

result.description: Fires on the word " datasets" (also " dataset") in machine-learning and data-science text, especially after "labeled" or "large". Members are mostly detectors of data, dataset and sample words. Weakly fires on "vised" in "Supervised".
result.label: ' datasets' token in ML text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'igen' inside 'antigen' (also weaker in 'Indigenous'), mostly in immunology text. It is built from members detecting 'igen'/'ogen' pieces and immune context such as 'foreign' and 'immune'.
result.label: 'igen' in antigen

result.description: Fires on the token ' future' (also ' Future'), mostly as a modifier before a noun (predict future market trends, future generations). It predicts nouns like generations, trajectories, directions. Silent on the contrast text, which has no ' future' token.
result.label: ' future' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token " result" (also weaker on resulted/results), mostly as a verb or noun in causal "result in / result from / a result of" phrasing. Predicts suffixes like "ant"/"antly".
result.label: " result" token detector

result.description: Fires on adjective endings like -rical/-ical/-onal and " circular" in math/geometry text, especially after "cylind" or "spher". Silent on "geometrical". Predicts geometry nouns like shapes, coordinates, trig.
result.label: Round-shape adjective suffixes in geometry

result.description: Fires mostly on commas inside long lists of abstract nouns (reading, sleeping; reflection, feedback), plus some digits in number strings. Silent on some commas after list-final or clause-ending nouns, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Commas in abstract-noun lists
' external' in externalities
result.description: Fires on ' external' when it begins the word "externalities" (economics: positive/economic externalities). Stays quiet on ' external' in other uses like "external factors" at the start of a text. Predicts the suffix "ities".
Fires on the word piece 'pers' inside "super-" words such as superset and supersymmetric (math/physics), after the "su" piece. Weak activation on other mid-word pieces like 'ni' in millennium.
result.label: 'pers' in su-pers-ymmetric/superset

result.description: Fires weakly on assorted function words (' to', ' of', ' kept', ' power', ' as') in academic or technical prose, often after participles like "raised", "kept" or "product". Peaks are inconsistent and the target is silent on many identical tokens.
result.label: Scattered function words after participles

result.description: Fires on "semantic"/"Semantics" as a word or word piece (Sem|antic, ' semantic'), strongest at document-start headings like "Semantic Primitives". Mostly silent when "semantic" follows "literal" in running prose.
result.label: Semantic / Semantics word

result.description: Fires on present-participle verb endings (-ing, -ulating, serving, carrying, providing) in a participial phrase after a comma, where a verb is about to take an object (predicts both/them/everything). Silent on 'crafting' used as a noun or gerund subject, and on 'coloring'.
result.label: Participial -ing verb before object

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'able' completing the word "unpredictable" (and weakly "predictable"). It stays silent on 'able' in durable, achievable, sustainable. Pushes toward nouns like nature, terrain, weather, consequences.
result.label: 'able' in unpredictable

result.description: Fires on the token " convergence" (and the piece "gence" in Convergence), mostly in mathematical text about sequences, series and convergence types. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same word. Predicts continuations like "towards" and "point".
result.label: ' convergence' token detector
Decade digit in second year of range
result.description: Fires on the decade digit (mostly '7', also 6/8) in "19X0" when it ends a year range, such as "1950s-19[7]0s" or "1962–19[7]0". It stays silent on '7' in other years, such as 1750 or 1874, and in earlier-century dates.

Fires on ' for' right after a form of "allow" (allows for, allowing for, allowed for), in academic or analytical prose. It stays silent on ' for' after adjectives or nouns such as "crucial for" or "techniques for".
result.label: 'for' after allow/allows

result.description: Fires mainly on " noise" in technical contexts like noise levels, noise reduction and signal filtering. It also fires on "aster" in "disaster" and a few odd word pieces. The contrast has "sounds", where it stays silent.
result.label: ' noise' token (acoustic/signal)
Open bracket after word, inline annotation
result.description: Fires on an opening square bracket '[' (also ',[' or ')[') attached directly to the preceding word with no space, where a footnote-like or tag-like annotation begins (e.g. "[citation needed", "[note"). Silent on ordinary prose.

Fires on the object right after a form of "save" (save money, saves the planet, save time), especially in energy-efficiency text. Silent on "money" after "than" or "making". Predicts saved resources like money, costs, time.
result.label: Object after "save" (money/the planet)

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'ocity' (as in "Velocity Components"), plus a few title-like words such as 'laration', ' Missouri' and ' Article' in document-title phrases. It stays silent on 'ocity' in some Vel-ocity contexts. Members are weak, generic and mixed.
result.label: 'ocity' in title-like phrases

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start pieces like ' liter' (literacy), ' orn' (ornamental), ' traject', ' diag', mid-word, where the continuation is a suffix such as 'acy' or 'ament'. Predicts those word completions.
result.label: Word-start fragments: liter-, orn-

result.description: Fires on the degree sign '°' after a number and on 'si' in 'Celsius', i.e. temperature/angle unit tokens. Weak, mixed activity elsewhere (' TO', ' ON'), so the circuit is only partly coherent.
result.label: Degree sign and Celsius 'si'

result.description: Fires on word pieces like 'ough' in t-ough(er/ness) and 'ild' in m-ild, adjective stems of texture/strength/temperature that take suffixes such as -ness, -er, -ly. Silent on 'ough' in 'dough'.
result.label: Adjective stem pieces: tough, mild

result.description: Fires on the word piece " citiz" (start of "citizen") in civic-engagement and urban governance text, e.g. "citizen participation" or "citizen science". It predicts the "en" continuation. Weaker on related pieces like "civ" and "en".
result.label: " citiz" start of citizen

result.description: Fires on the word " actual" as an adjective before a noun (the actual device, actual growth, actual performance). Upstream members detect " actual" and near-synonyms (true, practical, concrete, physical). It pushes toward suffixes like -ity and -ized.
result.label: ' actual' adjective token

result.description: Fires on "improve" (improve, improving, improved) and the word right after it (their, the, in), where the next token is an object like "upon", "overall quality", "skills". Silent on "-ving" in evolving or problem-solving.
result.label: Improve verb and following slot

result.description: Fires on the word " digital" (also "Digital" and the "ital" piece) as a modifier before nouns like economy, technology, platforms or media. It pushes toward nouns that follow, such as infrastructure, transformation and economy.
result.label: ' digital' adjective token

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tra' when it starts a word, most strongly in genetics text where it begins "traits" (genetic, dominant, inherited traits). Also fires on other ' tra' starts like trapezo- and trademarks, more weakly.
result.label: ' tra' word-start (traits)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " demonstr" (occasionally " illustr" or " sign") at the start of demonstrating/demonstrative/demonstration, predicting suffixes like -ating, -atives, -ative. Members are detectors of demonstr/illustr tokens.
result.label: ' demonstr' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'histor' inside words like "Prehistoric", where a suffix such as '-ic' is expected next. Members detect similar mid-word pieces (strat-igraph, Paleol-ith, phys-, onom-). Silent on ordinary text.
result.label: 'histor' piece in Prehistoric

result.description: Fires mostly on an opening square bracket " [" (also "|", "...", "(") after a word or operation, as in "operation [" or "+ [". Weaker, scattered hits on other tokens. The circuit is mostly " [" detectors; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Opening square bracket token

result.description: Fires on the word "engineering" (also "engine" in "engineers") when used as a field modifier or discipline name, e.g. "various engineering applications", "Civil Engineering". Mostly in technical and mechanics text; predicts nouns like problem, discipline, applications.
result.label: engineering word detector

result.description: Fires on the word-initial fragment ' sm' (also ' Sm', occasionally ' op') that starts a longer word such as smiling, smoking or smudging. It predicts continuations like 'ells', 'arts', 'oking'.
result.label: Word-initial ' sm' fragment

result.description: Fires on word pieces completing infrastructure/communication technology terms, mainly "tele-graph", also rail-"ways", road, ads, in lists of transport and communication networks. Predicts network/line/railway-type continuations. Silent on generic transportation prose.
result.label: Telegraph/railways infrastructure word endings

result.description: Fires on verbs meaning "represent/indicate/denote" (representing, represent, indicate, represents) right after a plural subject noun, especially "nodes representing", in technical or explanatory text. It predicts a following description like "whether", "how" or "various".
result.label: represent/indicate verb after subject noun

result.description: Fires on ' statistical' and on 'cal' in 'Fiscal' (fiscal policy), at the adjective position before a noun like analysis, policy or property. Silent on hypothesis-testing text without the word itself.
result.label: statistical / fiscal adjective

result.description: Fires on the token " Revolution" as the head of named historical revolutions (French, Russian, Industrial, Scientific, American). It predicts suffixes like "ary" and "ized". Members are mostly detectors of "revolution" tokens.
result.label: Revolution token in named revolutions

result.description: Fires on "integration" and on "-ation" in "incorporation"/"Integration", i.e. the noun meaning combining or incorporating things into a system. Silent on other "-ation" words like propagation, innovation, differentiation. Predicts "into"/"with"/"of".
result.label: integration / incorporation noun

result.description: Fires on the word " philosophy" when it follows a regional or tradition adjective (Eastern, Asian, Indian, African, Western). It stays quiet when " philosophy" starts a document or sentence with no preceding modifier. Members are mostly philosophy-word detectors.
result.label: Modified 'philosophy' after tradition adjective

result.description: Fires on " both" right after a preposition like "in" or "for", where it begins a paired "both X and Y" phrase (e.g. "important in both theoretical and applied"). It stays quiet on other tokens, including the contrast list of areas.
result.label: "both" after preposition

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ir' in the middle of words (asp-ir-ations, ch-ir-p, St-ir-ling, resp-ir-atory), plus ' of' in "Internet of Things" and ' ship'. Predicts mid-word continuations like 'voy', 'teen', 'ky'.
result.label: Mid-word 'ir' piece (aspirations, chirp)
Decade plural 's' after year
result.description: Fires on the 's' ending a decade expression like 1950s, 1980s, after a single four-digit year ending in 0. It stays silent when the decade follows a range ("1990 to 2000s") and on possessive 's.

Fires on the piece 'ig' inside "sovereignty" (also in words like pigment, paradigm), predicting a following 'nt'-type continuation. Mostly needs the word-internal 'ig' of these words; occasional weak firing on ' Nash'.
result.label: 'ig' in sovereignty

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'od' in the middle of a word, mostly "mel-od-ies/ic/ious", also par-od-ies and Ge-od-etic. It predicts suffixes like -ic, -ies, -ial. It stays quiet on 'od' at word start or in "embodiment".
result.label: 'od' inside melodies-type words

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' e' / ' E' when it begins "ecology", "ecosystem" or "ecological" in ecology text, and pushes the next token towards 'col' or 'cos'. Silent on some 'e' tokens before "cosystem" in other phrasing.
result.label: ' e' starting ecology/ecosystem

result.description: Fires on " music"/" musical" in technology and software contexts, such as modern music production, DAWs and music notation software. It stays silent on genre-modified uses like "heavy music", "folk music" and "rock music". It predicts production and computing words next.
result.label: music in tech/production contexts

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece "dec"/"Dec" that begins words like decoding, decryption or decisions, and predicts continuations such as "oding", "ryption" and "isions". It is strongest in "Encoding/Decoding" text.
result.label: Dec- word-start piece (decoding/decision)

result.description: Fires on the noun or word piece completing "a new ___" (paradigm, frontier, era, level), where the next word is an abstract noun about novelty or change. It is silent on "paradigm shift" without "new" before it.
result.label: Completing "a new ___" abstract noun

result.description: Fires on auxiliary/passive verbs and connectors (' are', ' be', ' has', ' and') right after a plural or abstract subject noun in business/improvement prose, where a passive participle like "made" or "realized" is expected. Silent on many ' are' tokens.
result.label: Passive auxiliary after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the word piece " condu" (as in conducive, conduit, conduction), mostly in "a conducive environment". It predicts continuations like "cive", "ci", "ction". Members are mostly detectors of " condu" and similar word-start fragments.
result.label: ' condu' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece " won" (mostly the start of "won't"), where an apostrophe-t contraction is expected next. Members detect contraction stems like don, doesn, didn, isn, wouldn. Rare peaks on unrelated tokens in other scripts.
result.label: " won" before contraction 't

result.description: Fires on the word " known" itself, as in "known as", "later known as", "is known for", and "all known". Many upstream members are also detectors of " known".
result.label: ' known' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word-initial prefix ' dis' (disorder, disaster, disruption, discharge) before the rest of the word is seen. It pushes next-token predictions toward completions like 'order', 'aster', 'rupt' and 'joint'.
result.label: ' dis' prefix before completion

result.description: Fires on ordinal words " Second" and " Third" in "Newton's Second/Third Law", predicting "Law" or similar next. Members detect ordinals like First, Second, Third, Last. Silent in unrelated physics contexts like momentum.
result.label: Newton's Second/Third Law ordinal

result.description: Fires on ' financial' and on word endings like 'cial' (Finan-cial) and 'ical' (Mathemat-ical) in adjective-like heading words, predicting abstract nouns such as theory, concepts, strategy. Members are mostly financial/cial detectors.
result.label: financial / -cial / -ical adjective endings

result.description: Fires on the piece 'me' inside "permeability", "permeate" and "permeable" (after "per"). It stays silent on 'me' in other words such as "omelets". Logits favor completions like 'ability', 'ates' and 'able'.
result.label: 'me' in per-me-ability

result.description: Fires on ' one' used as the generic impersonal pronoun ("one can", "one must") as the subject after a clause-opening comma or conjunction. Silent on ' one' as a numeral or in "each one" and "sometimes one".
result.label: Impersonal pronoun 'one' as subject

result.description: Fires on the token " Middle" (as in Middle Ages, Middle East, Middleware), including when it begins a word like "Middleware". Members are mostly detectors of " Middle" or similar word-start pieces.
result.label: ' Middle' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token 'ure', both as a word ending (sculpt-ure, expos-ure, adventure) and as a standalone fragment at the start of a heading or sentence. Members are mostly 'ure' token detectors.
result.label: 'ure' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word "gravity" and on pieces of "gravitational"/"gravitation" (mainly 'ational') in physics text. Upstream members are detectors of gravity-word pieces and related physics words like forces and relativity.
result.label: gravity / gravitational word

result.description: Fires on the token 's' after a closing quote mark at the end of a sentence (like "...scenarios.'s the measure"), where it stands for "is/as". It stays silent on ordinary "let's" and possessive 's contractions after a word.
result.label: 's after closing quote mark

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Per' (also 'th') when it begins "Perfect", especially in grammar tense headings like "Past Perfect". Members detect Per/per word-starts that precede a completion such as -fect or -ception.
result.label: ' Per' in "Past Perfect" tenses

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ton' in "proton" (including "unprotonial"), in physics/chemistry text. It stays silent on 'ton' in the name "Dalton", so it needs the pro- prefix.
result.label: 'ton' in proton

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Communic' (also ' Integr') after a modifier in list-like topic headings (e.g. "Interpersonal Communication."), predicting a suffix like -ation. Silent on other heading lists.
result.label: Communic- piece in heading lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' corpor' (start of corpora, corporate, corporation), most strongly in linguistics text where it is followed by 'a' in 'corpora'. Predicts 'a' as next piece. Weaker on corporate-governance uses.
result.label: ' corpor' word piece (corpora)

result.description: Fires on the word-start pieces ' incorpor' (incorporate/incorporating/incorporation) and 'comp' in 'encompass', mid-word, where the next piece is a suffix. Members detect incorpor, integr, util, evalu stems. Silent when incorporating starts the text.
result.label: incorpor- / encomp- word stem

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ference" completing "interference" (wave, signal, or political), with weaker firing on "distortion". Members are mostly "ference" detectors in earlier layers plus "inter-fer" pieces.
result.label: "ference" in "interference"

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'er' in "polym|er" (mostly polymerization), when the word is split as polym + er. It predicts continuations such as 'ization', 'ic' and 'izations'. It is much weaker on the plural 'ers'.
result.label: 'er' inside polymer

result.description: Fires on the verb " sought" (rarely " attempted") after a subject like powers, nations or colonialism, in historical or academic text, where "to + verb" is expected next. Members are detectors of seek/sought forms.
result.label: "sought" verb after a subject

result.description: Fires mostly on the split-off piece ' ing' in "ingredient(s)" (tokenized as ' ing' + 'redient'), with weaker firing on scattered tokens like digit '0' and 'etal'. Members are mainly ' ing' detectors in cooking/ingredient contexts.
result.label: ' ing' in ingredient split

result.description: Fires on the ' ing' piece that starts the split word "ingredients" (e.g. "measuring ingredients"), in cooking text. It stays silent when ' ing' is the first token of the document, and members detect ' ing' in this slot.
result.label: ' ing' starting "ingredients" split

result.description: Fires on the word " section" when it refers to a part of a text or document, often after "the" (e.g. "the conclusion of the section", "the section you requested"). Silent on "This section explores…" at the start of a sentence.
result.label: ' section' as document part

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ur' inside words like blur, Heuristic and bifurcation, with weaker firing on ' expansion', list commas and some function words. The peaks are mixed, and the 'ur' piece is the strongest and best-supported part.
result.label: 'ur' word piece (blur, heuristic)

result.description: Fires on " patterns" (also system/systems, shifts) right after a climate or weather noun such as weather, wind or precipitation. It stays silent on "patterns" in generic or social contexts like "predictable patterns".
result.label: Climate/weather "patterns" noun

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ism' completing "realism" (Real+ism), including in art-style contexts. It stays quiet on 'ism' after other stems like modern, Pragmat, connection.
result.label: 'ism' in "realism"

result.description: Fires on function words (the, for, a, which) in statistics text about significance levels, hypothesis testing and Type I error, where the next word is likely a statistical term (alpha, Type, Null). Silent on 'the' in general math or definitions.
result.label: Function words in hypothesis-testing text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ake' in "st-ake" when it begins "stakeholder(s)", predicting 'holder'/'hold' next. Silent when 'ake' stands alone at the start of a text without the 'st' before it.
result.label: 'ake' in st-ake-holder

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' vin' (in vinyl), 'div', ' der', where the word continues in a following piece. It mostly peaks on ' vin' before 'yl'. It is silent on ' vin' at the very start of a text.
result.label: ' vin' word-initial fragment (vinyl)

result.description: Fires on function words (of, a, the, listing) in text about restaurant menus, right where a noun like menu/business/profit-related terms may follow. Silent on 'of' in other culinary prose, so it needs the menu-design framing.
result.label: Function words in menu-design text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in abstract academic prose (' economic', ' their', ' differences', ' industrial', 'ino'), often where a noun like a social or economic phenomenon is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent, and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse academic-prose modifier slot

result.description: Fires on word pieces after a capital "D" at the start of a word, mainly "riv" and "rav" in "Dravidian", also "D-f-D" and "Dijkstra". Silent when the word lacks the D-prefix (e.g. "Tamil").
result.label: Word pieces after D in Dravidian

result.description: Fires on varied function words (from, the, of, in) and suffixes like -izing in text about Impressionism and art movements, where the next word is likely an art-related name or term. Silent on 'from' in other art passages, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Function words in Impressionism art text

result.description: Fires on the ending of a persistence adjective (unrelent-ing, relent-less, unyield-ing, ongoing) that modifies an abstract noun like drive, pursuit or curiosity, often after "humanity's". Predicts words like desire, quest, spirit. Silent on ordinary verb -ing.
result.label: Relentless-type adjective before drive/pursuit

result.description: Fires on ' to' as the endpoint marker in a "from X to Y" range or transition (sweet to spicy, concept to completion). It stays silent on infinitive "to" (in order to, ability to).
result.label: "to" in from-X-to-Y ranges
'ge' word-piece fragment
result.description: Fires on the token 'ge' as a word fragment, e.g. in bad-ge, ge-ometric, bour-ge-ois, and weakly on 'ged' in tra-ged-y. It predicts continuations like 'vity', 'ois', 'ometric'. Silent on unrelated text.

Fires on the word-piece ' re' used as a prefix starting a longer word (revenue, reactor, redefine, repercussions, retraining), predicting continuations like 'venue', 'forms', 'active'. Silent when ' re' is at the start of the text.
result.label: ' re' prefix mid-sentence

result.description: Fires on "Global" and the "ization" of "Globalization" when it appears as a short heading in a list of topic headings (e.g. "Economic Globalization."). It stays silent on "ization" in other words like Optimization or Decolonization. Predicts nouns like Revolution, Exchange, Media.
result.label: Globalization heading in topic lists
'yg' piece in hygiene
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yg' in "hygiene" (h-yg-iene), predicting 'iene' next. Upstream members are mostly 'yg' detectors, including ones from "polygon". It also fires weakly on 'les' in "ecclesiastically".

Fires on verbs of reducing or minimizing (reduce, reducing, minimize/minimizes, decrease) where the next word is likely an undesirable thing such as risk, waste, or errors. Members detect reduce/minimize/prevent verbs.
result.label: reduce/minimize verbs before negatives

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, and, from, under) in text about the Russian Revolution and Russian/Soviet empire history, where the next word is likely Russian, Czech or Tsarist. Silent on 'the' in generic century or era phrases.
result.label: Function words in Russian history text

result.description: Fires on ' one' used as a pronoun standing in for a noun after a determiner or adjective ("the one that", "the first one", "the extended one"). It stays silent on generic "one" as subject ("one must", "one wants") and on "in one place".
result.label: ' one' as noun-substitute pronoun

result.description: Fires on the word " marine" (or " Marine") in ocean-life text, such as marine species, animals, habitats, or Marine topic headings. Members are mostly detectors of " Marine" and "aquatic".
result.label: Marine token detector

result.description: Fires on the piece "elling" at the end of "compelling" (comp-elling), predicting persuasion nouns like arguments, reasons, evidence, stories. It stays silent on "elling" in "storytelling".
result.label: "comp|elling" word-piece before arguments

result.description: Fires on words meaning a baseline or yardstick: ' standard' (standardized, standard deviation), ' reference' (reference frame/point), ' benchmark'. Appears in technical or scientific text about measurement and geodesy. Predicts nouns like deviation, frames and points.
result.label: standard / reference / benchmark words

result.description: Fires on the 'ist' piece inside "epistemic/epistemology" (ep-ist-). It stays silent on the suffix 'ist' in words like "consumerist" or "foundationalist". It predicts continuations such as "em".
result.label: 'ist' in epistemic/epistemology

result.description: Fires on the plural noun " artists", mostly as the subject starting a clause or sentence about art. It stays silent when " artists" is the very first token of the text.
result.label: ' artists' as clause subject

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ver" (and sometimes "val") at the start of words like verbs, verbal, verification, predicting continuations such as "bal", "bs", "itable". Mostly in language/grammar text.
result.label: "ver" word-start piece (verb/verbal)

result.description: Fires on the word "known" (also "well-known", "later known", "commonly known") in passive or participle uses leading into "as" or "for". Members are mostly detectors of "known" and similar words like "referred".
result.label: "known" before as/for

result.description: Fires on the token " conscious" (as in "environmentally conscious", "consciousness"), mostly when a word like "environmental(ly)" or "nature of" precedes it. Members are detectors of "conscious" and of suffix pieces that lead to "-ness".
result.label: ' conscious' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token " capabilities", typically after a modifier or noun (unique, IDS, spatial mapping, processing). Members are mostly detectors of "capabilities" and similar words (skills, abilities, features). Next-token logits favor "beyond" and "within".
result.label: ' capabilities' token detector

result.description: Fires on mixed word pieces and function words mid-word or in lists (' rev' before 'italize', 'proof' in soundproofing, ' and', commas), where a verb or word continuation is expected. It stays silent on ' rev' in 'revitalization' noun contexts.
result.label: Word-start pieces predicting verb continuations

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'atives' in "initiatives" (and less on ' efforts') when it names programs or projects, e.g. conservation or inclusion initiatives. It stays silent on 'atives' in "narratives".
result.label: initiatives / efforts noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece "it" inside longer words, mainly "facil|it|ator" and also "necess|it|ates". It stays silent on "exhibit" and "prioritizes". It predicts suffixes like -ators, -ates, -ating.
result.label: "it" piece in facilitator

result.description: Fires on the word " literal" (as in "literal meaning", "literal vs figurative") in discussions of language and meaning. It predicts meaning/interpretation/definition as the next word. Members are mostly detectors of "literal" and related words such as physical, direct and abstract.
result.label: ' literal' before meaning

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' t' when it is a split-off start of a longer word, such as tense, tenses, tone, tissue or tune. It pushes towards continuations like 'ense', 'une', 'issues' and 'endencies'.
result.label: Word-initial ' t' fragment

result.description: Fires on an opening quotation mark that introduces a quoted example word or sentence in English grammar explanations, such as listed prepositions or pronouns. Silent on a quote opening a legal-style phrase.
result.label: Opening quote of grammar examples

result.description: Fires at points after "providing/offering X (with)" where a noun like "opportunity", "support" or "unparalleled/unprecedented level" is likely next. Peaks on varied tokens (oversight, unparalleled, them, with, the). Logits favor opportunity, support, advantages.
result.label: Predicting offered benefit noun after providing

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ain' in "stainless" (after "st"), with a few 'ized' cases. It stays silent on 'ain' at the start of a word or in "sustain-" words such as sustainability.
result.label: 'ain' in "stainless"

result.description: Fires on the final '0' of a decade year like 192[0]s or 198[0], right after a 3-digit year prefix, in historical or timeline text. Next-token logits favor verbs like "laid", "gave", "provided". Silent on some 197[0]s and 2[0]00s cases.
result.label: Decade-year final zero

result.description: Fires on the 'ive' piece of "Effective" when it begins a document or title, right after "Effect". It stays silent on 'ive' in other words such as "attentive" and "passive". It predicts nouns like communication, management and implementation.
result.label: "Effect-ive" word completion at start
