result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'it' in "prior-it-ize" (also "emphas", "mand", "advoc" stems) where a verb ending like -ize/-izing is expected next; also on long dash separator runs. Silent on 'it' in other words.
result.label: Word stem before -ize suffix ('prior-it')

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside technical science/engineering terms, mostly 'ator' in actuator/insulator, also 'con' in superconductors, 'zo', 'actu'. Predicts continuations like 'crete', 'duct', 'chan'.
result.label: Technical word fragments (actuator, superconductor)

result.description: Fires on the word "we"/"We" (pronoun, sentence start or mid-sentence). Output logits favor continuations like "aving", "ave", "aved", so it seems to treat "we" as a possible start of a word such as "weaving".
result.label: "we"/"We" token, weave-continuation

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ively' (occasionally 'ive') in "progressively", especially before a comparative like "more". It stays silent on 'ively' in other words such as "actively". Logits favour comparatives like ' more', ' stronger', ' higher'.
result.label: "progressively" suffix before comparatives

result.description: Fires on ' and' or commas right after the noun "characters" (e.g. "characters and", "characters, settings") in writing about storytelling and narrative. It stays silent on 'and' after other nouns like pace or dialogue.
result.label: "characters" followed by and/comma

result.description: Fires on ' stream' (and some word-piece fragments like 'al' in 'anomalies') where the word is incomplete or being built, predicting 'line'/'lined' continuations. Mixed with word-fragment detectors; evidence is partly scattered.
result.label: ' stream' / word-piece predicting 'line'

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ao' in "Taoism", mostly at the start of a document. It also fires weakly on a few other mid-word pieces ('imal', 'ros'), where the next token is a suffix such as 'ist' or 'istic'.
result.label: 'ao' in Taoism
' of' after reflection/expression nouns
result.description: Fires on ' of' after nouns meaning a representation or manifestation of something (reflection, expression, symbol, indicator, marker, representation). Silent on ' of' after other nouns like amalgamation, experience, realms, aspect.
Fires on the word piece "gence" in "emergence", especially "the emergence of ..." in passages about technology or change. Weaker on similar noun endings like "proliferation".
result.label: "emergence" word-ending 'gence'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' to', ' a', ',', ' of', ' can') in generic essay-style prose about personal growth, learning, and organizations. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same ' to' stays silent in other sentences. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is a weak fit.
result.label: Function words in self-improvement essays

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: commas after abstract noun pairs ("modularity and extensibility,"), "synth", "id", "2", "ancient". No dominant token or clear condition; the circuit failed faithfulness and looks mixed.
result.label: Mixed commas and word pieces

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (hyphen in "city-state", " gods", "Par-then-on", "Athen-ian") inside text about ancient Greece. Silent on the same hyphen in Rome or other non-Greek contexts. Members are ancient-civilization and Greek detectors.
result.label: Ancient Greece context tokens

result.description: Fires mostly on the possessive 's after "Fermat'" (and occasionally "of", "on", "the" in text about Fermat's theorem). Silent on 's after other names like Euler or generic possessives, so it needs Fermat context.
result.label: Fermat possessive 's

result.description: Peaks scatter over unrelated tokens ('2' in "every 20 minutes", 'ES', 'found', ' you', 'aint') with no shared meaning. Silent on '2' in century expressions like "20th century". Circuit failed and members are generic; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (family, of, and, to, commas, -an suffixes) in text about languages, language families and endangered-language revitalization. Mixed, low-consistency peaks; it stays silent on 'family' in a non-linguistic sense.
result.label: Language-family and revitalization text

result.description: Fires on scattered function tokens (commas, " that", " from", " a", a "lation" piece) mid-sentence in essay-style text about history, narrative, or methods. Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit failed and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered function tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on function words and connectives (' in', ',', ' and', ' but', ' the') in essay-style prose, often in lists or coordinated phrases after an abstract noun or adjective. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak; contrast ' in' after nouns stays silent.
result.label: Connectives in abstract essay prose

result.description: Fires on function words (' is', ' and', '.') and 'Ad'/'ad' pieces in science text where a technical prefix such as iso- or adiabatic comes next, mostly thermodynamics and chemistry. Silent on ordinary ' is' in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Thermodynamics iso-/adiabatic term predictor

result.description: Fires in text about goal-setting and SMART objectives (measurable, achievable, targets), on goals/targets words and following function words or punctuation like "that", "are", ",". Silent on "quality goals" in a different context.
result.label: Goal-setting and SMART objectives

result.description: Fires on digits (and spaces) in the later part of a year, mostly the second year after a range marker like "1900 and 19", "1903–19", or "1901-1". Silent on single years or the first year of a range.
result.label: Digits of range end year

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on ' ideas', ' the', ' and' and 'x' in academic or expository text. It stays silent on ' ideas' after verbs like express or develop. Members are generic and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Mixed academic function words, ideas

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit. It peaks mostly on ' exists' after "a substance/material" in phase-condition text, with scattered other peaks (' and', 'H'). Members are generic context, not discriminative. Evidence is thin.
result.label: ' exists' after substance (weak)

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied tokens (' recording', ' and', ' appropriate', 'est', a comma), often in food/wine or art-related text. Members are mostly generic token detectors with no discriminative signal; the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered unclear mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and verbs (evoke, explore, blends, 'an') in passages about fiction and storytelling. Members mostly detect narrative-writing context and predict story-related words. Peaks are scattered; the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in fiction-writing text

result.description: Fires on tokens inside or just after a negated verb phrase ("does not contain any specific content", "does not consider ...,"), including commas and 'but' that continue the negated clause. Members detect negation-then-object words like contain/content/any.
result.label: Inside negated clause after "does not"

result.description: Fires on the "ve"/"ves" piece of "delve(s)" in "As we/one delve(s) deeper into…" openers. It stays quiet on "ve" in other words like "evolve" or "convey". Members detect delve-like words and "deeper/into" continuations.
result.label: "delve" word-piece in "delve deeper into"

result.description: Fires mostly on " known" (also known as, later known as, known outcomes), and occasionally on "to" after "referred" or "validate". Members are mainly detectors of "known". Weak, mixed on other tokens.
result.label: "known" in "also known as"

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied mid-sentence tokens (' the', ' of', ' un', suffixes like -ing, -ers) in expository text. The peak token is also silent in other contexts, and the logits show no clear next-token pattern.
result.label: Diffuse mid-sentence function-word latent

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' students', 'ized', ' /', ').', ' the') in educational or mathematical text. Upstream members mostly carry math/algebra context. The peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in math/education text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (the, comma, for, closing paren, is) mid-sentence in expository academic text, where the next word is an abstract noun. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast is silent on 'the' after verbs/of. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'and', 'DNA', word pieces) inside molecular-biology text about gene transcription and DNA. It is silent on commas in other genetics passages, so the peak token matters less than the context.
result.label: Molecular biology transcription text context

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit that peaks on varied tokens (' and', document start, ' depth'). Fires on some ' and' joining abstract noun phrases but stays silent on very similar ' and' contexts; members are generic and the circuit failed.
result.label: Mixed ' and' / start tokens (unclear)

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (' and', commas, word pieces like 'ent', ' someone') in the middle of descriptive phrases. The peaks share no clear token or construction, and members are generic and non-specific.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function tokens

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (to, it, which, for, that, can) in abstract expository sentences about understanding or mastering a topic, where a verb or object comes next. Peaks are scattered; the contrast is not clearly separated.
result.label: Function words in explanatory academic prose

result.description: Weak, scattered circuit that fires on mixed tokens (word pieces like ' gar', ' out', ' as', ' the') in expository text. Members are generic, with no discriminative ones. The circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token, low-confidence circuit

result.description: Fires on scattered punctuation and function tokens (commas, 'and', semicolons, 'bias') in expository technical text, often mid-list or clause boundaries. Peaks are inconsistent, and the contrast silences it on commas too, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered commas and conjunctions in expository text

result.description: Fires on 'century' (and the following word or comma) after an ordinal like 19th or 20th in historical period phrases. Silent on some 'century' cases such as 17th and 21st, so it is inconsistent. The circuit is mostly century-token detectors.
result.label: Ordinal + century phrases

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (explore, understand, studying, using, "study of") that come right before an object in text about quantile regression and statistics. It is silent on many "of" tokens elsewhere. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Analysis verbs in quantile regression text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (on, were, methods, commas) in passages describing how things were done in earlier, pre-modern or pre-digital times, in the slot just before a description of old methods. Weakly specified.
result.label: Historical past-practice description slot

result.description: Fires on scattered function tokens (commas, 'and', 'a', 'to', 'would') in expository prose, mid-clause where a continuation follows. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast stays silent on commas too, so the trigger is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse function-word mid-clause slot

result.description: Fires on the modal/verb slot (mostly " would") in the main clause after a "without X," phrase, as in "without it, we would have...". It is silent on "would" in other contexts, such as relative clauses or "there would".
result.label: would after "without X," clause

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, from, to) right after a verb of measuring or in descriptions of the Gini coefficient (e.g. "measures the extent of inequality"). It is silent on "measures the" in other statistical contexts, so it seems tied to the Gini coefficient passage.
result.label: Function words in Gini coefficient descriptions

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied function words and word pieces (' of', ' their', ' through', commas, mid-word fragments) in abstract expository prose. Silent on many ' of' tokens elsewhere. Members are generic; evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires mostly on the '1' starting a year (e.g. 1970, 1980) in "from 1960 to the mid-1970" ranges, plus a few odd peaks (document start, 'atory'). Silent on '1' in other year contexts. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Year '1' after "to the mid-"

result.description: Fires on ' gal' (galactic) and nearby tokens like 'the', 'of', or commas in astrophysics text about galaxies and stars. Members detect gal/Gal pieces and galaxy-cluster words. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: galactic astronomy gal- token

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' and', 's', ' classical', ' of') within Renaissance/classical antiquity revival text, e.g. "rebirth of classical antiquity's". Members are humanism/medieval-revival detectors; ' and' stays silent elsewhere. Weak, failed circuit.
result.label: Renaissance classical-revival phrase tokens
Separators after policy/regulation list items
result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "with", "alongside" right after a policy-type noun (policy approaches, policy-making, policy adjustments) in a list of strategies or measures. Silent on commas in other social or educational lists.

Fires on commas and conjunctions (and, or, as well as) in a list of effects or outcomes after a subject with "can" (e.g. "X can improve A, B, and create C"). It is silent on commas that begin a relative clause or follow an adverbial.
result.label: Conjunctions in "can" effect lists

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (of, with, in, as, commas) in graph and network technical text, especially after verbs like modeling or representing. It stays silent on 'of' right after nouns like concept or collection. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Linking words in graph-theory text

result.description: Fires mostly on sentence-final periods, and sometimes on 'ing', ' contrast' or ' speed' in lists of parallel items. Fires on only some periods and stays silent on others, with no clear rule. The circuit looks weak and mixed.
result.label: Sporadic sentence-end period, mixed

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (the, colon, for, calculating) in food cost accounting text, at slots where a cost-related term is expected next. Silent on 'the' in general culinary text that is not about cost calculation.
result.label: Function words in food costing text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (of, through, as, an, the, and, commas) inside abstract academic or expository prose. No dominant token, and it is silent on many ' the' cases. The evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word right after "avoid" (e.g. "avoid using", "avoids causing", "avoid exaggerating"), where a bad thing to be avoided comes next. It also fires weakly after prevent-type verbs. Predicts error or problem words.
result.label: Token after "avoid"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (digit '1', quotes, 'and', periods, 'for', word pieces) in expository text with no single pattern. Circuit failed and members are generic; the evidence is too mixed to say what it needs.
result.label: Scattered mixed tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on commas (and pieces like 'rum', 'wner') inside lists of items or roles after "such as"/"include", e.g. "Product Owner, Scrum Master, and...". Silent on commas ending ordinary clauses. Evidence is weak; the circuit failed.
result.label: List-item commas in enumerations

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (' and', ' to', ',', ' of') and some nouns in abstract, academic-style expository prose, mid-phrase. Peaks are scattered and the contrast shows ' and' silent in similar contexts. The circuit failed, so evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires weakly on assorted function tokens (commas, 'is', 'that', 'on', 'through', 'often') in expository academic text, mid-clause where a continuation follows. Peaks are scattered and the circuit fails faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on commas and function words (that, to, in) in technical text about challenges, difficulties, errors and complications, where the next words are likely to name a problem or obstacle. Silent on the same commas in neutral technical contexts.
result.label: Function words before problems/difficulties

result.description: Fires on function tokens (and, of, commas, colons, "wave") in physics text about waves and wave-particle duality, where the next word is likely a wave or particle term like packet or discrete. Silent on "and" in general earth-science text.
result.label: Wave physics connectives

result.description: Fires on ' (' and a few other function tokens (' their', ' like', ':') in technical or linguistic explanatory text, especially after a quoted example word like 'child' (to children). Weak, mixed circuit; silent on many ' (' tokens, such as abbreviations.
result.label: Parenthesis after quoted example word

result.description: Fires on function words (to, comma, are, and, the) in abstract technical text about databases and system components, mid-clause where a database-related noun or verb comes next. Silent on many other 'to' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in database technical text

result.description: Fires on the word right after the opening "With the" of a document, where a rise-of-something noun begins (emer-gence, rise, advent, Industrial, widespread). Silent on the same tokens when they appear mid-sentence.
result.label: Document-initial "With the emergence" noun

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (' the', ',', ' who', ' methods', ' urban') in expository academic or technical prose. Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is diffuse with no discriminative members, and its logits are mixed.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on tokens following "rapid" in phrases like "rapid pace of", "rapid expansion of", "rapid growth of", i.e. words continuing a "rapid X (of)" phrase about fast change. Members include "rapid" detectors. Silent on "the pace" without "rapid".
result.label: Words following "rapid" (pace of)

result.description: Fires on the first or second piece of a name or word at the start of a document or list line (e.g. ' Em' in Emily, ' Steven', ' Jeff'). Silent on names later in a list of famous authors. Mixed evidence, low faithfulness.
result.label: Name-start pieces at line start

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' it', 'ures', ' system') in definitional passages about systems and scalability; the logits favor '-ability' nouns. Silent on ' the' in other topics, and the circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Systems/scalability text function words

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'ative' piece of "narrative" (also on 'and' or 'in' right after "narrative structures"), in essays on literature and art movements. It stays silent on some 'narr|ative' cases, so the extra condition is unclear.
result.label: narr-ative suffix in literary essays

result.description: Fires on function words (to, for, it, which, the) in explanatory text about data scaling, preprocessing and statistics, mostly in the opening of technical definitions. Silent on many ' to' tokens elsewhere. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Function words in data-scaling explanations

result.description: Fires on varied words in IT governance/compliance text, such as "ensure", "ensuring that", "IT" and "data", where the sentence is about making sure technology or organizational goals are met. It is silent on "data" after "and" in lists. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: IT governance 'ensure' contexts

result.description: Fires on "of" after nouns like development, collapse, use, utilization in Iron Age/ancient-history text, plus occasional "1", " in", " saw". Silent on many other "of" cases in similar text, so the boundary is unclear. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: "of" after nouns in Iron Age text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in academic or mathematical text, including digits inside years (1883, 1962), ' book' and ' and' in author lists. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in academic text

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on scattered tokens (' and', ' decode', ' sound', ' better') in technical text about algorithms and AI. Silent on many ' and' tokens in lists. Members are generic and low-specificity, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered tokens in technical algorithm text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (that, a, The, the, of, commas) in expository text about the Index of Forbidden Books and similar essays. The peak tokens are mixed and the contrast has the same tokens silent, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in essays

result.description: Fires on the '0' right after a leading '2' in years of the 2000s (2000, 2001, 2009, 20th century). It stays silent on '0' in later positions, as in 1920s or 1980s.
result.label: '0' in 2-0-xx years

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cul' at the start of "culinary" (also "culminating"). It is strongest after "and", "by", "of" or "help" in food and cooking text. It stays silent on some "culinary" contexts, such as after "realm of" and "towards".
result.label: ' cul' in culinary

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' st' when it begins a longer word, most strongly in "striving/strive" after a subject and adverb (e.g. "still striving"). Weaker on "stakeholder" and "starring". It predicts continuations like "riv".
result.label: ' st' start of "striving"

result.description: Fires on commas and "and"/"or" inside lists of color names (green, orange, and purple), where another color is likely to come next. Stays silent on "and" in lists of non-color items like techniques or effects.
result.label: Separators in color-name lists

result.description: Fires on ' as' used in a role or function sense after verbs like serve, act, used, or "not only", introducing what something serves as (e.g., "serving as a base"). Silent on "such as", causal "as", and "as well".
result.label: ' as' in role/function sense

result.description: Fires on the word piece " electro" (as in electrostatic, electrolysis, electrode), mostly in chemistry text about ionic bonds and electrochemistry. It predicts continuations like "static", "weak" and "chem".
result.label: " electro" prefix in chemistry

result.description: Fires on the final 'ry' in "Brønsted-Lowry" (acid-base theory), supported by chemistry members for Lewis, bases, OH and the hyphen. It stays silent on 'ry' in the name "Humphry".
result.label: Lowry in Brønsted-Lowry

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fost' as the start of "foster", usually after "can" or "to" with a subject that promotes something. It stays quiet in some cases where "fostering" or "fosters" starts a clause.
result.label: ' fost' in foster (verb)

result.description: Fires on the piece "une" in "imm|une", mainly when followed by "system" or "system's" in the windows. It is silent on "imm|une" before "response" or "cells", so it seems to need a system-type continuation.
result.label: imm-une before "system"

result.description: Fires on ' principle' when it starts a sentence right after a full stop, as the subject of a new sentence (e.g. "principle of conservation of…"). It stays quiet when 'principle' follows an adjective or determiner such as "fundamental" or "this".
result.label: Sentence-initial ' principle'

result.description: Fires on adjective-ending suffixes (-ive, -ic, -ative, -ble, -ous, -al) or adjectives like "fine" and "right" that end an item in a list of adjective types or categories, e.g. "coarse, medium or fine". Silent on the same suffixes in other contexts.
result.label: Adjective suffix in type lists

result.description: Fires on verbs like "is", "are", "have", "operate" right after a subject in economics definitions of efficiency or equilibrium (e.g. "where production is", "firms operate"). It stays quiet on "is" in cooking or other non-economic text.
result.label: Copular verbs in economics definitions

result.description: Fires most often on the word piece ' prov' (prove/provisions) but also on scattered function words and commas in explanatory academic text. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: ' prov' plus scattered function words
'lor' inside chlor- words
result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'lor' after 'ch' in chemistry words like chloride, chlorophyll, chloroplast. It stays silent when 'lor' starts a word (lorophyll). Weak activity on a few scattered tokens in chemistry text.

Fires on function words and connectors (and, to, on, for, commas) that continue a list or verb phrase in abstract expository text describing what a process or field "involves". Contrast shows it is silent on some 'and' joining nouns.
result.label: Connectors in 'involves…' expository lists

result.description: Fires mostly on a bare 't' token (apostrophe-t, as in "'t" after a stripped negation stem) and sometimes on ' and', 's', ' any'. Silent on ordinary "n't" contractions like "isn't", "don't". Members detect 't' and 'not' tokens. Weak and mixed.
result.label: Stray 't' after apostrophe, not n't

result.description: Fires on the prefix ' un' in the middle of a sentence, typically after "to" or a verb (e.g. "to un|cover", "un|ravel", "un|tangle"). Silent when ' un' starts the document. Members are ' un' detectors.
result.label: ' un' prefix before verb stem

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Th" (also " in") when a word like Thermodynamics or Theme is being started, mostly after "Law of". Predicts continuations such as "erm". Silent on ordinary running text.
result.label: " Th" word-start, Thermodynamics

result.description: Fires on "to" (or "in") right after causal verbs like "leading", "led", "resulting", where a consequence follows. Silent on other uses of "to" such as "extends to" or "approach to". Predicts outcome words like increased, improved, greater.
result.label: Causal "leading to / resulting in"

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " aut" at the start of a longer word, such as autocorrelation, autonomy, autocracy or autism. It fires most strongly in autocorrelation, and its logits favour continuations like "ocr".
result.label: ' aut' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' green' (greenhouse, greenery, green chemistry, green marketing), mostly in environmental text, as a prefix-like word predicting continuations such as 'house' or 'ery'. Members are mainly green/color detectors.
result.label: ' green' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " as" when it begins a conjunction or comparison clause, often after a comma (", as well as", "as its harmony..."). It stays silent on " as" in "such as" and "serve as".
result.label: Conjunctive ' as' after clause

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " im" that begins "imputation"/"imputed" in statistics text about missing data. Members are mostly " im" prefix detectors. Weak elsewhere (" settlement", "sch").
result.label: " im" start of imputation

result.description: Fires on enabling/allowing words (' for' after "allows", "enabling", "instantaneous", "enables") in tech or traffic text about real-time feedback and data. It stays silent on "allows for" in generic improvement or efficiency contexts.
result.label: Enabling words in real-time traffic feedback

result.description: Fires on possessive determiners (' their', ' its', possessive 's/') that start a subject noun phrase, often in biology or science text, where an abstract noun like structures, enzymes or adaptation comes next. Silent after prepositions like 'around their' or 'Despite their'.
result.label: Possessive starting a subject phrase

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "Battle" in named battles (Battle of Bull Run, Battle of the Somme). It stays silent on other " of" uses such as "representation of" or "dance of", so it needs the battle-name construction.
result.label: "of" in "Battle of ..."

result.description: Fires mostly on word-fragment tokens, especially 'ust' at the start of "Sustainable/Sustainability", plus 'ques' and some hyphens or mid-word pieces. It seems to predict a word continuation. Mixed evidence, weak faithfulness.
result.label: Word-start fragments, 'Sust' in Sustainable

result.description: Fires on ' property' (also ownership, land) in economics/legal text about property rights and ownership. It stays silent when 'property' follows 'intellectual', so it needs the physical or economic sense, not the IP sense.
result.label: Property (not intellectual) in economics

result.description: Fires mainly on commas separating items in a list of abstract nouns (traditions, customs, arts, languages), plus a few word pieces like 'ically' and ' V'. Silent on commas after clauses or introductory phrases.
result.label: Commas in noun lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (commas, "to", "of", " natural", "ye") in passages about dyes, materials and crafts. It seems to predict word continuations like "-les" or "-le". Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered tokens in dye/material text

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "or" in lists of abstract nouns (ideas, feelings, thoughts) in texts about communication, right after the first list item. Silent on similar commas in other lists and topics.
result.label: List separators in communication text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ev' when it begins a longer word such as evaporate, evoke or evidence, following a preceding word. Silent on text without that token. It predicts continuations like 'oke' or 'iden'.
result.label: ' ev' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the article " A" (rarely " a") starting a sentence, right after a paragraph break, especially in technical or academic prose. Members detect " A"/"An" tokens, including before "I" or word pieces.
result.label: Sentence-initial " A" article

result.description: Fires on example-introducing words (' like', 'such as', 'including', 'include') that follow text about collaboration and communication tools, just before a list of examples such as shared workspaces. Silent on 'like' in other topics such as applications and monitoring.
result.label: Examples intro in collaboration text

result.description: Fires on " on" right after "embark/embarked/embarking", anticipating a journey, venture or undertaking. It stays silent on " on" after other words like "relies", "drawing" or "is".
result.label: "on" after embark

result.description: Fires on mid-compound pieces where a word continues: the hyphen in "on-the-go"/"on-the-move" and "stal" in "crystal" followed by "lattice". Silent on "Crystal" at document start. Mixed and weakly consistent.
result.label: Hyphen in on-the-go; crystal 'stal'

result.description: Fires on an apostrophe that begins a contraction ('s, 'll, 're) right after a sentence-ending period, where "It" or "They" seems to be missing. It stays silent on apostrophes inside words, such as possessives and "don't".
result.label: Apostrophe after period starting contraction

result.description: Fires on the word piece "Econom"/"econom" (Economics, economists, Economic) at the start of the word, before it is completed. It predicts continuations like "ics", "ist", "ic". Quiet on other academic fields such as Engineering.
result.label: Econom- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on a hyphen or dash joining a first word to a repeated or paired second element (non-verbal, word-to-word, consonant-vowel), in linguistics text. Silent on hyphens in compounds like cutting-edge, rule-based, pre-trained.
result.label: Hyphen in linguistic paired compounds

result.description: Fires on ' the' / ' The' when it begins a new sentence or heading, often after a period with no capital (e.g. ".[[ the]] 19…"). It stays silent on mid-sentence ' the' after verbs or prepositions.
result.label: Sentence-initial 'the' after period

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' of', also ' by', ' involve', ' the') right after a subject noun in definitional passages about economic cycles. Silent on many other ' of' tokens, so the pattern is topic-bound and only loosely consistent.
result.label: Function words in economic-cycle definitions

result.description: Fires on " new" as an adjective after verbs like explore, seek, or open to, mostly in creative or artistic text. It predicts a following noun such as ideas, sounds or techniques. Weakly fires on "innovative".
result.label: " new" after explore/seek verbs

result.description: Fires on varied word-start or word-piece tokens (e.g. '1' in "greater than 1", 'W' in acronyms, ' n', 'RA' in RAID) where the word is incomplete or a short symbol, often in math or acronym contexts. Silent on '1' in dates and headings.
result.label: Word-start pieces, math symbols, acronyms

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'igen', mostly in "indigenous" (also in antigen, eigenvalues), after a preceding 'ind'/'ant'/'E' piece. Members are mostly 'igen' detectors plus 'ind-' prefix pieces.
result.label: 'igen' word piece (indigenous)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "quest" inside "sequestration", mostly in carbon sequestration text. Members detect "quest" and other mid-word pieces. The contrast has no "quest" token.
result.label: "quest" in sequestration

result.description: Fires on the end of an action noun (manipulation, visualization, exchange, distribution, retrieval, transfer) after "easy/efficient/real-time" or "data" in software or tech descriptions. Silent on "manipulation" in other settings (array manipulation, modulation).
result.label: Process noun after easy/data in tech text

result.description: Fires on commas, "through", apostrophes and similar function tokens in text about early or ancient origins (early bilaterians, nervous systems, prehistoric writing). Seems to anticipate historical or developmental continuation; silent on commas in other historical passages.
result.label: Function tokens in early-origins history text

result.description: Fires mostly on " memory" in computer-science text about memory management, allocation and hierarchy, as the head noun after words like virtual, physical, or efficient. It stays quiet in "execution time and memory usage" and "main memory hierarchy".
result.label: memory in computing/memory management

result.description: Fires on connective words like " but", " where", " with", "who" that extend an analogy or simile in explanatory text (e.g., sets as clubs/bouncers, puzzles "but with added..."). Silent on "not just X, but also" constructions.
result.label: Connectives extending analogies

result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "work-life" (e.g. work-life balance), after "work". It stays quiet on hyphens in other compounds such as AI-based or long-term. Many members detect hyphens generally, others detect "work".
result.label: Hyphen in work-life

result.description: Fires on 'zone'/'zones' (and 'longitude', 'lines') in time-zone and geography text, especially after 'time' or 'hour'. Weaker firing on word endings like 'ories' and 'ems'. Members are mostly diffuse context features.
result.label: time zone / longitude geography words

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' prof' in "profound", ' in', commas) in essay-like academic text, especially about religious symbols and abstract meaning. Often silent on ' in' elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Mixed tokens in symbolism essays

result.description: Fires on function words (to, of, as, in, improved) in generic text about manufacturing/engineering benefits, where the next word would be a production-related noun (assembly, operator, production). Silent on ' to' in business/abstract text.
result.label: Function words in manufacturing benefit text

result.description: Fires mostly on commas inside long lists of parallel items (e.g. reflexive pronouns "herself, itself, ourselves,"), and sometimes on "such as" or "to" introducing examples. Silent on commas after an introductory phrase or clause.
result.label: Commas within enumerated lists

result.description: Fires on plural economic nouns (prices, wages, markets, rates, services) as the subject of an economics passage, especially in factor-market or price-setting explanations. Silent on 'markets' inside prepositional phrases such as 'financial markets'.
result.label: Plural economic subject nouns (prices, wages)

result.description: Fires on ' its' (occasionally ' their') right after a sentence-opening preposition like "With its" or "Despite its", where a descriptive noun such as "rich history" follows. Silent on 'its' after mid-sentence "due to" or "for".
result.label: Sentence-initial "With its" possessive

result.description: Fires on adverbs like "greatly", "widely", "significantly" right after "vary" or "differ", where a variation adverb comes before "depending on" or "across". Members detect vary/differ verbs and these adverbs.
result.label: Adverb after vary/differ

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ('als' in metals lists, ' of', commas, ' like') in technical or science passages, within enumerations of examples or classifications. Silent on 'als' in other words like integrals. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Mixed tokens in science enumerations

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verb pieces (of, which, with, -ating, both) inside technical expository text on math, computing and logic. Peak tokens are scattered, and the target is silent on some of its own peak tokens, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Technical text function words, mixed

result.description: Fires on a comma ending a clause about interdisciplinary or academic integration (fields, disciplines, laws), where a participial or elaborating phrase follows (fostering, inspiring, as well as, with). Silent on commas in other academic text.
result.label: Comma after interdisciplinary integration clause

result.description: Fires on " of" right after a network-like noun (web, network, networks, maze, ballet) in phrases like "complex web of", expecting a plural noun of connections or relationships. Silent on "of" after exchange, development or combination.
result.label: "of" after web/network nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' Trade', 'iff' in tariff, ' and', ' on, ' average') mostly in economics/trade and academic text. Stays silent on ' Trade' in fixed names like World Trade Organization. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered economics/trade tokens

result.description: Fires on " how" introducing a clause after study/understanding verbs in academic text (e.g. "the study of how", "examining how", "insights into how"). Silent on some " how" uses in other contexts, such as "exploring how" in an art/interdisciplinary passage.
result.label: "how" after study/understand phrases

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after "energy" (energy-efficient), predicting "efficient" next. It stays silent on hyphens after other words like cutting-, decision-, long-, and only weakly fires after "space-".
result.label: Hyphen after "energy"

result.description: Fires on varied word-ending pieces (-ated, -ises, -ed, -ured, -ation) and on ' equilibrium' in chemistry-like text, but is silent on some ' equilibrium' tokens. Mixed, low-consistency peaks with no clear shared role.
result.label: Mixed suffix pieces and 'equilibrium'

result.description: Fires on varied function words and abstract nouns (desire, quest, and, the, an) in art-criticism prose, where a noun like "desire for" or "possibilities" is expected next. Members are mostly art/artist-themed context. Mixed peaks, low consistency.
result.label: Art-writing abstract noun/function slots

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'son' piece inside "consonance"/"consonantal" in linguistics and phonetics text. It stays silent on 'son' in surnames like Erikson or Jakobson. It also fires weakly on scattered words such as ' various' and ' as'.
result.label: 'son' in consonant words

result.description: Fires on varied connective tokens (' through', ' and', ' track', commas) in generic text about creative techniques, such as audio and music segmentation or literary mixing. It is silent on ' through' in other creative-expression phrases. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Connectives in creative technique lists
' not' after auxiliary verb (not only)
result.description: Fires on ' not' directly after an auxiliary like has/had/were/may, especially in "has not only", "not just", "not always" patterns. Members are ' not' detectors that push toward only/just/necessarily/always. Silent on 'not' in other positions, e.g. after "are" in relative clauses.

Fires on the word piece 'igen' (occasionally 'ogen') when it completes a word, mostly in "antigen/antigenic" in immunology text, but also in eigenvalues and epigenetic. It needs the preceding word piece, e.g. 'ant', 'E', 'ep'.
result.label: 'igen' word piece (antigen)

result.description: Fires on plural-noun-like tokens about characters or relationships (' characters', 'acters', 'ationships', ' populations') in abstract essay-style text about people and stories. It is silent on ' characters' in many other contexts, and the reason is unclear.
result.label: Plural 'characters' and relationships nouns

result.description: Fires on the word " energy" in physics text, especially after "the", "kinetic", "quantized" or "discrete" (e.g. "the energy gap", "the energy difference"). It stays silent when "energy" opens the text with no preceding context.
result.label: ' energy' in physics context

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also commas in number lists, ' and') mid-sentence in linguistics and academic prose, where the next word is likely an abstract noun like "understanding" or "unique". It is silent on many other ' the' tokens, and the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' the' before abstract noun, linguistics

result.description: Fires on the word " building" (and "Building") in the construction/architecture context, both as a noun modifier (building permits, building systems) and as the verb form (building bridges). Predicts continuations like "blocks" or "up".
result.label: ' building' token detector

result.description: Fires on function words (' of', ' and', ' the', ' be') and some nouns in abstract academic prose about linguistics, structures and systems. It is silent on the same ' of' in similar morphology text, so the evidence is mixed and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (closing parenthesis, pieces of "laser", "strand", "multipotency") in science text, mostly physics and biology. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse and failed. Specific triggers are unclear.
result.label: Scattered science-text tokens, diffuse

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ensive" in "comprehensive", after "compreh". Members include detectors of that piece plus "detailed"/"thorough" words, all pointing to a noun like understanding, coverage or plans.
result.label: "ensive" in comprehensive

result.description: Fires on the ending of physics field names, mainly "ics" in "Mechanics" and " Theory", in lists of academic topics. It stays silent on "ics" in other words like Aesthetics, Dynamics, Infographics and Plastics.
result.label: Physics field name endings (Mechanics)

result.description: Fires on ' the' (rarely ' a'/' its') right after verbs of exceeding or surpassing, like "exceed the", "surpasses the", "exceeds a", in physics-threshold text. It stays silent on ' the' after verbs like "understanding" or "defines".
result.label: 'the' after exceed/surpass

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'icul' mainly inside "meticulous(ly)", also in "curriculum". Members are detectors of 'icul' and similar mid-word pieces that continue into -ous/-ously. It stays silent on some 'meticulously' cases.
result.label: 'icul' in meticulous

result.description: Fires on possessive determiners (my, your, his, her, our) mostly when they are listed or discussed in grammar text about possessive forms. It also fires on ordinary 'my' before a noun. Predicts kin or relational nouns next.
result.label: Possessive determiners (my, your, his)

result.description: Fires on ' based' right after a noun phrase, where it begins a "based on X" phrase (e.g. "categorize data into classes based on previous examples"). Members detect based/depending/relies and push toward " on".
result.label: "based" before "on"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (commas, 'of', 'as', 'that', 'od') in expository, explanatory text about science or English grammar. No dominant token, and the logits are mixed. The evidence is weak and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks in expository text

result.description: Fires on the piece "ological" completing "technological" (techn|ological), before nouns like advancements, innovation, progress. Silent when "ological" stands alone without the "techn" prefix.
result.label: techn-ological word completion

result.description: Fires on ' new' in the idiom "breathe new life into", where the next word is expected to be "life". It stays silent on ' new' in ordinary phrases like "creates new meanings".
result.label: "new" in "breathe new life"

result.description: Fires on connecting words (' of', ' and', 'merges') in text about musical theatre and music, where the next word continues a music/theatre phrase. It stays silent on ' and' in other topics such as transport, governance and code.
result.label: Connector words in musical theatre text

result.description: Fires on " based" (occasionally "built"/"centered") right after "are/is" in "X is/are based on", where a preposition "on" is expected next. Silent on the contrast, where "organ..." appears without this construction.
result.label: "are/is based on" construction

result.description: Fires on varied function words (and, that, a, of, '.') inside passages about fiscal and economic policy, where upstream members signal economics/government context. It is silent on the same '.' in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in fiscal-policy text

result.description: Fires on a modifier noun or word piece inside a compound noun phrase after "a/an" in analogies or descriptions (ball|room, story|telling, love story, text|book, comedy club). It predicts the head noun that completes the compound.
result.label: Compound-noun first part in analogies

result.description: Fires on " between" after a noun of conflict, tension, or relation (competition, rift, war, gap), mainly in geopolitical or historical text, where two parties come next. Quiet on the contrast text, which has no such "between".
result.label: ' between' after conflict/relation nouns

result.description: Fires on " the" (or "a") right after verbs like "laid", "established", "laid down", "paved" that introduce foundational work, predicting words like foundation, basis, groundwork. Silent on "the" after ordinary prepositions.
result.label: "the" after laid/established foundation verbs

result.description: Fires on conditional/temporal subordinators " if" and " when" (also "If", "When") that open a clause, mostly in expository economics or math text. Members are detectors of if/when/where tokens. Predicts a following subject pronoun.
result.label: Conditional 'if'/'when' clause openers

result.description: Fires mostly on hyphens joining name or compound parts (Sapir-Whorf, Ford-Fulkerson), plus scattered tokens like ' food', ' aqu', ' the' in technical text. Silent on some hyphens (first-, codon-), so the pattern is mixed and the condition unclear.
result.label: Hyphen in name compounds, mixed

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative ' these' in abstract or academic prose, mostly as a determiner after a verb or preposition (monitor these, drawing on these) before a plural noun. It is silent on some uses, such as after a semicolon or 'within these'.
result.label: ' these' as object determiner

result.description: Fires diffuse across mixed positions (commas, 'the', word pieces, 'processing') in technical or academic text. It pushes against conjunction-like next words (when, while, before, only). The evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Diffuse mixed tokens in technical text

result.description: Fires on the word " backup" (all 64 peaks) in data-protection and disaster recovery text, where it modifies a following noun like schedules, restoration or procedures. Members are recovery/response/planning detectors.
result.label: ' backup' in disaster recovery text

result.description: Fires on the token ' convey' when it is a word stem that is continued by a suffix, as in "conveyance" or "conveyor". It stays silent on ' convey' used as a plain verb ("to convey meaning"). It predicts suffix pieces.
result.label: ' convey' as stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on the final piece of technical physics/engineering terms, mostly 'ator' completing "Stellarator", also 'on' and similar endings in plasma/fusion text. Silent on 'ator' in unrelated words like "instabilitator".
result.label: Stellarator word-ending piece

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' t' when a longer word is split into pieces, such as t-arm-ac, t-acos, t-ango, t-au, t-ense. It is silent on other tokens, and members are mostly ' t' detectors.
result.label: Split-word initial ' t' fragment

result.description: Fires on the newline/document-separator token (shown as ¶) after a short list item in a list of topic or category headings (e.g. "Abstract nouns." then newline). It stays silent after lists of people's names.
result.label: Newline after topic-list items

result.description: Fires on the verb "ensure" and its inflections (ens-ures, ens-uring, ensure), also weakly on "guarantee", in technical text where a clause follows, predicting " that". Members detect ensure/guarantee tokens.
result.label: "ensure" verb forms before "that"

result.description: Fires on the word fragment " sympt" (start of "symptoms"), usually in health or psychological text. Members detect other split-word beginnings (dise-, ris-, inj-, bar-) that precede a completion like "-oms" or "-ases".
result.label: " sympt" word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered, unrelated tokens (commas, ' of', 'sin', 'ord', word pieces) with no clear shared pattern. It is silent on most commas, and the members are diffuse, so the circuit is poorly explained.
result.label: Scattered mixed tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on the word " binary" (also "Binary"), mostly as a modifier before nouns like trees, search, operations, logic or fission. Members are binary-token detectors. It was silent on one document-initial " binary" example, so the extra condition is unclear.
result.label: binary token detector

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (navigate, within, in, by, how, the) in abstract academic text about relationships, communication and theory, where a noun phrase on tensions or processes is expected next. Peaks are scattered, and the contrast text is narrative fiction.
result.label: Academic relational-theory function words

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'om' in the middle of longer words, mostly 'on|om|atopoeia' and also cohomology, biomarker, clinometers. Silent on 'om' at the start of a word like 'omatopusop'.
result.label: 'om' inside onomatopoeia-like words

result.description: Fires on the period after a section number at the start of a document or heading (e.g. "### 2." or "4.2."), where a title or subsection number follows. Silent on sentence-ending periods after text.
result.label: Period after section number

result.description: Fires mostly on ' back' in "more than just a back|drop" (setting as backdrop), also ' watch' and a few other word-start pieces. It is silent on 'backdrop' after adjectives or plural uses. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: 'back' in "just a backdrop"

result.description: Fires on the capitalized token ' A' when it begins a sentence or section, especially right after a heading line or at document start (e.g. 'Aesthetic' split as ' A'+'esthetic'). Members detect ' A'/' An' and ' a'.
result.label: Sentence-initial ' A' after heading

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verb pieces (' for', ' under', ' of', ' carried', ' want') in expository text, often cooking or science, where a preposition or complement is expected. Peak tokens are varied and the circuit is diffuse and weak.
result.label: Diffuse function words in cooking/science text

result.description: Fires on the word "role" (and "Ro|le") as the head noun of a "The (adj) role of X" title-like phrase, often at document start in economics, tech or religion text. It stays silent on "play an important role in" in environmental or biology text.
result.label: "The role of…" noun phrase

result.description: Fires on " the" after "half of", "dawn of", "start of" or "turn of" when a century or era name (20th, 21st, millennium) is about to follow. It stays silent on other "of the" uses.
result.label: "the" before century/era after part-of-period phrase

result.description: Fires on word-start or mid-word pieces (' Jeff', ' Fitz', ' nost', Cyrillic 'ово') in list-like text of short items, such as names or terms one per line. Weak, mixed evidence; the logits are not coherent.
result.label: Name/word pieces in line lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cor' when it begins "coral" (e.g. "coral bleaching"), in coral/reef text. Members mostly detect ' cor' itself, including its "corrosion" use. The contrast suggests it needs the coral-style continuation or context.
result.label: ' cor' piece in coral

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' cru' (predicting "cial") in "crucial", typically after "is", "making it/them", or "a". Members are mostly ' cru' detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: ' cru' start of "crucial"

result.description: Fires on words for political self-rule or liberation (independence, freedom, autonomy, self-determination, liberation) in text about colonial or national struggles. It stays silent on the decolonization passage about Vietnam, so it needs the sought-after-freedom framing.
result.label: Independence/freedom in anti-colonial context

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (that, the, of, ed, Robert) inside linguistics-themed text, such as language identity and vowel shifts. Members mostly push language-related next words. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on the final suffix piece of an abstract noun (existence, isolation, urgency, simplicity) when it ends a topic-title or concept-list entry, such as in lists of philosophy or academic subjects. Silent on concrete-topic lists.
result.label: Abstract noun endings in topic lists

result.description: Fires on " across" (occasionally the " different" right after it) when it introduces a spread over varied groups, regions or domains, as in "varied across different literary periods". It pushes towards plural scope words like regions.
result.label: "across" before varied categories

result.description: Fires on the word piece "erm" in "Thermodynamics" (also in therm- words like thermal, exothermic), where it predicts the continuation "odynamics". Members are mostly "erm" detectors and thermo-related pieces.
result.label: "erm" in Thermodynamics

result.description: Fires on ' field' used as a modifier before a noun, as in "field surveys", "field tests", "field recording", "fieldwork". It stays silent on ' field' as a head noun in "in the field of" or "this field".
result.label: ' field' as noun modifier

result.description: Fires on ' the' (also ' and') starting a new clause after a comma in technical text about data extraction, accuracy and challenges. Members suggest a context of difficulties or errors. Silent on many other clause-initial ' the' cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Clause-initial 'the' in difficulty-themed technical text

result.description: Fires on the word " reading" (the activity or skill, e.g. reading comprehension, reading speed), often as a modifier before a noun. Members are detectors of read/reading tokens. Predicts continuations like "comprehension".
result.label: Word "reading" before comprehension
'ron' in "acronym"
result.description: Fires on the piece 'ron' inside the word "acronym" (ac-ron-ym), predicting the suffix 'ym'. Much weaker on other tokens such as ' Rock' or ' Pop'. Upstream members are mostly 'ron' detectors, plus earlier 'ac' pieces.

Fires on the word-piece " meas" at the start of "measuring"/"measurable", mostly after verbs or prepositions like "involves" or "in". It pushes toward completions such as "uring". Members detect meas-, manufact-, metric, quant- and similar word starts.
result.label: " meas" word-start before "uring"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' prof' mostly when it begins "profound" (also proficient, profits), after words like a, more, most, as. Silent on some ' prof' contexts, so it is a word-start piece with a context need.
result.label: ' prof' piece of "profound"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ill' after a verb context like "can/to" where "illuminate" is the expected continuation; weaker on ' typ' and similar prefixes. Silent on ' ill' in "illumination" used as a noun after an adjective.
result.label: 'ill' predicting 'illuminate' (verb)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and modifiers (' which', ',', ' that', ' advanced', ' l') mostly in materials/composites or economics text, where a noun phrase or relative clause is being extended. Peaks are inconsistent and it stays silent on many ' which' tokens.
result.label: Scattered connectors in materials text

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'en' in "teen(age)", ' ass', ' un', ' or', and some function words, where a word is incomplete and a suffix may follow (logits favour 'hood', 'wards'). Silent on 'en' in "nomenclature" and "Listen". Mixed evidence.
result.label: Word-fragment 'en' in teen-like words

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' st' when it begins "stakeholders", in lists of people or groups such as "engineers and other st-". It is silent in a contrast example where "stakeholder" follows "emphasizes".
result.label: ' st' starting "stakeholders"

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns or modals/infinitive 'to' (that, can, could, which, to) right after a noun for built structures or buildings, in engineering text, where a verb about structural function (withstand, support, reach) comes next. Silent on 'that' in non-engineering clauses.
result.label: Structure nouns followed by that/can

result.description: Fires on the noun ' use' in phrases like "its use of", "innovative use of", "the use of", where it is followed by "of" and a technique or tool. Silent on other tokens in the contrast.
result.label: noun 'use' before 'of'

result.description: Fires on the piece 'pos' inside the word "Prepositions" (pre|pos|itions), in grammar headings about types of prepositions. Silent on 'pos' in "positional" after a sentence break.
result.label: 'pos' in "prepositions"

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative " this" when it follows a verb or preposition like explore, understand, shed light on, and introduces an abstract noun (issue, topic, phenomenon). Predicts nouns like issue/topic. Silent on sentence-initial or other " this" uses.
result.label: " this" before abstract topic noun

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-word pieces (famil, end, istic, M) and some function words like " of" in academic text. Peaks look unrelated and the circuit is diffuse, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-word fragments, unclear

result.description: Fires mostly on commas (also "and", "or", "as") inside lists of examples after "such as" or "like", e.g. "vegetables like carrots, beets". Silent on commas before "including" or after clauses. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Commas in example lists

result.description: Mixed, low-consistency target peaking on commas and semicolons in lists of technical/academic terms, plus scattered word pieces (' aer', 'urbed', ' classical'). Members are generic list and biology/science context features; evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: List separators in technical text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' clause', ' and', ' supporting', 'cluding', ' to') in expository text about language, grammar and structured components. Peaks are mixed; silent on 'clause' after dependent/subordinate/independent. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Grammar/structure exposition, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ative' completing "narr-ative" (narrative), in text about storytelling and literary technique. It stays silent on 'ative' in other words like creative, formative and comparative.
result.label: 'ative' in "narrative"

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Am' in "Daniel Kahneman and Am(os Tversky)", plus scattered weaker hits such as 'V', 'n' in formulas and ' humans'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is low-faithfulness.
result.label: ' Am' in Kahneman and Amos

result.description: Fires on ' chem' as the start of "chemists/chemistry" right after a verb like "allows", "helps", "enables", predicting the "-ists" ending. It is silent on ' chem' at the start of text or in noun phrases like "physical chemistry".
result.label: ' chem' after helps/allows verbs

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'ap' in ther-ap-ies and 'hed' in poly-hed-ra, where the word is unfinished and a suffix such as '-ies' or '-ra' comes next. It is silent on the whole word 'therapy'.
result.label: Mid-word fragment 'ap'/'hed' in technical words

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (term, commas, "and", "are", "phase", "case") in expository academic or technical prose, often right after a subject noun or compound modifier, before a predicate or elaboration. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse expository mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on the word completing a global-scale reference (Earth, universe, world, surface) right after a percentage or fraction quantity such as "27% of the universe" or "96% of the world's". Silent on Earth in other constructions, like "history of Earth".
result.label: Percent-of-whole: Earth/universe/world

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ed' when it is a mid-word fragment after an initial piece, as in h-ed-ging, Fe-ed-back, bip-ed-al, h-ed-dle. It stays silent on 'ed' used as a past-tense suffix (confront-ed, undervalu-ed).
result.label: 'ed' inside word (h-ed-ging)

result.description: Fires on relative/connective words (that, which, it after "as", "not only") that follow a cooking or technique description and introduce a clause about what the process does or contributes. Silent on "that" in other relative clauses.
result.label: Connectives after cooking process descriptions

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' stim' at the start of stimulate/stimulating/stimuli, before the 'ul' continuation. Predicts 'ulate', 'ulating', 'ulator'. Members are mostly other ' stim' detectors, plus similar prefixes like insp, motiv and mod.
result.label: ' stim' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on function words (from, of, the, by, and) in essay-style text about art, music and culture such as Flamenco, mostly after a verb or noun heading a phrase. Peaks are scattered, and the circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: Function words in arts/culture prose
'sten' in 'sustenance'
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'sten' inside 'sustenance' (after 'su'), predicting the suffix 'ance'. Only weakly fires on ' optim' in 'optimizing'.

Fires on varied function words and word pieces (the, to, time, -, gas, light) in technical, academic expository text, where the next word is a technical noun or compound. Silent on 'the' in many other contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Technical text mid-phrase function words

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (' and', ',', ' of', ' fundamental') inside expository technical or academic text on engineering, traffic and science topics. Peaks are mixed, and the same ' and' stays silent in other contexts, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Function words in technical expository text

result.description: Fires on word pieces in the middle of a longer word that is still being completed, such as ' shed' (before 'ding'), 'or'/'ore' in Pythagoras/Pythagorean, and 'art' in Sartre. It predicts continuation pieces like 'iral' or 'duct'.
result.label: Mid-word fragments (shed, Pythagor-, Sart-)

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments 'medi' (mediated, intermediates) and 'ub' (soluble, solubility) in technical science text, where the word is still incomplete. Predicts word continuations such as -ates or -ated.
result.label: medi/ub word-piece in science terms

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ain" inside "sust-ain-able/ability" (and "sustain"), in sustainability and environmental-economics text. It stays quiet on some other "sustain" contexts, such as document starts and business-model phrasing.
result.label: "ain" in sustainable/sustainability

result.description: Fires on the final word piece completing a plural disaster or hazard noun (floods, earthquakes, surges, droughts) in lists of natural disasters and catastrophes. Needs the disaster/hazard topic; it is quiet on unrelated text.
result.label: Plural disaster noun endings

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ron' inside "acronym" (ac-ron-ym), predicting the next piece 'ym'. It stays silent on 'ron' at the start of "ronyms".
result.label: 'ron' in "acronym"

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (dis-, re-, at, to, and) inside abstract text about formal logic, mathematics and philosophy, in the middle of a technical clause. It stays silent on 'dis' in a probability context.
result.label: Logic and math argument connectives
' sought' after a subject
result.description: Fires on the verb ' sought' (rarely ' seeking') right after a subject such as a group, movement or rulers, typically before 'to' plus a verb. Members are detectors of seek/sought/seeks forms.
Fires on ' while' as a clause-linking conjunction after a comma or semicolon, introducing a contrasting or simultaneous second clause. It stays silent on 'all while' mid-phrase.
result.label: clause-joining ' while' after comma

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words, suffixes and punctuation (' holds', ' of', ',', 'ative', ' like') in expository academic prose, mid-phrase after a topical noun. No dominant token; members are diffuse and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase tokens in expository prose

result.description: Fires on verbs like "set", "laid", "paved", "-ing" in the idiom of preparing a foundation: "laid the groundwork", "set the stage", "paved the way". Silent on "a set of" noun use.
result.label: laid/set the groundwork idiom verb

result.description: Fires on connective tokens (",", " that", " of", " and") after abstract nouns in academic text about interpersonal tensions and relational dialectics. Silent on commas in physics text. Peaks are mixed and the logits are unclear.
result.label: Connectives in relational-tension academic prose

result.description: Fires on the token " insight", mainly as the object of "provide(s)/providing" or "gain" in analytical or scientific text (e.g. "provides insight into"). Members are mostly insight-detectors plus provide-object features.
result.label: ' insight' after provide/gain

result.description: Fires mostly on 'PN' in 'VPN' and on '/' and other scattered tokens (um, re, mid-sentence function words). Silent on 'PN' in 'Prime Number Theorem (PNT)'. Members are diffuse and mixed, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: VPN 'PN' piece, mixed tokens

result.description: Mixed peaks: ' of' after duration words like "decades of" or "years of" in Dust Bowl text, plus digits and 'ord'. Silent on ' of' after "evolution of" or "forefront of" in cosmology text. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: "years of" in Dust Bowl text

result.description: Fires on the token " process" as a noun, especially at the start of a sentence or document ("The process of..."), and also in compounds like "process creation". Members are mostly earlier-layer " process" detectors.
result.label: ' process' noun token

result.description: Fires on list-introducing or list-continuing words (include, involves, such as, commas, and) in text about safety, disaster management or security measures, where a list of protective actions or measures follows. Silent on 'include' in generic task lists.
result.label: Safety measures list introducer

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, ' and', ' will', ' of', word pieces, math symbols) with no clear shared token or context. Contrast shows silence on commas too. Logits favor plural nouns weakly. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token, unclear target

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: the 'is' piece inside multi-piece words (Brava-is, Incept-is-ols), plus fragments of LaTeX/physics math notation like a backslash or garbled symbol after F₁ or \(. Silent on 'is' in 'emphasis'.
result.label: 'is' word piece and LaTeX fragments

result.description: Fires mainly on the word " justice" in academic discussion of social/global justice and rights theory (also stray 'amin', 'a'). Silent on one "as well as justice" example, so it seems to need a social-theory noun-phrase use.
result.label: "justice" in social-theory discourse

result.description: Fires on the word piece "aph" inside "metaphysics", "metaphor" and related words, right after "met". Members are mostly "aph" detectors that push toward continuations like "ys" and "ors".
result.label: "aph" in metaphor/metaphysics

result.description: Fires mostly on " for" (sometimes " in", " to") when it starts a new coordinated or parenthetical purpose phrase, such as "and for", "or for", "not for". It stays quiet on "for" directly after an adjective or noun like "critical for" or "support for".
result.label: "for" after conjunction, not after head

result.description: Fires on coordinating words (" or", " also", " and", commas) that join alternative modes or media, as in "on canvas, or in clay" or "not only in print but also in...". It predicts a following preposition such as in, through, at. Silent on "or" joining nouns.
result.label: Coordinators before prepositional alternatives

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after a sentence-opening "In"/"Within" (or similar preposition) in math-topic academic text, as in "In the fundamental study of…". Silent on ' the' after "of" or "explore" mid-sentence.
result.label: "In the" at start of math sentence

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative ' this' when it follows a preposition or verb and introduces a noun phrase (e.g. "into this", "in this", "through this"). It stays silent when ' this' starts a clause or sentence as a subject.
result.label: ' this' after preposition/verb

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'aren' inside "awareness" (e.g. environmental awareness, self-awareness), predicting the completion "ess". Weakly fires on similar mid-word pieces like "dis|reg|ard".
result.label: 'aren' in "awareness"

result.description: Fires on ' documentation' and ' control' (as in "version control") in software-engineering and process-management text, mainly when they follow related terms like "version" or "system"; silent when 'documentation' opens the text.
result.label: Software documentation / version control

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, mainly prime marks inside decade strings like 1950′ and the 'st' of '21st century', plus occasional function words. Peaks are inconsistent and the logits are unclear. The circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Decade prime marks and ordinal 'st'

result.description: Fires mostly on ' on' right after a verb like "putting" (putting on, wearing, walking on), a particle after a verb in analogy-style text. Silent on ' on' after nouns or in other prepositional uses.
result.label: ' on' after putting/verb particle

result.description: Fires on degree/strength qualifiers (' weak', ' strong', ' not', ' clear') in science text describing material or chemical properties, but is silent on 'weak' in weak-bases phrasing. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Strength qualifiers in materials science
' surr' in 'surroundings'
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' surr' at the start of "surroundings", usually after a possessive like "its" or "our". Members detect word-start pieces that continue with "ound" (prof-, surr-, pers-), so it predicts the word continuation.

Fires on mixed tokens: the word piece 'ire' (as in 'satire') and prepositions like ' to', ' for', ' of' after abstract nouns in expository or technical text. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: 'ire' piece and purpose prepositions

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' man' when it is the start of "managing" (or manager), as in "involves managing tasks". It predicts continuations like 'aging' and 'agers'. The contrast text lacks this word piece.
result.label: ' man' starting "managing"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'eth' inside "meth-" words in chemistry text (methane, methalate, methyl), where a word continuation like -ane/-yl follows. Silent on 'eth' starting a fragment after a full stop.
result.label: 'eth' in methane/methyl words

result.description: Fires on tokens in chemistry/atomic-physics text such as 'tons' (protons), ' chemical', ' element(s)', and some function words like ' which'. Members are mostly chemistry detectors. It stays silent on 'protons' in a different context.
result.label: Chemistry and atomic-structure words

result.description: Fires mostly on " increase"/"increases" after "an/significant/large", as in "an increase in brain size", plus scattered mid-word pieces ("ian", "p", "met"). The peaks are mixed and consistency is low. It is silent on one "increase" in an electronics context.
result.label: 'increase' in "an increase in"

result.description: Fires on ' each' as the start of the reciprocal "each other" after a verb plus "with" (interact with each other, understand each other). It stays silent on ' each' after "in" or "of", as in "each person's".
result.label: reciprocal 'each' before 'other'

result.description: Fires on the adjective " severe" (occasionally "extreme", "violent", "significant") placed before a noun of harm or weather, such as droughts, storms, or hardship. Members are detectors of severe/extreme/serious adjectives in negative-event contexts.
result.label: ' severe' before harm/weather nouns

result.description: Fires mainly on the word-piece ' rect' in "Latin rectangles", plus some 'es' and ' Ban' pieces, in math/technical text. Seems to be a mid-word piece in a particular term; the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Latin rect(angles) word piece

result.description: Fires on ' a' right after "in" (also "through", "for") when it starts a manner phrase like "in a predetermined/sequential order". Silent on ' a' after other verbs or prepositions introducing objects. Pushes toward manner words.
result.label: ' a' after 'in' (manner phrase)

result.description: Fires on the standalone token ' c' (a word-initial fragment or a variable like c1, c2), where the next piece completes a word starting with c (cats, cue, cacophony). Members are mostly ' c' detectors.
result.label: Standalone ' c' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' maxim' or ' minim' (also weakly 'mit-ig') right before the suffix '-ize', mostly after "to" in goal clauses ("to maximize", "to minimize"). It predicts 'ize'. It is silent on "which maximizes".
result.label: maxim/minim before -ize

result.description: Fires on ' their' right after a verb like encourage, develop, explore or achieve, where a people-subject's own abilities or qualities come next (their musical talents, their best). It stays silent on 'their' after 'consider' and at the start of a text.
result.label: 'their' after develop/explore verbs

result.description: Fires on ' it' as the subject pronoun starting a new clause after a coordinating conjunction, especially "and it", in explanatory text. Silent on ' it' as an object or after "as", "making", or "While".
result.label: Subject "it" after "and"

result.description: Fires on the word piece "erm" in the middle of split words like self-det|erm|ination, indet|erm|inistic and undet|erm|ined. It predicts a continuation such as "ination" or "ined".
result.label: "erm" inside determ- words

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ry' in "deep-fry" / "deep-frying" in cooking-technique text. Members detect cooking word pieces (saut-é, ro-ast, gr-ill) and 'ry' tokens. Silent on other cooking text without the word.
result.label: 'ry' in deep-fry

result.description: Fires mainly on " electron" in "two-dimensional electron systems/gas" (quantum Hall physics), with a few weak hits on other words. Silent on "electron pair acceptors" in acid chemistry. Members are Hall/conductance detectors.
result.label: Electron in 2D electron systems

result.description: Fires on protect/safeguard/conserve verbs (protect, 'ing' after protect/conserv, 'ard') when a goal object like resources, environment or rights is expected next, as in "efforts to protect". It stays silent on some 'ing' tokens, e.g. after maintain.
result.label: Protect/conserve verb awaiting object
