result.description: Fires mainly on " than" after a comparative (more, less, greater, faster, lower), and weakly on comparison words like "as" after "twice as powerful" or "to" after "superior". Needs the comparative construction.
result.label: Comparative "than" slot

result.description: Fires on " in" right after nouns like advancements, developments, breakthroughs, improvements, where it introduces a field or domain (technology, chemistry). Silent on " in" for dates, locations, or "in order to".
result.label: " in" after advancements/developments

result.description: Peaks mostly on ' domestic' plus scattered function words and punctuation (commas, 'an', 'inter', 'that') in explanatory science/econ text. Mixed and low-consistency; the circuit is weak and the ' domestic' detectors are the only clear part.
result.label: ' domestic' plus scattered function words

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' and', ',', ' to', ' b', ' III') in technical biology/academic text, especially around mitochondrial complexes and cytochromes. The evidence is mixed and the peaks are scattered. It stays silent on ' and' in math and economics lists.
result.label: Scattered function words in biochemistry text

result.description: Fires on the word piece "thesis" at the end of "photosynthesis" (also nucleosynthesis), in biology/biochemistry text. Weaker on other process-word endings like "respiration" and "reproduction".
result.label: Photosynthesis "thesis" ending

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments ' mult' and ' quad' that begin a longer technical word (multifaceted, multidisciplinary, quadrilaterals), where the next piece completes the word. Occasional weak firing on other tokens.
result.label: mult-/quad- word-start prefixes

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces or first words of short list-style headings (e.g. " Cir" in "Circles", " Su" in "Zhou Bi Suan Jing", " Process"), where a word is incomplete or a new list item starts. Peaks are scattered and weakly consistent.
result.label: Word-start pieces in heading lists

result.description: Fires on varied function words and suffixes (to, of, in, about, -ive, -ing) in text about leadership, employees and workplace communication, and pushes toward words like employee, manager, leader, leadership. Silent on 'to' in other topics.
result.label: Leadership/employee context predicting leader words

result.description: Fires on the word piece " real"/" Real" when it is the start of a longer word like realism or realm (Modal realism, realm of), predicting suffixes such as -m, -ms, -ities. Silent on the full word "reality".
result.label: ' real' as start of realism/realm

result.description: Fires on ' formula' (and sometimes ' equation') as a noun in mathematical or scientific text, typically after "the", "a" or "mathematical". It stays silent when the word starts a document with no preceding context.
result.label: ' formula' / ' equation' in math text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ien' in "aud|ien|ces" (audiences), where it is a mid-word fragment. Predicts suffix pieces like 'ces' and 'cies'. Weaker on similar fragments like 'ien' in immunodeficiencies.
result.label: 'ien' in audiences

result.description: Fires on ' than' completing a comparative after "more/greater/faster + adjective or noun". It is silent on "rather than". Logits favor continuations like "ever", "usual", "just", "any".
result.label: Comparative 'than' after more/-er

result.description: Fires on function words (for, of, that, which, -uring, permits) linking a noun or verb to its purpose or result in abstract physics explanations, such as thermal equilibrium enabling consistent measurement. Silent on some identical "allows for" cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Purpose/enabling function words in physics

result.description: Fires on the standalone word-piece ' b' when it is a split-off beginning of a word, such as "dog b|arks" or "a b|ustling". The next token completes the word (bark, bargain, bone). Silent on ordinary words.
result.label: Split-off ' b' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the suffix "ance" in "governance", mainly in corporate governance text about audit committees and boards. It stays silent on "governance" in other contexts, such as when it is followed by frameworks or processes.
result.label: Corporate governance 'ance' suffix

result.description: Fires on nouns like "time", "event", "moment" naming a point in a sequence, in explanations of English verb tenses (past perfect, "a specific point in time", "before another event"). Silent on "time" in other uses.
result.label: Point-in-time noun in tense explanations

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly commas and "and", and also on word pieces like "assign" and "ub", in abstract expository text. The contrast shows commas staying silent in similar text, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered commas in expository text

result.description: Fires mostly on ' for' (also ' to', '.', ' but') after a noun or verb in academic expository prose, e.g. "studied for many years", "groundwork for", "account for". Silent on some ' for' after "basis"/"conditions". Condition unclear.
result.label: ' for' after noun/verb in expository text

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ado' inside "paradox" (par-ado-x, paradoxes, paradoxical). It is silent when 'ado' starts a word, as in "adoxales". Upstream members are mostly 'ado' detectors.
result.label: 'ado' in "paradox"

result.description: Fires on varied function words and short words (likely, for, with, poor, leading, are) in economics and statistics explanatory text, where the next word is likely a noun or verb continuation. Peaks are scattered with low consistency; members are economics-topic detectors.
result.label: Economics/statistics text, scattered function words

result.description: Fires on the capitalized word " Human", mostly at the start of a heading or title such as "Human-Computer", "Human Factors" or "Human Resources". It is weaker in mid-sentence words like "Humanism". Members mostly detect "human"/"Human".
result.label: Capitalized "Human" in headings

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' and' ending a list, 'dough', ' as', ' of', digits, ')') with no coherent pattern. Silent on many ' and' tokens in lists. Members are diffuse and weak, so the circuit is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mixed function-word target

result.description: Fires on the piece "quisition" in "acquisition", mainly in "Language Acquisition" (e.g. "Language Acquisition Device") in linguistics text. It fires more weakly on "language learning" and on "acquisition" outside that area.
result.label: "quisition" in language acquisition

result.description: Fires on ' in' when it starts a prepositional phrase right after a comma, introducing a sentence-level adverbial (e.g. ", in the latter half", ", in its decline"). It stays silent on ' in' after a noun or verb, where it marks location.
result.label: Clause-initial ', in' after comma

result.description: Fires on mixed word-piece positions, most often mid-word ' agre' (before 'ements') and tokens ending a noun in economic/business prose (assets, operations, purchase). Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is diffuse and its members mostly track finance/economics context.
result.label: ' agre' and economic noun endings

result.description: Fires on ' and' or commas after an adjective in a list of adjectives or qualities (e.g. "bounded, simple, and"), where another adjective is expected next. It stays quiet on 'and' joining nouns.
result.label: Adjective-list 'and'/comma before next adjective

result.description: Fires on a standalone space token, mostly right after a markdown "###" heading marker or in lists of numbered items, where a digit like "1" comes next. Members are mainly space-token detectors that boost digits.
result.label: Space before numbered item

result.description: Fires on " others" in the parenthetical "among others" after a list of named people, where a verb comes next. Weaker firing on "and others" and other "etc."-style phrases.
result.label: "among others" after name list

result.description: Fires on the verb "represent" (represents, represented) right after a plural or abstract subject noun, where it means "stands for / constitutes" and is followed by an object like "a significant...". Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: verb "represent" after subject

result.description: Fires on the 'm' piece inside the word "pragmatic" (Prag-m-atic), predicting the continuation "atic". It stays silent on 'm' in other words such as "paradigm" or "realm".
result.label: 'm' in prag-m-atic

result.description: Fires on abstract category nouns like "type", "area", "mode", "field", "position" right before "of", in definitional or explanatory prose about communication, language, or discourse. The next token is probably a noun phrase after "of".
result.label: Category noun before "of"

result.description: Fires on the piece "ict" inside "pict-" words (pictogram, pictographic, pictorial), where it continues the word. It stays silent on "ict" in "depict".
result.label: "ict" in pictogram words

result.description: Fires on 'aging' in the verb 'managing' (the piece after 'man'), and on ' manage', when it takes an object such as resources, tasks or contracts. It stays silent on 'aging' in other words like 'paging' or 'disengaging'.
result.label: 'managing' verb, 'aging' piece

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ',', ' the', 's', ' to') in abstract academic or expository prose. Predicts adjectives or abstract nouns next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse; the contrast shows no clear condition.
result.label: Function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a new word or title, such as ' reven', ' Am', ' G' or ' Per', at the start of a list item or heading in topic-list text. It predicts word continuations like 'put' or 'odes'. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Word-initial fragments in title lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (' the', ',', ' as', ' of', ' just', ' made', ' an') in formal expository text, where a noun is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse and unreliable.
result.label: Diffuse function-word slot in expository text

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ni' in "millennium" (also in "omnipresent"), plus a few other mid-word fragments like ' dr' or ' Commun'. It seems to mark an unfinished word where the suffix comes next.
result.label: 'ni' inside millennium

result.description: Fires on ' general' in the phrase "in general" (also "within general"), where it closes a clause and means "as a whole". Members are mostly ' general' detectors, including those for generalization words.
result.label: "in general" phrase

result.description: Fires mainly on the capital letter "C" inside a chemical formula for a carbonyl group, "(C=O)", in organic chemistry text. It stays silent on "C" in "-C=C-". Weak activation on "to a" in similar chemistry contexts.
result.label: Carbonyl "C" in (C=O)

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and modifiers (of, both, and, common, significant, for) in academic or technical expository text, where a noun or adjective phrase is about to continue. The pattern is diffuse and inconsistent; the contrast shows 'of' often silent.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' f' (also ' F') after a preceding word, most strongly in "Nuclear fission". It also fires on function-variable f(x). Members are ' f' detectors that push toward continuations like 'ission', 'ruits', 'allacy'.
result.label: Split-word ' f' fragment (fission)

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' redund' (before 'ancy'), mainly in data, hardware or software redundancy. Weakly fires on other split word beginnings such as ' quant' and ' legit'. It predicts a word-ending piece like 'ancy'.
result.label: ' redund' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the token ' authentic' (including as the start of 'authenticity'), mostly in writing about dialogue, interactions and experiences. Members are mainly earlier-layer detectors of ' authentic' that boost 'ity'.
result.label: ' authentic' token detector

result.description: Fires on words meaning reduce/decrease/cut down (' reduce', ' reducing', 'asing' in decreasing, 'on' after cut down), where an object like risk, waste, or usage is about to follow. Members detect reduce-type verbs and predict negative objects such as losses, costs, errors.
result.label: Reduce/decrease verbs before objects

result.description: Fires on mixed function words and connectors (and, commas, adjectives after "a", "but", -ing) in expository technical text, where the next word is an adjective or modifier. Peaks are scattered and the contrast is silent on many ' and' tokens, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered connectors in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'fect' in "Perfect", most strongly in lists of English grammar tense names (Future Perfect, Conditional Perfect, Past Perfect). Also fires in "Perfectly" and "Perfect Information". The circuit is mostly 'fect'/'perfect' detectors.
result.label: 'fect' in Perfect (tense names)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly the suffix 'ing' (e.g. "sticking"), plus commas, ' holding' and ' that', in science and technical prose. The 'ing' is silent in many other words, and the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered 'ing' and function-word peaks

result.description: Fires mostly on 'eness' in "politeness", and weakly on commas, 'and' and other mid-phrase tokens in abstract academic text on linguistics and pragmatics. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: politeness 'eness' in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after a small-quantity noun (dash, pinch, bit, splash, punch of), where a mass noun like humor, flavor or color comes next. It stays silent on ' of' after abstract nouns such as part, rules, journey or subtleties.
result.label: ' of' after small-amount nouns

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on ' basic' after "from a" in tech-progress text, plus mid-word pieces like "smo-other" and "Ide-ologies". Silent on "from basic functions". Members are diffuse generic context; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered ' basic' and word pieces

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (Grice's 's, "introducing", "as", "in") inside text about Grice's pragmatics and the Cooperative Principle. Silent on possessive 's in other contexts, so it needs the linguistics/pragmatics topic.
result.label: Grice pragmatics discussion context

result.description: Fires on varied connective tokens (commas, "and", "by", "only", word pieces like "ul") in technical or scientific expository text, such as mining, chemistry or materials. Peaks are scattered and inconsistent, and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Connectives in technical expository text

result.description: Fires on a word-initial fragment of a verb stem (pre-, navig-, em-an, cont-, sp-an) that is followed by a suffix like -ating/-ined/-anning. It predicts verb endings such as 'ining' and 'anning'. It is silent on 'an' inside 'Companies'.
result.label: Verb-stem fragment awaiting suffix

result.description: Peaks mostly on ' fluid' (as in fluidity) and on verbs like 'arises', 'occurs', 'by' that introduce how an error or economic phenomenon comes about. Mixed evidence, low consistency; predicts word-continuation pieces like 'ity'.
result.label: fluid and 'arises/occurs' verbs

result.description: Fires on plural chemical-entity nouns ending a word (monomers, monomer units, active species, ions, elements) in chemistry text about polymerization or bonding. Silent on 'ers' in polymers or ethers.
result.label: Plural chemistry units like monomers

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (by, over, shared, in, providing, lack) in abstract expository prose about systems, culture or society, where a noun phrase is expected next. Peaks are scattered with low consistency, so the pattern is diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on ' or' (also ' nor') joining verbs or participles after a preceding verb, as in "cannot be created or destroyed". It stays quiet when 'or' joins nouns or adjectives, such as "type or other reactions".
result.label: 'or' joining verbs/participles

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' w' (space-w) when it starts a longer word, like "widespread", "wonders", "wavelength", "wool". It predicts word continuations such as 'ides', 'elf', 'onders'. It is quiet after "as well as" and "of".
result.label: Word-initial ' w' fragment

result.description: Fires on a standalone space token that comes right before a number, typically a year like "200…" or "191…", as in "culminating in the [ ]200". It is silent on many similar spaces, so it needs some further context.
result.label: Space token before year digits

result.description: Fires on the word " intended" as a modifier before a noun, as in "the intended message/meaning/audience". Members are detectors of "intended", "desired" and similar words that predict nouns like message, purpose or use.
result.label: " intended" before a noun

result.description: Fires on " the" right after the verb "laid" (also "setting/paving/providing the") in the idiom of laying the groundwork or foundation. Predicts words like ground, foundation, basis. Silent on " the" after other verbs or prepositions.
result.label: "laid the" groundwork idiom

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' processed', ' in', ' amplitude', ' spatial', ' range') in expository technical or organizational text, where a measurable quantity or attribute noun is expected next. Members predict measure/rating/data words. Peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: Measurement-context technical prose words

result.description: Fires on words expressing interconnection or integration (intertwined, integrated, interlaces) in abstract finance/management prose, where "with" typically follows. Weak activity on "shift". Circuit members are mostly finance/business topic context.
result.label: Intertwined/integrated with (business prose)

result.description: Fires on " correction" in the compound "error correction", mostly in quantum or coding-theory text. It predicts the next words as codes, algorithms or schemes. Earlier members detect "correction" and "error".
result.label: error correction (' correction')

result.description: Fires on ' by' introducing a means or method clause ("by + gerund") after a colon, comma or semicolon, following a complete clause. It is quieter on ' by' directly after a noun phrase with no punctuation.
result.label: ' by' introducing means clause

result.description: Fires on the word "customer"/"Customer", especially as a heading or modifier in business text about service, support and engagement. It pushes toward continuations like service, retention, care and relationships.
result.label: Customer token in business text

result.description: Fires on the word piece " gravit" (start of "gravitational") in physics text, when it is mid-sentence and the next piece is likely "ational". Silent when it opens the text as the first token.
result.label: ' gravit' before 'ational'

result.description: Fires on the word " reason" (also " reasons") as a noun in philosophical or Enlightenment-style text, e.g. "prioritized reason", "focus of rationalism is on reason". Members are mostly " reason" token detectors.
result.label: ' reason' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' while' (also 'whilst', 'whereas') as a conjunction joining a second clause or participle after a complete clause, often contrasting or concurrent. It is silent on 'while' right after 'that' at the start of a clause.
result.label: Clause-joining 'while' conjunction

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: ' language' in "second language", the 'x' in "antioxidant", and 'through'. Silent on ' language' after "for/of/in" in education text. Evidence is mixed, with a second-language/'second-' flavor in the members.
result.label: second language / antioxidant mixed
Project-process text, predicts analysis nouns
result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' and', 'ating', '-ing' endings, ' guide') in formal text about project or assessment processes. It boosts next tokens like 'scoring', 'reviews', 'analysis'. Contrast ' and' in lists stays silent, so the evidence is mixed.

Fires on mid-phrase words in climate/emission-policy and scientific text, most often " reduction" after "emission" and " targets", plus a few function words like "be" or "is". Members detect carbon/emission/climate context.
result.label: Emission reduction in climate text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' color', most strongly in "graph coloring" and color-theory text. Members are mostly ' color' token detectors across layers 4-7. Weak firing on a few unrelated tokens.
result.label: ' color' token detector

result.description: Fires on the 'ly' piece of "Supply" at the start of a document in the title "Supply Chain ...", and on "IT" in similar spots. Silent on adverb '-ly' endings like smoothly or cleverly.
result.label: 'Supply' split at document start

result.description: Fires on the word " stages" (also " phases", " stage", " steps") when it names the parts of a process or project, as in "all stages involved in" or "multiple stages". Members mostly detect stage/phase tokens.
result.label: process stages/phases noun

result.description: Fires on function words (of, beyond, just, mere, or) in essays about listening and communication, especially in phrases like "aspect of" or "beyond mere". It is silent on ' of' in many other communication contexts, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Function words in listening essays
'atur' piece in "saturation"
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'atur' inside "saturation"/"saturated" (also "maturity", "miniaturized"), where it follows 's' or 'm'. It is silent when 'atur' starts the text with no preceding piece.

Fires on plural nouns for countries (' countries', ' nations', ' states') when they are the subject or group noun in discussions of international or economic topics. Members detect country/nation words; silent on text about governments and economies without these words.
result.label: Countries/nations plural noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' back' when it is the start of a compound or prefix, such as back|ups, back|tracking, back|bone, back|stage. It predicts a suffix continuing the word. It is silent when the word is split differently.
result.label: ' back' as compound-word start

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ory' completing "sensory" (also 'ial' in "auditorial", 'itory' in "auditory"), in text about sensory experiences. Silent on 'ory' in other words like "allegory".
result.label: "ory" ending of sensory

result.description: Fires on the word " accessible", most strongly after "making X (more) accessible" in text about inclusion and access. It fires weakly on similar adjectives like "relevant" and "-able" endings.
result.label: ' accessible' after making/becoming

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ch' when it begins the word "chord" (geometric or musical), e.g. "seventh ch|ord", "another ch|ord". Members mostly detect ' ch' and its chord-related continuations.
result.label: ' ch' starting "chord"

result.description: Fires on the 'PS' piece in the acronym GPS (Global Positioning System), after 'G'. Weakly fires on similar acronym endings like GIS and HARPS. Members are mostly 'PS' detectors plus navigation and satellite context.
result.label: GPS acronym 'PS' token

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece 'clar' that starts "clarification needed" editorial tags inserted after claims, with weaker firing on a few other tokens (' Today', 'Setting'). Members detect 'clar', 'ification' and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: 'clar' of "clarification needed" tag

result.description: Fires on the 'p' piece in "under|p|ins" / "underpinned", after "under" in the verb "underpin". It predicts completions like "inned" and "ins".
result.label: 'p' in underpin

result.description: Fires on the leading '1' of a four-digit year (e.g. '17th' read as 1-7th) in Renaissance/history text, mainly in century ranges like "14th to the 1​7th". Silent on '1' starting plain years like 1605 or 1850.
result.label: Leading '1' in Renaissance century ranges
' building' before 'blocks'
result.description: Fires on ' building' (rarely ' struct') in the phrase "fundamental/essential building blocks", where the next word is expected to be "blocks". Members are mostly ' building' detectors that push ' blocks'.

Fires on mixed tokens: ' paragraph' (as in "paragraph 1"), repeated backslash/underscore/comma runs, and ' n'. Members are mostly generic writing, grammar and math topic features. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Paragraph and repeated-symbol runs

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' to', ' and', ' often') in expository science/chemistry-style text, such as reaction rates and formulas. Peaks are inconsistent and the same ' the' is silent in other contexts, so the pattern is weak and unclear.
result.label: Function words in technical science prose

result.description: Fires on the piece 'gs' in 'Higgs' (Higgs field, boson, mechanism), in particle-physics text. The contrast shows silence on other physics text, so it needs the preceding 'Hig'.
result.label: 'gs' in Higgs

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens ('elo', ' a', ' mid', ' the', Hebrew letters) mostly in mathematical or abstract expository text, e.g. the 'a' in a^{p-1}. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak; no clear single trigger.
result.label: Scattered tokens in math exposition
-ive in deductive/inductive reasoning
result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ive' in "deductive" and "inductive" (also "inferential") in discussions of logical reasoning. It stays silent on 'ive' in unrelated words like "immersive". Members are 'ive' detectors tied to reasoning and logic.

Fires on the word "distributed" (and pieces like "Dist-ributed"), mostly in computing contexts such as distributed systems, databases and hash tables. Weakly on "decentralized"/"centralized". It is silent on unrelated text.
result.label: "distributed" in computing contexts

result.description: Fires on the end of abstract plural or suffixed nouns in lists or academic/economic prose (decisions, outcomes, patterns, agreement, consequences), often completing a list item. Silent on one 'decisions' example in a different construction. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Abstract noun endings in lists

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ver' in "Adverbs" (and "verbs"), plus ' conjug' in conjugate, in grammar-lesson text. It stays silent on 'ver' in "never". Predicts continuations like "bs"/"bal".
result.label: 'ver' in Adverbs/verbs

result.description: Fires on function words (to, of, are, although, whether) mid-sentence in economics text about market structure, competition, and pricing. It predicts market-related next words such as entry, price and substitute. It stays silent on 'to' in non-market contexts.
result.label: Function words in market-competition text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' assim' (as in assimilation), predicting the continuation 'ilation'. Members detect other word-start fragments that need a suffix completion (poll-, catal-, persu-, anth-).
result.label: ' assim' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the token ' loyal' (as in loyalty, loyal customers), mainly in business and customer-retention text. It pushes the next token towards 'ty'. It is silent on unrelated text.
result.label: ' loyal' in loyalty/customer text

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a noun phrase or clause and opens a list or elaboration (items, "including", "which", "such as"). It stays quiet on commas after introductory phrases or connectives like "therefore".
result.label: Comma opening list or elaboration

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and tokens (y, through, sea, plastic, tree, cular) in the middle of a noun phrase or modifier, mostly after "not just/not only" style contrasts. Weakly pushes toward plural nouns like attempts, forms, models. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed mid-phrase word pieces, noun-ish

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (' in', ' for', ' to', '-', ' through') that follow a verb or noun and introduce a complement, e.g. "competing for power". Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered prepositions after predicates

result.description: Fires on a few specific tokens: the '+' in "B+ trees" or chemical/symbol strings, and ' tong' in "tongs" (kitchen tools). Also weakly on ' que' in "queues". Mixed, token-specific pieces rather than one theme.
result.label: '+' and 'tong(s)' token pieces

result.description: Fires on word-piece 'in' (and 'ize') inside a word or hyphenated compound where a continuation is expected, e.g. mar-in-ade, well-in-formed, familiar-ize. Silent on 'in' inside other words like distinctions or reminiscent.
result.label: 'in'/'ize' mid-word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ',', ' of', ' by') mid-phrase in linguistics/language-development text, predicting a following continuation like ',' or 'which'. Silent on 'and' closing lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in linguistics prose

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' of', ' not', 'ing', ' oil', ' out') in text about risk management and oil recovery, where a verb or process noun is expected. It stays silent on many ' of' tokens elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Risk/oil process text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the verb right after "not only" (provides, demonstrates, facilitate, reflects, safeguard), where "but also" is expected next. Silent on the same word pieces like "es" elsewhere. Members detect "not only/more than just" frames and "but".
result.label: Verb after "not only"

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' fla' when it starts a word like "flaws" or "flawed", mid-sentence. It stays silent when ' fla' is the first token of the document. Members detect ' fla' and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: ' fla' piece in flaws/flawed

result.description: Fires on the token ' I' when it is a word-initial piece of a capitalized term, such as "Ion", "Ionization", Roman numeral I, or acronyms like I/O. It predicts continuations like 'onic' or all-caps letter pieces. It stays quiet on the pronoun "I".
result.label: ' I' as start of word/acronym

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'od' inside "antibodies" (antib|od|ies), in immunology text. It stays silent on 'od' in other words such as "food". Members detect 'od' after anti-/antib- prefixes.
result.label: 'od' in antibodies

result.description: Fires on ' the' (or 's) right after an opening phrase like "Throughout history," at the start of a document, before a subject such as "tale/use of humanity". It stays silent on ' the' in other mid-text spots.
result.label: 'the' after opening "Throughout history,"

result.description: Fires on 'ass' in "brass" (musical instruments) and on a document-initial " When". Silent on 'ass' in bluegrass, encompasses, or a bare initial 'ass'. Members detect 'ass' and instrument words.
result.label: 'ass' in brass; opening 'When'

result.description: Fires on the adjective " distinct" used before a plural noun (distinct forms, subgenres, species), pushing toward suffixes like -ive/-ively. Members are detectors of distinct, unique and different.
result.label: ' distinct' adjective before noun

result.description: Fires on " only" (also " but") in conservation-of-energy statements of the form "cannot be created or destroyed, but only converted/changed". Silent on "not only" and on "can only be created" phrasing, so it needs the contrastive "but/rather only" construction.
result.label: "but only" in energy conservation

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' vol' (volcano, volatile) and 'ch' (game-changer, chord, synchrotron), where a longer word is continued in the next token. Mixed, weakly consistent peaks; the strongest context is 'ch' in "game-changer".
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments vol/ch

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and list/connector tokens (commas, "and", "including", "compar-" pieces) mid-sentence in expository text, where a noun or category item comes next. Peaks are mixed; evidence is weak and the circuit failed.
result.label: Mixed connectors before noun continuation

result.description: Fires on the auxiliary ' been' (also ' was'/' were') after a subject like "significant progress has", right before "made/achieved in". Silent on "been greatly improved" after other subjects, so it needs the progress/advancement-being-made construction.
result.label: "progress has been" auxiliary

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase tokens in abstract expository text (e.g. 'ological' in geological/biological, 'their', 'world', 'current', 'highlight'). No single token dominates; the peaks are inconsistent and it stays silent on some of the same tokens, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tant' when it starts a longer word, mainly 'tantamount' (also tantalize, tantalism, tantrums). Members mostly detect incomplete word-start fragments such as ' tant', ' inten', ' cor' and ' oscill'.
result.label: ' tant' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on function words (that, of, the, and, as, with, by) in music/brain/health science text, where the next word is likely a topic term such as music or neural. Silent on relative-clause "that" after a noun like "mechanisms that".
result.label: Function words in music-science text

result.description: Fires on a comma or "and" joining coordinated adjectives (personal, professional, educational), right after an adjective like "personal" or "professional". It likely predicts another such adjective (e.g. " professional"). It stays quiet on commas joining other clause types.
result.label: Comma/and between coordinated setting adjectives

result.description: Fires on ' hold' as the piece completing "stakehold(ers)", in business/project-management text. It stays silent on the same piece in "sharehold(ers)", so it needs the "stake" prefix.
result.label: hold in "stakeholders"

result.description: Fires on word pieces in biology/biochemistry text, such as 'ili' in pili, 'om' in chromosomal and 'ic' in organometallic. It stays quiet on 'om' in non-biological words like boom and atomizer. Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are scattered.
result.label: Biology word-piece fragments (pili, chromosomal)

result.description: Fires on " careful" (and "meticul-ous") as a modifier of an upcoming noun, mostly after "requires" or similar, in expository text about work needing care. It predicts nouns like planning, consideration and selection.
result.label: careful/meticulous before process noun

result.description: Fires on hyphen or en-dash (also soft hyphen) in the second hyphen of word-order terms like Subject-Verb-Object, where the next piece is a continuation. Silent on hyphens in other compounds like employee-friendly or tree-like.
result.label: Hyphen in Subject-Verb-Object terms

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' sp' in the middle of a word, mostly the start of "spelling" in education text. Upstream members detect ' sp' and its continuations (elling, ices, ont). It is silent when ' sp' starts the document.
result.label: ' sp' piece, as in spelling

result.description: Fires on the word piece " rec" that starts "recycling", "recyclability" and "recovery"-type words, mostly in sustainability and materials text. It is silent on the surrounding recycling-related context when that token is absent.
result.label: ' rec' start of recycling

result.description: Fires on commas, "and" and similar separators inside lists of cost or expense items in food-business text (labor costs, food cost, ingredients), where another cost item such as depreciation or rent is expected next. Silent on other commas.
result.label: Separators in cost-item lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' trans' split off at the start of a longer word, mainly in "phase transitions" (before -itions/-itional). Predicts suffixes like 'itions'. Silent on other words, such as thermal.
result.label: ' trans' in "phase transitions"

result.description: Fires on function words (of, to, the, reflected) in text about colonialism, independence and decolonization, where the next word is likely colonial or administrative. It stays silent on 'of' in other topics such as trade, industry or culture.
result.label: Function words in colonial/decolonization text

result.description: Fires on function words or word pieces (perpet-"uate", "by", "to", "on") right before a likely inequality or disparity term, in texts about social inequality, race, gender, and socioeconomic status. Logits favor "dispar" and "sympt".
result.label: Inequality-context connector before disparity terms

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, most often the piece "vent" in "unconventional", plus "level" in "sea-level", " the", " traditional", " section". No single token or context dominates, and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Scattered tokens, mostly 'vent'
'the' after identify/define verbs
result.description: Fires on ' the' (occasionally possessive 's) right after a transitive verb like identify, define, map out, outline, in business-process writing, where a noun like factors, structure or dynamics is expected. Silent on 'the' after prepositions.

Fires on " through" meaning "by means of", after an abstract noun of achievement or benefit (growth, diversity, change) and before the method noun. Quieter when it follows a participle of data collection ("collected through").
result.label: " through" as means of achieving

result.description: Fires on " Background" as the last word of "Cosmic Microwave Background" (or Neutrino Background) in cosmology text. Silent on "Background" as a section heading, so it needs the cosmic-background phrase.
result.label: Cosmic Microwave Background token

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ',', ' on', ' from', ' of', mid-word fragments) in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent, the contrast silences ' and' in lists, and the circuit is diffuse and unreliable.
result.label: Diffuse function-word and fragment firing

result.description: Fires on the word " email" (also " Email"), mostly as a modifier or topic in phrases like "email communication". Members are mainly email detectors from earlier layers. Weaker on "emails" and "mail"; silent on general messaging text without the word.
result.label: Word 'email' detector

result.description: Fires on the word " without" (rarely " no" or " little") when it introduces a clause about something absent, often right before "any". Members are mostly " without" detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: ' without' preposition detector

result.description: Fires on the word that takes an object in understanding/comprehension phrases: "compreh-end", "understand", "understanding", "grasp of", "knowledge of", expecting a following topic noun phrase. Silent on 'end' inside other words like "interdependence" or "ascend".
result.label: Understanding/comprehending verbs before object

result.description: Fires on function words (to, that, they, can) and 'continu-ously' in tech/UI text about user interaction and adaptive systems, where a verb is expected next (e.g. continue, update). Silent on 'to' in other analysis contexts. Upstream members are largely user/UI detectors.
result.label: Function words in user-interface/adaptive-tech text

result.description: Fires on a slash separating items in a list of alternatives (e.g. creator/user, administrator/successor), especially role or noun lists. Stays quiet on some slashes after abstract activity nouns, so it needs a particular list-of-nouns slot.
result.label: Slash in noun alternative lists
Commas/function words in physics lists
result.description: Fires on commas and some function words (a, that, the, represents) mid-sentence in technical explanatory text, mostly quantum physics or abstract concepts, where a list item or clause continues. Silent on many commas in similar science text.

Fires on the start of a word fragment (' col', ' n', ' et', ' d') in grammar and linguistics text, such as "collocation", "noun" or "dative", where a technical term is being spelled out. It stays silent on "colloquial".
result.label: Linguistics term word-start fragments

result.description: Fires mostly on sentence-initial additive transitions like " Additionally", " Furthermore", " Moreover" at the start of a text or paragraph; weaker, scattered firing on " the", " and", " or". Logits are not clear.
result.label: Additive transition words (Furthermore/Additionally)

result.description: Fires on the adverb suffix "ingly", almost always in "seemingly", where an adjective follows (disordered, random, mundane). Weaker on "otherwise" and other adverbs before adjectives. Predicts unusual or contradictory adjectives next.
result.label: "seemingly" adverb before adjective

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also commas, 'nes', 'ut') right after a colon or comma that introduces a list of components or parts, as in "three parts: the major premise, the minor premise", in academic and technical explanations. Silent on ' the' in culinary text.
result.label: 'the' in lists of components

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (have, with, to, has, about, create, present) that follow a subject in abstract economics/policy prose, where a consequence or effect is about to be stated. Silent on 'about' after 'concern' or 'discussions'.
result.label: Effect-introducing verbs in economics prose

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (in, of, to, shapes, defines) after a subject in text about fiction, worldbuilding and storytelling. It predicts story-related nouns like characters, conflict and protagonist next. Peaks are mixed across tokens.
result.label: Function words in storytelling/worldbuilding text

result.description: Fires on the word "database" (any case, plural) when it is used as a modifier or topic in technical text about data systems, e.g. "database management", "database systems". Members are database, SQL, and schema detectors.
result.label: "database" token in data-systems text

result.description: Fires on ' which' (sometimes ' that') introducing a relative clause after a comma or noun, especially in environmental or causal explanatory text ("...activities, which can have..."). Silent on some 'which' in other constructions or topics.
result.label: Relative 'which' in causal environmental text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ien' in "aud-ien-ces" (audiences), where the next piece is 'ces'. It is also weakly present in other words with 'ien' or similar pieces, such as immunodeficiencies.
result.label: 'ien' inside "audiences"

result.description: Fires on the word "whether" (and "Whether"), mostly when it opens a concessive or alternatives clause such as ", whether physical or digital". Members detect whether, either and both.
result.label: "whether" introducing alternatives

result.description: Fires on importance adjectives (' important', ' prominent', 'cial', ' significant') after "becoming increasingly/more" or "play a", in sustainability/technology trend prose. Silent on "it is important that".
result.label: Increasingly important (trend adjective)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and modifiers (' and', ' dynamic', ' like', 'going', ' a') in abstract technical or academic prose, where a noun or modifier is expected next. Peaks are mixed and the evidence is weak and inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on commas and conjunctions (and/or) separating items in a list of third-person verb phrases, like "promotes innovation, enhances X, and provides...". Predicts another verb such as allows, helps, increases. Silent on commas after other clause types.
result.label: Comma in verb-phrase lists

result.description: Fires mid-word on a word-piece such as 'ing' in "contingent/contingency" (also 'tr', 'per', some function words), where the word is unfinished and a suffix like -ent/-ency follows. Silent on 'ing' as a verb suffix in design-ing, model-ing.
result.label: Mid-word 'ing' in 'contingent'

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (apostrophe, 'the', 'of', 'a', word pieces) in formal expository prose about history, politics and institutions. Peaks are inconsistent; the apostrophe is silent after names like Plan or William. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository history prose

result.description: Fires on ' between' after nouns like connection, link, gap, bridge, in abstract math/theory prose describing a relationship linking two things. Also fires on bridging verb pieces like 'ges' and ' linking'. Silent on text without such a bridging relation.
result.label: 'between' after connection/bridge nouns
' world' after virtual/created
result.description: Fires on ' world' in the sense of a constructed or simulated world (virtual worlds, created worlds, worldview/worldbuilding), often before 's'. It stays quiet on 'world' after 'digital', 'social', 'today's' or a named domain.
Fires on words that introduce a list of examples after a general noun, mainly "such as", "from", "like", and sometimes commas. It stays quiet on "as well as" and causal "as".
result.label: Example-introducing "such as" / "from"

result.description: Fires on the closing parenthesis after an abbreviation or term in parentheses, such as "(DFS)" or "(RCSA)", typically a sentence subject, and pushes the next token toward a verb like "is".
result.label: Closing paren after parenthetical acronym

result.description: Fires on the 'ates' piece completing "plates" in tectonic/geology text (pl+ates). It stays silent on 'ates' ending verbs like originates, investigates, delineates.
result.label: 'ates' in "plates" (tectonics)

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment ' ren' (mostly in "renormalization") where the next piece is expected to complete a longer word, such as -ormal- or -owned. Weak firing on a few other incomplete word starts like monaster- and sample.
result.label: ' ren' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' the', ',', ' in', 'al', ' classical') in music, arts and education text, where the next word could be music-related. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Music/arts context function words

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, mostly 'ural' in "procedural"/"architectural", plus ' the', ' a', ' programming' in technical or computing text. Silent on 'ural' in "structural". Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Technical text 'ural' and function words

result.description: Fires on verbs like "involves", "includes", "requires", "include" that introduce a description of what something consists of or needs. It is silent on "involves" in some contexts, but the contrast does not clearly show why.
result.label: involves/includes/requires verbs

result.description: Fires on ' also' right after "but" in the "not only X but also Y" construction, typically in abstract academic prose. It stays quiet on other uses of ' also', such as after a subject or modal verb, or at the start of a text.
result.label: 'but also' in 'not only…but also'

result.description: Fires on ' be' as a sentence-initial imperative after a comma or clause ("be sure to", "be mindful", "be relevant"). Silent on ' be' after "to", "don't" or "'ll". Also fires on 'be' as a word-start piece.
result.label: Imperative ' be' after comma

result.description: Fires on the plural noun object (disciplines, practices, techniques, concepts, subjects) right after a verb of merging or combining, such as "merge", "meld", "fuse" or "converge". It stays silent on "disciplines" when no merging verb precedes it.
result.label: Objects of merging/blending verbs

result.description: Fires on plural nouns like "examples", "studies", "scenarios" that head a phrase presenting illustrative case material (e.g. "real-life examples of", "case studies"), in section overviews introducing case studies. Silent in other illustrate contexts.
result.label: Illustrative examples/case studies nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on ' in' (also ' across', ' shape', ' effective') after abstract nouns or verbs in essay-style text about communication, technology and management, e.g. "communication management in". Silent on ' in' after "roles in" or "phase in".
result.label: ' in' after communication-management nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also 'for', 'of') after a preposition like "in", "across", "part of" when a field or domain noun is expected next (e.g. "in the culinary field"). Often silent on 'the' elsewhere. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: 'the' after preposition before field noun

result.description: Fires on the verb "keeping"/"Keep"/"keep" (also the "ing" of "keeping"), mostly in advice or instruction text like "keeping everything clean" or "keeping up with". Members are detectors of keep/stay verbs.
result.label: keep / keeping verb

result.description: Fires on a word stem in the middle of an adverb-to-be (spont-, harmon-, fluid, tempor-) where the next piece is an adverb suffix like -ally, -iously, -ly. Predicts adverb endings.
result.label: Adverb stem awaiting -ally/-ly

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' ancient', ' early', 'ing', 'from') in history-of-transportation and technology text, where the next word is likely an era term like "ancient" or "primitive". Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is weak.
result.label: Historical-origins transport/technology context

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' these', ' in', 'al', ' that') inside text about grammar, demonstratives and language or math explanations. It is inconsistent and silent on many ' these' cases, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in grammar text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word endings (' the', 'ing', ',', ' social') in academic or technical expository text, mid-phrase where a continuation is expected. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' the' is silent after "of the" in some contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered function-word or suffix tokens ('ed', ' and', ',', ' even') in explanatory text about chemistry reactions or art technique, mid-phrase before a descriptive word. The peak token is inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed connectives in chemistry/art prose
'oph' in geophysics
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'oph' in "geophysics/geophysical", mainly in Earth-science text. It stays silent on 'oph' in "sophisticated". Members detect 'oph' and related geo- word pieces (geod-, geol-).

Fires mostly on the word piece ' bre' before 'eding' (selective/precision breeding), with weaker hits on 'osc' in chiaroscuro, ' long', and a sentence-initial ' In'. Mixed peaks; mainly a ' bre' word-piece detector.
result.label: ' bre' in breeding (mixed)

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: a bare ' ' before a number (e.g. in date or time ranges), ' invol' in "involvement", and some function words. It stays silent on ' ' before century numbers after "the". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Space before number, ' invol'

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', ' of', ' a') after "lack of awareness/understanding of/about" and similar abstract phrases in philosophical or psychological prose. Silent on many ' the' tokens in similar text, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in abstract philosophical prose

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'at' in "versatility" (also chromatographic, other word fragments like 'esian', ' ins'), where the word is incomplete and likely continues with 'ility'. Silent on ordinary whole-word text.
result.label: 'at' inside versatility-like words

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (the, of, connect, known, commas) in expository academic text where a noun is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens before noun

result.description: Fires on ' the' after "including", "and", or verbs like "underpins" in abstract science-application text, where a nominalization follows (the calculation of, the design of). Silent on ' the' after "to" or "about".
result.label: ' the' before abstract process nouns

result.description: Fires on ' is' (sometimes are/be) right after a long abstract subject noun phrase like "precise control over X" or "measurement of Y", predicting an adjective such as necessary, essential or required. Silent after short subjects like "It".
result.label: ' is' after technical noun-phrase subject

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' sch' (mostly in 'scholars'), especially after 'for', 'as well as' or 'enabled'. Members detect sch-, Sch-, and other word-start fragments. It is silent on text without this piece.
result.label: ' sch' piece of 'scholars'

result.description: Fires on the word piece " advoc" (advocates/advocated/advocating), strongest after an "-ism" subject such as Existentialism or Conservatism. Silent when it begins a document or sentence with no preceding subject.
result.label: ' advoc' after an ism subject

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after the prefix "self" (self-esteem, self-concept, self-healing), predicting a word that completes the compound. Silent on hyphens after other words like "non" or "create".
result.label: Hyphen after "self"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' nan' (or ' Nan') that begins nano- words such as nanomaterials, nanotechnology and nanometer, in materials-science text. It predicts continuations like 'ote', 'ometer' and 'osc'.
result.label: ' nan' nano- prefix

result.description: Fires on nouns of development or change (evolution, advancement, progression, progress, expansion) as the head of a phrase in abstract essay-style text, typically after adjectives like "continuous" or "incessant". Silent on "evolutionary".
result.label: Evolution/advancement/progress nouns

result.description: Fires on the subject noun or pronoun (our sentences, we, nuclear reactors, companies) in "without X / to prevent X" clauses, just before a predicted "would/could" or a negative outcome. Peak tokens vary; it tracks the subject slot.
result.label: Subject before hypothetical "would" outcome

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: ' into' after divide/subdivide, word-start pieces like ' Des', ' Dem', 'itive', and some commas, mostly in sampling or business/academic text. Peaks are scattered with low consistency; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered word pieces and 'into' after dividing

result.description: Fires on ' is' (sometimes ' are') right after a bare singular subject noun with no article, like "array is" or "set is", at the start of a definition. Predicts descriptive continuations such as "made up of" or "composed of". Silent in some other 'is' contexts.
result.label: ' is' after bare subject noun
' access' after memory/data nouns
result.description: Fires on the word " access" (or "Access"), mostly as the head of a compound after a noun such as memory, data or register, in computer-architecture text. Members are access detectors that push towards -ibility, patterns, controls and times.

Fires mainly on the word piece ' jo' in "joke" (after "a" or "clever"), predicting the continuation piece like 'ke'. Weak activations on other word-start fragments such as 'Rob' in "Robuchon" and 'plot'.
result.label: ' jo' piece before 'ke' (joke)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "clar" when it begins a word like "clarification" (as in "clarification needed" tags). It is mostly silent elsewhere, with rare weak firing on "ment" in Enlightenment.
result.label: "clar" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments that begin a longer word, mainly 'qui' in "inquiries", also 'genu', 'utter', 'ig'. It is a word-piece completion latent, with members detecting partial word pieces such as qui, rever, increment, indust.
result.label: Mid-word piece 'qui' in inquiries

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'ative', ' enthus', ' and', dashes) inside lists or noun phrases naming groups of people or professions, such as 'chefs and food enthusiasts'. It pushes toward person-noun endings like -ular, developers, people, children. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Person-group noun phrase continuation

result.description: Fires on "bone" completing "backbone", used figuratively as the essential support of something ("the backbone of X"). Weaker on " core". Members detect bone/rock/foundation/basis words in "foundation of" phrases.
result.label: Figurative "backbone" of something

result.description: Fires on the hyphen after a word like "one-of", "next", "state-of" or "first" in fixed compound phrases (one-of-a-kind, next-generation), predicting a specific continuation. Stays silent on hyphens after "-based" style modifiers (agent-, CRISPR-, real-).
result.label: Hyphen in fixed compounds (one-of-a-kind)

result.description: Fires on "ancient" (mostly the piece "cient" in "Ancient" and the word " ancient"), especially in lists of ancient civilizations. Members are detectors of this token, and the logits favor next words about ancient peoples and places, such as Greek and Egypt.
result.label: "ancient" token, ancient civilizations

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' in', ' when', ' an', '4', ' s') in technical expository text, mid-phrase where a technical noun or modifier is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse and weakly faithful.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase function words, technical text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly verbs like " adapt", " manifest", " interpret", plus " and" in "nuances and complexities", in abstract academic prose about language and linguistics. Peaks are mixed and weakly consistent; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Abstract linguistics prose, verbs like adapt

result.description: Fires on ' electron'/' electrons' and function words (of, the, each) right before a particle or physics term, in physics and chemistry text on bound states and quantum particles. It stays silent on ' electron' in atomic-configuration contexts.
result.label: Electron / physics-particle slot

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after a noun that is the object of "add/adds/bring" (e.g. "adds depth and elegance to your prose"), where 'to' introduces the recipient of the added quality. Silent on infinitive, "true to", or range 'to'.
result.label: 'to' after "adds X to"

result.description: Fires on the 'K' token in "Al-Khwarizmi" (the K after "Al-"), predicting the continuation "hw…". Weaker on other K-initial name pieces like Runge-Kutta and Kesh.
result.label: K in Al-Khwarizmi

result.description: Fires on ' which' opening a non-restrictive relative clause right after a comma following a historical period or era name (Renaissance, Romantic era). It is quieter after comma-linked abstract nouns like scientific method or feudalism.
result.label: "which" after period/era name

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ographic' in "Biogeographic" (especially at the start of a document or heading), and weakly in other -ographic/-istic word endings. It stays silent on 'ographic' in "geographic isolation".
result.label: Biogeographic 'ographic' suffix

result.description: Fires on clause-introducing conjunctions such as " that" and " because" (also " since", colons) after a verb or noun, where a full clause follows, mostly in abstract academic or explanatory prose. Predicts a clause subject like "all", "there", "it".
result.label: Clause-introducing 'that'/'because' connectives

result.description: Fires on nominalization suffixes or process nouns (-lication, -ization, -ulation, -ement, validation, integration) ending a technical process term in computing/engineering text. Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Technical process-noun suffixes

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after nouns like "version", "extension", "form", "type" (a variant or representation of something). Silent on ' of' after "development", "rise", "appreciation", "capable".
result.label: ' of' after 'version/extension' nouns

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ot' in "Robot(ics)" at the start of a document or heading, and on ' increasing' before an '-ly' ending (becoming increasingly). Silent on 'ot' in "promoters". The two triggers look unrelated.
result.label: Robot 'ot' and 'increasing(ly)'

result.description: Fires on the piece 'et' in the word "diet" (di|et), also weakly on "diets". It stays silent on 'et' inside other words like "Eetible" or "crochet". It pushes toward suffixes like -ary.
result.label: 'et' inside "diet"

result.description: Fires on words about thriving or flourishing (thrive, prosper, growth, success, longevity, viability, competitive), often in business or institutional text about continued success. Peaks vary across several word pieces.
result.label: Thriving, prosperity, success words

result.description: Fires on the infinitive marker " to" right after verbs of striving or wanting like "sought", "seeking", "wants", "strive", where a goal verb comes next. Silent on prepositional "to" (in response to, due to) and "helped to".
result.label: infinitive "to" after seeking/wanting verbs

result.description: Fires on ideology suffixes (-ist, -istic, -ial, -ism) completing words like nationalist, communist, anti-colonial in political/historical text, especially after "national". Silent when "ist" starts a text with no such stem. Pushes toward sentiment/interests.
result.label: Political -ist/-istic suffix after nation

result.description: Fires on forms of the verb "introduce" (introduce, introducing, introduces, introduced), mostly where something new is brought in (new, novel, additional carriers or variation). Predicts words like new, novel, additional.
result.label: verb "introduce" forms, bringing in new

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on mixed tokens (' and', ' motiv', 'ative', ' Nor', '/') in expository text about language, writing and literature, often mid-word or at a connector. Silent on many ' and' in narrative/character discussions. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Mixed connectors in language-topic prose

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix 'ic' in "catastrophic" (and similar negative-adjective stems), plus a few appositive/definition function words like ' a', ' or', ' essentially'. Silent on 'ic' in other words such as strategic or economic. Weak, mixed circuit.
result.label: 'ic' in catastrophic

result.description: Fires on "induction", "inference" and "inductive" (the 'ive' piece) when they name a reasoning method in logic or philosophy-of-argument text. Upstream members detect induct-, infer-, -ive and "argument/reasoning" context.
result.label: Inductive reasoning / inference terms

result.description: Fires on the word piece " strateg" (strategies/strategists) when it follows a modifying noun, such as "marketing strategies" or "survival strategies". It stays silent when the piece starts a sentence or is followed by "strategic" as in "strategic planning".
result.label: ' strateg' after modifier noun

result.description: Fires on the standalone word "in" (often after a dash or opening parenthesis, e.g. "—in particular", "(in New Hampshire"). It stays silent when "in" is a piece inside a longer word like "reminiscent" or "fascinating". Logits favor "particular" and "format".
result.label: standalone word "in"
Example-introducers after metrics/measures
result.description: Fires on "such as", "include", "including", "like" that introduce a list of examples, most strongly after nouns about metrics or measurements (e.g. "metrics include", "quantitative aspects such as"). It stays silent on "such as" after other kinds of nouns.
Fires on the word piece ' tour' at the start of tourism/tourist, in text about tourism and geography. Upstream members are mostly ' tour' token detectors. It predicts suffixes like 'ism' and 'ist'.
result.label: ' tour' in tourism/tourist

result.description: Fires on verbs meaning to lengthen duration, mainly " prolong" and " extend(s)", typically in maintenance or lifespan contexts, where the next word is likely "life", "lifespan" or "duration". Members detect extend/stretch/longer tokens.
result.label: Prolong/extend lifespan verbs

result.description: Fires on plural nouns naming analytical or testing methods (" tests", "analyses", " analysis") in scientific or materials-science lists of techniques, e.g. "mechanical tests including...", "thermal analyses such as...". Predicts a following list of methods.
result.label: Scientific test/analysis method nouns

result.description: Fires on the comma or "is" right after "instance" or "example" (e.g. "For instance," / "One example is"), where an illustration is about to be introduced. Silent on ordinary commas elsewhere.
result.label: Comma/is after "instance"/"example"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (century, form, stages, -ical, in, the) in abstract, academic descriptions of cultural or intellectual history and movements. Peaks are scattered and the contrast shows it silent on some 'century' cases, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Abstract cultural-history phrasing, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on ' new' (also fresh, evolution, interesting) right after the singular article "a/an", where a noun like "era", "frontier" or "realm" is expected next. It stays silent on "new" after verbs, as in "opens up new paths".
result.label: "a new" before singular noun

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ics' completing a science or engineering field name (Bioinformat-ics, Proteom-ics, Robot-ics), especially in lists of academic fields. Silent on 'ics' in therapeutics, aesthetics, plastics, infographics.
result.label: -ics ending of scientific field names

result.description: Fires on ' Cir' (and sometimes ' Begin') as the first token of a heading-like line at or near document start, e.g. a list of topic headings like "Polygons. Circles." It stays silent on mid-sentence mentions of circles.
result.label: ' Cir' starting a heading line

result.description: Fires mainly on ' partially' (also 'only', 'completely', 'not') in chemistry text about weak versus strong acids and bases dissociating or ionizing only partly. Members are acid/base and chemistry topic detectors.
result.label: Partial dissociation of weak acids/bases

result.description: Fires on the token " warm" (also the start of "warmth"), in both temperature and figurative senses. It pushes towards suffixes like "th", as in "warmth". Members are mostly detectors of " warm" and nearby temperature words such as cold, cool and heat.
result.label: ' warm' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " menu" / " Menu", especially in restaurant or menu-design text and as a repeated list heading ("Menu Theme. Menu Balance."). Members are mostly " Menu" detectors that push toward item/items/entries.
result.label: Menu token detector

result.description: Fires on prepositions (mostly " in", also on/within/at) right after "ensure/ensuring performance/stability/safety", introducing the setting or conditions ("even in the face of", "in real-world"). Silent on "in" in other uses like "in part" or "in terms of".
result.label: Preposition after ensuring/maintaining performance

result.description: Fires on " the" after a verb or conjunction like "embracing", "and", "reflecting" or "emphasized", where an abstract noun (spirit, desire, exploration) follows in art or history prose. Silent on " the" after sentence-opening prepositions such as "In" or "During".
result.label: "the" before abstract cultural nouns

result.description: Fires on the token " self" (also "self"/"Self") as a standalone noun or prefix, especially in philosophical or psychological talk about the self or identity. Predicts suffixes like "-", "hood", "ish". Members are mostly earlier " self" detectors.
result.label: ' self' token in identity contexts

result.description: Fires on ' that' introducing the result clause of a "so ADJ that" construction (e.g. "so large that they..."). Silent on relative-clause or complement ' that'. Predicts a following subject pronoun like they/it.
result.label: Result-clause 'that' after 'so ADJ'

result.description: Fires on 'front' completing "forefront" in the phrase "at the forefront of". It is weaker on "upfront". Members detect 'fore', 'front', and similar leading-position words.
result.label: 'front' in 'forefront'

result.description: Fires on the open parenthesis ' (' after a noun or name, especially where a year, date, abbreviation or aside is about to follow (e.g. "Descartes (1596", "Cathode Ray Tube (CRT"). Silent when ' (' starts a text.
result.label: Open parenthesis after noun phrase

result.description: Fires on the standalone word-piece ' g' (sometimes ' G') when it begins a word split across tokens, such as g|aming, g|amma, g|ases, g|land. Predicts continuations like 'aps', 'ases', 'aug'.
result.label: Word-initial ' g' fragment

result.description: Fires on ' cell', ' energy' and similar word pieces in biology/lipid text where the next word is likely an adjective-like continuation (cellular, architecture). Silent on some ' cell' tokens in other contexts, so the needed context is unclear.
result.label: Cell/energy before cellular continuation

result.description: Fires on the token ' I' when it starts a word or acronym such as "Ion", "Ionization", "ISA", or a Roman numeral, rather than the pronoun. It mostly fires at the start of a document or heading, and the next piece is often a word continuation.
result.label: ' I' as word-initial fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' be', ' in', ' will', ' means', ' value') in statistics/probability explanations, e.g. the Law of Large Numbers. It is silent on ' be' in other statistical passages, so the conditions are unclear.
result.label: Function words in probability explanations

result.description: Fires on a determiner or quantifier (' a', ' the', ' more', ' greater') right after "allows/allowed/allowing for", where the next word is an abstract capability noun like flexibility or freedom. Silent on ' a' after other prepositions.
result.label: Determiner after "allows for"

result.description: Fires on ' in' right after a noun that ends a simile or analogy ("akin to a Rubik's Cube in", "likened to a lighthouse in"), where a location-like phrase follows. It is quiet on ' in' in ordinary non-analogy sentences.
result.label: ' in' after analogy noun

result.description: Fires on word pieces of verbs meaning to harm or reduce (dis-rupt, dimin-ish, dist-ort, dil-ute), where an object like "the clarity/effectiveness" comes next. Mostly in essays about writing errors or damage.
result.label: Verbs of disrupting or diminishing

result.description: Fires on the verb after "as we" (mostly "move", also "enter", "transition", "navigate") in progressive, "as we move into/towards..." framing. Silent on "move" in other uses like "big move" or "and move beyond".
result.label: "as we move" verb

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' invas' (as in "invasive species"), predicting a continuation like 'ive'. Members are mostly detectors of ' invas' and other incomplete word-start fragments.
result.label: ' invas' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the 'ing' of gathering/collecting and nearby words (relevant, of, analyze) where the next word is likely 'data' or 'information'. It stays silent on 'ing' in unrelated verbs like marketing or uncovering.
result.label: Gathering/collecting, predicts 'data'

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after abstract quality nouns (quality, integrity, reliability, completeness, reproducibility) in technical text. Stays silent after 'one', 'use', 'components'. Logits favor nouns like results, data, contents.
result.label: ' of' after quality/integrity nouns

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after verbs or prepositions of influence or impact (impacting, influence on, contribute to, integral to, affect), where the next word is an outcome noun like development, richness, quality or effectiveness. Silent on ' the' after other verbs or prepositions.
result.label: ' the' after impact/influence phrases

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yth' in words like rhythm, rhythmic, polyrhythms (also Pythagoras), predicting continuations such as 'mic' or 'ms'. Silent on related words without this piece, such as polymeters.
result.label: 'yth' piece in rhythm

result.description: Fires on the prefix " non" / " Non" (non-linear, non-homogeneous, non-inertial) in technical math and physics text, predicting a hyphen or continuation. Silent on "non-polar" in a chemistry-like context.
result.label: Technical "non" prefix

result.description: Fires on the word piece " ul" at the start of "ultrasound/ultrasonics" in technical science text, where the next piece is expected to be "tras". It predicts the continuation of this split word.
result.label: " ul" piece of ultrasound

result.description: Fires on ' that' used as a relative pronoun right after a plural or concrete noun (pollution that, oil that, stream that), introducing a clause whose verb comes next. Silent on complementizer 'that' (said that, ensures that) and demonstrative 'that'.
result.label: Relative 'that' after noun
'ulation' in "articulation"
result.description: Fires on the piece 'ulation' completing the word "articulation", mostly in music or speech contexts. It stays silent on 'ulation' in "manipulation", so it needs the "artic-" prefix.
Fires on the word piece " Le" right after a leadership-style adjective (Inclusive, Servant, Democratic, Charismatic) in a heading, where "Leadership" comes next. Members are mostly " Le" detectors.
result.label: " Le" in "X Leadership" headings

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sust' (start of "sustainable/sustainability") mid-sentence, mostly right after verbs like "using", "use", "promote", "create". Silent when it starts a text or follows some other words (e.g. "for", "achieving", "the").
result.label: ' sust' after using/use verbs

result.description: Fires on the leading digit (3, 4, 5) of a year or century number in ancient-history date ranges (BC/CE, e.g. "Egypt (5000", "to 509 BC"). It stays silent on leading digits inside modern years like 1400 or 1840.
result.label: Ancient-history year leading digit

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'cent' in words like user-centric and incentive, where it is followed by a continuation such as 'ric' or 'ives'. Logits boost 'ric'. Members are mostly 'cent' detectors.
result.label: 'cent' word piece (-centric, incentive)

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of place names (states, countries, cities), as in "Paris, New York City" or "Norway, Denmark, Finland". Silent on commas in ordinary clause or phrase boundaries.
result.label: Commas in place-name lists

result.description: Fires on nouns meaning a blend or linkage of things (combination, amalgamation, interplay, intersection), mostly at the start of a sentence as the subject, where "of/between" is expected next. Silent on some "combination" cases after "this".
result.label: Combination/interplay noun as subject

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Gen" / " gen" when it begins a word like genetic, genome, genes or genres. It pushes toward continuations such as 'etic', 'ome' and 'omic'. It is silent on whole-word "gene" in the contrast text.
result.label: Gen- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative " These" (occasionally " This") as the first word of a document or sentence, where it refers back to earlier material. Weaker on lowercase " these" mid-sentence.
result.label: Sentence-initial " These" demonstrative

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'os' inside "monosaccharides" (after "mon"), and weakly on similar mid-word pieces like 'lig'. It stays silent on 'os' in other words such as ribosomes, chaos, ratios.
result.label: 'os' in monosaccharides

result.description: Fires on the 'quest' piece of "Norman Conquest" (and occasionally the year digits after it), in text about English language history. Silent in some post-Norman "Conquest" contexts, so the exact conditions are unclear.
result.label: Norman Conquest 'quest' token

result.description: Fires on nouns for a chemical or thermodynamic process (' equilibrium', ' reaction', ' process', ' system') in chemistry and thermodynamics text, e.g. Gibbs free energy and reaction shifts. Silent on one 'chemical equilibrium' example.
result.label: Chemical process nouns (equilibrium, reaction)
' math' before -ematician
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' math' when it starts a longer word, mostly "mathematician" after a nationality or descriptor (an amateur, a French). It predicts continuations like 'ematic', 'ém' and 'icians'.

Fires on incomplete word-start pieces like ' conver' (converge/convergent) and ' orn' (ornamental), where the word continues with a suffix. Predicts continuations like 'gent', 'ging', 'amental'. Silent on the complete word 'convergence'.
result.label: Word-start fragment 'conver'/'orn'

result.description: Fires on the suffix "able" in "unreliable", mostly in "unreliable narration/narrator" in literary-analysis text. It predicts " narr". It stays silent on "able" in words like "memorable" and "sociable".
result.label: "able" in unreliable (narrator)

result.description: Fires on abstract head nouns ending a noun phrase in academic text (process, landscape, ecosystem, methodology, domain, level), where a modifier precedes. Silent on 'process' used mid-phrase or as a verb.
result.label: Abstract system/domain noun ending phrase

result.description: Fires on the "ition" piece in "practitioners" (also "intuitionism"), with a few weak firings on function words in technical text. Members are mostly "ition" detectors predicting suffixes like -ers/-ists.
result.label: 'ition' in practitioners

result.description: Fires on the token 'ent' when it is the middle piece of "att-ent-ive" (attentive, attentiveness, attention), predicting suffixes like 'ive'/'ively'. It stays silent on 'ent' ending a word such as "intelligent".
