result.label: 'ent' inside "attentive"

result.description: Fires on ' and' (or a comma) right after "too much/too low/too high" clauses, where the next part says what goes wrong with an excess or shortage. Plain list-joining 'and' stays silent.
result.label: 'and' after "too much/too low"

result.description: Fires on contrastive conjunctions (' but', ' however', ' although', ' yet') that follow a clause stating something, mainly in descriptive or historical prose, where a qualifying or opposing clause comes next. Silent on 'not X but Y' style.
result.label: Contrastive 'but/however' after a clause

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ech' in "Speech", especially at the start of a document or heading such as "Speech Evaluation" or "Speech Synthesis". It pushes towards continuations like recognition, Act, and Synthesis.
result.label: 'ech' in Speech

result.description: Fires on verbs of supplying or giving, such as provide, providing, provides and offer, especially when an abstract subject (a method, tool or concept) supplies something like insight, a formula or a platform. Mostly in analytical or mathematical text.
result.label: provide/offer verbs with abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the last token of a multi-word theory or concept name from social science and management, such as "Power distance", "Hierarchy of Needs" and "Power distance index". Mixed peak tokens, weak consistency. Silent on "ance" in unrelated words.
result.label: Social-science theory term endings

result.description: Fires on verbs and verb-like pieces (processes, handles, stores, -ing) that follow a subject or "that/it" and describe what a system or component does with events or data. Silent when "processes" is a plural noun.
result.label: Verb slot after system subject

result.description: Fires on the token ' z' (word-initial z), mostly in "zinc" (zinc fingers, zinc bonds) in chemistry and biology text. Members detect z/Z tokens. It is silent on unrelated contexts such as the salad/quesadilla text.
result.label: word-initial ' z' token

result.description: Fires on ' that' as a relative pronoun right after a plural object noun (tools, entities, works, systems) introducing a clause about what they did or would do. Silent on complementizer 'that' and after verbs like 'discovered'.
result.label: Relative 'that' after plural noun

result.description: Fires on the adverb ' largely' (weaker on 'mostly', 'primarily') right after a form of 'be' or a passive/copular verb, as in 'is largely dependent on'. Members are detectors of largely/mostly/primarily/partly.
result.label: ' largely' degree adverb after 'is'

result.description: Fires on place names (countries, cities, states) right after the preposition "in" that locate something, e.g. "in Paris", "in southern France", "in Liverpool". Silent when the name is not a location after "in", like "nation-states like France".
result.label: Place name after "in"

result.description: Fires on the word "content" (and "Content"), mainly as a noun in digital media or content-management text. It is weak on the adjective "content" meaning satisfied. Upstream members are mostly "content" token detectors.
result.label: content token (digital content)

result.description: Fires on singular person or kin nouns (child, brother, owner, person, friend, girl) after a determiner or "one"/"her"/"my", often in examples about a generic individual. Predicts continuations like who, else, -hood or -mate.
result.label: Singular person/kin noun after determiner

result.description: Fires on the word "speech" (or its piece "ech" in "Speech") as a noun for spoken language or speaking, such as speech structure, speech therapy, direct speech and speeches. It predicts follow-ups like -es, patterns, recognition and acts.
result.label: "speech" token detector

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' Der' (Derrida, Derivative, Derain) and ' Liter' (Literary), occasionally ' hyper'. It marks an incomplete word start that is continued by a suffix piece such as 'r', 'iv' or 'ary'.
result.label: Der-/Liter- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'avel' in "wavelength" (after 'w'), predicting the continuation 'ength'. Members are detectors of 'avel' and similar mid-word pieces after 'w'.
result.label: 'avel' in wavelength

result.description: Fires on the word " mass" (or "Mass") in physics and chemistry text, such as relativistic mass, atomic mass, rest mass and mass analysis. Members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token.
result.label: Word "mass" in science text

result.description: Fires on ' activities' (also activity, practices, conduct, behaviors) as a noun for conduct after a modifier like "harmful", "economic", or "unlawful", mostly in economics, finance, and regulation text. Silent on "externalities".
result.label: Activities/practices after modifier, economics

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' eth' (start of ethics/ethical) when it follows a preceding word like "moral and", "virtue", or "Kantian" in philosophy or religion text. It is silent on sentence-initial or other ' eth' uses.
result.label: ' eth' in ethics after modifier

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ore' in the middle of a longer word, most strongly in "mechanoreceptors", "chemoreceptors" and "photoreceptors". Weaker in "choreography" and "folklore". Predicts continuations such as 'ograph' and 'ceptor'.
result.label: 'ore' inside -receptors words

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' flav' (start of flavor/flavors) in food and cooking text, predicting completions like 'or', 'ors', 'our'. Silent when it starts the document with no preceding context.
result.label: ' flav' word-piece before -or/-ors

result.description: Fires mostly on digits like '9', '8', '7' in number sequences or lists (times, series of numbers), with scattered weaker firing on function words. Silent on '9' inside a year like 1905. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Digits in number sequences

result.description: Fires on "maintain" and the "ing" of "maintaining", mostly in business or finance text about keeping levels, health or consistency. It predicts objects like accuracy, control, efficiency. It stays silent on "ing" in other verbs like adjusting.
result.label: maintain / maintaining token

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ged' in "emerged" (also 'emerging', similar verbs like burgeoned), mostly describing civilizations, empires or institutions coming into being. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: "emerged" verb ending

result.description: Fires on shape or form adjectives and word pieces (curved, flat, smooth, straight, -onal, -ine) in geometry or physical-shape descriptions, where a noun like "shapes", "edges" or "surfaces" is likely next.
result.label: Shape-describing adjectives (curved, flat, smooth)

result.description: Fires on scattered, unrelated tokens: 'process', the 'icing' piece of "Pricing", ' eastern' and ' cold' in climate (La Niña) text. No single meaning is clear; peaks are inconsistent and the members are mostly generic.
result.label: Mixed tokens: process, icing, eastern

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' rh' at the start of "rhythm" words, when it follows words like "how", "the", "of" or "syncopated". It is silent when ' rh' follows "and" in music lists such as "melody and rhythm". It predicts 'ythm'-style continuations.
result.label: ' rh' starting 'rhythm'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' econom' (mostly after "in" or "of", as in "in econom|ics"), where the next piece is likely 'ics', 'ists' or 'ies'. Members detect econom- tokens and economics-related context.
result.label: ' econom' word-start before -ics

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' rel' when it starts a longer word (relentless, relays, relatability, relational), predicting a continuation like 'ent', 'ays' or 'ational'. It stays silent when ' rel' is at the very start of the text.
result.label: ' rel' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on ' to' (or ' until') as the endpoint marker in a "from X to Y" time-range, especially after a year or century (e.g. "from 1750 to 19…"). Silent on ordinary 'to' such as "relating to" or "leading to".
result.label: 'to' ending a date range

result.description: Fires on possessive determiners (mostly " their") right after verbs like showcase, demonstrate or display, where a noun for abilities or qualities (skills, talent) comes next. It stays quiet on " their" after prepositions or conjunctions.
result.label: Their after showcase/display verbs

result.description: Fires on the 'ing' piece inside the word "contingent" (cont-ing-ent), in philosophical text about necessity. Weaker on 'il' in "resilient". Silent on ordinary '-ing' verb endings.
result.label: 'ing' inside "contingent"

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces of geometry terms (rect, tri, squ, circum) that precede "-angle/-angular/-ference", mainly in lists of shapes in geometry text. Predicts "angular"/"angle". Silent on "Latin rect-" outside geometry.
result.label: Geometry word-start pieces (rect, tri)

result.description: Fires on plural-subject copula ' are' (also 'being', 'were') after a plural noun subject in academic-style text, where a predicate like 'increasingly/also/now becoming' follows. Silent on some 'are' cases, e.g. after 'that' or certain subjects.
result.label: plural noun subject + 'are'

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'con' (also ' Con') at the start of a longer word, such as mis-con-ceptions, super-con-ductivity, con-junction. Predicts continuations like 'cept', 'vent', 'duct', 'vers'.
result.label: 'con' word-piece prefix

result.description: Fires on ' won' (mostly in "won't" contractions) and on ' the' after "of"/"to" in abstract academic phrasing, plus a few other tokens. Mixed peaks; evidence is thin and the circuit fits poorly.
result.label: ' won' contraction and ' the'

result.description: Fires on the word " visual" (and " Visual") as an adjective or prefix, e.g. "visual communication", "visual stimuli", "visualization". Predicts continuations like -ization, appeal, representations. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: Token "visual"

result.description: Fires on the word " settlement" (human settlement, rural or ethnic settlement patterns) in academic social-science text, and predicts "patterns", "sites", "districts" next. Members are mostly settlement detectors plus related abstract-noun detectors.
result.label: ' settlement' noun, settlement patterns

result.description: Fires on the token " nature", most strongly after adjectives like "dynamic", "evolving" or "intricate" in the phrase "ADJ nature of X". It predicts " of" next. Many members are plain " nature" detectors.
result.label: ' nature' after adjective

result.description: Fires on the word " community" when it is used as a modifier before a following noun, as in "community participation", "community growth" or "community building". It predicts words like spirit, involvement, participation, pride.
result.label: ' community' as noun modifier

result.description: Fires on the suffix pieces of "simplify" forms (simpl-ifying, simpl-ifies, simplify) and on "the" right after "simplifies", mostly in math or technical text. It predicts words like complex, complicated, calculations, problems.
result.label: simplify verb forms, predicting complexity

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Hyp" (before "othesis") in lists of named hypotheses, such as the Input Hypothesis or Monitor Hypothesis. It also fires weakly on other split-word starts like Pre.
result.label: " Hyp" start of "Hypothesis" names

result.description: Fires on the "-ates" ending of "necessitates" (also "necessitated"/"necessitating"), where the verb means "requires". It is silent on "ates" in other words like "integrates" or "vertebrates". Predicts words like careful, thorough, strict.
result.label: necessitates (requires) verb ending

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " bi"/" Bi" that begins bio- words (Biomedical, biological, biogeographic, biology, biopolitics). It predicts continuations like 'omed', 'ological', 'ology', 'ote'.
result.label: Bi- prefix of bio- words

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ens' (start of "ensures/ensuring/ensured") right after a subject noun or conjunction, predicting "ures/uring/ured". Silent in "beyond ensuring", so it needs the verb slot after a subject.
result.label: ' ens' piece of ensures

result.description: Fires on the word piece " ide" (or " Ide") that begins "ideology/ideological", mostly after "political" or an adjective. It predicts continuations like "ologies", "ology", "als". It stays silent when "ide" starts a document.
result.label: ide- start of ideology

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start pieces like ' mob' (mobility), ' occurr' (occurring), ' behav' (behaviors), ' symmet', where the next token completes the word with a suffix such as 'ility' or 'iors'. Silent on ' mob' at document start.
result.label: Word-start fragments awaiting suffix

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ra' when it begins a longer word, such as "cooling ra|cks", "ra|infall" or "ra|ises". The strongest case is "cooling rack". It predicts word continuations like 'inf', 'ref', 'cks'.
result.label: ' ra' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the token "linear", most strongly as the piece after "Non" or "non-" (Nonlinear Dynamics/Regression), and also on " linear" in math text. Predicts continuations like "ity", "dynamics" and "differential".
result.label: "linear" in nonlinear/math contexts

result.description: Fires on the word " user" (also users/User) used as a modifier before a noun, as in "user experience", "user-friendly", "user interface". It pushes the next token towards interface, experience or a hyphen. It was silent in one "meet user requirements" context.
result.label: "user" as noun modifier (UX)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' eth' (and ' Eth') that starts words like ethical, ethics, ethos, and also ethers. It predicts continuations such as 'ical' and 'os'. Members are mostly ' eth' detectors.
result.label: ' eth' word-start token

result.description: Fires on "reduction"/"reducing" (including pieces like redu|ction), mainly in chemistry redox contexts (reduction reactions, reducing agents), and weakly on "redox". Predicts "agent(s)" or "potential" next.
result.label: Reduction (chemical redox sense)

result.description: Fires on ' also' right after a singular subject noun or pronoun (it, this concept, this principle), before a verb like controls, describes, ensures. Silent when ' also' starts the text or follows 'is'.
result.label: ' also' after subject, before verb

result.description: Fires on words like "treating", "treat", "of", "as", "for", "like" that sit right before a disease name in medical text about treating or combating diseases. Predicts disease or cancer next. Silent on "-ating" in unrelated words.
result.label: Before disease names in treatment text

result.description: Fires on word pieces 'ult' (in socioc-ult-ural, interc-ult-ural) and 'switch' (code-switch-ing) in sociolinguistics text, predicting suffix continuations like 'ural'. Weaker on 'depth' and 'effects'.
result.label: 'ult' in sociocultural, code-'switch'

result.description: Fires on the prefix token ' un' when it begins a word like unfamiliar, uncharted or unexamined, usually after a preposition or verb such as "into" or "through". It pushes toward continuations like 'famil', 'pre' and 'chart'.
result.label: ' un' word-prefix after preposition

result.description: Fires on connectors (mostly ' and') right after "stable" or "stability" in economic/system-stability text, e.g. "stable and predictable", "stability and control". It stays quiet on ' and' ending ordinary lists of factors.
result.label: 'and' after stability/stable
Sentence-initial agent suffix 'ists'
result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ists' when it appears as a detached fragment starting a new sentence, right after a period, standing in for a plural agent noun subject. Stays silent when 'ists' completes a word like 'Artists' or 'scientists'.

Fires on the word piece " techn" when it starts "technological", especially after "factors such as", "due to", "influenced by", where a list of causes is expected. Silent on " techn" after "new" or "manufacturing" (techn-ologies as a product).
result.label: techn(ological) as a cause factor

result.description: Fires on the word "layer" or "layers" (and the "layer" piece in "layered"/"layering") across geology, networking, neural nets and abstract uses. Predicts suffixes like "ed" or "thick". Members are mostly "layer" detectors.
result.label: Token "layer"/"layers"
'fer' piece in Inter-/In-/refer words
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'fer' inside split words like Inter|fer|ometry, In|fer|ential and inter|fer|ing, and weakly in self-refer-ential. It predicts continuations such as 'ring', 'ential', 'enced'.

Fires on the word "distributed" (and the piece "ributed" in "Distributed"), mostly in computing contexts like distributed systems, computing, databases. Predicts nouns like environments, systems, computing. Also fires weakly on "parallel" and "consensus".
result.label: "distributed" in computing

result.description: Fires on the "ating" piece in "Oper|ating" (operating system) and on " operating", predicting "systems". Silent on other "-ating" words like illustrating or approximating.
result.label: Operating (system) word piece

result.description: Fires mainly on ' much' in "too much" (excess/quantity contrasts like "too much or too little"), plus excess-related pieces like "excessive". Silent on "how much more" questions.
result.label: "too much" excess quantity

result.description: Fires on the word piece " master"/" Master" when it begins a word like mastering, mastery, masterpiece, predicting suffixes such as -ing, -y, -fully. Silent on "master of" used as a standalone noun.
result.label: master- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the token ' health', mostly right after "the" or a possessive in phrases like "the health and safety" or "the healthcare industry". It is silent on some ' health' tokens after "of", "as" or "in". Logits favour compounds such as sheet, card, code.
result.label: ' health' after "the"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' c' right after "nonverbal" (or similar modifier), where the next piece is expected to be "ues" (cues). Silent on ' c' after "valuable" and in other contexts.
result.label: ' c' in "nonverbal cues"

result.description: Fires on the end of classification words, mainly "onomy" in "taxonomy" and " classification", also "categorization", mostly in biology text about plants and animals. It pushes toward "schemes" and "systems".
result.label: Taxonomy / classification word endings

result.description: Fires on ' foot' when it is the first piece of a compound like "carbon footprint" or "footprints", and on 'i' in "Fermi". It predicts the continuation "print" (or similar suffix).
result.label: ' foot' in footprint compounds

result.description: Fires on adjectives like " explicit" and " literal" (also "fancy", "particular") that modify a noun about meaning or communication, such as explicit signals or literal meaning. It's backed by explicit/implicit, direct/clear and formal detectors.
result.label: explicit / literal meaning adjectives

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'ic' (also ' mechanical', ' mechan') of "quantum mechan-ic(s)", in physics text after "quantum" or "mechan". Silent on 'ic' in other words like organic or microscopic. Predicts nouns like principles, effects, properties.
result.label: quantum mechan-ic word ending

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside art-technique terms in lists of drawing/painting techniques (Shading, Stippling, Sfumato, Impasto). Silent on lists of people's names. Members are art/painting detectors.
result.label: Art technique term pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function-like tokens (blank space tokens, ' yet', ' that', word pieces) mid-phrase in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent, with no dominant token; logits weakly favor verbs like 'seek' or 'find'.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on word endings that close mathematical/physics field names or terms (cohomology, renormalization, algebras, String Theory), where a noun like "group" or "theory" may follow. Silent on "ology" in biology and ethnomusicology.
result.label: Math/physics term-ending suffixes

result.description: Fires on ' to' right after an adjective plus "enough" (e.g. "powerful enough to", "simple enough to"), also weakly after "late to" or "power to". Silent on ' to' as a preposition or after other nouns and verbs. Pushes toward verbs like allow, explain, justify.
result.label: ' to' after "enough"

result.description: Fires on 'and' or a comma right after "efficiency" (or similar goals like efficient resource use) in a list of goals or benefits. It predicts the next item as cost, waste, low or minimize, and suppresses repeating efficiency. Silent on 'and' elsewhere.
result.label: 'and'/comma after efficiency

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' cal' at the start of a longer word, mainly calibration, calorimetric and caloric. It predicts continuations like 'ibr', 'orie' and 'ibration'. Weaker on 'calendulas'.
result.label: ' cal' piece before ibr/orie
' cl' word-piece, clay
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cl' when it starts a split word, mostly the start of "clay"/"clays" after a prefix like "natural" or "kaolin". It also fires on "cloning" and "cl-" fragments in other words.
Fires on the word-start piece " cor" (as in corrosion, coral) before the rest of the word is seen. It predicts continuation pieces like "rosion" or "al". Members are mostly " cor" token detectors.
result.label: ' cor' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' completing "empir-ical" (also 'experimental'), mostly before words like evidence, observation, verification. Silent on 'ical' in other words such as philosophical or Classical. Predicts evidence/proof/truth.
result.label: empirical (-ical after empir-)

result.description: Fires on the token "made" in the compound "human-made" / "man-made" / "hand-made", where it ends a hyphenated artificial-origin modifier before a noun like features or structures. Members detect artificial, natural, and -ed/-made word pieces.
result.label: hyphenated "-made" (man-made)

result.description: Fires on commas and "and" that separate items in a list of abstract process or property nouns (flow, movement, quality; acquisition, processing), where another list item is expected. Silent on commas that start a participle clause.
result.label: List separators after process nouns

result.description: Fires on a comma, "and", or "denotes" right after the abstract quality noun "clarity" (or similar quality words like "concise") in lists of communication virtues. It is silent on commas after other nouns in similar lists.
result.label: Comma/and after "clarity" in lists

result.description: Fires on the comma right after a sentence-initial "for instance" / "for example" (or "conversely"), where an example clause follows. It stays silent on ordinary mid-sentence commas.
result.label: Comma after "for instance/example"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'avel' in "w|avel|ength(s)", after a preceding 'w' piece. Weak on similar mid-word pieces (w-ard-robe, stain-less). Silent when 'avel' starts the text without the 'w'.
result.label: 'avel' inside wavelength

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' s' / ' S' (a space-prefixed lone s) that starts a longer word split into pieces, like s-ophistication, s-yllog, s-culpt. It boosts continuations such as 'oph', 'ynt', 'tere'.
result.label: Split-word initial ' s' piece

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'oth' (sloth), 'elt' (Celtic), 'ber' (strawberries) and 'enz', where the word is still incomplete. It is often in food or list contexts. Logits suggest suffix pieces come next (ts, os, horn). Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mid-word fragments oth/elt/ber

result.description: Fires on the word " tax" (also " Tax") when it follows a modifier or context word in taxation text, e.g. "better tax benefits", "effective tax planning". It is silent on a sentence-initial "tax-and-". Members are tax-token detectors.
result.label: ' tax' token after modifier

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'brid' in "hybrid"/"hybridization", mostly in chemical bonding text. It predicts suffixes like 'ization' and 'ized'. It stays silent when 'brid' starts the text with no 'hy' before it.
result.label: 'brid' in hybrid(ization)

result.description: Fires on words right after "symbols that represent/signify" in text about writing systems (logographic scripts), where the next word names what symbols stand for (words, sounds, morphemes). Silent in other descriptions of scripts.
result.label: Symbols representing words/sounds in scripts

result.description: Fires on ' well' in the conjunction "as well (as)", after "as". It stays silent on "how well" and does not fire for other uses like oil wells or "well-" compounds.
result.label: "as well (as)" on ' well'

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "integration" (also "use of", "introduction of"), in technical or academic text. It stays silent on "of" after other nouns like creation, emergence, wave, and sometimes even after integration.
result.label: ' of' after integration

result.description: Fires on the word " virtue" (and pieces like "ue"/"ues" in "virtues"), mostly in virtue ethics contexts. It predicts continuations like " eth" (ethics). Upstream members are mostly virtue-token detectors.
result.label: virtue token (virtue ethics)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "wh" (as in who/whom/whose/whisk) when it begins a word and is split off as its own token. It pushes toward completions like -ether, -atever, -ilst and -ose.
result.label: word-initial "wh" piece

result.description: Fires on abstract academic nouns like theory, principles, techniques, concepts ending a noun phrase in historical passages about the foundations of mathematics or knowledge. It stays quiet on 'theory' in other phrases, such as 'probability theory'. Predicts a following clause with temporal words.
result.label: Abstract field nouns in historical foundations

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (where, when, or, of, in) in text defining or explaining economic externalities and market failure. It seems to predict an upcoming "third (parties)" or "external" continuation. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low.
result.label: Connectors in externalities explanations

result.description: Fires on ' by' right after "followed" in historical or sequence descriptions (period X, followed by period Y). Silent on ' by' as agent marker (proposed by, marked by, while by). Pushes toward words like further, later, subsequent.
result.label: "followed by" in sequences

result.description: Fires on function words and commas (' in', ',', ' of', ' through') in passages about creativity, art and technology, where the next word is likely an art or craft noun (studio, sculpt, artists). Silent on ' in' in other discourse.
result.label: Function words in art-technology text

result.description: Fires on verbs of mixing or joining (blend, combine, merge) when they take a plural or compound subject and are followed by "together", "into" or "with". It stays silent on "blend" used as a noun, or "bend".
result.label: blend/combine/merge verbs

result.description: Fires on ' both' after a linking verb, mostly "that are both" or "can be both", where it introduces a pair of adjectives. It stays silent when 'both' starts a clause subject, as in "; both have". Next-token logits favour adjectives like effective and efficient.
result.label: 'both' after copula before adjective pair

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: ' in' after "established/took place" before a year, ' treated', 'est' in "aesthetic", list commas. Silent on ' in' after nouns like "changes in". Evidence is mixed and the peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: Mixed ' in' before years, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' t' when it begins "tension" in writing-craft text (creating, generating, weaving tension). It predicts the continuation "ension". Members are ' t' detectors plus narrative-craft context.
result.label: ' t' starting "tension" in narrative writing

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ur' in the middle of a word, mostly after 'pl' in "plurals", "plurality", "plurilingual". Also fires inside other words like bifurcation and heuristic, and predicts a continuing suffix.
result.label: 'ur' piece in pl-ur words

result.description: Fires on the last word of a tech term like "Machine Learning" or "Virtual/augmented reality", and sometimes on "AI", when listed in a coordinated series of emerging technologies, often just before an acronym in parentheses. Silent on other "machine learning" uses.
result.label: Machine learning / reality in tech lists

result.description: Fires on the comma that closes an introductory "By utilizing/using/employing X" phrase at the start of a text, where the main clause subject (you, one, we, scientists) comes next. Silent on commas inside lists or other clauses.
result.label: Comma after introductory "By using X"

result.description: Fires on the standalone word-initial token ' l' when it begins a longer word, mostly 'lymph' in anatomy text and also 'lens' or 'laminar'. Predicts continuation pieces like 'ign', 'amin', 'anth'.
result.label: word-initial ' l' (lymph, lens)

result.description: Fires on the capitalized word-initial piece ' N' at the start of a line or document, where a word such as Nuclear or Nouns begins. Predicts continuations like 'iels', 'ixon', 'ouve'. Silent on the contrast list of names.
result.label: Line-initial ' N' word start

result.description: Fires on the word " consent" (occasionally " compatibility"/" compatible") in data, privacy and ethics text. Members include consent detectors and privacy-related pieces like "acy", "confidentiality" and "authentication". Weakly predicts "ing" or "with" next.
result.label: ' consent' in privacy/data ethics

result.description: Diffuse target firing on varied function words and verbs (' the', ' that', ' corresponds', ' access') inside abstract, technical expository prose, mostly after "that"-clauses; predicts abstract nouns like intent, plan, target. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Abstract technical prose function words

result.description: Fires on a sentence-ending full stop that closes a complete sentence in expository text about languages, culture and society, where the next sentence is expected to start. It stays silent on abbreviation periods (e.g.) and some odd or fragmentary endings.
result.label: Sentence-final period in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word " character", mostly as the stem of "characterizes/characterized by" in descriptive academic prose. It predicts verb suffixes such as -ized, -ises and -istics. It also weakly fires on "encomp(assing)".
result.label: " character" as characterize stem

result.description: Fires on the auxiliary verb (are/is/was/'re/actually) right after a "what/who + subject" embedded clause, e.g. "what the author is trying", where a verb like saying/doing/trying comes next. Silent on "they are" in plain statements.
result.label: Aux verb in what-you-are clauses

result.description: Fires on the verb "ask" and its forms (asking, ask, asked), mostly "asking", in the sense of posing questions. It predicts question-related continuations such as "questions", "us" and "for". Members are ask-word detectors plus question and search detectors.
result.label: ask / asking verb (questions)

result.description: Fires on function words and connectives (and, of, on, for, measures, commas) right after metric terms like accuracy, precision, recall in evaluation or measurement text, where a measurement-related word is expected next. Silent on 'and' in other science contexts.
result.label: Function words after precision/accuracy metrics

result.description: Fires on the capital ' S' as a word-initial piece of a proper name, mainly in language and region names (Sino-, Southeast, Slavic, Sinitic, Sumerian, Scythian). It predicts continuations like 'out', 'umer', 'ansk'.
result.label: Capital S starting language/region names

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tar' when it begins "tariff(s)" in trade and economics text. Silent on ' tar' at the very start of a document, where there is no preceding context.
result.label: ' tar' start of tariff

result.description: Fires on ' and' (also ' with', commas) joining a religious term like "religious doctrine" or "religious" to a second item, in texts on religion and culture. It is silent on 'and' in lists of secular abstract nouns.
result.label: 'and' after religious terms

result.description: Fires on an opening quote mark (' or ") that begins the next quoted item in a list of quoted words, such as prepositions or pronouns ('at', 'by', 'on'). Silent in ordinary prose without such quoted lists.
result.label: Opening quote in quoted word lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ency' completing a word, mainly 'fluency' in language-learning and skills text. Members include detectors of 'ency' and similar suffix pieces plus language-acquisition context.
result.label: 'ency' suffix in fluency

result.description: Fires on scattered word fragments, odd byte pieces and rare tokens (' campion', 'rä', 'AR', 'buf', 'ühr') with no shared meaning. Members are token-piece detectors. Peak consistency is low and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered rare token fragments

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' w' that starts a split word (wage, welfare, wires, wavelength), mostly in economics text. It predicts continuations like 'ages', 'elf', 'ides', 'onders'.
result.label: Word-initial ' w' piece (wage/welfare)

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'log' inside "syllogism" (also 'istic' in "statistic", ' literally'), a mid-word fragment in logic/statistics text. Silent on 'log' at the start of a document, so it needs a preceding word piece.
result.label: 'log' in syllogism / statistic pieces
'esc' piece in "molescular"
result.description: Fires on the token 'esc' (occasionally 'asc') when it follows "mol", in the odd split of "molecular" as mol+esc+ular. It predicts the completion 'ular'. It stays silent on normally tokenized "molecular".
Fires on the piece 'ili' in "res|ili|ence", after "res" in the word resilience. It predicts the continuation 'ence'. Weaker activations occur on similar mid-word pieces such as ' flu' in fluency.
result.label: 'ili' in resilience

result.description: Fires on reporting verbs after a research or study subject (shown, revealed, highlighted, indicates, demonstrated), where a finding is about to be stated. It pushes toward "that" or "significant".
result.label: Research-finding verbs like "shown"

result.description: Fires mostly on the word-piece ' sp' (also 'cement' in 'placement') when a continuation like 'anning', 'elling' or 'ont' is expected, especially in "period, spanning from". Silent on ' sp' in 'spices' after 'herbs or'.
result.label: ' sp' piece predicting 'anning'

result.description: Fires on ' mirror' used as a metaphor noun after "serves/acts as a", as in art or literature being a mirror of society. It is silent on the verb use "also mirrors societal…".
result.label: metaphorical "as a mirror"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " gen" / " Gen" at the start of a word, mostly in "genres" (music genres) and also "genetic"/"genes". It pushes toward "res" as the next piece. It is silent on one "genetic" example.
result.label: ' gen' word-start piece (genres)

result.description: Fires on ' role' after "play a crucial/significant/important" (e.g. "gestures play a crucial role in"). Silent when "role" follows just "The" at the start of a text. Members are mostly role/roles detectors plus adjective-before-role detectors.
result.label: "play a crucial role" – role

result.description: Fires on plural setting nouns (areas, regions, systems, states, spaces) right after a modifier in an "in [adjective] X" phrase, such as "in dry areas" or "in solid states". It is silent on "various areas" or "all areas". Predicts "such", "like".
result.label: Setting nouns after "in ADJ"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' vent' (also ' conject', ' file') when it is an incomplete word start, as in "venturing" or "ventures", predicting a suffix like "ure". Members are vent/Vent detectors and other word-start pieces that predict "ure".
result.label: ' vent' word-start before -ure

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'lex' inside 'reflex-' words (reflexive, reflexivity, reflexively). It stays silent on 'lex' at the very start of a document, where there is no 'ref' before it.
result.label: 'lex' in 'reflexive'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' lingu' at the start of linguist/linguistics/linguistic, mostly after words like descriptive, computational or pioneering. It predicts suffix continuations such as -istic, -ists and -istics.
result.label: ' lingu' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the 'h' token inside the word "aesthetic" (aest|h|etic), in both lowercase and capitalized forms. Members are mostly 'h' detectors in this word, so it needs the "aest" prefix.
result.label: 'h' in aesthetic

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ic' completing "organic" (mostly "organic matter/material" in soil text). It stays silent on 'ic' in other words such as authigenic, endogenic and mutagenic. It pushes towards "matter".
result.label: 'ic' in "organic"

result.description: Fires on the word " film" (as in filmmakers, film scoring, film production), predicting compounds like making, maker, director, scoring. Members are mostly film/entertainment/animation detectors. The contrast shows no clear example of silence on the token.
result.label: ' film' before making/maker/scoring

result.description: Fires on varied word-ending tokens (care, ers, els, cities, changes, market) inside economic or business-benefit text, such as tourism, jobs and retail. It stays silent on 'market' in 'marketing'. Low consistency, mixed evidence.
result.label: Plural/noun endings in economic-benefit text

result.description: Fires on "willing" and the "ness" of "willingness", especially in economic text about consumers' or investors' willingness and ability to buy or pay. Predicts a following "to" or similar.
result.label: willing / willingness

result.description: Fires on function words and commas (",", " and", " of", " the") inside explanatory text about software maintenance and engineering processes, where a list of tasks or activities is continuing. Silent on commas in other technical or general text.
result.label: Commas in software maintenance task lists

result.description: Fires on the infinitive marker ' to' after a verb or noun that takes a to-infinitive (attempting to, learning how to, ability to, struggle to). Silent on prepositional 'to' (access to, given to). Predicts a bare verb like understand or read.
result.label: Infinitive 'to' before a verb

result.description: Fires on the word " urban" (or " Urban", and "metropolitan") in texts about urban studies, planning and development. It predicts continuations like areas, settings, populations. Silent on policy-list text without the word.
result.label: urban token detector
paved (the way) word piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'aved' in "paved the way/road" (also 'aving', 'ited' in "credited"), mostly in academic history or science text about developments paving the way. Members are detectors of 'aved'/'aving'/'ave'.

Fires on the word " financial" (also the "cial" piece of "Financial") as a modifier before a noun like institutions, services, crisis or stability. Silent on the Great Depression contrast text, which has no such word.
result.label: ' financial' modifier word

result.description: Fires on the token " person" (also "Person"), often as a word stem before suffixes like -ification, -ality, or in "first/third person". Predicts suffix pieces such as 'ality' and 'hood'. Upstream members are mostly " person" detectors.
result.label: ' person' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " government" as a noun, mostly in economics text on fiscal policy and Keynesian intervention. It is weaker on related words like "bank". Logits favor continuations like "intervention", "al" and "policies".
result.label: ' government' in economic policy text
'end' piece in 'bend'
result.description: Fires on the 'end' token (also 'ends', 'ending') when it completes the word 'bend', mainly in physics text about light or sound bending. It also fires on 'end' inside words like 'dendritic'.

Fires on a noun ending a phrase of the form "X's history/past/life/usage/over time", where a domain noun completes a noun phrase. It often predicts "such", "including" or "that" next. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Noun ending a domain phrase (history/time)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, 'for', 'describe', 'that') in expository prose about lists or concepts, mid-clause where a continuation follows. Peak tokens are mixed and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Mixed function words in expository lists

result.description: Fires on the prefixes " macro" and " micro" (also " Micro") when they begin a compound word, such as macroeconomic, microscale or microstate. It predicts a continuation like "scop", "e" or "econ". Silent on ordinary economics text without these prefixes.
result.label: macro/micro prefix

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " erg" before "onomic/onomics" (mostly mid-sentence). Weaker on other word-start pieces like " Ly", " Arist", "semi". It predicts word-continuation pieces. Silent on the capitalized "Ergonomics" at sentence start.
result.label: " erg" prefix of ergonomic

result.description: Fires on the token " ATP" in biochemistry text about energy metabolism, especially before "synthesis", "synthase" or "production". Members include ATP detectors and related biochemistry word pieces such as Krebs, mitochondria and citrate.
result.label: ATP in bioenergetics text

result.description: Fires on the additive connector in "while also considering/examining", "as well as", and similar, where a further topic or analysis is being added to a list of things discussed. It stays silent on "such as", "serving as" and "operating as".
result.label: Additive "also/as well as" connector

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'ain' in "unattainable" (also "attainment"), and weakly on ' opp' and some commas. It stays silent on 'ain' in "sustainable" or "Maintain", so it needs the unatt-/att- word.
result.label: 'ain' in unattainable

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Princi' (mostly in "X Principle" names like Uncertainty or Pauli Exclusion Principle), and weaker on ' per' (perception) and ' pur', where a completion like -ple or -ception comes next.
result.label: Princi- / per- word-start piece

result.description: Fires on " our" after a preposition (of, in, within) when it begins a noun phrase about shared human things like our world, body, daily lives. It stays silent after verbs like shape or fosters.
result.label: "our" after preposition

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Scient" (as in "Scientific Revolution"), a stem that needs a suffix like -ific or -ists. It is weaker on lowercase " scient" before "ists". It predicts 'ific' and 'ists' next.
result.label: " Scient" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the token 'e' when it is split off as a prefix piece before 'conomic', as in macro-e-conomic, micro-e-conomic and socio-e-conomic. It predicts 'conom' next. Members are mostly 'e' detectors.
result.label: 'e' in macro-e-conomic

result.description: Fires on the hyphen or en dash right after "cross" (cross-validation, cross-cultural, cross-hatching, cross-contamination). It stays silent on hyphens after other words like avant, large, cost or day.
result.label: Hyphen after "cross"

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces 'c' or 'ly' inside the word "cataclysmic" (cata-c-lysmic, catac-ly-smic), mostly in astronomy text. Silent on a 'c' in other words such as "mechanic(s)".
result.label: Inside "cataclysmic" word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece "au" inside names and terms like "tau" (tau neutrino, tau lepton) and "Landau". Weakly fires on "arma" in "pharmaceutical". Upstream members are mostly "au" detectors.
result.label: "au" word piece (tau, Landau)

result.description: Fires on the word " different" (also in "differentiation"), mostly as a modifier before a plural noun, as in "between different cultures". Predicts "iation", "types" or "kinds" next. Upstream members are mostly " different" detectors.
result.label: ' different' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' vig' at the start of vigorous/vigilance/vigilant, predicting continuations like 'orous' or 'il'. Members detect related word-start pieces (rig, Res, prem) that lead to similar endings.
result.label: ' vig' piece of vigorous/vigilant

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, with, for) right after a verb or predicate describing what syntax or semantics deals with, in linguistics text. It predicts linguistic nouns such as Syntax, clause, sentence. Silent on 'on the' in generic contexts.
result.label: Function words in linguistics definitions

result.description: Fires on the "actions" piece in "re|actions" (also " reaction") in chemistry text, especially after "chemical". It stays silent in some contexts such as "parasitic reactions" and "redox reactions".
result.label: chemical "reactions" word piece

result.description: Fires on "store", "stores", "storage" and "storing" in data and computing text, such as key-value stores, document stores, RAM and storage repositories. It is quiet on unrelated database text that lacks these words.
result.label: store/storage in data systems

result.description: Fires on ' and' joining a verb phrase about a subject's history, after a date, place or originator (e.g. "introduced by Husserl and then developed"). It stays silent when ' and' joins two nouns or names. Predicts a verb such as continued or later.
result.label: ' and' before a second verb

result.description: Fires on the word piece "oul" inside "Coulomb"/"Coulometry" (also Bernoulli), after an initial capital C or Bern. It predicts a continuation like "omb". Rare weak firing elsewhere.
result.label: "oul" in Coulomb/Bernoulli

result.description: Fires on the token ' Paris' in any use (city, Paris agreement, Paris Peace Conference, Parisian). Predicts suffixes like 'ian' or following nouns such as ' Peace' and ' Agreement'. Members detect Paris and other place names like York and Berlin.
result.label: ' Paris' token detector

result.description: Fires on the verb or article right after "communication" as the subject of an opening definitional sentence (" is", " a", " an", " has"). Silent on the same words when the subject isn't communication.
result.label: Verb after "Communication" subject

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' m', ' d', ' g', ' syn' that start a longer word, mostly in text about errors or miscommunication. It predicts continuations such as 'ish', 'istr' and 'itch' (mishaps, mistrust).
result.label: Word-start fragment 'm' before mis- words

result.description: Fires on the plural agent suffix '-ers' (also -ists, -icians, -als) completing a profession noun, mostly 'engineers', in technical or professional text. Silent when 'ers' is a standalone token or part of a name like Vickers.
result.label: Professional plural suffix -ers (engineers)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'gener' (and 'arg') at the start of a longer word such as generation, generating, generators, where the next piece is a suffix. Members are mostly 'gener' detectors and similar prefix pieces (manip, deriv, mut).
result.label: 'gener' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " techn" (before -ologies/-ological), typically after an adjective or noun modifier like "energy-efficient" or "computing". It predicts the suffixes 'ologies' and 'ological'.
result.label: " techn" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the verb slot (' is', 's', 'ly' in "increasingly") right after dummy-subject "it" in "it is/it's/it becomes ... [adjective]" openers, predicting evaluative adjectives like clear, evident, apparent. Silent on other subjects' "is".
result.label: "it is" before evaluative adjective

result.description: Fires on the word piece "electro" (or "Elect|ro") as the start of a chemistry or physics compound such as electrolyte, electrode or electrostatic. It predicts continuations like "static", "chem" and "weak".
result.label: electro- prefix in chemistry words

result.description: Fires mainly on " financial" as a modifier in the middle of a sentence about economics or finance, where a noun like assets, instruments or markets comes next. It also fires weakly on "term" and "currency". It stayed silent on " financial" at the very start of a text.
result.label: ' financial' modifier before finance noun
Aud-'itory' word piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'itory' completing "auditory" (after "Aud"/"aud"). Upstream members detect 'itory' and related hearing/sound pieces such as 'ial', 'ic' and ' sound'.

Fires at sentence or paragraph boundaries and subject slots ("In", ".", "this section", "we") in expository essay-like text, where a new sentence is about to begin or introduce/explain something. Peaks are mixed and inconsistent; it is silent on some periods.
result.label: Expository sentence-start and subject slots

result.description: Fires on the first word piece of a multi-token word (' se' in securitization, ' reli', 'in' in refinement, ' valu') after a noun in abstract technical text, predicting suffixes like -ability, -ention, -ation. Silent on ' se' in 'seamless'.
result.label: Word-start fragment awaiting suffix

result.description: Fires on the token ' we' (mostly the pronoun, also in the split 'we'+'aving' in weaving texts) and pushes the next token toward 'aving'/'ave'/'aved'/'aves', i.e. weaving word pieces. Silent on some ' we' in ordinary pronoun use.
result.label: ' we' predicting weaving pieces

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments in the middle of scientific words, mostly 'gener' in "neurodegenerative", also ' mechan' and similar stems. Members detect biology/chemistry word-pieces and stems like Conserv-, deriv-, discrimin-.
result.label: Mid-word science stems, 'gener'

result.description: Fires on the word piece " sous", mainly in "sous vide" cooking text, where a hyphen or "vide" is expected next. Members include detectors of name and prefix pieces that precede a hyphen (Jean, Pierre, semi, anti) and cooking-related members.
result.label: ' sous' in sous vide

result.description: Fires on ' is' as the main verb right after a long abstract noun-phrase subject (e.g. "the rise of a political regime is", "Great migration is"). It stays silent when 'is' starts the text or follows a relative-clause or fragment.
result.label: ' is' after abstract noun subject

result.description: Fires on plural-selecting quantifier/determiner words (different, various, multiple, all, certain, these) before a plural noun, in abstract text about writing, language and texts. Silent on some 'different' cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Variety quantifiers before plural nouns

result.description: Fires on the 'als' piece completing "metals" (met + als), in text about metals and materials. It stays silent on 'als' in other words such as "Waals" and "reveals".
result.label: 'als' ending "metals"

result.description: Fires on the plural suffix 's' ending "defects" (also flaws, errors-type plurals), in text about lattice or material defects. Silent on verb or possessive 's' such as "affects" or "material's".
result.label: Plural 's' on defect(s)

result.description: Fires on ' Bang' in "Big Bang" in cosmology and physics text, such as Big Bang theory and nucleosynthesis. Weak activation appears on a few other science word pieces. Members include cosmology detectors for universe, inflation, nucleosynthesis and dark matter.
result.label: Big Bang (' Bang')

result.description: Fires on varied words (financial, capital, international, border) in finance and international-business text, where the next word is expected to be an economic noun like trade or investment. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Finance/international modifier before economic noun

result.description: Fires on the piece 'mi' inside "epidemiology/epidemiological", where the word is being built up and '-ology' comes next. It stays silent on 'mi' in other words such as "arrhythmias".
result.label: 'mi' in epidemiology

result.description: Fires on the word piece " out" used as a prefix at the start of a longer word, as in outpace, outnumbered, outcomes, outbreak, outliers. It predicts word continuations like pace, comes, break, lines.
result.label: " out" as word-initial prefix

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'anal' inside a longer word, mainly in 'artisanal' (artis-anal, is-anal) and similar split words. Fires on the piece, not on the whole word.
result.label: 'anal' piece in artisanal

result.description: Fires on the word piece "crypt" (or "rypt") at the start of cryptography/cryptographic/cryptanalysis, when more letters are expected to follow. It predicts continuations like "ographic". It is silent on general security text that lacks the piece.
result.label: crypt- word-start piece (cryptography)

result.description: Fires weakly on varied connective words (then, with, and, by) and word pieces in instructional or technical step-by-step text, such as methods and procedures. Peaks are inconsistent and the same tokens often stay silent, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Connectives in technical procedural text
' the' in abstract philosophy questions
result.description: Fires on ' the' (rarely ' its') right after a verb or preposition introducing an abstract topic, such as questioning, scrutinizing, or questions about, in philosophy and academic text. It stays quiet on ' the' elsewhere, such as after a comma or at a clause start.

Fires on the copula ' is'/' are' (also 'being', 'be') right after an abstract noun subject such as outcome, variable, probability or computation, in technical or definitional text. It predicts a verb or adverb like 'assign', 'calculated' or 'often'.
result.label: Copula after abstract technical subject

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'ular' in "secular" and "modular" and 'icon' in "semiconductors", where the word continues with a suffix. It stays silent on 'ular' in "vernacular". The evidence is mixed and the logits are unclear.
result.label: Mid-word fragments 'ular'/'icon' (secular)

result.description: Fires on a field-of-study noun (arts, engineering, art, business) right after "In (the realm of) ..." at the start of a document, in an academic-domain opener. Silent when the same word appears mid-sentence, not in that opening slot.
result.label: Field noun after "In ..." opener

result.description: Fires on the last digit of a four-digit year (e.g. 1925, 1796) when it is attributed to a person's work, as in "Stein's 1925 paper" or "his 1950 article". Predicts a work noun like paper, theory or book next.
result.label: Final year digit before a work

result.description: Fires on a concrete noun (well, junction, processor, image, drill, hole) ending a noun phrase after "the", often in technical text. Predicts a following possessive, "itself", or surface-like noun. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Technical noun before possessive/itself

result.description: Fires on the token ' data' as a noun-compound head right after a preposition, conjunction or sentence start, especially in biological or scientific research text. Stays quiet after modifiers like 'economic' or 'sample'. Predicts data-related continuations such as collection or interpretation.
result.label: ' data' in research text

result.description: Fires on "rather", "also", "but" after a "not only/solely X, but ..." contrast, where the next word introduces the agent or cause (predicts "by", "from", "through"). Silent on "rather than".
result.label: "but rather/also" after "not solely"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' trom' (as in trombone), and sometimes ' susp' (suspension), when a longer word is being split into pieces. Members detect instrument-name fragments and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: ' trom' fragment of trombone

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' h' when it starts a split-off "hormone" (e.g. "peptide-based h|ormone"), in biology/endocrine text. It is silent when "hormone" begins the document, and it predicts 'orm'.
result.label: ' h' starting "hormone"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Spe' at the start of a heading or title, such as "Speech Evaluation" or "Speech Recognition", and pushes the next token toward 'ech'. It is silent on other heading tokens such as 'Public'.
result.label: ' Spe' predicting 'ech'

result.description: Fires on the word " According" at the start of a document, in the opening "According to..." phrase. Weakly fires on similar "to"-taking words like "referred" or "according". Members are mostly detectors of "According" and related words.
result.label: Document-initial " According" (to)

result.description: Fires on the end of "artificial intelligence" (' intelligence', 'elligence') and on the "I" of "AI", in tech/AI text. Predicts AI-system nouns such as systems, devices, chat, robot.
result.label: Artificial intelligence / AI term

result.description: Fires on comparative or increase words (higher, greater, increased, larger) in science text, mostly "the higher/greater the X" style relations about energy, bonds or density. Silent on "higher" used as a plain positional word.
result.label: Comparative 'higher/greater' in science

result.description: Fires on the word ' charge' in physics text about electric or color charge (total charge, types of charge, charge density). Predicts continuations like carriers, distributions, conjugation. Members are mostly earlier ' charge' detectors.
result.label: Physics 'charge' token

result.description: Fires on ' the' right after a verb of introducing, proposing or developing (introduced, conceptualized, established, use), where a named idea, concept or invention comes next. Silent on ' the' after 'are', 'until', or at text start.
result.label: 'the' after introduced/developed verbs

result.description: Fires on ' column' (also ' row', ' block') right before 'space'/'vector' in linear algebra text about matrices. Silent in general vector-space text that lacks this matrix column/row term.
result.label: Matrix column/row before space

result.description: Fires on the word " random" (also Random, randomly) in statistics and ML text, such as random sampling, randomization and random subspaces. It pushes toward suffixes like -ness, -ized, -ization and toward " sampling". Silent on related words like entropy.
result.label: " random" token detector

result.description: Fires on the first fragment of a split word (bl-, foc-, expos-, v-) in photography and optics text, such as depth of field, focal length and blurring. Members are photography and art topic detectors plus word-start detectors.
result.label: Word-start pieces in photography text

result.description: Fires on the "ate" piece completing "substr|ate" (enzyme substrate), especially before words like concentration or type. It stays silent on "ate" in other words such as pyruvate, phosphate, initiate and culminate.
result.label: "ate" in "substrate"

result.description: Fires on varied function words (to, of, in, beyond, quote marks) in texts about grammar and gender-neutral or singular "they" pronouns. It stays silent on many identical "to" tokens in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in gender-grammar text

result.description: Fires on the word " next" in phrases like "the next generation/decade/big thing", predicting continuations such as " generation". Weaker on similar forward-looking words like "ahead" and "latest".
result.label: " next" before generation/decade

result.description: Fires on the end of a measurable physical quantity term in science headings (Dens-ity, Intens-ity, Bond L-ength, width, speed, density), where a measurement or calculation is expected next. Silent on 'ity' in other nouns like viscosity or ubiquity.
result.label: Measurable quantity noun endings

result.description: Fires on plural person nouns like ' people' or ' individuals' as the subject of a clause, mostly right after 'that', 'how' or 'when', where a verb comes next. It stays silent on 'people' at the start of a text.
result.label: People/individuals as clause subject

result.description: Fires on geometric region nouns like " plane", " surface", " interval", " point" in math text (calculus, geometry, vector fields), where the noun names a space or domain being integrated over or located in. Silent on casual "place" uses.
result.label: Math geometric domain nouns (plane, surface)

result.description: Fires on the final word piece of a surname (e.g. 'orth' in Wordsworth, 'di' in Vivaldi) in a list of famous people after "poets like" or "artists such as". Likely predicts a following name separator or suffix.
result.label: Surname-ending piece in famous-name lists

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "discovery"/"detection" (discovery of X), also weakly on "discovered"/"discovering". Silent on " of" after other nouns like "nature", "establishment", "methods". Predicts a newly found thing.
result.label: "of" after discovery/detection

result.description: Fires on the token " group" (also Group/groups), mostly in mathematical group theory contexts (group representations, homomorphisms, action). Predicts math continuations like Theory, actions, isomorphism, rings. Members are mainly group-token detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: "group" in group theory

result.description: Fires on the token ' familiar' (including the start of "familiarize" and "familiarity"), strongest in "must familiarize themselves" and "require familiarity". It predicts suffixes like -ity and -ize next.
result.label: ' familiar' before -ize/-ity suffix

result.description: Fires on ' such' right after a plural noun like "issues" or "treatments", where "such as" introduces examples. Silent on 'such' in "of such innovative approaches" and similar. Pushes toward problem nouns such as errors and crashes.
result.label: ' such' introducing examples

result.description: Fires on the copula ' is'/' are' right after a relative pronoun "that" (or "who/which") that opens a defining relative clause, as in "a proposition that is always true". It is silent on plain subject-verb "are".
result.label: Copula after relative 'that'

result.description: Fires on the word " business" (or "Business") used as a modifier before a noun, such as business goals, leaders, strategies or intelligence. Members are mostly business-token detectors. Output favors nouns like cards, units, goals.
result.label: "business" as noun modifier

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ge' (or ' Ge') that begins geo- words like geography, geology, geophysics, in earth-science lists. Predicts continuations such as 'ographical', 'ological', 'och'. Silent on some sentence-initial or "political/cultural ge" cases.
result.label: ' ge' start of geo- words

result.description: Fires on the word piece "arr" inside "Narrative" (N-arr-ative), and to a lesser degree on " narr" and similar prefix pieces. It predicts suffixes like "ative" or "ator" that complete the word.
result.label: "arr" piece in Narrative

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ict' in "depict" (depicting, depictions), and more weakly on 'ray' in "portray". It predicts continuations like 'ions', 'ing', ' scenes', ' how'.
result.label: 'ict' in depict/portray

result.description: Fires mostly on ' corner' in "cornerstone" (e.g. "the corner|stone of"), predicting 'stone'. Also weakly on scattered tokens such as '/' in dates, 'ative', and 'front' in "forefront". The circuit is mostly corner detectors.
result.label: corner of "cornerstone"

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, the, these, this, with) in text about classifying or grouping things into classes, genera, or categories. It predicts next tokens like "classification", "categories", "subclass", "each". Silent on "of" in generic descriptive phrases.
result.label: Function words in classification text

result.description: Fires on ' who' as a relative pronoun after a plural profession or role noun (educators, writers, programmers) in "useful/essential for X who…" phrasing, predicting want/wish. Silent after fictional characters or "someone".
result.label: who after professions/audience nouns

result.description: Fires on the piece "gen" completing chemical element names, mainly "nitrogen" (also hydrogen, oxygen, estrogen). Predicts continuations like "fix", "ous", "dioxide". Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: "gen" in nitrogen

result.description: Fires on ' consider' when it is the stem of the noun "considerations" (after a modifier like ethical, safety, ergonomic), predicting the "-ations" suffix. Silent when ' consider' is the verb (should consider, we consider).
result.label: consider- stem of "considerations"

result.description: Fires on " international" / " International" (also " global"), strongest as a capitalized heading word at the start of a topic title like "International Trade". Pushes toward affairs, relations, commerce and diplomacy.
result.label: International / global (trade, relations)

result.description: Fires on connectors (as, and, like, from, in) that introduce or continue a list of animal examples in text about predators and animal species. Silent on the same connectors in non-animal contexts. Predicts animal-related continuations.
result.label: Connectors before animal example lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' Sh', ' of', 'atic', ' listener', ' environment') mostly in abstract academic or scientific prose, especially chemistry-like text. Peaks are inconsistent, and members are mostly generic attention latents with no clear shared token.
result.label: Scattered tokens in technical prose

result.description: Fires on mid-word or mid-phrase pieces that precede a continuation: 'ymn' in gymnastics, ' Life' in 'Software Development Life Cycle', ' unit' in 'per unit', 'itions' in prepositions. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Incomplete word/phrase fragment tokens

result.description: Fires on ' to' as an infinitive marker of purpose after a tool/agent noun (models, engineers, analytics, tools) in analytical or engineering text, predicting action verbs like calculate, analyze, advance. Silent after 'challenge you', 'leading to', 'crucial to', 'ability to'.
result.label: purpose infinitive 'to' after tools

result.description: Fires on the closing parenthesis after an acronym like (AI) or (ML) that abbreviates a tech term such as artificial intelligence, machine learning or virtual reality. It predicts plural tech nouns next (algorithms, systems, models). Silent on parentheses around other content.
result.label: Closing paren after tech acronym

result.description: Fires on the verb (' are', ' is', ' were') right after the relative pronoun 'that' or 'which' introducing a relative clause on a plural or mass noun, where a predicate adjective comes next. Silent on 'are' after a plain subject noun.
result.label: Copula after relative 'that'

result.description: Fires on mixed function words and adverb pieces (' be', ' as', ' just', '-ly') in abstract, essay-style philosophical or religious prose, where an adjective, adverb or predicate is expected next. Silent on many ' be' tokens elsewhere.
result.label: Abstract-prose predicate-slot function words

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ility' completing the word "mobility" (geographic, occupational, worker mobility). Silent on unrelated text. Logits favour mob-like continuations.
result.label: 'ility' ending "mobility"

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments ' fant' (fantasy) and ' inqu'/' enqu' (inquiry) that begin a longer word after an adjective or noun, mid-sentence. Silent when ' fant' opens the document. Members mostly detect ' inqu'.
result.label: fant-/inqu- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on ordinal suffix pieces ('st', 'th') after a number, like 21st or 20th, just before 'century'. Silent on 'st' in words like 'Amidst'.
result.label: Ordinal suffix before 'century'

result.description: Fires on ' plants', 'ician' (Ordovician) and similar words ending a noun phrase in text about prehistoric life, paleontology and early evolution (vascular plants, life forms). Silent on ' plants' in other contexts like ecology or general plant talk.
result.label: Paleozoic life-history nouns (plants, Ordovician)

result.description: Fires on ' and'/' or'/commas right after a list of time units (days, weeks, months, years), where another time unit or "even ..." item is expected. It is quiet on 'and' after other kinds of lists or clauses.
result.label: Conjunction after time-unit lists

result.description: Fires on word endings or head nouns that close a field or discipline name (-ics, -ology, 'techniques', 'analysis'), predicting sector/discipline-like continuations. It is silent on some -ics words such as robotics, economics and mathematics, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Field/discipline name endings (-ics, -ology)

result.description: Fires on words in a comparison with a conventional or earlier counterpart ("unlike its", "over conventional", "its syntactical counterpart"). It seems to predict "counter", "predecessors" or "ones". It is silent on ordinary ' the'.
result.label: Contrast with counterpart or predecessor

result.description: Fires on adjectives like "fundamental", "foundational", "valid", "very" in academic descriptions of a field investigating "the fundamental principles" of something. It is silent when "fundamental" is predicative or follows a verb, as in "are fundamental tenets".
result.label: Fundamental/foundational before principles
"dishes" plural in food text
result.description: Fires on the "ishes" piece completing "dishes" (d-ishes) in cooking and food writing, e.g. "create dishes that reflect...". Members are food, menu, recipe and ingredient detectors plus other "ishes" detectors. It predicts words like "prepared" and "made".

Fires on the piece "ersion" completing "immersion" (as in "language immersion programs"). Members detect the "imm" + "ers" pieces. It is weaker on "immersive" word pieces, and predicts nouns like "programs" or "schools".
result.label: "ersion" in "immersion"

result.description: Fires on function words (in, a, whether, to, with) in technical physics/science text, especially around moment of inertia, where the next word is likely a technical term. Silent on some ' in' tokens in other engineering contexts. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Function words in physics explanations

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ain' inside split words, mainly 'Sust-ain-able/ability' and also 'unsustain', 'Remain-der', 'Inpainting'. It predicts suffixes like 'able' and 'ability'.
result.label: 'ain' piece in Sustainable

result.description: Fires on the 'z' piece inside "hazards" (ha|z|ards), predicting the completion 'ards'/'ard'. Members are mostly 'z' detectors in the same word.
result.label: 'z' in "hazards"

result.description: Fires mostly on the mid-word piece 'mos' in "Atmospheric" at the start of a document or heading. It also fires weakly on other mid-word pieces such as 'ized', 'rive' and 'ural'. The circuit is diffuse and mixed.
result.label: 'mos' in Atmospheric (word piece)

result.description: Fires on the word ' traffic' (road traffic, signals, congestion, management) in transportation or traffic-control text. It predicts continuations like flow, lights, routing and management. The contrast is a network-isolation passage with no road traffic.
result.label: ' traffic' in road/traffic control

result.description: Fires on technology/design nouns (' design', ' technology', 'techn-ologies/ological') used as modifiers in noun phrases, e.g. "requirements or design specifications", "changing technology trends". Predicts a following plural noun like requirements or details. Silent on 'software design' as a head topic.
result.label: design/technology modifier before noun

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ple' at the start of "pleasing"/"pleasures", mostly after "aesthetically" or "visually". Members detect similar word-start fragments (appe-, decre-, multip-) that predict a suffix like "asing".
result.label: ' ple' fragment before -asing

result.description: Fires on the word ' tied' in the "tied to" sense of being connected or dependent, usually after "closely", "often" or "no longer". Upstream members detect related words such as tied, linked, connected, closely and likened.
result.label: ' tied' in "closely tied to"

result.description: Fires on the word " interpretation" as a noun, in analytical or scientific text (data, spectra, art, meaning). Members are mostly detectors of "interpret/interpretation" tokens. It stays silent on contrast text without the word.
result.label: ' interpretation' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " visual" itself, mostly as an adjective in arts, media and communication text (visual art, visual narratives, visual cues). Members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token. Logits are not clear.
result.label: ' visual' token detector

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece (-ing, -es, -ed, or "rich") completing the verb "enrich", e.g. "enriching", "enriches". Silent on -ing after other verbs. Predicts objects like "our", "lives", "the".
result.label: suffix completing "enrich" verb

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ually" in "mutually", mainly in "mutually exclusive". Members detect "mut" plus "ual/ually" pieces. It pushes toward "exclusive" and similar words.
result.label: "ually" in "mutually"

result.description: Fires on a word-start fragment (e.g. 'c' in trans-c-ends, ' el', ' enc', ' ep') after a subject noun, where a third-person verb like "transcends/elucidates/epitomizes" is being spelled out; predicts verb stem endings (-itated, -iled). Silent on some 'c' in similar words.
result.label: Mid-word verb stem fragment

result.description: Fires on world/universe/planet/Earth as a noun for the whole world, mostly after "our" or "the" (e.g. "in our world"). Silent on "worldwide" and "around the world" idioms.
result.label: "our world/planet/universe" noun

result.description: Fires on list separators (' and', commas, ' as', abbreviation openers) within enumerations of technical or scientific terms, such as hydrology processes or neural network types. It stays silent on many other list 'and' tokens, so the extra condition is unclear.
result.label: List separators in technical enumerations

result.description: Fires on the token ' English' as the name of the language, especially in linguistic-history or language-study text (Old/Middle English, "the English language"). It predicts language-related continuations like language, history and literature. It was silent on "American English Literature".
result.label: ' English' language-name token
Word-start ' ass' before -urance/-ess
result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ass' at the start of words like assurance, assent, assess, assay, assure, and predicts continuations such as 'urance' and 'esse'. Members are mostly ' ass' detectors plus other word-start pieces (ens-, supp-).

Fires on auxiliary verbs (is/are/be, sometimes "then") right after a plural or mass noun for a substance or supply (oxygen, nutrients, supplies), in a passive slot predicting verbs like distributed, transferred, supplied. Silent on "is" before adjectives or predicates.
result.label: Passive auxiliary after transported substance

result.description: Fires on connectors (' and', ' over', ' while', ' with', '-') right after "short-term" or "long", where the next word is expected to be "long/longer/long-lasting". Silent on ' and' after other words.
result.label: Connector after short-term, predicting long

result.description: Fires on " the" (or "comparing") right after verbs like evaluate/assess in definitions of cost-benefit analysis, where the next word is likely "cost"/"benefits". Silent on "the" in other evaluation contexts.
result.label: "the" before cost-benefit terms

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in wind, climate and geography text, such as "Southern", "west" in northwest, "rose" in compass rose, and "Lat" in Horse Latitudes. It seems to anticipate a following word about flows or circulation. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Wind and compass-direction terms

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'j' inside words split as Con-j-unctions or Dis-j-unctive, where 'unct' comes next. Also fires on 'j' in other split words like Abjad or Ujjain, and predicts 'unct'/'unction' as the continuation.
result.label: 'j' piece in conjunction/disjunction

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' population', ' to', ' of', Cyrillic 'но') mostly in genetics and evolution text about gene flow and alleles. It is silent on ' population' in ecology or health contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Gene-flow text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires mainly on the word " sentiment" (also "iment" in sentiment-like pieces), most strongly when it is the first word of "sentiment analysis/classification/scores" in NLP text. Weak activity on a few other word pieces.
result.label: "sentiment" before analysis

result.description: Fires on the token " reporting" as a noun modifier in compliance or business text (e.g. "mandatory reporting", "reporting standards"). Many members are reporting detectors. It pushes toward "on", "requirements", "reported".
result.label: ' reporting' noun-modifier token

result.description: Fires on plural nouns for connections or pathways (networks, channels, routes) right after a modifier like "trade" or "exchange", mostly in trade and exchange text. Weaker on similar plurals such as paths and mechanisms.
result.label: Trade/exchange networks, channels, routes

result.description: Fires on the end of an abstract value noun (self-expression, harmony, assertiveness, cohesion, diversity) that is the object of "prioritize/emphasize/value". Predicts a comparative continuation such as "over" or "above".
result.label: Prioritized abstract value noun
