result.description: Fires mostly on ' und' as the start of "undermine"-type words (also ' an', '.', ' and') in text about errors, bias and narration, where the next piece is likely a word-continuation like "erm". Silent on ' und' in "undependable".
result.label: ' und' before 'ermine' words

result.description: Fires on the hyphen right after a single capital letter, most strongly in "X-ray" (also chord labels like C-E, I-IV). It stays quiet on hyphens after words such as "super-", "high-", "electron-".
result.label: Hyphen after letter (X-ray)

result.description: Fires on plural-selecting quantifier adjectives like "different", "various", "diverse" after "across"/"within" in sociolinguistic or cultural text, predicting group nouns such as regions, communities, social. Silent after a verb like "explore".
result.label: across different regions/communities

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in expository text, most clearly ' comfortable' after "less" (less comfortable with the unfamiliar), also on apostrophes, ' the' and commas. Apostrophes before possessive 's are silent. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered peaks, 'less comfortable'

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a list or noun phrase about communication, emotions, intent or empathy, where a continuation like "which", "leading", "while" may follow. Silent on commas after introductory phrases or in writing/narrative contexts.
result.label: Comma after emotion/communication list

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (comma, "by", "and", "the", "of", "-able") mid-sentence in abstract explanatory text, where an adjective or noun like "natural", "basic" or "variable" may come next. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered function tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " di" when it begins a longer word split into pieces (dipole, diode, diagnostics, diet). It pushes toward continuations like "agnostics", "pole", "atomic".
result.label: word-initial " di" fragment

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly " of", also " a", " the") in statistics and probability explanations, e.g. "the number of", "the mean of". It stays silent on some " of" tokens in similar math text, so the rule is unclear.
result.label: Function words in statistics text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, mostly periods ending list-style topic or course headings (e.g. "Musicology."), and also on "and"/"or" in lists. It is silent on many similar periods, and the evidence does not say why.
result.label: Periods and conjunctions in topic lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " ded" in "deductive", "deducing" and "deduction", where the next piece is a continuation like "uctive" or "ucing". Mostly appears in logic and reasoning text.
result.label: " ded" start of deductive

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (as, in, from, of, another, this) in expository passages about the history or development of a field; peaks are inconsistent. Members look like history-narrative context (ancient Egypt/Greece, 'became', 'began'). Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in historical development prose

result.description: Fires on a comma that follows a sentence-ending period, where the comma sits oddly at the start of the next sentence (likely a corrupted or lowercased sentence start). It stays silent on commas inside ordinary sentences.
result.label: Comma right after sentence end

result.description: Fires on the word "risk" (' risk' or the 'isk' piece of "Risk"), especially in risk-management text such as headings like "Risk Assessment" or phrases like "comprehensive risk assessment". It is quiet on non-risk business text.
result.label: Risk word in risk-management text

result.description: Fires on the final noun or word piece of a "the use of X" style phrase (device, symbols, herbs, printmaking, arts), where the sentence is about to take a verb. The peaks are varied. It stays silent on "culinary arts" in some contexts.
result.label: Object noun of "use of X" phrase

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " govern" (also "Govern"), mostly as the start of "governments", "governance" or "governed". It predicts the suffixes "ments" and "ance". Members are mostly "govern" detectors.
result.label: ' govern' stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'atic' in "chromatic" and "achromatic/apochromatic", in optics text about aberration. It stays silent on 'atic' in "systematic", so it needs the chrom- stem before it.
result.label: 'atic' in chromatic

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' me' when it begins a longer word, mainly "meal(s)" and "meats", after words like "every", "your", "prepared". It predicts continuations like 'als', 'ats', 'al'. Silent on standalone 'me'.
result.label: ' me' start of meal/meats

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' lost' most often, also ' like', ' to', ' an', ',', ' by') in mid-sentence positions. Many members detect 'lost'/'lose'/'losing', but the peaks are mixed and the pattern is weak. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Mixed 'lost' and function-word positions

result.description: Fires on the word " why" (or "Why") introducing a why-clause or question, e.g. "understanding why", "reason why", "is why", "Why do". Members are mostly why-detectors. The contrast text has no "why".
result.label: Word "why" introducing explanation

result.description: Fires on the word piece "inal" completing "marginal" (also "nominal") in economics text, as in "diminishing marginal utility". Silent when "inal" starts a text with no preceding piece.
result.label: "inal" in marginal (economics)

result.description: Fires on metal and metallic element names (iron, copper pieces, "metal", "metals") in chemistry or materials text, often in lists of metals or alloys. Silent in organic chemistry text without metals.
result.label: Metal and element names in chemistry

result.description: Fires on " from" right after the noun "period" (e.g. "The period from the early…"), introducing a time span start. Silent on "from" after verbs like "shift away" or "took over", or after other nouns or adverbs.
result.label: "period from" time-span opener

result.description: Fires on ' the' (or ' its') right before "premises" or similar logic terms, in text about logical validity, e.g. "if the premises", "truth of the premises". Silent on ' the' in other math or general contexts. Predicts logic words like premises, conclusion, antecedent.
result.label: 'the' before premises in logic

result.description: Fires on ' a'/' an'/' both'/' also' (the slot before a predicate noun) in "more than just a X" / "not only ... but also a X" constructions. Silent on ordinary 'a' in other contexts.
result.label: Article after "more than just"/"not only"

result.description: Fires on ' an' (also 'a'/'the') right after a form of "play" in "plays an important role", expecting "role"; also on 'ol' in repeated "Decolonization". Silent on ' an' elsewhere, e.g. "are an ideal example".
result.label: "play an (important role)" article

result.description: Fires on the word piece " concentr" when it is the start of "concentrations" (chemistry and kinetics text, e.g. reactant or product concentrations). It stays silent on the whole word "concentration", so it needs the split-word form.
result.label: ' concentr' word-piece before -ations

result.description: Fires on " role"/" roles" right after "played/play a [adjective]" (e.g. "played a crucial role"). It stays quiet on "role" as a plain noun, as in "The role of geometry" or "on the role", and in some "playing an important role" cases.
result.label: "play a significant role" noun

result.description: Fires on " of" after collective quantity nouns like "series", "myriad", "succession", in historical or event-narrative text, anticipating a plural noun of events or actions. Silent on " of" after ordinary nouns like "end", "portrayal", "implementation".
result.label: " of" after "series/myriad" quantity nouns

result.description: Fires on the 'atic' piece completing "pragmatic" (also ' practical') in linguistics/philosophy text. It stays silent on 'atic' in other words such as systematic or idiomatic.
result.label: 'atic' in "pragmatic"
Comma after "cognitive" in list
result.description: Fires on the comma (sometimes "and") after an adjective like "cognitive" in a list of psychological or developmental domains (cognitive, emotional, social...). Silent on commas after other nouns or clauses.
Fires on the piece 'ci' inside the split word "glaciers" (also glacières, glaciation), after "gla". Silent when 'ci' starts a text without "gla" before it. Predicts word endings like 'ers' and 'ar'.
result.label: 'ci' in "gla-ci-er"

result.description: Fires on the word " nature" as the natural world (often after "of", "from", "with", "in"), in essay-like text about art and writing. Weaker on "human nature" or "in nature" meaning character. Silent on "changing nature of".
result.label: " nature" as the natural world

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (using, of, and, to, any) in abstract expository prose about processes, methods and analysis. The peaks are diffuse and the contrast is silent on only one 'using', so the trigger is mixed.
result.label: Function words in abstract process prose

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase words (' this', 'body', ' abstract', ' both', 'internal') in abstract, expository science/philosophy prose, often before a noun. Peaks are diffuse; members are mostly philosophy and biology context features. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered words in expository academic prose

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered function words (' to', ' the', ' if', ' of', ' and') and odd word pieces, including Arabic fragments. No clear pattern. It leans slightly toward predicting adjectives like "multiple" or "various". The circuit is diffuse and failed.
result.label: Diffuse function-word latent, unclear

result.description: Fires on mid-name word pieces of historical European scientists and artists, mainly 'ardo' in Leonardo and 'erm' in Fermat, where the surname continues next. Silent on plain lists of names.
result.label: Leonardo/Fermat name fragments

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ographic' completing words like "Biogeographic", mostly in title-like headings at document start. Weak activity on other word-ending pieces. Pushes toward nouns such as regions, features, provinces.
result.label: 'ographic' in Biogeographic

result.description: Fires on the word " social" (or " Social") as a modifier before a noun, mostly in business or society text such as "social media", "social impact" and "social responsibility". Members are mostly token detectors for "social".
result.label: word "social" as modifier

result.description: Peaks are scattered over unrelated tokens (' or', ' current', ' dense', ' in', a Hebrew piece) with only 12% consistency. Members are mostly economics/finance-flavored mid-sentence context. No clear single trigger; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token, finance-flavored context

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ro" inside "spect|ro|scopy" / "spectroscopic", predicting the continuation "sc" (scopy). Silent when "ro" begins the text without the "spect" prefix.
result.label: "ro" in spectroscopy

result.description: Fires on the word ' over' after nouns of control, power or preference (control over, group over another, intervention over, overlook/oversee), mostly in political or imperial-power text. It stays silent on non-'over' tokens.
result.label: ' over' after control/power nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on ' from' (also ' on', ' of', ' the') after verbs or nouns of benefiting or depending, such as "receive from" and "benefit from", in economic or financial text. It stays silent on ' from' in other senses, like "switch from".
result.label: 'from' after benefit/receive verbs

result.description: Fires on commas (and 'and'/'or') separating items in a list of clauses of the form "verb-s noun, verb-s noun", e.g. "enhances productivity, improves...", where the next item is another third-person verb. Silent on commas in noun lists or after other constructions.
result.label: Comma in verb-phrase benefit lists

result.description: Fires on the suffix "ibility" when it completes "access" (accessibility). It stays silent on "ibility" in "flexibility", so it needs the access- stem. Supporting members detect disabilities and accessibility context.
result.label: accessibility suffix after "access"

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns ' which'/' that' (sometimes ' it') after a comma following a defined technical term or symbol, e.g. "Ka, which is...", introducing a definition-like clause about a measure or constant. Silent on some chemistry-related "which" clauses.
result.label: Relative 'which' after defined technical term

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments and mid-word pieces (' architect' before -ures/-ural, ' m', ' p', ' t') and some function words like 'the' before a number. It looks like a word-continuation latent, but the peaks are mixed and the evidence is thin.
result.label: Word-start fragments awaiting suffix

result.description: Fires on the copula ' is'/' are' right after an abstract value noun (integrity, honesty, transparency) as subject inside a clause like "an environment where X is...". Silent on 'is' after other subjects in definitional statements.
result.label: Copula after value noun in 'where' clause

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in a possessive 's after a mathematician's or scientist's name (Euler's, Gauss's, Fermat's), where a theorem or law follows. Silent on quote marks, contractions like "'s important", and bare apostrophes.
result.label: Apostrophe after scientist name possessive

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ly' in "Supply" (mainly at document start in "Supply Chain" headings), and weakly on ' supply' before "chain". It stays silent on the suffix 'ly' in words like "increasingly" or "Elderly". It predicts ' chain'.
result.label: 'ly' in "Supply" (Chain)

result.description: Fires on verbs like "extends", "goes", "extend" right after an abstract subject (influence, history of music, application), where "beyond" is expected next. Predicts reach going beyond a domain.
result.label: extends/goes (beyond) after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the adjective " private" (and " public") as a modifier, especially in "public/private key" cryptography and "private sector" contexts. Members are mostly private/public token detectors. Contrast text about concealed IP addresses is silent.
result.label: private / public adjective

result.description: Fires on " of" right after probability/likelihood/risk/chance nouns (e.g. "reducing the likelihood of a Type I error"), in statistics and risk text. Predicts event or outcome words next. Silent on " of" after impact, threshold, significance.
result.label: "of" after likelihood/probability/risk

result.description: Fires on the token " conservation", mostly in physics text about conservation laws (momentum, energy), and also in ecological "conservation" uses. Weak on other word pieces like "quantization".
result.label: ' conservation' token detector

result.description: Fires on function or descriptive words (' high', ' offers', ' of', ' low') in energy and nuclear text, right before a property or attribute of an energy source such as "high energy density". Silent on ' high' in hyphenated or price uses.
result.label: Energy-source attribute slot (nuclear)

result.description: Fires mostly on " use" as a noun after "the" (e.g. "The use of ..."), plus occasional " an" before "essential" and a few abstract nouns. Silent on " use" as a verb or in some noun contexts; the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Noun "the use of" in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ert' in the verb "exert" (exerted, exerts, exerting), mostly after "force" or "pressure". It stays silent on 'ert' in "inertia", so it needs the "ex-" prefix.
result.label: 'ert' in "exert"

result.description: Fires on scattered function and modifier words (' unnecessary', ' and', ' religious', ' ger') in academic text about philosophy, humanism and the Renaissance, where an adjective or noun like 'classical' or 'religious' might come next. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Scattered words in humanist/philosophy text

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often 'CI' (as in CI/CD or HCI) plus scattered function words like 'to' or 'the' in technical, software-related text. Peaks are inconsistent, so the pattern is weak and mixed.
result.label: Mixed tokens, 'CI' in tech text

result.description: Fires on the 'ness' piece in "harness" (harnessed/harnessing sunlight, wind), where the word is unfinished and a suffix like -ed/-ing comes next. Weakly fires on other mid-word pieces such as 'vest' in harvest.
result.label: 'ness' in harness (word-piece)

result.description: Fires on ' even' (sometimes ' or') in a list of verbs, as in "enhance, or even completely negate", where another verb is expected next. Silent on some other ' even' uses, so the construction is the clue.
result.label: 'even' in verb-list escalation

result.description: Fires on the word " labor" (or " labour") in economics text, as in "labor market", "labor productivity", "labor force". Members are mostly detectors of labor/Labor and related worker words.
result.label: labor / labour word

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' una' (start of "unauthorized/unauthorised"), mostly after "prevent", "against" or "from" in security text. It predicts a continuation that completes the word. Weaker on ' deg'.
result.label: ' una' of "unauthorized"

result.description: Fires mainly on " external" (as in "externality") and " environmental" in sustainability and economics text about internalizing costs. It also fires weakly on "the" in that text. It is quiet on generic ecology text.
result.label: external(ity) in environmental economics

result.description: Fires on adjectives like "accurate", "precise", "detailed" (and "-itative") in technical or scientific text about analysis and methods, but not on every occurrence of "accurate". Weaker firing on other method-related words.
result.label: Precision adjectives in technical analysis

result.description: Fires on a word-fragment mid-word, mostly the 'r' in "nut-r-itional/nutrition" and the ' sk' in "skilled/skull", predicting the word's continuation (itional, illed). Silent on 'r' in "carbohydrates".
result.label: Mid-word 'r' in nutr-, ' sk' in skilled

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens ('und' in Hund, ' system', ' to', commas) typically ending a noun phrase subject, where a verb or continuation is expected next. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Scattered subject-noun-phrase endings

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (to, for, can, that, its, enabled) in expository passages about technology and processes, often after "not only... but also" or a verb expecting an object. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Function words in expository technology prose

result.description: Fires on function words (as, not, is, a, merely) in abstract philosophy or argumentation prose, mostly where a definition or contrast is being set up ("X is a...", "not as an..."). Silent on "as" meaning "because" or in "as well as".
result.label: Function words in philosophical definitions

result.description: Fires mostly on the lone letter piece 'c' in the middle of a word (skys-c-rapers, Cres-c-endo, glyc-ogenol) or as a subscript variable, plus occasional ' h'. Members are mostly 'c' detectors. Predicts a word continuation.
result.label: mid-word 'c' fragment

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (commas, 'the', 'of', 'to') inside text about measuring, assessing or evaluating proficiency, metrics and statistics. It seems to predict measurement-related next words like 'gauge', 'share' or 'market'. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in assessment/metrics text

result.description: Fires on " greatly" right after "vary/varies/differ", predicting a following "depending/across/from". It is silent on "greatly" before a verb, as in "can greatly enhance".
result.label: "greatly" after vary/differ

result.description: Fires on " clear" as an adjective right after an article or verb like "a"/"provides a"/"have", before an abstract noun (pattern, framework, indication). Quiet on "shape clear expression". Pushes toward nouns like distinction, indication.
result.label: Adjective "clear" before abstract noun

result.description: Fires on mid-phrase tokens, often adjective suffixes (vibrant, solidified, usable, delicious) or function words like "the"/"of", in energy, heat and cooking transformation text. Peaks are mixed; "the" is often silent in similar contexts.
result.label: Transformation text adjective suffixes, function words

result.description: Fires mainly on ' A' in "Middle Ages" (the A that starts a word split into pieces, predicting 'ges'), and weakly on other capitalized word-start fragments. Silent on sentence-initial ' A' as an article.
result.label: ' A' in "Middle Ages"

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' Dr' and 'j' (e.g. 'Dr.' at the start of a document, 'dis-j-unctive', 'Con-j-unctions'). Members detect 'conj'/'j' pieces predicting 'unction'. It is silent on ' Dr' inside a name like 'Jean Drèze'.
result.label: ' Dr' and 'j' word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on a comma ending a clause about sustainability, circular economy or societal themes, where a participial or relative clause (emphasizing, which, while) is likely to follow. Silent on commas inside lists or after other clauses.
result.label: Comma after sustainability clause

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', ' and', ' for', ' types') in finance/economics and technical expository text, but is silent on many ' the' tokens elsewhere. The members are mostly finance-flavoured and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in finance/technical text

result.description: Fires on suffix pieces like "-driven", "-powered", "sophisticated", "advanced" right after "AI" in technology text, marking an AI-enabled modifier. Silent on "data-driven" and on "ven" inside "avenues".
result.label: AI-driven / AI-powered suffix

result.description: Fires on the word " capital" (also "Capital"), mostly in finance text (capital structure, budgeting, expenditure) and also before "-ization/-ism" or in capital letters. Members are mostly detectors of " capital".
result.label: ' capital' token detector

result.description: Fires on the verb or preposition right after the subject "efficiency" in definitional phrases like "efficiency refers to", "means", "involves", "denotes". Silent on purposive or infinitive "to" (in order to, ability to).
result.label: Definition verb after 'efficiency'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' of', ' in', ' the', ' while') in descriptions of crafts, textiles, art and cultural traditions, where a cultural or artistic noun is expected next. Silent on many other ' of' tokens. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in craft/culture text

result.description: Fires on connecting function words or verb endings (of, using, employing, such as, by) right after mentions of the evolutionary or genetic-algorithm process. It is silent on the same words in other algorithm or technique text, so it needs this topic.
result.label: Evolutionary process linking words (genetic algorithms)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in expository academic prose, such as commas, verb endings (-ized, -ated) and 'and', mostly where a verb or clause continues after a noun phrase. Peaks are diffuse and the contrast is silent on commas, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mid-clause continuation in expository text

result.description: Fires on ' to' (also ' for', ' can') after tools, software or methods in statistics and data-analysis text, where a purpose phrase follows ("tools available to help"). It stays silent on some ' to' in similar "used to" contexts.
result.label: purpose 'to' after statistical tools

result.description: Fires on " are" after a coordinated list of plural subjects (e.g. "X, Y, and Z are") in academic or scientific text, where a phrase like "all important factors" or "key" tends to follow. Silent after a simple single plural subject.
result.label: " are" after listed subjects

result.description: Fires on function words (' of', ' the', ' in', verbs like 'defines') right after "register" in linguistics definitions, e.g. "register defines the variety of language". Silent on the same ' of' in generic communication text lacking the register topic.
result.label: Function words in linguistic register definitions

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ro' inside 'nitrogen' (nit-ro-gen), strongest in nitrogen cycle/fixation text; weakly on 'ro' in 'carrots'. Members are 'ro' detectors that mostly predict 'gen' next.
result.label: 'ro' in nitrogen

result.description: Fires mostly on commas and function words inside lists or enumerations of items (e.g. "hiring performers, stagehands, security"), where the next item or clause is expected. Silent on commas after introductory phrases. Logits are weak and mixed.
result.label: List-internal commas and connectors

result.description: Fires on the verb ' result' right after a modal like can/could/may/to, in "X can result in Y" causal constructions. Silent on the noun 'results' (e.g. "accuracy of results"). Predicts ' in' next.
result.label: verb 'result' before 'in'

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs like " the", " indicate", " suggest", " and" in explanatory text about topography, maps and terrain, where a verb or article is about to introduce a described feature. Silent on " the" in other business or abstract contexts.
result.label: Terrain and map text connectives

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'inu' in "Continuous" (also Continuum/Continuity), especially in tense names like Future/Past Perfect Continuous. Predicts word endings such as 'ous', 'um', 'ity'.
result.label: 'inu' in Continu- words

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'aterial' inside words like biomaterials and nanomaterials, right after a prefix such as biom- or nanom-. Mostly predicts a plural 's' or similar suffix next.
result.label: 'aterial' in biomaterials/nanomaterials

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and commas (",", " the", " of", " around") mid-sentence in explanatory expository text, often about grammar, history or ancient civilizations. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse, so the specific condition is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (growth, be, is, commas, word pieces) inside economic-policy text, such as fiscal policy and tax effects on growth. It is silent on "growth" right after "economic". The peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Economic policy text, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (mid-phrase function words, 'ao' of Tao) in passages about Taoism and philosophy, as the text moves into a philosophical concept. Members mostly push toward philosophy words. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low.
result.label: Taoism/philosophy passage context

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens in educational or technical prose: plural 'ers' endings, hyphens in compounds like "problem-solving", commas and some function words. Silent on many 'ers' tokens (fibers, learners, polymers), so the real condition is unclear.
result.label: Mixed 'ers' and hyphen positions

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fert' at the start of fertile, fertility, fertilizer or fertilization, before the rest of the word is seen. Members are mostly ' fert' detectors, and the target predicts word continuations like 'il'.
result.label: ' fert' word-start piece

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and verbs (was, by, supported, cause, an, over) mid-sentence in expository text, where the next word is likely a noun like levels, testing or studies. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Mixed function words before nouns

result.description: Fires on words after "playing/played" that lead up to "role" (a, an, crucial, increasingly, important, significant), anticipating "role" as the next word. Silent on 'an' in other constructions.
result.label: Modifiers before "play a ... role"

result.description: Fires on the word " selection", mainly in "natural selection" and evolutionary-biology text. It stays silent when "selection" starts a sentence or follows a verb like "simulate", without a preceding modifier such as "natural".
result.label: "selection" after "natural"

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' in', ' the', ' each', ' then') in science-explanation text, especially chemistry like atomic radius, nuclear charge, before a technical noun. Silent on the same ' in' in other contexts, so the pattern is mixed and weak.
result.label: Function words in chemistry explanations

result.description: Fires on the word-piece "desc" (also "asc", "sle") when it begins "descending"/"ascending" and the next piece is likely "end". Mostly in music, scale or air-flow contexts. Predicts word-continuation suffixes.
result.label: desc- of descending

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (of, the, commas, -atic, -ing, includes) in explanatory technical text, mostly where a descriptive noun or adjective is expected next. Silent on many ordinary 'of' phrases. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectives (' and', ',', ' must', ' based', ' that') in abstract expository text about security, compliance, management and leadership. It is silent on many ' and' tokens in similar text, so the circuit is diffuse and unclear.
result.label: Connectives in compliance/management prose

result.description: Fires on " in" right after a grammatical term or quoted preposition/pronoun (e.g. "among" in English, "by" in English grammar), in text about English grammar usage. Predicts "English"/"grammar"-type continuations. Silent on other " in" uses.
result.label: " in" after grammar term, "in English"

result.description: Fires on word-ending suffix pieces like -ual, -ional, -ory, -ership, -ation, completing a longer word split across tokens (e.g. concept|ual, fict|ional). Members mostly detect 'ual' and push toward -ization-type endings.
result.label: Word-final suffix pieces (-ual, -ional)

result.description: Mixed target peaking mostly on ' plut' (before "onium") in nuclear/energy text, but also on scattered tokens like ' that', ' Bern', and mid-word pieces. Upstream members are nuclear/radio-prefix predictors. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: plut- (plutonium) and scattered word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' color', ' and', commas, ' dynamic') in lists of technical or computing terms, such as graph coloring, compression and hashing. It stays silent on 'color' in art or design text. Evidence is mixed and inconsistent.
result.label: Technical-list 'color'/'and' mix

result.description: Fires on connective function words (" as" in "such as", " of", " about", " like", " where") in abstract business/society prose, where a noun like talent, employee, or labor could follow. Silent on some "such as" cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Connectives before abstract workplace nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'emat' inside "kinematics" (also 'roph', 'yt' in other technical words), predicting a suffix like -ics. Fires on a few function words in math/game-theory text. Silent when 'emat' starts the text.
result.label: 'emat' in kinematics word piece

result.description: Fires on a sentence-ending period in text about maritime exploration, trade routes and colonial expansion, where the next sentence would start with a subject like "The Empire" or "Vessels". Stays quiet on periods in other topics.
result.label: Period after exploration/trade history sentence

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Ens' (and ' Can') in "Grand Canonical Ensemble" in statistical mechanics text, with scattered weak firing on other mid-word or function tokens. Members are diffuse and mostly generic, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Grand Canonical Ensemble word pieces

result.description: Fires on the noun or conjunction right after "different/diverse/unique/range of" phrases, where a word like "styles", "levels" or "sizes" is expected next, e.g. "diverse range of abilities [and] preferences", "unique [learning] styles". Appears in accessibility and user-interface text.
result.label: Slot before "styles" after diverse/different

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'fr' when it is an incomplete start of a longer word, mostly in 're-fr-igerator/refrigeration', also in 'fr-iction' and 'in-fr-asonic'. Silent in unrelated text.
result.label: 'fr' piece in refrigerator words

result.description: Fires on function words (the, to, and, their, into) in academic expository text about science and language topics, right before a technical noun phrase. It is silent on 'the' in fixed phrases like 'on the basis' or 'on the other hand'.
result.label: Function words before technical terms

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (at, measurement, position, in, principle) in quantum physics text, such as superposition, measurement and exclusion principle. Members are mostly quantum-topic detectors. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Quantum physics scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside technical terms, mainly ' pron' in "Reflexive pronouns" and 'er' in "polymer"-type words, in chemistry/grammar text. It is silent on 'er' in "polymerization", so it depends on the specific word. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Word pieces in pronouns/polymer terms

result.description: Fires on varied function words (as, an, of, by, appropriate) in definitional or explanatory academic text on math, physics and geography, where a technical noun is expected next. Mixed peaks and weak consistency; the same tokens stay silent in other constructions.
result.label: Function words in technical definitions

result.description: Fires on the subject noun of a sentence about inequality (' inequality', ' society') and the following verb slot (' can', ' is'), predicting a verb. Silent on 'inequality' after economic/social modifiers in object positions.
result.label: Inequality as sentence subject

result.description: Fires on the token " Water" mid-text, mainly as the first piece of "Waterfall" (Waterfall Model), predicting "fall" and similar continuations. Silent when " Water" starts the document.
result.label: ' Water' before 'fall' (Waterfall)

result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "sight-reading" in music-skill text, and more weakly on "read"/"reading" and "quickly" nearby. It stays silent on hyphens in other compounds (fast-, ever-, self-), so it needs the music-skill context.
result.label: Hyphen in sight-reading (music skills)

result.description: Fires on ' to' introducing a purpose infinitive after a noun phrase (e.g. "resources to meet demand", "strategies to match inventory"), mostly in business/operations text. It stays silent on ' to' after "lead to", "crucial to" or "enable firms to".
result.label: purpose 'to' after business noun

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (of, with, for, hyphen, have) in sustainability/environmental text where the next word is likely an environmental term like waste or green. Peaks are mixed and inconsistent; the contrast shows no clear rule.
result.label: Environmental-topic function words, mixed

result.description: Fires on function words or "atomic" in the phrase "at the/an atomic (or microscopic) level/scale", in physics and materials text. Predicts scale words such as level or scale. Silent on "the" in other slots.
result.label: "at the atomic level" scale phrase

result.description: Fires on the word piece "urr" in "blurring" (and "deblurring"), the middle fragment of the word. Weak activation on similar fragments like "gauging". Members are detectors of "urr"/"ur" pieces.
result.label: "urr" piece in blurring

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'om' inside a longer word, most strongly in "onomatopoeia" (on-om-atopoeia), and also in words like cohomology and clinometers. Members detect 'om' mid-word after a prefix piece.
result.label: 'om' piece in onomatopoeia

result.description: Fires on the piece "ib" in "Caribbean" (Car-ib-bean), right after "Car", and predicts the "bean" continuation. Weak activations appear on a few unrelated tokens. The circuit is weak and noisy.
result.label: "ib" in Caribbean

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'cos' in 'ecosystem' (also 'col' in 'ecology'), with weaker activity on 'of' after 'group/gathering' in ecology or diplomatic-gathering contexts. Silent on 'cos' in 'viscosity'-type words.
result.label: 'cos' in ecosystem

result.description: Fires on the token ' ess' when it starts "essence" right after "the", mostly in "capture/convey the essence of". It stays silent on ' ess' in "personal essence" or "essays".
result.label: "the ess-ence" after capture

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, their, commas, relatively) inside text describing linguistics and language structure, where upstream members carry language/grammar topic. Silent on 'the' in other contexts; the peak token is not consistent.
result.label: Function words in linguistics text

result.description: Fires mostly on ' follow' when it is the start of "followers" (a word piece expecting -ers), as in influencers' followers. Weaker, scattered firing on function words. The circuit is low-faithfulness and mixed.
result.label: 'follow' as start of followers

result.description: Fires on linking words (on, of, through, upon, using) after "built/based/foundation/use" that introduce what something is built from or done with, mostly in tech/VR descriptions. Silent on "focus on" or "depending on".
result.label: Basis/means prepositions: built on, use of

result.description: Fires on ' be' when it is a word-start fragment of a longer word (bees, beaks, beverages, beehive, beads, beef), not the standalone verb 'be' (cannot be, will be), where it stays silent.
result.label: ' be' as word-beginning fragment

result.description: Fires on " is" right after a sentence-initial demonstrative "This" (also "this is", "that is"), at the start of a document or sentence. It stays silent on " is" after a noun subject, as in definitions like "elasticity is".
result.label: " is" after "This"

result.description: Fires on ' additional' and ' extra' as a quantity adjective right after verbs like provide/add/adding, where a noun like layer, details or clarity comes next. Silent in unrelated contexts.
result.label: additional/extra after provide/add

result.description: Fires on prepositions (of, for, on, in) and verb pieces right after an abstract noun in war, military and international-conflict history text. It predicts military or war-related next words like war, World, NAT. It stays quiet on 'of' in non-conflict contexts.
result.label: Prepositions in war-history text

result.description: Fires on adjective suffixes or word pieces like -ful, -ive, -fficient in positive quality words (Successful, Effective, Efficient) at the start of a document or title, typically before "communication"-like nouns. Silent on -ful in respectful or meaningful.
result.label: Success/effective adjective suffix at start

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (')', ' of', ' and', ' the', 'S', 't') in technical or academic text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse; it is silent on some ')' tokens, so no clear rule emerges.
result.label: Scattered function tokens in technical text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (' human', ' be', ' to', ' adopt') in abstract ethics/philosophy text, where a normative or conceptual continuation follows. Silent on ' human' in humanism/humanity contexts. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Ethics/philosophy text function words

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after the preposition 'at', especially in 'at the [scale/level]' contexts like nano- or molecular scale. It predicts scale words such as sub, macro, atom, mole. Silent on ' the' after other words.
result.label: ' the' after 'at' (scale level)

result.description: Fires on function words (the, by, to, through, ' mental') in technical or explanatory science/engineering text, just before a technical noun. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; members are mostly diffuse topic features, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Function words in technical explanations

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' v' (a split-off start of a word) mostly before "owel" in vowel-related text. Weaker on ' v' before "accination" or "ibrating". Predicts continuations like "owel", "ibr", "ivid".
result.label: ' v' as start of "vowel"

result.description: Fires on plural noun endings (-es, -ies, -ms, ' companies') for businesses and organizations or groups of people, as the subject of an upcoming verb. Silent on singular "corporate" wording.
result.label: Plural business/organization subject nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered connective tokens (hyphen, comma, 'and', ' imag', 'trans') in the middle of a word or list, where a next word piece is expected. Peaks are inconsistent; the hyphen is silent in many contrast cases like 'non-', 'real-'.
result.label: Mixed connectors mid-phrase, unclear

result.description: Fires on verbs and prepositions (incorporate, integrating, "commitment to", "through") in corporate sustainability/CSR text, where the next word is likely an eco or sustainability term like "green" or "waste". Silent on the same words in sales or other business text.
result.label: Slot before sustainability terms in CSR text

result.description: Fires on the word piece " pack" when it is the start of "packaging"/"packing", mid-sentence after a modifier (food, edible, sustainable). Silent when "packaging" begins the text.

result.description: Fires on ' that' (also ' which') as a relative pronoun right after a noun naming a system, technology or thing, introducing a clause describing what it does. Silent on complementizer 'that' (it was discovered that) and cleft uses.

result.description: Fires on function words (and, in, on, with, their, verb -s) in abstract academic prose on philosophy, ethics and social theory, where the next word is likely a abstract concept. Silent on many ' and' tokens, so the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in a singular possessive or contraction right after a singular noun (artist', writer', chef'), expecting 's next. It stays silent on plural-possessive apostrophes after "characters'".
result.label: Apostrophe after singular noun (possessive)

result.description: Fires on " experiences" (also " experience") as a noun after an adjective like personal, diverse, sensory or immersive, mid-sentence. It stays silent when the word starts the text with no preceding modifier.
result.label: Noun 'experiences' after modifier

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' data', ' to', commas, 'determine') in text about network routing and data packets finding efficient paths. Silent on ' data' in generic data-quality or dataset contexts, so it needs the networking/routing topic.
result.label: Network routing and data packets

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (of, with, the, commas) in history-of-ideas or time-period text, such as "the time of" or "as time went on with". It's quiet on "of" in other phrases like "economies of scale". Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on an adjective like "significant", "crucial" or "important" right after "played a" or "plays a", where the next word is "role". Silent on "significant" before other nouns, such as transformation, milestone or progress.
result.label: Adjective before "role" in "played a"

result.description: Fires on an adjective like "essential", "important" or "crucial" (often 'cial') in the extraposed "it is ADJ to..." construction, right before an infinitive. Stays silent on "crucial" used as an attributive or predicate modifier of a noun.
result.label: "it is essential/crucial to" adjective

result.description: Fires on a comma, "and", "/" or "or" right after "positive" (or similar evaluative adjective) in a list of feedback or sentiment types, where "negative" is expected next. Silent on ordinary clause-separating commas.
result.label: Separator after "positive", expecting "negative"

result.description: Peaks are scattered across mid-word pieces and function words (random variable, ergonomically, joined forces, can be, its) with no shared token or topic. Members are generic context features, so the circuit is poorly explained.

result.description: Fires on function words or verbs like " involves", " the", " by" in abstract expository text about coordinating, integrating or combining things (project management, integration). Silent on sentence-initial " involves" after a subject-less period. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Integration/coordination verbs in expository text

result.description: Fires on a sentence-ending period (or '."') after a sentence in listening/communication-themed text, where a new sentence or paragraph is expected. Silent on periods in other topics like grammar, geography and travel.
result.label: Sentence-final period, communication text

result.description: Fires on the preposition (mostly ' to', also 'with', 'following') right after adhere/adherence/comply/follow, where a rule, standard or guideline is expected next. Silent on other uses of ' to' such as infinitives or 'lead to'.

result.label: Function words in philosophy text

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Cont" at the start of a capitalized word, mostly before "inuous"/"inuity" in headings and titles. It stays silent on the full word "continuity" in running text. Weak activity on a few other tokens.
result.label: Cont- word-start piece (Continuous)

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' (rarely ' an') right after "maintain/maintaining" (also weakly after "ensure", "commitment to"), where an abstract noun like balance or approach comes next. Silent on ' a' after other words.
result.label: ' a' after "maintain"

result.description: Fires on clause-boundary punctuation (';', ',', '),', ' while') after a list or classification of technical terms, especially chemistry/polymer structure types. Silent on some ';' in general science text. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Clause punctuation in technical classification lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' t' when a continuation like "ension", "ense" or "onal" is plausible, mostly in writing or music text about tension, tense or tones. It stays quiet on ' t' in "folk tune" and "future perfect tense".
result.label: ' t' predicting tension/tense

result.description: Fires on ' O' in "Big O" (complexity notation) in computer science text. It stays silent on ' O' directly before a parenthesis, as in "O(n log...)". Members are O-token detectors plus algorithm and complexity context.
result.label: Big O notation ' O'

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces of technical or academic nouns (-ers, -ologies, -eters, -ity, closing parentheses) in lists of fields or technologies, where a relative clause or modifier like "that/which/designed" tends to follow. Inconsistent across contexts.
result.label: Technical noun endings before relative clause

result.description: Fires on function words and suffixes (' of', 'ing', ' in', ' that') right after "maintain(ing)" or similar in food-safety and kitchen hygiene text, where the next word is likely equipment or tools. Silent on many ' of' elsewhere.
result.label: Maintaining hygiene in kitchen text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' person', 'on', commas, ' rate', ' to') in expository academic text, often within lists or linguistics/technical prose. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the logits are not coherent.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' a', ' and', ' but') and verbs like 'facilitate'/'supports' in abstract essay prose about communication, emotion and understanding. Silent on ' the' after plain verbs elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in communication essays

result.description: Fires mostly on " heavily" after verbs like "relies/relied" (reliance adverb before "on"), with weaker hits on commas, quotes and other mid-list tokens. Silent on "heavily" after "GPS" before "utilize", so it needs the "relies heavily on" construction.
result.label: relies heavily on

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' ex' (esp. "cultural ex|changes") and ' syn' that begin a longer word, mostly after "cultural". Silent on some ' ex' in other contexts, so the condition is partly unclear.
result.label: ' ex' fragment in cultural exchanges

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ological' when it completes "technological" (techn+ological), predicting words like advancements, innovation, progress. Silent on 'ological' in bi-ological, Ge-ological or standalone.
result.label: techn-ological word completion

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'lic' in "implicature" and 'lev' in "Relevance", in linguistics/pragmatics text. Silent on 'lic' in "acrylics". Weak, mixed circuit; predicts word continuations like 'ature'.
result.label: 'lic'/'lev' in implicature, relevance

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'ure' of the word "exposure" (expos|ure). It stays silent on 'ure' in other words such as "pressure", so it needs the word piece 'expos' before it.
result.label: 'ure' completing "exposure"

result.description: Fires most on the 'yg' piece in 'hygiene' (also 'polygons'), plus scattered mid-sentence function and verb tokens in formal expository text. Mixed and weakly consistent; the circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: 'yg' in hygiene, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on varied function words and connectors (' to', ' and', ',', ' a', ' lower') in economics/business text about production, costs and efficiency, where a change or effect is being described. Peak tokens are scattered and consistency is low.
result.label: Economics text connectors, scattered

result.description: Fires on ' used' (also 'employed') as a passive verb after "is/are/be" in explanatory text about a concept, method or term, typically before "to", "in" or "for". Silent when the sentence has no passive "used".
result.label: Passive 'is used' in explanations

result.description: Fires on " in" right after a noun of change or development (transformation, shift, changes, advancements) when the subject "underwent/experienced" a significant change. Silent on " in" after other nouns like "advancements in gene expression" or "in particular".
result.label: " in" after "underwent significant change"

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after a quantity or proportion word (percent, %, millions, hundreds, portion), where a total or amount comes next. Silent on ' of' after abstract nouns like extinction, beginning, welfare.
result.label: ' of' after percentages/quantities

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-sentence tokens (suffixes, 'of', 'this', hyphen, ' conditional', ' contain') in abstract explanatory prose about writing, math, or cooking. Peaks are inconsistent. Next-token logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in explanatory prose

result.description: Fires on the verb ' learn' / ' learning' (also 'acquire') in text about language learning and education, as a standalone word. It stays silent when 'learn' is only the first piece of 'learners'.
result.label: learn / learning as standalone word

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment " correl" (as in "correlative conjunctions"), when a word is incomplete and likely continues with a suffix like -ative. Members detect correl-, rel-, figur-, cry- and similar stems.
result.label: " correl" word-start fragment

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on mixed function words and word pieces (' the', ' of', ' by', 'ric', 'ible') mid-phrase, often before a noun in abstract or technical prose. Silent on many ' the' cases; the evidence doesn't show what distinguishes them.
result.label: Mixed function-word mid-phrase positions

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and word pieces (' and', ' of', ' or', 'ates', 'ler') in abstract expository prose about communication, writing, or art. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' and' is often silent in lists, so no clear trigger.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (commas, "where", "which", "(", "include") that open a clause or list elaborating on writing systems, language or scripts. Peak tokens are varied. Upstream members mostly carry language and script topic.
result.label: Clause openers in writing-system text

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ab' inside words and names (Al-Kitab, al-Jabr, syllabaries), plus some function words like 'of', 'and', 'as' after economics or labor nouns. Mixed and weakly faithful, so the function-word part is unclear.
result.label: 'ab' word piece, plus linking words

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (and, a, of, to, in, commas) in expository, abstract essay-style text, mostly where a noun or skill-type word is expected next. Silent on 'and' in lists of nouns. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on manner adverbs (quickly, -ly, dynamically, effectively) directly after verbs like respond, react or adapt, in business-style text about responding to change. Often precedes "and effectively".
result.label: Adverb after respond/react verbs

result.description: Fires on 'ough' in "Dough" at the very start of a document (a heading-like recipe step title such as "Dough Kneading"). It stays silent on 'ough' in "dough" mid-sentence. Weak activity on 'resolved'/'solved'.
result.label: Document-initial "Dough" heading
enhance/increase verbs in narrative analysis
result.description: Fires on the end of verbs like "enhance/enhances/enhancing" (and "increase") when a literary or narrative analysis text says something improves the narrative or character development. It stays silent on noun "-ance" in words like relevance and resonance.

Fires on scattered function words and connectors (' se', ' the', ' and', commas, ' of', ' to') in technical expository text, mid-phrase before a noun object. Evidence is mixed; the logits lean weakly towards verbs like consult/govern/apply.
result.label: Function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires mainly on ' grande' as a word-start piece in "grandeur" (after "the", "and", "of"), where the next piece completes the word. Members detect other incomplete word-start pieces (poly, sec, abs, commit).
result.label: ' grande' in grandeur

result.description: Fires on the word piece " under" when it begins a compound like underpinnings, undercurrent or underlying, most often after abstract adjectives such as "philosophical", "conceptual" or "psychological". It is weaker on sentence-initial "Under" in "Understanding".
result.label: ' under' prefix after abstract adjective

result.description: Fires on words within phrases about writing systems (e.g. "influential syllabaries", "logographic system", "among the many") in text on scripts like Chinese, Japanese, Hangul. Silent on "orthographic" and "cartographic", so it needs the script-type context.
result.label: Writing-system descriptors (logographic, syllabaries)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sed' when it starts a split word like sediment/sedimentary, mostly in geology text. It predicts the word continuation (iment, iments).
result.label: ' sed' start of sediment

result.description: Fires on the verb "ensure" and its inflections (ens-ures, ensuring, ensure) when it introduces a result clause, e.g. "X ensures that…". It stays silent on "ures" in "failures", so it needs the ensure word.
result.label: verb "ensure" inflections

result.description: Fires on a period ending a sentence or a short heading in soil/earth-science text (e.g. "Soil Texture."). It stays silent on periods in other topics, such as headings about animals or geography, and on "e.g." Logits point to soil-related next tokens.
result.label: Period in soil-science text

result.description: Fires on the piece "through" completing the word "breakthrough(s)", mostly in scientific or technology text. Upstream members are detectors of "through" after "break". It pushes toward a plural "s" or following nouns such as "technology" and "science".
result.label: "through" in "breakthrough"

result.description: Fires on ' In' as a word-initial piece at the start of a longer word split into tokens (In-novation, In-complete, In-surance), predicting a continuation like 'sur', 'nov'. Silent on 'In' in Infrastructure.
result.label: ' In' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on causal or initiating verbs and links (initiat-ating/ates, cause, trigger, leading to, resulting in) in chemistry/biochemistry process text, where something leads to a following event. Silent on -ating in non-causal words like investigating.
result.label: Causal/initiating verbs in chemical processes

result.description: Fires on ' most' as the superlative marker after "the", "one of the" or a possessive, before an adjective like "common" or "effective". It stays silent on quantifier "most" ("most types", "most of them").
result.label: Superlative 'most' before adjective

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' with', ' the', ' of', ' to', ' every') and a few word pieces like 'ological' in explanatory academic text. It is silent on ' with' after a comma in descriptive lists. Evidence is mixed, and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ass" inside "all-encompassing" (adjective form, before "-ing"). It stays silent on "ass" in "encompasses" or "affect ass", so it needs that specific word.
result.label: "ass" in "all-encompassing"

result.description: Fires on commas (and "of", "standing") in philosophy-themed abstract prose, especially after sentence-opening phrases like "As such," or "In philosophy,". Silent on commas in other clauses, even in philosophical text. Predicts no clear next token.
result.label: Commas after philosophical sentence openers

result.description: Fires on verbs, prepositions and connectives (of, using, include, where, ;) in text about computer/network security and access control, where a security-related noun such as encryption or authentication is likely to come next. Silent on generic 'of' in other text.
result.label: Function words in security text

result.description: Fires on "the"/"The", mostly at the start of a sentence or clause in culinary-arts and historical-period text. It stays silent on many other "the" tokens, such as "during the early 2…". Members include culinary-topic features.
result.label: "the" in culinary history text
'of' after "array/multitude" in biodiversity
result.description: Fires on ' of' (and sometimes ' the'/' and') after quantity nouns like "array", "multitude", "range" in biodiversity definitions, before listing organisms. Similar ' of' contexts in nearby text stay silent, so the evidence for the condition is thin.

result.label: Materials behavior "under different conditions"
result.description: Fires on words like "different", "various", "to", "under" in materials-science text, mostly right after "under" or "subject to", where a conditions/loading noun is expected next. Silent on "different" in other constructions (e.g. "due to different").

Fires on function words (mostly " of", also "that", "by", "to") in physics text about Bose-Einstein statistics, right before a likely "bosons/identical particles" continuation. Predicts Bos/bos tokens. Silent on " of" in other physics contexts.
result.label: "of" before bosons in Bose-Einstein text

result.description: Fires mainly on " ray" (light rays, ray diagrams) and also " LED", in optics/light-technology text. Silent on other optics text without those tokens. Weak extras on a few other tokens.
result.label: Optics ' ray' and ' LED'

result.description: Fires on the word piece right after "further" when it starts a verb like refine, enrich, complicate or develop (e.g. "further [ref]inement", "further en[rich]ed"). It predicts the word continuation such as "ement".
result.label: Verb stem after "further"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verbs (of, the, impact, more) in expository text about design, art, maps or media, where the next word is a noun like Atlas or photos. It pushes away music words. Peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: Function words in design/art exposition

result.description: Fires on the word "global" (also "Global", "international", "-wide") used as a modifier, often before nouns like environmental, economy or issues. Predicts cooperation-type continuations. Silent on the contrast text, which has no such modifier.
result.label: "global" as modifier

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'om' inside words like bi-om-es, bi-om-ass, nan-om-aterials, clin-om-eters, where it is a mid-word fragment expecting a continuation. Silent when 'om' starts a word or sits in '-omics' words.
result.label: mid-word 'om' fragment (biomes)

result.description: Fires on function words (" to", " a", " in", " about") right after a causal verb like "leading", "precipitating", "bring about", "undergo", in environmental or climate text, where a consequence or change is about to be named. Silent on "to" after "limited", "important" or "complexity".
result.label: Causal verb + to/a before consequence

result.description: Fires on varied function words and mid-phrase tokens (the, and, a, by, of, through) in expository text, where a noun or list continuation is expected. Silent on 'the' after a date or introductory comma. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words mid-phrase in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word after ensure/guarantee/allow for/securing (e.g. "the", "-uring", "-es") in mathematical text about uniform convergence, predicting a property noun or "that". Silent on "the" after ordinary prepositions.
result.label: Object slot after ensure/guarantee (math)
"ino" piece in amino
result.description: Fires on the word piece "ino" in "amino" (amino acid, amino group) in biochemistry text. Weaker on other science word pieces like "Fermi" or "Neutrino". Members are mostly "ino" detectors.

Fires on "essential", "crucial" (cial), "vital", "necessary" when used as a postmodifying adjective right after a noun phrase (e.g. "interactions essential to…"), predicting "for"/"to". Silent after "is/are" or as a pre-noun adjective.
result.label: Postnominal essential/crucial/vital adjective

result.description: Fires on ' is' right after an abstract singular subject noun such as "principle", "concept", "theory" or "assumption", where a predicate is expected. It stays silent on ' is' after "it", "vectors" or "independence" in the vector-space text.
result.label: ' is' after abstract concept noun

result.description: Fires on forms of "contribute" (' contribute', 'contrib-uting', 'contrib-utes'), mostly where a subject adds something to an outcome, e.g. "contributing significantly to". The circuit draws on contribute-word detectors and on words that predict "to" or "significantly".
result.label: Forms of "contribute"

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' te' when it is the start of a longer word split into pieces (te|ch, te|enager, te|aspoon, te|legraph). It predicts continuations like 'ch', 'aring', 'legraph'.
result.label: ' te' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on intensity adjectives like "significant", "substantial", "severe", "immediate" after verbs of causing or leading to (cause, lead to, result in), predicting harm-type nouns such as damage, losses, consequences. Quiet on "has a significant impact".
result.label: Significant/substantial after causation verbs

result.description: Fires in definitions of prime/composite numbers, peaking on "1" in "greater than 1" and on function words like "are", "essentially" in such definitions. Silent on "1" in modular arithmetic or lists. Members are prime/algebra math-context detectors.
result.label: Prime-number definition context, "greater than 1"

result.description: Fires on commas (and 'and') in a list of resources right after "time" (e.g. "including time, budget and..."), predicting further resource nouns like money, cost, capital. Silent on commas after "time" in other constructions.
result.label: Comma after 'time' in resource lists

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a complete clause in technical computing/algorithm text, where a participial or relative continuation ("which", "thereby", "allowing") follows. It stays quiet on commas after "therefore", sentence-initial phrases, or in lists.
result.label: Clause-final comma in technical prose

result.description: Fires on a mid-word fragment (mostly 'inf' in rainfall, 'apt' in presynaptic/synaptic, also 'mit', 'pend') where the word is incomplete and a suffix follows. Seems to depend on being inside those specific words, in science text.
result.label: Mid-word fragments: rainfall, synaptic

result.description: Fires on the word " solutions" (also " solution") as a noun, typically after modifiers like "innovative", "end-to-end" or "storage". Upstream members are mostly detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' solutions' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token " real" when it begins "realm" (e.g. "in the realm of", "digital realm"), also "realization". It is silent on "real-time". Upstream members detect " real" and "realm of" style contexts, such as "the ___ of".
result.label: " real" in "realm"

result.description: Fires on the word " budget" in text about budget types and public finance. Members are mostly detectors of " budget" and budget-related word pieces. It pushes towards continuations like "ary", "allocation" and "constraints".
result.label: ' budget' token detector

result.description: Fires on " role" after an emphasizing adjective in "highlights the crucial/pivotal role that...", where the noun is the importance of something. It is quiet on "play a role" and "its role in" phrasing.
result.label: "crucial role" after highlights

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ical' specifically in the word "ethical" (eth|ical), predicting next words like questions, issues, consider. Silent on 'ical' in other words such as philosophical or ecological.
result.label: 'ical' in "ethical"

result.description: Fires on " to" right after "cater/catering" (also weakly "refers to", "appeal to"), where a noun phrase about audiences or needs follows. Silent on other "to" uses like "due to", "compared to", or infinitive "to".
result.label: "to" after cater/catering

result.description: Fires on the token ' grand' (as in "the grand spectacle", "grandiose", "grandmother", "grand canonical"), with a few stray hits on 'tz' in Boltzmann. Upstream members are mostly ' grand' detectors. The prediction is a continuation like 'io'.
result.label: ' grand' token detector

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ing' completing "Multitasking" (Multitask+ing), especially as a subject at the start of a computing text. It stays silent on 'ing' in other words such as maintaining, speeding and Layering.
result.label: 'ing' in Multitasking

result.description: Fires on ' patient' and on connecting words (' and', ',', ' as') after "improve/improving" in healthcare-technology text, where the next word is likely patient care, outcomes or treatment. Silent on improve in non-medical tech text.
result.label: Improving patient care in healthcare

result.description: Fires on commas and connectives (to, can, by, or) in text about DNA mutation and genetic change, where the next word is likely a mechanism like "random" or "mutation". Silent on commas in other biology or general topics.
result.label: Connectives in mutation/genetics text
Word stem before verb suffix
result.description: Fires on incomplete word pieces in the middle of a verb (eluc-id-ate, unders-coring, re-inv-igorate, util-ize) where a verb ending like -ate/-ize/-ifies is expected next. Silent on 'id' in the adjective 'lucid'.

Fires on ' both', 'a/an' or 'significant' right after a verb like "presents/poses/offers", where the next word is likely "opportunities", "challenges" or "difficulties". Silent on 'both' after prepositions or "promote/development of".
result.label: Presents both/a → opportunities/challenges

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'l' in "pro-l-iferation"/"prolific" (also 'w' in "prowess"), a mid-word piece after "pro" or "over" where a suffix like -iferation or -ess is expected. Weak on other mid-word pieces. Silent on 'l' in "potlucks".
result.label: mid-word 'l' in proliferation

result.description: Fires on abstract ML-capability nouns like "generalization", "models", "representations", "recognition", "rendering" in machine learning / computing text, often ending an item in a list of model qualities. Silent on "parallelization" in evolutionary algorithms.
result.label: ML capability nouns (generalization, models)
' full' before potential/range nouns
result.description: Fires on the word ' full' as a modifier, mostly in "the full potential/range/breadth of", and also in "full backups". It predicts extent nouns like spectrum, range, scope, extent and potential.

Fires on the hyphen right after "well" (and weakly "lesser") when it starts a compound modifier like well-oiled, well-known, well-ordered. It stays silent on hyphens after other words such as acetyl-, two-, bird-. It predicts "known", "defined", etc.
result.label: Hyphen after "well-" compounds

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' en' when it starts a word like "enhanced", "enriches" or "encompass", most strongly after "is" or "can be" in passive constructions. Predicts continuations such as "hanced".
result.label: ' en' prefix before 'hanced'

result.description: Fires on ' these' (also ' each', ' the', ' combined') after "of"/"combining"/"integrate" when referring back to a set of listed methods, models or components being combined. Predicts number words like two/three/factors. Silent on ' these' referring to plain physical objects.
result.label: 'these' before combined methods/components

result.description: Fires on function words (" of", " the", " their") inside redox/chemical-reaction text, especially after "gain/loss of" or before an expected chemistry noun like electrons or products. Silent on "of" in other chemistry contexts, so it is selective.
result.label: Function words in redox chemistry text

result.description: Fires on " those" right after "For" (e.g. "For those who are..."), a sentence-opening pronoun introducing a relative clause about a group of people. Members are detectors of " those" after "for" or "between".
result.label: "For those" who...

result.description: Fires on commas (sometimes 'and') inside lists of sound, perception or music-related properties (pitch, sounds, touch, hearing, visual), where another list item comes next. Silent on commas after clauses or before 'which'/'such as'.
result.label: List commas in sound/perception lists

result.description: Fires on connectives (commas, "and", "the", "or") inside lists or clauses in international finance and currency/exchange-rate text, where the next word is likely an economic noun such as "flows" or "predictions". Silent on commas in general text.
result.label: Connectives in currency/finance lists

result.description: Fires on infinitive ' to' (also 'can'/'could') after a technology or tool noun, introducing a purpose clause about what the tech is used for. It predicts verbs like create, simulate, monitor. It stays quiet on 'expected to' and 'back to'.
result.label: purpose 'to' after technology nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ass' inside words like reassurance, assume, potassium, but also on some other word pieces and function words after "development of". Silent on 'ass' in "encompasses". Mixed evidence.
result.label: 'ass' word piece (reassurance, assume)

result.description: Fires mostly on ' a' (also ' of', ' to') after a verb like "create", "employs" or "utilizes" in tokamak/fusion text, where the next word is likely "Tok"/"tor"-type (toroidal, tokamak). Silent on ' a' in unrelated contexts.
result.label: 'a' before tokamak/toroidal term

result.description: Fires on the token ' Tai' (also rarely ' Gram'), mostly when it is followed by a hyphen or dash and another name-like piece, as in odd "Tai-Kada" strings. The evidence is thin and noisy; weak activations appear on word fragments.
result.label: ' Tai' before hyphenated name

result.description: Fires on the word-ending pieces 'ion' in "internal combustion" and 'el' in "Diesel" within engine and thermodynamic cycle text. It stays silent on 'ion' in other subjects such as lithium-ion or corrosion. It pushes toward "engines" and "cycle".
result.label: combustion / Diesel engine word endings

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " As" when it begins a word like "Asset" (Current Asset, Asset Pricing), split from the rest of the word. It fires weakly on sentence-initial "As". It predicts word continuations such as "pect", "ym", "ynchronous".
result.label: " As" as start of "Asset"

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces like ' dup', ' imp', ' multip', ' rep' that are followed by "lication"/"licity" (duplication, implication, multiplicity, replication). Predicts the continuation 'lications'/'lication'. Members are detectors of these prefixes.
result.label: Prefix before -lication (dup/imp/multip)

result.description: Fires on the word " operating" (and "ating" in "Operating System"), strongest in "operating system(s)" contexts, and weaker in "operating temperatures/parameters". It pushes the next token towards "systems/system".
result.label: "operating" before systems

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ert' inside "inertial"/"inertia" (in|ert|ial), mostly in physics text. Weaker on a few other mid-word pieces like ' ende' and ' puzz'. Predicts suffix pieces like 'ia' and 'ial'.
result.label: 'ert' in inertia/inertial

result.description: Fires on " new" right after "open(ed/ing) up" (also "provided/creating new"), predicting door/opportunity-type nouns. It stays silent on " new" after "discover", "lead to" or "a new era".
result.label: "new" after "opening up"

result.description: Fires on the word " chemical" when it is used as a modifier after a preposition or verb, before a noun like industry, engineering, processes or operations. It stays silent when " chemical" starts the text or sits in "chemical and electrical".
result.label: ' chemical' as modifier

result.description: Fires on function tokens (comma, quote, "that", "in") right after a named seminal work or publication, where the next word is likely "published", "titled", or "book". Silent on commas after other nouns.
result.label: Punctuation after a notable publication

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' sed' and ' sent' that begin a longer word like sediment or sentiment/sentient/sentinel, predicting 'iments'/'iment'/'ience' next. Silent when the whole word is already given.
result.label: sed-/sent- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the token "IP" (intellectual property, or IPv4/IPv6 addresses), including with or without a leading space. Many members are IP detectors; others relate to rights and copyright. Predicts suffixes like "R", "right", "v".
result.label: IP token (intellectual property / IPv)

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces 'ient' (as in experiential) and 'ific' (Artificial) where the word is unfinished and the next piece is likely 'ial'. It mostly sits inside multi-piece words.
result.label: Word piece before 'ial' ending

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' pro' when it is a prefix starting a longer word, especially in science text where "proton" comes next. It stays silent on one ' pro' before "tons" in a counting context, so it needs more than the token.
result.label: ' pro' prefix, proton-like continuation

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments ' imag' (imaging, imagery, imaginary) and ' infl' (inflation) when a longer word is split, predicting suffix pieces like 'ery' or 'ation'. Mostly ' imag' detectors feed it.
result.label: imag-/infl- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the word "economic" (mostly the final piece 'ic' after "Econom", also " economic"), as an adjective before nouns like crises, growth, theory. Silent on 'ic' ending other words (strategic, systemic, esoteric).
result.label: Economic (Econom-ic) adjective

result.description: Fires mostly on " of" right after "survival" (survival of the species), and sometimes on "back" in "traced back". Silent on " of" after other nouns like "secrets", "combination", "myriad". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: "survival of" and "back" connectors

result.description: Fires on the word " rank" as a noun in mathematical or statistical text (matrix rank, rank as a measure). Members are mostly detectors of " rank" and similar technical nouns like variance and space.
result.label: ' rank' in math contexts

result.description: Fires on the space token that comes right before a year's digits, after "in" following an event or entity (e.g. "Friendster in [2004]"). It stays silent on spaces before years after periods or "from".
result.label: Space before year after "in"

result.description: Fires on sameness adjectives (" same", " identical", " similar") after verbs like share/have, right before a noun naming a property (forms, formula, level). Predicts property nouns such as characteristics, type, qualities.
result.label: same/identical before property noun

result.description: Fires on the token piece 'ocr' in Socrates/Socratic and also in words like democratic or endocrine. The next-token push is toward suffixes such as 'ates' and 'atic'. It stays silent on other Plato/Athens text that lacks the 'ocr' piece.
result.label: 'ocr' piece (Socrates, democratic)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' behav' (start of "behaviors"), mostly after adjectives or nouns like animal, social, adaptive. It predicts the suffix 'iors'/'iour'.
result.label: ' behav' piece before -iors
