result.description: Fires on ' beta' (also 'eta' in Beta, 'amma' in gamma) in radioactive decay text, e.g. "beta decay" and "beta-minus". It predicts decay-related continuations such as ' decay', '+' and ' minus'.
result.label: beta in radioactive decay

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Inter" (capitalized, with a space) when it begins a longer word such as Interactive, Interfaces, Interpreted or Inter-process. It pushes the next token toward continuations like active, mediate, action, pret and faces.
result.label: Inter- word-start prefix
'iqu' in etiquette
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'iqu' in "et-iqu-ette", after 'et', and pushes the next token towards 'ette'. Members are mostly word-piece detectors that also predict 'ette' as a continuation.

Fires on the word piece ' mit' (mitochondria, mitigation, mitral, mitosis) and on ' Luther' after 'Martin'. Both are word-start fragments that precede a continuation; the target is silent on unrelated biology text.
result.label: ' mit' fragments and Martin Luther

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sust' at the start of "sustainable/sustainability/sustain", predicting the continuation 'ain'. Members are mostly ' sust' detectors plus environmental/waste context features. Silent on a few ' sust' cases, with no clear reason.
result.label: ' sust' word-start predicting 'ain'

result.description: Fires on connectors (' and', commas, 'to') right after "efficiency" in business, engineering or sustainability text, in a list of goals. It predicts next words like reduced, waste, minimize, low and suppresses repeating efficiency.
result.label: Connector after "efficiency" in goal lists

result.description: Fires on the piece "out" in "Throughout" (also weakly on " throughout"), typically at the start of a sentence like "Throughout history". It predicts " history" and similar time-span words next.
result.label: "out" in "Throughout"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (of, in, their, -ive) in biology/taxonomy text about diversity, uniqueness and classification of organisms. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the same ' of' stays silent in other contexts.
result.label: Diversity/classification text, scattered function words

result.description: Fires on abstract plural or mass nouns ending a noun phrase (connections, constructs, spaces, processes, structures, patterns) in abstract social/academic prose, where a locative preposition like "within" or "among" may follow. Silent on some 'construct's in philosophical contexts.
result.label: Abstract plural noun before locative preposition

result.description: Fires on the noun " transformation", mostly in "underwent/experienced a (significant) transformation" sentences about a field or industry changing. Weaker on "Digital transformation" and similar change nouns like "changes" or "phase".
result.label: ' transformation' as change noun

result.description: Fires on commas, "), " and "or" separating items in a list of climate zone types (tropical, dry, temperate, ...), after a zone name. Silent on commas in other climate sentences that aren't listing zone categories.
result.label: Commas in climate zone lists

result.description: Fires on the word ' attention' in the sense of drawing, capturing, paying or demanding notice (e.g. "draws attention", "command attention"). Silent on the technical "attention" of computational text. It pushes towards "span", "paid" and "away".
result.label: ' attention' as notice/focus

result.description: Fires on cooking words (cook-ing, chef, recipe 'pe') in analogies where something abstract, like giving feedback or a model, is compared to cooking. Silent on 'ing' in non-cooking words.
result.label: Cooking word in analogy

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' fost' (start of foster/fosters/fostering), predicting suffixes like -ering, -ered, -er. Fires in every window, including repeated "fost" after "also", "to", "not only".
result.label: ' fost' piece of foster

result.description: Fires on ' only' (sometimes ' just') right after "is/are not" in a copular "X is not only ..." construction, where a "but also" continuation is expected. Stays quiet on "not only" after a verb or in mid-sentence use with a verbal subject.
result.label: "is not only" after copula

result.description: Fires on prepositions (from, of, by) and "-able" endings in risk-management text, where the next word is likely an unexpected or disruptive event (events, unexpected, sudden). Silent on ' by' in ordinary agent or means constructions.
result.label: Prepositions before unexpected disruptions

result.description: Fires on commas (also 'or'/'and') inside lists of media or document types (videos, articles, reports, emails), where another item of the same kind is expected next. Silent on commas after abstract design or policy items.
result.label: Commas in media/document type lists

result.description: Fires on a scattered mix of tokens (' Web', 'NO', odd byte pieces, ' spin', ' hierarchy', ' overflow'), mostly technical or math words. Members are generic fragment detectors with no discriminative signal, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered technical word fragments

result.description: Fires on ' range' (also array/spectrum) in "a diverse/wide range of ...", where the noun is followed by "of". Also fires on 'roid' in "embroidery", a minor side peak.
result.label: "diverse range of" quantity noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'asc' inside 'cardiovascular' (also 'vascular'), predicting the 'ular' continuation. Weakly fires on other mid-word fragments such as 'erc' in coercion.
result.label: 'asc' in cardiovascular

result.description: Fires on the token ' decision', mostly in "informed decision-making" and similar compounds, and pushes the next token towards "-" and "making". Members are mostly ' decision' detectors. Weak activation on "problem-solving".
result.label: ' decision' before -making

result.description: Fires on "have"/"having" (also "possess") as a main verb of possession or requirement, especially after "to", "should", "must", or "and" in advice-like text, predicting a noun phrase like "sufficient" or "a robust". Silent on "may have" and "some have".
result.label: have/having as possession verb

result.description: Fires on the ' Bern' piece of the name Bernoulli (occasionally 'oul'), in physics/maths text, where the next piece is expected to complete the surname. Members detect Bern and similar name-start fragments.
result.label: Bern- in Bernoulli

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' something', 'friend' in user-friendly, list commas, ' series'/' collection' after 'a') where a noun or compound continuation is expected. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered something/friend/list-comma slots

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' coh' (cohomology, cohesive, coherent) when it is split off as a separate token, predicting continuations like 'er', 'es', 'ort'. Also weakly on 'cis' in 'exercises'.
result.label: ' coh' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires mainly on ' transparent' (also 'clarify', 'ial' in confidential) in lists of organizational virtues like "transparent, inclusive, reliable" in governance and communication text. Weakly on related openness words.
result.label: Transparent in organizational virtue lists

result.description: Fires on ' in' or ' to' right after result/lead verbs (results in, resulted in, leading to, leads to), where an outcome comes next. Predicts outcome words like improved, increased, substantial. Silent on ordinary ' in' prepositions.
result.label: "results in / leads to" outcome preposition

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ens' inside the word "licensing" (lic|ens|ing), after the "lic" fragment. Members are mostly 'ens' detectors, including in other words like "comprehensiveness" and "censored".
result.label: 'ens' in "licensing"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'etic' in "Genetic", strongest when "Genetic" opens a document or a topic-heading line (e.g. "Genetic mutations", "Genetic recombination"). Weaker and sometimes silent when mid-sentence after lowercase "gen".
result.label: Genetic at start of heading

result.description: Fires on the word piece " techn" (start of "technological/technologies") and occasionally "olog" in "technologists", predicting the suffix "ological/ologies". It is quiet in "sensor technologies", so it may need an adjective or determiner before it.
result.label: ' techn' word-start before -ological

result.description: Fires on the final piece "is" of "emphasis" (as in "places greater emphasis on"), predicting "on/placed/upon" next. It stays silent on "is" inside other words like "Rubisco".
result.label: "emphasis" word-ending 'is'

result.description: Fires on the token " design" (or "Design") as a noun after a modifier in visual/graphic/web/UI design contexts, predicting suffixes like "ers" or nouns like "elements". Mostly silent in "computer-aided design" or "iterative designing".
result.label: ' design' in graphic/web design

result.description: Fires on clause-boundary tokens (semicolon, ' and', comma, period) after a negated or contrasting clause, where the next clause is expected to contrast or continue ("instead", "rather", "nor", "it"). Silent on some semicolons in other contexts.
result.label: Clause boundary after negated statement

result.description: Fires on the pivot word (" but", "'s", "also") in "not just/merely X but (also) Y" contrasts, where a noun or article like "a/an" is expected next. It is silent after "not only ... but also" in some contexts.
result.label: "not just X but Y" pivot

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ios' (or 'os') inside "angiosperms"/"gymnosperms" in botany text, where the next piece is likely 'perm'. It stays silent on 'ios' in other words like "biosphere".
result.label: 'ios' in angiosperms

result.description: Fires on the piece 'iment' inside "sediment" (sedimentary, sediment transport, sedimentologists), after the 'sed' piece. It stays silent when 'iment' appears without the preceding 'sed'.
result.label: 'iment' in sediment

result.description: Fires on the piece 'stal' in "crystal" (Cry|stal), mostly in solid-state and crystallography text. It predicts continuations such as "lography" or "lattice"-style word endings.
result.label: 'stal' in crystal

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'ut' in "poll|ut|ants" and "scr|ut|iny", plus a few similar mid-word pieces (conj, eg, circul). It stays silent on 'ut' in "pharmaceutical", so it needs the specific word context.
result.label: 'ut' inside pollutants/scrutiny
' as' as conjunction after a noun
result.description: Fires on ' as' right after a complete noun phrase or clause in technical or expository text, often introducing a clause ("as their size increases") or a role ("Truth as consensus"). Silent on "such as", "known as", "serve as".
Fires on the second ' as' of an equative comparison ("as important to X as it is to Y"), after "as ADJ" and a complement. Silent on ' as' meaning "serve as", "because", or other non-comparative uses.
result.label: Second 'as' in as-ADJ-as comparisons

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' co' when it begins a longer word (cocktail, cooperative, cooperation, copper, coating) and pushes toward continuations like 'oper', 'ck', 'aching'. It stays silent on whole words such as 'collaboration'.
result.label: ' co' word-initial fragment

result.description: Fires on connecting function words or verbs (with, including, through, by, as, of) that follow a clause about research or analysis in academic linguistics text, where a noun like studies, methods or analyses is expected next. Silent on ordinary "development of" style 'of'.
result.label: Linking words before research-method nouns

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (commas, '),', hyphen, 'of', 'the') in academic or technical expository text about science, math, or music, where a noun or technical term is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Punctuation/function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on the final noun of a casual or humorous noun phrase (coffee break, cover song, kitchen experiment, joke, comedic relief), where a light-hearted event or moment noun completes the phrase. Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are scattered.
result.label: Light-hearted event noun ending phrase

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-sentence tokens (function words, word pieces, 'as', 'the', 'a') in abstract explanatory text, often about geology or earth processes. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is thin.
result.label: Scattered tokens in explanatory science prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ground' when it begins a compound such as groundbreaking, groundwork, ground-based or grounded. It pushes toward continuations like 'bre', 'work' and 'water'. It stays silent when ' ground' is the first token of the document.
result.label: ' ground' as compound prefix

result.description: Fires on ' one' in the "from one X to another" construction, right after "from". It stays silent on other uses of ' one', such as the pronoun in "if one were" or "on one side". It predicts a noun like state or phase.
result.label: "from one ... to another" one

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's (or apostrophe) after a famous scholar's surname, like "Fourier's" or "Kierkegaard's", predicting words like pioneer or contributions. Silent on 's after common nouns, contractions ("it's") and lesser names.
result.label: Possessive 's after famous thinker

result.description: Fires on the word " objective", mostly as an adjective meaning impartial or fact-based (objective analysis, criteria, reality). It also fires more weakly on the noun meaning "goal". It pushes toward words like reality, evaluation and criteria.
result.label: ' objective' adjective (impartial/criteria)

result.description: Fires on "or" / "even" / "and" in escalating quantity phrases like "dozens or even thousands", predicting a larger number word (millions, thousands). Silent on "even" before comparatives ("even more").
result.label: Escalating quantity "or even" connector

result.description: Fires on the word piece " over" when it begins a compound such as "overview" (also overlaps, overlays), predicting "view" or "laps". It stays silent on "over" as a standalone preposition, as in "mastery over" or "control over".
result.label: "over" prefix in overview

result.description: Fires on the word " conservation", mostly in physics contexts like "energy conservation" or "conservation laws"; it also fires more weakly for environmental conservation. It is silent on related text that lacks the word. Members are mostly detectors of the same token.
result.label: conservation (energy/laws) token

result.description: Fires on ' only' at the start of a new sentence, in the inverted "Only does/was/is..." construction. It stays silent on "not only" and on a bare leading "only".
result.label: Sentence-initial 'only' inversion

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs in descriptions of buildings or artifacts "not just/only X but also Y", or "designed to reflect/symbolize/embody", where the next word is likely a purpose, function or quality (functionality, utility, spiritual, art).
result.label: Structures reflecting function and symbolism

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' per' when it begins a longer word such as perplexing, peril, perception, permeability or perpendicular. It pushes the next token toward continuations like plex, vas, cept and tain.
result.label: ' per' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'comple' in "Incompleteness" (Gödel's Incompleteness Theorem), a mid-word fragment. It stays silent on 'complex' or 'computational' words. Members are math and logic context plus word-piece detectors.
result.label: 'comple' in Incompleteness

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'atur' inside words like s-atur-ation / s-atur-ated (also m-atur-ity), predicting suffixes such as -ation, -ated, -ity. Silent when 'atur' starts the text with no preceding piece.
result.label: 'atur' piece in saturation

result.description: Fires on a period ending a sentence about applications or impact of a technique across fields, where the next sentence likely starts with a subject like a field or domain (sports, medicine). Silent on periods before paragraph breaks or in abbreviations.
result.label: Period after applications-across-fields sentence

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, by, a, "(") in text about Gibbs free energy and thermodynamics, where the next word is likely a term like "free energy" or "Gibbs". Silent on the same words in other thermochemistry text.
result.label: Function words in Gibbs free energy text

result.description: Fires on the "ile" piece in "Agile"/"agile" (software methodology), pushing toward words like method, response, iteration. Weaker on "ile" in other words and on "crowdsourcing". Members are mostly "ile" detectors plus agile-topic context.
result.label: Agile 'ile' token

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yl' inside longer words, mostly chemical terms (methyl, acetyl, diethyl, polyethylene), and weakly in Chernobyl and syllogisms. Members are mostly 'yl' detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: 'yl' word piece in chemical terms

result.description: Fires on the word " research" (or "Research") as a noun, especially where "researchers" is a likely continuation, as in "…, research|ers can…". Mostly sentence or clause starts in academic text. It pushes the next token toward "-ers".
result.label: ' research' predicting 'ers'

result.description: Fires on "provide" verbs (provides, providing, offering) after a subject, typically "it/which provides" in explanatory text about a concept or field. It predicts benefit nouns such as guidance, structure, framework or insight. It is silent when the verb starts a text with no subject.
result.label: Provides-verb predicting benefit nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece " alleg" at the start of "allegory/allegories/allegorical", mostly in literary-analysis text. Members are mostly detectors of the same " alleg" piece, plus narrative-related context.
result.label: ' alleg' (allegory) word piece

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a capitalized proper name or name stem (Han, Mong, Pear, Leonard, Num) that is likely to continue into a longer name or word, e.g. Han Dynasty, Mongolian, Pearson. Mostly Chinese/Mongol history contexts.
result.label: Name-start piece like Han, Mong

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (of, the, in, and, most, flat) in abstract academic expository text, where the next word is an open content slot. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Mid-phrase function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the article ' a'/' an' after "is"/"becomes" when a definitional noun phrase follows, in essays about language and rhetoric (understatement, oxymoron). It predicts nouns like device, technique or literary.
result.label: Article 'a' defining rhetorical device

result.description: Fires on the word " products" (also "product"/"goods" upstream) as the object of verbs like create, provide, deliver, in business or product-development text, often before "or services". Members are mostly product/goods token detectors.
result.label: ' products' as business object noun

result.description: Fires on the digit (mostly 0, also 9, 8) or hyphen inside a year right after "mid-" (mid-1850s, mid-2020, mid-to-early). Silent on the same digits in years without "mid-". Predicts "century" or "decade".
result.label: Year digits after "mid-"

result.description: Fires on the word " context" after a modifying adjective (sociocultural, historical, linguistic, formal), often where a plural or "-ual" suffix could follow. Silent in "a given context".
result.label: ' context' after adjective modifier

result.description: Fires on the token "off" (also "offs"), mostly as the second piece of a compound like trade-off, run-off, or dance-off. Members are mostly detectors of "off" at earlier layers.
result.label: "off" in compounds (trade-off)

result.description: Fires on function words (of, as, where, from, in) in texts about ancient Greece and classical antiquity, where the next word is likely a Greek city or figure (Arist-, Spart-, Ath-). Silent on 'of' in modern or generic contexts.
result.label: Function words before ancient Greek names

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'sc' in the middle of a word, mostly 'land|sc|apes', and also in 'spectro|sc|opy' and 'micro|sc|opy'. It pushes the next token towards 'apes', 'opy' and similar endings.
result.label: 'sc' mid-word (landscapes, microscopy)

result.description: Fires on the word piece "van" as a fragment, mainly in "galvanic" and "galvanically", and also when it starts a split word like "vancements" or "vanica". Predicts word-completing suffixes.
result.label: "van" piece in galvanic

result.description: Fires on the pronoun " it"/" It" as the subject of a new clause or sentence, usually in historical or descriptive text, right before a verb like was, became, had. Silent in the contrast, where there is no subject "it".
result.label: Subject "it" before a verb

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' El' as the start of a longer word or name, most strongly in 'Elamite' / 'Elam' in ancient-history text. Members also detect ' El' in other words (Elastic, El Niño).
result.label: ' El' word-start (Elam)

result.description: Fires on the word piece " contrib" when it is the start of a participle like "contributing", usually after an adverb such as "ultimately" or "significantly". It predicts "uting", "uted" or "utions" next.
result.label: ' contrib' before -uting
'yn' piece before 'thesis' words
result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'yn' inside technical words like nucleosynthesis, photosynthesis, polynomial and Keynesian, predicting 'thesis'-like continuations. Weaker, scattered firing on other tokens (' two', ' on', ' more').

Fires mainly on " together" (also combine/combined) after verbs of joining, merging, or collaborating, where the things are being brought into one whole. Predicts create/forming-type continuations. Silent on text about word arrangement without joining.
result.label: Joining things together

result.description: Fires on the hyphen after "out" in "out-of-order" (also "out-" and "off-" compounds), plus scattered word-internal pieces like "ash" in Krashen and "for". Silent on hyphens after long, energy, water or Bio. Mixed evidence.
result.label: hyphen after "out" (out-of-order)

result.description: Fires on the "id" piece inside "Solidarity" (Sol|id|arity), after the "Sol" token. It is silent on "id" in "rigid" or at text start. Members detect solid/Sol/sol word pieces. Logits favour suffixes like "itude" and "arin".
result.label: "id" in Sol-id-arity

result.description: Fires on the word " food" / " Food" as a standalone noun or heading, e.g. "Food and Religion" or "makes food delicious". Quiet in "types of food items", where it modifies a following noun.
result.label: Word "food" as noun or heading

result.description: Fires on a colon that ends a list-item heading or introduces a list or tips, in bulleted or advice-style text. It predicts an imperative or item-starting word next. It is quiet on colons in other positions, such as after a run-on clause.
result.label: Colon after list-item heading

result.description: Fires on the noun " balance" (also " equilibrium") after "the"/"delicate" in ecological, scientific or economic text, as in "the balance of...". Silent on some uses like "ecological balance;" or "this balance demands", so it needs a particular slot.
result.label: "the balance of" noun

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ged'/'ges'/'ge' completing the verb "emerge" (emerged, emerges), usually after a subject like a technology or idea. Predicts " as" or "from" next.
result.label: emerge verb ending (emer-ged)

result.description: Fires on the "dependent" piece in "interdependent" (mutually dependent things, e.g. mind and brain, social forces), and weakly on linked/connected. It predicts words like web, threads, phenomena.
result.label: interdependent 'dependent' token

result.description: Fires on prepositions and connectors (mostly "on", also "in", "of", "and") after teaching/training/instruction words in education descriptions, where a field of study or subject is about to be named. Silent on "on" in other uses like "focused on interpretation".
result.label: Preposition before subject taught

result.description: Fires on "government" (also federal, public sector) used as a modifier before a noun like policy, agencies, layers, predicting suffixes such as -al, officials, agencies, offices. Silent on bare policy-list headings.
result.label: government as modifier word

result.description: Fires on the word piece " mo" when it begins "moisture" (after soil, atmospheric, release, adequate), predicting a continuation like "isture". Members are mostly " mo" detectors.
result.label: " mo" start of "moisture"

result.description: Fires on the token " transformations" (rarely " transformation" or "transform"), mostly in linear algebra text such as "linear transformations". It is quiet in nearby linear-algebra text that lacks the word.
result.label: ' transformations' in linear algebra

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' br' in text about brushes, where it begins 'brush', 'bristle' and similar words. It is silent when ' br' starts the document, with no brush context before it.
result.label: ' br' piece in brush text

result.description: Fires on the word piece " trad" when it begins "traditions", strongest after "culinary". Weaker after "oral" or "some". Silent when the word is at the start of a document or after "sowing/grooving".
result.label: ' trad' in culinary traditions

result.description: Fires on ' applications' (also programs, software) meaning computer software, in tech or cloud contexts. Silent when 'applications' means uses or uses-in-a-field, as in "broad applications in various areas". Predicts software nouns like packages or modules.
result.label: Software 'applications' noun

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after Gutenberg's name in text about the printing press, pushing toward print/printing words. It stays silent on 's after other names or nouns like Chandrasekhar or era.
result.label: Gutenberg possessive 's (printing)

result.description: Fires on " communication" right after an evaluative adjective like "effective" (or successful, authentic), as in "effective communication". It stays silent after "nonverbal", "of", "in" or "by".
result.label: "communication" after "effective"

result.description: Fires on the word piece "mult" (and "im" in "multidimensional") at the start of multi- compounds like multidimensional, multifaceted, multicultural, predicting continuation pieces such as "if", "id", "itude".
result.label: multi- prefix (multidimensional)

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments of longer technical words, mostly ' prec' (before 'ursor'), also 'VP', 'ium', ' diagn'. Logits promote continuations like 'ursor'/'urs'. Appears in science and chemistry text, mid-word.
result.label: ' prec' word-piece before 'ursor'

result.description: Fires on function words (the, to, an) in explanations of periodic trends, especially atomic radius decreasing or increasing across a period or group, where the next word is likely a change word like decrease or increase. Silent on 'the' in other chemistry text.
result.label: Periodic trend: atomic radius change

result.description: Fires on the token 'o' as a short piece, often right after an opening parenthesis (where "often" follows) or inside words like aerofoil, smoothing, QoS, IoT. Pushes the next token towards 'ften' and similar completions.
result.label: Letter 'o' piece, predicts 'ften'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Mag' at the start of a word like Magnetic or Magnets, mostly in physics headings. It predicts continuations such as 'net' and 'ellan'. It is quiet on 'Electromagnetic', where the piece is not word-initial.
result.label: ' Mag' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on domain adjectives (social, political, scientific, cultural) in lists of broad societal factors or drivers of historical change, e.g. "the social and economic changes". Predicts nouns like changes and factors.
result.label: Societal-domain adjectives before changes

result.description: Fires on ' understanding' (also 'comprehension') as a noun after an adjective like "thorough" or "comprehensive", typically in "requires a thorough understanding of". Silent when it follows a preposition such as "in understanding" or "for understanding".
result.label: Noun 'understanding' after adjective

result.description: Fires on the suffix "ative" in "indicative", as in "is indicative of". It stays silent on "ative" in other words such as "communicative". Weaker activation on "indications" and "due" (to).
result.label: "indicative" suffix before "of"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cru' at the start of "crucial", "crucible" and "crude", predicting a continuation like 'cial' or 'cible'. Members are mostly ' cru' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' cru' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " att" as the start of a longer word (attitudes, attraction, attribution), predicting continuations like "raction", "itudes", "ribution". Silent on unrelated tokens.
result.label: ' att' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on degree intensifiers before an adjective, mostly the "ibly" of "incredibly" and " quite", also "particularly". Predicts positive adjectives like effective, useful, powerful. Silent where no such adverb precedes an adjective.
result.label: Intensifier before adjective (incredibly, quite)

result.description: Fires mainly on the word " skill" as a bare noun, typically after "requires" (e.g. "requires skill and precision"). Silent on "skill" in "this skill", "writer's skill", or "skillful". Weak firing on a few other tokens.
result.label: "skill" after requires

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces 'ra' in "engraving" and 'eb' in "lifeblood" (also eyebrow), where a word is partly spelled and a continuation is expected. Weak firing on a few other tokens.
result.label: 'ra' in engraving, 'eb' in lifeblood

result.description: Fires on ' can' directly after a noun-phrase subject (often abstract or plural, e.g. "misuse of colons can"), where a verb like be/cause/help follows. It stays quiet on pronoun or relative-clause subjects such as "they can" or "readers can".
result.label: ' can' after noun-phrase subject

result.description: Fires on " needs" as the noun after a stakeholder word like consumer, customer, user or market (e.g. "meet consumer needs"). Also fires weakly on "demands" and "expectations" in business and marketing text.
result.label: Customer/consumer "needs" noun

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' its', ' with', 'ifications', commas) in technical or descriptive prose, where a descriptive noun or modifier phrase is expected next. The peaks are inconsistent, and ' its' is silent in some contexts.
result.label: Scattered function words before descriptive noun

result.description: Fires on word-fragment tokens mid-word, mostly 'ph' after 'al'/'ale'/'as' (alphabet, aleph, asphalt), also 'ak' in Nanak and ' pre' before 'historic'. It is silent on 'ph' at word start or in 'deciphering'.
result.label: Mid-word 'ph' fragment in al- words

result.description: Fires on ' approach' as the first word of a sentence, as a bare subject noun (". Approach serves/involves…"). It stays silent when 'approach' follows 'this', 'an' or 'follow this', or sits at the very start of the text.
result.label: Sentence-initial ' approach' as subject

result.description: Fires on scattered mid-phrase tokens (' and', ' personal', ' shared', ' like', ' on') inside text about human communication and relationships. Peaks are inconsistent; members mostly carry communication/listening topic context.
result.label: Communication-topic scattered function words
' cul' before 'inary'
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cul' when it begins "culinary", after a preceding word such as "the", "their" or "classic". It is silent when "cul" starts the text or follows "are". Members are mostly ' cul' detectors that predict "inary".
Fires on the noun completing "feedback loop(s)" / "feedback mechanisms" (loops, loop, isms, cycle), after the word "feedback". Silent on control-systems text without that feedback phrase.
result.label: feedback loop/mechanism noun
Word-initial "ad" fragment token
result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " ad" / " Ad" that begins a longer word such as adjectives, adverbs, adhesives or adverse. It predicts continuations like ject, verb, hesive, verse. Strongest in grammar text about adjectives and adverbs.
Fires on the final 't' token completing the word "debt" (deb|t) in finance and economics text, e.g. debt reduction, debt relief. It stays silent on 't' in other words such as fine-tuning.
result.label: 't' completing "debt"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, prepositions, word pieces like 'etic', 'ac', 'ways') in chemistry/biology text, especially around "synthetic" and molecules. It is inconsistent: 'etic' itself is silent after "synth" in the contrast. Evidence is mixed; the circuit failed.
result.label: Chemistry/biology text, scattered tokens

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Tr" / "tr" (e.g. start of "Truth", "Altruism"), a token that is followed by a continuation like "uth", "ust", "ouble". Mostly at the beginning of a word or title.
result.label: Tr word-piece detector

result.description: Fires on a mid-word fragment (h in Al-Khwarizmi, bo in carbohydrate, Ne in von Neumann) in a rare multi-piece word, where the next piece is a predictable continuation. Silent on misspelled or garbled variants like "bohydrates".
result.label: Mid-word piece in split rare words

result.description: Fires on function words and commas right after a historical period phrase (e.g. "15th and 16th centuries,", "period marked by", "saw the") in Renaissance or medieval history text, where a description of the era follows. Silent after similar period phrases in other contexts.
result.label: Era phrase connector in Renaissance history

result.description: Fires on prepositions and linking words (of, in, on, supporting) right after "role/determinant/impact" phrases in soil moisture and plant-growth text, predicting plant, soil or agriculture terms next. Silent on similar "role of" phrases in general ecology or climate text.
result.label: Soil moisture linking prepositions

result.description: Fires on the word ' never' (occasionally ' ever') in any context, often mid-clause before a verb or participle. It pushes toward adverbs and words like 'theless', 'fully', 'truly'. Upstream members are mostly 'never' detectors plus related negation words.
result.label: ' never' token detector

result.description: Fires on the last token of an abstract noun subject (texture, practices, complexity, cohesion, ethics) inside a "that ..." clause, where a verb like "is/are/cannot/alone" is expected next. Silent on "diversity" followed by "and".
result.label: Abstract noun subject awaiting verb

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' stream' when it is likely to continue as 'streamlines' / 'streamlined' (e.g. fluid dynamics streamlines), predicting 'line', 'lined', 'lines' next. Upstream members are mostly ' stream' detectors.
result.label: ' stream' before -line/-lined

result.description: Fires on the word piece " ins" when it starts "insights", after verbs like offer/provide or adjectives like important/practical. It stays quiet on " ins" in other words such as insurance or insulators, and in one "giving deep ins" case.
result.label: " ins" of "insights"

result.description: Fires on ' results' as a noun for findings or outcomes, mostly in scientific or analytical text after an adjective (reliable, biased, reproducible). It predicts words like 'obtained' or 'gathered'. Silent on the verb use "results in".
result.label: ' results' as noun (findings)

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ivid' in 'vivid' (after 'v'), mostly in writing and imagery text, where it is followed by nouns like imagery, detail, scenes or colors. Upstream members are mostly 'ivid' detectors.
result.label: 'ivid' in 'vivid'

result.description: Fires on the word " art" right after "an" or "the" when it is a standalone noun, as in "an art form" or "an artistic technique". It stays silent on "art" inside compounds or after other words, such as "food art".
result.label: ' art' after "an" (art form)

result.description: Fires on the piece 'al' completing "focal" (focal point/length) in optics and photography text. It stays silent on 'al' in other words such as "reveal". It predicts "point", "points" or "length" next.
result.label: "foc|al" in focal point/length

result.description: Fires mid-word on pieces like 'ole'/'cular' in "intermolecular", plus apostrophes before t/s in contractions (isn', won'), and some other word fragments. Pushes toward ' forces'. Mixed, low-consistency peaks.
result.label: Intermolecular fragments and apostrophes

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'vent' inside "inter-vent-ions" (also con-vent-ional, sol-vent, ele-vent-h), predicting suffixes like 'ions'/'ional'. A few weaker peaks on other mid-word pieces (all-ure, teleport-ation).
result.label: 'vent' mid-word piece (interventions)

result.description: Fires on ' the' after a verb or preposition (where, by, keep, represents, driving) in macroeconomics and monetary-policy text, such as central bank or market discussions. It is quiet on ' the' in non-economic or generic contexts.
result.label: ' the' in economics/finance text

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ash' in "clash"/"clashes"/"clashing" (conflict between parties). Members include 'ash' detectors plus conflict/tension words (dispute, tension, contrast, disagreement). Silent on a contrast text about tension without the 'ash' piece.
result.label: 'ash' in clash (conflict)

result.description: Fires on nouns meaning constituent parts (components, blocks, elements, parts), mostly after adjectives like "essential", "key", "fundamental building", "all three". Predicts "of" next. Silent on "system components" as a plain compound.
result.label: Essential components / building blocks

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces, mostly ' in' and ' of' after a noun, plus 'iders' and 'ut'. Members are many ' in' detectors, including the 'in-' prefix. It is silent on some ' in' after nouns like belief or trust. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed ' in' / ' of' connector tokens

result.description: Fires on the word piece that ends an "eco-" or "environmentally" adjective ("ally" in environment-ally, "co" in e-co), after "both sustainable and". It pushes toward "friendly", "conscious" or "-" next.
result.label: eco-/environmentally before friendly

result.description: Fires on the final piece of a split food-ingredient word (choc-olate, pot-ato, tom-ato, pump-kin) in culinary or recipe text, where a noun like sauce, breast or roll tends to follow.
result.label: Food ingredient word endings
Connectives in technical business/data text
result.description: Fires on connectives like ' and', ',', ' of' and ' data' in expository text about software, business intelligence, data and technology, where a list or noun phrase is continuing. Silent on many ' and' tokens in other contexts.

Fires on ' this' (occasionally ' these', ' entire', ' total') when it comes right after a comma and starts a new clause, as a demonstrative referring back to an earlier idea. It stays quiet on ' this' after a preposition or verb.
result.label: Clause-initial ' this' after comma

result.description: Fires on the end of an adjective or field word (pharmaceut-ical, biotechn-ological, industrial, medical, engineering) that is likely followed by a noun like "industry", "sector" or "landscape". Silent on "ical" in analytical or statistical.
result.label: Sector adjective before 'industry'

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (of, that, with, shapes) in philosophical text about death and existence, where the next word is likely 'death' or 'existence'. Silent on 'understanding of' in other philosophy contexts.
result.label: Function words in existential death philosophy

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece "um"/"UM" completing "datum" (dat+um) in geodesy text, with a few weaker hits on other tokens. Members detect "dat", reference frame, coordinate and geodesy terms.
result.label: "um" ending "datum" in geodesy

result.description: Fires on " the" after "continued into/in" (or similar period-spanning verbs), where a decade or era like "the 1980s" or "the late 20th century" comes next. Silent on "the" in other constructions.
result.label: "the" before a time period

result.description: Fires on word endings like -ists, -ology, -istics naming an academic field or its practitioners (linguists, anthropology, linguistics), especially in linguistics-related academic text. Silent on humanists, empiricists, economists.
result.label: Academic field/scholar suffixes (-ists, -ology)

result.description: Fires on the middle sub-word pieces 'ene' and 'ur' inside the split word "entrepreneur(ship/ial/s)". It predicts word-completing suffixes such as 'ial', 'ship', 'urs'.
result.label: entrepreneur word-piece 'ene'/'ur'

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Thom" when it begins "Thomson", mostly in Thomson scattering physics text. It predicts a following "son" suffix. Related word-start pieces (Sch, Pr, Bo) contribute as members.
result.label: " Thom" before "son" (Thomson)

result.description: Fires on the hyphen in "decision-" (and data-, leader-) where "making/maker" is expected next, and on "standpoint"/"perspective" in "from an X standpoint/perspective". Silent on hyphens in other compounds like long-term or thrill-seekers.
result.label: decision-making hyphen / standpoint

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " influ" (as in influential, influences), including "influ" mid-word before "ential"/"ences". It predicts completions like "ential" and "ence". Members are mostly "influ" detectors.
result.label: " influ" word-start piece
Word-initial "pro" piece
result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " pro" / " Pro", as in proactive, proton, probability, probe, proletariat. It predicts continuations like "active", "gression" and "tot". The contrast has no "pro" token, so it stays silent there.

Fires on ' each' when it begins an appositive-style clause right after a comma following a plural set (periods, styles, schools, states), as in ", each with its own...". Members are mostly detectors of each/every.
result.label: ", each" after plural group

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fi' when it begins "fiber" (dietary fiber, carbon fiber, fiberglass), predicting 'ber' next. Weak activity on a few other tokens.
result.label: ' fi' piece of "fiber"

result.description: Fires on the token " no" after a plural subject noun, where it begins "no longer" (e.g. "musicians no longer need"). Predicts " longer" next. Members detect " no" broadly, including "no" as the start of words like "noisy".
result.label: " no" in "no longer"

result.description: Fires on the word-start pieces " intr" (intricate, intrigue) and " del" / " Del" (delving, delicate), predicting continuations like 'icate', 'igue', 've'. Appears in descriptive, literary-style prose; silent on the contrast text, which lacks these pieces.
result.label: intr- / del- word starts (intricate, delve)

result.description: Fires mostly on " its" (also "the", "a", "be") after "since"/"from"/"to", where a word like "early", "initial" or "inception" is expected next. Silent on " its" in other constructions, such as "contributed to its ongoing". Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: "its" before early/initial-type words

result.description: Fires on the word piece " comp" when it starts a word, mostly in chemistry text where "compounds" is expected next. It predicts "ounds"/"ound" as the continuation. It is weaker on "compilers" and "compasses".
result.label: " comp" start of "compounds"

result.description: Fires on the word pieces completing "Swiss Army knife" (' kn', 'ife', 'ives'), also ' Sur' in "Surface". Silent on 'ife' in ordinary "knife" phrases without Swiss Army, so it needs the Swiss Army Knife idiom.
result.label: Swiss Army knife completion

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' convers' (start of conversation/conversational) and predicts a suffix like 'ational' or 'ations'. It was silent on one text-initial 'conversational AI' example, so it may need preceding context.
result.label: ' convers' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on ' CPU' (also ' memory', ' RAM') in computer-architecture text about memory hierarchy, caches and processors. Silent on memory-related text without this hardware framing. Predicts hardware nouns such as controller, chip, cores.
result.label: CPU / memory in hardware text

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in a possessive 's after a proper name (Le Chatelier's, Cramer's, Luther's), especially eponymous principles and rules. Stays silent on plural-possessive, decade, and contraction apostrophes like It's.
result.label: Possessive apostrophe after proper names

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' sust' (of sustainability/sustainable), predicting continuations like 'ain'/'aining'. It is stronger after function words or abstract nouns and silent after 'create', 'a' or 'environmental' before sustainable.
result.label: ' sust' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ifer' inside 'proliferation' (also non-proliferation, proliferate), predicting suffixes like -ation/-ate/-ant. Members are mostly 'ifer' detectors plus other mid-word pieces that precede a suffix.
result.label: 'ifer' in proliferation

result.description: Fires on the letter "A" (' A' or 'A') used as a variable or label, such as event A, matrix A or set A in probability, set theory and linear algebra text. Weaker on sentence-initial article "A".
result.label: Letter A as math variable

result.description: Fires on the piece 'et' inside "multifaceted" (multifac|et|ed), predicting the suffix 'ed'. Members detect 'et' and 'fac' pieces; it is weaker in the hyphenated "multi-faceted" form.
result.label: 'et' in multifaceted

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on mixed tokens (word pieces, commas in repeated-backslash text, function words, non-English fragments) in technical or academic prose. Weak consistency; logits mildly favor 'simulation'-type words. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Diffuse technical-prose mid-word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' certain', ',', ' the', 'into', 'of') in abstract expository text about communication or concepts, where the next word is a mid-phrase noun or word piece. Peaks are inconsistent; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'ed' of "trac-ed" in "can be traced back to" (origin tracing), with a weaker secondary peak on ' b' in "(ionic) b-onds". Silent on other '-ed' endings like "rooted" or "sprouted".
result.label: 'traced' back-to-origin 'ed'

result.description: Fires on word pieces that start 'conscious' (' conscious' before -ness, 'apt' in 'synaptic') in neuroscience and philosophy-of-mind text. It predicts suffix continuations like 'ness'. Silent on at least one 'conscious' after 'human'.
result.label: conscious / synaptic word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on function words (the, their, to, -ly) inside a playful chemistry text describing atoms/ions as party guests and hosts. Silent on 'the' in other topics. Predicts party/guest/electron words.
result.label: Atoms-as-party-guests function words

result.description: Fires on the subject word or pronoun (is, they, can, it, -ism) inside a "whether ..." clause in abstract philosophical text, just before the predicate. It predicts adverbs like truly, really, or sufficiently. It stays quiet on plain "X is" statements.
result.label: Subject inside 'whether' clause, philosophy

result.description: Fires on the '0' right after the initial '2' in 21st-century year/decade strings like "2020s" or "2030s", where the next digit is 2 or 3. It stays silent on '0' in 1950s, 1980s or 300 BC.
result.label: '0' in 2020s-style years

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly "the", "an", "a") in text about black holes and event horizons, where the next word is likely a black-hole term such as Hawking, Event, or Schwarzschild. Silent on "the" in other cosmology contexts.
result.label: Determiners before black-hole terms

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in the possessive "Newton's" (before s), especially in physics text about Newton's laws. It predicts ordinal or law words such as Third and Second. It is weaker after other names like Shakespeare.
result.label: Apostrophe after Newton

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' imp' at the start of a longer word such as implications, impeding, impasses or impurity. It pushes the next token toward continuations like 'lications', 'urity' and 'eding'.
result.label: ' imp' word-start piece

result.description: Fires mainly on the "une" piece in "fine-tune" (also "fine tuning"), where something is being adjusted or regulated. It stays silent on "une" in "immune". Weaker hits on other word pieces.
result.label: "tune" in fine-tune

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' tit' in words like titration, titrant and titanium, where more word pieces follow. Members are mostly ' tit' detectors, plus detectors for other incomplete word-start fragments (rec, li, neut).
result.label: ' tit' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ities' completing "externalities" (also 'b' in "herb"), in economics text on externalities and public goods. It stays quiet on 'ities' in other words like "irregularities".
result.label: "external-ities" suffix token
Sentence-initial adverb suffix (-ically)
result.description: Fires on adverb endings like "-ically", "-ally", "-ively", "-ly" and "Often" when they start a sentence, right after a period, as in "Historically, ..." or "...ically speaking". It stays quiet on mid-sentence "-ically" inside a clause.

Fires on the word "digital" (including "Digital"), especially in audio, media and analog-to-digital contexts. Upstream members are mostly detectors of "digital" and similar words like virtual or electronic. It pushes toward nouns like keyboard, computers and signals.
result.label: "digital" word detector

result.description: Fires on a plural abstract noun (ideas, problems, designs, themes, equations) right after "complex", "intricate" or "complicated". It stays silent on "themes" without such a preceding adjective. Logits favour continuations like "involving", "requiring" and "simpler".
result.label: Noun after complex/intricate adjective

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' tw' (as in twist, twisty, twisted, intertwine), predicting continuations like -isted, -ist, -itch, -irls. Members are mostly ' tw' detectors that push these same completions.
result.label: ' tw' word-start piece (twist)

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' f' when it is split off from the rest of a word (fractious, flip, fused, fission, flare, fruits, fuzzy, fallacy). It predicts continuations like 'law', 'lick', 'ract', 'ruits'.
result.label: Split word-initial ' f' fragment

result.description: Fires on the word "theme" (also "them-" pieces like "themes" and "thematic") in essay-style text about music, writing or composition. Upstream members are mostly theme-token detectors, with some topic and tone detectors.
result.label: Token "theme" in essays

result.description: Fires mostly on " graphics" after "computer", "modern" or "game", in technical computing text. It also fires weakly on scattered function words like "the", "of" and "at". Members are mostly graphics and animation detectors.
result.label: ' graphics' in computing contexts

result.description: Fires on prepositions (mostly ' of', also in/from/by) right after "collective behavior" in swarm intelligence text, predicting a following plural noun like "decentralized" agents. Silent on 'of' after other nouns such as design, aim, help.
result.label: 'of' after "collective behavior" (swarm)

result.description: Fires on the final word or piece of an academic topic or field name (Conflict, relationships, dynamics, integration, equilibrium, language) in heading-like lists. It pushes toward 'theories', 'systems', 'theory'. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Academic topic-term endings in headings

result.description: Fires on the word "there" (or "There") as the existential subject starting a clause, e.g. "there is/are/may be", at sentence start or after a conjunction or colon. Members are mostly "there" detectors.
result.label: Existential "there" clause subject

result.description: Fires on 'and', commas, 'or' that join items in a list of verb phrases (actions or practices) where a new verb in -ing/base form comes next. Silent on 'and' joining plain nouns in a list.
result.label: Conjunction before next verb phrase

result.description: Fires mainly on the ' Sh' token starting a name such as Shor, Shapley or Shannon, often in quantum or algorithm text. It also fires weakly on LaTeX ' $\' openers. It pushes toward name continuations like 'or', 'amos' and 'l'.
result.label: ' Sh' name-start in technical text

result.description: Fires on adjectives or comparative modifiers (different, simple, complex, -er, ordinary, remaining) in cooking and culinary text, where a noun like ingredients, cuts or flavors is expected next. Silent on non-modifier tokens in the same cooking passages.
result.label: Culinary adjective/modifier before food noun

result.description: Fires on word-ending pieces like 'ic', 'mic', 'ple', 'th' in technical chemistry/thermodynamics words (exothermic, endothermic, participle, affinity). Silent on 'ic' in other words like symbolic or isochoric. Members are chemistry-reaction context.
result.label: Chemistry word suffix pieces (exothermic)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' co' when it is a prefix that starts a word like cooperation, cooperative, coaching or coexistence, and pushes the next token towards 'operation' or 'oper'. Quiet on unrelated text.
result.label: ' co' prefix before 'operation'

result.description: Fires on particles and verb-completing tokens after a verb, such as "coming out", "comes together", "pops up" and "sprouted". It also fires weakly on a stray digit. Silent when " out" is inside a word like "outlet" or in "sniff out". The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Verb particles: out, together, up

result.description: Fires on connecting function words and verb endings (such as, by, includes, -ates) in biology/psychology/stress passages, where a biological or cognitive term is expected next. Silent on "such as" in cooking and genre text.
result.label: Connectives in biology/stress text

result.description: Fires on the '0' in the third digit of a decade year like 180/170 in "the late 1800s" phrasing, right before the final 's'. It stays silent on '0' in standalone years or ranges such as "between 1960 and".
result.label: Decade-year '0' before 's'

result.description: Fires on the word " virtue" (also "principle", virtue-word pieces) in moral philosophy and virtue-ethics text. Members are mostly virtue detectors plus philosophy-context members. Predicts suffixes like "-hood" or "-ality".
result.label: virtue in ethics discussion
' virt' word-piece before 'ues/uous'
result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' virt' (start of virtues/virtuous), with weaker hits on ' product', ' where' and similar prefixes. It predicts suffixes like 'uous' and 'ues'. Members are mostly ' virt' detectors.

Fires on the token " access" used as a noun after a modifier (increase access, direct access, limited access, greater access), often before "to" or "-ibility". It stays quiet when "access" is a verb or starts a text.
result.label: noun ' access' after modifier

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cru' when it begins "crucial", typically after "is" or "being" in sentences saying something is important. It predicts the continuation "cial".
result.label: ' cru' start of "crucial"

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece " mel" (as in melody) in music-related text, with weaker peaks on " and" in lists and on "op" in Mesopotamia. It predicts word continuations like "ody". The circuit is mixed and only partly faithful.
result.label: " mel" start of melody

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' lear' when it begins "learner" (a lear|ner), in education text. It is silent on the full word "learning". Members include other word-start fragment detectors that predict the 'ner' continuation.
result.label: ' lear' as start of learner

result.description: Fires on the opening parenthesis after a technical term, mostly biology or science nouns, where an abbreviation or short gloss is expected, e.g. "growth hormone (GH)". Predicts acronym-like or term continuations.
result.label: Parenthesis after technical term
Calvin 'vin' piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'vin' in "Calvin" (Calvinism, Calvin's), predicting suffixes like -ism/-ist. Members mostly detect 'vin' and similar mid-word pieces. Weak activation on 'win' in Darwin.

Fires on the word piece ' math' when it is the start of a longer word such as 'mathematician', mostly after "a/an amateur/Italian/French". It pushes the next token towards 'ematic', 'ém', 'emat' continuations.
result.label: ' math' before -ematician

result.description: Fires on the word piece " pen" (also " Pen"), usually as the start of a longer word such as penetration, penalty or peninsula, and also in the standalone noun "pen". It predicts continuations like "etr", "alt" and "chant".
result.label: " pen" word-start token

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ster' (also ' Ster') when it begins a longer word like steroid or sterile. Members are detectors of other word-initial fragments (fert-, cot-, ris-, invas-) that predict a continuation.
result.label: ' ster' word-start fragment
Passive 'research conducted/carried out'
result.description: Fires on ' conducted' (occasionally ' out' in 'carried out') after a research, study or experiment noun, typically in passive or participle use ('research was conducted', 'studies conducted'). Predicts experiments, studies, done.

Fires on capitalized acronym pieces like 'ER' and 'NER' (also POS, NL) in technical text, such as Entity-Relationship (ERD) or Named Entity Recognition (NER) in NLP/ML contexts. Predicts acronym continuations like NER or POS.
result.label: NLP/database acronym 'ER'/'NER'

result.description: Fires on the word piece "strateg" (' strateg' or 'ateg' in "Strategic") in business-management text, where the next piece is likely "ic/ies". Silent on some occurrences in other phrasings, so context matters.
result.label: strateg- piece in business text

result.description: Fires on ' Dr' at the start of a new line in a list of names (e.g. "Dr. Johnson.¶ Dr. Williams."). Stays silent on lists of names without the Dr title. Weak activity on a few list commas.
result.label: ' Dr' in name lists

result.description: Fires on quantity-of-options nouns like "variety", "combination", "range", "multi" after "a" (e.g. "employ a variety of"), mostly in technical or method-related text. It predicts method or technique words next. Silent when "variety" starts the text.
result.label: "a variety/range/combination of" slot

result.description: Fires on varied words (those, together, over time, student, and) in text about people collaborating, connecting and sharing ideas. Logits favour ' themselves', ' they', ' independently', ' alone'. Peaks are inconsistent, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Collaboration and togetherness text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' proc' at the start of "procurement" (or "procure"), mostly in supply chain text. Members detect ' proc' and similar word-start pieces like ' rec', ' alloc' and ' fil'.
result.label: ' proc' in procurement

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'arg' in 'bargain' and its derivatives (bargaining, bargained, bargainer), predicting the continuation 'aining/ained/ain'. Weak activation on other mid-word pieces like 'ilib' and 'ut'.
result.label: 'arg' in bargain

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (allows, of, in, enabling, developing) in technical or academic text about technology and research, where a plural noun like methods, tools or ways is likely next. Mixed peaks, low consistency; evidence is thin.
result.label: Technical text slot before plural nouns

result.description: Fires on art/discipline nouns like "writing", "fiction", "painting" when a modifier precedes and the term is the subject of a comparison (e.g. "formal writing", "informal writing"). It predicts verbs like "excel", "tends", "typically". Silent on some "writing" uses.
result.label: Genre/discipline noun as subject

result.description: Fires on the verb (mostly ' is', also ' can', ' be') right after an abstract subject like mastery of or understanding a skill or concept, where an evaluative predicate such as essential, crucial or necessary comes next. Silent when there is no such subject.
result.label: Verb after skill/understanding subject

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'iv' inside multi-piece words like capt-iv-ating, p-iv-otal, omn-iv-ores, predicting a suffix such as 'ating' or 'otal'. Weaker on some other mid-word pieces (mult, tri, fasc-in).
result.label: 'iv' mid-word piece (captivating)

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start fragments, mostly ' multip' (before "licity") and 'omed' in "Biomedical", where the next piece completes the word. Members are mostly ' multip' detectors plus other word-start pieces such as retr, quant, cul and emp.
result.label: Word-start fragments: multip, omed

result.description: Fires on the word " mixed" (also "ixed" after M), mostly in "mixed media" art text, and predicts " media" next. Weaker on "mixed up" or "mixed with".
result.label: "mixed" before "media"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Tri" / " tri" (as in Pascal's Triangle, triangles, triangular), and predicts continuations like "angle", "angular", "angles". Mostly a token detector for this prefix.
result.label: Tri- prefix before "angle"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' emp' when the context is about empires and territorial expansion. It predicts 'ire'/'ires' next, with some 'ower' (empowerment) members in the circuit.
result.label: ' emp' piece before 'ire'

result.description: Fires on "that", "to", "which" or a comma after a noun or verb in text about symbols, maps and visual communication. It sits where a verb like convey, communicate or denote is expected next. It stays silent on "that" in other topics.
result.label: Symbol-conveying relative 'that'/'to'

result.description: Fires on passive past participles of distribution/handling verbs (distributed, maintained, managed, delivered, transported) after a passive "is/are/be" subject, especially for electricity or goods. Silent on attributive "distributed systems".
result.label: Passive distribution/handling participles

result.description: Fires on connector words and commas (such as, including, like, of) in water-cycle and hydrology text where a list of components or factors is about to follow. Predicts water/model/simulation terms. Silent on plain 'of' elsewhere.
result.label: Hydrology list-introducing connectors

result.description: Fires on the word piece "or" inside "rhet-or-ic" (rhetor, rhetorical, rhetorician), predicting suffixes like -ic, -ical, -ician. Also weakly on similar mid-word pieces such as "aud-it". Silent on "or" in other words like "elect-or-ate".
result.label: "or" inside rhetor-ic words

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' co' in materials/chemistry text, where it is the start of a word like coating, copper or coated. Predicts continuations such as 'pper', 'ating', 'ated'.
result.label: ' co' word-start in coating/copper

result.description: Fires on the word " historical" (rarely "histor-"), mostly in academic discussion of history, philosophy and interpretation. Many upstream members detect the same token. It pushes toward nouns like context, method, inquiry and narrative.
result.label: ' historical' adjective detector

result.description: Fires on ' of' directly after "one" (also "some") in the partitive "one of the most/many…" construction. It stays silent on ' of' after nouns like "terms", "part", "challenge", "demands".
result.label: 'of' in "one of the"

result.description: Fires on the token ' ten' (as number, in "nearest ten", "power of ten", or as the start of "tenor"). It is silent on unrelated text. Logits favor suffix pieces like 'or', 'acity', 'ets', so it seems to treat ' ten' as a word-start piece.
result.label: ' ten' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on commas inside a list of items, especially the SMART goals acronym list (Specific, Measurable, Achievable). Silent on commas in ordinary prose clauses, such as "for example," or "on the other hand,".
result.label: Commas in SMART-style lists

result.description: Fires on plural subject nouns like "databases" (also "systems", "which", "that") when they are the subject of a clause about NoSQL or non-relational databases, just before a verb like "are designed to". It stays quiet when "databases" is an object or follows a preposition.
result.label: NoSQL databases as clause subject

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ing' (or 'ating') ending an evaluative adjective like intrigu-ing or fascin-ating, before a noun such as puzzle, aspect or prospect. Silent on verb -ing endings like deconstructing or analyzing.
result.label: Adjective -ing in intriguing/fascinating

result.description: Fires on function words and suffixes (-ing, of, to, for, the) in positions right before an object noun about harm, damage or environmental/efficiency effects, e.g. "at the expense of", "neglecting". Predicts words like damage, existing, functionality.
result.label: Connectors before damage/impact nouns

result.description: Fires on the token ' hands' (occasionally ' hand'), most strongly in 'hands-on' phrases about learning, and also in hand-washing text. It pushes the next token towards '-'. It stays silent on 'manual'.
result.label: ' hands' token, as in hands-on

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied mid-phrase tokens (' of', ' in', ' new', ' previous', word pieces like ' Sem', 'ing') in academic or encyclopedic text. No clear shared token or construction; the logits are mixed.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase academic tokens

result.description: Fires on commas, "for", "of" and verbs within lists or noun phrases of technical processes (planning, production, design, engineering) in technical expository text; silent on other commas. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Technical process list separators

result.description: Fires on 'by', 'that', 'within' or 'of' right after "goods and services (produced)" in economics definitions of aggregate supply or output. It predicts a producer-type noun next (producers, firms). It stays silent on 'that' as a complementizer or relative pronoun elsewhere.
result.label: Economics 'goods and services produced by'

result.description: Fires on ' highlight' (also ' eng', ' Lock') as a finite verb after a subject noun, as in "design highlighted the importance" or "philosophy highlights". It stays silent on the infinitive "serves to highlight".
result.label: Verb 'highlight' after a subject

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after a technical math noun like derivative, kernel, rank, or null space, where a mathematical object follows ("kernel of a matrix"). It stays silent on ' of' after words like aspect, collection, or use.
result.label: ' of' after math object nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' fer' that starts "fermentation" (mid-sentence, in biology/food-science text), predicting the continuation "ment". Silent on ' fer' at the start of "fermenting" in the contrast. Weak activity on a few other word fragments.
result.label: ' fer' in fermentation

result.description: Fires on " otherwise" (occasionally " previously") as an adverb before an adjective or verb, as in "to otherwise dull texts" or "would otherwise be". Predicts negative or un- words like impossible, unknown.
result.label: "otherwise" / "previously" adverb

result.description: Fires on varied mid-sentence words (verbs, adjectives, determiners like "the", "your", "unique", "significant") in explanatory academic-style text, where a noun is expected next. Peaks are scattered and inconsistent; logits are weak and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase word before noun

result.description: Fires on sentence-initial additive transition words (Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover) that begin a new sentence or paragraph, typically at the start of a document or after a full stop. Silent on ordinary sentence starts.
result.label: Sentence-initial additive transitions

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' were', ' the', ' of', ' closely', word endings like 'lings') where the next word is likely a verb or continuation in academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent; the evidence is mixed and the pattern is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-clause academic continuation

result.description: Fires on the token ' housing' (affordable housing, housing market, urban housing) in urban, economic and policy text. Predicts continuations like prices, value, scarcity. Members are mostly ' housing' detectors plus urban-context cues.
result.label: ' housing' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word " artificial", mostly in AI and deep-learning text where "intelligence" comes next. It predicts " intelligence", " agent" and " neural". Upstream members mainly detect " artificial" itself.
result.label: ' artificial' before intelligence

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments of science words that are incomplete and need a continuation, such as 'ilib' in Equilibrium, 'ov' in photovoltaic, and ' energ' in energies. It fires in technical or scientific text, on the word piece before the suffix.
result.label: Incomplete science word fragments (ilib, ov, energ)

result.description: Fires on verbs or prepositions in academic-summary prose that introduce what a section or analysis covers (delves into, examines, highlights, detailing, considers). It predicts a following topic noun like urban, political or historical. It stays quiet on idiomatic "into" such as "come into play" or "taking into account".
result.label: Academic "examines/delves into" topic-introducer

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " alle" in genetics text, where it begins "alleles" (dominant, recessive alleles). It predicts a continuation like "les". It stays silent on the capitalized "allELEs" spelling.
result.label: " alle" piece of "alleles"

result.description: Fires on "distribution" or "density" (also "spread") in probability/statistics text, where the next word is likely "function" (as in cumulative distribution function, probability density function). Needs a probability-theory context.
result.label: Probability distribution/density before "function"

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative ' these' (or ' These') starting a subject noun phrase, typically after a comma or at sentence start, referring back to a previously listed set of things. Silent when 'these' follows a verb as an object.
result.label: Sentence-initial 'these' referring back

result.description: Fires on the verb or function word (' is', ' are', ' has') right after the subject noun "trend"/"trends". Silent on ' is' after other subjects such as "life cycle" or "consumption".
result.label: Verb after "trend(s)" subject

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' when it introduces an abstract noun object after "with" or a verb like "have/exposes", as in "with a pronounced shift" or "have a significant impact". Silent on ' a' after other verbs or prepositions.
result.label: ' a' after "with"/have, abstract noun

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " ins"/" Ins" when it begins a longer word such as insulators, inscribed, insurance or insights. It predicts continuations like "ights", "ula", "ur". It stays silent on "ins" in "inspection" after a broken token.
result.label: word-initial " ins" piece

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (as, and, use, include, from, in) that introduce a list or example in text about animal behavior, predators and species. Silent on "such as" in other subject areas like disease or research.
result.label: Connectives before lists in animal-behavior text

result.description: Fires on the quantifiers "Many" / "some" / "many", most strongly as a sentence-initial subject determiner (e.g. "Many people believe"). Pushes toward verbs like believe/argue and nouns like critics.
result.label: Many/some quantifier as subject

result.description: Fires on a bare space token that precedes digits (e.g. a year or number after "between", "the late") and on the piece ' pred' in "predator/predation" after prepositions. Silent on some spaces before numbers after "under"/"during the".
result.label: Space before number / ' pred' piece

result.description: Fires on the word " lives" (plural of life), mostly after a possessive or article such as "our lives" or "the lives of". Members are detectors of lives/life tokens in earlier layers. Weakly fires on " life" and " people".
result.label: " lives" after possessive/article

result.description: Fires on the word " quantum" (also " Hall" in quantum Hall, and "topological") in physics text, where a noun like systems, states, phases or mechanics is expected next. It is silent in one non-physics context about computational algorithms and information security.
result.label: ' quantum' in physics text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (control, focus, and, in) in passages about attention and cognitive control, e.g. "attention control" or "better focus". Silent on "control" in engineering or interpersonal contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Attention/cognitive control passages

result.description: Fires on verbs and connectives (express, introducing, incorporating, discuss, such as) in texts about modal logic, where the next word is likely necessity/possibility/modal. Silent on 'express' in general language or symbol-related texts.
result.label: Modal logic verbs predicting necessity

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe right after "you" (you're, you'll, you've), predicting a contraction like "re". Weaker on n't after could/can. Silent on the apostrophe in "let's", "'s" at the start of a word, and "don't".
result.label: Apostrophe after "you" contraction

result.description: Fires on abstract nouns like "world", "space", "relationships", "reality" ending a phrase in geometry/spatial-reasoning text (e.g. "three-dimensional world", "understanding of space"). Silent on some "relationships" tokens in the same topic.
result.label: Spatial-concept nouns in geometry text

result.description: Fires at the end of "Development Goals" (als/s) and the following " (" where an acronym like MDG/SDG is about to be given. Silent on ordinary words ending in "als" such as "professionals".
result.label: Development Goals before acronym

result.description: Fires on "important", "crucial" (cru-cial) and "essential" in the predicate of an "'s important/crucial to…" clause that follows a sentence end. Silent on "crucial" in some other contexts, such as "…ity is crucial for".
result.label: important/crucial after "'s" clause

result.description: Fires on " to" or " and" right after a starting year in a date range ("from 1750 to", "between 1900 and"), where the end year is expected next. Silent on " to" in other uses.
result.label: Year range connector before end year

result.description: Fires on 'and' or commas right after visual-art element nouns like shape, form, line in lists of art elements (e.g. "shapes and lines"), predicting another element or property like function, size, space. Silent after 'depth and'.
result.label: Art elements list: shape/form and

result.description: Fires on the 'rich' piece in the verb or noun 'enrich' (enrichment, enriching, enriched), where a suffix like -ment or -ed is expected next. Members are 'rich' detectors plus similar stem pieces such as 'emp-ower' and 'augment'.
result.label: 'rich' inside 'enrich-' words

result.description: Fires on the word right after "don't let" / "let's" (this, not, be, 's', concept) in imperative advice, where a verb like "take", "fool" or "stop" is expected next. Silent on "not" after "may/might/it's".
result.label: Word after "let's / don't let"

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "itive" completing "cognitive" (also "neurological", "neural") in neuroscience or psychology text, where a noun like processes, systems or development comes next. Quiet on "repetitive" and some other "cognitive" contexts.
result.label: "cognitive" suffix in neuroscience text

result.description: Fires on " of" (also in/to/for) right after a noun like "aspect", "part", "component" in "became an important/integral/essential aspect of X". Silent on other " of" uses such as "dawn of" or "explosion of".
result.label: "became integral part of" preposition

result.description: Fires on the final token of an abstract noun naming the inner nature of something, mostly "ence" in "essence", also " structure", " nature", " properties", where "of X" typically follows. Silent on "ence" in other words like prevalence or interdependence.
result.label: essence/nature noun before "of"

result.description: Fires on quantifier-like adjectives (various, different, multiple, diverse) right after verbs or prepositions of combining/integrating (combine, integration of, balancing), before a plural noun like types, sources, layers. Silent after "in/across various domains".
result.label: various/different after combining verbs

result.description: Fires on the word piece " lingu" at the start of linguistics, linguistic or linguist, mostly in academic text. Upstream members are mainly " lingu" detectors. The output pushes toward continuations like "istics", though the listed logits are noisy.
result.label: ' lingu' in linguistics/linguist

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (word pieces, ' of', spaces, ' models') in abstract academic or essay-style prose. Consistency is low and the contrast shows no clear rule. The circuit is diffuse and its members are mostly generic context.
